title: Ambush on Internal Security Forces leaves one dead and two injured
content:
The Internal Security Forces personnel patrolling Syria’s coastal region were targeted by armed individuals.




In a written statement, the General Directorate of Ports and Customs announced that one of its customs patrols had been targeted in an armed ambush.




The statement confirmed that one person was killed, and two others were injured.

author: Unknown
title: From France to Kurdistan: How well do we understand society in transition?
content:
France occupies a special place in the political memory of the modern world. The Enlightenment, the Revolution of 1789, and the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen gave freedom and equality universal significance. Yet proclaiming rights does not necessarily mean that all social groups can exercise them equally. The Republic’s promise of equality has repeatedly been put to the test by colonialism, class divisions, and discrimination against citizens with migrant backgrounds.




Against this backdrop, the words of jurist and statesman Robert Badinter, who lost his father during the Nazi occupation and played a key role in abolishing the death penalty in 1981, take on particular significance: “France is not the country of human rights, but the country where the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen was proclaimed.” The gap between the historical legacy of these rights and contemporary social realities continues to demand critical examination.




The new language of the streets




The protests by students at French secondary schools, which began in mid-September and continued throughout October 2026, offer valuable insights into contemporary French society. Teacher shortages, long school days, overcrowded classrooms, poor conditions in school cafeterias, and anxieties about the future are among the students’ concerns. Some protest signs also reveal a sense of humor: the irony of a student complaining that his overloaded timetable leaves him no time to see his girlfriend may seem trivial at first glance. Yet these young people are questioning not only the conditions of their education but also the way their everyday lives are organized.




After five weeks of sustained protests, the government announced a plan on October 26 that included changes to the Parcoursup* higher education admissions system, reductions in class sizes, and the creation of additional university places. School and university student organizations considered these measures insufficient. The fact that problems raised for years only make it onto the political agenda following mass mobilization by young people highlights the difference between merely listening to the youth and genuinely responding to their demands.




Taking to the streets is nothing new in France. The country has a deeply rooted culture of protest, stretching from the revolutions and May 1968 to workers’ strikes and demonstrations against pension reforms. Today’s Generation Z, however, has a different relationship with traditional institutions. Digital communication tools make it easier to mobilize around specific demands in a very short time. Yet this is not simply a matter of new means of organization. Young people refuse to let others determine their lives and futures. They demand that their voices, living conditions, and expectations be taken seriously, and they want to play an active role in shaping their own future.




How well do we, who are intimately familiar with May 1968 and the political struggles of the past, truly know today’s French youth and the social realities in which they live?




We live in an age when access to information is easier than ever before. Yet having access to information is far from the same as understanding society as it is lived today. Young people who do not carry the political memory of previous generations can still fight against the injustices they experience themselves. Rather than judging them by the standards of the past, we must listen to them and understand what they have to say today.




Between solidarity and racist violence




The social reality of France cannot be understood solely through young people’s protests and their search for solidarity. In a country where the ideals of freedom and equality have a significant historical legacy, discrimination, exclusion, and racist violence also persist.




After the protests by secondary school students had dominated public debate, an armed attack in Trappes and La Verrière on October 23 once again brought another, darker side of France into focus. One person was killed and five others were injured, including a twelve-year-old child. President Emmanuel Macron described the incident as a “racist terrorist attack.” Investigations are underway on suspicion of a racist motive and terrorist offenses.




No direct causal link can be established between the students’ protests against their educational conditions and this attack. However, the fact that both occurred during the same period illustrates how social tensions can manifest in different ways. The growing influence of the far right in Europe is another social reality that cannot be overlooked. Economic insecurity, migration, and anxieties about the future can, under certain circumstances, foster solidarity, while under others they can encourage exclusionary identity politics.




The key is not to hastily interpret social developments through existing ideological frameworks, but to understand them in terms of their own causes and contradictions.




Neo-nationalism and youth in Turkey




The anxieties about the future experienced by young people in France raise the question of what political orientations similar forms of social uncertainty might produce in other countries. The neo-nationalism emerging among young people in Turkey is particularly revealing in this regard.




According to a study published in December 2025 by researcher Selin Gücüm at the French Institute for International and Strategic Affairs (IRIS), a survey conducted by GoFor and KONDA in February 2024 among people aged 18 to 30 found that approximately 39 percent of respondents identified as nationalist, while 44 percent identified primarily as Kemalist. These figures refer to all young people surveyed, not exclusively to those holding neo-nationalist views.




Neo-nationalism is not merely a continuation of traditional conservative nationalism. It is also found among segments of urban, secular youth who are critical of authoritarian forms of rule. Some young people who express concerns about economic insecurity and restrictions on fundamental freedoms simultaneously perceive refugees or the political demands of Kurds as threats to national unity and sovereignty.




Why does someone who demands freedom for themselves fail to recognize the freedom of others as part of the same principle?




This political orientation cannot be explained solely as a spontaneous reaction emerging among young people. One of its key historical foundations lies in the homogenizing conception of national identity that the Turkish state has repeatedly reproduced through the education system, official historiography, and security-related discourse.




Selin Gücüm’s study highlights another important aspect: Some young people with neo-nationalist views do not regard the “father state” as a sacred and infallible authority, but instead criticize it for its inability to provide social and economic security. However, this criticism is not accompanied by an equal recognition of different identities. According to the report, Kurdish, Circassian, and Armenian identities are tolerated in these circles only insofar as they remain within the framework of “Turkishness.” This is therefore a political orientation that, while differing from traditional state nationalism, does not fully overcome its homogenizing conception of national identity.




No simple contrast can be drawn between young people in France and those in Turkey. Rather, the crucial question is why similar anxieties about the future foster solidarity under certain conditions, while under others they encourage a politics that denies other people their rights.




A shared future and social transformation




Can Kurdish and Turkish youth come together in a common democratic struggle in the face of poverty, unemployment, and anxieties about the future?




Shared problems do not necessarily give rise to a shared political consciousness. The experiences of Kurdish youth, shaped by language, identity, and historical memory, serve as a reminder that equality cannot be achieved solely on the basis of economic demands.




Moreover, shared problems are not experienced to the same extent everywhere. A report by the Center for Kurdish Studies comparing data from the SEGE-2017 and SEGE-2025 socioeconomic development indices describes 16 predominantly Kurdish-populated provinces as a “region of inequality.” After nearly a decade, none of these provinces had managed to move up to a higher level of development; all remained in the bottom 16 positions in the nationwide rankings. This does not indicate absolute stagnation, but rather that their relative position compared with the rest of Turkey has remained unchanged. While the region moved marginally closer to the national average, the gap between it and Istanbul actually widened.




Economic performance continued to improve in some provinces, but their rankings in education and healthcare remained virtually unchanged.




In the 2019/20 school year, the preschool enrollment rate in the region stood at 36 percent, compared with 46 percent in the other provinces. Understanding the lived realities of young people requires recognizing these conditions as well.




Kurdish youth may have a strong sense of patriotism and a deep identification with their origins. However, this should not be equated with adopting the political and organizational patterns of previous generations. Embracing Kurdish identity does not require rejecting other identities and can be reconciled with universal values of freedom and equality.




Everyone engaged with the Kurdish question and the cause of Kurdistan can make an effort to speak directly with the young people around them. Equally important, however, is listening to their answers without trying to change them. Young people’s political and ideological views may differ from our expectations. Interpreting these differences as a rejection of patriotism or the historical struggle would be an overly simplistic conclusion.




The living conditions of Kurdish youth in the four parts of Kurdistan, in cities outside Kurdistan in Turkey, Syria, Iraq, and Iran, in the Caucasus, and in other regions of the world are by no means identical. Education, working life, migration, women’s demands for freedom, and technological change are reshaping their relationship with politics.




One of the central challenges facing the Kurdish freedom movement is passing on the legacy of its historical struggle to future generations. Yet methods that brought success yesterday may become a weakness tomorrow if they are no longer sufficient to understand a changing society and its new dynamics. Passing on this legacy does not mean imposing the language and organizational forms of previous generations on young people, but enabling them to give meaning to that legacy within the context of their own lives and in their own language.




We are living through a period of polycrisis, characterized by interconnected crises in which wars, economic crises, mass migration, technological upheavals, and political tensions mutually reinforce one another. Wars are no longer fought solely on the front lines, but also in the realms of economics, technology, and information. It is as though we are living on a simmering volcano. Beneath the events we perceive on the surface, deeper tensions are building.




At such a time, political movements that seek to drive social transformation and change society must question not only their political discourse but also their established ways of listening and organizing. It is these young people who will live through the future. We, meanwhile, are increasingly the bearers of experiences from the past. These experiences are valuable. Developing visions for the future, anticipating developments, and exploring possible paths forward are also among the responsibilities of political movements.




Yet the experiences and insights of the past do not give anyone the right to determine alone how the future should be shaped. The real challenge lies in finding ways to envision and shape the future together, without imposing historical experience on new generations against their will.




How well do political movements that seek to transform society truly understand society in transition? Perhaps the question we must first ask ourselves is even simpler: How attentively do we actually listen to the young people to whom we say the future belongs?




*Parcoursup: France’s national online platform through which final-year secondary school students and other prospective students submit applications to universities and other higher education programs.

title: Hatimoğulları: Alevis should play an active role in the peace process
content:
DEM Party Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları called on the Alevi community to actively participate in the peace and democratization process in Turkey. At a meeting with representatives of Alevi organizations in Istanbul, she criticized the exclusion of Alevis from parliamentary deliberations and warned against leaving the future of the process solely in the hands of the government. Lasting peace, she argued, could only be achieved on the basis of equal citizenship, legally guaranteed fundamental freedoms, and the democratic restructuring of the republic.




The meeting took place at the Kazım Karabekir Cemevi in Istanbul’s Ümraniye district. Alongside representatives of Alevi associations and institutions, numerous other guests attended the event. Speaking here, Hatimoğulları emphasized that the process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan must not be understood as a power struggle between political camps. “We do not view peace in terms of one side winning and the other losing. Peace means building a shared life and giving one another our consent to do so. Genuine peace can only emerge when all 86 million citizens of this country can live in justice, freedom, and peace.”




Criticism of the exclusion of the Alevi community




The DEM Party co-chair recalled the decades of persecution, massacres, and assimilation policies targeting Alevis. Despite these experiences, she said, the Alevi community expanded its social and political organization in Turkey and Europe. Rather than allowing the history of injustices it suffered to paralyze it, the Alevi community drew strength from these experiences for its resistance and self-organization, she underlined. Hatimoğulları also addressed the massacres of Alevis in Syria by the Islamist forces of HTS, which have ruled the country since late 2024. She noted that international solidarity actions against this violence was warmly welcomed by the affected population.




Regarding the peace process, she particularly criticized the Turkish parliament speaker’s refusal to hear representatives of the Alevi community. “We have repeatedly asked the government why Alevis are not being heard. A faith community to which millions of people in this country belong cannot be ignored. Peace cannot be built without speaking to Alevis.” Remarking that the DEM Party has repeatedly insisted on their participation, she described Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş’s rejection of this demand as politically unacceptable.




Peace process amid state repression




Hatimoğulları spoke at length about the contradictions between the government’s official declarations of commitment to peace and its continued policies of repression. She pointed out that restrictions on freedom of expression, the persecution of opposition politicians, the imprisonment of critical voices, and the appointment of state trustees to opposition-run municipalities stood in the way of credible democratization. She also addressed questions that Alevi organizations had raised with the DEM Party: How can a peace process be advanced under conditions of severe state repression? Is there a risk that the AKP will exploit the process for its own electoral interests? And does participating in the talks mean politically aligning oneself with the government?




“These are all legitimate questions. As a party, we raise them with the same clarity as you do. The concerns and objections of the Alevi community must be taken seriously and discussed openly, Hatimoğulları stated. In this context, she also criticized the political instrumentalization of ongoing investigations and the unequal treatment of alleged financial crimes. “While opposition figures and smaller businesses are being targeted with considerable severity, the names of politically influential individuals allegedly implicated in the major investment fund scandal remain undisclosed.”




“If these were names from the opposition, wouldn’t they have published them on every front page long ago? But now they won’t even reveal the names. Why? Because the matter reaches into their own ranks. Despite the contradictions between the peace process and government policy, the democratic opposition must not abandon the struggle for a political solution.”




“We do not need religious brotherhood, but equal rights”




One of the DEM Party’s central demands is the legal guarantee of equal citizenship, Hatimoğulları said, rejecting a conception of social coexistence based on shared religious identity while ethnic, cultural, and religious differences continue to be politically subordinated. “Despite all these concerns and criticisms, we have no choice but to establish peace in this country. We do not need brotherhood based on the ummah, but solidarity based on equal citizenship. Religious brotherhood is not enough for us. We need equal rights, and this equality must be guaranteed by law.”




According to the DEM Party co-chair, Alevis must therefore not merely observe the process from the sidelines: “Their active participation is also necessary to prevent the government from determining its course and outcomes alone. If we manage to stand together at the heart of this process, take ownership of it, and move it forward, those who are carrying it forward will not be left alone. Peace will then no longer be left to the goodwill of this government.”




A democratic republic as a shared vision




Hatimoğulları reaffirmed that the demands of the Alevi community are an integral part of the DEM Party’s political program. These, she said, include recognition of religious and cultural diversity, a science-based education system free from state-imposed religious homogenization, and guaranteed access to education in one’s mother tongue. “Education policy, in particular, demonstrates how deeply state assimilation policies are embedded in social institutions,” she said, noting that the DEM Party opposes a homogenizing education system that excludes different identities, faiths, and languages from public life.




On the occasion of the 103rd anniversary of the founding of the Republic on October 29, Hatimoğulları emphasized the need for fundamental democratization of the political system. “The Republic must be the common home of all 86 million citizens. To achieve this, it must treat everyone equally and deny no one’s identity. What we need most urgently in Turkey today is the democratization of the Republic and the establishment of a democratic republic.”




Following her speech, the meeting with representatives of Alevi organizations continued closed to the press.

title: Iranian security bodies block medical leave for Kurdish political prisoner
content:
Iranian security bodies have blocked medical leave and access to adequate treatment for Fahim Ebadi, a Kurdish political prisoner in Orumiyeh Central Prison who suffers from diabetes, high blood pressure and high blood fat levels, the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported.




Iranian forces arrested Ebadi, who is from Orumiyeh and is serving a 45-month sentence, in the city around two years ago.




After several weeks of interrogation at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, he was transferred to Orumiyeh Central Prison, where he has remained since.




After several months in detention, a branch of the Islamic Revolutionary Court of Orumiyeh sentenced him to 60 months in prison on charges of “membership of opposition groups” in connection with membership of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).




His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months after he waived his right to appeal and requested a sentence reduction.

title: Resistance against solar power plant project in Kulp on day 91
content:
Resistance against the planned solar power plant project.in the village of Cixsê, in the Kulp district of Amed (Diyarbakır), has continued for three months. For 91 days, residents have maintained a vigil in protest against the project, which threatens grazing lands, water sources, and agricultural livelihoods. An investigation by the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) has now confirmed significant shortcomings in the environmental impact assessment. The organization is calling for the immediate cancellation of the project.




Representatives of the TMMOB Coordination Council in Amed presented their findings during a protest in Cixsê. The findings are based on a site inspection conducted on October 14, during which experts examined both the proposed construction site and the information contained in the environmental impact assessment documentation.




Grazing lands and water sources at risk




According to Filiz Kaçar, a member of TMMOB’s Energy and Ecology Commission, approximately 30 hectares of land within and around the project area are used as grazing grounds for livestock. The installation of solar panels, fencing of the site, and construction of access roads would fragment continuous grazing areas and significantly restrict their use. The commission is particularly concerned about the potential impact on local water resources. The affected area contains a pond and several streams that are important for supplying water to livestock. The planned construction work could damage these natural resources.




Cixsê is also an important center for silkworm breeding and cocoon production. Alongside livestock farming and crop cultivation, this sector forms a vital foundation of local livelihoods. According to the experts, habitats of migratory birds such as cranes, storks, and swallows would also be affected.




Significant shortcomings in the environmental impact assessment




According to Kaçar, TMMOB’s investigation found that key ecological and economic factors had been inadequately addressed in the project documentation. These include existing bodies of water, the traditional use of grazing lands, biodiversity, natural hazards, and the planned energy storage systems. The organization does not fundamentally oppose the expansion of renewable energy, but rather its implementation at the expense of local residents and their livelihoods. “The transition to renewable energy is necessary. But an energy transition that ignores nature and life is not sustainable. The solar project planned in Cixsê must be stopped immediately,” Kaçar stated.




Fatoş Nujen Ayhan of the TMMOB Coordination Council also criticized the economic interests behind the project: “Cixsê’s energy resources must be used and managed by the local population itself. We cannot allow corporations to exploit our resources and then sell the energy generated from them back to the people at high prices.”




Incorrect photographs previously discovered in environmental report




The new findings have intensified the dispute over the approval of the project. As early as September, it emerged that the environmental impact assessment report contained photographs that had not been taken in the proposed project area. The Amed Bar Association and the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) subsequently filed a criminal complaint against officials of the environmental consultancy Global ÇED and the construction company VBZ İnşaat. However, the public prosecutor’s office in Kulp found insufficient grounds for suspicion of document forgery and closed the investigation. The lawyers appealed the decision. Separately, the decision approving the environmental impact assessment is the subject of administrative court proceedings.




“Our land belongs to us”




The DEM Party also supports the villagers’ resistance. Berivan Turan, a member of the party’s provincial executive board in Amed, warned of the long-term social and ecological consequences during the protest. She stated that the loss of agricultural land and natural resources could exacerbate unemployment, poverty, and migration. “The people do not want a solar power plant on this grazing land. They have been expressing their opposition for months,” Turan said. She placed the resistance in Cixsê within the broader context of local struggles against the economic exploitation of natural resources in Kurdistan, citing the vigil in Arzoxlî as an example.




“We do not want to lose our cemeteries, our culture, or our memories. We will not allow any further plundering of Kurdistan. Yesterday we were in Arzoxlî; today we are in Cixsê. Our struggle continues,” Turan said.




Remarking The local population would not give up its livelihoods, she stated: “Our land belongs to us, and we will not give it to anyone. The natural environment of Cixsê is indispensable to us. We are resisting the solar project because we want to pass this heritage on to our children intact. We demand energy production that serves the people, not projects imposed against their will.”

title: Concern for at Least 14 Kurdish prisoners facing death sentences in Iran
content:
30 October has been declared International Day of Political Prisoners. A review of published human rights reports identifies at least 14 Kurdish political prisoners and protesters facing death sentences in Iran.




This list brings together reported cases and includes both initial court rulings and sentences upheld on appeal. Pakhshan Azizi, Hatem Ozdemir, Yousef Ahmadi, Pezhman Touberehrizi, Arman Marefati, Mohammad Faraji, Raouf Sheikh-Maroufi and Mohsen Eslamkhah are eight of these prisoners.




Earlier human rights reports warned that they could face execution. The reports described unfair and secretive proceedings, torture, pressure to obtain forced confessions, and violations of their right to defend themselves.




Hatem Ozdemir is a Kurdish citizen of Turkey imprisoned in Iran. Khosrow Mohammadnia, Masoud Toushmalani, Sirwan Shabani, Borzou Rezaei and Omran Amani are five others on the list. They were sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests. The sentences against the first three were reported on 1 October, and Rezaei’s on 6 October. On 29 October, it was reported that 21-year-old Omran Amani had been formally informed of his death sentence at Great Tehran Penitentiary.




Varisheh Moradi, a Kurdish political activist and member of the East Kurdistan Free Women’s Society, is also among the 14. On 14 October, Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced her to death for a second time. The Supreme Court had overturned her earlier sentence because of an incomplete investigation and problems with the trial process. Her lawyers say the court repeated the death sentence without addressing those problems.




The cases are at different stages of the legal process. The Supreme Court has previously upheld the death sentences against Pakhshan Azizi, Hatem Ozdemir and Yousef Ahmadi. One of Ahmadi’s two death sentences was changed to financial compensation and imprisonment. However, his other death sentence, on a charge of “armed rebellion,” remains in place.




This year’s International Day of Political Prisoners places a strong emphasis on keeping prisoners’ names in public view and supporting their families.




In a joint statement, the 30 October Coalition called for sustained international attention and the immediate, unconditional release of people imprisoned for exercising their basic rights. It also stressed the need to hold those responsible for abuses accountable.

title: Human rights violations against Kurds continue in Iran
content:
The Iranian regime’s practices of detention, imprisonment and punishment targeting Kurds continue. According to information reported by the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), a request for medical leave by Fehîm Ebadî, a Kurdish prisoner with diabetes held in Urmia Central Prison, has been rejected, preventing him from accessing medical treatment.




Ebadî was detained by Iranian regime forces in Urmia two years ago. He was sentenced to five years in prison on the allegation of being a “member of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).” His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months.




Detained without a warrant




Mohammad Reza, who lives in the Malekshahi region of Ilam Province, was detained by Iranian regime forces and taken to an undisclosed location. According to KHRN, Mohammad Reza was detained at his family home in the early hours of the morning on 29 October, without the authorities presenting an arrest warrant. No information has yet emerged regarding the grounds for his detention.




Kurdish cultural activist arrested




Metîn Feremerzpûr, a Kurdish cultural activist and doctoral student in philosophy at the University of Tabriz, was also detained by regime forces on allegations of “propaganda against the state” and taken to Mahabad Prison. According to KHRN, Feremerzpûr was detained on 8 July at Şêx Şaltut Park in Mahabad. After being released, he was summoned to give another statement and was detained again when he appeared.




Prison sentences handed down to two Kurdish political prisoners




KHRN also reported that prison sentences have been handed down to Kurdish political prisoners Mîlad Nasirîran and Afşîn Ezîzî, who were transferred to Urmia Central Prison. Nasirîran was sentenced to 11 months in prison, while Ezîzî received a three-year prison sentence. Mîlad Nasirîran was reportedly detained by Iranian regime forces in Ilam Province three months ago and transferred to Urmia Central Prison a few days ago.

title: ATE protestó frente al Ministerio de Defensa por el cierre de la IOSFA
content:
La movilización rechazó la decisión del Gobierno nacional de ‘disolver y liquidar’ el funcionamiento de la Obra Social de las Fuerzas Armadas (ex IOSFA) y que afecta a 352.000 afiliadas y afiliados a nivel nacional.







Fotos: Camila Rey y Chiqui Rodríguez.




Este jueves ATE llevó adelante una Jornada Nacional de Protesta en defensa de las funciones de la Obra Social de las Fuerzas Armadas y del Personal Civil (IOSFA/OSFA), ante la reciente resolución impuesta por el Gobierno nacional que disuelve y liquida el organismo, poniendo en riesgo la continuidad laboral de 1450 trabajadoras y trabajadores.

Mercedes Cabezas, Secretaria General Adjunta de ATE Nacional, expresó: “Multitudinaria la marcha que protagonizamos al Ministerio de Defensa, en defensa del trabajo de 1450 trabajadoras y trabajadores, de las farmacias y de los hoteles de la antigua IOSFA, actual OSFA. También para construir una política de defensa y de seguridad que tenga en cuenta los deseos, las necesidades y los derechos del pueblo argentino. El genocidio planificado de Javier Milei que ataca el sistema de salud, de defensa, de seguridad, y lo pone al servicio de políticas colonizadoras, genera no solo que se vacíe la obra social sino que se atente contra nuestro pueblo porque el sistema de salud está desfinanciado. Esta obra social, que es la única nacional estatal que queda en pie en la Argentina, es entregada a manos privadas, a Medicus que fue la primera prepaga que se acercó a hacerse cargo de la Prefectura y Gendarmería y comenzó el vaciamiento de la obra social”. Y agregó: “Ese sistema de salud que colapsa no solamente deja sin atención a las fuerzas armadas y de seguridad, sino también a las y los trabajadores civiles, con el malestar que conlleva eso. Los salarios no alcanzan para pagar coseguros o acceder a prácticas médicas mínimas, porque la obra social empieza a no cubrirlas. Sostener esa obra social es posible con una buena administración y con la conciencia plena de que estamos defendiendo los derechos del pueblo. Milei plantea no solamente un plan colonizador, sino también un plan entregador de soberanía que solamente puede llevarse a cabo con el sistema privado de obras sociales y sus negocios”.




En el marco del Plan de Lucha que está llevando a cabo ATE en defensa de la Obra Social, se marchó hacia el Ministerio de Defensa nacional para protestar por el cierre de las 31 farmacias propias, los 1450 puestos de trabajo que están en riesgo y la preservación y sostenimiento del patrimonio – hoteles, delegaciones y Auditoría de Facturación de Prestaciones Regional – que se pretende rematar.




La concentración tuvo lugar en la intersección de Avenida Belgrano y Azopardo de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, desde donde las y los dirigentes de ATE repudiaron el cierre de áreas clave que permiten no solo facilitar la atención personalizada para miles de usuarios a lo largo y ancho del país sino también que forman parte de los controles del organismo para que funcione de forma adecuada, impidiendo la doble facturación y otras irregularidades.




Es importante subrayar que de concretarse el cierre de los centros médicos, se perjudicará aun más la atención a las y los afiliados ya que no podrán acceder a prestaciones básicas como por ejemplo consultas clínicas o pediátricas. Además, si hubiera cuando retrasos o suspensiones en los pagos a proveedores no habrá posibilidades de acceder a los servicios de salud.

author: Clare Hymer
title: Police Threaten to Arrest Anyone Helping Protesters at Palestine Action Demo
content:
The Metropolitan police has said it will arrest anyone providing “logistical support” to those protesting the Palestine Action ban in London on Saturday. 




This means people could be arrested for bringing water to elderly and disabled people holding placards, organisers Defend Our Juries (DOJ) said.




Commander Adam Slonecki, who is 

leading the policing operation

 outside the US embassy, said: “I want to be clear – it is not just those who hold up placards who should expect to be arrested.




“Anyone officers consider to be playing a key role in organising the event, giving instructions to others and/or providing logistical support will very likely be committing an offence and face enforcement action.”




DOJ also raised concerns that this could also include their own media liaisons.




When approached by Novara Media for clarification, a Met spokesperson said: “

Section 44 of the Serious Crime Act 2007 makes it an offence to intentionally encourage or assist an offence.




“We are not going to define the terms we’ve used in our press release beyond their plain English meanings. Each incident is assessed on its own merits, and it is for officers to form the reasonable grounds to suspect an offence has taken place.”




A spokesperson for DOJ said in a statement: “How can the Met possibly justify arresting people who are not defying the ban themselves, who are simply providing logistical support to the peaceful protesters, many of whom are elderly or disabled and in need of support?




“It is also reckless and irresponsible, putting the safety of elderly and disabled people at risk… The moral bankruptcy of the Met is complete.”




The London protest is due to be held at the same time as another in Edinburgh, just days before the start of a supreme court challenge to the ban on Palestine Action. 




Both protests hope to draw attention to 

questions over whether

 Keir Starmer’s government announced the proscription under pressure from US president Donald Trump, following the spray-painting of Trump’s Scottish golf course by Palestine Action protesters in March 2025.




Palestine Action became the first direct action group in British history to be proscribed as a terror organisation in July 2025. Over 3,300 people have since been arrested for peacefully defying the ban on expressing support for the group.

title: Sciopero generale: l’Italia si blocca
content:
Giornata di sciopero generale: numeri ancor più massicci delle prime manifestazioni dell’autunno scorso. Blocchi in tutta Italia e cortei da decine di migliaia di persone, dalle metropoli alle province. 




Contro la guerra, contro il carovita, contro il riarmo voluto dal governo Meloni. E ancora, contro una vita precaria e indignitosa, per dire basta ai sacrifici che il governo italiano, insieme ai governi di tutta Europa, vogliono imporre alla popolazione. La partecipazione è stata impressionante, da Sud a Nord, oltre un milione in tutta Italia. Il Paese che per anni è stato narrato come il bacino dell’indifferenza e che nei migliori dei casi avrebbe voluto “fare come in Francia” in queste settimane, sull’onda del ciclo di movimento iniziato un anno fa a sostegno della Palestina e contro la complicità dei governi con il genocidio, sta dando un segnale chiaro: è giunto il tempo di alzare la testa. 




Grazie ai giovani che a fronte del peso di un futuro rubato stanno occupando scuole e università da un mese per affermare la propria esistenza, ai giovani che con rabbia calciano indietro la sfrontatezza dell’ingiustizia, oggi grazie alla chiamata allo sciopero generale indetto dall’Unione Sindacale di Base, si sono uniti i lavoratori e le lavoratrici che non hanno nessuna garanzia di vedere riconosciuto il proprio lavoro. Ma precarietà e sfruttamento non sono più un orizzonte accettato. Gli agricoltori e gli autotrasportatori che al Sud hanno bloccato le merci lo dicono da settimane, insieme a studenti, famiglie e a chiunque individua la causa di questa situazione alle scelte politiche dall’alto, sottomesse ai diktat europei e trumpiani: non c’è più disponibilità. 




Il governo Meloni deve fare i conti con il fatto che in piazza c’è il paese che porta avanti l’ingranaggio di questo sistema e che se decide di fermarsi non ci sarà alcuna prova di forza in grado di reggere il confronto. Le briciole di una finanziaria che tenta di mascherare in ogni modo che l’unico interesse governativo è trovare i soldi per il riarmo non hanno alcuna possibilità di convincere la popolazione. 




A Bologna, Pisa, Livorno, Roma, Torino, Treviso, Milano, Reggio Calabria, Palermo, Bari, Trieste, Pavia, Vicenza, Modena, Padova, Mestre, Cosenza, Napoli, Genova sono state bloccate le arterie principali delle città, gli snodi delle tangenziali e i porti. 




Livorno: la mattinata parte con il blocco del porto, prosegue poi con un corteo di oltre 20 mila persone e continua con il blocco della circolazione al varco Zara. 




Bologna: 50 mila persone nonostante i blocchi della polizia aprono un varco e arrivano a inondare l’autostrada. 




Modena: giovani e famiglie in corteo contro guerra e carovita.




Torino: un corteo diramato in tutta la città, dal centro alla tangenziale, raggiunge quota 100 mila persone, viene rilanciato l’appuntamento alle 18 per un altro corteo cittadino. 




Cosenza: corteo di massa di 7mila persone ha invaso le strade della città e bloccato autostrada e superstrada.




Pisa: un corteo di 20 mila persone si conclude con l’occupazione del Palazzo della Sapienza, nel pomeriggio appuntamento per una grande assemblea.




Brescia: 10 mila persone in corteo hanno tentato di raggiungere l’autostrada, cariche della polizia. 




Milano: 80 mila persone raggiungono la tangenziale. 




Pavia: grande manifestazione contro guerra e carovita. 




Qui le dirette di 

Radio Blackout

 e di 

Radio Onda d’Urto

 con i collegamenti dalle piazze in tutta Italia.

author: paradox-a
title: Die falsche Welt des Gute-Laune-Faschismus
content:
Zum Posterboy des Gute-Laune-Faschismus wurde Ulrich Siegmund gekürt, der AfD-Ministerpräsident in spe aus Sachsen-Anhalt. Die AfD fuhr hier mit 43,8% ihr bislang bestes Ergebnis ein. Je strukturschwächer, gottverlassener und migrationsärmer die Gegenden sind, desto stärker ist der Zuspruch zum nationalistischen Autoritarismus. So bereisen die ewig grinsenden Rattenfänger das Land und punkten unter Deutschen, die die Überwindung ihrer eigenen bürgerlichen Existenz herbeisehnen und hoffen dies auf dem Weg der Zerstörung der liberalen Demokratie zu erreichen.




Der Wohlfühl-Faschismus ist ein Phänomen, das vor zwanzigdreißig Jahren noch völlig unvorstellbar gewesen wäre. Und in zweidrei Jahrzehnten werden wir uns ebenfalls fragen, was in dieser Phase eigentlich passiert ist. Wer sie verstehen will, muss sich dazu nicht nur die Wahlkampf-Strategien der AfD anschauen, sondern auch kultur- und medienwissenschaftlich vorgehen. So ist es kein Zufall, das seit Anfang des Jahres 2026 massenhaft KI-generierte Songs bei Youtube erscheinen. Aufgrund ihrer hohen Klickzahlen landen diese wiederum durch die Algorithmen sehr schnell in der Vorschlagleiste.




Die extrem rechte Propaganda-Maschinerie bedient sich somit nahezu perfekt abgestimmt der Mittel, die der Plattform-Kapitalismus entwickelt hat. Und sie greift auf eine künstlich-sentimentale Popkultur zurück, die unterm Strich meistens schon sehr schlicht und beschränkt war. Ob volkstümelnd wie Heino, oder neu-deutsch-hart wie Rammstein, sülzig wie Julia Juls, Runa&Rebellin oder pop-rockig wie Weimar, Sleipnir und andere – Vorbilder für die extrem rechte Computermusik gibt es genug…




Sicher könnte man auch dagegen halten und sagen, dass die Generierung von Musik und Video-Material durch technische Sprechapparate von allen möglichen Leute mit kommerziellen Absichten, um Aufmerksamkeit zu erhalten oder einfach nur aus Langeweile generiert wird. Und das stimmt auch. Bedenkt man, wie durchproduziert und geglättet kommerziell erfolgreiche Musik heute ist, scheint der Schritt zur sogenannten KI klein zu sein. Dennoch gibt es eine spezielle Affinität von faschistischem Denken zur offensichtlich künstlichen Kultur, die den Anschein von menschlicher Kreativität verlässt und damit post-human ist. Laut Jason Stanley wird damit auf die Herstellung von „Unwirklichkeit“ abgezielt.




Um ein paar Beispiele von viralen KI-generierten Songs und „Künstler“ zu nennen, sind da beispielsweise:


– „Spätestens HIER wacht jeder auf! Der Sound des Wandels“ („Aufbruch Deutschland“, 501.537 Aufrufe)


– „Steh auf, wenn du Deutscher bist | Stolz auf Heimat und Kultur“ („Ottilie“, 339.081 Aufrufe)


– „Was ist aus unserem Land geworden? | Ein Lied über den Verlust der Heimat“ („Fenja“, 338.697 Aufrufe)


– „Dorfmarie – So war es, so soll es wieder sein“ („Dorfmarie“, 160.534 Aufrufe)


– „DIE WACHT AM RHEIN (LIVE) | Rock-Version eines historischen Gedichts“ („Julia im Exil“; 113.198 Aufrufe)


– „Kein schöner Land… WO DIE EICHEN STEH’N“ („Freya“; 18.974 Aufrufe)


– „Thüringen Ein Land Eine Geschichte Ein Herz“ („Der Heimatklang“, 4334 Aufrufe)


– „Heimweh nach Deutschland“ („Liv Eisen“, 2067 Aufrufe)




Die Titel verraten schon das Wesentliche. Wenn man die Textzeilen hört oder liest, wird deutlich, dass die immer gleichen Narrative, endlos wiederholt werden. Stets geht es um den Verlust einer imaginären „Heimat“ oder glorreichen „Nation“, um eine angebliche „Überfremdung“, anknüpfend an den Verschwörungsmythos eines „großen Austauschs“. Der Gute-Laune-Faschismus lebt in der ewigen Wiederholung von Mustern immer gleicher Opfer-Inszenierungen, dem Streicheln narzisstischer Kränkungen, sowie der Vorstellung einer zukünftigen Größe, die nur durch die Erniedrigung der ausgemachten Feinde erreicht werden kann. All dies sind Produkte einer staatlich-kapitalistischen Gesellschaftsform, die mit Patriarchat, Rassismus und Naturbeherrschung verknüpft ist. Zusammengefasst ist die Computer-produzierte Lyrik in ihrem billigen Abklatsch armselig – und faschistisch.


Dabei darf man nicht vergessen, dass auch der historische Nationalismus keine naturwüchsige Volksbewegung war, sondern ein Elitenprojekt, das eine Nation und eine darin angeblich ursprünglich vorhandene Kultur verordnete, anerzog und drillte.




Hört man die künstlich erzeugten Lieder und ihre Texte an, greifen Form und Inhalt ineinander. Bekanntlich ist den Fans derartiger wohlfühlfaschistischer Erzeugnisse vollkommen egal, ob sie ein KI-generiertes Lied hören. Ganz im Gegenteil müssen Kulturprodukte, die sie ansprechen kitschig, einfach und manipulativ sein, um auf Interesse zu stoßen. Wenn ein paar hunderttausend oder wenige Millionen Leute neofaschistische KI-Songs feiern, könnte man sagen: geschenkt, dieser faschistische oder mit dem Faschismus sympathisierende Teil der Bevölkerung ist verloren und nicht zu überzeugen. Als Nebenprodukt einer bestimmten Herrschaftsordnung erstarkt er in ihrer Krise, kann aber nur mit dieser überwunden werden. Und das ist richtig. Dennoch ist es gerade der melodiöse Gute-Laune-Faschismus, dem die Anschlussfähigkeit an immer weitere Bevölkerungsteile gelingt. Doch woran liegt das?




Was damit klanglich und sprachlich angesprochen wird, ist das Gefühl einer umfassenden und tiefgreifenden Entfremdung. Im Kunstprodukt, dass seine eigene Künstlichkeit ironisiert und dadurch jede potenziell authentische Erfahrung verunmöglicht, kommt ein faschistisches Begehren zum Ausdruck. Dieser Computer-Kitsch ist das ästhetische Pendant zur Untergrabung jeglichen Wahrheitsgehalts von Aussagen durch deren absolute Relativierung mittels „alternativen Fakten“, die sich in der Lyrik niederschlagen.


Wie bei den Grundregeln der Werbung gilt hier: Die Rezipient*innen müssen vom Gehörten und Gesehenen nicht überzeugt werden – es reicht, ihnen solange Lügen einzuhämmern, nein, einzusäuseln, bis sie kapitulieren und diese als mögliche Wahrheit akzeptieren.




So weitet sich die bürgerliche Toleranz auf fatale Weise aus und lässt vormals überzeugte Demokrat*innen zweifeln: „Die Faschisten glauben eben, das ihre schöne Heimat verloren gegangen ist. Nun ja, ich weiß nicht, aber wenn sie das so fühle? Aber sie sind stolze Kämpfer und lassen sich das nicht bieten. Nun ja, immerhin stehen sie für was! Sie holen ihr Land zurück und wollen eigentlich nur, das am Ende alle glücklich sind.“ Außer jene, die abgeschoben, inhaftiert oder ermordet wurden. Abgesehen von denen, deren Arbeitsbedingungen schlechter, deren Lebensbedingungen prekärer werden, während die öffentliche Infrastruktur weiter zerbröckelt und die Ökosysteme komplett zusammenbrechen.




Daher ist die Musik des Gute-Laune-Faschismus auch ein Vorschein der schönen neuen Autokratie, die damit errichtet werden soll. Es wird schon hör- und sichtbar, womit jene ruhiggestellt werden sollen, die dazu beitragen, ihre eigene Lebensgrundlage zu vernichten. Der Grund dafür liegt wiederum in der tiefgreifenden Entfremdung der Menschen – von ihren Produkten, von der Mitwelt, von ihren Mitmenschen und von sich selbst: Wer sich von seinen Tätigkeiten und Produkten entfremdet, mag zum Schluss kommen, das heimtückische „Globalisten“ die naturwüchsige Automobilproduktion nach China verlagern; Er mag von deutschen Wäldern schwärmen, aber den Rest davon durch den Klimawandel vertrocknen lassen; Er kann mit den Schultern zucken, wenn die nicht-weißen und/oder oppositionellen Nachbar*innen abgeholt werden und sich über seine Teilhabe an der Volksgemeinschaft freuen; und schließlich mag er sich den Rhythmen der nationalistischen Autokratie unterwerfen und gleichzeitig tief empfinden, das Demokratie eigentlich diktatorisch wäre…




Somit dockt der Wohlfühl-Faschismus an die Entfremdung an, die ein Produkt der industriell-modernen Herrschaftsordnung ist und verstärkt sie zugleich. Denn es wäre ja ohnehin alles egal, alles falsch, alles zerrüttet. Also kann man auch KI-generierten Glitzer-Schleim darüber gießen um von kräftiger Jugendlichkeit, wilder Männlichkeit, sanfter Weiblichkeit, ursprünglicher Natürlichkeit, rechtschaffener Arbeit, schicksalhafter Volksgemeinschaft, heroischem Kampf und glorreicher Nation zu träumen… Was soll man dazu sagen? Außer trotzig: Wer zuletzt lacht, werden wir noch sehen. Und: mehr als drei der faschistischen KI-Songs sollte man sich nicht anhören, wenn man halbwegs klar im Kopf bleiben möchte.

author: Agenda2029
title: Sabotage gegen Rheinmetall – Niemals Kriegstüchtig!
content:
In Kassel soll das größte Panzerwerk Europas gebaut werden. Wir stellen uns dagegen, zur Rüstungshauptstadt für die kommenden Kriege zu werden. Deshalb haben wir in der Nacht die Baustelle des Logistikzentrums von Rheinmetall in Kassel-Calden sabotiert und mehrere Bagger und Radlager angezündet.




Zeitenwende in Nordhessen




Wer in Nordhessen lebt, spürt was Zeitenwende heißt. Tag für Tag überschlagen sich die Nachrichten von Rüstungsinvestitionen. Fast kein Abend vergeht ohne Panzer in unseren Straßen zu sehen, die in die Kriegsgebiete der Welt exportiert werden. Kaum ein Kommunalpolitiker, mittelständisches Unternehmen oder Forschungsstandort der nicht hofft, etwas von den Milliarden der Zeitenwende abzubekommen.




Wir haben uns dafür entschieden, dabei nicht länger zuzuschauen und ein zentrales Projekt der Aufrüstungskampagne angegriffen: den Defence Hub Nordhessen von Rheinmetall.




Der Defence Hub Nordhessen umfasst den Ausbau des Panzerwerks in Kassel sowie den Bau eines Logistikzentrums auf 30.000 Quadratmetern und eines militärischen Drohnenzentrums am Kassel-Airport. Mit 260 Millionen Euro von Rheinmetall und über 20 Millionen Euro vom Land Hessen soll das Projekt bis Ende 2027 hochgezogen werden.




Für das Pressespektakel zum Auftakt verkündete Rheinmetall Chef Armin Papperger stolz: Kassel wird zukünftig das größte Panzerwerk Europas und „eine neue Drehscheibe“ der Rüstungsindustrie sein. Boris Rhein ergänzte: Der kriselnde Flughafen Kassel-Calden wird „künftig noch stärker als militärische Drehscheibe, für Trainingsflüge der Bundeswehr sowie zur Erforschung und Erprobung neuer Drohnen-Technologie“ dienen.




Während jeden Monat Millionen an Steuergeldern in einen leeren Flughafen versenkt werden, von dem nur die Privatjets von Superreichen starten, soll das Aufrüstungsprogramm nun die Rettung sein: Drohnen, Bundeswehrflüge und Logistik ersetzen die Passagiere und Urlaubsgäste, die partout nicht kommen wollen.




Mit Staatsgeldern in die Krise




Was in Kassel-Calden passiert, ist ein Sinnbild für die Zeitenwende in Deutschland: Der Staat tritt als Auftraggeber auf und versucht mit Milliarden an Rüstungsinvestitionen die schwächelnde Wirtschaft anzukurbeln. Deutschland tritt die Flucht nach vorne an. Wenn die Autoproduktion auf dem Weltmarkt nicht mehr konkurrenzfähig ist, dann immerhin der Leopard-Panzer und vielleicht auch bald wieder das deutsche Heer.




In einer Zeit, die weltweit von imperialistischen Konflikten und Kriegen geprägt ist, will die Bundesrepublik ihre Krise durch militärische Aufrüstung lösen und zukünftig ohne die USA an der Spitze Europas stehen können. Was uns als notwendige Investitionen in die Verteidigungsfähigkeit verkauft wird, ist die Option, die eigenen Interessen wie Zugang zu Ressourcen und Handelsrouten mit militärischen Mitteln außerhalb Deutschlands durchsetzen zu können. Der Bau von eigenen Langstreckenwaffen oder die Befugnisse der Geheimdienste zur Sabotage im Ausland sind offensive Fähigkeiten. Es ist die Möglichkeit, künftig weiter die Konfrontation mit dem russischen Regime um die Vormachtstellung in Osteuropa eingehen zu können.




Von der Drehscheibe …




Wir wissen aus allen Konflikten der Großmächte, dass am Ende die einfachen Menschen, die Frauen und die Jugendlichen am meisten unter den Folgen des Krieges leiden werden. Nicht Armin Papperger und Boris Rhein oder deren Kinder sollen im Schützengraben von der Drohne zerfetzt werden, sondern wir. Wenn wir den Kriegsvorbereitungen nicht international entgegen treten, haben wir bald keine Perspektive für unser Leben mehr.




Je mehr Geld in die Rüstungsprojekte fließt und je weiter der Umbau ziviler Wirtschaft zur Kriegsindustrie voranschreitet, desto größer wird auch hier die wechselseitige Abhängigkeit und die Verflechtung zwischen Rüstungskonzernen und den staatlichen Auftraggebern werden. Gleichzeitig gehen die Panzer, die am Ende von Rheinmetall und Co. durch Staatsgelder produziert werden, nicht wieder produktiv in den Wirtschaftskreislauf ein. Die Aufrüstung wird die Krise der letzten Jahre nicht lösen, sondern höchstens verschieben.




Wenn in ein paar Jahren die Hallen voll mit Panzern und Sprengköpfen sind, werden die Probleme der deutschen Schwerindustrie und der mittelständischen Zulieferer nicht gelöst sein. Für Kassel bedeutet das: Geht die staatliche Nachfrage nach Kriegswaffen in ein paar Jahren wieder zurück, wird auch die davon abhängige Industrie zusammenbrechen und zahlreiche Menschen ihre Arbeit verlieren. Wird das Kriegsgerät im Einsatz verbraucht, hält das zwar die Produktion am Laufen, macht Kassel aber auch in kommenden Kriegen erneut zur Zielscheibe. Während sich die Aktionäre und Vorstände von Rheinmetall, KNDS und Co. die Taschen voll machen, können wir bei dieser Kalkulation langfristig nur verlieren.




…zum Ort des Widerstands




Lasst uns Nordhessen von einer Drehscheibe der Aufrüstung zum Ort des Widerstand gegen den Kriegskurs der Eliten machen. Lasst uns gemeinsam dafür Kämpfen, dass Menschen nicht mehr vor der Entscheidung stehen, ihren Job zu verlieren oder zu Rheinmetall zu wechseln. Lasst uns dafür sorgen, dass Elbit Systems und Co. nicht in Ruhe produzieren können und aus Kassel nicht länger Krieg und Genozid in die Welt exportiert wird.




In Gedenken an den Kasseler Studierenden Yousef Shaban, der am 24. Oktober 2023 mit seinen Familienangehörigen durch die IDF in Gaza ermordet wurde.




In Verbundenheit mit den russischen Kriegsgegner:innen und Saboteuren, die heute entweder im Straflager sitzen oder vom Regime getötet wurden.

Ob an der Universität, an die die Kassler Rüstungskonzerne drängen. Ob an den Schulen, wo gegen die Wehrpflicht gestreikt wird. author: Aldrey Olegario
title: ‘Primavera Brasileira’: como ato de estudantes virou onda global contra extrema direita
content:
Na noite de 4 de outubro, quando Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) terminou à frente de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no 1.º turno das eleições, a seguinte mensagem chegou num grupo de WhatsApp de alunos da Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF): “O momento pede ação”. Na noite seguinte, 5 de outubro, o Brasil assistiu ao primeiro ato dos jovens.




“Nós vimos a vitória do Flávio de uma forma muito acachapante. Ninguém estava esperando. Aquilo gerou um sentimento de descrença muito forte no campo progressista. Mas na Faculdade de Direito da UFF, pela nossa história, enxergamos de forma contrária: com esperança e com vontade de ir à luta”, diz Kayky Moraes, aluno do curso de direito da UFF que participou do primeiro levante.




Realizada em Niterói, na região metropolitana do Rio de Janeiro, a marcha dos estudantes saiu do prédio da Faculdade de Direito rumo à reitoria da universidade. 

As imagens tomaram as redes e iniciaram um efeito dominó que impulsionou mobilizações estudantis nos cinco cantos do país. “Ali a gente sentiu que dava para brigar.”







Neste momento manifestação contra Bolsonaro pelos estudantes nas ruas Niterói 

pic.twitter.com/7sqGGEq7TV

— Fã do Rei Pelé e da Rainha Marta 

 

 

 (@silvaS1963) 

October 5, 2026







O resultado desse “efeito borboleta” veio no dia 25 de outubro, três semanas depois. Um feito histórico: Lula virou o jogo e 

venceu as eleições

 por uma vantagem de 4,4 milhões de votos, algo que nenhum candidato a presidente que terminou como segundo colocado no 1º turno havia conseguido fazer antes. Os eleitores de Lula e os estrategistas de campanha do PT tiveram apenas três semanas para mudar a rota. “Essa foi a campanha menos organizada que participei desde 1989”, chegou a dizer o presidente Lula em uma reunião com parlamentares em Brasília.




“Os jovens tomaram as ruas de forma orgânica e organizada para defender um projeto de país, mas também um projeto de ser humano. Quando Lula disse aquela frase para a gente ser ele amanhã, porque ele já foi a gente ontem e para a juventude botar a cara a tapa, acho que é isso mesmo”, diz Kayky, em referência a um trecho da entrevista de Lula para o podcast Flow. 

“Estamos fadados a viver o futuro e a gente tem que construir o futuro que a gente quer.”




A “primavera brasileira”, como começou a ser apelidada a vitória eleitoral frente à extrema direita, também pode ser vista por como uma posição do Brasil 

como símbolo de resistência aos interesses dos Estados Unidos, defende Mayra Goulart, doutora em ciência política pela UERJ.




“O Brasil será um pólo da resistência à relação imperial que os Estados Unidos tentam restabelecer. Na última assembleia geral da ONU, Lula disse que o Brasil não iria ser o quintal de ninguém. O presidente Lula recupera a tradição de não alinhamento automático da diplomacia brasileira a potências estrangeiras e a adoção de um caminho próprio e soberanista. Isso é entendido muitas vezes como um caminho que vem a liderar outros países periféricos”, diz.




A “Primavera Brasileira” vista do exterior




No México e na Espanha, a virada eleitoral brasileira foi recebida não apenas com alívio geopolítico, mas como um estudo de caso sobre como conter a ascensão da extrema direita.




Para Homero Campa Butrón, cientista político e professor da Universidade Nacional Autônoma do México (UNAM), a manutenção do governo progressista no Brasil evita o isolamento regional no continente. “Brasil e México representam 55% da população da América Latina e 60% da economia da região. O resultado no Brasil foi vital para o governo mexicano, pois evita o isolamento diante da onda de vitórias da direita na região nos últimos meses”, analisa Campa, destacando que a comunicação entre a presidenta mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum e Lula é direta e estratégica.




O impacto também ressoa na Europa. “Se o Brasil conseguiu, a Espanha também consegue”, disse o primeiro-ministro da Espanha Pedro Sánchez

, em um comício em Gijón, na região de Astúrias, realizado na segunda-feira, 26 de outubro. “Vamos fazer o mesmo que Lula fez no Brasil. O mundo está olhando para nós”, completou.




Com eleições gerais agendadas para o próximo mês na Espanha, onde as pesquisas têm indicado a predileção do eleitorado à direita, o desfecho brasileiro renovou o ânimo das forças de esquerda. “Certamente, no México e na Espanha, percebe-se um enorme interesse no modelo de mobilização social promovido por meio das redes sociais, coordenado pelo deputado André Janones. Entende-se que a estratégia de comunicação digital foi um fator fundamental no resultado”, diz o professor da UNAM.




A 

Agência Pública

 identificou que ao menos três grupos de WhatsApp internacionais reproduzem as táticas de engajamento de Janones para mobilizar apoiadores.

 É do caso do “Frenteamplistas” (37 mil seguidores), da Espanha, “L’équipe de Mélenchon” (152 mil seguidores), da França, e do “Ejército del Peronismo” (61 mil seguidores), da Argentina.
















Canais de Whatsapp internacionais reproduzem estratégia digital de André Janones




“A mobilização nas redes sociais é uma tendência global. O Brasil adere a isso de uma maneira muito acelerada e acredito que essa tendência seja muito similar em outros países. Ao mesmo tempo, isso não desconsidera a importância dos atores tradicionais, como o movimento estudantil e sindicatos, que foram acionados a partir das redes, mas permitiram um engajamento muito grande no mundo real. Se é que podemos dizer em uma fórmula, ela deve ser buscada na sinergia entre o mundo físico e as redes sociais”, pontua Goulart.




Ainda nesta semana, viralizou um vídeo compartilhado por Ada Colau, ex-prefeita de Barcelona e candidata à presidência da Espanha pela Frente Ampla, no qual ela pede para que os apoiadores ergam as mãos em “L”

 — um aceno ao presidente brasileiro. “Vamos todos levantar o braço com o ‘L’ de Lula”, disse ela, durante ato no município de Móstoles na quarta-feira (28).




“Eu me lembro desse momento. O gesto de Acolau foi bastante simbólico e foi num dia próximo ao da notícia da vitória de Lula. Acho que foi uma surpresa para todo mundo. Acho que a maioria das pessoas dava como certo que a probabilidade do filho do [Jair] Bolsonaro ganhar era muito alta. O gesto reafirma a vitória de Lula e diz que nós, por aqui, também temos plena capacidade de fazer o mesmo”, conta Euge, 22, morador da cidade de Madrid que esteve no comício organizado pela Frente Ampla.




“Acredito que Lula tem sido um vislumbre de esperança para as pessoas de esquerda e para os trabalhadores da Espanha e do mundo todo. Estamos vivendo um momento em que temos governos de extrema direita como nunca antes. Lula conseguiu vencer com a maioria das pesquisas dizendo o contrário. A mensagem que chegou aqui na Espanha foi de que, ainda que pareça que tudo está contra, é possível vencer. Se conseguirmos mobilizar todas as pessoas progressistas, nós venceremos”, continua ele.




Também fizeram o “L” de Lula, a presidente do México, Claudia Sheinbaum, o senador do México Gerardo Fernández e parlamentares do Congresso Nacional do Chile.

 Já utilizado como chacota, especialmente entre bolsonaristas, o “L” agora ganha espaço no cenário político mundial como símbolo da mobilização contra o avanço da direita.







 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

View this post on Instagram

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 







“O Brasil desponta como liderança da resistência à extrema direita em termos globais. A extrema direita é globalizada, sistêmica e se reúne em fóruns, como a CPAC [Conservative Political Action Conference]. A esquerda começa a se articular e essa articulação pode ter como centro a liderança do presidente Lula”, diz Goulart.




Nascido na cidade de Getafe, ao sul da região de Madri, Euge se interessou por política ainda na adolescência. Em 2019, aos 15 anos, decidiu participar do Más Madrid, um partido de esquerda com atuação a nível municipal em Madri. Para Euge, a participação de jovens na política é importante, mas não se distingue do papel das outras faixas etárias. “Sempre falam aos jovens: ‘vocês são o futuro!’ Bom, não é que a gente seja o futuro, somos o presente de um país. Temos que estar em igualdade tanto de reconhecimento quanto de possibilidade de participar da vida pública e da vida política. As decisões que os governos tomam nos afetam da mesma forma, e muitas delas ainda mais do que ao resto das pessoas.”




Sobre o recado que deseja que as próximas eleições da Espanha passem ao mundo, Euge diz esperar que seja o mesmo que o do Brasil: “Uma mensagem de que não baixamos os braços, que demos de tudo e conseguimos mobilizar a população com temas essenciais para sua vida, como moradia, pensão e serviços públicos.”




A mobilização da juventude




Além do protesto organizado pelos estudantes da UFF logo após o resultado do primeiro turno, outra engrenagem importante passou a se movimentar: os fandoms (comunidade de fãs) brasileiros.

 Longe de se restringirem ao entretenimento, esses grupos já vinham consolidando uma ponte direta com a política institucional.




No final de agosto deste ano, o 

Palácio do Planalto

 recebeu representantes desses grupos em uma cerimônia oficial, na qual o presidente Lula assinou um decreto com novas regras para a venda de ingressos de shows e eventos culturais no país. A medida, voltada ao combate do cambismo digital e à falta de transparência nas plataformas, foi fruto das demandas levadas pelos próprios fãs ao governo federal.




E esse pode ter sido um grande 

efeito borboleta

 da campanha: a mesma capacidade de mobilização que esses jovens utilizam para apoiar seus ídolos foi redirecionada no momento mais decisivo da disputa eleitoral, sendo uma das principais apostas da chapa Lula-Alckmin para furar bolhas e alcançar a virada. Para o leitor que ainda busca entender como esse movimento funciona, os fandoms são comunidades hiperconectadas e altamente disciplinadas, capazes de organizar mutirões de votação e subir hashtags mundiais.




Assim, as páginas passaram a publicar conteúdos de conscientização política, convocando mutirões de engajamento, dialogando com seguidores indecisos e pedindo o posicionamento de artistas sobre a defesa da democracia no Brasil.


















































































A relevância do movimento foi tamanha que o candidato à reeleição abriu sua fala reconhecendo a força dessa articulação num dos discursos proferidos na Avenida Paulista após o 1º turno.







“Eu não sei se eu começo a minha fala dizendo ‘companheiros e companheiras’ ou se eu começo dizendo: fandoms do Brasil, obrigado pela iniciativa de vocês!”

O presidente Lula agradecendo à juventude organizada em fandoms por puxar o ato de hoje na Paulista 

#FandomsComLula

 

pic.twitter.com/dWPL8ISHS6

— ERIKA HILTON (@ErikakHilton) 

October 11, 2026







Janonismo cultural e a urgência de regulamentação das Big Techs




Ao longo desta primeira semana pós 2º turno, o livro 

Janonismo Cultural: O uso das redes sociais e a batalha pela democracia no Brasil

, de André Janones, figurou entre os 10 títulos mais vendidos da Amazon no nicho de Política e Ciências Sociais.

 Exitoso ao encabeçar a estratégia digital de Lula, Janones foi destacado no primeiro discurso do presidente reeleito.




Apesar do otimismo com a capacidade da sociedade brasileira de reverter os algoritmos, Campa faz um alerta sobre a vulnerabilidade desse modelo: “a falta de regulamentação das grandes empresas de tecnologia constitui um perigo para a vida pública no mundo inteiro. O que ocorreu no Brasil foi muito positivo: uma reação social massiva e bem organizada para reverter o algoritmo. No entanto, receio que essas empresas estejam tomando nota do que aconteceu no Brasil para introduzir controles maiores e evitar que se repita”, pontua Homero.




A 

Pública

 mostrou em 

reportagens

 como a moderação da Meta atingiu de forma desproporcional as candidaturas, beneficiando em vários casos a de Flávio em detrimento da de Lula.




Nesse cenário, a regulamentação das plataformas surge como uma demanda democrática, observa Goulart. “No discurso de vitória, Lula disse que um dos objetivos do governo seria regulamentar as plataformas para que elas aumentem a isonomia das entregas entre diferentes grupos. É importantíssimo que isso seja feito. Caso contrário, a valorização desproporcional dos conteúdos da extrema direita quando comparados com outros conteúdos irá continuar, principalmente com o sistema de recomendação e hierarquização do feed.”




Para o analista mexicano, a esquerda global precisará acelerar sua adaptação aos novos modelos de comunicação, ao mesmo tempo em que pressiona por regras claras contra a interferência de grandes corporações de tecnologia nas democracias. “A mensagem que fica do Brasil é de otimismo e confiança na sociedade diante dos grandes grupos tecnológicos e da ultradireita. O Brasil demonstrou uma liderança inegável para todo o Sul Global” conclui.




Na visão de Kayky, da UFF, a mobilização não se encerra com o resultado das urnas. “Acho que daqui nasce a esperança de um futuro melhor. O recado de um levante que começou aqui em Niterói está se espalhando pelo mundo. Dá para ver o jardim da primavera florescendo pelo mundo todo. Mas é sempre importante manter a vigilância e continuar nas ruas para defender essa visão de mundo.”

content:

Sus reclamos sobre el incremento de haberes, la entrega de medicamentos y el financiamiento del PAMI son urgentes, pero desoídos por la gestión. Sin recibir respuesta, mantienen su ronda por la Plaza del Congreso, a la que se suman manifestantes de distintas organizaciones.

author: David Swanson
title: The 10 Worst Congressional Excuses for Voting for More Military Spending
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 30, 2026




Every year for many years now, the bitterly divided, grid-locked, virtually civil-war-waging United States Congress (as it’s commonly depicted) has harmoniously voted for vastly more money in war spending than it had done the year before. Our lords and misrepresentatives are 

threatening

 the same again right now.




It’s a heartwarming story of cooperation and understanding, no doubt, but how can you, as an elected official, explain to constituents living third-world lives in a wealthy nation that, not only can you not tax the rich or the corporations, but you also cannot afford to fund education, energy, environment, transportation, retirement, healthcare, or housing because the weapons dealers just want more and more?




The trick, of course, in most cases is to keep your head down and your mouth shut until a bigger military spending bill than last year’s is guaranteed to pass no matter how you vote, and then vote No. You’ll be untouchable. It’s golden. You won’t have publicly organized your colleagues or used various available procedures to actually try to reduce the war spending, but you’ll have an “I voted No” shield, and that’s all you’ll need. Constituents will fall for it without fooling any weapons dealers.




But what if it’s your turn? What if you’ve drawn the short string this year? What if you can either vote Yes or anger your party’s “leader”?




Never fear! That’s what this handy guide is for! Here are 10 popular categories of excuses that have proven effective through the past quarter-century.







You can easily depict an increase to military spending as a decrease if it’s a smaller increase than someone — ideally the president — had initially proposed. This one is in the works right now and may prove very successful. A variation on this is to claim that the bad political party (the one you’re not in) would have gotten a larger increase if you hadn’t hurried or stalled, depending on which party is gaining or losing a majority.




Almost foolproof is the oft-used explanation that you focused your efforts on doing exactly what the peace activists wanted by removing some nasty section from the bill. “You didn’t want the U.S. and Israeli militaries to merge. You said to only vote for the bill if that was removed. We got it removed on condition that we vote for the bill. This is how things work in the real world.” This excuse gets a 5 out of 5 on Yelp. Anyone who objects is a silly dreamer, so you need not address their concerns.




Almost matching the batting record of #2 (removing something) is adding something. It hardly matters how absurd the thing or how out of place in an institution of mass-murder and destruction, as long as it’s humanitarian. Create an agency of environmentally sustainable carpet bombing, or eliminate discrimination against transgendered pilots, or establish a proactive contracting program to minority-owned surveillance companies. Whatever. Anyone who objects will be objecting to that thing you voted for. You should be clear that it is only that thing for which you voted; nothing else exists.




If you cannot use the top three steaming turds of the coming apocalypse, or don’t have time to come up with anything concrete, just fall back on troopism. You voted to fund the troops. Anyone objecting hates the troops, wants the troops left in the wars but their armor and weaponry carefully collected and brought home without them. If you can, grab an actual troop or three to stand in front of and ask one of them to slap you in the face really quickly until there are tears visible in your eyes before the cameras are ready.




Numerous other excuses can work beautifully, depending on the circumstances. There’s always a most-unpopular war among the current wars. Right now, for example, some people are more upset about the crumbs going to the war on Iran than about the mountain of loafs going to the Pentagon in its entirety. So, here’s what you do. You make getting a war powers resolution on Iran vetoed part of a grand bargain in which you vote for the money to create 10 more similar wars. Or you join in a lawsuit against the war on Iran. Or you actually include in the spending bill or elsewhere a ban on spending money on that particular crime — but make clear to everyone that it’s part of a grand bargain on a 4-D chessboard. You voted for increased war money FOR PEACE and so that you could end 

THE

 war!




While changing the topic is a losing argument when done too blatantly, it can be very, very effective when done through omission and media saturation. If you can make something else the big story and do something peace-ish on that big thing, you can get huge mileage out of it. For example, you vote for more war money but you also VOTE TO IMPEACH HEGSETH. That doesn’t remove Hegseth, much less the guy whose every whim he obeys, but it’s AWESOME!




Pretty darn powerful, as well, is the futile legislation ploy (FLP). You may vote to increase military spending by 20 percent, but if you are a cosponsor and champion of separate legislation that would reduce military spending by 10 percent, your peace-loving constituents will understand that you are with them.




You don’t actually need me to tell you this. You know it’s there when the time is right. Anyone who objects to your war votes is anti-Semitic. QED.




Sure, you may have voted for increased spending on wars, but you’re in a super-purple district. If you were to give the forces of darkness the chance to label you “weak on defense” then your constituents would end up with a racist, sexist pig voting for increased mass-murder funding in place of you doing it. Which would they rather have?




Putin.
