title: Суд в Финляндии утвердил отказ Миграционной службы предоставить убежище 44-летнему анархисту из Петербурга Михаилу Луньковскому
content:
Об этом написала «Медиазона». Фотографию Луньковского также публикует издание.

Его постановили депортировать в Россию.

Луньковский рассказал «Медиазоне», что в самом начале войны он отправлял деньги в украинские фонды вроде «Повернись живим» с российских карт. Он открыто выступал против вторжения и оставлял антивоенные комментарии в различных чатах в телеграме.

С 2017-2018 годов, по словам Луньковского, и по настоящее время он занимается модерацией в чате преследуемого в РФ и жёстко критикующего Путина публициста Аркадия Бабченко. В последние годы несколько человек получили большие сроки за донаты Бабченко.

По версии финского суда, «деятельность заявителя в социальных сетях носила весьма незначительный характер». Суд не нашел подтверждений, что «заявитель представляет особый интерес для российских властей».

По данным Автономного Действия, Луньковский был активен в питерских либертарных инициативах в 2000-х годов. Решение суда в Финляндии попытаются оспорить.

author: Anele Mbi
title: Buffalo City’s broken houses and decades of empty promises
content:
A housing rectification project in Braelyn Extension 10 in Buffalo City Municipality (BCM) has left residents frustrated with the municipality’s failure to address severe structural faults.




Serious defects in the RD houses include cracked walls and roofs, leaking roofs, and inadequate foundations. Braelyn residents say they have repeatedly complained to the municipality, which has promised to rebuild the houses since 2004, but has taken no action until today, except for a laydown yard constructed by the sitting, ANC ward councillor, Mendi Wetsetse.




The stalled housing project intersects with service-delivery defects across the ward, including unpaved and potholed roads, poor refuse collection, and electricity shortages brought about by the growing Inkandla informal settlement.




Recently, President Cyril Ramaphosa authorised the Special Investigating Unit (SIU) to probe allegations of extensive corruption and maladministration of major BCM tenders.




According to Braelyn residents, talks about rectifying Braelyn Ext 10 RDP houses began before 2010. The then ward councillor, Thabo Myira, who served as a councillor between 2005 and 2010, confirmed the claim.




Media reports also indicate that in 2009, the then minister of human settlements, Tokyo Sexwale promised people living in faulty RDP houses in East London that their houses would be rebuilt. Today, councillor Wetsetse, who is campaigning for a third term in the upcoming local government election, promised to rectify the situation.




Housing defects




Ntombizanele Mabala, an 80-year-old pensioner, said since residents arrived in Braelyn in 1997, they have complained to councillors and the municipality about the poor condition of their houses, but their pleas were ignored. “These are not houses but hokkies. We have children and a family of six. Rain comes in from every direction – through the roof, the walls and underneath – because these houses have no foundations,” she said. “The councillor promised that the housing rectification process would begin before 4 November, but there are still no signs of work apart from a laydown-yard fence erected two years ago.”




Another pensioner, Nothembile Mqhayi, whose house was built below ground level, said her house floods when it rains. She showed 

Elitsha

 a hole she had made at the bottom of a wall to let water that entered the house drain out.




The Mqhayi family had to make a hole in the wall to drain out water when the house floods.




Ziyanda Mpakantsho (42), who recently joined an EPWP project and earns R3,000 a month, said rectification is urgently needed because she lives with a sick and disabled person. “I grew up hearing that the cracks in the walls would be repaired, but many years have passed. These Braelyn houses have no proper foundations, so water leaks in when it rains. The houses have not been rectified because the money is being squandered,” she said.




Zama Thutha (70) said the government had not fixed the RDP houses because it was corrupt and unaccountable to voters. “Even the EPWP jobs created recently will end after the elections. Our system of government is capitalism, which puts profit before the needs of ordinary people,” he said.




Recurring delays and more promises




Responses from both the BCM and the Eastern Cape department of human settlements (DHS) are not only conflicting but also suggest the rectification process remains a false hope for Braelyn residents. When asked whether the municipality or its ward councillor has made any promises of rectification, the municipality said the provincial government is responsible for the rectification process.




“The Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality wishes to clarify that it does not currently run a municipal housing rectification programme; this falls outside local government funding allocations. What we can say is that the laydown yard established on-site remains a site-securing measure for future development once capital is allocated.”




The laydown yard is overgrown

.




The provincial DHS said that, despite the constitutional principle of cooperative governance that compels the various spheres of government to share information and support each other, implementation requires compliance with the necessary technical, administrative, planning, and budgetary processes. The department has not denied the fact that rectification has been recognised for several years.




“The programme, which focuses on the rectification of existing two-room RDP houses, was prioritised following engagements involving the current ward councillor and the executive mayor of BCMM,” said Yanga Funani, the DHS spokesperson.




“In the current financial year, Braelyn, Ducats and Dimbaza have been identified among the priority areas for rectification,” said Funani. “The project is currently at an advanced preparatory stage, with implementation targeted to commence in November 2026, subject to the completion of outstanding administrative and implementation requirements,” he added.

title: Pisa: IL 30 OTTOBRE SCIOPERO GENERALE – Insieme possiamo bloccare tutto
content:
Lo sciopero generale del 30 ottobre, proclamato da USB e sostenuto da tanti sindacati di base, è l’occasione per reagire a una crisi che pesa ogni giorno sulle nostre vite.

 




Di seguito ripubblichiamo l’indizione di 

MULTI – Sindacato Sociale

 che aderisce allo sciopero e sarà

 

nei luoghi di lavoro, di studio e nei quartieri per costruire questa

 

giornata.

 In allegato l’adesione allo sciopero da parte dei lavoratori di Amazon. 




Non possiamo andare avanti così: lavorare costa sempre di più, gli stipendi non bastano e gli affitti sono impossibili. Imprese e istituzioni scaricano i costi della crisi su chi lavora, attraverso part-time involontari, ore non pagate e contratti precari. Gli ospedali non garantiscono cure adeguate, scuole e servizi si impoveriscono, mentre aumentano le risorse destinate al riarmo.




Scioperare è un sacrificio, soprattutto per chi ha già pochi soldi. Ma dobbiamo

 

ribellarci a una normalità che ci impoverisce e ci toglie autonomia e

 

futuro. Fermarci insieme significa trasformare la fatica e la rabbia individuali in

 una forza capace di cambiare i rapporti di potere.




In tutta Europa crescono le proteste. Autotrasportatori e agricoltori si mobilitano contro l’aumento dei costi e l’indebitamento; giovani delle periferie e studenti occupano scuole e piazze, stanchi di essere criminalizzati e privati di 

opportunità. Conflitti diversi, una domanda comune: perché dobbiamo

 

essere sempre noi a pagare?




Dalla Palestina all’Ucraina, le guerre devastano popolazioni e territori mentre si spendono soldi pubblici per produrre e acquistare armi. Banche, industrie militari, imprese energetiche, grandi supermercati, case farmaceutiche, multinazionali della logistica e fondi immobiliari continuano ad accumulare 

profitti. Noi, invece, veniamo derubati della ricchezza che produciamo:

 

con salari insufficienti, affitti insostenibili, prezzi sempre più alti e

 

servizi pubblici impoveriti. Il nostro lavoro fa ricco lo Stato e le grandi

 

aziende, ma a noi restano sacrifici e rinunce. Ora basta.




Da Amazon a Carrefour, da Dussmann agli appalti pubblici, fino alla Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna, alla Scuola Normale e alle scuole, dobbiamo far sentire la voce di chi manda avanti la società con il proprio lavoro e la propria cura. Vogliamo salari più alti, contratti stabili, la fine del lavoro gratuito e del part-

time imposto, case accessibili e servizi pubblici funzionanti. Le risorse

 

collettive devono servire la vita, non la guerra e i profitti di pochi.




Per questo dobbiamo portare lo sciopero ovunque, collegare le vertenze e fermare i flussi di lavoro e di ricchezza che noi stessi produciamo. Non basta indignarsi: 

dobbiamo organizzarci e ribellarci insieme per conquistare

 

ciò che ci viene negato.




Il 30 ottobre, dalla mattina presto, saremo con 

picchetti nei luoghi di

 

lavoro, di studio e nei quartieri per promuovere lo sciopero

. Dalle ore 9 ci muoveremo in corteo verso il Comune di Pisa.




Per aderire, segnalare la partecipazione o costruire iniziative, contattate MULTI – Sindacato Sociale:

info@multisindacatosociale.org

title: Senator Briefed on Trump’s Iran War Plans Warns of “Devastating Escalation”
content:
Sen. Chris Murphy said the plans would lead to the “destruction of our commitment to the rule of law” if carried out.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

A senator who was briefed on President Donald Trump’s plans to launch intense strikes on Iran after the midterm elections has warned that the attacks are slated to be so horrific that they will lead to the “destruction” of the U.S.’s “commitment to the rule of law.”

At an event hosted by the Middle East Institute on Wednesday, Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Connecticut), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said that he was recently in a “fairly detailed” briefing with Pentagon officials about the war plan.

“I will just say this: Their plan … will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law,” Murphy said.

“The plan that they have developed will lead, in my view, to a prolonged escalation of this war that will be devastating for our security interests,” he went on, adding that it would also put the lives of U.S. soldiers at risk when Iran retaliates.

Murphy said that he couldn’t share details of the plan, but, when asked to elaborate, he pointed to recent reporting on the campaigns that the Pentagon has drawn up on behalf of President Donald Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.

On Tuesday, The Wall Street Journal reported that the U.S. has informed Gulf countries that it is prepared for a “short, intense military campaign” after the election next week. The Pentagon has created plans to strike a wide variety of targets, reports have said, including Iran’s nuclear energy facilities.

Trump has reportedly explicitly ordered the military to target a large amount of energy infrastructure — largely considered to be civilian in nature. One plan prepared by the military, CNN reported, is for the U.S. to drop the “Mother of All Bombs,” the largest conventional weapon by weight in existence, a 21,000-pound bomb with the ability to destroy everything within its massive blast radius.

The plans, if carried out, may “use tactics that are even more provocative and dangerous, and potentially violative of international law,” Murphy said — worsening tactics that the senator acknowledged have already violated the international war guardrails.

“Every first year law student could tell you that this war is illegal” in the domestic sense, Murphy said. “But it is also clearly in contravention of international law and commitments that we have made to the rule of law to deliberately target civilians and to use the harm or potential harm of civilians as leverage in war.”

Murphy’s comments suggest that Trump is slated to go even further in the illegal war that has already had devastating consequences for Iran’s civilians and economy.

According to an analysis by the National Iranian American Council, U.S.-Israeli strikes have already destroyed or damaged nearly 1,300 schools, 80 energy facilities, and scores of transportation facilities and sites like airports and bridges. The harsh sanctions regime has also ravaged the economy, with over 1 million jobs lost and massive inflation for basic goods like food, even as the value of the rial hits record lows.

The opening strikes of this war also involved the U.S. bombing an elementary school in Minab, Iran, killing over 160 people, including 123 children under 13 years old.

Trump and his cabinet have repeatedly stoked concerns that they may commit even more heinous war crimes against civilians with the president’s repeated genocidal threats to “annihilate” Iran. In his speech to the UN general assembly last month, Trump mused about whether he should “drive [Iran] into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations.”

Adding to concerns of the administration’s wanton disregard for military procedures and briefings to Congress is the Pentagon’s secrecy regarding its ever-shifting operations.

Murphy noted that, on top of never having sought congressional approval for the war, Pentagon officials have been guarded in private briefings about the war. He said that he gets the sense that, internally, Pentagon officials believe more strikes won’t be effective in achieving the U.S.’s goals — as previous reports have said — but that they have become more reluctant to voice their disagreements with the military’s top brass under Hegseth when speaking with Congress.

Indeed, on Wednesday, Hegseth fired the military’s top planner just days before strikes could potentially restart. The Pentagon said Hegseth fired Brett Sylvia, the head of strategy, plans, and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff, accusing him of leaking information about Iran and Russia to journalists without providing evidence.

This is the latest high-level firing by Hegseth, who has also ousted several generals because of reported personal disagreements over how the military should be run.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

Truthout produces reporting you won’t see in the mainstream: journalism from the frontlines of global conflict, interviews with grassroots movement leaders, high-quality legal analysis and more.

title: Torino verso lo sciopero generale
content:
Riprendiamo indizione della mobilitazione da parte dei coordinamenti cittadini di 

Torino per Gaza

 e 

Torino contro il riarmo

 in vista della mobilitazione dello sciopero del 30 ottobre. In allegato anche un registrato delle voci del 24 ottobre a cura di 

Radio Blackout

.




BLOCCHIAMO L’ITALIA SCIOPERO GENERALE

Domani scendiamo in piazza ancora una volta per ribadire che siamo contro il riarmo, contro il carovita e contro ogni forma di guerra.

Sono settimane che vediamo l’Italia intera scendere in piazza per dire che non ce la fa più, che arrivare alla fine del mese è diventato un lusso sempre più riservato a pochi, che non è più possibile accettare un presente fatto di precarietà e impoverimento. Di fronte a tutto questo, le risposte del governo italiano sono sempre più orientate alla repressione. Attraverso abusi di polizia e limitazioni al diritto di manifestare, si tenta di restringere sempre di più gli spazi del dissenso, obbligando le persone a lasciare il centro delle città e relegando le proteste nelle periferie, lontano dagli occhi di chi governa e di chi vorrebbe continuare a fare finta di niente. Ci chiediamo allora: queste fantomatiche vetrine valgono forse più della vita di milioni di persone che non riescono ad arrivare alla fine del mese? Vale più la tutela delle vetrine del diritto di esprimere il proprio dissenso, di protestare contro le guerre e di rivendicare condizioni di vita dignitose?

Ancora una volta, la domanda non dovrebbe essere perché le persone scendano in piazza, perché giovani e studenti si mobilitino collettivamente, perché un’intera generazione rifiuti di accettare le condizioni che le vengono imposte. La vera domanda è perché, di fronte a queste rivendicazioni, la risposta delle istituzioni continui a tradursi nella violenza e nella repressione.

Scendere in piazza è quindi sempre di più una necessità, un dovere collettivo. Perché non possiamo accettare che la guerra diventi normalità mentre le nostre condizioni di vita peggiorano, che miliardi vengano destinati al riarmo mentre milioni di persone sono costrette a scegliere tra pagare le bollette, fare la spesa e arrivare alla fine del mese. Vediamo un vento di rivolta e rivoluzione arrivare dal mondo intero, da paesi molto vicini al nostro; Francia, Spagna, Albania, paesi nei quali le settimane di mobilitazione hanno messo in crisi i propri governi. Un solo grido ci attraversa tutti: No alla guerra e sì per una vita dignitosa.

Come Coordinamento Torino per Gaza, sappiamo bene, guardando alla resistenza palestinese, cosa significhi lottare, cosa significhi resistere e cosa significhi non arrendersi di fronte alla violenza. Sappiamo che le lotte non sono separate, che ciò che accade in Palestina non è distante da ciò che viviamo qui. La guerra e il genocidio in Palestina si inseriscono in un sistema di dominio e di violenza che si alimenta anche attraverso il riarmo, l’economia di guerra e politiche che scaricano il costo delle proprie scelte sulle vite di chi lavora, studia e vive in condizioni di crescente precarietà.

Con la stessa forza e determinazione che abbiamo mostrato lo scorso anno con Blocchiamo tutto, vogliamo tornare a bloccare. Bloccare questo sistema, fermare la macchina della guerra, opporci a un modello politico ed economico che ci vuole sempre più sfruttati, sempre più impoveriti, sempre più disposti a chinare la testa.

Vogliamo bloccare l’Italia per l’Italia stessa, per la nostra liberazione, per costruire un futuro in cui le risorse siano destinate alla vita e non alla guerra, ai diritti e non al riarmo, alla dignità delle persone e non ai profitti di pochi.

Domani scendiamo in piazza per scioperare, per bloccare, per opporci alla repressione e per mettere un punto a tutto questo.

Contro il riarmo. Contro il carovita. Contro ogni guerra. Per la Palestina, per la nostra liberazione.




Alcune voci dal corteo del 24 ottobre a Torino contro guerra, riarmo e carovita.

author: By Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: Minneapolis March Against Police Brutality Connects Local, State and Federal Violence
content:
Minneapolis, MN — For the 31st annual National Day of Protest Against Police Brutality on Oct. 22, activists drew the connection to the violence perpetrated by local, state, and federal law enforcement as they marched from the memorial site of 

Alex Pretti

 to 

Renée Good

‘s memorial and ended at 

George Floyd Square

. 




Organizing the march for the twenty-sixth straight year was 

Communities United Against Police Brutality

 (

CUAPB

). “We want to draw the lines, make the connections, help people understand that it does not matter whether that brutality is by a local law enforcement, a county law enforcement, a state police, or the federal law enforcement. It doesn’t matter when somebody loses their lives to police brutality, misconduct, and abuse of authority. We will always be out here demanding justice. That will never change,” said Michelle Gross, the president of CUAPB.
















Before the march started from Alex Pretti’s memorial at 26th St. and Nicollet Ave., 

Brass Solidarity band

 got the crowd moving and singing along to their resistance songs. In attendance for the action were several impacted families and friends of families with stolen lives, including, but not limited to, 

Tekle Sundberg

 (Minneapolis Police), 

Paul Castaway

 (Denver Police) and 

Kobe Heisler

 (Brooklyn Center Police).




Toshira Garraway, whose fiancé 

Justin Teigen was found dead in a recycling center

 after an interaction with the St. Paul Police in 2009, spoke at the rally and reminded the crowd that before the deadly Operation Metro Surge, Minnesota police have been deadly. 




“Let’s think about the brutality and the evil and the corruption that we were facing right here in Minnesota by our local law enforcement before the Ice agents even showed up,” said Garraway, “and then the ICE agents showed us up and brutalized us even more.”




























After marching to Good’s memorial on 33rd St. and Portland Ave., activist Jae Yates noted that Good’s “identity was erased repeatedly after she was killed. Nobody wanted to talk about the fact that this is also violence against the queer community,” they said, “that this is violence against a queer mom who moved here specifically for the safety that she thought that she would find in Minneapolis.”







“This is what we mean when we say all of these struggles are connected. Because if you can murder a white queer woman in the street. What do you think is happening to Black and brown people? If you can kill a Native woman [

Allison Lussier

], not investigate her death, and then face zero consequences within your department? What do you think is happening to the rest of your neighbors?”




Jae Yates




Also at Good’s memorial, Jaylani Hussein, the Executive Director of the Minnesota Chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (

CAIR-MN

) reminded the crowd of the collective power that the Twin Cities community showed to push out the federal occupation.




Hussein noted that it was Minneapolis neighbors looking out for their neighbors like Renée Good “who stood on the streets with their whistles and with their phones,” that got Greg Bovino, the former “commander at large” of the Border Patrol and Kristi Noem, the former Homeland Security Secretary, fired. He implored Minnesotans never forget what happened and to continue to make strides toward justice.




The march ended at George Floyd Square where the community met at independent photojournalist 

KingDemetrius Pendleton

‘s 

Listen 2 Us Studio

 on 37th St. and Chicago Ave for refreshments and rides back to the march’s starting point.

title: Karayılan commemorates fallen guerrillas from Shengal
content:
Murat Karayılan, a member of the Central Headquarters of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG), has issued a statement commemorating seven fallen Kurdish guerrilla fighters from Shengal. He paid tribute to their contribution to defending the Yazidi population against the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS) and to establishing independent self-defense structures in Shengal. Karayılan also commented on the talks between the Iraqi government and the leadership of the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ). He welcomed the prospect of integrating the YBŞ into the Iraqi army, provided that the units retain their local character and remain permanently responsible for protecting the population.




In his statement, Karayılan recalled the genocide perpetrated by ISIS against the Yazidis in August 2014, which the Yazidi community refers to as the 74th Ferman, as well as the role of the Kurdish guerrillas in defending Shengal. He regards the YBŞ and YJŞ forces established during that period as a crucial achievement in the struggle to prevent another genocide.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/7ec6516d_20261029095010_2026-10-29-navenda-nuceyan-murat-karayilan-peyama-ji-bo-malbaten-sehiden-sengale-1.mp4











The full statement reads as follows:




“With our greetings and respect to our people in Shengal!




Seven of the fallen fighters whose deaths we are announcing and whom we wish to commemorate came from Shengal. In honor of them all, we remember our comrades Agir Botan and Çiçek Öcalan with respect and gratitude, and bow before their memory. We renew our pledge to our fallen comrades to remain faithful to the path of our common cause until the very end.




On behalf of the leadership of the Kurdish movement and the HPG Central Headquarters, I extend my condolences to the families of our martyrs and to the entire population of Shengal, particularly the Yazidi and Arab peoples. I hope that our people will duly recognize the significance of these martyrs. We firmly believe that they will follow in their footsteps, preserve their memory, and give them a dignified welcome.




“The 74th campaign of extermination did not go unpunished”




Dear Families!




Our Yazidi people have been subjected to 74 fermans throughout their history. Each of these campaigns of extermination involved massacres and genocide. Yet not a single one was ever brought to justice. Whoever committed these crimes went unpunished.




However, we know that the 74th campaign of extermination did not go unpunished, thanks to the ideas and philosophy of Rêber Apo [Leader Abdullah Öcalan] and the awareness he instilled in us. Once again, massacres took place. More than 12,000 of our people were killed or taken captive. ISIS had a far-reaching objective: it sought to completely eradicate the Yazidi faith. But the guerrillas of the Kurdish freedom movement, acting in accordance with Rêber Apo’s vision, could not stand by and watch. As soon as they learned of the attacks, they decided to intervene and immediately mobilized.




As is well known, attempts were made to prevent this intervention. But that was not all. At the time, no one was able to stand up to ISIS. Even states fled in the face of its advance. The intervention and resistance in Shengal gave courage to many other forces. ISIS continued its attacks because it could not tolerate being met with resistance. However, it had no experience in mountain warfare and was unable to prevail against our guerrillas. It failed to occupy the mountains.




By contrast, ISIS had experience in urban warfare. It therefore considered Kobanê our weakest point and attacked the city in an attempt to take revenge. Our movement responded to both the attacks on Shengal and those on Kobanê. Even at that time, it was declared that these crimes would have far-reaching consequences—not only in Shengal and Kobanê, but everywhere.




The crimes committed against Kurdish and Yazidi women and the victims of the campaign of extermination did not go unpunished. ISIS’s system of rule was dismantled. The city of Raqqa, which it had declared its capital, became the scene of its defeat. The fighters of the Apoist movement pursued ISIS all the way to Baghuz and brought an end to its system of rule.




The reason for this was the atrocities ISIS had committed in Shengal. In other words, the crimes did not go unpunished, and the blood of the victims of the campaign of extermination was not forgotten. History did not repeat itself. The campaign of extermination did not go unanswered.




“The responsibility for defending Shengal was entrusted to the YBŞ”




To prevent a 75th campaign of extermination in the future, the necessary precautions were taken, including by the young people of Shengal themselves. During the war, the YBŞ and YJŞ were established. The steps taken under the leadership of comrades Mam Zeki, Hesen Seid, Dijwar Feqir, Zerdeşt, Berxwedan, Dilgeş, and Bêrîvan were intended to secure the future of our Yazidi people. The aim was to establish an independent defense force capable of preventing further campaigns of extermination.




This is where the significance of the YBŞ lies. It consists of young Yazidis and members of the Arab population associated with them, capable of defending itself against all forms of attack and provocation, protecting both its members and the wider population. It is not a temporary force, but a permanent, preventive, and reliable self-defense structure.




The YBŞ and YJŞ were established on this basis. Their formation was also made possible by the efforts of our fallen comrades. Their aim was to prevent another campaign of extermination, secure the future of the Yazidi people, and create the conditions for them to protect themselves without depending on others. This was in line with Rêber Apo’s vision. Although there were shortcomings, the work was carried out on this basis. The YBŞ continues this work. It was entrusted with this responsibility.




After we, as the HPG, withdrew from Shengal, responsibility for defending the region was transferred to the YBŞ, including at the level of its command structures. We are convinced that it will continue to preserve this legacy and fulfill its mission in the future.




“The guerrilla intervention was historic”




Our esteemed people, we lost comrades in Shengal. The guerrilla intervention was a historic and honorable undertaking. We are proud of our martyrs. We witnessed young people from Shengal, the daughters and sons of this community, joining our ranks. They wanted not only to fight in Shengal but also to come to the mountains of Kurdistan to stand alongside their comrades.




These remarkable young people joined us, and some of them fell in battle. This is a source of honor for you. The young people of Shengal came to support the guerrillas. This is something deeply valuable and honorable. Just as we are proud of them, you have every right to take pride in them as well. I wish to express my appreciation to the families of these fallen comrades and to the mothers of those young people who came from Shengal to the mountains of Kurdistan and lost their lives in battle, in recognition of the legacy they have left behind.




We commemorate them with deep respect and profound admiration. For us, this carries both an ideological significance and the meaning of a bond forged through blood shed together. It is a deep, meaningful, and firmly rooted comradeship. We firmly believe that all our people and the families attach the same importance to these values.




“The agreement on the YBŞ is a step in the right direction”




We have learned that talks are taking place between the YBŞ leadership and the Iraqi government. We have also learned that an agreement has been reached to grant the YBŞ official status as a local and autonomous defense force, enabling the people of Shengal to protect their own region.




Such an agreement is appropriate. Our people should also welcome it in this spirit. Our fundamental concern is to prevent a 75th campaign of extermination and ensure that the necessary precautions are taken. If the YBŞ is integrated into the Iraqi army under this agreement while retaining its permanent responsibility for defending Shengal as a local force, it will be able to fulfill their role. This would be a sound and appropriate decision.




In this way, the legacy of our martyrs could also be preserved. We firmly believe that the members of the YBŞ and YJŞ, together with our esteemed people in Shengal, will be able to safeguard the achievements made possible by the efforts of our martyrs and continue to pursue the cause for which they stood.




Once again, I extend my respect and condolences to our esteemed families. Şehîd namirin – The martyrs are immortal.”




The seven fallen fighters from Shengal




 




Amara Şengal (Nesîma Îbrahîm)




Avesta Mazlum Şengal (Necla Celal Dexil)

title: Bar associations file criminal complaint against deforestation in Gabar and Besta
content:
The bar associations of Siirt and Şırnak have filed criminal complaints over the ongoing deforestation in the Gabar and Besta regions. They are demanding an immediate halt to the tree felling and criminal investigations into those responsible. The complaints target both individuals involved in the deforestation and public officials suspected of bearing responsibility.




According to the environmental and urban development commissions of both bar associations, the relevant complaints were submitted to the public prosecutors’ offices in Siirt and Şırnak. They concern tree felling carried out between April 20 and July 29, 2025, which reportedly continued beyond that period.




The lawyers are calling for investigations into suspected illegal tree felling, the unlawful transportation of timber and other forest products, and possible complicity in these activities. They are demanding that prosecutors identify those responsible, initiate criminal proceedings, and order examinations of the affected logging and storage sites to secure evidence.




At the same time, the bar associations are demanding full disclosure of the official permits and environmental decisions authorizing the logging operations. These include any environmental impact assessments, information on the number and species of trees felled, transportation documents, and reports on environmental inspections conducted by the authorities.




The bar associations are calling on the relevant authorities to halt the logging immediately. They have pledged to continue their efforts to protect the forests and the wildlife inhabiting them, as well as the population’s right to a healthy environment.

title: Kurdish protester wounded by IRGC sentenced to prison and fined
content:
Milad Ebrahimi, a 31-year-old Kurdish man from Kamyaran, Kurdistan Province, who was shot and wounded by Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces during the December 2025–January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to one year in prison and fined four billion rials on charges of “disturbing public order”.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Branch 101 of the Kamyaran Criminal Court Two tried Ebrahimi in mid-October. He was notified of the verdict on 25 October.




IRGC forces shot Ebrahimi in the lower back with live ammunition during protests in Kamyaran on the evening of 8 January 2026.




He was taken to a medical facility in Sanandaj, the provincial capital, where he underwent surgery before returning home to recover.




Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested him on 1 February, despite his need for further hospitalisation because of an infection caused by his gunshot wound, and took him to the ministry’s detention facility in Sanandaj.




He was denied access to a lawyer and medical care during his detention and was provisionally released on bail on 27 February.

title: Broad support for resistance against solar project in Arzoxlî
content:
Resistance against the controversial Zenkar-2 solar energy project in the Arzoxlî village of Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), is gaining further support. On the eighth day of the vigil against the development of communal grazing lands, a delegation from the Democratic Institutions Platform visited the protest camp in the village. Following a joint march from the village square to the vigil tent, representatives of political parties and environmental organizations called for the complete cancellation of the project.




Ruçem Vefa Elyakut, co-chair of the DBP’s provincial branch in Amed, praised the local community’s struggle. “The people of Arzoxlî have been putting up dignified resistance for days,” she said. She placed the conflict within a long history of displacement and economic exploitation of Kurdish lands. “The mentality that sought to dominate this land has tried to drive its people away. Today, it wants to plunder this land using the same methods. We will never accept that.”




Construction work resumes despite ongoing court proceedings




At the center of the dispute is the “ZENKAR-2 Solar Power Plant and Energy Storage Facility” project developed by the company Zenkar. The company was granted a 49-year electricity generation license for two planned solar power plants equipped with energy storage systems. The facilities are to be built on land that is essential to the local population’s agricultural and livestock activities. Legal proceedings are ongoing against the reclassification of communal grazing lands, the zoning plans, and the favorable environmental impact assessment decision for Zenkar-2. A court-appointed panel of experts concluded that implementing the project in its current form would be unsuitable.













Violent clashes had erupted in March when the company first attempted to enter the site. Five villagers were injured, one of them seriously, during an operation by Turkish police and gendarmerie forces. Fifteen people were temporarily detained. On October 21, the company once again entered the disputed land under the escort of security forces. Since then, residents have been holding a vigil to protest the continuation of construction work and restrictions on their access to communal grazing lands.




“Thousands of years of natural habitats are being sacrificed for profit”




During the solidarity visit, Sabri Kılıç, co-spokesperson of the Amed Ecology Council, criticized the increasing commercialization of natural resources essential to sustaining life. He argued that solar and hydroelectric power plants, mining projects, and oil extraction were part of a broader development trend that increasingly disregarded the needs of local communities. “Land, water, mineral resources, sunlight, and wind are being turned into commodities in the process of capital accumulation,” Kılıç explained. “Mining, oil, hydroelectric, and solar energy projects in our valleys, mountains, and plains are destroying our habitats, which have existed for thousands of years, through policies aimed at maximizing profits.”




Kılıç particularly criticized the role played by the police and military. During the assault in March, he said, they had been deployed not to protect the population but to enforce the company’s interests. “The security forces, whose duty is to protect the people, attacked them as though they were the company’s private security personnel.”




Kılıç pointed out that the planned solar park threatens the agricultural use of the land and, with it, a vital source of livelihood for the village community. He warned of the potential displacement of residents and long-term ecological damage. He also emphasized the historical significance of the area, arguing that it should be officially recognized as a protected cultural heritage site.













Resistance to be expanded




Ruçem Vefa Elyakut stressed that preserving the grazing lands is inseparable from the population’s right to live in their homeland and have a say in its future. “This is our land, our life. We inherited it from our ancestors. We will never allow profiteers and those in power to plunder this land and this heritage,” the DBP politician declared. He vowed that the resistance would continue until the project was stopped.




The Democratic Institutions Platform also announced that it would support the people both through legal action and in their protests. Kılıç called on the relevant authorities to halt the project and protect the livelihoods of local residents. “As the Democratic Institutions Platform, we will support the legal proceedings, stand alongside the people in their practical and legitimate resistance, and expand the resistance.”




The rally concluded with the slogan: “Long live the land, long live labor, long live the resistance!”

title: Environmentalists demand projects in Zîlan Valley to be halted immediately’
content:
The Van Ecology Association, the Mesopotamia Ecology Movement, the Van Bar Association, and the DEM Party’s Erciş (Erdîş) district organisation issued a joint press statement opposing work being carried out on the Zîlan Stream under the pretext of an irrigation canal project.




Reading the statement, Rojhat Özgökçe, a representative of the Mesopotamia Ecology Movement, said the works threatened agricultural land, water resources, and biodiversity.




Özgökçe said that disrupting the natural flow of the Zîlan Stream could have irreversible consequences for the Erciş Plain, the Çelebibağ Wetlands, and the habitats of endemic species.




Stating that environmental impact assessment procedures had not been carried out adequately, Özgökçe said: “This ecological siege, stretching from Zilan Valley to the plain and the lake, threatens the living environments not only of today’s generations but also of future generations. Under Article 56 of the Constitution, which guarantees the right to live in a healthy and balanced environment, as well as under relevant international conventions and environmental legislation, we demand that all these projects be halted immediately, that their permits be revoked, and that the existing damage be remedied.”




Gülderen Varlı, a DEM Party MP representing Wan, also stated that the activities in the valley were affecting not only nature but also the region’s collective social memory.




Varlı said: “The valley is home to wildlife such as otters, salamander species, and the Erciş barbel. Blocking the flow of water affects not only aquatic life but also the entire interconnected ecological system. We will not accept this, and we will continue to monitor and challenge the destruction. Our struggle will continue until you take your machinery, your dirty mentality, and your mentality of war away from here.”

title: Criminal complaint filed against tree felling in Gabar and Besta
content:
In a statement issued by the bar associations’ Environment and Urban Affairs Commissions, it was reported that applications had been submitted to the chief public prosecutor’s offices in Siirt (Sêrt) and Şirnak (Şirnex) over tree felling said to have taken place between 20 April and 29 July 2025, and to have continued thereafter.




The complaint called for investigations to be opened and criminal proceedings to be brought against the relevant public officials and those carrying out the felling, over allegations of unlawful tree cutting, the transportation of illegally obtained forest products, and aiding these activities. It also requested on-site inspections of the felling and storage areas to identify and document evidence.




The bar associations called on the authorities to disclose the administrative permits authorising the felling, environmental impact assessment (EIA) decisions, information on the quantities and species of trees cut down, transport documents, and environmental inspection reports. They also urged the authorities to halt the activities.




The statement emphasised that the bar associations would continue to defend forests, wildlife, and citizens’ right to live in a healthy environment.

title: Εκδηλώσεις – συγκεντρώσεις για τα 82 χρόνια από την απελευθέρωση της Θεσσαλονίκης από τους Ναζί, Παρασκευή 30/10
content:
>Εκδήλωση μνήμης και τιμής για την επέτειο απελευθέρωσης της Θεσσαλονίκης από τους Ναζί, στις 17:00 στη μαρμάρινη στήλη για τους απελευθερωτές της πόλης – μαχητές του ΕΛΑΣ, στο πάρκο μεταξύ  Λ. Πύργου και Βασιλικού Θεάτρου, επί της «Λεωφόρου 30ης Οκτωβρίου 1944. 




>Συγκέντρωση για την απελευθέρωση από τον ΕΛΑΣ της πόλης από τη ναζιστική κατοχή, στις 19:00 στην πλατεία Αγ. Σοφίας.







ΕΤΑΙΡΕΙΑ ΔΙΑΣΩΣΗΣ ΙΣΤΟΡΙΚΩΝ ΑΡΧΕΙΩΝ (Ε.Δ.Ι.Α.) ΜΑΚΕΔΟΝΙΑΣ 1940-1974




82 Χρόνια από την απελευθέρωση της Θεσσαλονίκης από τους Ναζί




Εκδήλωση Μνήμης και Τιμής 




Εκδήλωση μνήμης και τιμής για την επέτειο απελευθέρωσης της Θεσσαλονίκης από τους Ναζί, στις 

30-10-1944

, οργανώνει, όπως κάθε χρόνο, η 

Ε.Δ.Ι.Α.

 

Μακεδονίας 1940-1974

 

την 

Παρασκευή 30 0κτωβρίου 2026

, 

στις 5.00΄μ.μ.,

 μπροστά στη μαρμάρινη στήλη που  έχει αφιερώσει ο Δήμος Θεσσαλονίκης στους απελευθερωτές της πόλης – μαχητές του 

ΕΛΑΣ

, στο πάρκο μεταξύ  Λ. Πύργου και Βασιλικού Θεάτρου, επί της «

Λεωφόρου 30ης Οκτωβρίου 1944».




Η 

30

η

 Οκτωβρίου 1944

 είναι μία πολύ σημαντική επέτειος για την πόλη μας, καθώς τη μέρα εκείνη οι αντάρτες της 

Ομάδας Μεραρχιών Μακεδονίας του ΕΛΑΣ

 με την είσοδό τους στην Θεσσαλονίκη, μετά από σκληρές μάχες στον περίγυρό της κατά των Γερμανών και με την επέμβασή τους απέτρεψαν την ανατίναξη των βασικών υποδομών της πόλης που είχαν υπονομεύσει με εκρηκτικά οι κατακτητές- όπως τα δύο εργοστάσια ηλεκτρισμού, το υδραγωγείο, ο σιδηροδρομικός σταθμός, ο λιμενοβραχιόνας, οι αλευρόμυλοι «Αλατίνι», κ.ά.




Η επέτειος έχει επανενταχθεί στο 

δημοτικό εορτολόγιο

 με απόφαση του 

Δ.Σ.Θ.

 στις 

3 Νοεμβρίου 2014, 

ενώ με το 

ΠΔ 50 / ΦΕΚ 81/Α/9-5-2016, 

καθιερώθηκε ως ‘

δημόσια εορτή τοπικής σημασίας για τον Δήμο Θεσσαλονίκης’. 







Συγκέντρωση: Επέτειος της Απελευθέρωσης της Θεσσαλονίκης από τον ΕΛΑΣ







 Στις 30 Οκτώβρη του 1944, ο ΕΛΑΣ μπαίνει στη Θεσσαλονίκη και η πόλη απελευθερώνεται από τη ναζιστική κατοχή.




Ήταν η κατάληξη ενός σκληρού αγώνα, στον οποίο πρωταγωνίστησε ο ίδιος ο λαός, με το ΕΑΜ και τον ΕΛΑΣ να αποτελούν βασικούς πυλώνες της Εθνικής Αντίστασης. Οι αντάρτες με την ένοπλη δράση τους, οι εργάτες με τις αιματοβαμμένες απεργίες, η νεολαία από τα ξυπόλυτα τάγματα μέχρι τους σπουδαστικους λόχους της ΕΠΟΝ, οι δομές λαϊκής αλληλεγγύης που εσωσαν τον κόσμο από την πείνα, απέδειξαν πως κανένας αντίπαλος δεν είναι ανίκητος όταν βρίσκεται απέναντί του ο οργανωμένος λαός.




 Η απελευθέρωση όμως της πόλης, όπως και του μεγαλύτερου μέρους της χώρας, από τις δυνάμεις του ΕΛΑΣ δεν σήμανε και την δικαίωση όσων και για όσα αγωνίστηκαν. Οι συνεργάτες των ναζί και οι μηχανισμοί της κατοχικής εξουσίας δεν έφυγαν μαζί με τα γερμανικά στρατεύματα. Αντίθετα σημαντικό μέρος τους μαζί με το πολιτικό προσωπικό που είχε εγκαταλείψει την χώρα, συγκρότησαν το μεταπολεμικό αστικό κράτος. Ενώ από την άλλη αυτοί και αυτές που πολέμησαν και ελευθέρωσαν την χώρα ήρθαν αντιμέτωποι με διώξεις, φυλακίσεις, εξορίες και εκτελέσεις. Η πορεία προς τα Δεκεμβριανά και τον Εμφύλιο φανέρωσε πως ο αγώνας για μια ελεύθερη Ελλάδα χωρίς φτώχεια, φασισμό και με τον λαό κυρίαρχο, δεν μπορούσε να αφορά μόνο την σύγκρουση και απελευθέρωση από τον κατακτητή, αλλά και το ποιος θα καθόριζε την επόμενη μέρα.




 Δεν είναι λοιπόν τυχαίο ότι η επέτειος της 30ής Οκτώβρη παραμένει σχετικά άγνωστη, σε αντίθεση με άλλες επετείους που τιμώνται κάθε χρόνο στην πόλη. Η υποβάθμιση της απελευθέρωσης και η αποσιώπηση του ρόλου της Εθνικής Αντίστασης και τον πρωτοπόρο ρόλο των κομμουνιστών σε αυτή, εξυπηρετούν μια ιστορική αφήγηση που θέλει να εξισώσει τα θύματα με τους θύτες και τους προδοτες με τους αντιστασιακούς. Αφηγησεις που δεν μπορούν να δεχτούν τον λαό ως πρωταγωνιστη και όχι απλό θεατή των εξελίξεων.




 Σήμερα 82 χρόνια μετά, η μάχη για την ιστορική μνήμη συναντά τις μάχες του σήμερα. Τον αγώνα ενάντια στον σημερινό πόλεμο, την φτώχεια, τον φασισμό και τον εθνικισμό. Σε μια περίοδο που οι ανταγωνισμοί των ιμπεριαλιστών οξύνονται, οι πολεμικές δαπάνες αυξάνονται και οι λαοί καλούνται να πληρώσουν το κόστος με την εξαθλίωση των ζώων τους και το αίμα τους. Η ιστορική μνήμη δεν είναι απλώς μια μάχη για την αλήθεια του χθες, αλλά μια ζωντανή απόδειξη του τι μπορεί να καταφέρει ο λαός όταν οργανώνεται, αγωνίζεται και παίρνει την υπόθεση της ζωής του στα χέρια του.

Εκδηλώσεις – συγκεντρώσεις για τα 82 χρόνια από την απελευθέρωση της Θεσσαλονίκης από τους Ναζί, Παρασκευή 30/10

infolibre

.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Santiago del Estero: Corrupción y desalojo contra comunidad originaria La Armonía
content:
Un operativo policial intentó desalojar este miércoles a una familia del territorio ancestral de la comunidad indígena Lule Vilela La Armonía, en el Departamento Copo de la provincia de Santiago del Estero, a instancias de una persona ajena a la comunidad, Isabel Salas, que reclama la tierra comunitaria como propia y pretende venderla. La resistencia frenó el desalojo y la orden fue temporalmente suspendida.




Intento de desalojo en la comunidad La Armonía. Captura de video de MOCASE VC




“Así es el atropello para desalojar a campesinos indígenas de la comunidad indígena Lule Vilela La Armonía”, denunció el Movimiento Campesino de Santiago del Estero (MOCASE) Vía Campesina al publicar un video del despliegue policial ocurrido durante la mañana de este miércoles 28 de octubre.










 


































Ver esta publicación en Instagram






































































 




Una publicación compartida por MOCASE VC (@mocase_viacampesina)













“Así es la mafia de la venta ilegal de tierras a los que les gusta la plata”, agregaron desde la organización, y responsabilizaron a una persona llamada Isabel Salas, alias “Chabela”, de la localidad de Monte Quemado, como la impulsora del operativo. Desde la comunidad La Armonía agregaron que se trata de una situación repetida, y que Isabel Salas “le paga al Oficial de Justicia”.




Vender el territorio ancestral




Rosa Córdoba, Consejera de la Comunidad Lule Vilela La Armonía, detalló la situación que están enfrentando: “Hemos sufrido un atropello aquí en la comunidad, en el lugar denominado 5 Hermanos donde vive la familia Tévez y Salto. La familia está conformada con 5 hijos, nietos, yerno, nueras. Ellos viven de hace más de 10 años en el lugar, pero es territorio relevado, ancestral de la comunidad. Como la comunidad siempre ha tenido una idea de eso, de los territorios que están relevados y vacíos, que se le den a hijos de compañeros del lugar, y esto ha sucedido así”.







https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Rosa-Cordoba-Consejera-MOCASE-La-Armonia.ogg




Audio: Rosa Córdoba




El campesinado santiagueño, criollo e indígena, 

sufre históricamente situaciones de violencia e indefensión jurídica y social

 ante sujetos que buscan apropiarse de tierras comunales y fiscales, muchas veces con la complicidad activa y manifiesta de funcionarios judiciales y de las fuerzas de seguridad.




Así ocurre en este caso. Rosa cuenta que “esta mujer, Isabel Salas, alias Chabela, conjuntamente con su hijo, Federico Guzmán, se quieren apropiar del lugar diciendo que es de ellos, y tan solo se quieren apropiar para venderlo. Ya esta mujer lo ha vendido varias veces haciendo esas solicitudes truchas, que desde Colonización 

(nota: se refiere a la ex 

Dirección de Colonización

 de Santiago del Estero)

, lo sabía hacer a estas solicitudes que se le daba a cualquiera y en cualquier lugar, sin importarle quién viviese en el territorio ese. Entonces, estas personas vendían esos lugares a cordobeses, a chaqueños, y ellos se iban apropiando así de los lugares. Entonces, llega esta mujer queriendo vender cierta cantidad de hectáreas que dice que son 3200 hectáreas, que es territorio ancestral de la comunidad”.




Intento de desalojo en la comunidad La Armonía. Captura de video de MOCASE VC




La resistencia frenó el desalojo




“Nosotros estamos organizados con el MOCASE en la comunidad La Armonía, y nos despertamos con esta noticia”, contó Rosa.




“En realidad, no nos despertamos porque todos aquí estamos trabajando en las tareas laborales en el campo, y todo el mundo se ha puesto alerta, dejando lo que teníamos que hacer, por ir a solidarizarse con el compañero para que no sea desalojado. Entonces, ahí nos damos que todo ha sido arreglado, como esta mujer le paga al Oficial de Justicia, le paga a la Policía de Santiago del Estero para que haga este desalojo”.




“Entonces, aquí, como nosotros vamos al lugar y comenzamos a resistir en el lugar, a decir que no lo van a desalojar al compañero, porque el lugar es de la comunidad, es del compañero, está produciendo en el lugar. Que nos oponíamos a todo eso. Entonces, al ver toda esta resistencia de la comunidad que hubo, el juez dictamina que se cancele el desalojo y que hagan todo un inventario y que hagan una investigación profunda”.




Intento de desalojo en la comunidad La Armonía. Captura de video de MOCASE VC




“Y, entonces, ahí, el Oficial de Justicia y el otro señor que andaba, el Comisario Cejas, nos dice que en el expediente solo figura que el compañero vivía en una choza, que estaba usurpando el lugar, que él no tenía tal magnitud que el compañero estaba produciendo tanto”.




“Porque como si bien el compañero está produciendo animales, vaca, cabra, chancho, gallina, y no 2, 3, sino mucha cantidad. Tiene más de 80 cabras, más de 40 ovejas, tiene cabrito, cordero, tiene más de 10 chanchas madres, tienes vacas, tiene un cerco de más de 2 hectáreas que siembra, y te puedo seguir diciendo muchas otras cosas más de productividad que tiene”.




“Y, asimismo, hemos logrado otra vez otra vez frenar otro desalojo en la comunidad indígena Lule Vilela de La Armonía. Pero a todo esto, gracias a dios, hoy podemos decir y reconocer, como siempre hemos reconocido, una memoria histórica que lo tenemos presente, que hemos organizado con el MOCASE, con compañeros que vinieron desde Tintina, desde Quimilí a dar su testimonio, y hoy seguimos sembrando ese fortalecimiento, esa enseñanza de defender nuestros derechos. Y a base a toda esta enseñanza de sabiduría que han tenido los compañeros que han formado el Mocase hoy podemos decir, otra familia ha quedado en su territorio gracias a la solidaridad de todos los compañeros de la comunidad indígena, Lule Vilela La Armonía.




La entrada 

Santiago del Estero: Corrupción y desalojo contra comunidad originaria La Armonía

 se publicó primero en 

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.

author: Pinko Collective
title: Letter in Support of the Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá and Trans and Queer People Facing State Repression Worldwide
content:
We reprint the open letter below in support of the Dolls of Berlin. To add your name as a signatory, follow the link at the bottom of the page.

On the afternoon of Sunday 18 October a large police squad forcibly entered Casa Kuá, a queer community center in Berlin, Germany, where at that point The Dolls of Berlin, a transfem social collective, was gathering. Police detained several women for hours while ransacking Casa Kuá. We, the undersigned, stand in support with The Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá, and queer and trans people facing state violence, repression and erasure everywhere. We are demanding that the German State drop the case and immediately stop the criminalization of trans spaces and solidarities. We are urging everyone to contribute to the fundraiser, to help our comrades continue their essential work and activities, and keep 

nourishing much needed survival spaces for the most vulnerable communities

. 

The attack against the Berlin Dolls comes at a time of unprecedented rise of state fascism, both in Germany where the AfD recently won local elections in Saxony-Anhalt, in neighbouring European countries, and in India, Brazil, Argentina, the United States and elsewhere. This rise of the far right has been accompanied by a massive increase on attacks on queer and trans people. In Turkey between 12-14 September, in coordinated overnight raids across five cities, Turkish police targeted seven LGBTQI+ rights organizations, two groups supporting people living with HIV, and 13 bars and clubs where queer people gather. Board members of some of the country’s oldest LGBTQI+ associations, including Kaos GL and Lambda Istanbul, were 

taken from their homes

. Human Rights Watch reports that at least 

112 people were arrested and that 82 remain in detention

 by court order. On 3/4 October Taiwan police 

raided a Taipei queer bar

 detaining 51 persons and abusing disabled customers.

At the same time, increasingly authoritarian states, including Germany, are seeking to erase trans existence through administrative violence, putting barriers in front of access to trans healthcare. As European governments divert public spending to remilitarisation efforts, access to housing, welfare, jobs and education become circumscribed. In the UK, the drastically curtailed access to trans healthcare in recent years has led to trans suicides on an 

unprecedented scale

. Recent government guidelines on so-called 'single sex spaces' are likely to cause more deaths such as that of trans woman, Joelle, who died after being 

denied cancer care for 16 days

. A stark example of the hypocrisy on the part of the ruling elite came on 21 October when openly gay Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jette and his partner celebrated the expected arrival of their child, while his government 

denies queer refugees the right to family reunification

. The attacks on queer and trans people are accompanied by attacks on, and further marginalisation of the disabled, migrants and refugees, precarious workers, poor Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, the unhoused and incarcerated, compounded for those in multiple of these categories. It is a tell-tale sign of fascism when particular communities are rendered vulnerable, disposable and presented as scapegoats for the various harmful effects of racialised capitalism. 

That the relatively small community of queer and trans people, and racialised trans femmes in particular, has become a target for (proto-)fascist and authoritarian regimes globally is no surprise. Transness especially stands out as a visible transgression of cis hetero patriarchal norms on which fascist authority is built. It forms a thorn in the eye of regimes dependent on popular internalisation of its structural "truths". Transness thus becomes a powerful wedge issue that allows states to whip up fear and distrust of trans people which is consolidated through state carceral and administrative violence. It is also no surprise that state attacks on queer and trans people are on the rise globally at a time when Gen Z, along with older social movements are rising up in France, Albania, Brazil, India, Argentina, Indonesia, Greece and across the planet. Time and again, queer and trans people have stood at the helm of 

social movements and popular struggles for liberation

.

 

The 18 October attack on The Dolls of Berlin at Casa Kuá is historic. Coming at this conjuncture in history, it is signaling the moment that demands we all stand up not only with and for our Queer and Trans siblings, but for humanity itself. We, the undersigned, stand with 

the Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá, and Trans and Queer people facing state repression worldwide, and heed their call to get organised! Be enraged! Stay glamorous! If you would like to stay informed, spread awareness or become more involved, you can follow on Instagram @thedolls_ofberlin and @casakua. Support committees are forming in Berlin, in Europe and worldwide to gather endurance and momentum for this struggle that is just starting. To add your signature to this letter add your details in the form linked at the very bottom of the page. [

Auf Deutsch

]

Signatories :

title: “Δεν υπήρχε σπιθαμή στο σώμα του που να μην ήταν χτυπημένη” – Πώς η δικαιοσύνη επιβραβεύει την αστυνομική βία
content:
“Δεν υπήρχε σπιθαμή στο σώμα του που να μην ήταν χτυπημένη” – Πώς η δικαιοσύνη επιβραβεύει την αστυνομική βία




Στις 21 Σεπτεμβρίου 2024, ο Μοχάμεντ 

Καμράν

 Ασίκ δολοφονήθηκε από αστυνομικούς στο Α.Τ. Αγίου Παντελεήμονα. Τον Ιανουάριο του 2026, ο εισαγγελέας Σωτήρης Μπουγιούκος αποφάσισε να αρχειοθετήσει την υπόθεση, ισχυριζόμενος ότι δεν υπήρχαν επαρκή στοιχεία για να παραπεμφθεί σε δίκη. Ως αποτέλεσμα, δεν υπάρχουν πλέον νομικά μέσα για τη συνέχιση της υπόθεσης στα ελληνικά δικαστήρια. Οι αστυνομικοί που τον ξυλοκόπησαν μέχρι θανάτου συνεχίζουν τη ζωή τους χωρίς καμία συνέπεια.







Ο Μοχάμεντ Καμράν Ασίκ, εργάτης από το Πακιστάν, συνελήφθη, μεταφέρθηκε και κρατήθηκε σε πέντε διαδοχικά αστυνομικά τμήματα, όπου υπέστη επανειλημμένη σωματική βία, χωρίς ουσιαστική επικοινωνία με την οικογένειά του ή πρόσβαση σε νομική υποστήριξη. Στις 21 Σεπτεμβρίου 2024 βρέθηκε νεκρός μέσα στο Αστυνομικό Τμήμα Αγίου Παντελεήμονα, στον μοναδικό χώρο που δεν είχε κάλυψη από κάμερες. Ακόμα και η ίδια η κρατική ιατροδικαστική πραγματογνωμοσύνη κατέληξε στο συμπέρασμα ότι ο θάνατός του προκλήθηκε από ισχαιμία του μυοκαρδίου, ως αποτέλεσμα έντονου σωματικού και ψυχικού στρες που συνδέεται με τον συνεχή ξυλοδαρμό κατά την κράτησή του.




Τη δολοφονία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν ακολούθησε εκτεταμένη συγκάλυψη της υπόθεσης (όπως τέτοια ακολούθησε και το κρατικό έγκλημα στην Πύλο). Οι αστυνομικοί του Α.Τ. Αγίου Παντελεήμονα ισχυρίστηκαν ότι «αυτοτραυματίστηκε λόγω στερητικού συνδρόμου αλκοόλ». Ο εισαγγελέας Σωτήρης Μπουγιούκος πολύ στοχευμένα παρέλειψε στην επίσημη αναφορά το ιατρικό συμπέρασμα που ξεκάθαρα αποδίδει την καρδιακή αποτυχία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν ως αποτέλεσμα του εκτεταμένου και άγριου ξυλοδαρμού του. Αυτή η απόφαση είναι ξεδιάντροπη συγκάλυψη του βασανισμού και της δολοφονίας του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν από την ελληνική αστυνομία.




(Ενημερωτικό απόσπασμα από το κάλεσμα της Ανοιχτής Συνέλευση Ενάντια στην Κρατική Δολοφονία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν σε πορεία για τα 2 χρόνια από τη δολοφονία του Καμράν)




Οι ζωές μας στις γειτονιές της Αθήνας γίνονται καθημερινά όλο και πιο ασφυκτικές μέσα σε ένα κλίμα κρατικής βίας, εκφοβισμού και πρακτικών συνεχούς επιτήρησης.




Η κρατική εξουσία μέσω νεοφιλελεύθερων πολιτικών πασχίζει να εδραιώσει και να φυσικοποιήσει πρακτικέςπεριθωριοποίησης και εκτοπισμού αυτών των ομάδων που αντιστέκονται καιεναντιώνονται στην απαξίωση των ζωών τους. Η καπιταλιστική πολιτική «ανάπτυξης» στη συνέχεια στοχεύει στην διάλυση και στον αφανισμό κάθε είδους κοινότητας και συλλογικοποίησης. Προσπαθεί να δημιουργήσει γειτονιές απονέκρωσης, φόβου, αποσιώπησης και υποταγής χτυπώντας στους κατεξοχήν τόπους συγκέντρωσης, μοιράσματος και ζύμωσης: τις πλατείες.







Η πλατεία Βικτωρίας αποτελεί εδώ και πολλά χρόνια ένα πεδίο μάχης και συλλογικών αγώνων. Οι γειτονιές κάτω από την Πατησίων είναι ο επόμενος στόχος της λεγόμενης “ανάπλασης”, ενός σχεδίου που υπόσχεται “αναβάθμιση των ζωών”, αλλά στην πράξη συχνά μεταφράζεται σε αποκλεισμό, εμπορευματοποίηση και έλεγχο του δημόσιου χώρου. Από τα pushbacks και τα στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης, από τη θάλασσα και τα χερσαία σύνορα μέχρι τις φυλακές και το δημόσιο χώρο, το κράτος δείχνει το ρατσιστικό του πρόσωπο. Μέσα σε ένα σκηνικό συνεχών ελέγχων, τραμπουκισμού, ξυλοδαρμών, συλλήψεων και βασανισμών, τα περιστατικά αστυνομικής βίας και κρατικών δολοφονιών μόνο αυξάνονται. Θοδωρής Ζαβραδινός, Κώστας Μανιουδάκης, Ζάκι, Βασίλης Μάγγος, Σαμπάνης, Κώστας Φραγκούλης , Μία Χαριζούλ , Εμπουκά Μαμάν Σούμπεκ, Μοχάμεντ Καμράν, βιασμός 19χρονης στο Α.Τ Ομονοίας και τόσα ακόμα περιστατικά κρατικής τρομοκρατίας που δεν έχουν καταγραφεί.




Η Βικτώρια είναι μια γειτονιά μεταναστευτική, ζωντανή, γεμάτη ιστορίες και πολιτισμούς. Οι άνθρωποι της προσπαθούν καθημερινά να πάρουν ανάσες ελευθερίας, μέσα σε ένα κλίμα αυξανόμενης και ασφυκτικής αστυνομικής παρουσίας.




Δεν είναι δύσκολο να θυμηθούμε κάποιες από τις εικόνες των προηγούμενων χρόνων: τις σκηνές των προσφύγων στην πλατεία, το κύμα αλληλεγγύης που απλώθηκε αυθόρμητα, τα ξηλωμένα παγκάκια και τα κάγκελα που τοποθετήθηκαν για να μην κοιμούνται προσφύγισσες, πρόσφυγες και μετανάστες, τις ρατσιστικές επιχειρήσεις-σκούπα, τους ελέγχους για χαρτιά. Μέσα σε αυτό το κλίμα όμως άνθισαν παρεμβάσεις απέναντι στην καταστολή, το ρατσισμό, την ομοφοβία και την κρατική βία. Μικροφωνικές επανοικειοποίησης, πορείες, παρουσία κοινωνικών ιατρείων, κινήσεις γειτονιάς που αντιστάθηκαν στη σιωπή. Αυτή η “αορατότητα” είναι ακόμα πιο έντονη για κάποια σώματα— τα σώματα των μεταναστών, των προσφυγισσών, των φτωχών. Παίρνοντας πίσω την πλατεία Βικτωρίας, δεν διεκδικούμε απλώς έναν χώρο.




Διεκδικούμε την ορατότητα των πολλαπλών μορφών ζωής που ανήκει σε όλες/α/ους· Μια πλατεία που θα γίνει ξανά πυρήνας ζωής, σημείο αναφοράς και κοινής φροντίδας. Η Βικτώρια δεν είναι απλώς μια πλατεία. Είναι η διεκδίκηση μιας πόλης που θα ζει με τους ανθρώπους της, όχι ερήμην τους

.




Μέσα από τους κοινούς μας αγώνες προσπαθούμε να σπάμε το φόβο και τον αποκλεισμό. Σε αυτήν την περίοδο που ο έλεγχος και η καταστολή αναβαθμίζονται, απαντάμε με συλλογικοποίηση και αντίσταση, διεκδικώντας την ελεύθερη πρόσβαση στο δημόσιο χώρο. Σε αυτόν τον ένα χρόνο μας στήνουμε αναχώματα ενάντια στο ρατσισμό και την απομόνωση με πρόταγμα την πολιτισμική πολυφωνία μέσα στο δημόσιο χώρο.Λίγες από τις δράσεις μας είναι η Συλλογικής μας κουζίνας, η φιλοξενία κουκλοπαικτικών παραστάσεων, το παιχνίδι και οι δημιουργικές δραστηριότητες για παιδιά, η στήριξη από χορωδίες και διαφορετικούς μουσικούς, το αυτοοργανωμένο καρναβάλι και η παρέλαση στη γειτονιά με γιορτινούς ρυθμούς, οι κουβέντες και οι εκδηλώσεις με άλλες συλλογικότητες που αφορούν στους πολύμορφους αγώνες για την υγεία, τη στέγη, την αξιοπρέπεια.




Να πάρουμε πίσω την κλεμμένη χαρά, το παιχνίδι, την ανεμελιά, μακριά από τα κάγκελα και τους περιορισμούς. Να κάνουμε την πλατεία ξανά τόπο συνάντησης, χώρο μοιράσματος και συλλογικότητας.




Ενάντια στην κρατική και συνοριακή βία.


Κοινότητες αγώνα και αλληλεγγύης σε κάθε γειτονιά.




(Τοποθέτηση 

από το κατειλημμένο κοινωνικό κέντρο “Ζιζάνια” στην εκδήλωση με τη δικηγόρο που χειρίζεται την υπόθεση της δολοφονίας του Καμράν)

author: Chris Walker
title: “Our Democracy Is in Danger” — Judge Rejects Trump Bid to Block 20K Votes in CA
content:
Washington State officials also found several errors in a list of voters the White House has deemed ineligible.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The Trump administration’s attempts to discount the votes of tens of thousands of voters it has dubiously deemed ineligible to participate in this year’s midterm elections hit two major roadblocks on Wednesday, as officials in Washington state and a judge’s ruling in California challenged the White House’s reasoning.

In August, the administration issued a report claiming that 24,000 people who took part in the 2020 election were noncitizens. Though many observers noted major flaws in the report, the White House has continued to push its disenfranchisement campaign, sending lists of residents’ names to several states and demanding that officials segregate their ballots.

After the administration sent Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs a list of people in his state that they said should be deemed ineligible to vote, a preliminary review of the list by Hobbs’s staff found that many of its claims were erroneous. The list included several names of U.S. citizens, for example.

The list is “not reliable,” Hobbs wrote on Wednesday in an open letter to the administration. “Without individualized proof of ineligibility, it would be both irresponsible and illegal for election officials to decline to process a registered voter’s ballot.”

A “significant number” of the names on the list are people who are simply “not currently registered to vote or are on inactive status,” he said.

Hobbs was emphatic in his refusal to comply with the White House’s demands to segregate ballots.

“State and local election officials in Washington work tirelessly to administer free and fair elections,” Hobbs wrote. “They are truly heroes of democracy. … Rather than distract these dedicated public servants from their important work at this late hour with a meritless lawsuit, I strongly encourage you to revisit the deeply flawed data you provided earlier this week, identify any actual proof, and work collaboratively with my office in the weeks or months to come.”

Also on Wednesday, a federal judge ruled against the administration in a lawsuit it had filed against California. The suit seeks to segregate 20,000 ballots belonging to supposed noncitizens in that state’s upcoming elections. Notably, in paperwork filed with the court earlier this week from Los Angeles, officials discovered that a “high percentage” of the names belong to people born in the United States.

Judge David O. Carter did not mince words in his decision.

“This case is about the right of every American citizen to vote in a free and fair election,” the federal judge wrote. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch.”

“In bringing this lawsuit, the Executive would have this Court believe that it reigns as a sole sovereign. But California and its people are sovereign, too,” Carter added.

The request by the administration to segregate ballots “violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections” that could have long-term precedential consequences, Carter said.

Constitutional rights and our democracy are at stake. The public interest favors their protection. Individuals who have met the requirements of California’s voter registration laws must not be deprived of a core right merely because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors.

“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable,” Carter wrote in the conclusion of his ruling. “Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred. If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger. This Court declines to be a party to such process.”

The refusal by Washington state officials to comply with the administration’s demands, as well as the legal ruling from a federal judge, could be challenged by the White House. But with only a few days left before the midterms, it’s unlikely that any action — short of one that is drastic and potentially unlawful — could occur in time for an appeal.

These two events come as recent polling indicates that most Americans are skeptical that President Donald Trump will accept the final outcome of the midterm elections, especially if Democrats win one or both Houses of Congress, as they’re projected to do. Trump himself has indicated that he will only accept the results if he deems them to be “honest.”

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

Truthout produces reporting you won’t see in the mainstream: journalism from the frontlines of global conflict, interviews with grassroots movement leaders, high-quality legal analysis and more.
