author: Sharon Zhang
title: US Journalist Detained by Israeli Forces After Being Beaten by Israeli Settlers
content:
The incident came as a UN expert issued a report detailing Israel’s “mediacide” in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

A U.S. journalist was detained by Israeli forces after being beaten by Israeli settlers while documenting attacks on Palestinians amid the olive harvest in the occupied West Bank.

Independent journalist Jasper Nathaniel, along with journalist-activists Russian Adele Shoko and Russian-Israeli Andrey Khrzhanovskiy, were in the village of Umm al-Khair when they were beaten by Israeli settlers. Umm al-Khair, in Masafer Yatta, is one of the most heavily besieged areas in the West Bank by Israeli settlers, and the journalists have been documenting fierce settler raids against Palestinians as they conduct the olive harvest.

Video taken by Shoko shows armed settlers attacking Khzhanovskiy, shoving him to the ground as Nathaniel tries to protect him. According to Shoko, Khzhanovskiy “was severely beaten and lost consciousness several times in front of police,” suffering a concussion. Another video taken by a different activist shows Khzhanovskiy falling to the ground and losing consciousness as a policeman blocks a paramedic from reaching him.

Settlers initially blocked the ambulance from reaching the scene, and Israeli officials denied Khzhanovskiy hospital treatment, instead taking him to the police station.

Shoko says she and Nathaniel were also beaten, and that Nathaniel was pepper sprayed and arrested by Israeli authorities.

"This is what we are willing to die for as Palestinians", Hazem Jbara told us, showing us half a bag of olives—all he managed to harvest in 10 minutes before settlers attacked him. I watched from the rooftop as they came from two sides, trying to trap Hazem and @infinite_jaz… pic.twitter.com/CJo1EgdmbX

Both Nathaniel and Khzhanovskiy were released on Thursday afternoon local time, Shoko said. However, they were banned from the West Bank for 60 days. “This is a clear example of Israel trying to prevent us from covering the terror it commits in the West Bank,” Shoko said.

The incident comes less than two weeks after Israeli settlers threw Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine to the ground and beat her, sending her to the hospital. That attack was documented by Nathaniel and Khzhanovskiy, who accompanied her as she received medical care.

Wearing a cast on her wrist, Levine said in an interview with CNN’s Jake Tapper last week that the violence she faced at the hands of Israeli settlers is just a glimpse into what Palestinians have to deal with on a daily basis.

“I can now really understand what others have gone through, what Palestinian women, children, men have gone through,” she said. “I’ve covered funerals of young people that have been killed by these Jewish settlers. It was always very difficult to meet people — even a man that was sexually abused and tortured in front of his family.”

“I’m an American, I work for the Washington Post, my story is getting a lot of attention around the world, everyone wants to talk to me — but I can’t imagine what it’s like for all the victims that have gone through the same ordeal and are living with the threat of this violence on a daily basis,” Levine went on.

Last week, Democratic House candidate Brad Lander was also detained by the Israeli military during a visit to the West Bank with an international delegation to harvest olives with a Palestinian family.

The attack on Nathaniel and other journalists comes just after UN Special Rapporteur for the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese presented a report to the UN accusing Israel of “mediacide” in its continued targeting of journalists and media workers in Palestine, especially amid Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

In the report, Albanese notes that Israel has systematically targeted journalists and media workers, with hundreds of them “killed, injured, arbitrarily detained, tortured, intimidated and smeared as terrorists while documenting the destruction of their own society.”

This targeting has been essential to Israel’s genocide and assaults as it seeks to erase those who exposed it to the world.

“[T]hese practices constitute an assault on truth that is intrinsic to the genocidal violence they are intended to conceal,” Albanese wrote. “The elimination of witnesses, the suppression of freedom of expression and the abandonment of fundamental journalistic ethics may amount, in many ways, to ‘mediacide’: the systematic destruction of the media’s public function.”

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Israel’s Election Still in Deadlock After Palestinian Parties’ Surprise Upset
content:
Netanyahu has claimed that the Palestinian parties have “stolen” the election.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

With the results of Israel’s election on Tuesday finalized on Thursday, the right-wing bloc around current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has won 53 seats out of the 120 in Israel’s parliament, the Knesset, while the opposition bloc around Gadi Eisenkot has won 48 seats. Both are short of the majority needed to create a ruling coalition government.

The real upset, however, is with the Palestinian parties, after Palestinian citizens of Israel came out in record numbers to vote Tuesday: The Joint List has won 11 seats, and the United Arab List eight seats. This gives the Palestinian parties 19 seats in the Knesset — more than their previous record of 15 — and makes the Joint List, a progressive alliance of three Palestinian-led parties, the third largest party in the Knesset.

Over the coming weeks, party leaders from Eisenkot and Netanyahu’s blocs will negotiate and work to form a ruling coalition. If they cannot form a ruling government, they will face another round of elections.

But in order for Eisenkot’s bloc to form a ruling coalition and oust Netanyahu, it would need to create an alliance with the Palestinian political parties. Eisenkot has stated that he will not work with Arab parties — but this means that his choice is either to hand the victory to Netanyahu, or create a larger opposition coalition with the Palestinian parties.

In 2021, Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid briefly ousted Netanyahu by creating an alliance with the United Arab List. However, the Joint List, which won more seats than the Arab List in Tuesday’s election, is explicitly anti-Zionist and progressive — making it a scapegoat of the Zionist parties more than a likely coalition partner.

Netanyahu used the fact that the opposition will need to create alliances with Palestinian parties in his fearmongering around the election — his slogan, “Yamin o Falastin,” or “Right Wing or Palestine,” framed the election as a choice between his Likud party or handing power to Palestinians. The Likud Party and its far right allies had also attempted to ban the Palestinian-led parties from participating in the elections entirely — but only managed to force out candidate Sami Abu Shehadeh, chair of the Balad party within the Joint List.

Since Tuesday, Netanyahu has claimed that the Palestinian parties have “stolen” the election, saying there has been interference by “foreign entities” who aim to facilitate “a foreign takeover of the Knesset, [and] the Islamization of Israel.”

Balad’s Abu Shehadeh said the claims that Palestinian parties stole the election amount to a new phase of incitement against Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up 20 percent of Israel’s citizen population.

Netanyahu has led the right-wing Likud Party for 19 years across six terms. In the course of his sixth term, he has overseen the three-year long genocide in Gaza, and launched calamitous wars on Lebanon and Iran. But while he is wanted by the International Criminal Court for war crimes, his political tenure was challenged inside Israel for different reasons — a longstanding corruption trial, his failures on and after October 7, and resentment over exemptions for Haredi Jews from military service.

The first Israeli election since October 7 and the start of the genocide in Gaza, this election saw former general Gadi Eisenkot position himself as an alternative to Netanyahu. This is because, as political analyst Daniel Levy told Truthout, Eisenkot is new to the political scene, and is “untainted by the corruption and failures of the [Israeli] government, in particular not having been in a leadership position on October 7.”

“In contrast to Netanyahu, who is considered to have put personal considerations over national interest, Eisenkot lost his son and two nephews in the war, and this personal sacrifice has been highlighted in staking out such a difference” in the eyes of the Israeli public, Levy added.

But this does not mean that there are significant policy differences between Eisenkot and Netanyahu. In fact, none of the Israeli “opposition” parties — save the Palestinian-led political parties — oppose Israel’s genocide in Gaza, or apartheid and ethnic cleansing policies across the occupied territories.

For his part, Eisenkot has said repeatedly that he opposes Palestinian statehood, calling it “delusional.” He has even worked to position himself to the right of Netanyahu on the issue of security, settlements, and anti-Palestinian racism — in a competition of who can espouse more racism against Palestinians.

Throughout his campaign, Eisenkot boasted of the “Dahiya Doctrine” as part of his security credentials — a strategy he formulated as a commander in Israel’s 2006 war on Lebanon that calls for massive, disproportionate force and targeting of civilian areas. The doctrine has been used throughout the Gaza genocide and concurrent war on Lebanon.

In March 2026, Eisenkot encouraged the Israeli government to continue to use the Dahiya Doctrine in Lebanon, stating on X, “The Dahiya Doctrine has never been more relevant than it is now, and it must be implemented.”

Thus, while Eisenkot’s new Yashar! Party is considered “centrist” within Israel, it rests on the same fundamental premises of all the other Zionist political parties — the dispossession of Palestinians and expansion of the state of Israel.

As Palestinian human rights lawyer Diana Buttu said at a recent event hosted by the Institute for Middle East Understanding, “Genocide is not on the ballot. There is not a single party [among the Zionist parties] that is talking about the genocide.”

Meanwhile, Netanyahu is likely to double down on his anti-Palestinian rhetoric in the coming weeks — as well as his attacks and escalations in the West Bank, Gaza, and Iran — in an attempt to prevent a handover of power.

author: Mary Stuart
title: How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power
content:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s 

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 is critical reading for anyone seeking to understand and push back against the far-right coalitions wielding considerable state and corporate power around the world.




Klein and Taylor posit that today’s fascists believe that end times have arrived, and have made it their mission to profit from cascading global crises, while hunkering down and protecting themselves as the world burns around them.




The book details three factions of end times fascists, united by their shared apocalypticism. The religious fundamentalists believe end times are upon us, but they will be saved by their messiah. The Silicon Valley technologists are building technologies they say could be world-ending, that in the meantime are killing jobs, consuming vast resources, and polluting communities. The ethno-nationalists espouse conspiratorial ideas about cultural replacement and treat immigration as an existential threat.




DeSmog Canada editor/reporter Mary Stuart spoke with Astra Taylor about how climate change fits into end times fascism, the importance of AI data centre fights, and how we can understand Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s neoliberal moves in response to U.S. President Donald Trump.




Taylor is a writer, documentarian, and activist. She co-founded the 

Debt Collective

, a membership-based union for debtors, and is the author of several books, including 

The Age of Insecurity

 and 

Democracy May Not Exist But We’ll Miss It When It is Gone

.




This interview was conducted by phone and has been edited for length and clarity.




Mary Stuart:

 

I

 

want to start by

 

asking how your book can help us understand some recent elections. Jair Bolsonaro’s son Flávio won the first round of voting in Brazil’s election and

 

nearly

 

became president. The far-right AfD recently won in Saxony-Anhalt.

 

How do these wins fit into your analysis of end times fascism?




Astra Taylor:

 One phenomena we describe in End Times Fascism relevant here is the role of Pentecostal religious communities in turning out the vote. To paraphrase reporting from Brazil, a voter said “my heart’s with Lula, but my pastor told me to vote for Flávio”.




The incredibly difficult conditions that we’re living under created fertile terrain for prophecy and religion, for kinds of pentecostalism, a faith that is focused on prosperity, individual advancement and banking on the idea that life is suffering here on earth, but you will be rewarded in the afterlife.




There’s also interference from Tech oligarchs. We don’t know the half of it at this moment, but the way the platform [Meta] refused to run ads for Lula’s party and beyond is certainly a factor. And the Trump regime [is playing a role] as well.




AfD is a similar. Naomi and I wrote a piece in the 

Financial Times

 and we open with the images that went viral this summer of the Danube River drying, and Nazi warships emerging. Hundreds of Nazi warships sank during WWII, and as the river receded, this paraphernalia was coming out of the mud. We thought it was a powerful metaphor for today. What’s really striking is the riverbed— the fact that it’s drying because of climate change. Our point is that fascism always emerges from crises. And we cannot separate the ecological and economic crises people are facing.




People are really struggling with affordability. People are feeling that they don’t have a future. And actually quite strikingly, rates of immigration are quite low, right? So [Saxony-Anhalt is] one of the places with the least immigration, but [the AfD] step in and say “the problem is the immigrants, it’s not a larger economic system.” This is a classic fascist move that we describe throughout the book.




MS:

 

What role do climate change and climate denial play in end times fascism?




AT:

 Naomi and I are insistent that the planet is a player in our politics. Fascism always surges in moments of crisis.




We are in a world that is being roiled by disasters and shocks. We’ve reached a point where the consequences [of climate change] are undeniable. You cannot deny a heat dome when you’re inside it. You cannot deny a hurricane when it’s blowing the roof off your house. Of course, you can still deny why the storm is coming. You can embrace a Marjorie Taylor Greene perspective and say that it’s due to space lasers or you can say “the climate has always chained, this is nothing new, we don’t know if it’s human causing it.”




The far-right is adapting to circumstances … where ecological catastrophes are the norm, people can’t pay their property insurance bills anymore because the rates have been jacked up or because the insurers have pulled out, or where people have to pay the cost of fixing their homes or moving because of disasters.




The far-right is having to acknowledge that there are fires, there are storms, that people are suffering. They’re responding by deflecting, by saying, “don’t blame the fossil fuel companies and the politicians who take their money, blame the globalists in the EU and their climate policies, or blame the immigrants”.




We saw this really vividly after Hurricane Helene, a tropical storm that hit Appalachia. Trump and Elon Musk were going around saying “FEMA has no money for you because the Democrats spent it on immigrants.” So they use the hurricane to advance the Great Replacement Conspiracy. It’s an amazing pivot to go from a storm destroying tens of thousands of houses to say, “the problem is the globalists are importing immigrants to replace you”. But it’s working.




People have been warning for many years about ecofascism being the consequence of climate change. Ecofascism is the consequence of decades of denial, not just from the far-right, but by liberals who insisted that we could address this crisis through market policies that were doomed to fail.




It’s absolutely criminally irresponsible to not talk about climate change right now because that will create a vacuum for this pivot from the real arsonists to the immigrant victims. And we need to insist on robust climate policies. Not just renewables. It’s investments in care work and in all sorts of low carbon important initiatives. It needs to be at the centre of our politics.




There was a time when liberals could think people will stop denying climate change when they experience it firsthand. We’re seeing that is not true. People in that state of vulnerability and shock are more susceptible to strongmen and scapegoating, and we need to be right there with a different plan and a different story.




MS:

 

In the book you talk about

 

a number of site fights and bright spots, one of them being the AI data centre backlash. What is the importance of AI data centre fights in defeating end times fascism? Can these fights be sites of expansion for movements to touch on other issues as well?




AT:

 The data centre fight is an amazing opportunity to weave together all of these issues that we know are interconnected. People aren’t fighting data centres in their backyard for just one reason. They are fighting them because they care about their air and water, because they don’t want a future where all the jobs are gone and every bit of economically valuable work, as OpenAI calls it, is performed by robots. It’s also a democracy fight. These data centres are coming in under the cover of non-disclosure agreements, often with little input from even the city council and no input from the community.




But it’s more than that. There’s such intensive capital, like borrowing on capital markets right now. That’s part of why interest rates are being jacked up around the world, which increases the cost of borrowing for ordinary people. Rates are going up, it’s making homes more unaffordable. The fact that the population is buried by debt is a huge part of what drove Flávio Bolsonaro’s surge in recent months.




All of these factors are compounding, and so it would be foolish for environmentalists not to intervene and try to connect those those dots. The data centre fight has to be connected to affordability.




MS:

 

In Canada, our Prime Minister Mark Carney is a former investment banker who Naomi recently referred to as the ‘paragon of liberalism’. He’s privatizing key pieces of Canadian infrastructure, doubling down on fossil fuels, other extractive projects, and AI, while using the language of standing up to Trump. His approval ratings are incredibly high. How are we to understand this?




AT:

 Naomi might call him a paragon of liberalism. I call him 

Sir banks a lot

. I don’t trust bankers, especially those who are committed to the kind of neoliberalism and financialization that he’s proposing.




It’s dangerous to say “peer into the window, asset managers of the world. Canada has lots of resources that you can purchase and we have a healthcare system that can still be privatized and higher education system that still has some public funding that we could siphon off to the private sector.”




These are the policies and conditions that created fertile terrain for the far-right. Carney does not seem to have learned that lesson. It was striking when he gave that speech at Davos, about there being a rupture. The world was so ready for Canada to lead, and to project onto that speech that he was actually standing up for true universalism and for international law.




Instead he’s doing this nostalgic hyper-nationalist neoliberalism that isn’t really nationalist, because it was reported by the the 

Toronto Star

 that the amount of money going to [the] American tech sector from the Department of National Defense has doubled in the last year. He’s spending Canadian money to enrich the very companies that are behind Trump. You cannot fight oligarchy with oligarchy. You definitely can’t fight fascism with oligarchy. You fight it with solidarity and with democratic socialism, with addressing the root crises.




People want to believe that this figure can protect them when the truth is protection is in building collective power and insisting on a deep economic and political transformation. What he’s doing is incredibly dangerous. And the fact that he’s rolling back already weak climate policies when Canada’s main export is wildfire smoke, is just incredibly insulting and incredibly dangerous. The world needs Canada to stand firm against fascism.




MS:

 

You talk about the power of stories, and detail the stories that the end times fascists are telling.

 

What’s a counter story that’s been missing?




AT:

 In the book we talk about how we need to tell stories not of end times but of better times. We are entering a period where there are going to be roiling crises. We need to figure out how to live together well under these conditions.




I think we need stories that just remind us of how critical this fight is and that ground us in a love of this world. Naomi and I want stories that connect people to that, that remind people that we do live in a planetary paradise. It’s worth defending.




Ultimately, the organizer in me says we need more than stories. I think it’s incumbent on all of us to try to find a political home, to face the fact that fascism is not something that we can fight alone, we can only fight it together. If there’s not something for you to join, where you live, then start something … It takes not just stories, but actions, however imperfect, however small, however inadequate, but when we all take them, it adds up.




End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 can be ordered in 

Canada

, the 

U.S.

 And 

UK

.




The post 

How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power

 appeared first on 

DeSmog

.

author: Unknown
title: Bottom-Up Organizing: How We Got Clean Porta-Johns
content:
The first day I showed up on the Marriott construction site in downtown Detroit, everyone warned me about the state of our bathrooms. 




You could smell them halfway across most floors. They were full in 24 hours, urinals were often clogged, and some people had taken to using buckets and hiding them in closets. 




Every electrician already had the same idea: we wanted the cleaning schedule changed from twice a week to three times.




I had a long conversation with the steward about what had been tried. The first instinct of a construction worker is to “drag” (quit), drive over to the union hall, and pick up a new job. As expected, there was a steady trickle of drags, but no improvement to conditions.




OSHA had been called and walked the site, only to say that the number of bathrooms was up to their standard. The electrical contractor had been notified, but because the bathrooms were for all the trades, our bosses didn’t feel it was their responsibility to pay for additional cleaning. 




Our Electrical Workers (IBEW) Local 58 contract only gestures vaguely to “sanitary facilities,” and protects us explicitly should we leave the site to find a “sanitary” facility. This clause was exercised regularly, but no one could say for sure whether the boss was even aware we were leaving.




A PLAN IS HATCHED




I was asked to fill in for the steward while he was out for a few days. When I walked the job to make sure everyone had my number, more than half the conversations touched on the bathrooms. I then introduced myself to the stewards from other trades, who were all hearing the same from their members.




We hatched the idea to take the issue above our bosses and straight to the general contractor (who hires out each trade and is responsible for the job site at large).




Together we wrote a letter titled “Unacceptable Bathroom Conditions,” which opened politely and assumed the boss was ignorant of the problem. The letter referenced the impact on our work and a widespread feeling that we were not being treated with respect.




We reminded him that many of us had decades of experience and were not new to the idea of using a plastic box as a bathroom, but these conditions were exceptionally bad. 




We suggested that the person responsible for scheduling should use our bathrooms for a week to better assess the need for more cleanings, hand sanitizer, and a wash station. We gave one week for a response.




BUT WILL IT WORK?




Every worker who was presented with the letter signed immediately. Most people felt like the bosses would just laugh at our demands, but were interested in the idea of swarming their trailer at lunch and forcing them to read it in front of us.




We fielded many suggestions, from going straight home after delivering the letter to tipping over porta-johns on our way. We told our co-workers that if our response date came and went without change, we would be coming back around “to have a different conversation.” 




But first the demand had to be made collectively and clearly. Many of our one-on-one talks were focused on assuring the workers that we would escalate if the letter went ignored: “This is only the beginning.”




We warned people about possible counter-strategies from the boss, and stressed the importance of demonstrating solidarity, especially across the trades. We didn’t invite the officers at the union hall or our reps, though we did inform them. “Every member is a steward” has become sort of a slogan for us.




IT WORKS




In the end we had 105 signatures and roughly 35 folks across four trades who gave up their lunch break to deliver the letter. The contractor read it, was brought outside to look at us, and immediately conceded to our terms.




Maybe they didn’t know how bad the bathrooms were, maybe they didn’t know how widely and deeply felt the issue was on site, or maybe they figured it was fine to ignore.




All we know for sure is, when even a fraction of us came together, with the backing of three times as many signatures, it didn’t matter if we had the union hall behind us. We are the union, the working people who don’t just walk away from a job which doesn’t satisfy us, and our demands have been met. 




Kevin Szczesny is a member of IBEW Local 58 (Electrical Workers) in Detroit. A version of this story first appeared in his union newsletter.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Israel Tries to Poach UK Doctors to Work on Illegally Occupied Land
content:
An Israeli government agency is encouraging doctors in London to emigrate to Israel and the occupied West Bank to compensate for a domestic brain drain amid the ongoing genocide and increased restrictions on the number of Palestinian doctors in its healthcare system. 




A medical fair, MedEx UK, was hosted in London last Sunday by the Israeli Ministry of Aliyah and Integration, alongside Zionist groups Nefesh B’Nefesh and the Jewish Agency for Israel, Middle East Eye reported. 




Attendees were invited to meet Israeli hospital representatives at the event and take on site Hebrew language tests required to obtain Israeli medical licences. 




Leaflets from medical providers Terem and Clalit, which operate in illegal West Bank settlements, were offered to guests. Representatives from Leumit Health Services, which 

claims to run 30 establishments

 in the occupied West Bank, were included on a list of attendees seen by Middle East Eye. 




“They had a lot of very eminent professors there. They were only there for the day, and flew back the next day,” said an activist who infiltrated the event. They added that representatives for Clalit told guests: “Truly wherever you want to go in Israel, we can help with accommodation.”




Sunday’s MedEx event was held as part of a years-long drive to bring 2,000 doctors to Israel by 2029 as increasing numbers of its doctors go abroad. Some 

1,369 medics left Israel 

between 2023 and 2025, marking a fivefold increase over the previous decade.




The drive to recruit British doctors also comes as the Israeli Ministry of Health intensifies its efforts to exclude Palestinian medics. In 2019, the government brought in new restrictions on the number of foreign medical schools whose graduates are allowed to sit Israel’s licensing exams. Students from occupied Palestine cannot enrol in Israeli medical schools, forcing them abroad, whilst Palestinian citizens of Israel face structural barriers to entry. 




At the same time, the Israeli government has introduced financial incentives and streamlined processes aimed at attracting suitable foreign doctors. In 2025, it was announced that doctors with 10 years of experience could waive Israel’s licensing exam, down from 14 years.




The number of Palestinian doctors in Israel has skyrocketed in the last decade, with almost 45% of newly licensed medics categorised as “Arab and Druze” in 2023. But this number is expected to plummet as Palestinian doctors who started studying at foreign medical schools in 2019 are no longer considered eligible to practice in Israel.

author: Paige Collings
title: Tech Tips for Parents this Digital Parenting Week
content:
In today’s digital world, the internet is an 

essential resource

 for young people to access information, explore community, and find themselves. But we know that this often comes alongside fears of experiencing online harms like doxxing, grooming, or bullying.




Trying to protect your family from everything all the time is impractical and exhausting, but some thoughtful planning can help families devise a workable plan that meets their needs and addresses their concerns.




That’s why this Digital Parent Week, we’re sharing easy tips on how parents and their children can work together to co-curate a digital safety plan that helps all members of the family enjoy the benefits of technology while protecting their online privacy and safety. 




Start with Open Conversations




Online safety begins with communication, not just restrictions. Talk with a young person about how they use the internet: their favourite apps, games, and social media platforms for example. Creating a supportive environment helps young people feel comfortable asking for help if something goes wrong online.




Together, you can think about:







What do we want to protect? 

e.g., I want to protect a young person’s privacy and mental health when they’re playing Roblox. They love Roblox and use it to communicate and hang out with their best friend, so we’d like to find a way to make it as safe as possible.




Who do we want to protect it from?

 e.g., messages from strangers, staying up too late playing, wasting money on pointless digital junk in games.




How bad are the consequences if we fail? 

e.g, losing some money on a scam or having creepy conversations with strangers that could escalate into something more nefarious or dangerous.




How likely is it that we will need to protect it? 

e.g., I don’t know the likelihood of a stranger messaging you on Roblox because I’m not sure how communication works on the platform, but I’ve heard from their friends that strangers message them all the time in some games.




How much trouble are we willing to go through to try to prevent potential consequences? 

e.g., I’m willing to learn from my child how the game works, play the game with my child, and learn how to work the parental controls. 




Who are our allies?

 e.g., my partner, our parents, as well as a young person’s best friends and their parents.







It's easy to think of a young person's experience on the internet as being totally disconnected and different from your own. But now is a great time to also interrogate your own internet habits, like the sorts of sites you engage with, tools you use, and privacy settings you've set. These questions are as valuable to help you as a parent as they are just an internet user.




Sometimes even just figuring out what conversations are worth having can take some effort, we've put together some ideas to get you started in 

our guide

.




Make Privacy a Family Priority




Digital security training can feel overwhelming but this is why a 

community-oriented approach

 helps. In speaking with your family and friends, you can build out digital security practices that work for you. This makes it more likely that your privacy practices will become second nature to you and your loved ones.




Use secure messaging services for every communication:

 Choosing a secure service ensures that your privacy is protected from government and corporate surveillance. If you can convince your family to get on board, options like Signal provide the most extensive privacy protections out of the box through its use of end-to-end encryption and limited data collection. But we understand that sometimes it's easier to stick with whatever the family already uses for a group chat, like WhatsApp, Apple's iMessage, or Google Messages, so take the time to familiarize yourself with the 

limits of WhatsApp

 and 

RCS encryption

.




Consider the content posted online: 

It's easy to accidentally share personal information through photos, messages, and other content.

 

Children and adults may unknowingly share personal information through photos, messages, location settings and app permissions. Take time together to review privacy settings, check which apps can access the camera or location, and discuss why personal details should be shared carefully. Make sure you have family agreement about when and where to post photos of each other or your home.




Create incident response plans: 

Developing a plan for if or when something bad happens is a good practice for anyone, but especially with younger people. It’s important to strategize with your family around what to do in the event of such things happening, and doing so before an incident occurs is much easier than when you’re presently facing a crisis.




Alongside this, simple steps like using strong and unique passwords on all devices, including those that are shared in the family, can make a real difference. Regardless of age, there’s no time like the present to get started on good security hygiene, and for many that starts with a 

password manager

 and 

two-factor authentication

.




How to Think About Parental Controls




Many sites permit parents to control features such as personalization, algorithmic feed, autoplay, endless scroll, reactions, notifications, and time limits. Talk as a family about which features are important and useful and which are problematic. The conversations above around boundaries and digital literacy are a more effective way to prepare youth for accessing the internet. To develop true autonomy, young people need the privacy to discover the world for themselves without their parents monitoring the contents of every conversation they have.




Explore new apps together and revisit family rules as they grow. These decision points where you’re exploring with a young person what you’re both comfortable with can be good moments to “find your way to a yes” for whatever feature or tool or game they’re asking about. The questions they ask, along with your responses, provide a road map for what to look for in privacy controls that can get you to a place where everyone is comfortable engaging with that technology. 




Small Steps = Big Difference




There is no one size fits all to the tech questions and concerns a parent will face, and keeping young people safe online is not about removing every risk and monitoring every click. This Digital Parenting Week, you can start to focus on what’s important for your family and how to best achieve those goals. 




If you're still not sure where to start, installing EFF’s Privacy Badger on every computer in your household is a great starting point to protecting everyone's privacy.




For more detailed information on all these tips and more, visit 

EFF’s Online Privacy Guide

 for Parents and Youth.

author: Andrea DiP
title: Solidão “premium”: como redes sociais e consumo transformam estar só em desejo
content:
No Pauta Pública desta semana, Andrea Dip recebe Lucas Liedke e André Alves, psicanalistas, pesquisadores e fundadores da Float Vibes, instituto de estudos culturais e pesquisa comportamental. Apresentadores do podcast Vibes em Análise, eles discutem como as redes sociais transformam a noção de coletividade e de individualidade e como as empresas por trás dessas plataformas se beneficiam da solidão. Para Lucas, o consumidor solitário tende a ser mais rentável para o mercado. 




Segundo um 

relatório

 da Organização Mundial da Saúde, uma em cada seis pessoas no mundo se sente sozinha, com impactos significativos na saúde e no bem-estar. Para os entrevistados, as redes sociais prometem conexão e pertencimento, mas também podem intensificar o avanço da solidão entre as pessoas e transformar em espetáculo. “Quem filma a solidão […] no limite também está colocando a câmera como testemunha, ou a suposta audiência como testemunha… um artifício para não estar exatamente sozinho”, resume André Alves. Para Lucas Liedke, este é exatamente o ponto de atenção, já que as plataformas lucram com essa dinâmica. “O imaginário divertido e hipersocial das mídias sociais pode ser opressor”.




As redes sociais não só contribuem para este fenômeno como podem transformá-lo em uma espécie de espetáculo. 




Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.























































EP 239


											A solidão “premium” – com Vibes em Análise							













23 de outubro de 2026


					·
				


				Psicanalistas do Vibes em Análise falam sobre o aumento da solidão e como as redes transformaram a ideia de coletividade





























































0:00




-:–



















15




15
































































Veja mais episódios desta série










Vocês escreveram esse texto, Solidão Premium, que é uma análise sobre muitos temas que se entrelaçam. Então pra começar, o que é a solidão premium?




Lucas Liedke:

 A discussão sobre solidão vem acontecendo enquanto sintoma global há algum tempo. Com certeza com mais força há uns cinco anos, a partir da pandemia, do trabalho remoto, do isolamento social. Alguns fenômenos que já eram uma realidade, mas que foram ganhando expansão, se tornando uma necessidade e nós sabemos que muitas pessoas nunca conseguiram voltar ao que era antes.




No Japão tem esse fenômeno do 

hikikomori

, que são os indivíduos que não saem de casa, de forma alguma, e ficam nesse confinamento extremo. Na China, a gente viu o lançamento de um aplicativo, que tem um nome bastante macabro, que é 

Você Está Morto?

, onde as pessoas são convidadas a fazer um check-in a cada dois dias para mostrar para as outras que elas ainda estão vivas.




Nesse contexto, a gente começou a perceber um movimento também de influenciadores de solidão. Pessoas que afirmam ter um um orgulho de não ter uma família próxima, de não ter muitos amigos, de passar um sábado à noite sozinho em casa, assistindo o que quiser no streaming, comendo o que quiser no delivery, sem ter que negociar os seus gostos, as suas escolhas com ninguém. E isso é um contraste curioso para as redes sociais, que sempre foi um lugar mais de expor o quanto você é sociável, o quanto você se diverte, as suas conexões, enquanto uma espécie de capital social. Essa contradição foi o que nos levou a escrever esse texto “Solidão Premium”.




André Alves:

 Tem o famoso relatório da 

OMS de 2025

 sobre como uma em cada seis pessoas no mundo se sente afetada pela solidão. Sob à luz da psicanálise – que é o campo de onde a gente parte – a definição da solidão parte de uma espécie de déficit relacional. “Eu não tenho quantitativamente e ou qualitativamente relações suficientes na minha vida”. Claro que nunca a gente tem a suficiência na psicanálise, a gente está sempre trabalhando exatamente com ausências e faltas, mas no caso da epidemia de solidão, é algo que diz sobre faltar demais, sobre eu não ter relações profundas o suficiente, e/ou pessoas o suficiente na minha vida com quem eu possa trocar e que considerem a minha dor como algo importante.




A Solidão Premium, da qual a gente tem falado e esse texto que o Lucas escreveu, parte da ideia de que, no estado atual desse movimento, a gente tem observado muitos criadores de conteúdo, e não só, mas também outras áreas da cultura e da vida de uma forma geral, promovendo uma espécie de estetização da solidão. Um 

rebranding

 da solidão: a solidão passando a ser algo ou um estado não só difícil, vergonhoso, culposo, negativo, mas também como um estado aspiracional, algo que eu quero ter na minha vida, pertencer, e acho que dá para a gente falar, inclusive, um pouco sobre como o consumo afeta essa história.




Lucas Liedke:

 Porque essa solidão espetacularizada, o quanto ela é uma escolha? Ou o quanto que é tentar se contentar com o que tem, ou com o que não tem. Porque talvez o que a gente tenha perdido, muitos de nós, não seja só a proximidade com os outros, mas a capacidade e o desejo de se relacionar. Então, nesse espetáculo tem algo meio contraditório, que é você pode estar disposto a não ter mais o valor das relações interpessoais, mas, ao mesmo tempo, tem um gozo em possuir uma audiência e agradar uma audiência, que está validando ali a sua vida solitária, mas que está cheia de prazeres e que custa caro. Como o André falou, ela é aspiracional. Tem uma ostentação, tem um luxo de um certo consumo de que é: “eu estou sozinho, mas eu sou feliz aqui no meu castelo”.



















Lucas Liedke e André Alves, psicanalistas, pesquisadores e fundadores da Float Vibes, instituto de estudos culturais e pesquisa comportamental







Sobre essa ideia da solidão performada;

 

de que solidão estamos falando, quando uma pessoa monta um esquema para se filmar curtindo estar sozinha, para depois apresentar para as pessoas e esperar delas curtidas e comentários? De que tipo de solidão estamos falando quando pensamos nessa solidão performática para o outro?




André Alves:

 Eu vou trazer três autores para pensarmos a solidão. O 

Winnicott

, psicanalista britânico, tem um texto muito importante, do final dos anos 50, em que ele fala sobre a capacidade de estar só, sobre como a solidão ou a solitude é um estado conquistado. A criança aprende a estar só. Primeiro com os cuidadores observando a criança brincar sozinha, e depois a criança vai integrando essa capacidade de estar feliz em sua própria companhia, ou satisfeita minimamente na sua própria companhia.




Vamos guardar essa informação. Tem uma outra autora que é pouco falada quando se discute solidão – pelo menos nas minhas andanças por aí – que é a 

Melanie Klein

. Já no final de sua obra, tem um texto em que ela descreve a solidão muito ligada a uma nostalgia de um estado perfeito de compreensão total, que nunca existiu mas é a fantasia da relação sem palavras com o objeto primário. A fantasia de que há um outro que me entende completamente, totalmente e me suporta integralmente.




Eu trouxe esses dois autores porque os dois estão falando, de alguma forma, desse ambiente perfeito. E a gente não anda muito bom de desidealizar as coisas. Pelo contrário, a gente anda muito bom de ideais saturados. É o que o consumo especialmente nos promove ou nos promete, né. É exatamente o ambiente perfeito. A casa que ela tem é maravilhosa a ponto de você não querer sair mais dela. Ela faz total sentido, ela reflete todos os seus gostos, né. Esse ambiente de conveniência máxima como se fosse um ambiente perfeito. Que a gente sabe, não existe, mas ao mesmo tempo parece que o consumo tem ficado especialmente bom em nos convencer do contrário.




E aí entra a viralidade e o conteúdo promovendo essa repetição em 

loop

. Eu falei que eram três autores, e acho que tem um terceiro autor importante também da psicanálise britânica, que é o 

Christopher Bollas

, que tem uma grande obra também no século XXI, de como o que a gente busca no consumo é o que o bebê geralmente busca na mãe. Não só um objeto, mas uma experiência de transformação. É isso que o consumo nos promete. “Use isso, tenha isso, viva isso, e você sairá dessa muito melhor, transformado, muito mais aspiracional, inclusive”. É como se a conveniência entrasse também como uma suplantação da carência e de uma constante presença.




Por que a gente tem visto tantos 

creators

 ou criadores de conteúdo falando sobre solidão? Exatamente para remontar esse ambiente perfeito e idealizado, colocar nos objetos e nessa casa perfeita cheia de coisas incríveis a ideia de experiência de transformação ou de preservação, e três, uma fala constante e ininterrupta sobre solidão exatamente para não ter que experimentar a solidão. Porque quem filma a solidão ou transforma a solidão em espetáculo – como o Lucas estava dizendo – também está colocando a câmera como testemunha, ou a suposta audiência como testemunha como também um artifício para não estar exatamente sozinho.




Lucas Liedke:

 Existem dados 

científicos

 de como o sentimento de solidão atua como um fator de risco para a nossa saúde, tanto quanto ser sedentário, quanto obesidade, ou tabagismo. Tem até essa ideia de que a solidão é considerada tão prejudicial à saúde quanto fumar 

15 cigarros

 por dia. Mas a solidão é bem subjetiva, você pode estar cercado de muita gente, ainda assim se sentir só, ou o contrário. Então, é claro que não é tanto sobre estar sozinho apenas por opção, mas ter a opção de sair do isolamento quando você quer ou precisa.




Então vale a gente problematizar um pouco que o imaginário divertido e hipersocial das mídias sociais pode ser opressor. Mas a gente também pode demonizar uma vida solitária, assim como romantizar um sentimento de solidão. A gente enxerga que são dois becos sem saída porque tem um empuxo muito do nosso tempo hoje do hiper indivíduo de um grande projeto de se auto-otimizar. E aí as relações nem sempre ajudam nisso, porque você tem que abrir mão de alguma coisa. Precisa se adaptar, quebrar sua rotina, sacrificar alguma coisa. E aí o outro produz um tipo de diferença, ou de atrito, ou de imprevisibilidade nos seus planos. E aí quem entrega essa vida “social” sem fricção é a economia da companhia artificial. A inteligência artificial enquanto essa solução para um problema que foi criado pelas próprias tecnologias.




Não podemos deixar de lado como essa solidão serve ao capitalismo neoliberal, a individualização extrema. Por um lado, a libido tem que estar totalmente investida no trabalho, porque estamos sendo esmagados o tempo inteiro por demandas e não tem mais separação do trabalho para casa, nem fisicamente, nem na nossa cabeça. E aí quais os impactos dessa ideia que os vínculos interpessoais podem oferecer risco para o grande projeto de auto-otimização do super indivíduo?




Lucas Liedke:

 Tem um tratado do jornalista 

Derek Thompson

 que ele chama de século antissocial. Ele fala por esse viés mais do consumo, de a quem que interessa a gente ficar mais e mais sozinhos. Porque mesmo os aplicativos de relacionamento são projetados de forma que você continue lá. Eles não querem perder esses clientes e consumidores. 




O consumidor solitário tende a ser mais rentável para o mercado. São as porções menores e mais caras, é mais embalagem, tem mais transações individuais. A gente tem hoje uma análise de dados também, de algoritmo, que funciona de um jeito muito menos genérico, – como era a visão demográfica do consumidor – hoje, é muito singular, muito específico. E a gente vai sendo suprido com muita conveniência, como se isso desse conta da complexidade do nosso afeto e das nossas carências.




André Alves:

 O 

Bumble

 lançou esse ano o concierge de IA. Você não precisa mais conversar com 10, 50, 100 pessoas até achar uma pessoa que seria “perfeita”. Porque a gente sabe que o trabalho relacional começa exatamente depois do encontro, e não necessariamente no encontro perfeito, do objeto perfeito que vai satisfazer todas as suas necessidades. E aí o concierge de IA, na verdade, filtra quem são as três pessoas perfeitas. Depois, os concierges de IA vão conversar entre si para encontrar a sua probabilidade perfeita.




Então, é um sintoma social, da mediação relacional e também da comunicação assíncrona, de uma quantidade muito grande de ansiedades sociais, da evitação do conflito e principalmente – do que a gente no Instituto Float Vibes, que eu e o Lucas temos – chamamos de era das intimidades sintéticas. A gente fica acostumado demais não com as relações, mas com aquilo que é “sabor-relação”, que me dá o simulacro de relação o simulacro de comunidade, pegando um termo do Zygmunt Bauman.




Outra coisa que eu acho interessante pensar, bem fisheriano, é como essa relação é um golpe de mestre do capitalismo tardio. Primeiro, ele degrada a coletividade e depois nos vende ela de volta, só que com mensalidades, com grupos, com clubes. E aí nós vamos tentando reintegrar a nossa necessidade de fazer pontes e de pertencer através de serviços pagos. Só que, junto com isso, há uma tese em curso que ganha força – especialmente no final dos anos 80 e nos anos 90 –, de que o sucesso é uma questão de disciplina e especialmente de dedicação. Thompson, citado por Lucas, escreveu bastante sobre como o trabalho suplanta a ausência de religiosidade e espiritualidade desse período, consequentemente, o trabalho vira um sistema de devoção. 




Porque se o sujeito contemporâneo, do hiper desempenho, acredita que o sucesso é uma questão de disciplina, as relações vão se transformando em distrações. A relação tem um risco especialmente para os homens, como temos acompanhado em alguns estudos que temos feito e publicado. As relações vão sendo encaradas não mais como algo que você tem que fazer para pertencer ao meio social, mas sim, algo que você pode evitar para continuar comprometido com o seu projeto de sucesso e ascensão.

author: Anonym
title: Génération Niketout¹
content:
„Uns bleiben noch ein paar Gramm Leben, und wir werden alles geben“

Was lachen wir doch gut in euren tristen Straßen angesichts eurer bestürzten Gesichter beim Anblick unserer Lagerfeuer. Versteht uns nicht falsch, liebe Zuschauer, in unseren Handlungen steckt viel Angst, mehr als Verzweiflung oder Hass. Jeder Ausbruch von Unruhen ist ein Würfelwurf direkt ins Gesicht eurer Republik. Wir wissen, dass es hart werden wird, und wir nehmen den offenen Konflikt in Kauf.

Wir wissen nicht, was die Zukunft bringen wird, und wir ahnen, dass die dunklen Tage nur mehr werden. Wir wissen nicht einmal, gegen was oder wen wir uns aufregen sollen, und eure Bullen sind uns scheißegal.

Die Macht ist unpersönlich, also werden wir alles zerstören, auch wenn wir verstanden haben, dass die Gebäude, die die Bullen schützen, und die gesicherten städtischen Gebiete genau die Orte sind, an die man gehen muss. Wir werden nicht aufhören, solange eure Bullen oder eure Soldaten uns nicht mit Kugeln beschießen … und wir ahnen sehr wohl, dass es bald aus dem Ruder laufen wird – es läuft bereits aus dem Ruder.

Wir wissen nur, dass in eurem beschissenen System etwas nicht stimmt und dass es den Bach runtergeht. Wir haben einfach keine Lust, mit ihm unterzugehen, und wir werden alles geben. Kennst du dieses Gefühl, bei dem sich ein Knoten im Magen bildet und man vor lauter Beklemmung am liebsten aus voller Kehle schreien möchte? Dein Beton? Deine Kameras? Deine Bullen? Deine Anordnungen? Deine Werbung? Deine beschissene Zukunft? Das muss es sein – wir brauchen Luft.

Wir, die Niemande, die kleinen Nervensägen, die Pissköpfe, die Hungerleider, ‘les shlags’ [2], die „Autonomen“, die „Ultra-Linken“, die Randalierer, das Gesindel – an diesen Demonstrationstagen lassen wir all diese Frustration raus.

An Tagen, an denen es nach Tränengas riecht, befreit uns das vom Dogma; es lässt uns leben, wenn wir spüren, dass alles ins Wanken gerät. Die blassen Gesichter deiner Marionetten im Fernsehen, die die Worte der Machthaber nachplappern, sagen uns viel über den Verfall deiner Marionettenrepublik aus. Jetzt wissen wir, dass deine Festungen nicht uneinnehmbar sind! Und je öfter sich die Bilder wiederholen, desto mehr wird uns klar, dass wir kurz davor stehen, alles in die Luft zu jagen.

Auf der Straße lieben wir uns nicht besonders. Wir sind keine „Genossen“ oder „Brüder“ oder sonstiger linker Quatsch dieser Art, aber dieses verrottete System hat uns an denselben Ort gebracht, zu denselben Praktiken und mit einer gewissen Piraten-Komplizenschaft in deiner Welt, und wir alle teilen eine gewisse Vorliebe für Piraterie und den Wunsch nach einem Tapetenwechsel.

Es stimmt, dass wir ein paar Beutezüge nicht verschmähen, die wie eine kleine Belohnung für die Risiken sind, die wir eingehen. Aber mit drei Lacoste-Poloshirts und einem Paar TN-Schuhen werden wir noch lange nicht zur Ruhe kommen. Das macht uns nur etwas weniger nervös und gibt uns das Gefühl, ein bisschen in deiner Stadt mitgearbeitet zu haben, die uns das ganze Jahr über Waren vor Augen führt, die wir uns nicht oft leisten können.

Es ist Weihnachten! Und wie so oft nach den Feiertagen ist der Kater am nächsten Tag heftig, weil sich eigentlich nichts geändert hat. Wenn der Adrenalinschub vorbei ist, sagt man sich, dass man es besser hätte machen können und dass der nächste Aufstand der wirkliche sein wird. Man fragt sich sogar, wann man vor deinen Smith-Agenten [3] nicht mehr fliehen muss.

Live vom Ende der Welt – oder besser gesagt: von dieser Welt – werden wir weiterhin ganz gemächlich Chaos stiften und dort zuschlagen, wo ihr uns am wenigsten erwartet.

Fürchtest du immer noch um deinen Platz in diesem verrotteten System? Du glaubst noch ein bisschen daran, oder? Gib’s zu! Stellst du dir vor, wie du in 10, 20, 30 Jahren gemütlich deine Rentenbeiträge zahlst, für einen Platz an der Sonne, um Krebs oder Krieg zu entkommen? Wenn du immer noch an diesen ganzen Mist glaubst, dann haben sie dich gut reingelegt und du bist erledigt. Du bist nur eine kleine Schachfigur in der Reservearmee der bestehenden Ordnung, du bist reif für die Gaskammer der Banker à la „Soylent Green” [4], den Krematoriumsofen des Kapitals, das Lager des Konsums von Leclerc! [5] Und wir wollen nicht so enden wie du! Mit der Kraft unserer kleinen Schwärme, ohne Strategien und völlig unorganisiert, haben wir seit 2018 mit den Gelbwesten verstanden, dass wir die Oberhand gewinnen und dich destabilisieren können. Tausende von Schwärmen, die von überall her zuschlagen. Wir mussten uns an diesem 17. Oktober wiederfinden und unsere Entschlossenheit erkennen. Und jetzt, wo alles in Flammen steht, wird es nicht an Gelegenheiten mangeln, die Widerstandsfähigkeit deiner Mauern auf die Probe zu stellen. Die Praxis des Aufruhrs, die Gesten des Aufruhrs, die Kleidung des Aufruhrs sind mittlerweile allseits verbreitet. Schwarze Jogginghosen liegen für alle im Trend! Machen wir weiter so und vertrauen wir auf diese Intelligenz der Massen – sie haben gezeigt, dass sie ohne nachzudenken verstehen, wie der Schwarmflug der Stare. Eine Kultur des „Zbeul“ [6] ist mittlerweile fest verankert, die über die Kleidung und die Botschaften an den Wänden hinausgeht und in Wirklichkeit die Negation in Aktion ist, die wieder an die Oberfläche kommt. Sie lässt sich nicht vereinnahmen, denn sie ist ein Vatermord an den früheren Generationen, vom Typ Bernard Tapie, dem „Golden Boy“ mit der Zigarette im Mundwinkel und der Sorglosigkeit der Kaufhäuser. Wir rächen uns an diesem Erbe, das uns Leukämie und 50 °C im Sommer bescheren wird. All euer zurückgelassener Mist ist doch ein paar brennende Barrikaden wert, oder? Aber genau das verspricht weitere schöne historische „Erschütterungen“ oder sogar revolutionär gesehen interessante Momente. Es bedarf weder eines Handbuchs noch eines Plans bzw. eines Maximo Leaders, um die gesichtslosen Massen zu lenken. Denn ob Geschäfte nun zerstört werden oder nicht: Das Übel der Demokratie betrifft den größten Teil der Jugend, die nicht mehr daran glaubt und die in drei Wochen Blockaden intensiver gelebt hat als in einem ganzen Jahr in deinem klimatisierten Kerker, sei es die Schule, die Uni oder der Scheißjob. Sich also eine Sturmhaube überzuziehen und Sachen kaputtzumachen, ohne etwas zu erwarten, ist wie ein Training für das, was uns erwartet. Die Barrikade ist die Fortsetzung der Blockade, die wiederum die Fortsetzung jahrelangen, einsamen Schimpfens auf der Schulbank ist … nur dass wir jetzt zu vielen auf der Straße sind, die keine Forderungen mehr haben und unter keinem Banner demonstrieren. Unsere einzige Parole: Das Feuer. Unsere Generation weiß, dass sie nicht einmal den kleinsten Krümel von den Früchten deines widerwärtigen Systems ernten wird. Man muss „Das Kapital“ nicht mehr lesen, um zu verstehen, dass uns die Widersprüche der Wirtschaft langfristig alle umbringen werden und dass wir am Ende angelangt sind, lieber Fernsehzuschauer! Die „Métro Terre“ erreicht ihre Endstation! Jetzt, da die faulen Früchte deines Marktes unsere Körper und unseren Geist, unser Leben und unseren gespenstischen Alltag direkt vergiften, brauchen wir keine verworrenen Erklärungen und keine deutsche Fachsprache mehr. Wir erleben es am eigenen Leib, und es zehrt an uns, es ermüdet uns, es nervt uns, es macht uns krank, es tötet uns und unsere Angehörigen … Wir haben die Lektion verstanden, aber wir haben auch erkannt, dass es Schwachstellen gibt. Diese werden wir also ausnutzen, solange wir noch in dieser beschissenen Welt leben müssen. Die ‘génération Niketout’ ist nichts anderes als ein Überlebensakt einer Bevölkerung, die keine falschen Träume mehr zum Festhalten hat: „Demokratie“, „Kaufkraft“, „Lebenserwartung“, „Rente“, „Zukunft“ sind zu Running Gags geworden, die Politikern und Gewerkschaften über die Lippen kommen. Die ‘génération Niketout’ weiß, dass der Kuchen bereits gegessen wurde und dass er vergiftet war; daher hat sie nichts mehr zu verlieren, sie hat keinen Hunger mehr, sie will einfach nur leben. Die ‘génération Niketout’ wird keine Hilfe von Papa Staat oder Mama Wirtschaft bekommen, also verlässt sie sich nur auf sich selbst. Die génération Niketout’ ist ein Fehler. Aber ein Fehler, der euch um die Ohren fliegen wird! Schöne Albträume für die nächsten Jahre. Egal, wer wir sind – was zählt, ist, was wir tun werden. Eigentlich unübersetzbar erschließt sich die Überschrift hoffentlich mit diesen Anmerkungen dem deutschen Leser. 2. “les shlags” – bedeutet sowohl soviel wie die Verwahrlosten, Unangepassten (Kleidungsstil betreffend) als auch ‘lost’ sein, verpeilt. 3. author: nodes of resistance
title: Rechenzentren, „KI“ und Strategien für emanzipatorischen Widerstand
content:
Im Vorfeld der bundesweiten Konferenz zur Vernetzung von Widerstand gegen „KI“ und Rechenzentren. am 7.11.26 in Berlin veröffentlichen wir folgendes Diskussionspapier




Es regt sich Widerstand gegen Rechenzentren und das, wofür sie stehen. Damit dieser Widerstand möglichst weit trägt, halten wir eine Diskussion zu drei Themen für wichtig:


1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“


2) Gemeinsam kämpfen für Klima- und soziale Gerechtigkeit, gegen Faschismus und Militarisierung


3) Wirksamer Widerstand durch Vielfalt und Unberechenbarkeit




1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“




Der massive Ausbau von Rechenzentren und der Hype um „KI“ hängen unmittelbar zusammen. Denn: Der Hype um „KI“ mobilisiert die finanziellen Ressourcen und die politisch einstimmige Unterstützung für einen in Geschwindigkeit und Umfang beispiellosen Ausbau materieller Infrastruktur. Der Zusammenhang umfasst die technische, ökonomische und politische Dimension.


• Der technische Zusammenhang: Rechenzentren sind gewissermaßen die Fabriken von „KI“. Während es schon länger Rechenzentren gibt (seit dem Aufkommen von „Cloud“ als zentral verwaltete Rechenkapazitäten), macht „KI“ noch viel mehr und größere Rechenzentren erforderlich: Manche Rechenzentren dienen primär dem Training von „KI“-Modellen (diese brauchen besonders teure Halbleiter-Chips und liegen oft eher ländlich), andere primär der Inferenz, also dem Errechnen von „KI“-Outputs basierend auf trainierten Modellen (diese liegen meist möglichst nah an Internetknotenpunkten, oft urban). Rechenzentren liegen am Ende einer komplexen globalen Lieferkette: Besonders deutlich ist die erhöhte Nachfrage nach seltenen Erden und Metallen sowie nach Wasser und (fossiler) Energie, die an vielen Stellen dieser Lieferkette benötigt werden: Bei der Herstellung der Lithografiemaschinen, die wiederum nötig sind, um Chips zu produzieren zu können, die wiederum nötig sind, um ein Rechenzentrum zu betreiben. Die Infrastruktur rund um Rechenzentren und „KI“ ist seit einigen Jahren in erheblichem Aufbau und schließt zunehmend auch Endgeräte ein, deren Funktionieren an eine kontinuierliche Anbindung nicht nur an Internetkonnektivität, sondern auch an „KI“ und Cloud gebunden ist (von Heimgeräten über industrielle Produktion hin zu Kampfjets).


• Der finanzielle Zusammenhang: Der Finanzierung von Rechenzentren liegt ein quasi-religiöser Glaube an die Unausweichlichkeit und die Spekulation auf zukünftige Profitabilität von „KI“ zugrunde. „KI“-Unternehmen fahren jährlich Milliardenverluste ein, weil ihre Ausgaben in Form von Kosten von Rechenkapazitäten, Energie und Löhnen über den Einnahmen liegen. Rechenzentren sind dabei der Knotenpunkt für finanzielle Risiken: Die Chipherstellung ist (bisher) profitabel (siehe Bilanzen von Nvidia, TSMC, SK Hynix), das gleiche gilt für die Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten als Dienstleistung, die vor allem die drei Hyperscaler-Unternehmen Amazon, Microsoft und Google anbieten. Rechenzentren sitzen zwischen der Chipherstellung und der Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten und werden häufig nur angemietet von denjenigen, die dann wiederum Rechenleistung nutzen oder verkaufen. Rechenzentren sind extrem kapitalintensiv (bis zu mehreren Milliarden Euro pro Rechenzentrum) und hochspekulativ, sodass auch Menschen aus der Rechenzentrumsbranche (anonym/vertraulich) sagen: „Wer das Risiko versteht, wird nicht investieren.“ Das Risiko (also die Wahrscheinlichkeit von Verlusten) ergibt sich u.a. aus einer kurzen Lebensdauer von Chips (je nach Quelle ein, zwei oder max. sieben Jahre), der langfristigen Finanzierung von Rechenzentrumsbau (oft 15-20 Jahre), einer hohen Unsicherheit über die Verfügbarkeit und den Preis von Chips, Energie und Wasser und einer ebenfalls hohen Unsicherheit über die Nachfrage nach „KI“-Rechenkapazitäten. Diese Risiken werden aktuell immer neu verschachtelt durch komplexe Zirkelkäufe zwischen „KI“-Unternehmen, Chipherstellern und Rechenzentrumsbetreibern, was selbst Finanzanalyst*innen kritisch bewerten. Bereits seit mehreren Jahren attestieren u.a. Analyst*innen von Goldman Sachs das Vorliegen einer „Blase“.


• Der politische Zusammenhang: Die vermeintliche Unausweichlichkeit von „KI“ wird politisch verknüpft mit einem Wettbewerb um geopolitische Vorherrschaft (v.a. zwischen USA und China), einem Streben nach „Souveränität“ (z.B. durch Chipherstellung und Rechenzentren in Europa) und dem (Un-)Heilsversprechen immer mächtigerer „KI“-Modelle. Dementsprechend wird die Frage danach, ob und wofür Rechenzentren gebraucht würden, nicht gesellschaftlich diskutiert, sondern ihre Notwendigkeit wird politisch gesetzt. Zivilgesellschaftliche Organisationen stellen aktuell bestenfalls die Frage danach, ob ein geringerer Umfang oder ein nachhaltigerer Betrieb genügen könnte. Das ist unzureichend und verhindert eine Beschäftigung mit den hochpolitischen Auswirkungen von Rechenzentren und „KI“ als Brandbeschleuniger bestehender Krisen:


◦ Die Umweltzerstörung nimmt zu, denn entlang der Lieferketten (mit Minen, fossiblen Kraftwerken und Chipfabriken) werden ganze Regionen der „KI“ geopfert und für jegliches Leben vergiftet.


◦ Arbeit wird entfähigt und verdichtet, denn „KI“-Automatisierung zwingt Arbeitende im Globalen Süden in immer intensivere Ausbeutung und entwertet und entfähigt Arbeitende im Globalen Norden.


◦ Die Fähigkeit zu kollektiver Organisierung nimmt ab, denn „KI“-Modelle sind dazu gemacht, menschliche Kommunikation vorzutäuschen und soziales Miteinander zu verdrängen.


◦ Rassistische und antifeministische Kräfte werden gestärkt, denn „KI“-Modelle verstärken weiße, cis-männliche Machtverhältnisse und verringern gesellschaftliche Vielfalt, indem sie die statistischen Muster der vermeintlichen Mehrheit überhöhen. Dies gilt gleichermaßen für weitere Ausgrenzungs- und Herabsetzungsformen, wie Ableismus, Antisemitismus, …


◦ Soziale Ungleichheit wächst, denn die Gesellschaft soll Austerität und Entbehrung mittragen zugunsten einer „Blase“, die absehbare Verluste auf die Gesellschaft abwälzt.


◦ Militarisierung und Gewalt werden technologisch verstärkt und mit dem Anschein von mehr Effizienz und Präzision verharmlost.


◦ Macht und Kontrolle werden weiter konzentriert, während Rechenschaft und Verantwortung technologisch verschleiert und ausgelagert werden.


◦ Faschistische Gedankenwelten werden normalisiert durch das Streben nach einer vermeintlichen Superintelligenz, die mit eugenischen Konzepten für das Sortieren in wertvolles und unwürdiges Leben verknüpft ist.




2) Gemeinsam kämpfen für Klima- und soziale Gerechtigkeit, gegen Faschismus und Militarisierung




Die vielfache Zerstörungskraft in Form von „KI“ und Rechenzentren betrifft eine große Breite an politischen Themen. Das bedeutet, dass viele Bewegungen ihre Kräfte bündeln können im Widerstand gegen den technologischen Angriff. „KI“ und Rechenzentren sind eine der derzeit greifbarsten Manifestationen von Ungleichheit, Profitstreben und ökonomischer Macht. Damit sind sie auch eine Gelegenheit für Bewegungen, alternative, zukünftige Gesellschaftsentwürfe abseits von Markt und Privateigentum zu formulieren und zu gestalten. Viele Anstrengungen stecken noch in einem frühen Stadium, doch ihr Ineinandergreifen könnte ihnen erlauben, sich wechselseitig zu verstärken. Für folgende Bewegungen sehen wir mögliche Ansatzpunkte für Kämpfe rund um Rechenzentren und „KI“.


• Klimagerechtigkeit: Wasserverbrauch, fossile Energien, Bergbau, Flächenverbrauch, Elektroschrott sind alles mögliche Ansatzpunkte. Angesichts zunehmender Dürre in weiten Teilen Europas können zukünftige Kämpfe um die Ressource Wasser einen möglichen Schwerpunkt für Kämpfe gegen „KI“ und Rechenzentren bilden. Reformistische Kosmetik für mehr Effizienz oder „Small AI“ würde die kapitalistische Zerstörung nur stabilisieren und beschönigen.


• Soziale Gerechtigkeit: Denkbar und wünschenswert ist eine Allianz derer, die „KI“ entwickeln, derer, deren Arbeit sie ersetzen soll und derer, deren Bildung durch „KI“ sinnentlehrt wird. Es gibt bereits erste Ausdrücke von Widerstand wie kollektive Ablehnung der Nutzung von Daten für „KI“-Training und Streik gegen „KI“. Entwickler*innen können dazu beitragen, „KI“ zurückzuweisen und zu unterminieren und Universitäten können Orte des Widerstands sein durch kollektive Ablehnung von „KI“. Auch die „KI“-beschleunigte und Verantwortlichkeit verwischende Automatisierung des Sozialabbaus macht Widerspruch erforderlich.


• Antifaschismus: Die Verbindung von politischer und wirtschaftlicher Macht mit antidemokratischen bis faschistischen Ideologien zeigt sich nicht nur in den USA mit Trump mit „KI“-Beschwörern Musk, Thiel und Co. Deren Auswirkungen sind auch hier spürbar und finden Nachahmung, beispielsweise durch Tech-Milliardär Gotthardt, der mit dem „Nachrichtenportal“ Nius faschistoide Propaganda verbreitet. Widerstand zeigt sich bereits gegen Tesla und gegen Nius. Eine antifaschistische Bewegung muss sich mit den ungleichen Bedingungen politischer Öffentlichkeit zugunsten rechter Propaganda auseinandersetzen und nicht nur Nazis, sondern auch eben diese Technologien angreifen.


• Antimilitarismus: Hochrüstung mit „KI“ verspricht effizienteres Töten und trifft auf eine sich neu formierende Antimilitarismusbewegung. Ansetzen kann sie an den vielfältigen Prozesse und Knotenpunkten, in denen sich das Zivile ins Militärische einwebt. Es ist bereits gut dokumentiert, wie vermeintlich soziale Interaktionen das Training militärischer „KI“ füttern und wo militärische „KI“ auch in Berlin an Einfluss gewinnt.


Damit dieser Widerstand ganz natürlich möglichst wenig Anknüpfungsmöglichkeiten für rechte Heimatschützer*innen bietet, sollten wir klare emanzipatorische Inhalte ins Zentrum setzen. Hierbei kann es helfen, früh praktische internationale Solidarität aufzubauen und sich auf die Kämpfe um indigene Terroritorien und solche gegen „KI“-getriebene Datenarbeit zu beziehen.




3) Wirksamer Widerstand durch Vielfalt und Unberechenbarkeit




Die Strategie für Widerstand gegen ein politisches und ökonomisches Großprojekt will gut gewählt sein. Erfahrungen aus der Bewegungsgeschichte deuten darauf hin, dass vielfältige und unberechenbare Kämpfe die größte Wirkung entfalten können.


Ein Beispiel für die gelungene Verschränkung von Aktionsformen und -orten sehen wir bei der Anti-Atom-Bewegung. Sie hatte sich zur Verhinderung der Atomenergienutzung aus strategischen Gründen für den Widerstand gegen Atommülltransporte entschieden: Die abgebrannten Brennelemente mussten regelmäßig in Wiederaufbereitungsanlagen ins Ausland verbracht werden und gemäß internationaler Verträge nach der Wiederaufbereitung zur Endlagerung wieder rückgeführt werden. Die Pläne der deutschen Regierung sahen ein zentrales Endlager für hochradioaktiven Müll in Gorleben vor. Damit gab es zwei Punkte für Interventionen: Erstens, die Atommülltransporte von den Atomkraftwerken in die Wiederaufbereitungsanlagen als Ankerpunkte für (über-)regionalen Widerstand, und zweitens, die Rücktransporte nach Gorleben als Kristallisationspunkt für bundesweite und sogar internationale Bewegungen. Bei diesen Punkten gab es ein Zusammenwirken unterschiedlichster Aktionsformen, die nicht zentral gesteuert, sondern dezentral verantwortet wurden.


Die meisten heutigen Kampagnen haben Vielfalt und Unberechenbarkeit verloren oder sogar bewusst abgelegt. Beispielsweise Deutsche Wohnen Enteignen und Widersetzen sind dazu übergegangen, das Widerstandsszenario möglichst vorhersehbar zu machen. Mit vorgezeichneten Aktionsbildern und der Selbstbeschränkung auf Methoden des (maximal) zivilen Ungehorsams hoffen Organisator*innen auf mehr Teilnehmende. Dadurch fehlt bei größeren Ereignissen immer öfter jeglicher Kontrollverlust für die Ordnungskräfte. So wird es schwierig, praktische Möglichkeitsräume und damit neue gesellschaftliche Denkräume aufzustoßen. Den Wirkungsverlust sehen wir auch klar im Kampf gegen große Wohnungskonzerne, wenn der politische Gegner die legalistische Kampagne durch neue Gesetze einfach aushebelt.


Für eine vielfältige und unberechenbare Bewegung gegen „KI“ und Rechenzentren wäre folgendes denkbar: Kristallisationspunkt könnte z.B. ein in der Bedeutung herausragendes Rechenzentrum und/oder der europaweit größte Hochleistungs-Chiphersteller ESMC in Dresden sein. Auch der Lithografiemaschinen-Hersteller ASML in Eindhoven mit seiner weltweit technisch wie geostrategisch einmaligen Position als Flaschenhals der Chipproduktion könnte ein Kristallisationspunkt einer gesamt-europäischen Bewegung werden. Alle, die wir der Kohleverstromung im Gelände ein Ende bereiten, die wir uns den Rechten widersetzen, die wir Rheinmetall entwaffnen, die wir Vonovia/Deutsche Wohnen enteignen wollen: Hören wir auf zivil-und-gehorsam zu sein und beginnen wir unberechenbaren Widerstand zu leisten. Schließen wir uns mit denen zusammen, die sich in weniger sichtbaren Zusammenhängen organisieren und mit denen, die aus guten Gründen noch nie sichtbar waren.


Bilden wir Banden statt nur Bezugsgruppen, verbinden wir autonome Spontanität mit Kampagnenarbeit, seien wir unberechenbar und nehmen wir solidarisch aufeinander Bezug. Drängen wir gemeinsam „KI“ aus unseren Alltagsroutinen und unserer politischen Praxis und blockieren wir ihre zerstörerische Materialität in Rechenzentren!

content:

„Die Solidarität lässt für sie, so sagt Daniela, die Sonne aufgehen“


————————————————————————————-




Hallo,




wir rufen zu einer weiteren Kundgebung am Samstag, d. 5. November 2026 um 15 Uhr vor dem Frauenknast in Vechta auf. Daniela hat an diesem Tag Geburtstag.




Daniela ist weiterhin in der JVA Vechta, wie lange sie noch dort sein und wann sie nach Frankfurt-Preungesheim verlegt wird, wissen wir nicht.


Es hängt von einer Entscheidung des Oberlandesgerichts (OLG) Frankfurt, 8. Strafsenat, wann die Anklageschrift, die Ende März von der Bundesanwaltschaft an das OLG ergangen ist, für einen weiteren Prozess in Frankfurt zugelassen wird. Wir gehen davon aus, dass der Prozess erst in 2027 beginnen wird.




Wer einen Redebeitrag auf der Kundgebung halten möchte, sagt uns bitte rechtzeitig Bescheid.




Eine weitere Kundgebung wird es am 17. Dezember geben. Geichzeitig findet in Frankfurt am Main vor dem US-Konsulat die Kundgebung zu Mumia Abu Jamal statt. Daniela ist die Solidarität zu Mumia sehr wichtig. Er wurde am 9.12.1981 festgenommen. Sollte Daniela aber doch schon in Preungesheim einsitzen, findet dann vorher dort diese Kundgebung statt mit einer anschließenden Demo zum US-Konsulat.




Das Foto (siehe Anhang) ist von der Demo/Kundgebung „FREE THE ULM 5“ am 26. Otober 2026 in Stuttgart. Einige Genoss*innen von uns waren da.




Den Aufruf zur Veranstaltung am 7. November in Zürich veröffentlichen wir hier noch einmal.




Gruppe: Solidarität mit Daniela


solidarisch-mit-daniela@t-online.de / www.solidarisch-mit-Daniela.de
