title: ICE Is Running One of the Largest Anti-Left Surveillance Operations in US History (Wired)
content:
ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations is engaged in far-reaching spying against left-wing activists that rivals the FBI and CIA crackdowns on the Civil Rights and anti-war movements.

Attorneys for 15 Minnesota residents facing federal conspiracy charges have obtained evidence of a sweeping, possibly unconstitutional spying operation carried out by Immigration and Customs Enforcement against left-wing social movements in Minnesota and beyond.

The high-profile Minnesota 15 prosecution makes clear that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), flush with federal funds and newly hired personnel, is now President Donald Trump’s primary tool against dissent, with a powerful array of post-9/11 investigative authorities brought to bear against everyday Americans organizing their communities.

Nothing of this scale has been seen in the United States, experts say, since the federal government’s counterinsurgency against the New Left and the anti-war movement in the 1960s and 1970s.

Among the records revealed during the discovery process in these cases are dozens of reports, audio transcripts, emails, intercepted Signal chats, photographs, database queries, and more. They reveal the inner workings of the domestic terrorism investigations, running under the names Project Whipple Shield and Operation Puppet Master, authorized by the controversial National Security Presidential Memorandum 7.

Published following Charlie Kirk’s assassination in September of last year, NSPM 7 instructs federal law enforcement to use every tool available against organizations and people who criticize the administration’s policies and espouse “anti-Christian” ideas. The full scope and extent of the investigations it authorizes remains unknown.

Defense attorneys for the Minnesota 15 claim that the prosecution stems from a broader nationwide surveillance operation aimed at opponents of the Trump administration’s immigration policies. One attorney in the case directly compares the DHS-run campaign to the FBI’s infamous Counterintelligence Program, or COINTELPRO, which unconstitutionally surveilled, infiltrated, and blackmailed racial justice, civil rights, and anti-war movements from the 1950s through the early 1970s.

Three former law enforcement officials who reviewed filings concur, telling WIRED that the case is almost certainly part of a wider intelligence-gathering operation that began long before the administration invaded Minnesota in December 2025.

Dueling motions in the case over discovery of DHS’s surveillance program reveal that personnel with Homeland Security Investigations—one of ICE’s two components—repurposed funding mechanisms and investigative tools for serious criminal probes and turned them on domestic dissenters. Operation Keyhole, the HSI undercover program that bankrolled the Minnesota 15 prosecution, dates back to 2008. As of June 2026, it was underwriting a half dozen active undercover investigations in the Minneapolis–Saint Paul area.

Around 120 HSI agents, many drawn from specialized units across the country that have served as the leading edge of the administration’s militarized immigration enforcement operations, were assigned to the case—including 11 undercovers. They used highly invasive surveillance techniques, including the deployment of Reaper drones and Patriot Act tools usually restricted to money laundering and terrorism investigations. Undercover operatives also infiltrated churches in apparent violation of a court order.

The Minnesota 15 indictment stems from the Trump administration’s demand that the Justice Department “go big and go loud” to crack down on community response networks during last winter’s Operation Metro Surge. Twin Cities activists organized volunteers to monitor DHS agents and their vehicles using encrypted Signal groups, homebuilt vehicle databases, and a centralized dispatch system. Government prosecutors claim that this amounts to a criminal conspiracy to block immigration enforcement, unlawfully identify and stalk federal agents, and even assault them.

Their defense attorneys say the heavy charges filed against the Minnesota 15 don’t align with their alleged conduct. “This is the first time I’ve had a client who’s accused of a conspiracy and went on a speaking tour,” says Kevin Riach, who represents defendant Isaac Sant.

An internal ICE document laying out the scope of Operation Puppet Master—which led to the indictment of the Minneapolis 15—ends by noting, “This case has also been accepted under CUC Op Keyhole.” According to prosecutors, Operation Keyhole is a long-standing program created by HSI’s Saint Paul office to fund “undercover activity”—primarily equipment purchases and personnel costs—in a region covering Minnesota, North and South Dakota, Iowa, and Nebraska. The program has funded at least 77 investigations into “narcotics trafficking, child sexual abuse, financial investigations, and counter-proliferation” since it started in December 2008.

The CUC prefix, per an internal 2008 DHS handbook unearthed by the independent media outlet Unicorn Riot, refers to Certified Undercover Operations, a formal designation with clearly defined oversight mechanisms, procedures, and reporting requirements. Operation Keyhole’s parameters are reviewed every six months by a committee comprising senior DOJ and DHS officials. As of June 2026, when it was last renewed, Keyhole funded six active investigations, including Project Whipple Shield, which was initiated in February to probe claims of assault, stalking, and doxing of DHS agents and other federal employees, and underpins the Minnesota 15 indictment.

At least 11 undercover agents working under Operation Keyhole infiltrated Twin Cities anti-ICE activists, participating in martial arts and know-your-rights trainings, marches, general strikes, and community meetings. They also infiltrated activists’ communications network for identifying possible undercover ICE vehicles and dispatching activists to tail them through the Twin Cities, and penetrated several activist group chats on Signal, transmitting their contents back to other HSI colleagues for analysis and eventual inclusion in the indictment.

Activist conferences as far away as Seattle, Michigan, Chicago, and New York City were placed under surveillance as part of the investigation, and HSI teams photographed and ran the license plates of every car parked in the lot of a meeting location or seen transporting activists. There is also drone footage from unarmed Customs and Border Protection Reaper drones of the activists moving around the Twin Cities area.

The undercovers were part of a much broader group of more than 50 HSI agents, including at least two dozen from HSI’s little-known Special Operations Group, that took part in the investigation and surveillance of the defendants, both digital and in-person. Feds with decades of experience on complex financial crimes, drug cartel investigations, human trafficking, and organized crime were pulled into the Minnesota 15 investigation.

Several of the Minnesota 15 case agents are from out of state and appear in court records for the prosecutions of anti-ICE activists in other cities. This includes Los Angeles–based HSI agents Robert Kurtz III, who specializes in financial fraud, and Ryan Ribner, who allegedly assaulted SEIU California president David Huerta at a June 2025 protest of an ICE enforcement operation, arrested him, and then claimed the then 58-year-old Huerta attacked federal law enforcement. (Huerta’s charges were dropped in July after videos contradicting Ribner’s account surfaced.) HSI records show Ribner was also involved in at least two prosecutions of Southern California residents who physically confronted ICE and Border Patrol agents last year.

Other agents from the conspiracy investigation have also been involved in recent high-profile incidents. Tim Gerber, the “team leader” of an HSI Special Operations Group squad, led the investigation of former CNN host Don Lemon for reporting on a protest at a Minneapolis Church where an ICE agent was a pastor. Fellow SOG agent Yue Her was present at the scene of a 2025 incident when Renee Good’s killer, ICE Special Response Team agent Johnathan Ross, was dragged by the car of a man he tried to apprehend.

“This operation does not seem in any way limited to Minnesota,” says Spencer Reynolds, a former DHS attorney and counterterrorism lawyer who now works at the NAACP Legal Defense Fund. “As we saw with the boots on the ground in the streets, with Greg Bovino leading CBP and Border Patrol special forces units on sweeping raids across the country, this is the intelligence and undercover investigative apparatus that is running in parallel to the door-kicking.”

Mike German, a retired FBI agent who worked undercover domestic terrorism cases for years before becoming a sharp critic of post-9/11 federal law enforcement, likens the Minnesota 15 case to federal law enforcement’s long history of suppressing left-wing social movements, including the CIA’s Operation MH/Chaos, which surveilled the anti-war movement during the Vietnam War for evidence of foreign influence. One difference is the sheer scale—this time, it’s bigger.

According to a 2011 book by former CIA officer Frank Rafalko, the CIA secret investigation into suspected foreign influence on the New Left and anti-Vietnam War movement had 42 officers working the case at its peak. Court records show 119 HSI agents worked on the Minnesota 15 case alone.

“Broad monitoring of social media, communications, and financial transactions are used to link an ever increasing number of people as potential subjects of investigation and prosecution,” German says. “These are exactly the kind of intelligence activities J. Edgar Hoover adopted to suppress the Civil Rights and anti-war movements in the 1960s.”

The key difference today, German says, is the vast pool of data available to the feds.

HSI used highly invasive measures—including scrutiny of wire transfers, PayPal reimbursements, and other financial transactions; forensic digital analysis of website traffic; 15 terabytes worth of infiltrated Signal chats; and information from a commercial data broker—to identify individuals under investigation.

After a local activist uploaded a license-plate search tool on Fly.io, a developer-focused public cloud platform, to an infiltrated Signal chat, HSI agents reviewed website DNS queries and Stripe data along with data purchased from a commercial broker. This gave HSI access to SSH session logs, outbound connection records, the Fly.io account’s signup IP, and a Stripe card fingerprint on an account that had never completed a payment. Agents fused that with Minnesota DVS records and commercial data from the Thomson-Reuters CLEAR platform to produce a driver’s license number, Social Security number summary, years of address history, phone numbers, property records, and jointly registered vehicles.

Documents concerning financial records requested through the Treasury Department’s 314(a) suspicious activity reporting program—created by the Patriot Act to enable speedy tracking of finances for terrorism and money-laundering investigations—show that the feds targeted records of 29 “subjects” during queries conducted on March 31, 2026. Emails viewed by WIRED between several HSI agents based in Los Angeles and Arizona show that batches of records were turned over pursuant to those inquiries, including some dealing with SEIU that a senior Minnesota HSI agent sent to a LA-based colleague to be filed “wherever these records are stored.”

HSI investigators used similar workarounds to warrants and grand jury subpoenas to obtain phone records for several journalists who covered Operation Metro Surge, as first reported by The Guardian. Court records show the feds used an administrative summons request reserved for violations of customs and taxation requirements, which does not fit the activity that made up the criminal charges filed by the Minnesota US attorney against former CNN anchor Don Lemon and others.

The Minnesota 15 case is the clearest example yet of DHS pursuing the Trump administration’s efforts to crack down on what have long been upheld as First Amendment–protected activities. But it’s unlikely alone.

Riach, the defense attorney, says the HSI reports show the agency is complicit in what he called “the new COINTELPRO.”

“What we saw during the immigration surges last year was that ICE is the administration’s paramilitary force, the projector of strength,” Riach says. “Here, we see that HSI are taking the FBI’s place as the investigative secret police—it’s the classic one-two punch of authoritarian regimes around the world.”

author: Theia Chatelle
title: High Palestinian Turnout in Israeli Elections Came Down to Matters of Survival
content:
“We fear that if we do not get this government out of power, we will lose everything,” one Palestinian voter said.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Jaffa, Israel — Outside of Ahva Elementary School in Ajami, a historic Palestinian neighborhood just south of central Tel Aviv, the mood was defiant on October 27, the day of Israel’s national elections. “We fear that if we do not get this government out of power, we will lose everything,” one Palestinian voter told me after casting her ballot.

It came as no surprise that she, like most of the Palestinian citizens of Israel I interviewed on Election Day, asked not to be named. Since October 7, 2023, more than 400 Palestinian citizens of Israel have been investigated by police for “incitement,” often over social media posts, according to the legal rights group Adalah.

During the 1948 war, which Palestinians call the Nakba, most of Jaffa’s nearly 100,000 Palestinian residents fled or were expelled. The fewer than 4,000 who remained were concentrated in Ajami, fenced in with barbed wire, where they lived under Israeli military rule until 1949.

Just weeks ago, it was not clear that the parties most Palestinian citizens of Israel vote for would even appear on the ballot. In September, Israel’s Central Elections Committee, a body of party representatives, voted to disqualify both Arab parties — which are led by and draw most of their votes from Palestinian citizens of Israel — from running in the election. The Joint List is an alliance of three parties running together to clear the 3.25 percent threshold needed to enter the Knesset.

Hadash, a left-wing party with roots in Israel’s Communist Party, is the only one of the three with both Jewish and Palestinian members. Ta’al’s platform has historically focused on the rights of Palestinian citizens of Israel. Balad, a Palestinian nationalist party, calls for Israel to become a state of all its citizens, with equal rights for everyone.

The other party, running independently, is Ra’am, a conservative Islamist party led by Mansour Abbas, which in 2021 became the first Arab party to join an Israeli governing coalition.

The two Arab parties were eventually reinstated and allowed to run in the Israeli election, but only after an appeal to Israel’s Supreme Court.

As Israelis vote to elect the country’s 26th parliament (Knesset), Palestinian voters in the Ajami neighborhood said Gaza was at the top of their minds. Just down the road is a public memorial displaying photos of some of the more than 20,000 children who have, according to a UN commission, been killed by the Israeli military in Gaza since October 7, 2023.

The memorial, at Hajj Kahil Square, has been torn down more than once. In May, according to Bokra, a Palestinian news site, two men, one of them carrying a rifle, ripped the photos from the walls. The next day, Jaffa residents put them back up and renamed the traffic circle the “Gaza Children’s Roundabout.” Police, who ultimately answer to Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s far right minister of national security, have also tried to stop protesters from displaying the images.

Whether or not to participate in Israel’s national elections has long been a fraught topic among Palestinian citizens of Israel.

Whether or not to participate in Israel’s national elections has long been a fraught topic among Palestinian citizens of Israel. Some fear that voting in the election would lend legitimacy to a state that expelled most of their families in 1948 and maintains a military occupation over Palestinians in the West Bank, and that human rights groups say has committed genocide in Gaza; but others view it as their only way to gather power in the Knesset, especially more than three years after October 7.

An unprecedented wave of homicides in the community has also pushed many to the polls. At least 184 Palestinian citizens of Israel have been killed this year, putting 2026 on pace to surpass last year’s record of 252, according to the Abraham Initiatives. Police filed indictments in just 12 percent of homicides in Palestinian communities by June 2026, compared with a historic rate of indictments in 65 percent of cases involving homicides committed against Jewish Israelis.

On Israel’s Election Day, a recorded voice message went out to more than 1 million Palestinian voters from Sousan Sultan, whose sister Susan was killed in April 2025, and whose husband, Ziad, was murdered last August. “My sister was murdered, and she cannot vote in the election,” Sultan said in the recording, asking voters to cast their ballots in her sister’s name.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main challengers have all ruled out forming a coalition with the Arab parties, even as polls suggest the opposition may struggle to reach a majority without them. Throughout the campaign, Likud (Israel’s largest right-wing party) and its allies have made those parties a frequent target of their campaign ads, using Palestinian electoral power as a way to drum up turnout among anti-Palestinian blocs.

Some ads depict images of Palestinian political leaders, including Ahmad Tibi, who was an adviser to Yasser Arafat, alongside center-right politician Gadi Eisenkot, whose Yashar party leads the opposition, proclaiming the choice is “the right” or “Palestine.”

In the Negev, the desert region in Israel’s south that is home to most of the country’s roughly 300,000 Bedouin citizens, many of whom identify as Palestinians, voter turnout has historically been low. But in this election, that appears to have completely shifted. In the Bedouin village of al-Atawneh, turnout had reached 64 percent by noon on the day of the election, the highest in the country, according to Central Elections Committee data. In the last election, it was 41 percent for the entire day.

“We are seeing record-breaking voter turnout in the Naqab [the Arabic name for the Negev] today for the Knesset elections, reaching unprecedented levels,” Huda Abu Obaid, advocacy coordinator with the Negev Coexistence Forum, told Truthout on Election Day. “However, right-wing groups are intentionally delaying the voting process, forcing voters to wait in excessively long lines.”

Many of the Negev’s Bedouin citizens live in villages the state does not recognize, which lack connection to the national water and electricity grids and where homes face demolition for being built without permits. Israeli authorities demolished a record 5,187 buildings in Bedouin communities in the Negev in 2024 alone, up from 3,283 the year before, according to the Negev Coexistence Forum.

Far right parties sent their own observers to polling stations in Palestinian communities, and rights groups reported long delays in the Galilee, in the north, and the Negev, both home to large Palestinian populations. The Central Elections Committee said it had found no evidence of systematic tampering and that polling stations would stay open past 10:00 pm for anyone still in line.

On Election Day in 2015, Netanyahu warned in a video that Palestinian voters were heading to the polls “in droves,” a message widely credited with driving a late surge in support for Likud. This year, he did it again, warning his base of high Palestinian turnout and claiming, without evidence, that his opponents were trying to steal the election.

With about 84 percent of all votes counted by Wednesday afternoon, no party bloc was close to reaching the 61-seat threshold required to form a majority in the Knesset. Netanyahu’s bloc was the largest, at 54 seats, but it was still down from 68 he held in the outgoing Knesset. Meanwhile, the opposition bloc (composed of all non-Arab parties running to unseat Netanyahu) won 49 seats. The Arab parties won a combined total of 17 seats, the most they have ever won in history. Turnout among Palestinian citizens reached an estimated 80 percent, breaking a record set in 1999, and surpassing the turnout rate among Jewish Israeli voters for the first time ever.

Jafar Farah, director of the Mossawa Center, a Haifa-based advocacy group for Arab citizens of Israel, cautioned against reading too much into the numbers. Farah was elected to the No. 2 spot on Hadash’s slate in May but withdrew in September. He said the rise in Palestinian turnout does not necessarily mean Palestinian citizens have renewed faith in the Israeli state or its institutions, or believe the ballot can end the military occupation of the West Bank (a theme in some of the Joint List’s campaign ads), or change conditions in Gaza. Instead, Farah said, many voters see casting a ballot as a form of “damage control.”

At least 184 Palestinian citizens of Israel have been killed this year.

“The increase in turnout projected in the 2026 polls, if it materializes, cannot automatically be interpreted as a return of trust in the Israeli establishment or in the Arab parties,” Farah said. “It may also reflect a growing sense of the need for political protection in conditions marked by uncertainty.”

A May poll by Tel Aviv University’s Moshe Dayan Center found that while more than 77 percent of Palestinian citizens of Israel want an Arab party in the next government, only 40 percent believe Jewish Israelis genuinely support a political partnership with them.

Netanyahu’s challengers offer little on the issues many Palestinian voters care about. Eisenkot’s party says it supports Jewish settlement wherever it is carried out legally and opposes a Palestinian state. Eisenkot himself has said anyone still thinking about a two-state solution after October 7 is “simply delusional.” Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the B’Yachad list, has ruled out ceding any land to what he calls Israel’s enemies, an apparent reference to a Palestinian state.

As of today, the math appears simple: Without the Joint List or Ra’am joining the coalition, the opposition appears to have no way to form a majority in the Knesset. Yet Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman, two right-wing opposition leaders, are still ruling out any government that relies on Arab parties, and Eisenkot has not dropped conditions for coalition partners that most Palestinian lawmakers are unlikely to accept.

Palestinian citizens of Israel turned out in record numbers to get the Netanyahu government out of power, but it remains to be seen whether the other opposition parties will join in their efforts.

Truthout is funded almost entirely by readers — that’s why we can speak truth to power and cut against the mainstream narrative. But independent journalists at Truthout face mounting political repression under Trump.

title: We’re Proud to Join Stop Arming Israel Coalition (Labor for Palestine National Network)
content:
A post shared by Labor4Palestine (@labor4palestine)

The Stop Arming Israel Coalition just launched, and we’re proud to be part of it.

In the face of rising fascism and repression, we need to move strategically, and we need to move together as a united front. The Stop Arming Israel Coalition will unite over 60 national organizations and local grassroots groups across the country in a shared commitment to Palestinian freedom and collective liberation. It is steered by Palestinian-led organizations and convened by @uscpraction.

Our solidarity is our greatest strength. Together we will fight to stop arming Israel and fund care for our communities, on the path toward a free Palestine and a liberated world.

title: Η αντιφασισατική Θεσσαλονίκη έδωσε απάντηση σε φασίστες, Κασιδιάρη, κυβερνητική τρομοκρατία, αστυνομική βία
content:
Οι αντιφασίστες της Θεσσαλονίκης έδωσαν το παρόν στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου επί της Εγνατίας όπου είχε καλεστεί συγκέντρωση ενάντια στη φασιστοσύναξη του νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη σε ξενοδοχείου του Βαρδαρίου. Όμως τα κυβερνητικά σχέδια προστασίας του προσφάτως αποφυλακισθέντα χρυσαυγίτη, ακολούθησαν η απαγόρευση της συγκέντρωσης από την αστυνομία και τελικά η εκτεταμμένη χρήση βίας από τα ΜΑΤ που είχαν ζώσει την περιοχή.




Οι αντιφασίστες πολίτες ανταποκρίθηκαν στα καλέσματα σωματείων, συλλόγων, οργανώσεων, συλλογικοτήτων και προήλθαν από  ευρύ πολιτικό φάσμα: τον αντιεξουσιαστικό χώρο, τη ριζοσπαστική αριστερά, το ΚΚΕ. Έδειξαν δε μεγάλη αποφασιστικότητα στην πραγματοποίηση της συγκέντρωσης και παρέμειναν στο χώρο παρά τα χημικά, τα δακρυγόνα, τις κρότου λάμψης που έπεσαν σωρηδόν από την ελληνική αστυνομία και τις δύο προσαγωγές.




Χαρακτηριστικά του δυναμισμού και παλμού της αντιφασιστικής συγκέντρωσης ήταν και συνθήματα που καταγράφηκαν: Μπλόκο στους φασίστες, καμιά ανοχή στα τσιράκια των αφεντικών. Είστε η σαπίλα όλου του ντουνιά, μπλόκο στους φασίστες σε κάθε γειτονιά. Φασίστες από το λαό θα τη βρείτε. Το φασισμό τσακίζουν αγώνες λαϊκοί. Έξω οι νεοναζί από τη Θεσσαλονίκη. Στη φυλακή οι νεοναζί. Φασίστες, χίτες, μαυραγορίτες. Ούτε σπιθαμή γής στους φασίστες. Ούτε με φυλακές, ούτε με νόμους, ο φασισμός τσακίζεται στους δρόμους.

title: Správa o aktivitách počas Medzinárodného týždňa proti nevyplácaniu miezd (2026)
content:
Cieľom „Týždňa“ je poukázať na nevyplácanie miezd a ukázať, ako sa dá proti tomu brániť. Potešilo nás, že tento rok sa zvýšil počet participujúcich a že sa medzi nimi prvýkrát objavili organizácie z Ázie, Južnej Ameriky a Kanady. Väčšinou išlo o propagačné aktivity online a v uliciach, ale uskutočnili sa aj stretnutia pracujúcich, protestné akcie či workshopy. Pre lepšie zobrazenie článku odporúčame pozrieť tu: 

https://priamaakcia.sk/sprava-o-aktivitach-pocas-medzinarodneho-tyzdna-proti-nevyplacaniu-miezd-2026.html




PA (Slovensko) 




Zväz Priama akcia pripravil pred Týždňom a počas neho viaceré aktivity v Bratislave. 




Zverejnili sme článok o Týždni ako takom a vyzvali sme ľudí, aby sa podelili o svoje skúsenosti a problémy.




Ozvalo sa nám niekoľko pracujúcich s otázkami týkajúcimi sa nevyplatených peňazí v prípade živnostníkov, kontaktovania zo strany nadriadených ohľadom pracovných záležitostí počas pracovného voľna a venovali sme sa aj problému zahraničného zamestnanca, ktorý si chcel overiť správnosť vyplatenej mzdy.




Zorganizovali sme tiež stretnutie venované nevyplácaniu miezd

, ktoré zopakujeme aj v novembri. 




V uliciach Bratislavy sa tiež objavili nálepky PA. Jedným z miest bolo aj okolie 3 The Clubhouse, čo je podnik prepojený s ľuďmi okolo VegaNany, s ktorými vedieme spor o nevyplatené mzdy. K sporu sme uverejnili článok s novinkami 

https://priamaakcia.sk/veganana-dalsi-prehraty-sud-nove-dlhy-ai-slop-a-nevyplatene-mzdy.html

. Pre viac informácií pozri 

https://priamaakcia.sk/tag/veganana

.




ZSP (Poľsko)




Viaceré aktivity uskutočnil aj Zväz syndikalistov Poľska. 




Už nejaký čas bojuje proti firmám ako Ochrona Mega Marcin Kowalski a Protego, ktoré vlastní jedna rodina. Po protestoch a priamych akciách týkajúcich sa nevyplácania miezd skončili niektoré prípady na súde a bolo vynesených niekoľko rozsudkov v prospech pracujúcich. ZSP už dávnejšie poukazoval na fakt, že spoločnosť Ochrona Mega Marcin Kowalski dostala veľkú sumu peňazí od štátnej agentúry, ktorá poskytuje zamestnávateľom dotácie na zamestnávanie osôb so zdravotným postihnutím.




Po proteste ZSP, na ktorom zväz požadoval, aby podniky, ktoré nevyplácajú mzdy, nedostávali príspevky z verejných zdrojov a aby sa začalo vyšetrovanie, agentúra dotácie zastavila. Druhá dobrá správa prišla 19. októbra – štátna agentúra bude od firmy žiadať vrátenie dotácií vo výške 3 miliónov zlotých (takmer 700 tisíc eur). 




Zväz nahral aj video o Týždni, v ktorom zdôraznil, že úrady by mali ukončiť činnosť firiem, ktoré nevyplácajú mzdy. Aktivity za dosiahnutie tohto cieľa budú pokračovať. 




V uliciach a pri podnikoch, proti ktorým v minulosti prebehli kampane za nevyplácanie miezd, sa objavili aj tematické plagáty. 




ZSP tiež preložil do španielčiny brožúru o nevyplácaní miezd pre workshop, ktorý sa konal 24. októbra pre španielsky hovoriacich pracujúcich v Poľsku.




SF (Británia)




Federácia solidarity rozšírila informácie a protestovala proti workfare. Ide o systém, ktorý núti príjemcov sociálnych dávok vykonávať neplatenú prácu, ak si chcú zachovať nárok na tieto dávky. Podľa SF ide o priamy útok korporácií a štátu na celú pracujúcu triedu a nie iba iniciatívu zameranú na odbornú prípravu. SF proti tomuto systému viedla kampaň už aj v minulosti, pozri napríklad 

https://priamaakcia.sk/Dolezity-uspech-kampane-proti-workfare--priame-akcie-prinutili-Holland--Barrett-vystupit-zo-systemu.html

. Prvky podobné workfare platia od 1. 9. 2025 aj na Slovensku (pozri kritické zhodnotenie napríklad tu: 

https://www.amnesty.sk/ziadost-o-vetovanie-zakona-meniaceho-podmienkypristupu-k-pomoci-v-hmotnej-nudzi/

).  




V septembri bol v Británii spustený nový program s názvom Opening Shift, v podstate je to však len nový názov pre rovnaké politiky ako v prípade workfare. Cieľom programu je umiestniť viac ako 100 000 mladých ľudí vo veku 18-24 rokov na dvoj- až štvortýždňové stáže v britských maloobchodných reťazcoch, ako sú napríklad Tesco, John Lewis, Marks & Spencer, Costa Coffee atď. Za túto prácu nedostávajú mzdu, ale musia ju robiť, inak by nedostali dávky. Vláda takto v podstate poskytuje korporáciám bezplatnú pracovnú silu, čo zhoršuje možnosť nájsť si platené zamestnanie.




Skupina SF v Liverpoole zorganizovala akcie proti firmám, ktoré sú súčasťou programu Opening Shift.




CNT-AIT (Francúzsko)




Začiatkom októbra navštívila miestnu organizáciu Národnej konfederácie práce v Toulouse skupina pracujúcich z jednej upratovacej spoločnosti. Chceli sa poradiť, ako postupovať voči zamestnávateľovi, ktorý im nevypláca mzdu v plnej výške, keďže ignoruje príplatky dohodnuté v kolektívnych zmluvách a neprepláca všetky nadčasy. Na ďalších stretnutiach vypracovali plán postupu. Prvý krok bude list s požiadavkami adresovaný šéfovi a v prípade, že neuspejú, zorganizujú verejné akcie. 




Nebýva bežné, aby zväz kontaktovala skupina pracujúcich. Zvyčajne ide o jedného človeka. CNT-AIT považujú túto zmenu za pozitívny dôsledok ich neustálej činnosti a snahy zvyšovať povedomie o kolektívnej sile pracujúcich. 




Počas Týždňa prebiehala vo Francúzsku veľká spoločenská mobilizácia, ktorá sa dotýka aj nízkych miezd. CNT-AIT sa zúčastňuje týchto protestov v rôznych francúzskych mestách a informuje o nich v rôznych jazykoch na stránke 

https://cnt-ait.info/author/cnt-ait/

.




ASI (Srbsko)




Anarchosyndikalistická iniciatíva sa zamerala hlavne na tri prebiehajúce spory. 




Zverejnila príspevky o prípade, v ktorom vyzvala na bojkot detského rekreačného strediska, kde bol v minulosti zamestnaný pracovník, ktorému firma dlhuje 88 989 RSD (približne 750 EUR). V reakcii na výzvu vyplatiť dlžné mzdy reagoval majiteľ, bývalý policajt, prostredníctvom viacerých kanálov hrozbami, že na bývalého zamestnanca pošle políciu. Prípad stále prebieha.




Zväz usporiadal aj dve protestné akcie na podporu nespravodlivo prepustených kolegov. V jednom prípade išlo o prepustenie zo strojárskej firmy ALL3. Prepusteniu predchádzala šikana po tom, ako sa pracovník odvážil požadovať podmienky na pracovisku, na ktorých sa dohodol so zamestnávateľom pred nástupom do práce. Jedna akcia sa konala už skôr a jeden zo šéfov sa počas nej pokúsil prejsť autom našich kamarátov. ASI požaduje primeranú finančnú kompenzáciu za doterajšiu prácu, zlé zaobchádzanie, vykorisťovanie, lži a jednostranné prepustenie, alebo návrat do práce, kde budú pracovníkovi zabezpečené primerané pracovné podmienky.




Druhý protest sa týkal bývalého zamestnanca spoločnosti IGT pôsobiacej v oblasti iGamingu, ktorého prepustili po tom, čo bol zaradený do programu na zlepšenie výkonnosti (PIP) kvôli zdravotným problémom. Pritom pred zaradením do PIP bol pracovník chválený ako vynikajúci zamestnanec a jeho zdravotné problémy sa začali kvôli nadčasom. Pred prepustením sa ho firma pokúsila dotlačiť do dohody o ukončení pracovného pomeru a ponúkla mu smiešnu kompenzáciu. Zväz požaduje primeranú kompenzácia alebo opätovné prijatie do zamestnania a spravodlivé zaobchádzanie.




Ďalšími aktivitami ASI bol vylepovanie nových nálepiek. Cieľom je osloviť nové členstvo. V pláne je aj špeciálne vydanie časopisu „Direktna akcija“ venované Týždňu.




CA (Španielsko)




Anarchosyndikalistická konfederácia v Albacete organizovala 17. októbra celodenné informačné podujatie o nevyplácaní miezd. Konala sa aj benefičná večera a protest na námestí. 




Zväz v Gijóne publikoval viacero príspevkov a zhrnul aj novinky o legislatívnych zmenách týkajúcich sa pracovných zmlúv v Španielsku.




ASN (Nemecko)




Anarchosyndikalistická sieť propagovala Týždeň v uliciach formou plagátov a bannerov.




PRO-IWA Korea (Južná Kórea)




Súčasťou Medzinárodnej asociácie pracujúcich (MAP) sa stala v lete 2026 so štatútom Kontakt aj skupina v Južnej Kórei s názvom PRO-IWA Korea. Informácie o Týždni propagovali online aj v uliciach.




SO (Čile)




Solidarita pracujúcich v meste Valparaíso pripravila plagáty a nálepky o nevyplácaní miezd a venovala sa aj téme námezdnej práce ako takej. V uliciach sa objavili aj graffiti.




KRAS (Rusko)




Konfederácia ruských anarchosyndikalistov pripomenula, že aj v Rusku je nevyplácanie miezd akútny problém. Celkový dlh na mzdách zo strany zamestnávateľov dosahuje takmer 2,5 miliardy rubľov (cca 27 miliónov eur). 




KRAS spomenula štrajk smetiarov v moskovskej oblasti, ktorý sa odohral práve počas Týždňa, pričom smetiari sa zorganizovali sami. Príčinou štrajku bol predošlý dlh na mzdách a informácie o znížení miezd takmer o polovicu. Za september napríklad dostali necelých 450 eur, pričom robili náročné 12-hodinové zmeny. Väčšina pracovníkov buď štrajkovala, alebo išla na PN. Vedenie ich najprv vyzvalo, nech teda dajú výpoveď, čo situáciu vyhrotilo, no po prvom dni sa začalo vyjednávanie. Firma napokon súhlasila s doplatením septembrových miezd, prehodnotením podmienok odmeňovania a výrazným zvýšením základných miezd (minimálna mzda vodičov by mala stúpnuť na cca 1 200 eur). Zamestnanci sa tiež vrátia k systému odmeňovania podľa výkonu a k špeciálnym príplatkom za ručný zber odpadu, ktoré boli predtým zrušené. Zdôraznili, že ak firma nedodrží svoje sľuby, sú pripravení obnoviť štrajk.




Cercle des ami.e.s de l‘A.I.T. (Kanada)




Skupinou so štatútom Kontakt MAP je od roku 2025 aj Kruh priateľstva s MAP z Kanady. 




V súvislosti s Týždňom zorganizoval verejný workshop s cieľom pomôcť pracujúcim zlepšiť povedomie o mzdových podmienkach a právach vo všeobecnosti na miestach, kde nepôsobia odbory. Samotný workshop mal na starosti člen montrealskej komunitnej skupiny Au bas de l’échelle (v preklade „Na dne sociálno-ekonomického rebríka“), ktorá funguje už niekoľko desaťročí a venuje sa obrane práv pracujúcich na pracoviskách bez odborov. Vďaka workshopu sa ľudia dozvedeli veľa informácií o individuálnych mzdových právach. Dokonca aj zamestnanci z pracovísk, kde odbory pôsobia, zistili, že zamestnávatelia im riadne nevyplácajú nadčasy, čo je dôkazom nedostatkov tradičných odborov v oblasti vzdelávania členstva. Workshopu sa zúčastnilo členstvo z Montrealu aj Quebecu a budúci rok ho počas Týždňa plánujú zopakovať.




NSF (Nórsko)




Nórska syndikalistická federácia informovala o Týždni a poukázala na fakt, že vďaka zákonu, ktorý má údajne chrániť pracujúcich pred nevyplácaním miezd, skončili za posledné roky na súde len tri prípady. 




Jeden prípad sa v lete 2026 dostal na Najvyšší súd. Išlo o 13 pracujúcich v čistiarni, ktorým neboli vyplatené mzdy a preplatená dovolenka za obdobie zhruba pol roka vo výške NOK 465 457, čo je takmer 45 000 eur. Najvyšší súd rozhodol, že za toto konanie bude zamestnávateľovi uložený trest odňatia slobody na 9 mesiacov. NSF poukázal aj na to, ako rôzne postihuje systém rozličné porušenia zákona – za daňový podvod (DPH) dostal rovnaký zamestnávateľ v minulosti 2 roky a 4 mesiace odňatia slobody. 




Podobne ako v predošlých rokoch pripomenul NSF aj viacjazyčnú publikáciu o právach pracujúcich zo zahraničia v oblasti miezd, pracovných hodín a zmlúv, dovoleniek či pracovného prostredia.

author: Rizomatica
title: 534 años de resistencia: a propósito de la marcha histórica del 12 de octubre en la ciudad de Temuco 2026
content:
Por: Cheuquelen Ñancucheo Ñanculeo




Empatía y solidaridad con la resistencia Mapuche y las diferentes Luchas.

El pasado 12 de octubre se realizó la marcha por la resistencia Mapuche en la ciudad de Temuco convocada por los familiares de los presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de dicha ciudad y comunidades en resistencia, en conmemoración a los 534 años de invasión española.

La denominada Marcha por la Resistencia Mapuche del año 2026 fue una marcha histórica por diversos motivos: el primero es la gran convocatoria que tuvo y que se vio reflejado en varios centenares de personas que marcharon por el centro de la cuidad de Temuco. Autoridades tradicionales del pueblo Mapuche, así como diferentes representantes de los diversos Lof en resistencia; hogares estudiantiles de distintas regiones, así como colectivos e individualidades, tanto mapuche como del pueblo chileno. 




El segundo: lo emotivo de dicha marcha no solo por la fecha, sino por el trabajo realizado previamente, el cual se vio reflejado en las más de un centenar de banderas azules con sus respectivos colihues, las que representaban cada una con su propio número a los más de 113 presos políticos Mapuche que se encuentran recluidos en las diferentes cárceles del estado Chileno. 




Lo tercero: es la mezcla de la primera y la segunda, vale decir, en la impronta de una marcha tan masiva cargada de simbolismos en varios aspectos, como por ejemplo: la visualización de las demandas del movimiento Mapuche, la que se vio reflejada en múltiples y coloridos lienzos , el primero de estos se llevó en el frontis de la marcha y representaba al módulo de presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Temuco; el segundo lienzo, representando a los prisioneros políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Angol, ambos con la frase: Kiñewaiñ Weichan mew, unidad en la lucha; el tercero , fue uno que decía relación con la exigencias al término del estado de excepción constitucional de emergencia, el que a la fecha lleva 4 años y cinco meses, lo que significa netamente una segunda ocupación militar del territorio Mapuche, está vez en el siglo XXI. Así sucesivamente, diferentes lienzos y consignas hasta el final de dicha marcha.

























Además de lo anterior, las 113 y una banderas realizadas por los familiares de presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Temuco, dieron una impronta y un simbolismo emocional como pocas veces vistos. Ver la marcha cargadas de banderas azules flameando al viento – sobre todo en la parte final de esta- dio un toque emotivo importante, porque no solamente era una bandera azul con un colihue, cosa que ya es simbólico en una cuidad como Temuco, sino que además cada bandera llevaba el nombre de un preso y Presa Política Mapuche recluidos en diferentes cárceles de Wallmapu; Cada bandera representaba a ese peñi o esa lamgen que está tras las rejas, pero además representaba a una familia de un Lof en lucha y el conjunto de aquello, a un pueblo en resistencia.

Visualizar personas de diferentes partes del Gulumapu, además de los diferentes Lof y autoridades del pueblo Mapuche que se hicieron presentes ese día, hace reflexionar una sola cosa : cuando un pueblo apuesta por la unidad en su legítima lucha y se trabaja socialmente por aquello, respetando las diferencias de cada pensamiento que compone dicho movimiento, tarde o temprano se va haber reflejado en algo. No es de un día para otro, porque detrás de esto hubo un trabajo y porque la diferencia es algo inherente a todo pueblo y todo movimiento.

No olvidar que la ‘Marcha del 12 de octubre’ o la «Marcha por la Resistencia Mapuche» como se conoce comúnmente, representa para los diferentes gobiernos de turnos- sobre todo para el de Bachelet, Piñera, Boric y Kast- la expresión social del principal enemigo interno del estado de Chile, el Movimiento Mapuche en Resistencia o Autonomista, criminalizado históricamente por los medios de comunicación burgueses, sobre todo los últimos 30 años.

Pero ahí estaba nuestra gente, representada en niños y niñas, jóvenes, adultos y adultos mayores, tanto del pueblo Mapuche como también del pueblo Chileno que llegaron ese dia; los hijos e hijas de los presos políticos Mapuche; los jóvenes y adultos de comunidades en resistencia que han crecido bajo los patrullajes mixtos y que han tenido que soportar los más de 730 mil controles de identidad, además de la adultez mayor, la que permanentemente junto a la infancia, tienen que soportar los más de 6 tipos de ruidos que asedian Wallmapu: el dron helicóptero; dron avioneta; avión no tripulado; dron convencional; carros anfibios Mowats; Jeep tipo zorrillo, helicópteros del ejercito y carabineros, entre otros.

EMPATÍA POR LAS DIFERENTES LUCHAS

En la denominada marcha por la Resistencia Mapuche que se realizó en la cuidad de Temuco estuvieron presentes 113 banderas azules que representaban a cada uno de los presos políticos Mapuche, sin embargo hubo una bandera de color negra con la imagen de una persona y con una frase en mapudzungun que decía lo siguiente:

«Juan Aliste Vega Yem

Tukulpaniegaymün weichan mew»

El pasado 11 de noviembre falleció Juan Manuel Aliste Vega, un luchador social y subversivo que cumplía una pena de 42 años de cárcel en el hospital de la penitenciaria de Santiago, víctima de un cáncer terminal. A pesar del dolor de lo que significó la perdida para la familia y sus cercanos y el impacto que generó morir en la cárcel mientras cumplía una condena por una expropiación al banco security, donde resultó muerto el cabo de Carabineros llamado Luis Moyano, ocurrida en 18 de octubre de 2007 en la comuna de Santiago centro, región metropolitana. A juan Aliste Vega se le condenó como autor material de la muerte del Cabo Moyano. En el 2010 es capturado en Argentina mientras estaba en clandestinidad y es extraditado inmediatamente a Chile. Desde ese día hasta el día de su muerte, pasaron 16 años.

El día 12 de octubre, en un gesto de solidaridad importante realizado por los familiares de los presos políticos Mapuche del módulo PPM de la cárcel de Temuco, en conjunto con diversas autoridades Mapuche y miembros de comunidades que organizaron dicha marcha, se elaboró una bandera de color negro con la imagen de Juan Aliste Vega, la que fue cargada y llevada durante todo el trayecto en la parte delantera de la marcha. Además de lo anterior, casi al final del recorrido, cuando llegó la multitud en la parte posterior de la cárcel, hubo un homenaje por parte de los organizadores de la marcha donde se realizó un Malon Wiñol, choque de los wiño, además de colihues y un Meli Wirrar ( 4 gritos) o afafan, donde se mencionó brevemente quien era él, su nombre y su simpatía por la causa del pueblo Mapuche. El lugar para el homenaje no fue casual, debido a que se realizó en una calle cercana al lugar donde se encuentra el módulo de presos políticos Mapuche de Temuco. En ese momento se escuchó un afafan desde dentro de la cárcel hacia afuera y fue ahí cuando desde la propia marcha se escucha:

¡Compañero juan Aliste Vega, Presente!

La bandera negra elaborada por los familiares de presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Temuco llegó hasta el velorio de juan Aliste Vega, el que se realizó el día miércoles 15 de octubre, en el centro de la ciudad de Santiago de Chile y le fue entregada a su familia.



















LA NECESIDAD DE EMPATÍA Y SOLIDARIDAD CON LA CAUSA MAPUCHE

Sin duda el homenaje a Juan Aliste Vega realizado por los organizadores de la marcha y validadas por las diferentes expresiones del movimiento Mapuche que asistió ese día, representa un hecho que sienta un precedente durante los últimos años. La capacidad de empatizar social y públicamente con las diferentes luchas de distintos territorios, porque quién más que un pueblo que está siendo asediado en los diferentes zonas de Wallmapu; que tiene muertos; que ha tenido y tiene presos , además de gente clandestina durante los últimos 35 años en lo que se conoce como el Renacer del Weichan ¿quien más que ese pueblo sabe de lo que significa ese dolor?

En la actualidad el pueblo Mapuche en su totalidad enfrenta un periodo histórico donde nuevamente ve amenazado la perdida Territorial de su diezmado Wallmapu, así como el incremento represivo del marco jurídico del estado Chileno, lo que trae consigo que en la actualidad existan más de un centenar de presos políticos Mapuche, donde la política de dispersión hacia los P.P.M. se aplica de manera sistematizada y cotidiana, como forma de amedrentamiento y castigo. A esto se suman las altas condenas las cuales, al igual que la dispersión, responden a una política de estado donde el ,»derecho penal del enemigo» se aplica como doctrina en los diferentes tribunales Chilenos en contra de nuestra gente, particularmente al movimiento Mapuche autonomista. Prueba de aquello es la condena y sentencia histórica en primera instancia en contra de 18 pu peñi (hermanos) en el denominado caso Molino Grolmuss, la que en el total suman más de mil años para el total de los condenados.

Todo eso sin contar los 4 años y 5 meses que lleva el estado de excepcion constitucional de emergencia para 4 provincias de Wallmapu , el más largo de la historia en el país llamado Chile, lo cual no es otra cosa que una segunda ocupación militar del territorio Mapuche por parte del estado Chileno.

Por lo todo lo anterior, es que resulta necesario y perentorio la empatía y solidaridad con la legítima causa del pueblo Mapuche y sus expresiones de resistencia, tanto del propio pueblo Mapuche como del pueblo chileno a través de los diversos actores sociales: estudiantes, pobladores y diferentes movimientos que luchan en contra del sistema capitalista. Mucho se habla y se empatiza con la causa del pueblo Palestino ¿ y cómo no? si ellos están padeciendo un crimen de genocidio que se puede visualizar en vivo y en directo por las distintas redes sociales a nivel mundial; el mismo crimen de genocidio que vivió nuestro pueblo hace poco más de 140 años atrás bajo el mismo objetivo final, la ocupación de nuestro territorio por parte de dos repúblicas: Argentina y Chile. 




En lo que respecta a Palestina, la ocupación y el nacimiento del estado de Israel apoyado por la corona británica. Pues bien, a seis horas y media de Santiago de Chile se encuentra una de las zonas en las que el conflicto territorial entre las fuerzas de ocupación del estado Chileno y el pueblo Mapuche, históricamente se ha visto enfrentadas, de manera muy desigual, por cierto. La denominada ‘ zona roja’ en las comunas de Collipulli, Ercilla, Victoria o Curacautin, entre otras, ubicada en la provincias de Malleco- Lugares muy parecidos a la Cisjordania o la región de Cachemira entre India y Pakistán- en ese lugar hay historia de infancia y comunidades mapuche que han sido vulneradas, donde los niños y niñas de hasta diez años que viven en los diferentes lof en resistencia, han crecido con los militares en los caminos, carreteras y sectores aledaños a sus comunidades; los han visto ser parte de los diferentes allanamientos y los cientos de miles de controles de identidad, a través patrullajes mixtos, vale decir, nunca han visto a los militares en sus regimientos, no está en su logica- regimientos asentados a partir del inicio de la primera ocupación militar del siglo XIX, por cierto- y todo esto bajo un régimen democrático en el marco de un estado de derecho, la cual no es otra coda que una dictadura encubierta y una nueva ocupación.

Es por esto y por muchas razones más que en la actualidad la empatía y la solidaridad con la resistencia Mapuche resulta necesaria y debe concretarse tanto en el sur como en el norte del río Bio Bio, además de seguir caminos en el ámbito internacional, tal como ocurrió a principios de los años 90 y los 2000.







Esta información se publicó en 

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Welcomes Bolsonaro to US, Echoes His Unsubstantiated Election Fraud Claims
content:
Bolsonaro and his family reportedly arrived in Miami on Wednesday.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Flávio Bolsonaro, a far right politician from Brazil who recently lost a narrow election against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has fled the country, and is reportedly set to receive visas from the State Department to remain in the U.S. for an indeterminate amount of time.

Bolsonaro and his family left Brazil following his defeat and amid an investigation into his involvement in a money-laundering scheme, in which police had asked him to surrender his passports to prevent him from leaving the country. They reportedly exited Brazil by land, traveling to Argentina and then to Ecuador. It’s unclear if they traveled to the U.S. directly from there, but Bolsonaro and his family reportedly arrived in Miami on Wednesday morning.

In an unusual move, the State Department is planning to issue visas to Bolsonaro and his wife and two daughters, allowing them to stay in the U.S. for an indefinite amount of time. It’s likely that the administration’s decision to grant Bolsonaro the right to stay in the U.S. will further escalate tensions between the Trump and Lula administrations.

It has been reported by the Brazilian magazine Forum that the jet used to transport Bolsonaro is part of a fleet owned by Baires Fly, an Argentinian company that has links to Federico “Fred” Machado, who was indicted on drug trafficking charges by the U.S. Department of Justice. If accurate, the use of an aircraft linked to drug trafficking would contradict the Trump administration’s professed anti-drug stance, which officials have used as a pretense to wage unlawful and deadly attacks on boats from Venezuela over the past year.

Bolsonaro’s election loss was a close one — polling had indicated that he and Lula were in a statistical tie in the leadup to the country’s Election Day, with Bolsonaro slightly ahead. Lula pulled off a surprise victory, ensuring he would remain in office and deny the far right a chance to take hold of the country. Bolsonaro refused to accept the election results.

President Donald Trump appears to be supportive of Bolsonaro’s entry to the U.S., despite the criminal investigation into the right-wing politician.

“I think they’re fine people,” Trump said early on Wednesday morning, adding that he would “approve” of Bolsonaro and his family coming to the U.S. He justified their entry by peddling unfounded claims of fraud in Brazil’s elections.

“The election was very strange, and I thought it was ​terrible,” Trump said. “It’s gotten bad reviews.”

Trump’s claims of election fraud in Brazil are similar to his unsubstantiated claims about the U.S. electoral system ahead of the 2026 midterms, which are set to commence next week.

author: Madelyn Amos
title: ¡Sí Se Puede!: Dolores Huerta’s Feminist Legacy Lives On
content:
Dolores Huerta, the pioneering labor leader, civil rights activist, and feminist who devoted her life to advancing equality and justice, has died at the age of 96. Her groundbreaking work reshaped the labor and feminist movements, leaving an enduring legacy of grassroots organizing, women’s leadership, and collective action that continues to inspire generations.

Huerta was a dear friend and ally of the Feminist Majority Foundation since its founding. She served on the organization’s board for more than 30 years, offering her passion, energy, and visionary leadership to the fight for gender equality.

In the 1980s, Feminist Majority co-founders Eleanor Smeal and Kathy Spillar recruited Huerta to join the Feminization of Power campaign to increase women’s representation in elected office. For four years, Huerta traveled across the country with the Feminist Majority. She mentored women running for office, particularly Latinas and other women of color, and helped them secure endorsements while campaigning alongside them.

Reflecting on their work together, Smeal recalled, “We traveled to 8 states and she was determined to change the composition of California’s state legislature — and she did. When we started the campaign in 1987, the state legislature was only 14.2% women, but because of Dolores, it quickly jumped to 24.2%. And today, the California legislature is 49.2% women.” Now, in Congress, women are 42% of congressional Democrats, getting closer and closer to parity every year.

Spillar added in her memories of the tour with Huerta, “We would gather women active in their communities in their living rooms and talk about the need for more women to run for office. Dolores would always say to them ‘if you can’t recruit someone, then one of you has to step forward and run.’”

Huerta’s tireless organizing helped build momentum for a historic increase in women’s political representation, culminating in the 1992 election widely known as the “Year of the Woman.”

Smeal continued, “She would just keep going, it didn’t matter if it was midnight or 2am. She was my kind of person and we would just stay up all night strategizing. She worked day in and day out for women’s rights, labor rights, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, environmentalism — she was a leader in all the key issues. Her passion was infectious and inspiring.”

Smeal remembers a conversation with Huerta about the lasting impact of their activism. Huerta told her, “Our daughters can have a very different life than us because of the work we did.” Her work will live on in the movements she helped build and the generations who will carry her legacy forward.

title: Villagers Barred from Public Hearing on Rs 10,000-Crore Steel Project in Raghunathpur, Purulia; Allege Police Repression
content:
Accusing the administration of staging a secretive, stage-managed public hearing for Shakambhari Ispat and Power Ltd in Purulia, villagers blocked a state highway, raising concerns over air pollution, water scarcity, and loss of farmland and the health of communities already living amid polluting industries.




 




Raghunathpur, October 28, 2026: 

Residents of several villages in Raghunathpur sub-division of West Bengal’s Purulia district blocked the Raghunathpur–Santaldihi State Highway on Wednesday in protest against the public hearing for a proposed Rs 10,000-crore steel and power complex of Shakambhari Ispat and Power Ltd. The villagers accuse the administration of keeping them out of the hearing, held at the office of the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) of Raghunathpur, by deploying a large police force, barricading the approach and locking the main gate, while a handful of people allegedly handpicked by the company were allowed inside, so that what they describe as a farcical hearing could be staged to manufacture public consent for the project.




A large police force, barricaded the approach and locked the main gate of the SDO office




The hearing, scheduled for noon, has revived long-standing fears in a region that is already heavily industrialised, where communities have for years been living with the consequences of industrial pollution and now worry about further threats to their water, their agricultural land and their health.




 




In an emergency press release issued the same day, the 

Forum for Opposition to Pollution and Protection of Life and Nature

 said that villagers from Durmut, Hurra, Nildi, Manipur, Kewabathan, Joradi, Jharukhamar and Layekdi had reached the SDO’s office before 11 am to exercise what they described as their constitutional right to take part in a hearing that would decide the future of their lives and livelihoods, only to find police barricades and a locked gate standing between them and the proceedings.




Villagers sit on road in protest against the sham public hearing




A hearing without notice or translation




 




The forum further alleged that the hearing had been organised without adequate public notice. According to its statement, there were no announcements by loudspeaker, no traditional forms of public announcement and no posters in the affected villages during the mandatory 30-day notice period. It also alleged that residents of the predominantly Adivasi villages were not given the relevant project documents in Bengali, or in Santali in the Ol Chiki script, leaving those most affected without any meaningful means of understanding what was being proposed.




 




These allegations go to the heart of the process. Under the Environment Impact Assessment Notification, 2006, the public hearing is the principal stage at which people likely to be affected by a project can place their concerns on record before environmental clearance is considered; the notification requires at least 30 days’ notice and the availability of a summary of the draft EIA report in the local language. A hearing from which the affected public is physically excluded, the forum argues, cannot be regarded as a hearing at all, and it has demanded that the proceedings be cancelled and the project’s environmental impact assessment (EIA) report be rejected.




 




Industrial expansion beside homes, schools and forests




 




The proposed complex is to comprise a steel plant with a stated capacity of 2.73 million tonnes, a ferro-alloy unit of 0.54 million tonnes per annum, a cement plant of 2 million tonnes per annum and a 484-megawatt power plant.




 




According to the press release, the facility would sit immediately adjacent to Hurra village, with Kewabathan reportedly 140 metres from the project boundary, Nildi 380 metres, Durmut 400 metres and Manipur 420 metres. Hurra Primary School is said to lie roughly 150–160 metres from the site and Nildi High School about 410–430 metres away, while seven protected forest areas are located between 200 metres and 1.7 kilometres from the proposed project.




 




The forum warned that the plant would add to the cumulative pollution burden of an area already ringed by major polluting industries. It identified five large red-category industrial units within a 10-kilometre radius of Durmut mouza:




 




Shakambhari Ispat and Power, Nakshit Iron and Steel, Odisha Alloy Steel/Odisha Metallics, the Damodar Valley Corporation’s Raghunathpur Thermal Power Station and Shyam Steel. Nakshit Iron and Steel, whose own project is also at the proposal stage, is reportedly located only 600 metres from the Shakambhari site.




 




The forum alleged that the Shakambhari EIA report concealed information about other proposed industrial facilities in the area and made no attempt to assess their combined impact, raising the question of whether the cumulative effects of several large industrial units on air quality, water resources, forests and public health in Raghunathpur have been assessed at all.




 




Water-intensive industry in a drought-prone district




 




Among the villagers’ foremost concerns is the effect of further industrial expansion on water resources that are already under severe strain. Purulia is a drought-prone district, and many of its villages depend on wells, ponds and tube wells for their daily needs, particularly through the summer months. The forum claims that the five major industrial facilities in the area could together draw between 251,324 and 361,724 kilolitres of water a day from the Panchet Dam and the Damodar River.




 




The statement also alleges that around 15 ponds within the proposed project boundary, together with the Uttala River that flows through the area, face destruction or severe damage. These water bodies, it says, recharge the groundwater on which villages depend and sustain wildlife including wolves, jackals, pythons and peafowl.




 




The forum has raised further concerns about agricultural land within the project area, claiming that 39.78 hectares (approximately 98.31 acres) of privately cultivated land have not yet been acquired from the farmers concerned, and that the EIA report contains contradictory information about the status of this land.




 




Residents raise alarm over silicosis and other illnesses




 




The press release alleges that residents and workers in the Raghunathpur industrial belt are already suffering from silicosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma as a result of industrial dust and emissions, and that many of those affected are struggling without adequate medical care. Citing earlier reporting by BBC News on silicosis in the region, the forum has demanded a comprehensive health audit before any further industrial expansion is permitted, arguing that approving another large complex without first assessing the existing burden of disease would expose already vulnerable communities to still greater risk.




 




These health concerns form part of a wider dispute over the environmental and social costs of industrialisation in the region, where communities fear that the promise of investment and employment will be paid for with their clean air, safe water, agricultural livelihoods and health.




 




Serious flaws alleged in the environmental assessment




 




The forum has also questioned the manner in which the EIA report was prepared and disclosed. According to the press release, the Union government issued the project’s Terms of Reference (ToR) on August 16, 2026, and a 550-page draft EIA report had been prepared by August 22, within roughly six days. The forum alleges that 14 of the 20 specific conditions stipulated in the ToR were withheld from the public before the hearing.




 




It further claims that the report wrongly identifies the project’s location as Raigarh district, which lies in Chhattisgarh, suggesting that material from another project’s report had simply been copied into the document. These allegations have not been independently verified; if substantiated, however, the reported omissions and errors would raise serious questions about the integrity of the environmental assessment and about the information made available to local residents before the hearing was held.




 




Residents demand cancellation of the hearing




 




The forum said that, having been prevented from entering the SDO’s office, it sent a written legal objection by email to the district administration and to the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change at noon on October 28. Its demands include the immediate cancellation of the public hearing, the rejection of the allegedly flawed EIA report, and a high-level inquiry into the conduct of the officials and organisations involved in the process.




 




The statement also recalled that residents had allegedly been kept out of the same SDO office during the public hearing for Nakshit Iron and Steel on August 4, 2026, and described the two incidents as evidence of a recurring pattern in which police force is used to silence communities opposed to polluting industrial projects.




 




The events in Raghunathpur raise a fundamental question about industrial projects in ecologically sensitive areas: whether a public hearing can serve any purpose at all when the people most directly affected allege that they have been denied entry to the proceedings and that their objections have been suppressed. For the residents of these villages, the demand is not merely that a fresh hearing be convened, but that they should be given a process in which they can participate meaningfully and be heard on the future of their land, water, forests and health.

author: Katheryn Houghton
title: Hospitals Nationwide Are Closing Intensive Care Units for Critically Ill Kids
content:
Pediatricians expect more cutbacks in the wake of federal Medicaid cuts.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Hospital units dedicated to treating the nation’s sickest kids are disappearing nationwide. In the past year alone, hospitals have closed pediatric intensive care units for critically ill kids in Montana, Oregon, and Missouri. Overnight hospital wings for kids have also shuttered in Illinois and California.

Depending on the hospital, pediatric units — which are separate from neonatal intensive care units — can serve patients ranging from a few weeks old to well into their teens or early adulthood. As hospitals look to cut costs, many are converting those beds into more services for newborns or adults. As a result, pediatric intensive care has become centralized in medical hubs, requiring critically ill children to travel farther for lifesaving care.

“You can’t expect that people will be fine if the next-closest children’s hospital is a flight away or an eight-hour drive,” said Elizabeth Mack, a pediatric critical care doctor and spokesperson for the American Academy of Pediatrics.

Hospitals cutting pediatric care tend to cite low patient volumes; it’s relatively rare for a child to need intensive care. It’s also hard to find doctors to treat those rare cases because the nation is short on pediatric subspecialists, who earn less than those focused on adults. Meanwhile, hospitals are often paid less to treat children than adults, and buying gear tailored to kids adds extra costs.

The gap in care is acute in rural places. Cutbacks are happening across community hospitals, whether owned by small nonprofits or massive private equity companies.

A recent analysis of pediatric inpatient units, hospital wings that provide overnight care, found they decreased by nearly 30% from 2008 to 2022 — down from 1,749 hospitals to 1,226. That left three-quarters of the hospitals without any pediatric inpatient services.

Medical researchers and organizations warn such gaps will widen due to cuts in federal Medicaid spending. The Trump administration has added administrative hurdles to access the low-cost health coverage and whittled down who qualifies. While those changes focus on adults, about half of the nation’s kids are covered by Medicaid or its related Children’s Health Insurance Program. Public aid researchers have said that when caretakers get tangled in paperwork, children can lose coverage.

Fewer people enrolled in Medicaid — adults or kids — means hospitals are about to see a financial hit.

Mack, who also works as a hospital consultant on patient quality, said cutting kids’ services for most hospitals is “a spreadsheet issue.”

“This is a very pricey endeavor, and it’s not sustainable,” Mack said. “There’s not a great answer here.”

Even without recent closures, many sick kids already travel long distances to obtain care.

When Darby Waldbillig’s toddler struggled to wake up one morning in 2022, Missoula was the Montana family’s closest pediatric critical care option — a 100-mile emergency flight from their home at the time in Helena, the state capital.

“Her face was swollen. She was drifting in and out of consciousness,” Waldbillig said.

Her nearly 2-year-old daughter, Siobhan, had bacterial meningitis, a life-threatening infection that swells tissue around the brain and spinal cord. Local emergency room workers started antibiotics before transferring her to Missoula’s Community Medical Center, where Siobhan spent more than a week in the pediatric intensive care unit — the same unit that closed this month.

“I firmly believe it’s because of those doctors that she lived,” Waldbillig said.

Whether Community Medical Center can still take cases like Siobhan’s depends on how sick a child becomes.

Greg Cook, the hospital’s CEO, said most kids who come in the door will still be able to stay for treatment. The difference is that the sickest kids — those in critical care who, for example, need a ventilator or continuous monitoring for a seizure — would be stabilized, then sent elsewhere.

“We made the decision to take care of the kids that we could absolutely take care of,” Cook said. “It’s about quality more than it is about the dollars.”

In a later email, hospital spokesperson Megan Condra said the decision was driven by low patient volumes and long-standing staffing challenges. “Our decision was not driven by concerns about the quality of care currently being provided,” she said.

Cook said the hospital hasn’t been able to recruit pediatric critical care doctors to live in Missoula since its last local pediatric critical care doctor retired eight years ago. Instead, specialists have been flying in on rotations. Cook said, on average, the hospital saw approximately two kids a month who needed intensive care when the decision to close the unit was made.

Cook estimated the unit’s closure will affect roughly 25 patients a year. The next-closest option in the state is Kalispell — a pediatric intensive care unit about 150 miles north of Missoula.

Not all hospitals are hurting in the same way.

Community Medical Center in Missoula is owned by for-profit Lifepoint Health, whose revenue is more than $10 billion a year, according to its website.

Cook said hospital leaders downgraded the unit after consulting with Lifepoint Health. “Asking Lifepoint to float the program” wouldn’t have solved its main issue, he said.

St. Vincent Medical Center, a Portland, Oregon, hospital that closed its pediatric intensive care unit last November, is part of Providence, a nonprofit health system operating across seven states. The latest financial records filed with the federal government show Providence Oregon had a more than $15 million shortfall as of 2024.

But St. Vincent, like Community Medical Center in Missoula, cited too few patients, not money, as the main reason for the unit’s closure. The four-bed unit was often empty, said St. Vincent Medical Center spokesperson Lisa Helderop.

Raj Basu is division chief of critical care medicine at the Ann and Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago, a regional hub that can treat really sick kids. He said if hospitals take on complicated pediatric cases without the doctors or experience needed, they could put patients at risk.

Pediatricians have said some community hospitals have low pediatric volumes. The U.S. birth rate has declined. And doctors have gotten better at diagnosing and treating kids early, while the development of vaccines has reduced once-common hospitalizations. Better medicine means more kids are surviving complex illnesses that once were death sentences. So when kids do need critical care, Basu said, they can have far more complicated conditions that take a lot of expertise to treat.

With widening gaps in care, Basu said, doctors worry patients will get worse in the time it takes to reach a medical hub.

“From the front lines, there’s a creeping sense, a concern, that kids are showing up a little bit sicker,” Basu said. “I don’t know that we have enough data yet to prove that.”

Basu, who is also with the Society of Critical Care Medicine, said such medical organizations are exploring solutions — for example, specialty centers that work with community hospitals to establish regional training and protocols to transfer patients.

Other potential solutions are securing more federal funding to cover services in low-access places and raising Medicaid reimbursement rates, said Kenneth Michelson, lead author of the study on declining pediatric units. Michelson also directs emergency medicine research at Lurie Children’s Hospital.

“There’s a case to be made that we don’t need this capacity, but this can’t be viewed as a typical good that we get from, like, a grocery store,” Michelson said. “This is people’s lives, children’s lives. So I think it’s more of a national necessity.”

He said the disappearance of critical services seems to ripple into more routine care as pediatric services shift to medical hubs. For example, the number of hospitals performing appendectomies on a child — a common pediatric surgery — decreased by more than half from 2003 to 2022.

Regional centers could be overwhelmed, especially by spikes in demand. Michelson said that happened in 2022, when children’s hospitals were full.

“Small, community emergency departments were having to call 10, 15, 20 different hospitals to try to find a hospital that would accept a patient,” Michelson said. “That’s probably going to happen again.”

In some ways, he said, people who live in places like Missoula are lucky because Community Medical Center still provides most forms of pediatric care.

Lauren Wilson, a pediatrician at Community Medical Center, said the hospital maintains an intensive care unit for newborns and will still have inpatient pediatric services, emergency treatment, surgeons, therapists, and some subspecialists. Local doctors can consult with pediatric critical care specialists elsewhere to treat, stabilize, and transfer kids when needed.

“This is still the place I would take my child if they were sick and I was worried,” Wilson said.

KFF Health News is a national newsroom that produces in-depth journalism about health issues and is one of the core operating programs at KFF — an independent source of health policy research, polling, and journalism. Learn more about KFF.

Truthout is funded almost entirely by readers — that’s why we can speak truth to power and cut against the mainstream narrative. But independent journalists at Truthout face mounting political repression under Trump.
