author: Cas Smith
title: Brazil: Lula’s election victory was won in the streets
content:
Australia’s Brazilian community joined their compatriots worldwide in a wave of street mobilisations in support of incumbent President Luiz Inácio “Lula” da Silva, ahead of his election victory on October 25.

Lula, who was first elected president in 2002, pulled ahead of right-wing opponent Flávio Bolsonaro — the son of jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro — winning the second round run-off election by 4.4 million votes.

Significantly, this came after Bolsonaro won the first round on October 4, which prompted Brazilians to hit the streets in a significant movement to bolster Lula’s profile, and to prevent a “second Bolsonaro” presidency.

Students and the country’s working class largely led these mobilisations, which included a gathering of more than one million Lula supporters on Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana Beach the day before the election.

Around Australia, similar protests were held prior to the election, including at Scarborough Beach in Boorloo/Perth, on October 22. Organiser Pedro told Green Left that many Brazilians were afraid their country could become mired in corruption and instability under a Bolsonaro government.

“Unfortunately, we experienced Bolsonaro snr’s government for four years between 2018 and 2022,” he said.

“They were the ones in power during the [COVID-19] pandemic, which was devastating for the country in many ways, because we were denied access to vaccines and the government failed to invest in our healthcare system; the doctors were completely ignored.

“This was only a tiny part of what this government did — we have seen enough.”

Pedro said Flávio Bolsonaro’s close ties to United States President Donald Trump was a concern, highlighting Trump’s coup against Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro earlier this year and his influence on far-right Argentine President Javier Milei.

The October 25 election delivered a comprehensive win to Lula, who received 64.3 million votes, compared to Bolsonaro’s 59.8 million. This was the first time that a candidate won the presidential election after a first-round defeat.

Despite Lula’s victory, when the new Congress convenes in February next year, Bolsonaro’s party will control 28 seats in the Senate (35% of the total) and 121 seats in the lower house (24%) as well as five governorships (19%), which — once alliances are factored in — will mean the right will have bigger majorities in both houses for Lula’s next administration.

“We are trying to unite the maximum number of people in this movement,” Pedro said.

“We want to show that we are here for our freedom, our democracy, and we have something to defend against the people who are trying to take over the government again in Brazil.”

Despite Bolsonaro’s initial pledge to annul the outcome, the leader of his Liberal Party, Valdemar Costa Neto, issued a statement on October 26 accepting the election result.

Bolsonaro’s protest revolved around a last-minute extension to voting hours, which prompted him to say, in a post-election speech to supporters, that “We will take legal action.”

This was despite the fact that both sides had called for the extension: Bolsonaro’s camp said that heavy rains in the country’s south (where he enjoys popular support) would prevent people from reaching polling stations.

Lula’s side meanwhile, said that extended voting hours were necessary, citing the alleged restriction of public transport by some city administrations, which they said was an attempt to curtail the working-class vote. Bolstering this interpretation were media reports that Pablo Souza, a transportation official in the city of Salvador, had been arrested on election day.

The decision to extend voting hours was made by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, who had been appointed to the court by Lula in 2023, and had previously been the president’s personal lawyer. These factors prompted Bolsonaro to cry foul, claiming the decision negatively impacted his voting base.

However, close analysis of the election results suggests the extension allowed for only 35,000 additional votes across Brazil, comprising 0.03% of the total. Given Lula’s victory by 4.4 million votes, this appears negligible.

Some of Bolsonaro’s supporters questioned the result, with Trump describing it as “another rigged election”. However, he did not go so far as to promise intervention on behalf of Bolsonaro.

Given Jair Bolsonaro’s failed coup against Lula after the latter’s election victory in 2022, many analysts are watching to see what his son will do next. Brazilian news outlet Folha de S.Paulo reported on October 26 that legal advisors and political allies encouraged Bolsonaro to drop his annulment request, based on Lula’s significant victory margin, in addition to its validation by the Supreme Court and election authorities.

Analysing the election, Revista Movimiento, the publication of Brazil’s Socialist Left Movement (MES), said: “The victory, however, has not resolved the country’s political contradictions. Although Lula gathered enough votes to win, the new Congress continues to be predominantly conservative, and will likely hinder any social, economic, and environmental measures or partial implementation of Lula’s program.

“Lula’s re-election demonstrates that the advantage gained in the first round was not irreversible. The combination of in-person mobilisation, digital organisation, a change in strategy and greater voter turnout allowed the president to overcome the initial disadvantage and win another term.

“The result also highlights the limitations of a presidential contest isolated from the composition of the legislature. The left won the national election, but will have to face a strengthened parliamentary opposition and a society that remains politically divided.

“The next term will therefore be marked by a dual requirement: to transform the commitments made during the campaign into concrete policies, and to preserve the mobilisation capacity that helped produce the electoral turnaround. The strength demonstrated in the streets and on social media will be an important political asset, but its influence will depend on the continuity of popular organisation and the ability to convert social support into effective achievements.”

As reported in International Viewpoint, journalist and ecosocialist Iain Bruce, who was in Brazil for the election, said: “This is the most important defeat for the far right we have seen anywhere in the world in recent times, and its impact will be felt worldwide. Seeing those millions and millions of people pour onto the streets across this vast country to celebrate was enough to make you weep.

“The seemingly impossible turnaround in the second round is not a simple electoral victory. It was won in the streets and on socials.

“Immediately after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, won in the first round, thousands of mainly very young people took to streets in Niteroi, across the bay from Rio de Janeiro, to demonstrate against the likelihood of a neo-fascist government in Brazil. The same thing happened in cities in the Northeast, the most impoverished region. This was repeated throughout the country in the three weeks between the rounds.

“In parallel, younger members of congress from a smaller party supporting Lula’s Workers Party, completely revamped the campaign’s lacklustre social media presence. Lula’s Army, a Whatsapp channel launched by André Janones of the Rede party, went from 50,000 followers to a million in two days. Now, it has 10 million.

“What the Brazilian people have achieved can be a huge inspiration for all of us facing resurgent varieties of neo-fascism and the far right in different parts of the world. But they will also need support. We should be thinking now about how to organise that solidarity.”

author: Andrea DiP
title: Um beijo em uma mulher trans
content:
A cena toda deve ter durado cerca de três segundos: A deputada federal Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) faz um vídeo comemorando a eleição de Lula após a contagem das urnas, no dia 25 de outubro. Ele passa por ela, pega seu rosto, tasca um beijo carinhoso em sua bochecha e sai do quadro. Um gesto simples, espontâneo, terno, um carinho. 




Eu não sei se Lula tem noção do tamanho da declaração que fez pro mundo.

 O presidente de um país, que acaba de ser reeleito em um processo histórico e inédito em tantos níveis – com participação popular e engajamento sociais sem igual, em uma virada épica que acontece apesar de todo tipo de sabotagem das 

Big Techs

 ao governo Trump, de tentativas de boicote ao 

transporte público

 para que as pessoas não chegassem às urnas a uma grande imprensa tacanha jogando contra – 

um homem de 81 anos, que tem os olhos do mundo virados para si, mostra publicamente afeto a uma mulher trans. 
















Trecho de vídeo publicado por Erika Hilton




Essa cena me emociona por diferentes motivos. Tenho passado os últimos anos me infiltrando em eventos da extrema direita pelo mundo e entrevistando essas figuras. Posso afirmar que não houve um desses congressos sequer, nenhuma dessas conversas, que não passou por discursos ultraviolentos contra pessoas trans. 




Já escrevi bastante sobre isso, inclusive sobre como no governo Trump essa violência levou a resoluções e políticas públicas desde seu primeiro dia de mandato. Não vou me repetir aqui sobre a maneira como essas narrativas são construídas com base no pânico moral e na ideia da destruição da família e de valores sagrados. O que quero ressaltar é que 

a demonização de pessoas trans está hoje no epicentro político da extrema direita. É um tema de consenso entre eles, usado para mobilizar o medo, o ressentimento e o ódio e que tem efeitos concretos na vida de milhares de pessoas. 




E a mobilização desses afetos não é exclusiva da extrema direita, também é importante dizer. Não sei dizer quantas vezes eu mesma fui perseguida, ameaçada e exposta por mulheres que se dizem feministas radicais trans excludentes ou quantas vezes o Pauta Pública foi alvo de ódio quando apontamos nosso microfone para pessoas trans. Tudo bem. Como me disse Judith Butler, ser perseguida por essas pessoas é um distintivo de coragem. 




Um outro ponto importante é que 

o Brasil é um dos países que mais mata transexuais no mundo

. Quando Lula faz esse gesto, que mensagem ele manda para o povo? E que mensagem ele manda para as pessoas trans?




A cena me lembrou o relato de Suzanne Hommel, uma alemã nascida em 1938 que falou no documentário “Encontro com Lacan” sobre o tempo em que foi paciente do psicanalista francês. Ela carregava traumas profundos de sua vivência durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial, mas, em uma de suas sessões com Lacan, contou de um sonho recorrente que a acordava sob forte angústia todos os dias pontualmente às 5h da manhã. Acrescentou o contexto histórico de sua infância: “Era às 5h da manhã que a Gestapo vinha buscar os judeus em suas casas”. Ao ouvir a palavra “Gestapo” (polícia secreta oficial da Alemanha Nazista) o psicanalista levantou-se rapidamente da poltrona e fez um carinho suave em seu rosto. Quando ela conta isso no documentário, imediatamente leva a mão ao rosto imitando o gesto. 




Através desse ato físico e verbal, Lacan transformou a palavra “Gestapo” em “geste à peau”, que em francês significa “gesto na pele”, e introduziu ternura onde antes habitava apenas o horror e o trauma. No documentário, ela se emociona ao dizer que isso não apagou seu sofrimento mas o modificou de forma definitiva e que mesmo décadas depois, ela ainda sentia aquele toque que mudou a forma como olhava para a própria história e sua própria dor. 




O “geste à peau” de Lula em Erika Hilton neste momento da nossa história, me parece muito poderoso, simbólico, um marco de posição diante do mundo, que pode ressignificar um monte de afetos pra muita gente. E ao mesmo tempo é tão bonito precisamente porque foi um afago espontâneo em um país que está ressignificando sua relação com a política, que ainda sofre com o trauma dos quatro anos sob o governo genocida de Bolsonaro – e que escolheu neste domingo apostar na ternura ao invés do horror.




Aliás, que fique marcado aqui: Erika Hilton foi reeleita como a mulher mais votada da história para a Câmara dos Deputados e, com 1,5 milhão de votos conquistados em São Paulo, é a segunda parlamentar no país a romper a barreira de 1 milhão de votos para o cargo.

author: Sabrina Engel
title: Weniger Schutz für „Versuchstiere“: 80.000 Menschen unterschreiben gegen neues Gesetz
content:
Die Bundesregierung plant ein eigenes Gesetz für 

Tierversuche

 und die Herausnahme der Tierversuchsregelungen aus dem Tierschutzgesetz. Dies könnte den Schutzstandard der Tiere enorm schwächen und es könnte erlaubt werden, was zurzeit noch strafbar ist, unter anderem massenhafte Tötungen, Eingriffe ohne Betäubung und Verstümmelungen. Weniger strenge Kontrollen könnten ebenfalls eine Folge sein.   




Ein solches Gesetz könnte Tieren den ohnehin unzureichenden Schutz nehmen und sie noch größerem 

Leid im Versuchslabor

 aussetzen.  




Daher haben wir von PETA Deutschland gemeinsam mit zahlreichen weiteren Tierschutzorganisationen Anfang des Jahres eine Bundestagspetition gestartet – mit großem Zuspruch: Innerhalb von sechs Wochen haben weit über 80.000 Menschen die Petition unterzeichnet. Damit wurde die erforderliche Zahl von 30.000 Stimmen für die weitere Behandlung im Bundestag weit übertroffen. [1] Die Petition fordert die Bundesregierung auf, Regelungen zu Tierversuchen im Tierschutzgesetz zu belassen und aktuelle Standards zum Schutz der Tiere nicht noch weiter herabzusenken.   




Anhörung im Bundestag legt Mängel im Vorhaben der Bundesregierung offen

 




Am 12. Oktober 2026 fand die offizielle Anhörung vor dem Petitionsausschuss statt. [2] Der Jurist und Hauptpetent Dr. Christoph Maisack (Deutsche Juristische Gesellschaft für Tierschutzrecht) – unterstützt von Dr. Tamara Zietek (Ärzte gegen Tierversuche) – machte die Mängel des Vorhabens der Bundesregierung sowohl in seiner Rede als auch während der Diskussion deutlich.  




Die zahlreichen Fragen der anwesenden Bundestagsabgeordneten an die Regierungsvertreter:innen legten vor allem offen, was wir in der Petition schon darlegen: Ein eigenständiges Tierversuchsgesetz ist weder notwendig noch der richtige Weg, um die Forschenden zu entlasten – birgt aber die große Gefahr, dass Tiere in Laboren noch weniger gesetzlichen Schutz bekommen.  




Die Petition befindet sich nun in der Prüfung. Wir setzen uns weiterhin dafür ein, dass die Regelungen zu Tierversuchen im Tierschutzgesetz bleiben und der ohnehin unzureichende Schutz der Tiere nicht weiter geschwächt wird. Dazu arbeiten wir beispielsweise gemeinsam mit anderen Organisationen an der Modernisierung und Aktualisierung anderer Dokumente (z. B. der Allgemeinen Verwaltungsvorschrift für das Tierschutzgesetz), die die Umsetzung des geltenden Tierschutzrechts einheitlich für alle Tiere festlegen.  




 

Wir bedanken uns bei allen, die die Petition unterschrieben, verbreitet und gemeinsam mit uns zur erfolgreichsten Bundestagspetition im Bereich Tierschutz aller Zeiten gemacht haben!

  




Hintergrund zum geplanten neuen

 

TierVERSUCHSgesetz: Das könnte die Entkopplung vom TierSCHUTZgesetz bedeuten 

 




Die Bundesregierung kündigte an, ein eigenständiges Gesetz für Tierversuche erschaffen zu wollen: 

Tierversuche sollen damit vom Tierschutzgesetz abgekoppelt werden

. Für 

die unzähligen Tiere

, die in Versuchen missbraucht werden, könnte das noch 

weniger Schutz

 und noch 

mehr Leid

 bedeuten: 







Das 

Tierschutzgesetz

 enthält zentrale 

Schutz- und Wertungsnormen

. 




Diese Grundnormen gelten bislang 

für alle Tiere gleichermaßen

, auch für Tiere in Tierversuchen. 




Sie stellen eine wesentliche 

rechtliche Schranke

 gegen das 

Zufügen von Schmerzen, Leiden und Schäden

 und gegen das 

Töten von Tieren

 aus wirtschaftlichen Gründen dar. 




Genau diese 

Schutzwirkung

 könnte durch Herausnahme der sogenannten Versuchstiere aus dem TierSCHUTZgesetz und die Einführung eines TierVERSUCHSgesetzes 

beseitigt

 werden. Auch die Tierärzteschaft spricht sich deutlich gegen dieses Vorhaben aus. [1] 







Mögliche Folgen eines neuen Tierversuchsgesetzes

 




Eine zentrale Konsequenz dieser Entkopplung könnte z. B. für sogenannte 

überzählige „Versuchstiere“

 entstehen: Das 

Töten von überlebenden oder „überzähligen“ Tieren

 aus rein wirtschaftlichen Gründen – was bislang nach dem Tierschutzgesetz strafbar ist – könnte 

ausdrücklich erlaubt

 

werden

. 




Darüber hinaus könnte ein eigenständiges TierVERSUCHSgesetz zu einer weiteren 

Absenkung des ohnehin unzureichenden Schutzniveaus

 führen: 







Die Tierversuchslobby fordert die 

Vereinfachung von Genehmigungsverfahren

 und die 

Reduktion der behördlichen Prüftiefe

 (insbesondere in Form von Nachfragen). 




Die Funktion von 

Kontrollen

 könnten außerdem 

weiter geschwächt

 werden. 







Bereits heute belegen zahlreiche Fälle, dass die Kontrolle von Tierversuchen häufig unzureichend ist (Vollzugsdefizit). 




Geplant ist zudem eine 

Verlagerung und Zentralisierung der Genehmigungen

 in die 

Zuständigkeit des Bundesministeriums

 für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt. 




Der aktuelle „Schutz“ von sogenannten Versuchstieren darf nicht verschlechtert werden!

 




Der Schutz von Tieren in Versuchslaboren ist Stand heute bereits unzureichend. Das belegte unter anderem das gegen Deutschland geführte EU-Vertragsverletzungsverfahren wegen 

mangelhafter Umsetzung der EU-Tierversuchsrichtlinie

 2010/63. Trotz dessen Einstellung 2022 nach gesetzlichen Anpassungen bestehen weiterhin 

Defizite in der deutschen Rechtslage

. Statt diese zu beheben und den Tierschutz zu stärken, könnte mit einem eigenständigen Tierversuchsgesetz nun eine 

weitere Verschlechterung

 

drohen

. 




Seit 1972 hielten alle Bundesregierungen an dem Grundsatz fest, dass ein 

einmal erreichter Tierschutzstandard nicht wieder abgesenkt

 werden darf. [3] Dieser Grundsatz ist durch das Staatsziel Tierschutz in Art. 20a Grundgesetz (GG) verfassungsrechtlich anerkannt und gestärkt worden, unter anderem mit der Verpflichtung zum „Schutz der Tiere vor nicht artgemäßer Haltung [und] vermeidbaren Leiden“. Ein eigenständiges Tierversuchsgesetz würde durch Verminderung der zentralen Schutzmechanismen diesem Verfassungsauftrag widersprechen. 




Die Diskussion über Tierversuche darf nicht von Personen beherrscht werden, die ihre 

Karriere mit Tierversuchen

 begründet haben und die Chancen einer 

tierversuchsfreien, zukunftsorientierten Forschung

 nicht erkennen oder nutzen. 













Die Herauslösung des Tierversuchsbereichs aus dem Tierschutzgesetz könnte einen 

gravierender Rückschritt für den Tierschutz

, für rechtsstaatliche Prinzipien und das Vertrauen der Gesellschaft in eine nach ethischen Grundsätzen verantwortungsvoll handelnde Wissenschaft bedeuten.
















 

Jetzt lesen













Speziesismus







Tierversuche & Ethik: Tiermissbrauch ist moralisch nie vertretbar




Passen Tierversuche und Ethik zusammen? Erfahren Sie, warum Tierversuche moralisch nicht vertretbar sind.




Jetzt lesen
















 




Wir fordern von der Bundesregierung, dass

 







sie den ohnehin laschen Schutz von Tieren, die in Versuchslaboren gefangen gehalten werden, nicht weiter abbaut, sondern verstärkt. 




sie sich für den Ausbau einer modernen und humanrelevanten Forschung ohne Tierversuche einsetzt. 







Jetzt Ausstieg aus Tierversuchen unterstützen

 




Die Bundestagspetition ist beendet – doch unser Einsatz für eine moderne, tierfreie Forschung geht weiter. Mit dem Research Modernisation Deal haben PETA-Wissenschaftler:innen eine konkrete Strategie entwickelt, die aufzeigt, wie Tierversuche schrittweise beendet und durch moderne, für den Menschen relevante Methoden ersetzt werden können. 




Unterstützen Sie jetzt den Research Modernisation Deal und fordern Sie gemeinsam mit uns einen

 

verbindlichen Plan für den Ausstieg aus

 

Tierversuchen.

 








		Jetzt Ausstieg aus Tierversuchen fordern	







Häufige Fragen










Bringt die Petition überhaupt etwas?







Wenn eine Bundestagspetition mindestens 30.000 Unterschriften innerhalb der Frist erhält, muss der Bundestag sich mit dem Thema auseinandersetzen.

 




Und darum ist es wichtig, 

solche 

Petitionen zu unterstützen:

 







 Petitionen sind ein direktes demokratisches Mittel







Sie zeigen, welche Themen der Gesellschaft wichtig sind. Eine Petition ist ein deutliches Signal an die Politik: „Wir fordern Veränderung – und zwar von euch!“

 







 Petitionen beeinflussen politische Entscheidungen mittel- und langfristig







Und zwar durch erhöhten öffentlichen und politischen Druck. Viele Verbesserungen im Tierschutz, Umweltschutz und bei sozialen Themen begannen mit einer Petition. Das heißt: Petitionen schaffen Bewusstsein, stoßen politische Prozesse an und bereiten den Weg für spätere Gesetzesänderungen.

 







Jede Stimme zählt.







Es sind 30.000 Unterschriften erforderlich

, um das Thema in den Bundestag zu bekommen. 

Eine 

Stimme kann genau die sein, die am Ende den Unterschied macht.

 







 Petitionen regen gesellschaftliche Diskussionen an







Gerade Themen, die sonst ignoriert oder verdrängt werden (wie z. B. Tierversuche an Affen), rücken so in den Fokus der Medien und Politik. Petitionen können Debatten in Medien, der Gesellschaft und Parlamenten auslösen und ethische Standards verschieben.

 







 Wer nicht handelt, ändert nichts







Petitionen sind eine einfache Möglichkeit, aktiv zu werden – ohne Geld, mit nur wenigen Minuten Aufwand, aber mit Wirkung. Die Petition unterschreiben heißt: 

Ich sehe nicht weg, ich akzeptiere keine Tierquälerei!

 













Wie viele Menschen haben die Petition unterstützt?







Innerhalb der vorgegebenen Frist haben

 80.700 Menschen die Bundestagspetition gegen das geplante Tierversuchsgesetz unterzeichnet. Damit wurde die erforderliche Zahl von 30.000 Stimmen deutlich überschritten.













Wie geht es nach Ende der Petition weiter?







Die Mitzeichnungsfrist endete am 31. August 2026. Die Petition befindet sich nun in der Prüfung. Da mehr als 30.000 Menschen die Petition unterstützt haben, muss sich der Petitionsausschuss mit dem Anliegen befassen.













Was fordert die Petition?







Die Petition fordert, das geplante eigenständige Tierversuchsgesetz zu stoppen und die Regelungen zu Tierversuchen im Tierschutzgesetz zu belassen. Damit soll verhindert werden, dass bestehende Schutzmechanismen für Tiere in Versuchslaboren geschwächt werden.






















Quellen







[1] Deutscher Bundestag. Petition 194593. Tierversuche. Stopp des geplanten Tierversuchsgesetzes vom 02.02.2026. Accessed September 3, 2026. 

https://epetitionen.bundestag.de/petitionen/_2026/_02/_02/Petition_194593.$$$.a.u.html

 

 




[2] Bundestierärztekammer e. V. Anträge zum 30. Deutschen Tierärztetag mit Beschlussempfehlungen des BTK-Präsidiums und Abstimmungsergebnissen. 

October 10, 2025. Accessed September 3, 2026. 

https://www.bundestieraerztekammer.de/btk/tieraerztetag/2025/Antraege_inkl-Beschluessen.pdf

 




[3] Deutscher Bundestag. Gesetzentwurf der Bundesregierung. Entwurf eines Gesetzes zur Änderung des Tierschutzgesetzes. 

Drucksache 13/7015. February 21, 1997. Accessed September 3, 2026. 

https://dserver.bundestag.de/btd/13/070/1307015.pdf

 




[4] Deutscher Bundestag. Gesetzentwurf der Bundesregierung. Entwurf eines Gesetzes zur

 Änderung des Tierschutzgesetzes. Drucksache 13/7015. February 21, 1997. Accessed September 3, 2026.

 

https://dserver.bundestag.de/btd/13/070/1307015.pdf

Weniger Schutz für „Versuchstiere“: 80.000 Menschen unterschreiben gegen neues Gesetz 

 appeared first on 

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

author: Mag
title: unter_bau: Alternative Hochschulgewerkschaft an der Goethe-Universität Frankfurt
content:
Dossier




„

Heute geht die Gewerkschaftsinitiative unter_bau erstmals an die Öffentlichkeit. Dabei handelt es sich um einen Zusammenschluss rund 50 Hochschulangehöriger aus unterschiedlichen Statusgruppen, die seit knapp einem Jahr den Aufbau einer alternativen Gewerkschaft für den Frankfurter Hochschulbereich vorbereiten. Die angestrebte Gewerkschaft soll alle Angestellten- und Statusgruppen der Universität umfassen und nach partizipatorischen und föderalen Prinzipien funktionieren. Insbesondere will die Initiative die Organisation nicht auf die klassischen Gewerkschaftsfelder beschränken, sondern darüber hinaus (hochschul-)politisch auf die allgemeine Verfasstheit der Universität Einfluss nehmen. Als perspektivisches Ziel benennt die Initiative eine grundlegende Transformation der Hochschule in eine basisdemokratische Selbstverwaltung

…“ 

Pressemitteilung vom 20. April 2016 auf der Homepage der Initiative unter_bau

 

 und alle Informationen bis zur nun vollendeten Gründung und den Aktivitäten danach:







Goethe-Universität streicht Hunderte Hilfskraftstellen – unter_bau kündigt Widerstand gegen Kürzungspolitik an 

 


„

An der Goethe-Universität Frankfurt droht ein massiver Stellenabbau unter studentischen Beschäftigten. Im Rahmen des sogenannten „Stellenumbaus“ sollten die bisherigen Hilfskraftstellen in den Bibliotheken, im Hochschulrechenzentrum (HRZ) und in der Verwaltung ursprünglich in reguläre, tariflich bezahlte Beschäftigungsverhältnisse überführt werden. Doch statt besserer Arbeitsbedingungen und tariflicher Absicherung droht nun die Streichung von rund 300 bis 400 Stellen. Ab Januar 2027 sollen in den Bibliotheken keine neuen Hilfskraftverträge mehr vergeben werden. Auch in der zentralen Verwaltung sollen künftig kaum Studierende mehr beschäftigt werden. Für die Hochschulgewerkschaft unter_bau ist klar: Die Beschäftigten dürfen nicht die Rechnung für die Kürzungspolitik der Landesregierung und des Universitätspräsidiums bezahlen.


„Die Universitätsleitung verspricht tarifliche Beschäftigung und streicht gleichzeitig Hunderte Stellen. Das ist ein Schlag ins Gesicht der Kolleg_innen, die seit Jahren die Bibliotheken, die Verwaltung und andere zentrale Einrichtungen am Laufen halten. Wir werden nicht zulassen, dass die versprochene Überführung in den Tarifvertrag als Vorwand für einen massiven Personalabbau genutzt wird. Wir werden gemeinsam mit unseren Mitgliedern alle uns zur Verfügung stehenden gewerkschaftlichen Aktionsmittel ausschöpfen, um diese Stellenstreichungen zu verhindern“, erklärt Daniel Katzenmaier, Pressesprecher der Hochschulgewerkschaft unter_bau.


Der geplante Abbau trifft nicht nur die unmittelbar betroffenen Hilfskräfte. Die Aufgaben in Bibliotheken, Verwaltung und Hochschulrechenzentrum verschwinden nicht einfach mit den gestrichenen Stellen. Vielmehr drohen eine massive Arbeitsverdichtung für die verbleibenden Beschäftigten und weitere Einschränkungen für Studierende.


„Seit Jahren wird an den Hochschulen gespart, während die Arbeitsbelastung steigt. Jetzt sollen ausgerechnet diejenigen ihren Arbeitsplatz verlieren, die ohnehin häufig unter prekären Bedingungen beschäftigt sind. Statt die Arbeitsverhältnisse endlich tariflich abzusichern, will die Universität einen Großteil der Stellen beseitigen. Wir brauchen mehr Personal, bessere Arbeitsbedingungen und eine vollständige Überführung der betroffenen Beschäftigten in den Tarifvertrag – keine Entlassungswelle!“, erklärt Katzenmaier abschließend.


Die Hochschulgewerkschaft unter_bau fordert einen sofortigen Stopp des geplanten Stellenabbaus. Die ursprünglich angekündigte Überführung in tariflich abgesicherte Beschäftigungsverhältnisse muss umgesetzt werden, ohne dass dabei Arbeitsplätze verloren gehen. Die Gewerkschaft unterstützt die heutige Hilfskräftevollversammlung des Hilfskräfterates um 14 Uhr am Campus Westend und wird sich in den kommenden Wochen an den Protestaktionen der Hilfskräfte beteiligen

.“ Pressemitteilung der Hochschulgewerkschaft unter_bau vom 26.10.2026 per e-mail, siehe auch auf deren Homepage die 

Einladung

 

 zur Hilfskräfte Vollversammlung am 27.10.2026







Siehe auch im Dossier: 

Hochschulpakte und Sparmaßnahmen an den Hochschulen: Kürzungen stoppen – Hochschulen und Studierendenwerke unterstützen!

: Bildung hat Priorität: An hessischen Hochschulen wächst der Widerstand gegen Kürzungspläne der Landesregierung und Hochschulleitungen










Prekarisierung studentischer Arbeit: »Wenn alle streiken, wäre es still an der Uni« – bekommen aber an der Frankfurter Goethe-Uni nicht einmal die Arbeitsmittel 







Hilfskräfte fordern: Goethe-Uni soll notwendige Arbeitsmittel endlich zur Verfügung stellen




„

An der Goethe-Universität Frankfurt arbeiten über 2.000 studentische Hilfskräfte unter prekären Bedingungen – viele von ihnen ohne Zugang zu dienstlichen Arbeitsmitteln. Immer wieder wird von Hilfskräften erwartet, dass für wissenschaftliche Tätigkeiten wie Recherche, Korrekturen oder der Vorbereitung und Durchführung von Tutorien private Laptops genutzt werden. Das stellt nicht nur eine finanzielle Belastung dar, sondern ist auch datenschutzrechtlich problematisch.


„Ich habe selbst erlebt, wie absurd das ist: Als Hilfskraft musste ich mit meinem eigenen Laptop arbeiten, dabei besitze ich keinen und kann mir so eine Anschaffung nicht einfach leisten. Ich kenne viele Kolleg*innen, denen es genauso geht. Die Universität lässt uns im Regen stehen“, sagt Chenoa Luna Brach, studentische Beschäftigte und Gewerkschaftssekretärin bei unter_bau.


Zwar erkennt die Dienststellenleitung das Problem an, verweist jedoch auf die Institute – diese wiederum verweisen auf fehlende Finanzmittel. Die Hochschulgewerkschaft unter_bau kritisiert diese mangelnde Verantwortungsübernahme in einem Beschluss vom 15. April 2025. (…) Deshalb fordert die Gewerkschaft, dass die Dienststellenleitung der Goethe-Universität ein eigenes Budget für Arbeitsmittel schafft, etwa durch einen zentral verwalteten Laptop-Pool, auf den Institute und Hilfskräfte unkompliziert zugreifen können. Dieser Schritt soll nun auf einem Gründungskongress vom 18. bis 20. November vollzogen werden. Anna Yeliz Schentke und Manuel Müller erläutern im Interview, warum die Gruppe so vorgeht und wie es weitergehen soll. Der Text von Peter Ullrich (S. 6) beleuchtet die schwierigen Bedingungen, unter denen sich verhaltene Organisierungsbemühungen des wissenschaftlichen Mittelbaus entwickeln

…“ 

Interview erschienen in express, Zeitung für sozialistische Betriebs- und Gewerkschaftsarbeit,  Ausgabe 08/2016

 










Auf dem Weg zur Hochschulgewerkschaft: Frankfurter Initiative unter_bau kündigt Gründungkongress im November an


„

Mitte April ging die Initiative unter_bau – damals ein Zusammenschluss rund 50 Hochschulangehöriger – an die Öffentlichkeit mit dem Ziel, den Aufbau einer alternativen Gewerkschaft für den Frankfurter Hochschulbereich voranzutreiben. Die angestrebte „Gewerkschaft anderen Typs“ soll statusgruppenübergreifend und basisdemokratisch funktionieren, zugleich soll sie sich nicht auf die üblichen Tätigkeitsfelder von Gewerkschaften beschränken. Zu ihrem Programm gehört auch die politische Perspektive einer grundlegenden Neuordnung der Hochschule, um Wissenschaft, Lehre und Studium eine soziale Ausrichtung zu geben. Nun, nach dem Ende des Semesters, zieht die Initiative Bilanz zu ihrer Organisierungskampagne und kündigt ihren Kongress zur offiziellen Gründung der Gewerkschaft für Mitte November 2016 an. (…) Als Termin für den Gründungskongress nennt die Initiative den 18. bis 20. November 2016

.“ 

Pressemitteilung vom 1.8.2016 










Vorläufiges Programm


„… 

Im vorläufigen Programm der Initiative werden zahlreiche Missstände benannt, die die Gewerkschaft kurz- und mittelfristig überwinden möchte. Dazu zählt etwa das Outsourcing verschiedener Dienstleistungen und Angestellter, eine fehlende tarifliche Absicherung der Hilfskräfte, die Prekarisierung des wissenschaftlichen Personals durch ständige Befristung sowie die Geschlechterhierarchien in allen Bereichen. Langfristig ist das Ziel eine umfassende Demokratisierung der Hochschule, die die Initiative gegenwärtig als „Ständesystem“ bezeichnet

…“ Aus der PM zur Gründung, siehe 

das vorläufige Programm auf der Homepage der Initiative unter_bau 










Uns besonders sympathisch: 

„Gewerkschaft jenseits der Sozialpartnerschaft“


„… 

Uns schwebt eine unabhängige Gewerkschaft für die Frankfurter Hochschulen vor, die föderalistisch und basisdemokratisch organisiert ist. Durch die Organisierung in Form von Instituts-, Fachschafts- und Verwaltungsgruppen soll Raum für aktivistische Potentiale geschaffen werden, um am Puls der konkreten Probleme im Hochschulalltag zu agieren. Die Etablierung einer solchen Alternativgewerkschaft an der Uni Frankfurt stellt eine große Herausforderung dar. Insbesondere in die Position zu kommen, eine der zentralen Kompetenzen von Gewerkschaften wahrnehmen zu können – Tarifverhandlungen zu führen –, ist nicht einfach. Als Minderheitengewerkschaft einen Vertretungsanspruch für die gesamte Hochschule geltend zu machen, ist vermessen, und einzelne Bereiche der Universität tariflich zu separieren, nicht vertretbar. Deshalb verstehen wir uns tarifpolitisch zunächst als Schrittmacher: Wir stellen Forderungen und bauen Druck auf, damit sie Eingang in die etablierte Tarifpolitik finden. Mittelfristig wollen wir tarifpolitisch koalieren, ohne eigene Standards aufzugeben, und langfristig selbst Tarifpolitik gestalten

…“ 

Die Strategie auf der Homepage der Initiative unter_bau 

 







Der Beitrag 

unter_bau: Alternative Hochschulgewerkschaft an der Goethe-Universität Frankfurt

 erschien zuerst auf 

LabourNet Germany

.

author: Alan Robinson
title: Overcoming Schizophrenia and Transforming Psychiatry: An Interview with Dr. Daniel Fisher
content:
Editor’s Note: This Mad in the World report features an interview with eCPR founder Dr. Daniel Fisher, interviewed by Locura en Argentina founder Alan Robinson.




D

r. Daniel Fisher is an international pioneer in the mental health recovery movement who helped transform psychiatric care by demonstrating that full recovery from severe mental health conditions is possible. After personally overcoming a diagnosis of schizophrenia, he earned his medical degree from Harvard Medical School to reform the mental health system from within as a psychiatrist. A former member of the White House Commission on Mental Health and co-developer of Emotional CPR (eCPR), Dr. Fisher’s work has shifted international policy toward human connection and peer-led empowerment rather than forced treatment and lifelong institutionalization. He is also the author of 

Heartbeats of Hope: The Empowerment Way to Recover Your Life

, which is being translated into Spanish.







Alan Robinson: Welcome, Dr. Daniel Fisher. In the early 1970s and 1980s, the Mental Patients Liberation Front (MPLF) was rooted in radical resistance. What was your first interaction with them like, and how did working with them shape your vision for peer-run alternatives?




Daniel Fisher:

 I first learned about the Mental Patients Liberation Front by reading a radical mental health newsletter called 

Madness Network News

, which was published by a group in San Francisco starting in the early 1970s. At the time, I was completing my medical school training and discovered that the MPLF was located in Boston. When choosing where to do my psychiatric residency, I specifically sought a Harvard teaching hospital in Boston because the MPLF was there—not primarily because of Harvard itself. I instinctively felt that my best education would come from people with lived experience in the mental health system.




Prior to that, I had been hospitalized three times—twice before medical school and once during. Those experiences taught me that the mental health system desperately needed major reform, as the treatment was barbaric. I believed I could change the system from within by becoming a psychiatrist.




Daniel Fisher. Photo by Kermit Cole.




In 1976, I wrote to the MPLF asking to join. They sent back a postcard stating I could join as an ex-patient, but not as a psychiatrist. When I arrived in Boston and began my residency on an inpatient unit, a couple of hospitalized clients whispered to me that they knew who I was, as I had to keep my history quiet due to the severe stigma attached to a schizophrenia diagnosis. Eventually, they formed a group called “Friends of MPLF” for professionals with lived experience. Through that group, I met Judy Chamberlin, author of 

On Our Own

, who became my lifelong mentor starting in 1976.




Later, another member blurted out to her psychiatrist—who happened to be Dr. Lee Mock, the head of my psychiatry department—that I was in the group. When I approached Dr. Mock, he called my lived experience a “great asset,” though he advised keeping it secret from other psychiatrists who would not understand.




Robinson:

 How did you handle the potential confusion or conflict of being both a former patient on one hand and a practicing doctor on the other?




Fisher:

 Bridging those two worlds has been a lifelong task. Initially, I coped by leading two separate lives and keeping my lived experience secret for three years, sharing it only with the head of the department. Over time, I earned the trust of survivor advocates. Judy Chamberlin used to joke that I was one of only three psychiatrists in the U.S. whom advocates accepted—the other two being Peter Breggin, author of 

Toxic Psychiatry

, and Peter Stastny.




I waited until I finished my three-year residency before publicly disclosing my history. At the end of my residency, I was invited onto a television talk show, 

People Are Talking

, to debate forced treatment. I invited my former supervisor to debate me. Right before we walked onto the stage, I told him I was going to reveal my past hospitalization. He sarcastically responded, “It’s very fashionable these days to have been hospitalized”.




Robinson:

 

Both you and Dr. Pat Deegan received diagnoses of schizophrenia, were told you would never recover, and went on to earn doctorates. Did you feel living proof that the system’s prognosis was completely wrong?




Fisher:

 Yes, absolutely. Pat Deegan, who earned her doctorate in psychology, co-founded the National Empowerment Center (NEC) with Judy Chamberlin and me.




When giving talks to psychiatric audiences, many psychiatrists remained deeply skeptical about recovery. One psychiatrist told me after a talk, “You couldn’t possibly have had schizophrenia, because your presentation made sense”. The assumption was that people simply do not recover from schizophrenia.




Years ago, a friend attending a graduate-level abnormal psychology course at Boston University challenged her professor when he told the class that people never recover from schizophrenia. She mentioned that a friend of hers—a psychiatrist—had recovered. When the professor claimed I must have been misdiagnosed, they went through the DSM-III criteria item by item, confirming I met every single criterion, including catatonia, mutism, and being out of work and social functioning for over six months. Facing this evidence, the professor shifted his response to: “Well, if he met the criteria, he must still be sick—he’s just a case of a disabled psychiatrist”. It shows how deeply entrenched the belief in non-recovery was.




At the National Empowerment Center, we developed six core criteria for recovery. The primary criterion is that neighbors and community members would not suspect your psychiatric history—that you can pass as another member of the community, make your own decisions, build an independent support network outside the mental health system, and feel capable of running your own life. Whether someone takes medication or not is not the determinant of recovery, as many people lead full, meaningful lives while taking medication.




Robinson:

 In the 1980s, figures like Leonard Roy Frank and Howie the Harp were central to the radical ex-patient movement. How were you received when entering those spaces, and how did collaborating with leaders like Howie influence your approach to peer support?




Fisher:

 Howie the Harp was initially skeptical, but having Judy Chamberlin vouch for me gave me credibility. Leaders like Howie inspired me tremendously. As a shy person who disliked public speaking, their courage encouraged me to find my voice. Howie was a burly man who used a cane, and at the start of meetings he would lift his cane and shout, “I’m raising Cain!”. Their fearlessness was incredible.




They recognized that because of my credentials, I could enter settings and reach audiences they could not access. In 1984, a rehabilitation specialist informed me of a Medical Director opening at a community mental health center. I stated I would only apply if I could openly disclose my lived experience. They agreed, which allowed me to hire other professionals with lived experience. However, working within the traditional system remained stressful because its primary orientation was control, making mutual support groups among staff essential.




Robinson: 

Judy Chamberlin famously attributed her recovery to being a non-compliant patient. How did working with her influence how you practiced psychiatry, and how did you navigate these radical perspectives alongside federal funding at the National Empowerment Center?




Fisher:

 Judy and I shared a deep outrage and passion for reform. At the National Empowerment Center, we received 70% to 80% of our funding from the federal government, which meant we constantly had to push the boundaries while navigating what the government would accept. When Judy wrote an article titled 

Confessions of a Non-Compliant Patient

 for our newsletter, we debated how funders would react, but they ultimately accepted it.




However, in 2010, when we invited author Robert Whitaker (

Anatomy of an Epidemic

) to keynote the national Alternatives conference, federal funders initially objected. After a massive email campaign sent directly to the White House during the Obama administration, federal officials permitted Whitaker to speak on the condition that another psychiatrist, Dr. Mark Ragins, present a critique. Navigating these dynamics is a tightrope walk where you push for radical change while assessing how much pushback the organization can sustain.




Robinson: 

You were appointed to the President’s New Freedom Commission on Mental Health in 2002. How did that policy battle unfold, and how did you ensure recovery became a central focus?




Fisher:

 When I was appointed as a commissioner in 2002, there was significant debate within the movement about whether I should join or if it would result in co-optation.




At our very first meeting, broadcast on C-SPAN, I declared in my opening statement that recovery must be the central theme of the commission. At the time, other commissioners were focused on clinical remission at best. When a group of fellow advocates sitting in the audience stood up and applauded my speech, an official sitting next to me asked what was happening, as he had never seen applause at a government meeting. I told him, “This is a movement. Millions of us are watching”.




I fought to expand the public testimony time from 15 minutes to 45 minutes at our monthly meetings across the country, bringing in local advocates to share their stories with passion. By the end of the year, recovery was adopted into the official mission statement of the White House Commission report: “We envision a future where everyone with a mental illness will recover”. That report became a landmark document used globally to legitimize recovery.




Afterward, activist Sally Zinman and I recognized the need to train emerging leaders. Together with Judy Chamberlin, we created the “Pioneer Voice” training based on the “P’s of Empowerment”—including Peer support, Purpose, and transforming anger into Passion.




Robinson:

 You and Laurie Ahern co-developed the PACE curriculum. How did you translate survivor movement principles into practical, real-world alternatives to traditional psychiatric care?




Fisher:

 Laurie Ahern, a journalist and advocate with lived experience, joined the Empowerment Center and pointed out that full recovery was a well-kept secret that needed to be broadly communicated. We obtained federal funding to conduct a qualitative study interviewing peers to define the core principles of recovery, identifying 13 key principles. This formed the basis of PACE (Personal Assistance and Community Existential).




PACE was also a critique of PACT (Program of Assertive Community Treatment). While PACT aimed to support people in the community, it often resulted in trans-institutionalization, where individuals remained trapped within a closed loop of continuous system supports without a path to true independence.




True alternatives are voluntary, home-like peer-run respites. The first peer-run respite was created in 1995 by Shery Mead in New Hampshire. Today, there are around 50 peer-run respites across the United States, providing intensive, non-coercive support operated entirely by people with lived experience.




Robinson: 

Looking back on your journey as a historical pioneer in this movement, what is your message for the future?




Fisher:

 The mental health system will not give up its power without a struggle. While I am not an abolitionist—because removing the mental health system without alternatives would leave prison as the only option—we must continuously organize laterally across the globe to demand our rights and demonstrate our capabilities.




Furthermore, as society turns increasingly toward artificial intelligence, we will see its limitations. AI lacks a heart; it cannot feed people’s dreams or replace genuine human connection. This technological shift highlights the urgent need to return to the root of our shared humanity—which is precisely what our movement represents.




Robinson:

 Dr. Daniel Fisher, thank you so much for this interview.




The post 

Overcoming Schizophrenia and Transforming Psychiatry: An Interview with Dr. Daniel Fisher

 appeared first on 

Mad In America

.

author: Leonard Wanyama
title: Misuse of the Tax Commissioner General’s Powers is Hurting Kenyans
content:
As I sat there listening to a friend who owns a small business, I wondered whether there are different tax regimes in Kenya depending on what form of commercial activity one undertakes.




Despite working in tax advocacy for the past nine years, this was the first time I was coming across a VAT Withholding Tax (henceforth referred to as VWT). 




Indeed, this is something different from what is generally understood as Value-Added Tax (VAT) and the fact that many small businesses are finding themselves being ambushed by it goes to show how much Kenyan taxation requires a lot more democracy.




VAT is the standard rate of 16 per cent tax that is charged on the consumption of goods and services supplied or purchased. Businesses charge it as part of the cost, then remit the difference between the price and the tariff to the government. Every good or service, from fuel to bread, usually has a 16 per cent cost added to it.




The VWT, on the other hand, is a mechanism to collect VAT at the point of supplies provision. This means that for selected businesses, there is a tax within a tax for every purchase they make. In this case, the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) appoints selected businesses or individual entities as their agents to deduct this tax at a fixed rate of 2 per cent on the advance payment to their suppliers.




Essentially, once the supplier gives you the price of a good or service inclusive of 16 per cent VAT, if you are appointed a KRA agent to implement VWT, you would hold on to 2 per cent of that payment for remittance to the tax collector. 




This must then be reconciled through the electronic Tax Invoice Management System (eTIMS). The system has unfortunately been experiencing frequent partial or full downtimes in recent months, preventing transaction matching between sellers and buyers for accurate KRA determination of tax demands or claims.

 




My friend had no idea how his business had been selected to become a KRA implementing agent. Moreover, even when he could not reconcile the taxes using eTIMS due to frequent system downtimes, his business was still automatically liable for penalties due to noncompliance. 




This happened because even as the eTIMS system was partially shut down, other functioning segments of the tax software platform continued accumulating taxes from other regular purchases he transacted, and recorded them onto the eTIMS portal as he carried out other business. 




This revelation by my friend was to me mind-boggling because I could immediately see the tense and awkward haggling that could harm a business relationship given the current difficult commercial environment. 




Such are the tribulations small businesses are facing on top of tax contestations around cash flow mismatches, informal supply chain problems, eTIMS-related costs due to system glitches, invoicing evidence rules, and digital literacy demands for revenue compliance.




Looking at 

Section 42 of the Tax Procedures Act of 2015

, it emerges that the application of the law in this instance is vague, thereby conferring unfettered discretionary powers on public officials under the authority of the KRA Commissioner General.




There are no objective criteria as to how VWT agents are determined and these appointments then come across as arbitrary decisions that not only confuse taxpayers but also leave them paralytically unable to predict the legal consequences of their actions.




It came as no surprise a few weeks later that traders had become angry over another tax that consolidated cargo clearance charges. Though separate from the VWT issue, the manner of application of this tax is annoyingly similar.




This has resulted in 

protests by traders

 that have forced President William Ruto to order a 

review of customs costs

 and differentiated implementation in the handling of ordinary consignments compared to high-value cargo. 




This means that containers carrying commercial merchandise, everyday consumer items, bulk or general cargo of low value will continue to pay KSh 2 million for clearance. 




Meanwhile, shipments of luxury goods, specialized electronics, high-end motor vehicles, and industrial machinery will undergo further assessment based on the value of the goods in the container, which is likely to raise costs.




The two examples above are a stark reminder of Professor Migai Akech’s treatise on the 

undemocratic application of administrative law

 in taxation, where power is abused and not practised based on the principles of equity, fair treatment, and accountability.




Politically, this transforms taxation into an oppressive tool that can break into anyone’s piggy bank at any time to attain undisclosed national budgetary goals or 

silence dissenting voices

 at the whim of the powers that be, a “preserve of autocratic governance” in which Kenya is governed as a tyrannical barony.




As a result, tax collection becomes inefficient because citizens are dissuaded from active compliance due to their distrust of established policies or processes.




Despite their willingness to pay taxes – as captured in research by Twaweza East Africa on 

Taxing Matters

 – and their being aware of the publicized intent for revenue collection measures to help settle debt obligations and service delivery demands, Kenyans are sceptical of tax authorities because they do not deem them to be fair.




Kenya’s National Taxpayers Association (NTA) points out in its 

2025 Tax Perception Survey Report

 that informal sector inclusion is highly contested, resulting in lingering pessimism because KRA is viewed as obstructive while its officers are perceived as dismissive and unhelpful in explaining tax law and the accompanying regulatory demands.




This is compounded by underlying grievances such as awareness of tax avoidance and fraudulent financial practices like corruption or theft that are not properly punished within the context of poor economic growth as captured by the East African Tax and Governance Network (EATGN) in the 

2021 Kenya National Tax Outlook Survey

.




With this in mind, how then can it be that anyone can simply be ambushed to become a KRA agent without a clearly stated legal mechanism categorizing taxpayers and clearly ascertaining their legal obligations for such roles?




First, this flies in the face of the right to fair administrative action under Article 47 of the Constitution, thereby making it an unrelatable process that comes off as a whimsical application of the law.




This is because it haphazardly changes the taxpayer’s legal obligations by designating roles which simultaneously expose one to compliance costs, penalties, interest, and unforeseen duties without clear justification, prior notice, consultation, or explanation of the criteria applied in the appointment of a VWT agent. 




Secondly, it is an unscrupulous transfer of costs and other administrative burdens to private entities, thereby infringing on the right to property under Article 40 of the Constitution, where incomes are broadly protected as “

property of any description

”.




In this instance, appointed agents deploy time (explaining processes at length to their fellow taxpayers who would obviously feel shortchanged discussing tax complexity while bargaining over margins with a non-state entity), resources, personnel, and finance systems without compensation based on unclear statutes.




Thirdly, Section 23A of the Tax Procedures Act disproportionately targets small businesses while Section 23A (3a) specifically shifts responsibility from suppliers to purchasers.




The VWT, therefore, adversely affects commercial activities at a small or micro level; in remote areas with poor internet access; for those trading informally or operating with limited digital literacy – for example, the elderly; and for those that cannot afford hardware or software upgrades.




A straight line can therefore be drawn between the negative public sentiment against eTIMS and the problem of how the current application of tax systems is not only inconvenient and prohibitive but is also punishingly expensive for small businesses or traders.




This is because it is inconsistent with the constitutional right to equality and freedom from discrimination under Article 27(1) of the constitution that guarantees that eTIMS application should offer equal protection and benefits under the law. Furthermore, Article 27(4) prohibits direct or indirect discrimination.




One must ask: how does a purchaser generate tax invoices within an unclear statutory framework where they cannot verify that the supplier’s annual turnover is below the legally prescribed threshold? Doesn’t that expose them to tax liabilities based on information they have no access to and that is the exclusive knowledge of the supplier?




Consequently, small-scale farmers and small trading operations are finding themselves subject to administrative actions that amount to unjustified interference that manifests as punitive assessments that charge them with noncompliance.




Going by paragraph 5(2) of the 

Tax Procedures (Electronic Tax Invoice) Regulations

 of 2024, taxpayers face further challenges because the existing process for notifying the KRA whenever the system is not working is impracticable and shifts the burden or consequences of a failed digital platform onto taxpayers.




In effect, a taxpayer is expected to “a) notify the Commissioner in writing within twenty-four hours of the user’s inability to use the system; and b) record sales using any other means as may be specified by the Commissioner” if they’re having problems using the system.




Additionally, the appeals timelines become unreasonable when businesses cannot use the relevant system functions because of connectivity problems, technology capabilities, or disruptions caused by lack of access to system components that are experiencing outages, while other capacities are accessible, functional, and working. 




As highlighted by Professor Akech, in the eyes of the public, most KRA failures can be attributed to the misapplication of discretionary powers or their outright abuse. This is made worse by the fact that the KRA does not seem to be obligated to respond within a reasonable timeframe to the satisfaction of taxpayers.




Hence, KRA acts in a high-handed manner that renders its processes excessively demanding and costly. This is even more painfully so when one is faced with long and winding judicial interventions when seeking redress. 




Ultimately, the efforts of the Ministry of Finance and the National Treasury to review the National Tax Policy should also consider how to establish guardrails around these powers to ensure that their application is legitimate. 




The post 

Misuse of the Tax Commissioner General’s Powers is Hurting Kenyans

 first appeared on 

The Elephant

.

author: James Crump
title: Dockworkers From 100 Ports to Disrupt Military and Energy Supplies to Israel
content:
Dock and port workers from 17 countries will disrupt and block exports to Israel on Friday, with workers joining from countries including Italy, Mexico, Turkey, the US, Morocco and India.




Representatives from more than 100 ports will participate in the international day of action on 30 October, calling for an end to Israel’s genocide against Palestinians and “US-Israeli wars of aggression”.




The Palestinian BDS National Committee (BNC)

 

announced on X

 that workers will take action by “peacefully disrupting and blocking the transfer of military, energy and other dual-use supplies to Israel, including by refusing to handle such supplies”.




Workers will also pressure governments to impose a full military embargo on Israel and end “trade, economic and academic relations serving its illegal occupation and apartheid”.




Explaining the day of action, the BNC said that Israel’s “criminal wars” are “exacerbating the cost of living and economic crises worldwide”.




“Military budgets are swelling in the colonial West, while families and workers struggle with the cost of health, housing, transportation, and education. Our struggles are interlinked,” it stated.




A further 17 Palestinian trade unions and federations have endorsed the action, stating: “Our struggle for justice in Palestine is inseparable from the global struggle against systemic racism, militarisation, exploitation, climate devastation and all forms of oppression.”




The day of action comes a year after dockworkers in Italy 

blocked the ports

 of Genoa and Livorno, with unions closing schools and stopping transportation as part of an Italy-wide general strike in response to Israel preventing the 

Global Sumud Flotilla

 from reaching Gaza in 2025.




The flotilla was the largest ever naval mission to attempt to deliver humanitarian supplies to Gaza, with around 20 vessels carrying delegates from at least 44 countries.




The flotilla was subject to drone attacks before being illegally intercepted by Israel in international waters. Those on board were detained and have accused Israeli forces of subjecting them to human rights abuses including assault, degrading treatment, and the withholding of medical care.

author: CNT Villaverde Alto - Comarcal Sur de Madrid
title: 29 de octubre y 4 de noviembre. La Sección Sindical de CNT en la UNED instalará mesas informativas sobre la Huelga General del 11N
content:
Desde la Sección Sindical en la UNED informamos de que instalaremos puestos para informar a los trabajadores y las trabajadoras sobre la huelga general del 11 de noviembre. Los próximos días 

29 de octubre, en el Campus Norte (Calle Juan del Rosal)

, y el 

4 de noviembre en el Campus de Paseo de la Senda del Rey

, colocaremos 

mesas informativas desde las 12:00

 para explicar a la plantilla de la UNED los motivos de la huelga general, las principales reivindicaciones y los derechos que tenemos como trabajadores y trabajadoras de cara a la jornada del 11-N.




Con el problema de fondo de la vivienda, el precio de los alquileres y el poder adquirido por el rentismo y los intereses especuladores, desde CNT-UNED hacemos 

un llamamiento a toda la plantilla de la Universidad para secundar la huelga general del 11 de noviembre

. Si nuestra capacidad adquisitiva se reduce por tener que pagar mes a mes unos alquileres disparados, por el estancamiento de los salarios y el aumento de la carestía de vida, la huelga general es una de nuestras mejores herramientas para decir basta y defender nuestros intereses como trabajadores y trabajadoras, nuestras condiciones de trabajo y de vida. Tenemos derecho a la huelga, y 

ejercerlo es la mejor herramienta para denunciar una situación insostenible que nos afecta a todos y todas

, a nuestras familias, a nuestros amigos y amigas y a nuestros barrios. 

Si tienes dudas sobre las exigencias de la huelga o sobre cómo has de realizarla, pásate por las mesas informativas o escríbenos un correo

.




Además, en la mesa del jueves 29 contaremos con la presencia de compañeras de la Plataforma Laboral de Escuelas Infantiles (PLEI), quienes informarán sobre la 

huelga indefinida histórica que sostienen desde el 7 de abril de este año

.




Como siempre, si deseas contactar con la Sección Sindical puedes escribirnos a uned@comarcalsur.cnt.es




¡EL 11-N PARAMOS EL PAÍS!




¡EL 11-N, A LA HUELGA GENERAL!




La entrada 

29 de octubre y 4 de noviembre. La Sección Sindical de CNT en la UNED instalará mesas informativas sobre la Huelga General del 11N

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

author: Thiago Domenici
title: Em fuga, Flávio Bolsonaro embarcou da Argentina rumo ao Equador e ainda não chegou aos EUA
content:
Durante a maior parte da terça-feira (27), circulou na imprensa brasileira, argentina e dos Estados Unidos a versão de que o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), derrotado por Lula no segundo turno no domingo (25), já estaria no ar, a caminho dos Estados Unidos. O registro oficial divulgado pelo governo argentino na madrugada desta quarta-feira (28) desmente essa cronologia. 

Segundo a Dirección Nacional de Migraciones, o senador só cruzou a fronteira às 22h50 de terça, e o jato que o levou decolou com destino declarado para Guayaquil, no Equador. Ainda não se sabe qual é o destino final a partir de Guayaquil

 – mas veículos têm noticiado que Flávio irá para os Estados Unidos, onde também vive o seu irmão, Eduardo.
















A Direção Nacional de Migrações informa que, às 22h50 do dia 27/10, ingressaram pelo posto de fronteira da Ponte Internacional Tancredo Neves, na província de Misiones, Flavio Nantes Bolsonaro e família




Em comunicado publicado no X, a Migraciones, que na terça de manhã havia afirmado não ter registro de entrada de Flávio na Argentina, divulgou a informação às 2h01. Segundo o órgão, o senador entrou pela Ponte Internacional Tancredo Neves, que liga Foz do Iguaçu (PR) a Puerto Iguazú, na província de Misiones. Ele estava com a mulher, Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, e as duas filhas do casal, o que 

confirma

 a informação divulgada pela 

Agência Pública

 sobre a ausência das filhas na escola em Brasília. 




De acordo com a publicação, todos apresentaram documentação de viagem válida, sem impedimentos legais, e a entrada na Argentina foi registrada sem incidentes. Quarenta minutos depois, às 23h30, o grupo embarcou em um voo privado da empresa Baires Fly S.A. com destino a Guayaquil, conforme o plano de voo.

 Sites que monitoram voos registraram a aeronave sobrevoando a cidade equatoriana por volta das 5h40. Depois, por volta das 6h20, a aeronave decolou novamente com direção ao Norte – aparentemente indo para os Estados Unidos. 




A saída de Flávio ocorre depois que o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal, determinou que Flávio entregasse seus passaportes à Polícia Federal e que ele fosse incluído no Sonar, o sistema de monitoramento migratório. O senador não cumpriu o prazo, que se encerrou às 11h da terça-feira, e a PF cancelou os passaportes emitidos em seu nome. Ele é investigado no STF por suspeitas de lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas.




Entre os países do Mercosul, a carteira de identidade é aceita como documento de viagem, o que explica a menção da Migraciones a “documentação hábil”. Ainda não está esclarecido como o senador atravessou a Ponte Tancredo Neves sem ser detido do lado brasileiro, já que constava no Sonar.




A aeronave pertence à empresa usada por Javier Milei, presidente argentino, para ir aos EUA após sua eleição. Segundo a imprensa argentina, a empresa teria vínculos com o empresário Maurício Macri, e à época, em 2023, o custo do voo de Milei foi alvo de questionamento. A viagem teria custado entre R$ 1,2 milhão e R$ 1,35 milhão. Milei, até o momento, não reconheceu a vitória de Lula nas eleições. 
















Imagens do jato da empresa Baires Fly onde Flávio e família teriam embarcado rumo aos EUA




Notícia de que já estava nos EUA não se confirmou




O horário oficial contradiz, por ora, o que vinha sendo noticiado pela imprensa, segundo pessoas próximas à família e o entorno político de Flávio, de que o senador teria partido para os Estados Unidos e que o avião já estaria em rota. O portal argentino Infobae relatou que ele teria cruzado a fronteira com a carteira de identidade rumo a Puerto Iguazú, de onde seguiria em voo privado para os EUA.




Pela cronologia oficial, quando essas versões circulavam, Flávio ainda não havia passado por nenhum posto de controle migratório argentino. O avião também não tinha decolado. O jato é um Gulfstream G400 de matrícula argentina LV-JQW. 
















Aeronave onde estaria Flávio decolou de Gayaquil por volta de 6h20 rumo aos Estados Unidos




Segundo o jornal Clarín, a decolagem foi retida durante a tarde devido a pendências na documentação de um dos passageiros. O portal Misiones Online havia noticiado que a aeronave estava no aeroporto de Puerto Iguazú e que partiria para Guayaquil.




As negativas oficiais da terça-feira (27), que pareciam contradizer as notícias sobre a fuga, eram compatíveis com o registro divulgado depois. Pela manhã, a Migraciones disse que não tinha registro do ingresso do senador. Mais tarde, o porta-voz do presidente Javier Milei, Fabián Fernández, negou à Bloomberg que Flávio tivesse entrado no país. Pelo comunicado desta madrugada da Direção Nacional de Migrações da Argentina, ele de fato ainda não tinha entrado.

contato@apublica.org

 ou doe em 

apoie.apublica.org

.

author: CNT Santander
title: Vivienda digna y asequible para todas las personas
content:
El acceso a la vivienda no es un lujo, es un derecho innegociable protegido por la Constitución y que ha de prevalecer sobre cualquier negocio privado. A las instituciones se les olvida rápido.




En muchas comunidades autónomas, incluida la nuestra, no protegen a la población y venden su futuro a fondos buitre. No declaran zonas tensionadas, no intervienen el mercado ni regulan los precios. No les importa lo que supone cada día para todas las personas que vivimos en Cantabria.




Cada día, la clase trabajadora sufre por la actual situación del acceso a vivienda, con la especulación por las nubes, el aumento de los precios de alquileres e hipotecas totalmente abusivos e inasumibles, y el problema de los arrendamientos temporales que provocan más desconcierto e incertidumbre por un futuro digno.




Según el INE, el salario más frecuente en Cantabria es de 1.495 euros netos al mes. Dependiendo del sector productivo, ese salario varia considerablemente, en aumento si se trata de la industria o incluso en algunos casos, como en el sector servicios, puede incluso bajar. Ya que el salario modal en hostelería en Cantabria roza los 16.000€/18000€ brutos al año, traducido en unos 1.142€/1.285,7€ brutos al mes, sin retenciones.




La realidad nos muestra también que el 12,4% de las mujeres cántabras y el 6,3% de los hombres están por debajo del SMI. Por lo que, si con el sueldo más frecuente en la comunidad ya se hace difícil acceder a la vivienda tal y como están los precios de alquileres e hipotecas, en su mayoría variables y pendientes del Euribor, ¿qué sucede cuando la clase trabajadora no llega ni al SMI sin contar las retenciones?




La respuesta es trágica.




No se puede acceder a la vivienda ni obtener las necesidades más básicas al mismo tiempo, si vives sola y sin ayuda familiar.




Recordemos que el precio del alquiler medio en ciudades como Santander ronda los 889€ por un piso de dos habitaciones en zonas residenciales normales, mientras que en Torrelavega cuesta unos 750€, hay muy pocas ofertas por debajo de ese precio.




En zonas como Noja o Laredo, mucho más turísticas y de segundas viviendas, son 1.073€ por un piso de las mismas características.




En algunos pueblos más pequeños como Polanco, en zonas residenciales a las afueras de Torrelavega y de las industrias, ya se ha subido tanto que salta de los 1.000, a los 1.200€ al mes en Cartes, 1.000€ en Renedo de Piélagos y en la costera Suances incluso llega a los 2.000€.




Dicen los economistas que cuando una persona tiene que destinar 

más del 30%

 de su salario al alquiler, la economía familiar se derrumba. En Cantabria

, la clase trabajadora destina incluso más del 50%.




¿Qué sucede entonces con la economía de las personas cántabras?




Nos ponemos en el supuesto:




Si una persona gana 1.495€ y paga unos 889€ de alquiler, le quedan 600€ para todo lo demás: comida, higiene, facturas de servicios, transporte público, coche y gasolina, seguros, estacionamiento regulado. Todo ello contando que no tenga que preocuparse de más personas, que no tenga hijas e hijos a su cargo.




Respuesta: Algunas personas conseguirán llegar a fin de mes sin poder ahorrar, otras lo harán en números rojos.




¿Qué sucede cuando solo entra un salario en casa, no hay más prestaciones y son familias con hijas e hijos?




¿Qué sucede cuando se es madre divorciada, soltera, con hijos? ¿Padre soltero con hijas e hijos?




¿Y cuándo se cobra menos del SMI y es una persona que vive sola y no tienes más ayudas?




Llega la imposibilidad de vivir de un salario, de acceder a un hogar en condiciones salubres y dignas, de pagar las facturas pendientes de servicios e incluso de hacer frente a las necesidades más básicas como la comida y la higiene, ya que la inflación ha encarecido los precios de la cesta de la compra de tal manera que apenas se pueden pagar los productos del día a día.




Y llegará el invierno y muchas familias tendrán que decidir entre pagar el alquiler, comer y encender la calefacción.




El 11 de noviembre saldremos a la calle para reivindicar nuestro derecho a una vivienda digna, junto con un incremento salarial para poder vivir sin dificultades.




¡Porque la situación es insostenible!




Porque mientras los negocios privados inmobiliarios, las rentistas y los fondos buitre se hacen ricas a costa de la clase trabajadora y productiva, la realidad de muchas personas en Cantabria, ya no es solo que sean expulsadas de sus barrios por la gentrificación, que no puedan habitar y ocupar espacios, es que cada día tienen más difícil e imposible el acceso a una vivienda, a tener una casa a la que poder llamar hogar y vivir una vida tranquila.




LA VIVIENDA NO ES UN LUJO CON EL QUE ESPECULAR. ¡ES UN DERECHO!




Lucharemos por ese derecho hasta dejarnos la voz. Muchas personas, como Mari Carmen y Amparo, se han dejado la vida en el proceso tras ser desahuciadas de sus casas.




Por ellas, por nosotras, por todas las personas de Cantabria, ¡

el 11 de noviembre a la HUELGA GENERAL!




Por 

Rebeca Bañuelos

VIVIENDA DIGNA Y ASEQUIBLE PARA TODAS LAS PERSONAS

 se publicó primero en 

CNT Santander

.

author: Unknown
title: Sara Blum - Martyr Culture
content:
Author

: Sara Blum

Title

: Martyr Culture

Subtitle

: Revolutionary Culture in Rojava

Date

: June 2025

Notes

: This essay was written by Sara Blum, and internationalist who spent several years with the YPJ in Rojava, to accompany and contextualize 

Orso: Wartime Journals of an Anarchist

,

 published in July 2025.

Source

: retrieved on 10/27/2026 from https://www.tangledwilderness.org/features/martyr-culture










I remain committed, until the end, to the struggle for liberation 

and to the beauty and love it creates.










Abdullah Öcalan










 Kurdish friends, upon meeting an internationalist, often ask about our decision to come to their homeland in Rojava, Kurdistan. When they’d ask how I first came into contact with the friends, I felt a bit embarrassed to say that, honestly, the first friends of the movement I met were those who helped me after I actually arrived in Mesopotamia. (Editor’s note: “The friends” is a colloquialism stemming from the literal translation of the word “heval” which has historically been used by members of the Kurdish liberation movement to refer to each other.) I told them I learned about the movement by reading articles on a few different anarchist websites and contacted the friends by email. In fact, I knew so little about the movement that I first emailed YPG (People’s Protection Units) instead of YPJ (Women’s Protection Units). The friends were often amazed at this, and in their generosity considered it some kind of bravery or indication of the depth of my belief in the revolution and the people, rather than of naivety or impulsivity. It’s a common story among internationalists from the so-called USA, because the Kurdish Freedom Movement doesn’t have a presence here like it does in many parts of Europe, where there is a bigger Kurdish diaspora. When I initially went, I planned to stay for six months or a year. I ended up staying for several years, and for most of that time I was with the autonomous women’s military defense forces, YPJ. 




 I decided to go in late 2018, and at that time it was hard to find much information about what to expect. Not much has changed in that regard. My dad told me to bring extra socks, and that before going I must read Che Guevara’s 

On Guerrilla Warfare

. Other than that, most of the practical information about what to bring I received from an internationalist fighter whom I reached through an online message board. He said to bring all sorts of supplies, sent a packing list, and told me to bring a bunch of US dollars. He emphasized that I should bring water for border crossing across the mountains, which he said would be long and difficult, but to not share my water because the Kurdish comrades would pass it down the line until there was none left, and then I wouldn’t have water. The YPJ friend I was corresponding with told me I didn’t need much, and if it came to be that I needed something when I got there or along the way, comrades would sort it out then. This seemed to me rather casual at the time. I felt frustrated at the vagueness. 




 Packing and repacking my bag, researching the weather conditions, trying to prepare as much as possible for what could be the rest of my short little life, I wanted all the information I could find and there wasn’t much. I didn’t realize then that I was encountering the first contrast of revolutionary and capitalist culture: different modes of being. The internationalist from the message board, with his best intentions, showed me one way to go about struggle, while the YPJ comrade showed me another way of joining the revolution. Preparing myself as an individual by making sure I had all the right specific things on the one hand, and on the other, preparing myself to take on the same circumstances as whomever I end up with and to sort all my needs within the context of our collective needs. As an internationalist from the West, the tension between these tendencies has long lived in me. I find that it still does, but I have also found that being out of water together always seems to be better than having water while the person next to me doesn’t. 




 Before I left, I tried many times to write letters to my family, close friends, and comrades, which I would leave in the hands of a trusted friend so that, in the event of my death, they could be sent. I was determined to leave loved ones with some words of strength—I didn’t want to die, but since it was a distinct possibility, it was important to ensure that my death would not be a weight or darkness in their lives. I had made this decision for myself, but I realized as time went on that I’d also made a decision for many other people. My mother became the mother of a YPJ fighter defending the Women’s Revolution. My close friends in the U.S. became personally involved in the defense of the liberated territories as their loved one would be there. Telling my family I was leaving was one of the hardest things I’d done in my life until that point, but writing those letters proved to be much more difficult. I found that I couldn’t finish them. The hours I spent writing and re-writing them, however, were the first I’d ever spent thinking so much about my own death and its meaning. It’s easier to think of dying than it is to think about the meaning of my own death for the people left behind. I told myself I’d finish the letters during my basic training. 




 I arrived first in Southern Kurdistan. After a short while, I ended up with a couple of other internationalists in a refugee camp where we stayed as we waited for the opportunity to cross the border into Rojava. We spoke not one word of Kurdish, and only very few words in Arabic, which as it turned out were all completely useless in the area we were staying. We couldn’t read any signs, or documents, or understand the most basic hand gestures which were, to my surprise, completely different from the ones of my culture. Nobody mentioned that on any message boards. I never imagined it could be so difficult to establish a shared understanding of “yes” and “no.” I felt like an incompetent toddler. Incompetent, I specify, because around me were quite often dozens of Kurdish toddlers each of a higher degree of competence within the context of Kurdish life. This is all to say that when encountering the world around me in those first weeks, as I waited in Başur (Southern Kurdistan) to cross the border into Rojava (Western Kurdistan), there was often no way anything could be explained to me with language, and often also not with a gesture, even given the downright maternal levels of patience of our Kurdish hosts.
