author: ROAPE
title: The sports commercializers are in town
content:
Two recent stories from Kenya reflect the rapid growth, rising ambitions, and increasing commercialization and professionalization of East Africa’s sports sector.




In the first, Helios Sports and Entertainment Group, a private equity firm focused on the continent, teamed up with Zaria Group, fronted by former NBA executive 

Masai Ujiri

, to build a $294 million sports and entertainment hub in Nairobi. Then, Oscar-winning actress Lupita Nyong’o 

announced

 she was investing in Nairobi City Thunder, which plays in the Basketball Africa League (BAL).




A few days later, reports said Nyong’o’s investment in Nairobi City Thunder may kickstart further investment in the BAL and sports in Kenya. This was followed by 

more bullish coverage

 of 

further investment

. What do we make of all this? What analytical language and tools do we have to observe and account for these significant on-ground events and dynamics?




One thing is clear: sports and commerce in East Africa are forming ever closer ties in countries such as Kenya and Uganda, across sectors, from rugby, boxing, basketball, and football to athletics, golf, badminton, and motocross, and, lately, e-sports. Major companies, often foreign, attach their brand assets to 

competitions

, 

leagues

, events, teams, and 

sports

 

champions

, with a wide range of promotional messages, causes, and sector representation (banking, insurance, telecommunications, 

betting

 and real estate, food and beverages, and tires).




The media in these two countries run numerous pieces every month about sports sponsorship partnerships that are signed, announced, 

renewed

, and upgraded (for example, in financial commitment). Weekends in Kampala and Nairobi during sports season are packed with competitions and events (including community and charity events), and the media again 

reports

 on them, naming the sponsors prominently.




TV live coverage is increasing; viewers can join in for free or pay a fee (for example, to follow 

boxing

 in Kampala or 

rugby

 in Nairobi). Ugandan newspapers Daily Monitor and New Vision, or sports news website 

Kawowo Sports

, for example, are full of articles, week after week, with headlines, pictures and stories about sport aspirations, achievement, triumphs, records, trophies, medals and rewards, 

players’

 pride, 

moves

 and 

signings

, or various aspects of 

fandom

. Thus, there is not just sports buzz (including participation among viewers/fans) but also commercial and media (including social media) interest.




Political

, including diplomatic, buzz also exists, with the governments of 

Kenya

 and 

Uganda

 regularly joining initiatives and events in varying roles and capacities, including supporting the hosting of major sports 

events

, national teams and champions competing at international events, and so on. Officially launching sports events and welcoming home athletes from competition elsewhere also get solid 

media

 

coverage

, with officials, sponsors, national flags, and fans joining in. Representatives of international sports federations; prominent, popular, or small but growing international sports competitions; or well-known global sports leagues, clubs, and personalities visit their counterparts to talk, inspect, plan, 

announce

, and so on.




Relatedly, both countries are also undertaking significant 

venue 

construction 

and repair. This is related especially to football (the upcoming AFCON 2027, hosted with Tanzania) but also to other sports (such as paddle), or other formats and purposes, such as 

multi-function

 sports facilities for rent for leisure or competitive activity (non-professional competitions, for example), or sports venues in the 

education

 sector for schoolchildren and students’ recreational and competitive activities. 

Hamz

 Stadium in downtown Kampala is one 

example

.




Significantly, the facilities upgrade and sport events, participation, commerce, and fandom buzz are also evident in viewing venues: the entertainment 

bars

 and 

clubs

 (even a 

cinema

 venue) that 

broadcast

 sports events, especially football (from the EPL to the World Cup and AFCON), some of them almost throughout the entire week; say, from Tuesday in EPL-heavy weeks; or the 

venues

 (clubs, bars, shopping malls) that host live sports such as 

boxing

 (professional and 

celebrity

 fights) or 

martial arts

.




These trends, dynamics, and transformations are part of the wider 

African Sports Economy

 (ASE), as they evolve in these two East African countries and their two capitals (which together have an estimated population of nearly eight million, mostly young people).




Empirical analysis of the ASE 2026 and moving forward, including the Ugandan and Kenyan sports economies (including sports commercialization), requires a data-informed account of the relevant business (and other non-state as well as 

state

) actors ( and actors’ alliances), the formats, investments, rationales and plans, as well as outcomes and results, related to sport-commercial undertakings, projects or partnerships; and the politics/political economy of it all.




We are beginning to learn more about the political economy of investment, 

commercialization

, leagues, prices, and broadcasting and the entertainment sectors and scenes reshaping African cities, especially megacities and their surrounding metropolitan areas. These developments are central to understanding 

ASE

 and the related broader corporatization and 

commercialization

 of African societies: the making of the 

corporate nation

 and 

corporate state

, and the forms of capitalism taking shape across the continent.




Rwanda is central to this phenomenon as well. Its

 ten-year agreement with Formula 1

 exemplifies how states use sports to pursue political, commercial, societal, and geopolitical ambitions; project national identity; attract capital; and reposition themselves within global networks, narratives, and perceptions.




The growing network of sports events, venues, and business partnerships in Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda is thus about more than making money and supporting livelihoods through sports. It also supports a broader political (and collective) effort to strengthen state capacity and power, reshape cities and leisure, compete for regional significance and influence, and change how African economies operate.




Comparative analysis can sharpen our perspective of ASE by examining sports commerce across African countries and sectors, alongside developments elsewhere: 

Inter Miami FC

 and its commercial strategy in football; the 

US Open

 and the political economy of popularity, access, and affordability in tennis; 

sports betting regulation in Brazil

 and its electoral implications; and 

China’s football market

, where clubs, commercial interests, and state priorities intersect. Together, these cases show how sports and entertainment have become arenas where states, corporations, and political actors negotiate power, capital, and national futures.




One of the most interesting aspects of following sport is understanding the diversity of actors, motivations, and interests shaping the business, and the economic, political, cultural, demographic, and technological forces driving it. In the African context, these include state–capital alliances; Afro-optimism and Africa rising discourses, imagineries and ambitions; urban and entertainment capitalism; commercialization (including marketing); transnational corporations; social mobility; national branding and 

sports diplomacy

; political capital and government legitimacy; the entrepreneurial state; youth-oriented politics and culture; consumerism; infrastructure; diaspora networks; celebrities; data; and media.




Understanding these forces (and their interplay) helps us better grasp, appreciate, anticipate, and interpret what is at stake when governments, corporations, and other players invest in sport. The economic, political, social, and professional gains can be considerable, as can the losses and fallout. Many actors are looking to score—on and off the field—in the coming months and years. Pay particular attention to the state’s multifaceted, evolving role in backing sports ventures, shaping markets, and pursuing political and commercial goals (revenues, etc.). Up-to-date data, though often difficult to obtain, is vital to understanding who is doing what, where, how, and why; who benefits, who appreciates, who pays, who is 

exploited

, 

harmed, 

or excluded, and what is at stake. 




This piece was first published by 

Eleven Named People

, and the original post can be read 

here

.





The post 

The sports commercializers are in town

 appeared first on 

ROAPE

.

author: Unknown
title: Hozat: Turkish authorities increase pressure on opposition to prevent broader support to process
content:
KCK Executive Council Co-Chair Besê Hozat spoke to Medya Haber TV about the current stage of the process, the women’s freedom struggle, practices in prisons, and regional developments.




Part one of the interview can be read 

here

. 




The government’s operations against municipalities continue. New trustees are being appointed. Most recently, a trustee was appointed to Halk TV. Many digital media accounts have been shut down, and some are being blocked. Attacks on newspapers are rampant, and arrests are on the rise. Overall, there are intense attacks directed at the press and media workers. It is as if the government is carrying out purges against those who do not align with it. What do these attacks signify at a time when the democratization of the republic is being debated?




That’s a good question. What is this state doing to prevent the process from becoming a societal movement? It is implementing a policy of oppression and hostility in the prisons. There has been no change in Rêber Apo’s [President Abdullah Öcalan] conditions to date. Isolation continues. While Rêber Apo took the initiative in this process, drove it forward, and brought it to this level, there is still no change in his conditions. Journalists were supposed to visit him, but it was prevented. The committee was supposed to go, convene, and work; that did not happen. His status was supposed to be formalized, but it didn’t happen. He was supposed to freely lead this process. There were supposed to be advisors, academics, and politicians visiting him. None of the things our leader demanded have happened. It’s a similar situation in prisons.




In order to prevent this process from gaining broader societal support in Turkey, the Turkish authorities are intensifying pressure on the opposition. They are attacking the press. There are particularly intense attacks on the opposition media. Dozens of journalists are being detained, arrested, and threatened. Yesterday, they held a very impressive march. I believe journalists marched in ten cities to voice their protests. I salute them. It’s truly very meaningful. These efforts need to develop further. There is intense pressure on the opposition press, on the opposition itself, and on workers. There is extremely intense pressure on all segments of society in Turkey that criticize this government or express dissatisfaction with it. This also prevents the process from becoming a social movement on the Turkish front. To prevent this process from becoming a societal movement – to prevent society from taking ownership of it – they are doing nearly everything in their power.




Like I said, there is currently intense pressure and oppression on the Turkish front as well. There is a policy of intense pressure targeting all opposition democratic, opposition liberal, and opposition groups. They do not want the truth to reach the public. That is why they’ve intensified the pressure on the opposition media so much. They don’t want the public to know the truth. Especially now that this funding crisis has come to the fore. The opposition media covered it extensively. A fierce wave of attacks has been launched. They also don’t want the government to be criticized for this process or for the truth to come to light.




And as a result of this intense attack, the process is not gaining traction among the Turkish public. It is blocking progress, and concerns regarding the state and the government on this issue are deepening even further. What kind of process is this? Can this process develop without democratization? That is the fundamental principle and philosophy of this process. It is the democratization of Turkey. Turkey cannot resolve the Kurdish issue without democratization. And Turkey cannot democratize without resolving the Kurdish issue. Turkey must embark on a democratic process. In this sense, the current government must take democratic steps. It must pursue very serious democratization in every legal, political, and social sphere. The opposite is happening. Increasing authoritarianism and an even more intense policy of repression and oppression are running rampant across all segments of society that oppose the government. Anti-democratic policies are intensifying and deepening. This process will neither become part of the social fabric nor develop in this manner. The development of this process depends on Turkey’s democratization. Currently, there are no signs of this.




The US has withdrawn from Iraq. Southern Kurdish forces have voiced their concerns about the upcoming period. They have indicated that a process similar to that of 2014 could unfold. Is there truly such a danger? How can these dangers be averted? What should the Kurdish forces do?




The US has withdrawn its ground forces from Iraq, as well as from Southern Kurdistan. As far as we know, only a small number of officials, playing an advisory role, remain. However, the US has not withdrawn from Iraq. It is not realistic to assess the situation that way. It is a hegemonic power. It is in the midst of a major war with Iran. It has a decisive influence in shaping the region. And the war continues to deepen. A stable order has not yet been established in the region. Therefore, the US remains in the region; the US is in Iraq. There is no question of any such withdrawal. It has military influence, political influence, and economic influence. It also has significant military bases in areas close to Iran. There are command centers directing this war right within the region itself. In that sense, it would not be realistic to describe this as a complete withdrawal. Because the US continues to have plans and interests in the region. The US has not relinquished its global hegemony. It is a hegemonic power. Whoever is the hegemon in the region becomes the hegemon of the world. That is a fact. Therefore, these dynamics continue.




Trying to strengthen the central states in the region is the nature of US policy. It sees its interests here. Tom Barrack’s statements, as well as Trump’s, have made this clear. They indicate that attacks may occur in the coming days. Current practices also point in that direction. We saw this in its Syrian policy. Something similar is unfolding in other countries as well – in Lebanon, and now in Iraq, too.




Of course, this situation poses a threat to the Kurds in Iraq – particularly regarding the status of the Kurds and the federal Kurdistan region. The strengthening of central governments naturally creates a threat and a risk for the status of Kurdistan as well. In order to eliminate these dangers and risks, democratic unity of the Kurds is needed. Truly, the only thing that will eliminate all these dangers from the Kurds’ perspective is the democratic unity of the Kurds – their democratic national unity. Therefore, every Kurdish organization – regardless of its structure or political orientation – must analyze the situation very carefully, recognize it, and be forward-thinking. They must understand that the only solution is democratic Kurdish unity and, on this basis, must change, transform, and take action. The development of such a process in Southern Kurdistan – and it playing an effective role in the matter of democratic Kurdish unity – is also linked to the overall democratization of the administrative system in Southern Kurdistan.




If the process of democratization develops within the governance model of Southern Kurdistan, then – in conjunction with other Kurdish organizations, institutions, and the civil society – such a problem will truly cease to exist for the Kurdish community. A strong national consciousness, spirit of unity, and sense of solidarity have emerged within society. There is significant social cohesion and unity. The problem lies within political organizations and structures. If a process of democratization develops in this regard and a democratic Kurdish unity takes shape, these threats to South Kurdistan can be averted. Democratic Kurdish unity is an urgent necessity.




Trump and Barack have stated that new attacks on Iran could occur in the coming days. The Tehran administration has lost a significant amount of power. What kind of change do external powers foresee in Iran? How can Iran find a way out of this process? And, most importantly, how should the Kurds respond to it?




The policy of international powers toward Iran is either to subdue the Iranian regime or to overthrow it. This is the framework within which the policy is developing. Iran has been severely worn down by the war waged against it so far. It has truly weakened. Of course, the US has also found itself in a serious impasse, particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz. In that sense, these powers have also faced difficulties—that is also a reality.




There is also a serious situation of weakness and contraction within Iran itself. To some extent, Iran’s current stance is providing a pretext for such interventions. If Iran were to democratize internally, if it were to respond to the demands of the people in Iran – including the demands of women – and undergo such a fundamental reform based on democratization, it could very easily repel these attacks. Even if the attacks were to occur, they would not achieve their goals. They claim to have the support of the people, but that is not the case. There is serious discontent and backlash within society. There is no point in deluding oneself. The policy of executions is leading to support for these attacks from many parts of society. The policy of executions generates serious anger and a serious anger and backlash – among the Kurdish community, within Iranian society, and in the international community. This, in turn, has a very serious negative impact on Iran.




The path forward is democratization. The struggle strategy developed by Kurdish organizations in this regard is very appropriate. The democratization of Iran based on local democracy is the most appropriate strategy. Kurdish organizations are waging a struggle on this basis. This must be carried out together with all the people of Iran, in conjunction with the democratic social dynamics within Iran, and in solidarity with the people.




It appears that Turkey has embarked on an intensive diplomatic effort. It signed the Mecca Alliance and joined the Badr Alliance. Furthermore, just a few days ago, it announced that it had renewed the agreement it had previously made with Libya regarding the Mediterranean. However, some countries, such as Israel and Egypt, have expressed their concerns regarding the agreement with Libya. Given these developments, what scenarios might emerge for the region in the future?




Turkey is attempting to fill the vacuum created by Iran’s weakening in the region. Clearly, the US and NATO have, to some extent, cleared the way for Turkey in this regard. The Mecca Alliance, the Badr Alliance, and the Libya Agreement were all established with some degree of US and NATO approval. None of this would have happened without them. However, a counter-front is naturally emerging in response to this. This has ever existed since the past. Israel, Greece, Egypt, and Southern Cyprus are increasingly forming a bloc against the defense and military alliances Turkey has been developing.




There is a major struggle for hegemony in the region. The region is undergoing a process of redesign. Turkey also wants to have a place in this reshaping; it wants to carve out a space for itself. In this sense, the decision to act in full alignment with NATO was made through the NATO agreement. Turkey has fully shifted its course toward the US and NATO. On the basis of representing US and NATO interests in the region, both the US and NATO have opened the way for Turkey to some extent. All these alliances and agreements have developed somewhat on this basis. In a way, this also demonstrates just how difficult, how weak, and how helpless Turkey’s situation is. In a sense, it has surrendered to NATO and to the US It is currently pursuing a policy in the region based on US interests. This Mecca Alliance was essentially formed in this way, against Iran. The US wanted this. And Turkey is trying to benefit from it as well. Within this framework, it is trying to carve out a place for itself in the region by relying on these alliances. Taking a stand against the Houthis also means opposing Iran.




Although they are striving to pursue a more coordinated and closely aligned policy on the Kurdish issue – and even though Turkey is making a serious effort to draw Iran toward that line, particularly on this matter – it is becoming clear that they will face serious conflicts over this issue in Yemen and in their regional policy. This is because Turkey, as a whole, is seeking to end Iran’s hegemony in the region and to consolidate its own position in the areas Iran has vacated. It’s a matter of Israeli hegemony versus Turkish hegemony. In this way, Israel and Turkey exist as two hegemonic powers in the region; in fact, over the past year, we have seen these two powers assert themselves even more. The mutual rhetoric is developing partly as a result of this. This led Turkey to face problems with Iran regarding the hegemonic dynamics in the region. That is clear. Even if they try to maintain harmony regarding the Kurdish issue, they will face problems in regional hegemony and regional politics. Because Turkey is pursuing a hostile policy toward Iran on this matter. As I said, it has surrendered to NATO and the US. It is trying to eliminate Iran’s influence in the region and position itself accordingly. But Turkey cannot ensure its own security in this manner.




There are deep fault lines in Turkey. One of these fault lines is the Kurdish issue, another is the Alevi issue. And there are many other social issues, such as the issue of women’s rights. They are very deep, very serious, and fundamental problems. Without resolving these fundamental issues on a democratic basis, Turkey cannot secure its survival, its future, or its very existence. Nor can it become a power in the region. It cannot become a lasting power. Periodically, by developing such military alliances and defense pacts, it has secured itself and guaranteed its existence; indeed, it has many such aspirations in the region as well, striving to establish itself as a hegemonic power. However, if Turkey does not resolve its internal problems – if it does not resolve these fundamental, historical issues, namely the Kurdish and Alevi issues – Turkey’s existence cannot be guaranteed. With this strategy and these interventions, Turkey will face serious challenges both at home and abroad. The reason Turkey has brought this process to an almost standstill, is precisely these developments in the region. It is trying to manage this situation in its own way through various means. But it is not able to manage it. These are very deep-rooted problems, and Turkey has been experiencing a civil war for over 50 years. If Turkey does not resolve this issue on a democratic basis, this civil war will deepen and throw Turkey into a completely different place. It should not delude itself. I find this important. Only by resolving the Kurdish issue and the Alevi issue, and by becoming democratic – only then can Turkey emerge unscathed from this storm.




There is a popular movement in France that was initiated by high school students and is gradually spreading. There have been periodic protests of this kind in France in the past as well. What do you think is the fundamental reason for the emergence of such movements at the very heart of capitalist modernity?




The system of capitalist modernity has been in a systematic crisis for the past 100 years, and it has especially deepened over the past 50 years. It is in a state of turmoil. The current social upheaval has turned into an explosion. It began primarily led by students but has now become a widespread social movement, spreading across Europe – especially in France and Italy – and has become a social uprising spreading everywhere. The streets are ablaze. This is the stage the crisis of capitalist modernity has reached. This system of exploitation – this multi-layered colonialism – has created a serious rift in society by diverting the economy’s resources, all of society’s resources, toward militarization, war, so-called defense, security, and the wealthy class. The rich have grown richer and richer. One segment – a tiny handful – has been condemned to deep poverty, while other segments of society have been condemned to deep poverty. This is the root cause of the current uprisings in Europe. The demand for social rights is at the heart of it. For instance, all resources are being diverted to military spending and such. They are flowing to the bourgeoisie, the upper bourgeoisie – in short, the wealthy class. A deep chasm has opened up between the poor and the rich. This is the deep crisis of capitalist modernity. This is the point to which the colonial system has arrived.




Now Turkey is capitalizing on this. It claims that it would be the center of democracy in these countries and points to the people’s plight, trying to gain some advantage for itself. Turkey’s situation is far worse than that of European countries. For years, Turkey has kept itself afloat through anti-Kurdish sentiment and the Kurdish issue. By militarizing society and fostering nationalism and racism, these regimes perpetuate themselves and stay in power. That is precisely why they leave the Kurdish issue unresolved. It is a fundamental form of capital – the capital of power. It has been turned into the law of maintaining power. There is no such intense issue in Europe right now. That’s why society is doing what it’s doing. Otherwise, in Turkey too, the exploitation of labor, the exploitation of women, social exploitation, and genocide are at their peak. Last time, a retired police officer committed suicide during protest actions. There are many suicides. Everywhere there is labor exploitation, poverty, and hunger. It’s rampant. Now, because Turkey is waging the biggest war, these resources are going toward the war. These resources are going toward militarization, leaving society hungry, destitute, and deprived of every right and freedom.




This is emerging as a systemic crisis, and Turkey is a part of this system. It is manifesting as a systemic crisis. And I believe this affects the entire world. These issues are not limited to Europe; they affect the whole world. Because this is a systemic crisis of capitalist modernity. It is a crisis of the nation-state system. It is a social explosion triggered by the Third World War. It is a state of upheaval. It is the outward manifestation of a crisis in this form. And these issues will not be limited to that region either. It in-fact began in the Middle East earlier. Now it is spreading everywhere, and the system is truly facing a downward spiral. This system is too much for this society to bear. Society can no longer bear it. It cannot bear this colonial and oppressive system.




It is very intense everywhere, and young people are leading the way. This is important. Huge crowds are in revolt, on their feet. This needs to become much more organized everywhere. With a program and strategy, a genuine alternative to capitalist modernity can emerge. That is why a program is important in the struggle, and strategy is important. Organized power – along with its program, strategy, and struggle strategy – is crucial. If this social popular movement, this movement of the peoples, can achieve this, it can gradually bring forth such an alternative to the system. These things are important.




In fact, the “democratic nation” and “confederal system” project developed by Rêber Apo is the remedy and alternative for the entire world. The alternative of democratic modernity against capitalist modernity… It is a genuine solution project that addresses the needs of the entire society, of the peoples, and of women.

title: DBP and DEM Party: We will be in Varto on 2 November
content:
The Varto (Gimgim) district organizations of the DBP and DEM Party set up a stand in Kox Square as part of the legal proceedings against the geothermal power plant project.




Speaking in a press conference, DBP District Co-Chair Aziz Oral said that the project threatens not only the natural environment but also the living spaces and cultural existence of the local population.




Oral pointed out that potential water pollution could affect agriculture and livestock farming, as well as a wider area of the Euphrates basin via the Murat River. He emphasized the need to protect nature, water resources, and the right of future generations to life.




The DBP and DEM Party called on residents to gather in the village of Xwarik on 2 November for an expert inspection related to the planned geothermal power plant (JES) project in Varto.

title: Iranian director Jafar Panahi sentenced to 5 years and 1 month in prison
content:
Iranian director and screenwriter Jafar Panahi was sentenced to 5 years and 1 month in prison in a case heard by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. The court ordered the confiscation of all his movable and immovable assets, banned him from social media activities for two years, and prohibited him from leaving the country.




According to a report by HRANA, citing Emtedad, Panahi’s lawyer, Mostafa Nili, stated that the verdict had been issued in his client’s absence. Nili said Panahi learned of the ruling after his bank accounts were frozen.




Lawyer Nili said that although his client returned to Iran on March 30, 2026, the case file listed him as being outside the country, and he had not been notified of the hearing date. Nili also stated that an arrest warrant had been issued for Panahi on May 20, 2026, and that the director currently faces three separate legal cases.




Panahi had previously been sentenced to one year in prison in a separate case on charges of “propaganda against the regime.” He was also given a two-year travel ban and prohibited from joining political and social organizations. His request for a retrial was rejected in June 2026.

title: Dayîka Îpek Erê: Heta Mûsa O. bê girtin, ez ê dengê xwe bilind bikim
content:
Çawişê pispor ê berê Mûsa O. êrişa zayendî li Îpek Era 18 salî kiribû û bûbû sedem ku Er xwe bikuje. Her weha 10 sal cezayê girtîgehê lê hatibû birîn. Mûsa O. bi tohmeta ku “bûye sedema xwekuştinê” dihat darizandin.




1emîn Dadgeha Cezê û Esliyê ya Êlihê di 22ê Cotmeha 2026an de biryar dabû ku tu delîlek şênber nîne ku Mûsa O. bûye sedem ku 

Îpek Er

 xwe bikuje. Her weha dadgehê biryara beraeta Mûsa O. dabû.




Dayika Îpek Erê, Hikmet Kilinçê derbarê beraetkirina sûcdar Mûsa O. de ji JînNewsê re axiviye û bertek nîşanî biryarê daye.



















Mûsa O., di doza Îpek Erê de beraet kir




26 Cotmeh 2026










"Ez nahêlim mafên keça min werin binpêkirin"




Hikmet Kilinçê berteka xwe ya li hember beraetê bi van gotinan anî ziman:







"Piştî veşartina keça min, mafê wî tune ku bi azadî bigere. Wî û hevalê wî keça min xapandin, derman dan wê, ew birin Îzmîrê û birin otêlan. Kesên din keça min hişyar kirin û gotin, 'Ji vir derkeve, ew ê te bifroşin.'  Dewletê ji min re got, 'Em nahêlin mafên keça te werin binpêkirin,' lê ev çênebû. Ez ê her tiştê ku ji destê min tê bikim. Divê dewlet teqez wî bigire. Ez dixwazim ew qatil were girtin ji ber ku ew qatilê min e. Gotinên dawî yên keça min ev bûn; 'Divê hûn nehêlin mafên min werin binpêkirin.' Min baweriya xwe bi dewletê anî, lê dewletê biryara beraeta Mûsa O. da. Ji bo lêgerîna edaletê ya ji bo keça min, çi ji destên min bê ez ê bikim. Divê dewlet teqez wî ceza bike."







"Ew ê sibehê tecawizî kesekî din bike"




Hikmet Kilinç, diyar kir ku ew ê bêdeng nemînin û wiha berdewam kir, "Divê dewletê ew girtiba. Ez nizanim çima ew nayê girtin. Mûsa O. zilamê dewletê bû û hîn jî wisa ye, ji ber vê yekê wî beraet kir. Mûsa Orhan dê sibehê yan roja din biçe û tecawizî jineke din bike. Ma ne şerm e? "



















Parêzerên Îpek Erê: Mûsa O. ji hêza dewletê sûd wergirtiye




6 Kanûn 2021










Hikmet Kilinç bal bir ser gotinên Suleyman Soylu û wiha domand:







"Dema keça min hat kuştin, Suleyman Soylu ji Sêrt, Amed, Stenbol û Misircê 20 parêzvan şandin Hamdûnayê. Ew bi xwe hat Hamdûnayê û got, 'Di tu şert û mercan de bi Kurdî neaxive, navûdengê xwe di çavên dewletê de xera neke. Ez nahêlim ku mafên keça te werin binpêkirin.' Suleyman Soylu ev yek bi xwe ji min re got. Min baweriya xwe pê anî û wekî ku wî got kir. Min got, 'Tekane tiştê ku ez dixwazim ew e ku kujer bê girtin.' Piştî şeş salan, beraeta Mûsa O. hat. Ji niha û pê ve, ez ê her tiştê ku divê bê gotin bibêjim."







"Ez ê heta ku Mûsa Orhan bê girtin têbikoşim"




Hikmet Kilinç da zanîn heta Mûsa O. bê girtin ew ê têbikoşe û wiha got, "Heta Mûsa O. bê girtin, ez ê dengê xwe bilind bikim. Ger dewlet Mûsa O. negire, ez ê her tiştê ku di hişê min de ye bibêjim. Ez dixwazim her kes rabe ser piyan, ez dixwazim her kes ji bo Îpek li edaletê bigere. Ez ê heta dawiya jiyana xwe ji bo keça xwe têbikoşim."



















Malbata Îpek Erê giliyê parêzerên Mûsa O.yî kiriye




6 Tîrmeh 2021













Çi bûbû?




Li navçeya Qubînê ya Êlihê, Î. E.ya 18 salî ya di 16ê Tîrmeha 2020an de hewl dabû xwe bikuje. Î. E. yê paşê aşkere kiribû ku Mûsa O. çawişê pispor tecawiz li wê kiriye. Î. E. ya ku li nexweşxaneyê dihate dermankirin, îro can daye.




Î. E. piştî ku xwestibû xwe bikuje û ew li nexweşxaneyê dihate dermankirin, malbata wê nameya wê dîtibû. Î. E. yê di nameya xwe de gotibû ku çawişê pispor Mûsa O.yî tecawiz lê kiriye.




Malbata Î. E. yê giliyê çawişê pispor kiribû û Mûsa O. heman rojê hatibû desteserkirin. Çawişê pispor di îfadeya xwe de ew tohmet qebûl nekiribûn.




Li gorî nûçeya Ajansa Mezopotamyayê Rapora Tipa Edlî aşkere kiribû ku Mûsa O. yî tecawizî Î. E. yê kiriye. Di encama vê rewşê de Mûsa O. yî îdia kiribû ku dema ew û Î. E. li Sêrtê hatine ba hev ew serxweş bûye.




Biryara “nepenîtiyê” ji bo dosyaya lêpirsînê hatibû dayîn. Çawişê pispor bi tohmeta ku “istismara zayendî ya xurt” kiriye şandibûn ber destê heyeda Dadweriya Silh û Cezayan a Nobedar a Sêrtê lê li vir bi şertê kontrola edlî serbest bûbû.




Malbata Î. E. yê ji bo alîkariya hiqûqî serî li Komeleya Mafên Mirovan a Êlihê dabûn.




Di 22ê Cotmeha 2026an de 1emîn Dadgeha Cezê û Esliyê ya Êlihê biryar dabû ku tu delîlek şênber nîne ku Mûsa O. bûye sedem ku 

Îpek Er

 xwe bikuje. Her weha dadgehê biryara beraeta Mûsa O. dabû.







(EMK/AY)

title: QUORN HUNT TRAINING HOUNDS TO KILL: WRITE TO YOUR MP
content:
The Hunt Saboteurs Association is asking our supporters to contact their MPs following the release of horrific drone footage involving the Quorn Hunt in Leicestershire.




Members of the Quorn Hunt use the fox’s body to encourage hounds to tear it apart. 

Image: Northants Hunt Saboteurs




On Friday 16 October 2026, Northants Hunt Saboteurs filmed an incident near Kirby Bellars in which a fox was killed by hounds during a Quorn Hunt cubbing meet.




Hounds converge on the fox as hunt staff look on. Image: 

Northants Hunt Saboteurs




The footage shows hounds seizing and tearing at the fox while hunt staff intervene to repeatedly encourage the hounds to attack. A hunting horn can be seen being blown over the hounds to reinforce the association between the horn call and the kill!




Take action: Contact your MP




Don’t let this disturbing footage go unnoticed.




Write to your MP, ask them to watch the video and to support robust legislation to strengthen the Hunting Act. 




Template letter below:




Organised Hunts hunting as usual – Famous Quorn Hunt filmed killing a fox




Dear [MP]




The 1st November will see the official start of the foxhunting season, but hunts have been out since August training their hounds to hunt and kill. This is called autumn hunting by them and cub hunting by the rest of us. 




This is illustrated by the film we obtained taken from a drone showing the Quorn Hunt killing a fox. This is ‘trail hunting’ in its bloody reality, and it happened just a few days ago, on the eve of the BHSA’s National Trail Hunting Day.




The full video can be viewed here: 

https://www.huntsabs.org.uk/smokescreen-saturday-exposed/




Cub hunting is not some isolated activity. It is the preparation for the hunting season ahead. Throughout the autumn, young hounds are taught what to chase, what to kill and how to respond to the huntsman’s commands. What they learn – or fail to learn – during these crucial weeks sets the tone for the entire season.




This is what makes the Quorn Hunt footage so damning. It shows hounds being deliberately encouraged to seize and tear at a fox, with hunt staff repeatedly intervening to reinforce that behaviour.




As the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) and the Countryside Alliance prepared to showcase so-called ‘trail hunting’ on National Trail Hunting Day – aka Smokescreen Saturday – the Quorn Hunt provided a horrifying glimpse of the reality behind the myth of trail laying.




The BHSA and defenders of so-called trail hunting want the public to believe the same hounds will spend the season following scent trails. Yet here they are, being trained on foxes, and of course, killing to the delight of the hunters.




The footage strikes at the very heart of the trail hunting smokescreen.




We need parliament to finish the consultation and push through a real hunting ban in the next parliament term as promised in the manifesto.




Regards




[Name]




[Address]




Find contact details for your MP here



















The post 

QUORN HUNT TRAINING HOUNDS TO KILL: WRITE TO YOUR MP

 appeared first on 

Hunt Saboteurs Association

author: Joseph Lee
title: For Indigenous peoples in Brazil, the election results offer a reprieve — not a resolution
content:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s reelection as president of Brazil gave Indigenous communities a measure of relief after a campaign in which his opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, promised to halt recognition of new Indigenous territories and push for more mining and development.




“For Indigenous Peoples, the reelection of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is more than a victory, and it is bigger than Brazil,” said Edson Krenak, who is Indigenous Krenak. “It is not about victory; it is about the possibility to dream and to fight without fear of death.”




But Sunday’s runoff election strengthened Bolsonaro’s movement in Congress, where his Liberal Party won the largest number of seats in both houses and the broader right gained a Senate majority. Leaders warn that this could open their territories to mining, weaken environmental protections, and roll back land rights, making it much harder for Lula to advance his Indigenous and environmental agendas.




Climate Observatory, a nonprofit coalition of 172 organizations, says 

70 percent of the incoming lawmakers

 oppose the climate and environmental agenda, according to The Associated Press.




The stakes were especially high for Indigenous peoples because Bolsonaro campaigned on policies aligned with those of his father Jair Bolsonaro, whose presidency from 2019 to 2023 saw an increase in mining, land grabs, 

deforestation

, and 

attacks on their rights

. Amazon deforestation reached a record in 2022, and Indigenous leaders say their communities endured unchecked violence from illegal mining operations during the elder Bolsonaro’s time in office.




His son finished more than 2 million votes ahead of Lula in the first election earlier this month, but neither candidate secured the 50 percent required to win outright. That result sparked fear in Indigenous communities and environmental advocates, who warned that 

the future of the Amazon was at stake

. Lula came back to win Sunday’s runoff by roughly 4.4 million votes, securing a fourth, nonconsecutive term as president.




In an interview between the two rounds of voting, Toya Manchineri, the general coordinator of the Coordination of Indigenous Organizations of the Brazilian Amazon, or COIAB, said Indigenous peoples across the rainforest were deeply concerned about the possibility of a Bolsonaro win. Much of the last three years of Lula’s administration were spent undoing the damage the Bolsonaro administration caused, Manchineri said.




Manchineri said Lula’s term has largely been a period of rebuilding as Indigenous peoples gained greater roles in decision making. “We were only beginning to see the resources returning,” he said.




In 2023, the administration established the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples and appointed Sônia Guajajara to lead it. Lula also revitalized the federal Indigenous affairs agency FUNAI after Bolsonaro had used it to support agribusiness, despite Indigenous resistance. The government also announced just before the election that Amazon 

deforestation had fallen to its lowest level

 since recordkeeping began in 1988, according to the AP.




Still, Indigenous leaders say the progress made under Lula has not resolved deeper conflicts over land, development, and decision-making.




“Lula’s victory prevents a president who promised to halt Indigenous land demarcation from taking office, but our territories are far from safe,” Alessandra Korap Munduruku, coordinator of the Munduruku Pariri Indigenous Association, 

said in a statement

. “We have demanded that Lula’s government respect our decisions and listen to Indigenous Peoples before advancing projects that affect our rivers and forests. Congress has become more dangerous for us, and we must remain organized. Our struggle does not end with an election’s outcome.” 




For Indigenous organizations, Lula’s victory is cause for hope, but they must now work with a Congress dominated by lawmakers who have already voted in favor of easing environmental protections and against Indigenous land claims. Given that dynamic, Krenak expressed concern about the difficulty Lula may face advancing his agenda. “The costs of negotiating with the Congress and senate will be very high, if ever successful,” he said.




The election also came amid years of Indigenous voters struggling to access the polls. Earlier this month, a court denied a request for transportation assistance filed by Indigenous peoples in the Javari Valley in northern Brazil. Other efforts were more successful: Court rulings elsewhere helped 

secure government transportation

 for Indigenous voters in remote areas, while Indigenous communities across the Amazon organized to increase turnout, AP reported.




“Despite the challenges faced throughout the electoral process, Indigenous peoples of the Amazon made their voices heard at the polls across all nine states of the Brazilian Amazon, reaffirming their commitment to democracy, national sovereignty, and the defense of Indigenous rights. We marked the ballot boxes in defense of life, our territories, and Brazil’s future!” COIAB said in a statement. “Brazil’s future is Indigenous, and it begins in our territories! WE ARE THE ANSWER!”




For Krenak, however, Lula’s victory is only the beginning. He says he wants to see more meaningful progress during the president’s next term.




“By 2030, success should not be measured by how many Indigenous leaders stand besides officials at summits,” he said. “But by whether Indigenous Peoples gain real authority to prevent their territories to become sacrifice zones, but territories of life, reciprocity and generosity.”




This story was originally published by 

Grist

 with the headline 

For Indigenous peoples in Brazil, the election results offer a reprieve — not a resolution

 on Oct 28, 2026.

title: Democratic Socialists of America & Libertarian Socialism
content:
Title

: Democratic Socialists of America & Libertarian Socialism

Subtitle

: A Debate

Date

: 1983

Notes

: 1983 debate from the Workers Solidarity Alliance magazine 

ideas & action

 on whether or not anarcho-syndicalists and libertarian socialists should participate in the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).

Source

: From 

ideas & action

 issue # 3, Spring 1983.

 Retrieved on 10-27-2026 from 

libcom.org/article/democratic-socialists-america-libertarian-socialism




Editors’ Note/Introduction: 

Bureaucratic Utopianism?

, 

by Tom Wetzel




The last few years have been a discouraging period for those in the U. S. who want fundamental change in the direction of freedom and equality. Though struggle against the powers-that-be goes on, as always, struggles in the last few years have tended to be episodic and isolated. It’s hard to find signs of a widespread willingness to fight the bosses and the government. This lack of movement among the mainstream of the population is, in all likelihood, the root cause of the general political drift to the right and, as well, the evolution towards social-democracy among so many leftists whose radicalism had been spawned by the movements of the late 60s and early

 ’70s. 

One evidence of this latter trend was the evolution of the New American Movement (NAM) away from the revolutionary New Left politics of its origin, culminating in its merger last year with Michael Harrington’s Democratic Socialist Organizing Committee

 (

DSOC) — a tiny social-democratic sect that had emerged from the break-up of the old Socialist Party in 1972. That split-up had been itself a reflection of the Vietnam War, since the Socialist Party of the 1960s had been firmly in the hands of the “State Department socialists” who thought the Communists were such a threat that it merited allying themselves with U.S. bosses, by supporting the U.S. government’s imperialist foreign policy. This fit in with the practice of cooperation with the bosses which characterized the union chiefs who controlled the Socialist Party in those days. The split in the SP created three groups

 — 

the majority formed the Social Democrats USA, made up of such class-collaborationist union leaders as Lloyd McBride of the United Steelworkers and Albert Shanker of the American Federation of Teachers. They had no compunction about supporting U.S. imperialism in Indo-China (and anywhere else) right to the bitter end. In 1981, for example, Shanker’s AFT ran a major spread in the “American Teacher” supporting U.S. policy in El Salvador as a struggle for “democracy” (even while members of the Salvadoran teachers union were being tortured or hunted down by forces of the local dictatorship). Another outfit that came out of the break-up of the old SP was the group headed by ex-Milwaukee mayor Frank Zeidler which resurrected the name “Socialist Party “ for itself. This group opposed the Vietnam war but more on the basis of liberal pacifist than class-struggle grounds. And finally, the third fragment from the old SP was Harrington’s liberal group who had no consistently anti-militarist or anti-imperialist position (for example, they have supported U.S. military aid to Israel until just recently) but who simply followed the evolution of the liberal mainstream in its belated opposition to the Vietnam War. Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) is the organization which resulted from the absorption of NAM by Harrington’s DSOC. Chris Nielsen, whose piece on “DSA and Libertarian Socialists” we are printing here, recommends the “democratic socialist” milieu — and specifically DSA — as an appropriate area for participation by anti-authoritarian socialists or anarchists. Though we disagree with Chris’ conclusion, we think he raises a number of issues worth discussing. Social democratic ideas are on the rise, and the sort of position Chris argues for is one that needs to be answered by libertarian socialists.




What is “social-democracy’’? Social-democracy is not unique in pursuing or supporting short-range changes to benefit working people — the revolutionary libertarian unions of the early decades of this century, such as the IWW in this country, used militant tactics for goals short of class emancipation. Social-democratic politics is typified by a reliance on electoral politics with the union bureaucracy providing the major base of support. Social-democratic tactics have traditionally led to a statist conception of what socialism is all about — socialist politics get defined in terms of what state policies the social democratic leaders will implement on our behalf once in office, and structure of socialism usually gets defined in terms of nationalization — and certainly this is the content of DSA’s politics. Of course, it is true that some people who have proposed the use of social-democratic tactics have not proposed statist solutions. There was the now-defunct People’s Bicentennial Commission (an off-shoot of NAM) which proposed the idea of “self-management” in a market framework, achieved through the electoral process. (An old idea, first advocated in the 1800s by LaSalle, the father of the German Social Democratic Party.) And then there are the tiny DeLeonist sects like the New Union Party and the Socialist Labor Party who propose to use the electoral process to abolish the state (eventually) and institute industrial self-management. Chris, on the other hand, is not recommending social-democratic politics for our participation because he wishes to defend the actual political content of social-democratic groups like DSA but only because he believes that such politics represent a necessary intermediate stage in the evolution of the consciousness of the American people towards a socialist future.

author: Unknown
title: Du moment et de la violence
content:
Un constat et une analyse sur le mouvement commencé en octobre 2026. Le rôle de la défaite et de la violence et ses possibles perspectives de victoires ou de défaites.




Article publié initialement dans


International Society of Historical Defeat




Le siècle dernier a été celui des défaites de tout mouvement cherchant à renverser ce monde. Le siècle qui commence attend une victoire.




ISHD

 a été fondé en 2016 en partant du constat de l'échec de toutes les précédentes tentatives de suppression de l'économie marchande, comme illusion et comme réalité, ainsi que des formes de domination nécessaires à son maintien et à son apparence. Cet outil a pour but l'analyse des défaites précédentes et la pratique de cette critique dans le moment présent.




Dans la manière dont le phénomène apparaît, son apparence produit aussi son négatif. Le positif chemine toujours avec lui. Qu'y a-t-il derrière le phénomène

 

? Rien : l'économie n'a pas de réalité propre dans le monde, et son apparence est ce qui la constitue. C'est ce qui rend la critique si difficile, car il n'y a pas d'essence cachée à dévoiler, seulement un système de croyances à défaire. De là vient le piège de la positivité immédiate. L'idée d'une positivité qui apparaîtrait d'elle-même et qui se donnerait les moyens de renverser ce monde est précisément l'apparence et la négation de ce renversement. On ne peut créer une positivité qu'à partir du négatif.




Les relents de l'histoire sont partout, et tout mouvement qui se donne pour but la suppression de cette société y est soumis. La première nécessité de ce siècle est la victoire.




Il existe une notion ancienne dans l'alchimie arabe, le Mizân : la balance, le mouvement qui penche d'un côté puis de l'autre, entre les lettres de l'ombre et de la lumière. Le poids de l'un dans l'autre. C'est toujours un moment délicat, un jeu entre l'événement, la liberté de ce qui arrive, la conscience et l'absence de conscience : un moment particulier où tout peut se jouer. C'est le moment où la guerre des pauvres contre les pauvres fait basculer l'émeute en insurrection. C'est la différence, avant tout, entre ceux qui croient et ceux qui n'ont plus rien à croire, entre ceux qui regardent, ceux qui font et ceux qui conservent. Dans l'affrontement présent, il y a donc, comme toujours, les acteurs, ceux qui brûlent les poubelles et ceux qui les protègent, et les spectateurs, ceux qui regardent.




L'organisation de la violence urbaine n'est pas la guérilla, contrairement aux mots mythiques accolés à la «

 

guérilla urbaine

 

». Ce n'est ni une guerre ni une guérilla : il faudrait qu'il existe une équivalence minimale entre les participants. Or il n'en existe aucune. Dans une guérilla, les partisans connaissent leur territoire, ils en maîtrisent les possibilités, ce qui peut parfois leur permettre de compenser la disparité entre leurs moyens et ceux de l'adversaire. Ce n'est absolument pas le cas dans les villes modernes : le parti adverse a lui-même organisé le territoire de l'affrontement, il le contrôle absolument, à la fois concrètement et abstraitement. C'est donc ailleurs que se situent les moyens à employer.




Il faut tout de même rappeler quelques principes tactiques légués par l'histoire de l'affrontement urbain.




Rappelons-en quelques-unes, très spécifiques, tirées du mouvement étudiant japonais de la fin des années 1960 :




La charge en «

 

serpent

 

» (snake dance)

. Les étudiants se tenaient fermement par le bras, en lignes larges de plusieurs dizaines de personnes, et chargeaient en courant selon un mouvement ondulatoire de gauche à droite. Ce balancier rendait la ligne très difficile à rompre pour la police, la force d'impact étant répartie sur toute la chaîne humaine.




Les gebabō (bâtons de combat)

. Contrairement aux émeutiers, qui usaient de projectiles de fortune, les militants employaient de longues pièces de bois carrées ou des tuyaux d'échafaudage. Ils s'en servaient de manière coordonnée pour tenir la police à distance, en piquant vers l'avant comme des phalanges antiques plutôt qu'en frappant en désordre.




Les barricades modulaires

. Dans la rue, ils utilisaient le mobilier urbain ou des rails arrachés. Sur les campus, ils ont théorisé la construction de barricades intérieures massives, destinées à transformer les bâtiments en forteresses autonomes capables de tenir des semaines. Les derniers affrontements parisiens et dans d'autres villes ont commencé à essayer de supprimer tout centre de manifestations et de cortèges en étant partout et nulle part. Cette tactique de manifestations diffuses a rencontré un certain succès.




Mais la tactique ne vaut que par ce qu'elle engage.




L'engagement




 Nous avons précédemment écrit qu'il y avait plusieurs manières d'étouffer la soif de débat qui se manifeste dans certains moments. La première est le discours sur la violence (voir les articles précédents), la seconde celui sur la démocratie.




Le mot «

 

démocratie

 

» est intouchable et indiscutable. Ce n'est que dans le moment où la dispute fait irruption que son sens peut changer. Cette irruption soudaine prend une forme et un nom : l'engagement. L'ambiguïté de ce mot (promesse, action d'engager quelqu'un, combat de courte durée et localisé, etc.) se retrouve dans le choix du moment où l'engagement apparaît nécessaire.




L'engagement dans la guerre civile, contrairement à la guerre, peut avoir lieu sans consentement mutuel, d'où l'importance, pour l'une ou l'autre des parties, d'en connaître le début. Une des premières choses à faire est de reconnaître l'engagement, car le premier à reconnaître qu'il a commencé prend un avantage certain.




Dans un engagement restreint, les pertes ou l'absence de pertes s'équilibrant, le but le plus évident est la victoire morale : la détermination, l'effondrement moral ou le coup porté au moral adverse. Le but d'un premier engagement est avant tout sa publicité.




Dans le moment présent : le silence pour eux, le bruit pour nous.





22 octobre 2026




Pour L'International Society of Historical Defeat




Section française : Mourad Beleksir




Section allemande : Jurgen Noll

title: Incendie de la mairie de Limoges
content:
point de vue anarchiste




Communiqué anarchiste




Réaction après l'incendie de la mairie de Limoges




À travers ce communiqué, voici un point de vue anarchiste sur l'incendie de la mairie de Limoges. 


Mr Guérin est une personne d'extrême droite, proche des réseaux de l'action française.




Le 17 octobre, c'est un mouvement révolutionnaire qui s'est formé.




Cependant il ne s'est pas formé du jour au lendemain, mais à travers des dizaines d'années de luttes.




L'anarchie n'est pas un parti mais un outil de réflexion autour de la société, avec notamment l'absence de pouvoir, de commandement et d'autorité. L'anarchie est un but à atteindre désirable et pratique. L'anarchie refait surface avec notamment un mouvement de jeunesse à l'international acquis à la cause, et souvent réprimé par les forces de l'ordre notamment à travers les Free Party.




Si la droite et ses idées extrêmes accompagnés par les renseignements territoriaux n'ont rien vu venir c'est qu'iels sont ignorantes, idiotes et qu'iels ne pensent qu'à leur confort et carrière au mépris des classes discriminées.




Abus de pouvoir, harcèlement, détournements d'argents publics, favoritisme, pantouflage, etc. sont légions dans les instances des collectivités territoriales.




À Limoges, Mr Guérin a gagné les récentes élections. L'attaque subie par la mairie est aussi une réponse au refus d'une société gouvernée par des personnes autoritaires, bercées par des idées de haines extrémistes envers certains groupes ethniques ou politiques.




Mr Guérin parle de maison commune, mais refuse toutes concertations avec Mr Maudet, élu et députée Haute-Vienne de la France Insoumise qu'il déqualifie sans cesse par mépris de classe. 


Drôle d'ambiance pour une maison commune




Cette personne n'est en aucun cas digne de diriger une mairie comme Limoges.




Si cet édifice a brûler ce 17 octobre, c'est aussi le fascisme qui a brûlé.




Face à la volonté de Mr Guérin de démissionner, n'est-il pas temps de profiter de cet instant, pour instaurer une société anarchiste à Limoges et expérimenter cet outil.




Pour terminer, les revendications, les recours administratifs et les actions menées depuis des années par les militant.e.s des droits humains et environnementaux n'ont eu pour réponse que la violence d'un État en faillite de sa propre devise.




La réponse collective à travers la France, (face à l'État totalitaire pour ne pas dire fasciste, du système libéral, mis en place Macron et ses sbires), en ce 17 octobre est une victoire politique. Et un premier avertissement.




La démission de la présidence et de l'ensemble de ce gouvernement est la seule et unique réponse possible et plausible.

author: dev
title: Les Voyageurs et le chtar
content:
Dans cette nouvelle lettre que Ritchy Thibault est parvenu à nous faire parvenir depuis la prison de Fleury-Mérogis, il revient sur le rapport que les voyageurs entretiennent avec la prison. Depuis son expérience personnelle et familiale, il raconte un « art de la carcérologie » qui est aussi une manière de ne jamais céder sur la dignité et la liberté

 [

1

]

.







« Nos ancêtres, nos vieux ont vécu pire, donc on garde la tête haute. » 




Mickaël Gilgenmann dans une lettre du 5 octobre 2026 depuis la centrale de Lannemezan où il est incarcéré non loin du site d'un ancien camp de concentration pour Nomades. 







Mickaël c'est mon 

pral

 [frère]. Ça fait maintenant quelques mois que l'on correspond. Il est rentré au 

chtar

 [prison] à 22 ans avec une peine de 5 ans pour un 

tchore

 [vol]. Il en a aujourd'hui 37 et est encore retenu derrière les barreaux suite à une série de « peines internes » prononcées contre lui du fait qu'il a toujours refusé de baisser la tête. La semaine juste avant d'être écroué, j'ai pris un café avec un autre de mes 

pral 

voyageurs dans le 95. Je lui ai dit : « T'as un beau tatouage sur la main. » Il a en effet trois points en triangle (mort aux vaches), signe et affirmation d'un profond rejet et mépris de l'autorité – que l'on est si nombreux à arborer sur nos corps chez nous. Mon 

papou

 [grand-père] l'avait sur sa main, lui qui a aussi connu le 

chtar

 en région parisienne avant de venir s'installer en Dordogne et de fonder sa famille. Après ma remarque, cet homme m'a répondu : « Je l'avais fait quand j'étais tombé au chtar à 22 ans pour un 

tchore

. » Quelques semaines avant de me faire ramasser par les 

klisté

 [arrêté par la police] et de finir entre ces vilains murs, j'ai mangé avec un copain voyageur avec qui je milite et son père. Le sien était sous le coup d'un mandat de recherche pour une peine de 10 mois de 

chtar

 et le mien y était déjà depuis presque 4 ans dans un centre de détention. Alors maintenant que je suis ici privé de ma liberté sous le régime de l'isolement, je suis dans l'obligation de me poser la question : sommes-nous condamnés à finir en prison lorsque l'on naît gitan ?




Des destins déjà écrits ? 




Quand j'étais petit, je me souviens que les gens de ma famille me disaient souvent : « Toi tu n'iras pas au 

chtar

, tu 

rakav

 [parles] bien. » Et bien force est de constater qu'ils se sont trompés. Comme mes deux frères, déscolarisés en primaire et au collège, je viens moi aussi d'y tomber alors pourtant qu'il est vrai que je suis dans une école qui se veut « grande ».




Dans une lettre du 12 octobre 2026, voilà ce que m'a dit Aurélie Garand, la sœur d'Angelo abattu de cinq balles en 2017 par le GIGN : « Mine de rien le destin des Voyageurs est quasi écrit d'avance par l'État. De Angelo à toi, d'une conduite sans permis à un étudiant de 22 ans avec des mots : les pieds dans le système carcéral. Au final c'est leur case. » Au fond si je me refais la trame il y a effectivement quelque chose de logique. Toutes les heures de route, les allers-retours dès mon plus jeune âge avec mes frères et ma mère pour aller voir mon père au parloir. Les moments où les enseignants nous interrogeaient sur les activités de nos parents et où je déclarais au sujet de mon père : « Il est en déplacement professionnel. » L'hiver dernier, je suis descendu lui apporter un « colis de Noël » auquel ont droit les détenus en fin d'année. Cet été, où une agente pénitentiaire est venue chez mes parents installer un bracelet électronique à mon grand-frère, handicapé et en proie à de graves crises d'angoisse – pour le châtier suite à une simple bagarre. J'ai enragé et il y avait de quoi puisque quelques jours après la pose de cet affreux appareil il a fait une tentative de suicide. Ma colère était telle que pendant qu'elle installait ce sinistre machin, j'ai coupé au couteau le câble d'alimentation d'un de ces boitiers en me disant que ça permettrait sûrement au prochain de gagner quelques jours en liberté. J'étais en compagnie de mon pote rom Spartacus qui a aussi connu l'enfer du 

chtar

. C'est lui qui m'a expliqué l'origine sémantique de ce mot. En effet, en romanès et en manouche, ça signifie littéralement « quatre », le nombre – comme les quatre murs qui te coupent du monde.




Dans une lettre du 7 octobre 2026, une Voyageuse m'a livré le témoignage suivant : « Mon arrière-grand-mère Aimée Leguenée a fait deux séjours (18 mois) à la prison de Tours pour vagabondage alors qu'elle avait 12 enfants. […] Je pense à ta maman. La vie a fait que je suis allée voir mon fils à la maison d'arrêt. » Le récit de cette femme avec qui j'ai un lointain lien de parenté résume le sort auquel l'État français assigne les Voyageurs : l'incarcération. Le père de mon arrière-grand-père écope lui aussi d'une condamnation pour vagabondage. Les condamnations ont frappé toutes les générations sans discontinuer jusqu'à la mienne.




Le prix à payer




Est-ce que les souffrances et cet engrenage liberticide pendront fin un jour ? Le jour où les Voyageurs n'iront plus au 

chtar

, l'État aura gagné, il nous aura assimilés et réduit à néant nos singulières inscriptions dans le monde. Si nous finissons autant dans la case prison, c'est précisément parce l'on refuse de rentrer dans leurs cases et dans leur moule uniformisateur. Pour paraphraser le poète Kery James, on paie le prix de la marginalité et de la rébellion. C'est parce que l'on refuse catégoriquement leurs lois et leurs codes qu'ils nous enferment.




Je me souviens d'un des nombreux reportages antitsiganes diffusés à la télé que j'avais visionnés lorsque j'étais petit, dans lequel un vieux gadjo disait : « Mais vous comprenez bien que ce n'est pas possible. Nous on dort la nuit et on vit le jour, eux c'est l'inverse. » Tant que l'on restera, que l'on préservera notre intégrité de Rabouins comme il est d'usage qu'on s'auto-désigne, ils voudront nous mettre à l'ombre du monde. Dans le fond ce qui nous arrive c'est bien malheureux mais ça a quand même une signification très positive : la société des gadjé n'a pas eu raison de nous. Ils encagent nos corps, mais nos esprits échappent à leurs griffes et demeurent libres.




Nous sommes tous des prisonniers politiques – voilà des siècles que nous affrontons avec des registres de tactiques diversifiées, l'État et la République française. Nos casiers judiciaires sont parsemés de condamnations pour « outrage et rébellion » car il nous est impossible de courber l'échine devant une pourriture déguisée de bleu. Nos casiers sont remplis de condamnations pour « violence » car nous savons pertinemment que nous ne pouvons compter que sur la force de nos corps pour défendre nos vies dans cette société hostile. Nos casiers comptent une myriade de condamnations pour ce qu'ils appellent du « vol » car nous n'occuperons jamais un monde dans lequel l'argent dort et s'accumule, il est fait pour circuler entre les mains de tous et quand cela n'est pas le cas nous ne quémandons rien et mettons fin à cette injustice par des actes.




Faire face au chtar – l'art de la carcérologie




Lorsque l'on est mis ici en dehors du monde, ce qui nous maintient en vie – qui s'avère impératif et vital – c'est de garder un lien avec l'extérieur. Et il faut dire qu'avec la dense mémoire et l'expérience continue que l'on a avec le 

chtar

, nous avons fini par en développer une expertise et/ou une science que l'on peut nommer la chtarologie ou la carcérologie du point de vue gadjikano.




Derrière ces notions, je veux évoquer le fait que nos familles maîtrisent avec subtilité un ensemble de pratiques permettant de soutenir les 

chtardiers

. Illustrons notre propos par deux anecdotes contées par une amie. Elle m'a raconté qu'après ma comparution immédiate de début octobre une dizaine de militants présents se sont retrouvés déboussolés face à mon maintien en détention provisoire et elle m'a dit : « Heureusement qu'il y avait des Voyageurs présents pour expliquer à tout ce beau monde comment la suite de la vie avec toi en prison allait désormais se passer. » C'est en effet les Voyageurs qui ont expliqué avec pédagogie les procédures pour m'envoyer des mandats, faire les demandes de parloirs, etc. Nous disposons donc d'un capital culturel important en matière de compréhension de l'univers carcéral – une carcéraloculture pouvons-nous dire.




Elle m'a également raconté qu'en venant me voir au parloir dans la longue, voire interminable attente avec les autres familles, elle a vu un nombre impressionnant de Voyageuses avec leurs enfants. Je peux attester à travers mon vécu d'enfance que chez nous les visites au parloir sont systématiques jusqu'à la libération des nôtres. Quand quelqu'un se retrouve enfermé comme chez beaucoup d'autres gens, il y a un sentiment prégnant d'incomplétude dans la liberté chez les siens qui dure jusqu'au terme de la sentence.




Parmi les autres pratiques de soutien chez les Voyageurs dont nous n'avons nullement le monopole mais chez qui il y a une récurrence frappante, il y a une série d'usages épistolaires. Ainsi depuis le début de mon incarcération quand je reçois des lettres de Voyageuses, de ma mère, d'amies ou d'inconnues, voilà les gestes qui reviennent : lettres abondamment parfumées, présence de photos, enveloppes timbrées et feuilles jointes au courrier pour permettre la réponse, versets bibliques pour les croyantes… Ce sont des attentions qui ont des effets décisifs sur la tournure que peut prendre notre détention. Recevoir une lettre ici, ça vaut de l'or. Sa lecture procure un sentiment d'évasion et de liberté.




Conclusion 




Pour commencer ma conclusion, j'aimerais apporter une clarification. Il s'avère que je suis étudiant en Master 2 d'anthropologie sociale à l'École de Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales et que je travaille sur le traitement réservé aux personnes catégorisées comme « gens du voyage » par le système pénal. Pourtant, vous l'avez remarqué ma plume n'est pas celle d'un apprenti chercheur qui se cantonne à la « neutralité axiologique ». Cette dernière n'est pas possible, je rejette cette lâche et dangereuse posture pseudo scientifique. Ce que Fanon formule si bien dans 

Peau noire, masque blanc

 : « La situation que j'ai étudiée, on s'en est aperçu, n'est pas classique. L'objectivité scientifique m'était interdite, car l'aliéné, le névrosé, était mon frère, était ma sœur, était mon père. »




Ceci étant énoncé, je vais finir. Il y a peu de temps au tribunal judiciaire de Paris un minable « journaliste » du torchon 

Marianne

 m'a posé la question qui suit : « Comment pouvez-vous affirmer que l'institution judiciaire s'acharne contre vous par antitsiganisme ? » Cette institution, elle me fait payer cher le mépris que j'exprime avec force à son endroit. L'expression sévère que j'ai à son égard trouve sa source dans ma condition de gitan, sinto, manouche, yéniche et voyageur. Ce qui m'a conduit au 

chtar

 comme les miens avant moi c'est le fait de refuser de baisser la tête devant ceux qui veulent nous voir disparaître.




Dans 

Les misérables

, dont je viens d'achever la lecture, Hugo dit : « Ce n'est rien de mourir ; c'est affreux de ne pas vivre. » Eh bien nous, nous ne vivons pas à demi ni à moitié, et c'est ce que l'on veut nous faire payer. Mais qu'importe le prix, on ne se met pas à genoux, on reste toujours debout comme le disait le grand et vaillant Raymond Gurême.




Pour échapper au 

chtar

, deux chemins s'ouvrent à nous : se rendre prisonniers de la société dominante en se laissant incorporer par cette dernière ; ou bien la détruire méthodiquement, la briser en mille morceaux, la terrasser et en faire advenir une nouvelle avec tous nos frères et sœurs d'humanité où notamment la plaie des prisons aura disparu.




Ritchy Thibault

, le 25 octobre 2026, prison de Fleury-Mérogis










[

1

] 

Une soirée de soutien à Ritchy Thibault aura lieu vendredi 30 octobre à Paris, plus d'informations sur le compte Instagram 

@liberte.pour.ritchy
