title: Besê Hozat: Abdullah Öcalan’s status must be formalized for the process to move forward
content:
KCK Executive Council Co-Chair Besê Hozat spoke to Medya Haber TV about the current stage of the process, the women’s freedom struggle, practices in prisons, and regional developments.




This is part one of the interview. 




25 October marked the 34th anniversary of the martyrdom of comrade Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş), who played a pivotal role in the development of the Kurdish freedom struggle and particularly the women’s resistance movement. What impact did the change she pioneered have on Kurdish sociology?




To begin with, I commemorate all the martyrs of the revolution and the struggle for freedom represented by comrade Bêrîtan with respect, love, and gratitude. Comrade Bêrîtan holds a special place in our struggle. Her place and importance are particularly unique from the perspective of the women’s freedom struggle. Comrade Bêrîtan is a symbol of resistance and of the struggle for freedom. Comrade Bêrîtan’s stance, character, and her resistance – the noble stance she took against the impositions of collaborationists, traitors, and capitulationists, as well as against the line of surrender – have had a tremendous impact on organizing women and on the development of women’s self-defense. Her influence on Kurdish women, in particular, has been immense.




There is a deep-rooted culture of resistance in Kurdistan. Kurdish women play a decisive role in the development and formation of this culture. Comrade Bêrîtan was shaped by this culture. When she joined the PKK’s struggle, she surpassed herself both in terms of her character and the struggle she was waging. Today, comrade Bêrîtan represents a guiding principle for both the women’s freedom movement and the Kurdish freedom movement as a whole.




Comrade Bêrîtan played a very significant role in deepening this culture of resistance, internalizing it, and turning it into a guiding principle. Her personality, her stance, and the attitude of resistance she demonstrated against surrender, betrayal, and collaboration remain very powerful. And, of course, she did have a particularly profound impact on women and society in South Kurdistan. Especially in the face of impositions of surrender and betrayal, she fostered a resolute stance among Kurdish women. The most fitting tribute to our comrade Bêrîtan is to wage a strong struggle for freedom, to adopt a stance of freedom, and to stand strong against all forms of surrender, betrayal, and collaboration.




It is necessary to organize this stance of resistance, transform it into a force for struggle, and gradually turn it into a social system and way of life. This is the most appropriate and meaningful response in her memory. If we renew this stance and attitude for today, the most meaningful response would be the following: Kurdish women have to be able to transform this stance of resistance and this freedom-oriented line into a democratic, free Kurdish unity. This is of the utmost importance. Kurdish women must be able to take the lead in this democratic Kurdish unity. By establishing their own unity – and by securing their internal unity based on democratic and free principles – they must be able to lead the way toward a democratic Kurdish unity. This is an urgent necessity, both from today’s perspective and in light of the period we are currently experiencing.




This can only be achieved through organization, through a stance of self-defense, and through a spirit of resistance. In this sense, comrade Bêrîtan’s path of struggle and life serves as an example. It is inspiring and encouraging, both for Kurdish women and for women in general. She serves as a model in expanding organization and self-defense and in establishing a democratic women’s unity, a Kurdish women’s unity, and a democratic Kurdish unity.




In light of the legacy of resistance and struggle for freedom created by her, how would you assess the sociological reality of Kurdish women and their role in the freedom struggle within the Kurdish freedom movement today?




The Kurdish women’s freedom movement has already developed along this legacy. There is also the legacy of the prison resistance of Amed, which was pioneered by comrade Sara. Comrade Sara also played a leadership role for Kurdish women. This is the struggle of the Kurdish women’s freedom movement. And comrade Bêrîtan is also a continuation of this legacy. She is a continuation of this tradition of resistance. The comrades like Bêrîtan, Zîlan, Sema, Gulan, Viyan, and Şîlan are all continuations of this tradition and legacy. This has become part of our culture; it has become a tradition, a culture, a style, and a way of understanding. It has created a new mindset, and the struggle that has developed through it has brought about a very significant change and transformation in Kurdish sociology as well. The influence of this has been immense in the development of democratization among the Kurds, a culture of freedom, a culture of equality, and the mindset and understanding of living freely and equally alongside other peoples.




A significant sociological transformation is taking place. This democratization among the Kurds – this understanding of freedom, equality, and justice – is a level that has emerged through the struggle developing along this cultural line and this trajectory: the construction of a shared life with other peoples, cultures, and faiths – what we call the “paradigm of the democratic nation” – and the building of a system for living freely and democratically together.




Femicides and acts of violence across society have reached an alarming level. According to official numbers, on average, two to three women are murdered every day, and many more are attempted. The statistics from September show that 26 women and 6 children were murdered. Additionally, 10 women and 6 children died under suspicious circumstances. In a situation where violence against women has intensified to this extent, is the current women’s struggle sufficient? What can women do against violence against women, and how can they develop their self-defense strategies?




Physical violence against women is one dimension of violence against women. But one has to see that women are subjected to multifaceted, multidimensional violence. There are many dimensions to it, including psychological and economic violence. Today’s dominant culture itself is a sexist, male-dominated culture – a culture that has developed over the course of thousands of years. Life has been shaped accordingly, and gender roles have developed on this foundation. This is reflected in the media, in art and culture, in politics, and in the economy. We are dealing with a male-dominated and sexist culture that permeates every aspect of life to its very depths. This, in turn, manifests as violence against women in every sphere of life. There is a profound exploitation of women.




In response to this – especially throughout the past century – there has been a significant awakening among women, and a rising struggle is taking place worldwide. The gender contradiction is becoming the primary contradiction. And everywhere, a serious solidarity among women and a shared struggle are developing. Against the male-dominated system – the most concentrated and institutionalized form of which is the system of capitalist modernity and the nation-state system – the system of capitalist modernity is experiencing a deep crisis, alongside the struggle of women, the peoples, and all social dynamics in general.




The intensification of violence against women – to the point of physical massacres and the genocide of women – is also linked to the deep crisis and chaos experienced by the mindset of capitalist modernity and the patriarchal system. To keep the system afloat, it is escalating violence, expanding its scope, and deepening its impact. But, there is also a strong and genuine women’s struggle against this.




The system of capitalist modernity is a system of war and a system of violence. There is war all over the world. Also in this region, the war has intensified, and the war centered on Kurdistan has deepened. There is also a policy of genocide targeting the Kurds. This spans a century, or maybe even longer. If one pays attention, one can see that many massacres against women in Kurdistan are being carried out directly by the state. These are being carried out as part of the attacks stemming from an organized, planned policy of genocide. Violence of every kind is intensifying in this way. There is a growing awareness of this. As I said, a process of raising consciousness, building resolve, and organizing is developing among women. Solidarity is also growing, as are collective actions and the struggle itself. However, this still remains insufficient.




It is important to strengthen this, and in order to make it stronger, it is necessary that we organize. Women must strengthen their organization everywhere, in every sphere of life. They must strengthen their self-defense. Self-defense comes through organization. The more you organize, the more that organization becomes your self-defense. It also becomes your collective strength in the struggle. When a collective struggle, a strong fighting force, and an organized stance emerge, the patriarchal system – and the manifestations of male violence that permeate society and even the family – naturally recede and weaken in the face of organized struggle. If this organized struggle and self-defense continue to grow, it will accelerate the collapse of the patriarchal system. It will also gradually eliminate this sexist culture. Women’s education, organization, self-defense, and collective struggle push back against the patriarchal system and culture and, over time, ensure their eventual eradication.




Two years have passed since the process began on October 22. As the freedom movement, you have taken significant steps. Turkish state officials have also made statements to a certain extent. Parliament has become active, and a commission has been formed. A law has also been passed. However, it appears there is a stalemate in the process. Where is the process at the moment?




Over the past two years, the Kurdish freedom movement has taken some historic steps. We have halted the armed struggle against Turkey, and many other steps followed. All guerrilla forces within Turkey’s borders have been withdrawn. Units in the cities have been withdrawn. Tunnels and caves near the border and some in more remote areas have been evacuated to diminish the risk of conflict. These are very concrete examples that demonstrate our sincerity, determination, and stance regarding this process. And, like I said, they are truly historic steps.




In contrast, there has been no serious movement on the part of the state. You asked if there is a stalemate. It might not be appropriate to put it exactly that way. But there is indeed a state of stagnation. There is a state of pause and stagnation. You could call it a deadlock, but there is a state of paralysis. The reason for this lies in the attitude of the state and the government. It is a state of paralysis on that front. They are not taking any steps. They are not taking steps toward democratization. The political and legal groundwork is not being laid. First and foremost, there is the situation of our leader. The isolation has not yet been lifted. Our leader is not enabled to steer this process. And that was our fundamental condition at the PKK dissolution congress. We ended the armed struggle, but for this to be put into practice – for all the decisions made at the congress to be implemented – Rêber Apo [Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan] needed to be enabled to freely steer this process. Democratic, political, and legal steps needed to be taken. The groundwork needed to be laid for waging a democratic political struggle. To achieve this, the state needed to implement very serious legal reforms. But there has been no progress on this front. Consequently, there is a state of stagnation, a freeze caused by the state. We can put it that way.




Most recently, there was a statement of your movement, announcing that you also emptied your remaining positions in the area of Metîna. After that, reports appeared in the Turkish press claiming that the tunnels and caves in Xakurkê, Xinêre and Garê had also been evacuated, and that weapons had been surrendered. Within the Kurdish community, a perception has formed that the state is using pressure to conceal what it itself should be doing. What is the current situation?




All of this is part of a strategy of special warfare. Since the state has not changed its mindset or policy, it is not taking any steps on this issue; instead, it is playing for time and buying time by creating agendas and shaping different perceptions. If they were serious and took steps – if the groundwork were laid politically and legally, starting with the freedom of Rêber Apo, and if an environment for democratic politics were created and that opportunity were granted – then, forget about Metîna, Xakurkê, and Xinêre – in all areas, the guerrillas would lay down their arms, come down from the mountains, and join democratic politics in an organized manner. That issue would be resolved, rather than focusing on this or that specific area. If the state were to take a serious step, we would naturally enter such a process as a whole. But it is not taking any steps. Its insistence on the current stance and policy of intransigence is leading to the emergence of these kinds of special war, made-up agendas. There are no concrete steps being taken.




Every day a different area is being debated, and attempts are being made to create a different perception. These are special war agendas. One must not give them any credence. Everyone needs to turn their attention to the state. Is it taking a step, or isn’t it? As I pointed out, there is currently a state of stagnation and paralysis. If the state takes a step, nothing will remain. That process will unfold on its own.




In an article he wrote a few days ago, Mehmet Uçum stated that even if Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan were given a role, there would be no change in his legal status. This gave the impression that they were approaching him as a tool to dismantle the freedom movement. How do you assess this evaluation?




Mehmet Uçum is a representative within the state of the tendency that insists on intransigence, on war policies, and on denial. He is a full-fledged agent of special warfare. There is a significant circle in Turkey that feeds off war and intransigence, and there are serious factions within the state. Mehmet Uçum acts as one of their representatives and spokespersons. It is appropriate to put it that way.




Rêber Apo is the leader of this people; he embodies the will of this people. Rêber Apo’s freedom is synonymous with, and inextricably linked to, the democratic resolution of the Kurdish issue. It is clear and unequivocal that the guerrillas will not take a single step forward unless Rêber Apo is freed, his status is formalized, and he is able to freely lead this process. Because this is the litmus test. The approach to our leader is the approach to the Kurds. However, they approach our leader, that is how they approach the Kurdish issue. If there is no progress regarding our leader’s freedom and the conditions for freedom, if his status has not been formalized, and if an official dialogue has not been established – this means that this state will approach the Kurdish issue in the same way. It will continue its policy of non-resolution and denial. That is what it means. From that perspective, everyone’s eyes and attention are, and should be, focused on Rêber Apo’s situation.




Mehmet Uçum’s remarks of this kind directed at Rêber Apo reveal his approach to the Kurds and his stance on the Kurdish issue. They reveal just how frivolous this approach is. And in a way, Mehmet Uçum is confirming and validating those who make such assessments. If this is the case, of course, this process will not develop. This process will not move forward. For this process to move forward and proceed successfully, the status of our leader must be formalized. Rêber Apo must be able to freely lead this process. Otherwise, it is not possible for this process to proceed successfully.




There are still quite a number of comrades who have been in prison for over 30 years. They are not being released even though their sentences have expired. Among them are some who are seriously ill. Reports indicate that the conditions in prisons remain very harsh.




The fact that this process continues in this manner – including the dimension of the prison situation – stems from the mindset we discussed a moment ago, exemplified by figures like Mehmet Uçum. Prisons are the most concrete expression of this mindset and worldview – one that insists on the absence of a solution, that insists on a kind of war, that insists on hostility toward Kurds, and that perpetuates this policy.




According to Turkish law, according to state law, they have served their sentence. Their 30 years are up. Yet, despite this, their sentence is being extended, and they are being held inside. They are seriously ill. Some have cancer, and some have heart problems, and the like. Despite all this, they are being held inside, and their sentences are being extended. A law of hostility is being enforced. This is unprecedented. They are not even applying their own laws. They are trampling on their own laws. It is unlawful, unethical, and politically irresponsible. And when I say “politics,” I am referring to the ethics of politics. Beyond all of this, an inhumane “law of hostility,” a “law of war,” is being enforced. One of the most striking and obvious places where this law of hostility and war is applied is, in fact, the prisons. It’s as if they’re taking revenge, trying to break one’s will. They have served 30 years, 32 years. They have devoted their entire lives to the cause of freedom, to the freedom of their people; yet they’re forcing them to repent, trying to break their will, trying to make them surrender. There is only one way to describe this: it is hostility. It is hostility toward the Kurds. It is a persistence in hostility toward the Kurds. It is a persistence in war. There is no other meaning to it. Over the course of two years, so many steps have been taken. Such a strong will has been demonstrated in pursuing democratic politics, and the armed struggle against Turkey has been halted; yet, despite this, a law of hostility is at work in prison – a law of war is at work.




Obviously, this generates immense anger. It fosters a profound lack of belief and trust both towards this process and toward the state and deepens anxieties. Consequently, the process is failing to gain societal traction. There are serious concerns and anxieties among the Kurdish people regarding this issue. They look at the situation of Rêber Apo; there is no change. They look at the prisons; a regime of outright oppression and hostility is in full force there. How can this possibly foster trust in society? How can it inspire faith in this process? So of course, the situation in the prisons is another factor that negatively impacts the process in a major way.

title: HPG and YJA-Star guerrillas: Bêrîtan embodies the truth of struggle
content:
People's Defence Forces (HPG) and Free Women's Units (YJA-Star) guerrillas commemorated commander Bêrîtan Hêvî (Gülnaz Karataş) on the anniversary of her martyrdom.




YJA-Star guerrilla Agirî Efrîn spoke about Bêrîtan Hêvî's martyrdom, saying: “I was inspired by comrade Bêrîtan, and it was on this basis that I joined the movement. Today marks the 34th anniversary of her martyrdom. Comrade Bêrîtan was a commander of the women's army, and Abdullah Öcalan developed the women's military organisation following her martyrdom. Her personality is like a light for us women. I had the opportunity to visit the Martyr Bêrîtan Academy myself, which was a great privilege. As a woman, comrade Bêrîtan showed me the right path. She understood Abdullah Öcalan and put his ideas into practice, and for this we owe her a great deal.







 







Comrade Bêrîtan made history through her resistance against the occupiers. No one would knowingly throw themselves off a cliff, but comrade Bêrîtan did so for a cause. In a short period of time, she had embraced and embodied the idea of the free woman. The position of women in society and within the party is different, and we can see this very clearly. The women's army belongs to all women. Women from every nation have a place in our military organisation. Every woman who recognises the importance of her freedom joins the ranks of the women's army. Comrade Bêrîtan is a symbol of the free woman, and this is also reflected in her struggle.




As women, we believe that we will follow comrade Bêrîtan's path and protect women against all attacks by the system. Comrade Bêrîtan is a symbol of resistance against the system of capitalist modernity, and she sacrificed her life for this cause. Our aim is to uphold the path she established.




Dozens of women sacrificed their lives during the development of the women's military organisation. Comrades Zîlan and Bêrîtan are among the women who have become symbols of the struggle for women's freedom. Patriotism and love for one's homeland were also embodied in comrade Bêrîtan. We renew our pledge to continue her struggle and intensify the struggle for the freedom of women and society.”




‘Bêrîtan represents the Kurdish people's struggle for national unity’




HPG guerrilla Mordem Amed commemorated all martyrs through the memory of Bêrîtan and said: “Comrade Bêrîtan was a woman with a purpose and a quest. Through her action and the message she conveyed, she became a historical figure. She wanted to write a novel about Abdullah Öcalan, which also reflects the depth of her understanding. Historical figures make history through their actions, and the meaning of their stance becomes clearer with the passage of time.







 







Comrade Bêrîtan embodies the true path of patriotism and national consciousness. She stood against all forms of reactionary forces and defended her homeland and her struggle. We can see this in both her life and her action. The attacks by the Turkish state, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the United States are aimed at destroying the Kurds. The year 1992 was extremely important for the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), with many significant developments taking place. Comrades like Bêrîtan understood this period correctly and acted accordingly. The resistance of that time ensured that the Kurdish people's struggle and values would endure.




As fighters following comrade Bêrîtan's path, it is extremely important for us to understand the current period correctly and act accordingly. The process we are going through today is also a historic one in which we must fulfil our role. All Kurdish forces must unite. The KDP's position on this issue is not right. This must change, and Kurdish unity must be built. As fighters following comrade Bêrîtan's path, we must defend Kurdish unity and continue the struggle.




Through comrade Bêrîtan's martyrdom, thousands of Bêrîtans emerged. Thousands of comrades made following her path the goal of their struggle. Her stance also became a symbol of the free and militant woman. It serves as a guide to struggle for all women. For male comrades, Bêrîtan's stance also represents the spirit of leadership.”




‘Comrade Bêrîtan's dreams will come true’




Free Women's Units (YJA-Star) guerrilla Arjîn Xebat said that martyr Bêrîtan represented the path of freedom and the militant woman, adding that thousands of women had continued the struggle in her footsteps.







 







Arjîn Xebat said that although they had never met Bêrîtan personally, her stance had profoundly influenced them. Arjîn Xebat also said, “Comrade Bêrîtan's stance brought women's hidden history to light and marked the beginning of the women's revolution. What comrade Bêrîtan experienced revealed the truth of her time. Her spirit can be felt throughout the mountains of Kurdistan. I feel this deeply myself.




Comrade Bêrîtan's personality gives me strength in every respect. As women, we are very fortunate to have pioneers like her. Building and developing a new life was comrade Bêrîtan's aspiration, and our responsibility as women is to nurture this spirit in all women. Martyr Bêrîtan dreamed of meeting Abdullah Öcalan and writing a novel about him. Today, however, there are thousands of comrades who can fulfil her dreams. Fulfilling comrade Bêrîtan's dreams will always be one of our fundamental aspirations, and we will certainly make them a reality.”

author: Λουκάς Σταμέλλος
title: Αίγυπτος: Στο εδώλιο η ανεξάρτητη δημοσιογραφία διά της… «αδειοδότησης»
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης: 

Αίγυπτος: Στο εδώλιο η ανεξάρτητη δημοσιογραφία διά της… «αδειοδότησης»




Σήμερα, 27 Οκτωβρίου 2026, πρόκειται να ξεκινήσει στο Κάιρο η δίκη της 

Λίνα Ατάλα

 (Lina Atallah), συνιδρύτριας και διευθύντριας σύνταξης του ανεξάρτητου αιγυπτιακού δημοσιογραφικού μέσου 

Μάντα Μασρ (Mada Masr)

, 

με την κατηγορία ότι ίδρυσε, διαχειρίζεται και λειτουργεί ενημερωτική ιστοσελίδα χωρίς άδεια

 από τις αρχές.




Η παραπομπή σε δίκη ανακοινώθηκε στις 22 Οκτωβρίου, μόλις μία ημέρα μετά την πολύωρη ανάκρισή της από την Ανώτατη Εισαγγελία Κρατικής Ασφάλειας της Αιγύπτου. Η Ατάλα ανακρίθηκε για περισσότερο από έξι ώρες και αφέθηκε ελεύθερη με εγγύηση 100.000 αιγυπτιακών λιρών (περίπου 1.590€). Αρχικά αντιμετώπιζε και την κατηγορία της 

διασποράς ψευδών ειδήσεων με σκοπό τη διατάραξη της δημόσιας τάξης

, η οποία δεν συμπεριλήφθηκε τελικά στο παραπεμπτικό της δίκης.




Η υπόθεση ενδέχεται να έχει σοβαρές συνέπειες για την ίδια την ύπαρξη του μέσου. Ο 

αιγυπτιακός νόμος 180/2018

 προβλέπει για την παράβαση της υποχρέωσης αδειοδότησης πρόστιμο από ένα έως τρία εκατομμύρια αιγυπτιακές λίρες (περίπου από 15.900€ έως 47.700€). Το άρθρο 105 προβλέπει επίσης, σε περίπτωση καταδίκης, κλείσιμο της ιστοσελίδας και κατάσχεση του εξοπλισμού του μέσου.




Πρόκειται για την έκτη ποινική υπόθεση κατά του Μάντα Μασρ και των δημοσιογράφων του 

μέσα σε έξι χρόνια

.




Αφορμή της δίωξης τα ρεπορτάζ για τις αιγυπτιακές φυλακές




Η τελευταία δίωξη ακολούθησε τη δημοσίευση 

ερευνών του Μάντα Μασρ σχετικά με τις συνθήκες κράτησης και τις κινητοποιήσεις κρατουμένων στις αιγυπτιακές φυλακές

.




Σε 

ρεπορτάζ της 14ης Οκτωβρίου

, το μέσο παρουσίασε καταγγελίες δικηγόρων και συγγενών κρατουμένων για κινητοποιήσεις σε διάφορες φυλακές, έπειτα από την αναβολή εφαρμογής, για ένα ολόκληρο έτος, του νέου Κώδικα Ποινικής Δικονομίας που προβλέπει μείωση στα όρια της προσωρινής κράτησης. Σημειωτέο ότι οι αιγυπτιακές αρχές δεν τηρούν ούτε τα όρια του σήμερα ισχύοντος Κώδικα, ωστόσο η κυβέρνηση του δικτάτορα Σίσι είχε παρουσιάσει τη μεταρρύθμιση ως «εγγύηση για τα δικαιώματα των κρατουμένων».




Σύμφωνα με τις μαρτυρίες που συγκέντρωσε το μέσο, κρατούμενοι πραγματοποίησαν απεργίες πείνας και άλλες διαμαρτυρίες, ενώ καταγγέλθηκαν βίαιες επεμβάσεις των δυνάμεων ασφαλείας και τιμωρητικές μεταγωγές σε απομακρυσμένες φυλακές. Το αιγυπτιακό υπουργείο Εσωτερικών ισχυρίστηκε ότι όλα είναι ψέματα.




Το συγκεκριμένο δημοσίευμα περιλαμβανόταν στον φάκελο που χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην ανάκριση της Ατάλα, μαζί με έγγραφα για το καθεστώς αδειοδότησης του Μάντα Μασρ, σύμφωνα με τους δικηγόρους του μέσου.




Είχε προηγηθεί, τον Αύγουστο του 2025, ακόμη μία 

ποινική έρευνα

 μετά από ρεπορτάζ για καταγγελίες κακομεταχείρισης κρατουμένων στη φυλακή 

Μπαντρ

 

3

. Τότε η Ατάλα ανακρίθηκε για τις δημοσιογραφικές πηγές και τη μεθοδολογία της έρευνας και αφέθηκε ελεύθερη με εγγύηση 30.000 λιρών (περίπου 480€).




Μια δεκαετία αποκλεισμών και διώξεων




Το Μάντα Μασρ ιδρύθηκε το 2013 από ομάδα Αιγύπτιων δημοσιογράφων και δημοσιεύει ανεξάρτητη ειδησεογραφία και έρευνες στα αραβικά και στα αγγλικά.




Από τον Μάιο του 2017 η ιστοσελίδα του παραμένει αποκλεισμένη από τους παρόχους διαδικτύου στην Αίγυπτο, στο πλαίσιο ευρύτερων αποκλεισμών εκατοντάδων ενημερωτικών και άλλων ιστοσελίδων.




Τον Νοέμβριο του 2019, αστυνομικοί με πολιτικά 

εισέβαλαν στα γραφεία του μέσου

, κατέσχεσαν ηλεκτρονικές συσκευές και κράτησαν το προσωπικό επί ώρες. Τρεις δημοσιογράφοι, μεταξύ των οποίων η Ατάλα, προσήχθησαν και αργότερα αφέθηκαν ελεύθεροι. Την προηγούμενη ημέρα είχε συλληφθεί ο συντάκτης Σάντι Ζαλάτ (Shady Zalat). Η επιχείρηση ακολούθησε δημοσίευμα σχετικά με τον Μαχμούντ Αλ-Σίσι, γιο του Αιγύπτιου προέδρου, και τη θέση του 

στις υπηρεσίες πληροφοριών

.




Τον Μάιο του 2020 η Ατάλα 

συνελήφθη έξω από τις φυλακές Tora

, ενώ πραγματοποιούσε συνέντευξη με τη Λάιλα Σουέιφ (Laila Soueif), μητέρα του τότε κρατούμενου ακτιβιστή Αλάα Αμπντέλ Φατάχ (Alaa Abdel Fattah). Αφέθηκε ελεύθερη την ίδια ημέρα με εγγύηση.




Το 2022 τέσσερις δημοσιογράφοι του Μάντα Μασρ, συμπεριλαμβανομένης της Ατάλα, ανακρίθηκαν μετά από δημοσίευμα με καταγγελίες οικονομικών ατασθαλιών στο Κόμμα του Μέλλοντος του Έθνους (Mostaqbal Watan) το οποίο 

δημιουργήθηκε από την Υπηρεσία Πληροφοριών του αιγυπτιακού στρατού για να υποστηρίζει τον δικτάτορα Σίσι

. Τρεις από τους δημοσιογράφους 

παραπέμφθηκαν σε δίκη τον Μάρτιο του 2023

.




Τον Οκτώβριο του 2023 το Ανώτατο Συμβούλιο Ρύθμισης των ΜΜΕ ανακοίνωσε νέο εξάμηνο αποκλεισμό της ιστοσελίδας, με αφορμή δημοσίευμα για ενδεχόμενη μετακίνηση Παλαιστινίων από τη Γάζα προς το Σινά. Τον Φεβρουάριο του 2024 η Attalah 

ανακρίθηκε εκ νέου

, μετά και από έρευνα σχετικά με επιχειρηματικά συμφέροντα που συνδέονταν 

με τη διέλευση ανθρώπων και αγαθών από το πέρασμα της Ράφα

.




Τον Μάρτιο του 2024 

συνελήφθη επίσης

 η δημοσιογράφος Ράνα Μαμντούχ (Rana Mamdouh), ενώ ταξίδευε για δημοσιογραφική αποστολή στην περιοχή Ρας Ελ-Χέκμα όπου είναι σε εξέλιξη μεγάλα επιχειρηματικά σχέδια τουριστικοποίησης («Αιγυπτιακής Ριβιέρας») με κεφάλαια από τα Ηνωμένα Αραβικά Εμιράτα.




Η άδεια λειτουργίας που δεν χορηγείται




Το Μάντα Μασρ επιχειρεί να αποκτήσει την άδεια λειτουργίας που έχει επιβάλει ο δικτάτορας Σίσι από το 2018. Υπέβαλε αρχική αίτηση στις 31 Οκτωβρίου εκείνου του έτους, καταβάλλοντας το σχετικό τέλος των 50.000 λιρών (περίπου 795€), και επανήλθε μετά την έκδοση του κανονιστικού πλαισίου το 2020.




Ωστόσο, το Μάντα Μασρ δεν ενημερώθηκε ποτέ επισήμως ότι η αίτησή του απορρίφθηκε. Έμαθε ότι υπήρχε απορριπτική απόφαση μόλις το 2022, κατά τη διάρκεια άλλης εισαγγελικής διερεύνησης, και προσέφυγε κατά της απόρριψης.




Το 2023 το Διοικητικό Δικαστήριο απέρριψε την προσφυγή του μέσου κατά της απόρριψης της αρχικής αίτησης. Όμως, σύμφωνα με τη νομική εκπροσώπηση του Μάντα Μασρ, δεν έχει δοθεί απάντηση ως τώρα στην εκ νέου υποβολή δικαιολογητικών που πραγματοποιήθηκε τον Ιούνιο του 2023.




Όπως επισημαίνει το επίσης ανεξάρτητο Al Manassa

, η μέθοδος καταστολής των ΜΜΕ από την δικτατορική κυβέρνηση του Σίσι βασίζεται σ’ αυτόν τον φαύλο κύκλο: ένα μέσο μπορεί να ζητά επί χρόνια άδεια λειτουργίας, να μη λαμβάνει οριστική απάντηση και να διώκεται ποινικά επειδή συνεχίζει να δημοσιεύει χωρίς την άδεια αυτή.




Νέες διώξεις και συλλήψεις ανεξάρτητων δημοσιογράφων




Η υπόθεση του Μάντα Μασρ εξελίσσεται παράλληλα με νέες διώξεις άλλων δημοσιογραφικών μέσων.




Στις 28 και 29 Σεπτεμβρίου 2026, οι αιγυπτιακές αρχές 

συνέλαβαν και τους έξι δημοσιογράφους της ανεξάρτητης πλατφόρμας Matsada2sh

 («Μην το πιστεύεις»), η οποία ειδικεύεται στη διασταύρωση πληροφοριών και επαλήθευση ισχυρισμών (fact-checking).




Για περίπου πέντε ημέρες, σύμφωνα με οργανώσεις ανθρωπίνων δικαιωμάτων, οι οικογένειες και οι δικηγόροι τους δεν είχαν πρόσβαση στους κρατουμένους ούτε ενημέρωση για τον τόπο κράτησής τους.




Οι δημοσιογράφοι κατηγορούνται, μεταξύ άλλων, 

για συμμετοχή και χρηματοδότηση τρομοκρατικής οργάνωσης

 και 

διασπορά ψευδών ειδήσεων

. Οι ίδιοι αρνούνται τις κατηγορίες και έχουν καταγγείλει βασανιστήρια και εξαναγκασμό σε ομολογίες, ενώ το υπουργείο Εσωτερικών της Αιγύπτου ισχυρίζεται και πάλι ότι είναι όλα ψέματα.




Στις 13 Οκτωβρίου η 

προσωρινή κράτησή τους παρατάθηκε για ακόμη 15 ημέρες

. Σήμερα, 27 Οκτωβρίου έχει προγραμματιστεί εκ νέου εξέταση της παράτασης κράτησής τους.




Στις 5 Οκτωβρίου ανακρίθηκε επίσης η δημοσιογράφος Ράσα Αζάμπ (Rasha Azab) για ανάρτηση στα κοινωνικά δίκτυα που ασκούσε κριτική στο υπουργείο Εσωτερικών. Αφέθηκε ελεύθερη με εγγύηση 10.000 λιρών (περίπου 160€).




Όπως 

σημειώνει η Επιτροπή Προστασίας Δημοσιογράφων (CPJ)

, αυτή η πληθώρα διώξεων συνθέτουν την εικόνα μιας περιόδου έντονης πίεσης προς τα εναπομείναντα ανεξάρτητα μέσα της Αιγύπτου.




Αντιδράσεις και παρέμβαση της Ένωσης Δημοσιογράφων




Η παραπομπή της Attalah προκάλεσε αντιδράσεις στην Αίγυπτο και διεθνώς.




Στις 23 Οκτωβρίου, 

119 οργανώσεις ανθρωπίνων δικαιωμάτων και δημοσιογραφικοί φορείς

 συνυπέγραψαν έκκληση για τερματισμό της δίωξης και προστασία της ανεξάρτητης δημοσιογραφίας.




Στις 24 Οκτωβρίου πραγματοποιήθηκε συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στην Ένωση Δημοσιογράφων της Αιγύπτου.




Στις 26 Οκτωβρίου ο πρόεδρος της Ένωσης, Χάλεντ ελ-Μπάλσι (Khaled El-Balshy), 

κατέθεσε επίσημο υπόμνημα

 στο Ανώτατο Συμβούλιο Ρύθμισης των ΜΜΕ, επισημαίνοντας τις παραλείψεις της διοίκησης στη διαδικασία αδειοδότησης του Μάντα Μασρ.




Η Ένωση ζητά να εξετάζονται οι σχετικές διοικητικές διαφορές από τη διοικητική Δικαιοσύνη, να τερματιστούν οι ποινικές διώξεις για ζητήματα αδειοδότησης και να θεσπιστούν διαφανείς και ισότιμοι κανόνες λειτουργίας των ενημερωτικών ιστοσελίδων.




Αυτό το είδος της περιστολής της ελευθερίας του Τύπου δεν αφορά αποκλειστικά το Μάντα Μασρ. Η 

αιγυπτιακή Ένωση για την Ελευθερία της Σκέψης και της Έκφρασης (AFTE)

 έχει καταγράψει ανάλογα προβλήματα αδειοδότησης για ανεξάρτητα μέσα, όπως τα Al Manassa, Feker Tany και Masr 360.




Η Αίγυπτος βρίσκεται στην 

169η θέση μεταξύ 180 χωρών στον Δείκτη Ελευθερίας του Τύπου 2026

 των Δημοσιογράφων Χωρίς Σύνορα.




Στα δικά μας: ανησυχητικές αναλογίες




Η περίπτωση του Μάντα Μασρ αναδεικνύει ευρύτερα ερωτήματα για τα συστήματα κρατικής αδειοδότησης και πιστοποίησης των μέσων ενημέρωσης.




Στην Ελλάδα, με τον 

νόμο 5005/2022

 της κυβέρνησης Μητσοτάκη, θεσπίστηκαν το Μητρώο Έντυπου Τύπου (ΜΕΤ) και το Μητρώο Ηλεκτρονικού Τύπου (ΜΗΤ), τα οποία τηρούνται στη Γενική Γραμματεία Επικοινωνίας και Ενημέρωσης, υπό την Προεδρία της Κυβέρνησης.




Η

 

εγγραφή στο ελληνικό Μητρώο Ηλεκτρονικού Τύπου δεν αποτελεί

 

μέχρι στιγμής

 

προϋπόθεση νόμιμης λειτουργίας μιας ενημερωτικής ιστοσελίδας

. Δεν προβλέπεται ποινική δίωξη επειδή ένα δημοσιογραφικό μέσο λειτουργεί εκτός του μητρώου.




Ωστόσο, η εγγραφή συνδέεται άμεσα με την οικονομική του λειτουργία. Τα άρθρα 22 και 23 του νόμου αποκλείουν τα μη πιστοποιημένα μέσα από την κρατική διαφήμιση και τα σχετικά προγράμματα κρατικής ενίσχυσης.




Παράλληλα, η πιστοποίηση εξαρτάται από σειρά οργανωτικών και εργασιακών προϋποθέσεων.




Σύμφωνα με το 

άρθρο 10

, ακόμη και μια μικρή επιχείρηση ηλεκτρονικού Τύπου, με ετήσιο κύκλο εργασιών κάτω από 80.000 ευρώ, πρέπει να απασχολεί τουλάχιστον έναν δημοσιογράφο και έναν επιπλέον εργαζόμενο. Προβλέπονται επίσης απαιτήσεις για οργανωμένο γραφείο, διακριτές θέσεις διεύθυνσης και άλλα στοιχεία της λειτουργίας της.




Οι προϋποθέσεις αυτές δημιουργούν εμπόδια για μικρά ανεξάρτητα, συλλογικά ή εθελοντικά δημοσιογραφικά εγχειρήματα, ακόμη και όταν αυτά παράγουν σημαντικό πρωτογενές δημοσιογραφικό έργο αξιοποιώντας στο έπακρο τις δυνατότητες των ψηφιακών τεχνολογιών.




Ο νόμος προβλέπει ακόμη 

διοικητικούς και επιτόπιους ελέγχους

, καθώς και δυνατότητα διαγραφής από το μητρώο εφόσον δεν πληρούνται οι απαιτήσεις πιστοποίησης, με περιορισμούς στην επανεγγραφή.




Η διαφάνεια της ιδιοκτησίας, η τήρηση της εργατικής νομοθεσίας και ο έλεγχος των δημόσιων χρηματοδοτήσεων είναι ασφαλώς ζητήματα για τα οποία οι ίδιοι οι δημοσιογράφοι πρέπει να απαιτούν ρυθμιστικό πλαίσιο, ειδικά σε μια χώρα όπως η δική μας, στην οποία τα περισσότερα ΜΜΕ ανήκουν σε λίγες επιχειρηματικές οικογένειες ή ομίλους.




Το ζήτημα είναι πώς γίνεται αυτή ρύθμιση και πώς εξασφαλίζεται ότι οι σχετικοί μηχανισμοί δεν θα χρησιμοποιηθούν επιλεκτικά ή ως μέσο πολιτικής και οικονομικής πίεσης, ιδίως μέσα στο κλίμα που διαμορφώνει η κυβέρνηση με δηλώσεις του κυβερνητικού εκπροσώπου, Παύλου Μαρινάκη, περί 

«ταυτοποίησης» χρηστών

 και 

απειλές του ίδιου εναντίον δημοσιογράφων

.




Στην 

έκθεση Media Capture Monitoring Report: Greece 2026

, το International Press Institute και το Media and Journalism Research Center επισημαίνουν ότι τα ελληνικά μητρώα ΜΜΕ θα έπρεπε να υπάγονται στην εποπτεία ανεξάρτητου φορέα. Η έκθεση αναδεικνύει επίσης την απουσία επαρκώς καθορισμένων, ανεξάρτητα εποπτευόμενων κριτηρίων για την κατανομή της κρατικής διαφήμισης, παρά τις σχετικές απαιτήσεις του 

Ευρωπαϊκού Κανονισμού για την Ελευθερία των ΜΜΕ (EMFA)

.




Το άρθρο 14 του ελληνικού Συντάγματος απαγορεύει τη λογοκρισία και τα άλλα προληπτικά μέτρα, ενώ το ευρωπαϊκό δίκαιο προβλέπει πρόσθετες εγγυήσεις για την ελευθερία των ΜΜΕ.




Η αιγυπτιακή εμπειρία δείχνει, ωστόσο, μια συγκεκριμένη «θεσμική» διαδρομή: 

η κρατική καταγραφή μετατρέπεται σε υποχρέωση προηγούμενης έγκρισης, η απουσία αυτής της έγκρισης ποινικοποιείται

 

και, τέλος,

 

η

 

κυβέρνηση

 

αποκτά τη δυνατότητα να καθορίζει ποιος μπορεί να ασκεί δημοσιογραφία.




Ακόμη και χωρίς ποινικές απαγορεύσεις, η σύνδεση της κρατικής πιστοποίησης με κρίσιμους οικονομικούς πόρους δημιουργεί διαφορετικού τύπου εξαρτήσεις, ιδιαίτερα για μικρά μέσα με περιορισμένη χρηματοδότηση.




Η υπόθεση του Μάντα Μασρ είναι χαρακτηριστική. Ιδίως με τις περιθωριακές «διεθνείς συμμαχίες» που επιλέγει η παρούσα ελληνική κυβέρνηση.




Αίγυπτος: Στο εδώλιο η ανεξάρτητη δημοσιογραφία διά της… «αδειοδότησης»

author: TGEU
title: TGEU welcomes the Trans Leaders Academy 2026-27 cohort
content:
We are delighted to introduce the inspiring 

Trans Leaders Academy

 cohort 2026–27. Over the coming year, the 16 leaders will take part in virtual and in-person trainings and peer exchange sessions.




To further strengthen their practice, they will also have the opportunity to join the Spring 

Leadership Kitchen Series

,

 a six-month coaching space made possible through a partnership between TGEU and 

Spring

. Through the coaching, they will have space to reflect, share and grow in leadership while connecting with a wider community of global change-makers from diverse social and ecological justice movements.




We are excited to welcome this group and to witness their leadership journeys as they reflect, share and grow in community.




Meet the Trans Leaders Academy 2026–2027 cohort:













Alia Lehner (she/her)

 was born and raised in Austria. She is the State Secretary and Queer Representative of the Young Generation (JG) Upper Austria, and the State Secretary and Transgender Spokesperson of the SoHo Upper Austria.

Change-making  leadership vision:

To build an inclusive, courageous, and intersectional movement where trans people are empowered to lead, shape political decisions, and create lasting social change.



















Beatriz Carmo Flores (she/her)

 is an activist and community organiser based in Portugal. As a Coordinator at GRIT, the trans reflection and intervention group of ILGA Portugal, she supports and strengthens community organising, from peer-support spaces to public advocacy.

Change-making vision:

To build collective power through community care, so that trans communities can lead the change for human rights while impacting positively each other’s lives and thrive together.



















Evi Gümüssoy (they/them)

 is from Turkey and works on the TIN* & Refugees team at the TransInterQueer (TrIQ) organisation in Berlin. 

Change-making leadership vision:

To transform these shared lived experiences into collective power by building community-rooted support networks that protect our sustainability, mental well-being, and joy.



















Jononi Zulaikho (she/her)

 is a poet and artist actively contributing to Colored Qollective through translation and creating and holding space for trans and queer communities.

Change-making leadership vision:

To hear and see one another, speak openly about our differences and the privileges that shape our experiences, while remembering that, despite our differences, we remain connected in different ways and are part of a larger whole.



















Mak Maslać (he/him)

 is a writer, editor and cultural worker based in Zagreb, Croatia. He is the editor-in-chief of VoxFeminae, a queer feminist online magazine focused on culture and societal phenomena, where he also writes on queer and feminist topics, literature and popular culture.

Change-making leadership vision:

To create and protect spaces for more open, critical and nuanced conversations about culture, queerness, sexuality and BDSM through writing, publishing and community work.



















Maui Angela Miranda

 

(she/her)

 is a writer, editor and cultural worker based in Zagreb, Croatia. He is the editor-in-chief of VoxFeminae, a queer feminist online magazine focused on culture and societal phenomena, where he also writes on queer and feminist topics, literature and popular culture.

Change-making leadership vision:

To create sustainable systems of care that center racialized trans migrants. I aim to cultivate “care-full” spaces where trans individuals can heal from systemic racism while building collective resilience and joy.



















Miia Kovanen (she/her)

 is from Tampere, Finland. In this project, she represents Transfeminiinit Ry / Transfeminines NGO. She works in the organisation under the title of a volunteer social assistant. She is also a member of the feminist organisation Naisasialiitto Unioni / The Finnish Women’s Association Unioni.

Change-making leadership vision:

To take on this new role given to her. Indeed, she has only been in the sphere of advocacy for a relatively short while. Her journey has necessitated rapid personal development, which she aims to continue in these new responsibilities.

Natsumi Hernandez

 

(she/her)

 is a transgender activist, model, runway coach, and personal stylist originally from Nicaragua. Since 2014, she has worked in human rights and transgender advocacy, collaborating with organisations such as USAID and local initiatives supporting vulnerable members of the LGBTIQ+ community.

Change-making leadership:

Creating safe spaces for her community, for her trans siblinx who are undocumented, experiencing addiction, or facing mental health challenges.



















Pie Formosa (they/them)

 is a Chinese human rights defender, non-binary activist and refugee based in Brussels, Belgium. They coordinate Protect Human Rights Defenders (PHRD.EU) and are part of TGEU’s Trans Refugee Network, working across trans liberation, refugee justice, democracy, accessibility and resistance to transnational repression.

Change-making leadership vision:

To turn survival into solidarity and lived experience into collective power  ensuring that those most affected can shape the systems, policies and movements that govern their lives.






















Queen Kevhoney Scarlett (she/her)

 is a visionary leader based in France, representing Miss Trans Global and Inspiration.s Worldwide. Crowned Miss Trans Global 2024, she draws strength from her rich mixed background spanning the West Indies, Asia, and Europe to champion equity and representation.

Change-making leadership vision:

To empower communities through inclusive, bold action that bridges cultures and transforms grassroots passion into sustainable global impact.



















René Fet (he/him)

 is a lifelong LGBTIQ+ activist, campaigner, professional gay, and community organiser with a refugee background, currently based in Luxembourg. Originally from Russia, he was at the forefront of the fight for LGBTIQ+ rights, co-organising Moscow Pride 20 years ago and challenging institutional homophobia through direct action, campaigning, and advocacy.

Change-making leadership vision:

To turn his lived experience, his voice, and his courage to speak up when others cannot safely do so into collective power — and use that power to change institutions, communities, and lives.



















Sean-Claude (he/him)

 is a Jamaican-born Creative Director, Curator, Storyteller and Community Organiser who migrated to the Netherlands as an asylum seeker in 2015. He is the founder of Freedom Work NL, a Black-trans-led DEIA (Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Accountability) and creative consulting firm working towards LGBTQIA+ justice and Black liberation, and Man.ish Cave, an organisation supporting BPOC transmasculine people in and around Amsterdam.

Change-making leadership vision:

My change-making leadership vision is rooted in storytelling, liberation, healing, community building, and creating spaces where freedom becomes possible.



















Theodoros Vlachos (they/them)

 is from Greece and works independently as a social worker and researcher on trans and queer studies. They hold an interdisciplinary background in Social Work and International Relations (MSc, Aalborg University), with professional experience across humanitarian, community, NGO, and corporate settings, focused on child and adolescent protection, support for vulnerable groups, and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) communications.

Change-making leadership vision:

To create spaces where lived experience becomes knowledge, participation becomes agency, and trans and gender-diverse people have the power to shape meaningful and lasting change.



















Tyler Dušak (they/them)

 is a queer transgender activist living in Croatia and a member of Zagreb Pride and Sjemenište kolektiv. Their focus is on building queer spaces where folk are welcome to express themselves and encouraging visibility and pride of all individuals in hopes of strengthening community efforts of transgender rights advocacy.

Change-making leadership vision:

Strength, compassion, and accountability with the ultimate goal of building a society with equality and equity for everyone and freedom from oppression at its forefront.



















Universe of Universal Friends (ey)

 is an intersectional trans activist in the Riga, LV area and beyond. With a focus on active inclusion and outreach, ey have been collaborating on the kviriem.lv queer resource and event compilation project, and running frequent, reliable trans community-building, artmaking, and connecting events.

Change-making leadership vision:

To make events  and connecting more accessible and enjoyable to a greater number of impoverished trans people, especially intersectionally oppressed trans women.



















Yuli Fernandez (she/her)

 is originally from Cuba and currently based in Greece. She is a Black trans woman, political refugee, migrant, and LGBTQIA+ activist living in Athens. She is a community facilitator, treasurer, and board member of her organisation, where she works to strengthen support, visibility, and inclusion for LGBTQIA+ people, particularly refugees, asylum seekers, and trans communities.

Change-making vision:

To turn lived experience into collective strength, create pathways for those who are often excluded, and build communities where everyone can lead with dignity and freedom.










Your support makes change possible




We work across Europe and Central Asia to advance trans rights, build strong communities, and drive change through research, advocacy, and community-building.




Your donation helps us continue this vital work — defending trans lives, amplifying trans voices, and advocating for justice every day.

author: Unknown
title: 4.971 stranên kurdî yên ku hatine tirkîkirin: Diziya ziman, bîranîn û nasnameyê
content:
"Dema ku stranek ji zimanê wê tê dûrxistin, ne tenê gotinên stranê diguherin; dîrok, bîr û nasnameya kesên ku ew stran afirandine jî di xetereyê de ye."




Muzîknas Veysi Varli, di lêkolîna xwe ya li ser 28,000 stranan de diyar kir ku herî kêm 4,971 stranên Kurdî wergerandine Tirkî. Ev hejmar ne tenê hejmarek ji arşîvekê ye, lê nîşaneya pirsgirêkek kûr a di derbarê ziman, çand, bîr û nasnameya gelê Kurd de ye.




Stranên Kurdî ji dilê gel derdikevin. Êş, evîn, koçberî, xerîbî, berxwedan, şahî û bîranînên nifşan dihewînin. Carinan, bi rêya deng û melodiyê, stran tiştên ku bi gotinên asayî nayên vegotin digihînin dilê mirovan. Dema ku dayikek lorîkekê dibêje, dema ku mezinek stranek kevin dibêje, an jî dema ku stranek li ser bûyerek dîrokî tê gotin, beşek ji bîra kolektîf a gel bi rastî tê parastin.




Lêbelê, dema ku ev stran bêyî parastina ziman, çîrok û eslê xwe ji bo Tirkî werin wergerandin pirsgirêk dest pê dike. Ji ber ku pirsgirêk ne wergera gotinan e; pirsgirêk ev e ku gelo stran dikare nasnameya xwe ya resen biparêze, an jî eger bi zimanekî din were pêşkêşkirin, gelo eslê wê dê bi demê re were jibîrkirin.




Wergerandin bi xwe ne sûc e. Her çandek dikare berhemên xwe yên bi zimanên din nas bike. Mirov dikarin stranên Kurdî wergerînin, da ku gelên din wate û bedewiya wan fam bikin. Lêbelê, di şert û mercên ku zimanê Kurdî bi salan qedexe bû, tepeserkirî bû û qada jiyana wê sînordar bû de, tirkîkirina stranên Kurdî bêyî rexneyê nayê nirxandin.




Gava stranek kurdî bi zimanê tirkî tê gotin, lê navê afirînerê wê, zimanê wê yê resen û koka wê ya çandî nayên eşkerekirin, ev yek dikare bibe rêyek ji bo windakirina nasnameya wê. Heke stranek wekî berhemeke tirkî bê pêşkêşkirin, bêyî ku were gotin ku ew ji çanda kurdî hatiye, êdî tenê zimanê wê nehatiye guhertin; têkiliya wê bi gelê ku wê afirandiye jî hatiye qutkirin.




Eger zimanê gelekî bê paşguhkirin, çanda wî/wê bêyî ku koka wî/wê were qebûlkirin, ji nifşekî din re were veguhastin û tiştên ku wan bi zimanê xwe afirandine hêdî hêdî ji bîra wî/wê werin jêbirin, divê ev wekî asîmîlasyon were hesibandin. Asîmîlasyon her tim bi rêya qedexekirinê nayê kirin; carinan ew guhertina nav, ziman û xwedîtiya berheman vedihewîne.




Stranên kurdî di nava malan, gundan, zozanan, cejnan û civînên gel de mezin bûne. Gelek stran ji devê dayikan, dapîran û kalên me derbasî nifşên nû bûne. Piraniya wan ne di nav pirtûkan de, lê di hafîzeya mirovan de hatine parastin.




Ji ber vê yekê, dema stranek tê tirkîzekirin û koka wê tê veşartin, tenê berhemeke hunerî zirarê nabîne. Têkiliya nifşên nû bi ziman û hafîzeya nifşên berê re jî dikare lawaz bibe. Zarokek ku stranek tirkî dibihîze lê nizane ku ew bi kurdî hatiye çêkirin, dibe ku ji beşek ji dîroka xwe bêpar bimîne.




Ev yek divê bibe sedema fikarê. Ji ber ku gel tenê bi axaftina zimanê xwe nabe gel; bi parastina stran, çîrok, gotinên pêşiyan, bîranîn û nirxên xwe jî hebûna xwe didomîne.




Dema ku 4.971 stranên kurdî tên tirkîkirin, pêwîst e ku em bipirsin: Ev stran kengî, li ku derê û ji aliyê kê ve hatine afirandin? Kîjan stran bi navê xwe yê resen tê zanîn? Kîjan stran bêyî nasandina koka wê hatiye tomar kirin? Û çiqas ji wan berheman di arşîv û qeydên fermî de bi awayekî rast hatine tomarkirin?




Bersiva van pirsan bi lêkolînên zanistî, arşîvkirina dengbêjî û muzîka gelêrî, nivîsandina gotinên stranên resen û nasandina afirîneran dikare were dayîn. Divê her stran bi zimanê xwe yê resen, bi navê xwe, bi agahiyên dîrokî û bi çîroka xwe ya çandî bê parastin. Heke wergera wê ya tirkî an bi zimanekî din hebe, divê ev werger wekî werger bê nasandin, ne wekî cihgirek ji bo reseniya wê.




Parastina stranên kurdî ne dijminatiya zimanekî din e. Ev daxwaz e ku tu ziman li ser hesabê zimanekî din neyê bilindkirin, tu çand bi navê çandeke din neyê veşartin û tu gel ji berhemên ku bi zimanê xwe afirandiye bêpar nemîne.




Lêkolîna Veysi Varlı divê bibe destpêka karêkî berfireh. Zanîngeh, muzîkolog, dîroknas, nivîskar, hunermend û saziyên çandî divê hevkarî bikin da ku stranên kurdî bi awayekî zanistî bên komkirin, tomarkirin, vekolîn û parastin. Divê arşîveke berfireh were avakirin ku deng, gotin, navên afirîneran, herêmên jêderê û guhertoyên cuda yên stranên kurdî tê de bên qeyd kirin.




Her wiha, divê hunermendên ku stranên kurdî ji nû ve dibêjin, çavkaniya wan eşkere bikin û mafê çandî yê gelê Kurd nas bikin. Ji ber ku naskirina koka stranê ne tenê erkekî akademîk e; ew erkekî exlaqî û çandî ye jî.




Em ne dijî wergerê ne. Em dijî wê yekê ne ku werger bibe amûra veşartina rastiyê. Em ne dijî pêşkêşkirina stranên xwe ji gelên din re ne. Em dixwazin stranên me bi nasnameyên xwe yên rastîn li cîhanê belav bibin. Em dixwazin ku stranek Kurdî, li her deverê ku tê gotin, wekî stranek Kurdî were naskirin.




Ji ber ku stranên me ne tenê li ser rabirdûyê ne; ew di heman demê de beşek ji pêşeroja me ne. Ger em wan biparêzin, em zimanê xwe, bîra xwe û girêdana xwe bi nifşên berê re diparêzin. Ger em li hember tirkîkirin û veşartina rehên xwe bêdeng bimînin, gelek tiştên ku bi salan di nav gelê me de hatine parastin, dê hêdî hêdî ji hêla nifşên nû ve werin jibîrkirin.




Divê stranên Kurdî werin parastin, ne ku werin tunekirin. Divê zimanê wan were bihîstin, ne ku bi zimanekî din were bêdengkirin.




Ji ber vê yekê, 4971 stran ne tenê hejmarek in. Ew bangek in ji bo parastina çandê, ji nû ve kifşkirina rastiyê û ji bo pêşîgirtina li windabûna bîra gelê Kurd. Parastina stranên Kurdî parastina hebûna me ye; û hebûna gelekî bi nasname, ziman û dengê wî tê parastin.Stranên me dengê gelê me ne. Dengê wan nede windakirin.




(AÖ/AY)

author: Peter C. Gøtzsche, MD
title: ADHD, a Unicorn in the Psychiatric (Be)wilderness
content:
A

ttention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder was invented in America and appeared in the American Psychiatric Association’s 1980 DSM-III diagnosis manual. But what is it?




At an NIH 1998 consensus conference, the chairman asked a leading ADHD expert, Mark Vonnegut, but he couldn’t explain what ADHD is:

1,2

 “They cannot sit still … they are difficult and they aggravate their parents … the diagnosis is a mess … I think, you know, we, uhm, I, I do, I think, part of the problem is that the profession keeps changing the diagnoses.”




Today, ADHD is a contagious, fashionable diagnosis.

3

 When youngsters look up descriptions of people who say they “have” ADHD on social media, they may be convinced they “have” it too and may even self-diagnose.




The diagnostic criteria for ADHD are so vague that when I lecture and ask people to try the adult ADHD test

4,5

 on themselves, it never fails that one quarter to half the audience test positive. Dr Iona Heath, Former President of the UK Royal College of General Practitioners, said in August that “if you want the diagnosis, you will be able to get it.”

6

 Many people are proud of their diagnosis and a British comedian said he needed to try the test five times before he passed.




Those who are too quiet can get the diagnosis of “predominantly inattentive” ADHD. So, what about those in the middle? It is so absurd that I invented a disorder for healthy people, Adult Symptom Deficiency Disorder (ASDD), with a 10-item test that guarantees that no matter what your score is, there is a treatment for you.

7




ADHD is one of the oddest creatures in the psychiatric (be)wilderness. I do not dispute that some people suffer from their symptoms, but if you examine the central tenets of ADHD scientifically and logically, you’ll see that the diagnosis falls apart.

5







The latest misinformation, the Fogany review




On 9 October 2026, a so-called independent review of ADHD and autism was published. It took up 599 pages plus a 230-pages technical annex.

8

 The Acknowledgements on page 463 show that a huge amount of people had contributed to the report but there are no declarations of conflicts of interest for anyone.




The review noted that the current system is not working but the authors were sitting on the fence and didn’t dare tackle the biggest problem of all: overdiagnosis. This is remarkable considering that the report stated that, by the end of 2025, open referrals in England for ADHD assessment exceeded 560,000, more than 17 times the number recorded in 2019.




In 2011, Allen Frances, chairman for the DSM-IV task force, said that the responsibility for defining psychiatric conditions needs to be taken away from the American Psychiatric Association because new diagnoses are as dangerous as new drugs:

9




“We have remarkably casual procedures for defining the nature of conditions, yet they can lead to tens of millions being treated with drugs they may not need, and that may harm them.” Frances noted that DSM-IV created three false epidemics because the diagnostic criteria were too wide: ADHD, autism and childhood bipolar disorder.




As I shall explain below, the summary in the Fogany review presented highly misleading statements. It called ADHD a strongly genetically influenced neurodevelopmental disorder, which influences attention, communication, behaviour, learning and how people experience the world; the patients are neurodivergent; and the diagnosis can help explain difficulties that significantly impair a person’s functioning, participation and quality of life.




The Fogany review recommended banning direct-to-public advertising of NHS-funded ADHD and autism assessments. But when the 

BMJ 

published a news item about the review,

10

 it was accompanied by an ad for methylphenidate:







Methylphenidate is a narcotic on prescription used against ADHD. In the US, Ritalin, Adderall, and methamphetamine, all used against ADHD, are Schedule II controlled substances, which cocaine, oxycodone, and fentanyl also are.




Respectable medical journals avoid placing drug ads close to an article describing that type of drug or disease. But the 

BMJ

 is no longer a respectable journal. This summer, the editor, Kamran Abbasi, refused to publish criticisms in print of its highly misleading suicide prevention articles 

11

 even though he could have contributed to reducing the meaningless suicides caused by antidepressants by telling their readers that antidepressants do not protect against suicide. They double suicides in adults,

12

 and very likely also in children.

5




The photo of the children has a link to an 

interview

 Abbasi conducted with Sir Simon Wessely, professor of psychiatry and vice-chair for the Fogany review. The headline shows 

BMJ

’s stance on the issue: “Overdiagnosis is not the biggest problem in ADHD and autism.”




Wessely says that he finds neurodiversity an incredibly useful term and that 20% of school children and young adults identify as neurodiverse (see below why this is bullshit). Eight years ago, Wessely rejected any link between antidepressants and suicide and stated, categorically, that the pills are “not addictive,” both of which are false.

5




The latest brouhaha, the Channel 4 documentary




On 18 August, Channel 4 in the UK showed the documentary, “The great ADHD myth?”

13

 which sought to determine whether ADHD is a genuine neurodevelopmental disorder or a social construct.

14

 The press release from 29 July acknowledged that, while the traits of ADHD undeniably exist, it asked if we should be giving children powerful, mind-altering drugs to treat it.

14




Child and adolescent psychiatrist Sami Timimi said that we have replaced corporal punishment with giving children a pill and Iona Heath said that ADHD is not a medical condition.

14




Heath’s former organisation, Royal College of General Practitioners, immediately denounced her. They made it clear that the quote attributed to a former College President was not made on behalf of the College and recognised ADHD as a neurodevelopmental condition.

15




Many people on social media were so outraged that they called for censorship even before they had seen the documentary.

16

 Most critics interpreted it as denying that ”ADHD exists,” yet none of the experts in the film denied that some people diagnosed with ADHD have serious problems.

17

 As I shall discuss next, asking pertinent questions in the public arena about one of psychiatry’s holy cows was too much for influential organisations.




Condemnations by ADHD UK




Two weeks before the programme aired, ADHD UK warned Channel 4 that it would cause harm in an open letter that was so misleading that it could have been written by a drug firm.

18

 The charity has a commercial relationship with ADHD 360, a private company whose business depends upon people being assessed, diagnosed and treated for ADHD.

19




In response to concerns from anonymous whistleblowers, external stakeholders, and people using the service, England’s healthcare regulator inspected ADHD 360 in 2020 and 2023 and found that improvement was needed.

20




A week before the documentary aired, ADHD UK’s CEO Henry Shelford, who offers paid ADHD coaching, called it “sensationalist nonsense” and urged ”the charity’s members (potentially over 10,000 people) to lodge complaints.”

19,20

 There was even a complaint form.




ADHD UK used a similar strategy in 2023 in relation to BBC’s Panorama investigation about private ADHD clinics, again complaining to the broadcaster before the programme aired.

19

 After the broadcast, ADHD UK announced they would complain to the BBC and ask as many people as possible to join in that complaint. It published a detailed step-by-step complaints guide and noted that “It is fine to copy/paste.”




There were 1,639 complaints, and ADHD UK declared that it was the most complained-about Panorama programme. They might as well have sent the same complaint 1,639 times.




ADHD UK claimed that ADHD is not a social construct but a neurodevelopmental disorder.

18

 This claim is everywhere, also in psychiatric textbooks

21

 and in messages from the UK National Health Service and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

22

 It gives people the impression that science has found out that there is something objectively wrong with the brains of people with an ADHD diagnosis.




This is totally false,

21

 but if you repeat something often enough, people come to believe it to be true. Psychiatrists use impressive, scientific-looking words to obscure their ignorance and to deceive people, just like quacks do. We call it scientism.

23

 Abnormal development of the nervous system involves structural and functional disruptions during embryonic and foetal growth, leading to congenital central nervous system anomalies, e.g. neural tube defects such as spina bifida. To claim that ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition is plain bullshit.




There is no evidence of a specific neurological state or process that gives rise to or is associated with ADHD.

17

 There are no biomarkers, it is not a dopamine deficiency disorder, and the brains are no different from those of people without the label.

5,24,25

 But 

Lancet Psychiatry

 nonetheless called it a disorder of the brain.

25




ADHD UK called Channel 4’s press release “materially misleading” because it noted that boys aged 10-14 comprise the largest group being medicated.

18

 Channel 4 referred to NHS data showing that its statement is correct.

18




ADHD UK called the ”chronic underdiagnosis of girls” a national scandal and claimed that the real story was not one of overmedication. This is what we always hear. Even though psychiatric drugs are the third leading cause of death,

26

 and harm people seriously in numerous other ways,

1,5,21,27,28

 we are always told that the problem is undertreatment.




ADHD UK noted that the programme put lives at risk; that ADHD drugs reduce the suicide risk; and that ”adults with diagnosed ADHD die on average around seven years earlier for men and nearly nine years earlier for women.”




This is extreme disinformation. ADHD drugs increase the risk of suicide and violence.

25,29,30

 and they don’t improve survival. ADHD UK didn’t provide a reference but I found the study, which is fatally flawed.

31

 People with an ADHD diagnosis had much higher rates of smoking, alcohol use, severe mental illness, and physical illnesses, which the authors of the study glossed over. I could equally well say that old people die earlier than young people but that would not make us wiser either.




ADHD UK claimed that ADHD is a lifelong condition, but many studies have documented that the symptoms that define ADHD can disappear when children grow up. A Canadian study showed that the prevalence of school children in treatment in the same class increased pretty much linearly over the months from January to December,

32

 with 50% more of those born in December being on drugs. This relative age effect was confirmed in a systematic review of 31 studies.

33

 If we allowed children to grow up and mature, fewer would receive an ADHD label and drugs.




A study spanning four decades showed that 90% of adult cases had no history of childhood ADHD.

34

 To circumvent this problem, psychiatrists have said that ADHD presents differently in adults, or in women and girls, but as psychiatrist professor Joanna Moncrieff noted, this is nonsensical, because how it presents is what it is, and if it is different, it is not the same.

17




About medication, ADHD UK noted that ”133 randomised, double-blind controlled trials, covering around 18,000 people, underpin its use, and its measured benefit is among the largest in psychiatry … research links treatment with better school performance, fewer accidents and injuries.”




The short-term benefit of the drugs is that children may sit still in class, but this effect disappears quickly. The package inserts, e.g. for Adderall, reveal that the harms include sudden death, mania, delusional thinking, aggression, hostility, tics, vasculopathy, and a high potential for drug abuse. There is no improvement in school performance and no reduction in accidents and injuries.

5




ADHD UK spoke about having ADHD and to live with ADHD,

18

 and the Fogany review noted that ADHD can influence attention and behaviour, but this is how the disorder is defined. A name cannot cause anything. ADHD is just a name for a collection of symptoms at one end of a normal behavioural spectrum where people are more energetic, impatient, and irritating than others. When we give a certain behaviour a name, we cannot say that a person behaves this way 

because 

he has ADHD. This reification, which is harmful,

22

 is circular evidence, a tautology. You can have a dog but you cannot have ADHD or live with ADHD, which just means to live with yourself, which we all do. When patients believe that a name can explain anything, they have been fooled.




Condemnations from the Global ADHD Network




The Global ADHD Network also condemned the film before they had seen it.

35

 They claimed that science had already answered the question if ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder and lamented that the question was reopened before a prime-time audience of hundreds of thousands of worried parents, undiagnosed adults, and vulnerable children.




The network claimed that ADHD is one of the most robustly evidenced conditions in psychiatry. If so, it says a lot about the rest of psychiatry!




We are told that genome-wide association studies have identified specific common genetic variants linked to ADHD, confirming a polygenic architecture, and that a condition that is roughly three-quarters heritable is not a “social construct.” However, the genetic emperor is naked. In one study, which claimed ADHD was related to genetic abnormalities, combining two tables shows that 99.7% of the patients don’t have genetic abnormalities.

36

 I have heard a professor say at a meeting that there is 80% agreement for identical twins.

5

 So, people who are identical behave similarly. Surprise, surprise.




The network claimed that people with ADHD have small brains, with reduced volumes in five regions. They referred to a 2017 review in 

Lancet Psychiatry

 with 58 authors,

37

 which has been debunked. The journal devoted an entire issue to criticisms of the study, and a re-analysis of the data, also in 

Lancet Psychiatry

, found no brain differences.

38

 It is scientific misconduct to quote the original results 9 years later as if they were true.




Like ADHD UK and the drug industry, the network tried to convince their readers by using big numbers. We are told that every major medical body has already answered the “myth” question and that more than 10,000 clinical and scientific publications on ADHD exist. This is amusing. PubMed lists 2,107 entries with homeopathy or homoeopathy in the title, but that cannot remove the fact that homoeopathy is bogus.

39

 There is nothing in it.




The network claimed that ADHD is underdiagnosed, especially in women, girls and adults. When we are done with that, we should perhaps turn our attention to underdiagnosed ADHD in dogs. Many of them are impatient, cannot sit still, and bark too much.




The network mentioned “the landmark NIMH Multimodal Treatment Study of ADHD (the MTA), showing that properly prescribed, monitored medication reduces core symptoms and impairment.” This study is fraudulent. A lot has been written about how the investigators manipulated their results or drowned them in incomprehensible statistics to conceal how disappointing the long-term results were.

5

 One of the investigators broke ranks and stated in an interview:

40

 “The children had a substantial decrease in their rate of growth … there were no beneficial effects – none … that information should be made very clear to parents.”




It wasn’t. The public was lied to. An NIMH press release stated that the improvement was sustained in most children and one of the authors, Peter Jensen, said that the investigators were struck by the remarkable improvement in symptoms and functioning across all treatment groups.

41

 And rather than saying that the growth of children on drug treatment was stunted, the press release said that children who were 

not 

on medication “grew somewhat larger.”




After 16 years, those who consistently took their pills were 5 cm shorter than those who took very little.

42

 I consider it likely that these drugs also harm the developing brain. And methylphenidate doesn’t protect against delinquency and substance abuse, which people usually claim; if anything, it causes them.

43




The network said they fight misinformation and that “evidence is our strongest weapon.”

35

 They distorted the science beyond belief and claimed that Channel 4 presented the views “of a small number of cherry-picked medical professionals as though they constitute fair and balanced representation of the science.” Thou shalt not criticise the Lord’s precious drugs.




The 

BMJ

 published sheer rubbish 




As so often before,

44-46

 the 

BMJ

 published a misleading article in support of a failed psychiatry.

47

 The 

BMJ

 editor must have thought it was important because it was commissioned, not externally peer reviewed, and published with record speed.




The article had the declarative title, “The Great ADHD Myth documentary is misleading and misinformed.” The authors postulated that a wealth of robust research supports the view that ADHD is a well established, extensively evidenced neurodevelopmental condition; that the disorder is associated with serious adverse outcomes, including substance misuse, suicide, and premature mortality (reification again); and that substantial evidence from randomised trials shows that ADHD responds to treatment.




The key reference is to a consensus report

48

 with 80 so-called authors. All top ADHD experts take drug company money,

49

 and the most interesting part of the consensus report is the financial disclosures. The first author, Stephen V. Faraone from the USA, declared that he, in the past year, had received support from 13 companies and in previous years from 13 other named companies. During a 10-year period, he had put his name on an article every 11 days.

49

 One of my colleagues once remarked that if a doctor had lent Shakespeare a pencil, he would have become co-author of 

Macbeth

.




Two of the three authors of the 

BMJ

 article work at departments of clinical neuroscience, even though ADHD has nothing to do with neuroscience. The third author is from the British Association for Neurodiversity and she declared under competing interests that she is neurodivergent.




This is bullshit. Neurodivergent is a nonmedical term coined in 1998 to recognise that everyone’s brain develops in a unique way.

50

 Thus, apart from identical twins, we are all neurodivergent, which renders the notion meaningless.




The authors accused the documentary of having “made the scientifically inaccurate claim that brain imaging studies have shown that ADHD is not a condition of the brain or development,” quoting the consensus report. However, the statement is accurate.

5

 ADHD is not a brain disease. A brain tumour is a brain disease.




The authors said that the “disorder is associated with serious adverse outcomes.” These tautological reifications are everywhere. People don’t realise that such statements are empty.




As usual, the authors also made sacrifices to the industry gods. They rejected that there was overdiagnosis and emphasised that “there is clear evidence of underdiagnosis.” They also claimed that drug effects are clinically meaningful, with significant reductions in adverse outcomes.




Like other authors, these authors opined that the implication that ADHD is a myth is “unhelpful and risks perpetuating stigma and prejudice. It speaks to an ongoing lack of parity between physical health and mental health/neurodevelopmental conditions.”




Mental health issues cannot be compared to physical health issues. If you have a broken leg, you want to have it fixed, not just to get an aspirin to lessen the pain. But in psychiatry, this is exactly what is offered.

5

 A drug that doesn’t really help the patient’s emotional pain

5

 is not a causal treatment like bone surgery is, and it doesn’t stigmatise the patients if their doctors were a little honest about the issues, for a change.




The Guardian

 got it right




The Guardian

’s reviewer of the documentary noted that the presenter, psychiatrist Max Pemberton, answered the questions he posed convincingly, and that the proposed redresses, which included making drugs the last resort, seemed neither radical nor uncompassionate.

6




A former president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists (Professor Dinesh Bhugra) said that “The industry around ADHD is about making money at the cost of the misery of others,” and child and adolescent psychiatrist Sami Timimi reminded people that the drugs most often involve amphetamines, which are controlled substances, and that there is a good reason why the rest of the population are warned about them.

6




When Pemberton took a dose of the amphetamine he was prescribed for his spurious ADHD diagnosis, he reported feeling subdued and antisocial.

17

 He didn’t want to talk to the people in his local shop as he normally would and wanted the film crew to leave him alone.




Other comments on what ADHD is




Many psychiatrists, psychologists, neurologists and others have documented how false the statements about AHDH offered by mainstream psychiatry are.

17,21-25, 51,52

 But the day after the documentary aired, the President of the Royal College of Psychiatrists wrote that we should not question ”the legitimacy of a well-established neurodevelopmental disorder.”

53




Critics of drug focused psychiatry noted that the institutional response to the film illustrated the confused thinking that underpins the mainstream understanding of ADHD.

24

 Most importantly, the claim that “ADHD is real” has multiple meanings. The experiential reality of the difficulties classified as ADHD are real, but the claim that ADHD is an established neurological disorder that explains those difficulties is not.




A consensus statement claimed

52,54

 that there is no disagreement; that numerous studies link ADHD to several specific areas of the brain; that the genetic contribution to the disorder is the highest for any psychiatric disorder, with one specific gene being reliably associated with ADHD; that the propaganda of ”fringe doctors” with a political agenda want the public to believe there is no real disorder; and that publishing stories that ADHD is a fictitious disorder “is tantamount to declaring the earth flat, the laws of gravity debatable, and the periodic table in chemistry a fraud.”




This is the talk of people who are desperately short of arguments. They tried to impress their readers by using big numbers: 86 people were co-signatories and there were 547 references, the largest number I have seen for any article. The first author, Russell A. Barkley, organised the statement and is a strong supporter of narcotics on prescription—amphetamine and amphetamine-like substances—for ADHD.




What should we do?




Some studies have shown that one child in five meets the diagnostic criteria.

25

 But calling ADHD a common disorder is false. It cannot be pathological that so many children behave rather normally. I can recommend Martin Whitely’s hilarious little video, “ADHD is BS”

55

 that mocks the ADHD pseudoscience. It is a good antidote against hubris and grandiosity.




The difficulties people experience should be understood and supported, without the need to apply a diagnostic label that implies a lifelong underlying neurological disorder. NHS England’s ADHD Taskforce recommends that support should be needs-led and should not require a clinical diagnosis which can be self-fulfilling and life-limiting.

24




My views, supported by the best evidence we have, are that the ADHD diagnosis is fake and should be buried in the graveyard of psychiatry’s many failures;

5

 ADHD drugs should be removed from the market because they are harmful; people with symptoms that qualify for an ADHD diagnosis should receive psychosocial interventions; triggers, such as poor parenting or poor schoolteachers, should be addressed; and the social structures that constrain parents and teachers from doing better and having the time and freedom to do so should be addressed.
