title: Communalist students discuss new forms of organizing in Amed
content:
Under the slogan “It is time to unite through communally organized universities,” hundreds of students and young people from Kurdistan and Turkey gathered for a conference in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) on Saturday. At the ÇandAmed Congress Center, they discussed the political and social role of youth in the peace and democratic society process, self-organized university structures, and the struggle against social exploitation, environmental destruction, and state repression.




Large portraits of Abdullah Öcalan were displayed in the conference hall, alongside banners bearing slogans such as “The women’s path is the path of life” and “We started young, we will triumph young.” Participants welcomed arriving members of the Peace Mothers Council with a standing ovation. Following a minute of silence, the Kurdish anthem “Çerxa Şoreşê” was sung.




“Youth are the fundamental force in building society”




Hasan Karsu, speaking on behalf of the students, focused his speech on social and ecological crises. In light of the ongoing destruction of nature, particularly in Kurdistan, and growing social insecurity, he called upon young people to take responsibility for creating an alternative way of life. “We must not underestimate the social power that students can generate. We must recognize that young people who develop their own independent will can achieve things beyond our imagination. Youth are the fundamental force in building society,” he stated.







Karsu pointed out that the current conditions are characterized by oppression, exploitation, bullying, and violence. “Young people are deprived of their autonomy and reduced to passive objects within society. However, these policies will not break the resistance of the youth. Those who impose all of this on us should know: You will not be able to take our youth away from us. You will come to realize that we are the voice of millions.” Karsu called for strengthening political organizing at universities and schools and intensifying the struggle for equal, free education in the mother tongue.




“Combining our historical role with practical work”




Referring to the new phase of the Kurdish freedom struggle, Karsu explained that while the means and methods of political struggle are changing, its fundamental objectives remain the same. “We have deviated neither from our spirit nor from our goals. We are simply in a phase in which our means and methods are changing. In this new era, we must combine our historical mission with our practical work.”




Karsu remarked that the students are part of a revolutionary tradition that transcends social boundaries and embraces far-reaching solidarity. He said their task is to build a democratic alternative to the existing system within universities. At the same time, he warned of social problems such as drug trafficking, organized crime, and violence against young people. He argued that these developments could not be viewed independently of state strategies aimed at weakening social organizing.







TJA activist Akgül: Dogmatism makes us grow old




Nesrin Akgül of the Kurdish women’s movement TJA devoted her speech to the question of how revolutionary openness and the capacity for social renewal can be preserved. She referred to Abdullah Öcalan’s political approach and his call of February 27, 2025. “With February 27, Abdullah Öcalan once again rejuvenated society and the movement,” Akgül said. She underlined that the Kurdish leader has maintained his capacity for intellectual and political renewal despite his many years of imprisonment.




“What exhausts young people the most and makes them grow old is dogmatism. It damages relationships and imposes limits on them. When we overcome rigid patterns of thought, we remain young. Living together with differences, with people who are different from us, keeps us young.”




Ahmet Emre Taştan spoke on behalf of the Free University Movement, linking his speech to the words, “The sun will belong to those who struggle at dawn.” The conference then continued with a film screening.







Rojava University calls for protection of autonomous university structures




One of the main focuses of the conference was messages of solidarity from various youth and student organizations. Alongside YUNA – Democratic Youth from Germany, messages of solidarity were also sent by the World Youth Strike Movement, the youth wing of the Party of the Oppressed (EHP), youth communes, the Revolutionary Students Union, Libertarian Youth, and the Revolutionary Youth Forces (Dev-Güç), among others.




A Kurdish-language message from Rojava University received particular attention. It emphasized the importance of the conference for organizing young people and warned of attempts to alienate youth from their cultural and political identity through drugs, social estrangement, and other methods of state influence. At the same time, the students criticized the slow progress of the peace process. They said Öcalan remains in isolation, and his physical freedom is an essential prerequisite for advancing the process and resolving existing problems.




Regarding the ongoing integration process in Rojava, the university emphasized that democratic integration must not be equated with abandoning social self-governance. “We want our universities and institutions to remain autonomous. We will give up neither our educational rights nor our linguistic rights. Only in this way can we preserve our identity and culture. You should know that you are not alone!”




Solidarity from Kobanê and Maxmur




Kobanê University also sent a video message describing the conference as a new step toward organizing young people. It urged students from all four parts of Kurdistan to support the initiative and strengthen their joint political efforts. “This conference is a new step, and young people must take further steps. Students from all four parts of Kurdistan should embrace this conference and its motivation and support this struggle. We are ready to do everything in our power.”




A message of solidarity was also received from the Maxmur refugee camp. It referred to the peace and democratic society process and criticized the failure to take the necessary political steps so far. “If the state had taken the necessary steps, we would also be in this hall today.”




The conference will continue with further discussions on student organizing and the establishment of communalist university structures.

title: El Partido por encima del capital: lo que Xi Jinping dijo a los empresarios chinos
content:
Xi Jinping al asumir un nuevo mandato el 18 de octubre de 2022.




Lo que Xi dijo a los empresarios




El 17 de febrero de 2025, Xi Jinping reunió en Pekín a los grandes empresarios privados de China: los responsables de Huawei, BYD y Xiaomi, así como los fundadores de Alibaba y Tencent. Era la primera cita de este nivel desde 2018. Quienes esperaban un cheque en blanco para el capital se quedaron sin él. Xi garantizó protección a la empresa privada, sí, pero dentro de un marco que dejó muy claro: esa política forma parte del sistema socialista con características chinas, y sus principios no pueden cambiar y no cambiarán. Aquí, donde los gobiernos se arrodillan ante los mercados, conviene fijarse en el contraste.




El Partido dirige, la ley protege




Xi lo explicó sin rodeos. Es el Partido Comunista quien dirige al pueblo en el desarrollo de la economía socialista de mercado. El sector público se consolida sin vacilaciones, mientras que el sector privado se alienta, se apoya y se guía. Y la protección tiene sus límites: se amparan los derechos legítimos, no las ganancias ilegales, y se protege conforme a la ley, sin «favores extralegales». China, recordó, es un país socialista regido por la ley, y ninguna forma de propiedad puede quedar al margen de una investigación si infringe esa ley.




La empresa, al servicio del país




A los empresarios les pidió que alinearan su pensamiento y su acción con las decisiones económicas del Comité Central. Les recordó que cuanto mejor es una empresa, mayor es su responsabilidad social: cuidar a sus trabajadores y fomentar relaciones laborales armoniosas, no buscar el desarrollo a costa de contaminar, colaborar en obras de interés público y dar un paso al frente cuando la patria lo necesite, sobre todo en tiempos de crisis. Y concluyó pidiéndoles que utilizaran su prosperidad para promover la prosperidad común.




Prosperidad común frente a oligarquía




No es una ocurrencia de última hora. En agosto de 2021, Xi defendió que China debe optar por la prosperidad común y no por un crecimiento sin límites, porque este genera una desigualdad excesiva. Esa política se asoció a la regulación de los ingresos excesivos y a la oposición a la expansión desordenada del capital. Según la revista Qiushi, Xi llegó a decir que la prosperidad común no es solo una cuestión económica, sino también un asunto político de primer orden que atañe a la base del poder del Partido. Alibaba y Tencent anunciaron aportaciones de miles de millones de dólares a esa causa.




Una década de mejoras sociales




Hablemos de resultados, con cifras oficiales. Entre 2012 y 2020, 98,99 millones de personas del medio rural salieron de la pobreza extrema, y los 832 condados y las 128.000 aldeas que figuraban como pobres dejaron de estar incluidos en esa categoría. Durante ese periodo, se construyeron o mejoraron 1,1 millones de kilómetros de carreteras rurales; más del 98 % de las aldeas pobres dispone hoy de fibra óptica y cobertura 4G, y más de 25 millones de personas vieron renovadas sus viviendas en ruinas. China dio el objetivo por cumplido en febrero de 2021, diez años antes del plazo de la Agenda 2030 de la ONU.




La protección social creció a la par. En 2020, el seguro médico básico cubría a 1.360 millones de personas, el 95 % de la población, y los seguros de desempleo y de accidentes de trabajo daban cobertura a 217 y 268 millones de trabajadores, respectivamente. La pensión básica cubría a más de 1.070 millones de personas en 2024. Entre 2012 y 2021, la renta disponible per cápita subió un 112,8 %, y la renta rural creció más rápidamente que la urbana (un 125,7 % frente a un 96,5 %), de modo que se redujo la brecha entre el campo y la ciudad. Además, en su discurso de 2025, Xi exigió que se pusiera fin a los impagos a las empresas privadas y que estas cumplieran con el pago de los salarios de sus trabajadores.




Más años de vida




La esperanza de vida alcanzó los 79 años en 2024, 1,1 años más que en 2020, según la Comisión Nacional de Salud. En 1960 rondaba los 44 años. En 2024, la mortalidad infantil descendió a 4,0 por cada 1.000 nacimientos y la mortalidad materna, a 14,3 por cada 100.000 nacimientos, ambas en mínimos históricos. Además, ocho regiones de nivel provincial superan ya los 80 años de esperanza de vida. El objetivo oficial es alcanzar aproximadamente los 80 años en 2030. El gasto sanitario total representó el 6,7 % del PIB en 2024.




Sanidad y educación: lo público manda, pero hay mercado.




Seamos rigurosos, porque la verdad no necesita adornos. En sanidad, la cobertura básica se articula mediante un seguro social público que alcanza al 95 % de la población. La red hospitalaria es mixta, aunque la atención está dominada por el sector público: en 2021, los hospitales públicos concentraron el 84,2 % de las consultas externas y el 81,4 % de los ingresos, además de alrededor del 70 % de las camas hospitalarias. Los hospitales privados son más numerosos (24.766 frente a 11.804), pero mucho más pequeños, y su cuota de consultas ha aumentado del 9,1 % en 2011 al 15,8 % en 2021.




En educación, la enseñanza obligatoria de nueve años, de los 6 a los 15, está financiada por el Estado, que se comprometió a ofrecerla gratuitamente. Se imparte tanto en escuelas públicas como en centros privados sin ánimo de lucro. Desde 2021, la política oficial busca que las escuelas públicas sigan siendo el principal proveedor de esta enseñanza: en teoría, no se autorizan nuevas escuelas privadas para la etapa obligatoria. La matrícula en centros privados de primaria representa el 6,4 % del total (2024). En cambio, en educación infantil, el 57 % de los niños acude a centros privados, frente a un tercio de media en la OCDE.




Por su parte, servicios básicos como la electricidad y las telecomunicaciones están en manos de grandes empresas estatales, como State Grid, China Mobile, China Telecom y China Unicom.




Qué es público, qué es mixto y qué es privado




No existe una lista legal única y cerrada. Lo que hay son directrices de la Comisión de Supervisión y Administración de Activos del Estado (SASAC) y listas de acceso al mercado que se han ido ajustando con los años. En la práctica, hay tres escalones.




Primero, los sectores estratégicos. En 2006, la SASAC fijó siete sectores en los que el Estado debía mantener el «control absoluto»: armamento, generación y distribución de electricidad, petróleo y petroquímica, telecomunicaciones, carbón, aviación civil y transporte marítimo. En electricidad, petróleo, gas, telecomunicaciones y armamento, el Estado debe ser propietario único o mayoritario; en carbón, aviación civil y transporte marítimo, debe conservar una participación de control.




Segundo, los sectores «pilares», en los que el Estado orienta el desarrollo y la propiedad es, en buena medida, mixta: automoción, química, construcción, electrónica, maquinaria y equipo, metales no ferrosos, prospección, acero y tecnología.




Tercero, los sectores competitivos, como el turismo, el inmobiliario, la manufactura general, la agricultura, la farmacia, los servicios profesionales y el comercio. En ellos, el Estado debe reducir su presencia y las empresas privadas pueden operar en condiciones de igualdad.




Desde 2013, la reforma de la propiedad mixta permite abrir empresas públicas al capital privado. En 2018, más del 70 % de las empresas centrales y el 88 % de las provinciales de los sectores competitivos ya habían emprendido este proceso, y se permite que el capital privado tenga una participación de control en algunas de ellas. Aun así, cerca del 80 % de los activos de las empresas centrales seguía concentrado en petróleo, petroquímica, electricidad, armamento, telecomunicaciones y minería.




Como regla general, la lista negativa de acceso al mercado de 2025 establece que todo lo que no figure en ella está abierto, en condiciones de igualdad, a las empresas públicas, privadas y extranjeras. Las empresas privadas representan más del 92 % del total de empresas del país.




Lo que yo defiendo




Aquí quiero dejar clara mi posición, sin medias tintas. Los sectores básicos y estratégicos, así como todos aquellos de los que depende la ciudadanía para vivir, deben estar totalmente en manos del Estado, y el capital privado no debe intervenir en ellos en absoluto.




El capital privado busca un beneficio económico, y es lógico que lo haga, porque para eso existe. Precisamente por eso, su entrada en sectores tan sensibles supone un peligro: cuando lo que está en juego es la energía, las comunicaciones, la sanidad o la educación, no se puede supeditar la vida de la gente a una cuenta de resultados.




En esto, yo iría más lejos que el modelo chino, que admite capital privado en los sectores «pilares» y abre algunas empresas públicas a la propiedad mixta. Pero que China mantenga el control estatal del petróleo, la electricidad o las telecomunicaciones, y que el Partido deje claro que el capital no está por encima del pueblo, apunta en la dirección correcta.




La edad de jubilación




Hay un dato que conviene conocer y que no voy a esconder: desde el 1 de enero de 2025, China está elevando gradualmente, a lo largo de 15 años, la edad legal de jubilación, algo que no se hacía desde hace décadas. Los hombres pasarán de los 60 a los 63 años; las mujeres, de los 55 a los 58 en los puestos administrativos y técnicos, y de los 50 a los 55 en los trabajos manuales. El periodo mínimo de cotización subirá de 15 a 20 años.




Quienes cumplan ese mínimo podrán jubilarse hasta tres años antes de la nueva edad legal, pero nunca antes de la edad que regía anteriormente. El punto de partida es una edad de jubilación muy baja: la esperanza de vida alcanzó los 78,6 años en 2023, y la edad legal de jubilación en China figuraba entre las más bajas del mundo, por debajo de la de Japón (65 años) o Corea del Sur (63 años). Proyecciones de instituciones estatales chinas advertían de que el principal fondo de pensiones se agotaría hacia 2035 si no se acometía una reforma. La medida no ha estado exenta de debate entre la población.




Dos modelos, una pregunta




Mientras en China el capital privado tiene que rendir cuentas ante el Partido y ante la ley, aquí los fondos buitre especulan con la vivienda, las puertas giratorias colocan a políticos en los consejos de administración y la derecha legisla al dictado de los grandes poderes económicos.




Cada cual puede sacar sus propias conclusiones sobre quién manda de verdad en cada lugar.




¡Até a vitoria sempre!




André Abeledo Fernández

author: Publicación Abierta
title: España: Feijóo ya habla como Abascal
content:
El presidente del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo







La careta se cae a trozosA cinco semanas de las elecciones generales del 29N, Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha dejado de disimular. El hombre que durante años se vendió como el gestor moderado, el político sensato que salió de la Xunta para poner orden en la derecha, abraza ahora, sin complejos y a lo bestia, el discurso reaccionario de VOX. Antiocupación a golpe de «fuera en 48 horas», pensiones puestas en duda, derechos en almoneda. Cualquier cosa por llegar a La Moncloa. Sabe que es su última oportunidad. Y no, no es que no sea presidente porque no quiera: no lo es porque es un político mediocre, sin límites ni principios.




Enfermar, un lujo que no nos podemos permitir




Feijóo llama «cáncer» a las bajas laborales, cuestiona que un trabajador cobre lo mismo estando enfermo que trabajando y promete imponer su criterio «con o sin acuerdo sindical». Lo dicen dos hombres que nunca han sido empleados de una empresa privada. Feijóo pasó de funcionario de la Xunta a vivir de la política desde los años noventa. Abascal encadena cargos públicos desde 1999, y su única experiencia fuera de ellos fue un bar en Vitoria que acabó en desahucio, embargos y condenas a su empresa por impagos a los trabajadores. Viven del dinero público que sale de los impuestos de los trabajadores y vienen a darnos lecciones.




Yo llevo más de dieciocho años en el comercio y sé lo que es el trabajo físico; sé que nadie se pone de baja por capricho. Ellos, que no conocen la palabra esfuerzo, nos piden sacrificios y pretenden dejarnos desnudos y desprotegidos ante los poderosos, ante sus amos.




Pensiones, eutanasia, aborto: nada está a salvo




La portavoz del PP en el Congreso, Ester Muñoz, dijo en un pódcast que el sistema de pensiones «va a petar» y que hay que cambiar el modelo con «valentía», sin explicar cómo. Cuando saltó la alarma, ella misma y Feijóo corrieron a decir que las pensiones son «innegociables» y que subirán con el IPC. Feijóo, además, intentó cerrar la polémica sin desautorizar a su portavoz.




Cuando le llovieron las críticas, Muñoz explicó que «petar» lo decía «en los términos que utiliza la gente joven». Una excusa de manual, porque quien habla de «valentía» para cambiar el modelo no se desdice: se disfraza.




No me lo creo: lo que dice la portavoz es lo que piensa el partido del que Feijóo es candidato. Conviene recordar que el PP votó en 2021 contra la ley que garantiza la revalorización de las pensiones con el IPC.




Hablan del «derecho del no nacido» mientras recortan los derechos de los trabajadores que enferman, y anuncian que reformarán la ley de eutanasia para «perfeccionarla». Que nos perdonen si no nos fiamos: cuando la derecha dice que va a «perfeccionar» un derecho, lo que suele querer es ponerle puertas. Y con VOX en el tablero, cada derecho conquistado es una pieza que están dispuestos a cobrarse.




PP-VOX, el tándem de la demolición




Lo que representa el tándem PP-VOX es la demolición de lo poco que queda del supuesto Estado del bienestar y de la justicia social: involución social y odio de clase. Recurren a las viejas estrategias de propaganda de Goebbels, el ministro de la Alemania nazi, ahora amplificadas por las redes sociales y los medios de desinformación: bulos, mentiras y odio a las minorías.




No quieren debatir su programa porque saben que perderían, así que solo les queda mentir y buscar chivos expiatorios. Siembran odio y el odio, tarde o temprano, cosecha violencia y sufrimiento.




Los amos de siempre




Feijóo y Abascal son, a mi juicio, títeres de las oligarquías, del Israel de Netanyahu y de los Estados Unidos de Donald Trump. Vendepatrias dispuestos a todo a la hora de defender los intereses de sus amos, sin límites morales ni éticos, sin patria ni empatía; solo hambre de dinero.




Humildes ante el poder y altivos con la clase trabajadora, son los encargados de dar la cara en nombre de los dueños del sistema.




La respuesta está en nuestras manos




Frente al odio, organización. Frente a los bulos, conciencia de clase. Frente a quienes nos quieren desprotegidos, sindicato, calle y unidad de la gente trabajadora. Ni un paso atrás en derechos.




¡Até á vitoria sempre!




André Abeledo Fernández

title: México: gran red de solidaridad recibirá al EZLN en su encuentro con familias buscadoras
content:
México




Una gran red de solidaridad se prepara para recibir al EZLN en su encuentro con familias buscadoras




23 octubre, 2026




Una gran red de solidaridad se ha tejido con el objetivo de preparar el recibimiento de más de mil 530 delegados del 

Ejercito Zapatista de Liberación Nacional (EZLN),

 quienes viajaran a finales de noviembre desde las montañas de Chiapas rumbo a la Ciudad de México (CDMX) para reunirse con 

familias buscadoras de personas desaparecidas.




Esta red une a más de 670 organizaciones, pueblos, comunidades, espacios culturales y colectivos que se preparan con diversas actividades, pleneación, estrategias de seguridad y reuniones organizativas para recibirles en la SEDE BASE 

Casa de los Pueblos y Comunidades Indígenas “Samir Flores Soberanes” en la CDMX

 inmueble bajo resguardo de la comunidad otomí residente en la capital.




Recientemente el EZLN precisó que en la delegación de la 

Gira Por la Vida-Capítulo México

 irán 709 hombres, 622 mujeres y 2 otroas, además de 24 del 

Comando Palomitas

: 10 niños y 14 niñas”. De la comunidad de jóvenes en común irán 110: 66 hombres y 43 mujeres. Del equipo de coordinación, 27: 7 mujeres y 20 hombres, así como 39 de Milicia: 16 milicianos y 23 milicianas.




El subcomandante Moises apuntó “nos hemos reunido toda la delegación para prepararnos bien y llevarles una buena palabra de aliento y apoyo. Muchos y muchas de nosotros y nosotras y nosotroas no sabemos bien la castilla. Nuestras lenguas madres son de raíz maya. Entonces tenemos que preparar también quién traduce.  Y corregir hasta donde podemos para que no salga torcida nuestra palabra”.




El comunicado fue acompañado por un video en el que se observa cómo en un campo, más decenas de zapatistas corren en bola detrás de un balón, mientras cientos observan a la orilla. El pie del video es: “La delegación en la Gira Por la Vida-Capítulo México, practicando la variante de fútbol conocida como ‘Fut en Común’ o ‘fut en bola’. Ningún balón sufrió daño alguno. De los jugadores pues… vean el video”.




Esta vez, la agenda se enfoca de manera exclusiva en las familias de personas desaparecidas. El itinerario de actividades, encuentros de escucha y jornadas de acompañamiento ciudadano en 

zonas como la región forestal del Ajusco

 se ajustará de manera estricta a los requerimientos de las buscadoras.




La comandancia del EZLN enfatizó que la movilización evitará confrontaciones con la población urbana trabajadora y rechazó propuestas enfocadas a realizar bloqueos viales, argumentando que restan legitimidad a las causas sociales. También se descartó utilizar en enero el 

Zócalo de la Ciudad de México

, previendo la saturación de eventos oficiales de la jefatura de gobierno y se optó por celebraciones comunitarias y dislocadas en las inmediaciones de la Casa de los Pueblos.




Durante la sesión informativa celebrada el pasado fin de semana, en la que participaron organizaciones como el 

Centro de Derechos Humanos Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Frayba)

, acordaron la recopilación y resguardo de los datos de las personas buscadoras asistentes. “Para evitar filtraciones y garantizar la seguridad de los familiares”, se diseñó un sistema de registro basado en 

software

 libre y privacidad informática, rechazando explícitamente el uso de herramientas de 

Inteligencia Artificial

.

title: Jornada de lucha frente al Congreso del colectivo de discapacidad, jubilados y movimientos sociales
content:
El miércoles 21, colectivos de la discapacidad, jubilados y movimientos sociales se concentraron frente al Congreso de la Nación en el marco de una mega-sesión donde el Gobierno buscaba imponer su agenda. Camioneros y la Bancaria acompañaron con ollas populares y mate cocido, mientras el Frente de Lucha Piquetero se sumó tras marchar a Desarrollo Social por salario para las cocineras de comedores populares.




El saldo legislativo fue la media sanción de una Ley de Fortalecimiento del Sistema de Discapacidad, que contiene parte del contenido de la Emergencia en Discapacidad, y la restitución de la Ley de Tierras con la eliminación de un artículo del DNU 70/2023. Pero, también la aprobación de la degradación de la Ley de Expropiaciones para blindar las privatizaciones y los desalojos exprés, los dos puntos del proyecto de Sturzenegger -denominado “Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada”- que sobrevivieron 

a su paso por el Senado

 el 

6 de agosto pasado

.

El miércoles 21 fue una nueva jornada de lucha frente al Congreso de la Nación de colectivos de la discapacidad, jubilados y jubiladas y movimientos sociales, en el marco de una mega-sesión donde el Gobierno nacional pretendía imponer su agenda legislativa.




En horas de la mañana, el colectivo de la discapacidad se hizo presente en el Congreso, reforzando sus reclamos por las pensiones y las prestaciones de salud. La persistencia de esa lucha tuvo como resultado que la Cámara de Diputados de la Nación diera media sanción en la jornada al proyecto de Ley de Fortalecimiento del Sistema de Discapacidad.




Desde el mediodía, los jubilados y las jubiladas se hicieron presentes como todas las semanas, mientras que el gremio de Camioneros acompañó con cuatro ollas populares de fideos con pollo y la Bancaria aportó su ya clásico mate cocido con tortas fritas.







https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Eduardo-Belliboni.mp4




Eduardo Belliboni. Video: Indymedia Argentina




Durante la protesta se acercaron las columnas del Frente de Lucha piquetera, que previamente marcharon al Ministerio de Desarrollo Social. Eduardo Belliboni, dirigente del Polo Obrero, contó que las organizaciones piqueteras y movimientos sociales reclamaron ante el Ministerio de Desarrollo Social “el salario que corresponde a las compañeras cocineras, a las compañeras que hacen los merenderos, que trabajan socialmente en los barrios y que han tenido el golpe de que les sacaran el Volver al Trabajo”.




“Necesitamos ese reconocimiento de un salario que les permita a las compañeras desarrollar esa tarea como corresponde, con el salario que les corresponde. Estamos peleando aquí y en todo el país por ese reconocimiento, y ahora marchamos al Congreso a unirnos con los jubilados y con los compañeros discapacitados que están peleando para que no se caiga la Ley de Emergencia en Discapacidad, que el gobierno de Milei quiere dar de baja, dando muestras una vez más de su crueldad”, agregó.

La Ley de Tierras en “Inviolabilidad”




Otro logro en el Congreso para los intereses populares fue la restitución de la Ley de Tierras. Allí el oficialismo de la Cámara baja tuvo que ceder y ratificar en el proyecto la Ley de Tierras y la eliminación de un artículo del Decreto de Necesidad y Urgencia (DNU) 70/2023 de Javier Milei. Por dos tercios, quedó blindado para su pase al Senado. Aunque hay serias dudas sobre un futuro veto presidencial que vuelva a voltear la Ley de Tierras.




Pero ese logro queda opacado porque la restitución de Tierras se hizo al incluirla en el infame proyecto de ley de Federico Sturzenegger, denominado “Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada”. Es el proyecto que generó una gran movilización popular de rechazo, y una feroz represión, el pasado 6 de agosto ante el Congreso de la Nación.

Tras esa jornada de lucha, el proyecto de Sturzenegger había quedado mutilado de sus capítulos de Extranjerización de Tierras y también, de Manejo del Fuego, dos segmentos orientados a beneficiar los intereses de grandes empresas foráneas, particularmente de Estados Unidos, Reino Unido e Israel. Y además había quedado congelado, sin fecha de tratamiento.




Tras ese traspié del gobierno, la Corte Suprema tomó la posta y suspendió con una argucia técnica la vigencia de la Ley de Tierras, dando de baja una cautelar contra el DNU 70/23. Entonces, la oposición tomó impulso para derogar ese mega-DNU, pilar de las políticas económicas de Milei, lo que generó un estado de pánico en el gobierno de ultraderecha.




Para desactivar esa iniciativa, el oficialismo incluyó la restitución de la Ley de Tierras -en su sentido contrario al original- en el proyecto de Sturzenegger, dándole una excusa a la oposición amigable y restando votos a la ofensiva contra el DNU 70/23.




El problema es que la aprobación de la restitución de la Ley de Tierras terminó operando como Caballo de Troya para que pasen por Diputados los dos puntos sobrevivientes de “Inviolabilidad”, la degradación de la Ley de Expropiaciones para blindar las privatizaciones y los desalojos exprés contra inquilinos y comunidades originarias.




Ahora, vuelve al Senado.

title: Über 20 LKW-Fahrer aus Belarus für polnische Spedition MBC streikten bei Venlo erfolgreich für ausstehende Löhne der Warschauer Leihfirma „Super Job“
content:
„

Rund 25 Lkw-Gespanne des polnischen Transportunternehmens MBC Trans stehen im Zusammenhang mit einem Streit über mutmaßlich ausstehende Lohnzahlungen still. Die Forderungen der Fahrer belaufen sich nach deren Angaben auf rund 150.000 Euro. Die Protestaktion begann in Deutschland und verlagerte sich anschließend in die Niederlande, wo sich überwiegend belarussische Fahrer am Truckstop Venlo aufhalten. (…) Mit dem Konflikt befassen sich auch die niederländische Gewerkschaft FNV und nach Angaben aus dem Umfeld der Fahrer die Stiftung Road Transport Due Diligence (RTDD)..

.“ 

Artikel von Agnieszka Kulikowska-Wielgus vom 23.10.2026 in Trans.info

 

 („25 Lkw in den Niederlanden blockiert. Im Hintergrund: ein polnischer Frachtführer und ein Streit um 150.000 Euro“) – siehe mehr Informationen aus der Recherche von chefduzen.de zum nun erfolgreich abgeschlossenen Streik:







Informationen aus der Recherche von chefduzen.de


Gerüchte über einen wilden Streik migrantischer LKW-Fahrer auf dem Rastplatz Venlose Heide in der Nähe der deutsch-niederländischen Grenze wurden von einem Gewerkschafter der niederländischen FNV bestätigt.


Die Fahrer, die nun auf der niederländischen Seite stehen, sind für das polnische Transportunternehmen MBC unterwegs.


Die Gewerkschaft FNV wurde am Montag, dem 12.10. von zwei Quellen informiert, einmal von Fahrern und auch von der polnischen Leiharbeitsfirma mit dem Namen SuperJobs, dass die Fahrer sich im Streik befinden und man bat die Gewerkschaft um Hilfe. Es sei ungewöhlich, dass ein Arbeitgeber die Gewerkschaft in einer solchen Sache anschreibt. Die Gewerkschaft hat mit den Streikenden gesprochen, 22 Fahrer aus Belarus, die bestätigt haben, dass das polnische Transportunternehmen die Löhne nicht zahlt. Da aber die Fahrer bei dem Unternehmen nicht direkt angestellt waren, sondern bei der Leiharbeitsfirma, sollte angeblich letztere die Löhne zahlen… (siehe zur rechtlichen Lage die entsprechenden Ausführungen im o.g. Trans.info-Artikel)




Richard Vervoorn von der FNV-Stichting VNB:




„

Es ist natürlich ziemlich bemerkenswert, dass eine polnische Zeitarbeitsfirma die FNV kontaktiert, um uns mitzuteilen, dass die Fahrer faktisch streiken. Mitarbeiter der FNV-VNB besuchten den Standort, während russischsprachige Mitarbeiter der RTDD telefonische Interviews mit den Fahrern führten, um die Situation zu untersuchen. Darüber hinaus wurde Kontakt mit der Zeitarbeitsfirma und dem Transportunternehmen in Polen aufgenommen. Alle beteiligten Parteien stellten Informationen zur Verfügung.“




Die Untersuchung ergab, dass sämtliche Lkw Ladungen transportierten, die über LKW Walter organisiert worden waren, und dass die Fahrer Transporte für Unternehmen wie Heineken, Lidl, Hornbach, Volkswagen und Red Bull durchgeführt hatten. Anschließend informierte die RTDD mehrere Unternehmen über die Gründe, weshalb ihre Waren nicht zugestellt worden waren.




Aus den Interviews mit den Fahrern ging hervor, dass sie bei der polnischen Zeitarbeitsfirma Super Jobs beschäftigt und an die polnischen Transportunternehmen MBC Trans und MBC Development überlassen worden waren. Die Fahrer erklärten, dass sie nahezu ausschließlich in Westeuropa arbeiteten, in ihren Lkw-Kabinen lebten, die vereinbarten Löhne nicht erhielten und ihnen Unterlagen wie Lohnabrechnungen nicht ausgehändigt wurden.




Die vorgelegten Informationen zeigten, dass MBC die von Super Jobs ausgestellten Rechnungen bezahlt hatte, Super Job jedoch die Fahrer nicht entlohnt hatte. Darüber hinaus wurde deutlich, dass MBC und Super Jobs keine klaren Vereinbarungen hinsichtlich der Einhaltung der geltenden Gesetze und Vorschriften, einschließlich des europäischen Mobilitätspakets, getroffen hatten.




Die RTDD hat kürzlich einen Leitfaden für multinationale Unternehmen veröffentlicht, der ihnen dabei helfen soll, ihre Transportdienstleister zur Einhaltung der geltenden Gesetze und Vorschriften zu verpflichten und deren Einhaltung zu überprüfen. Abschnitt 3.7 (Seite 27) dieses Leitfadens befasst sich ausdrücklich mit dem Einsatz von Fahrern, die über Zeitarbeitsfirmen zur Verfügung gestellt werden:  Road Transport Due Diligence Compass – 

https://www.rtdd.org/compass/

 




In diesem Fall ist offensichtlich, dass LKW Walter nicht überprüft hat, ob MBC die geltenden Gesetze und Vorschriften einhielt. MBC wiederum traf unklare Vereinbarungen mit einer Zeitarbeitsfirma und übte keine ausreichende Kontrolle aus, um die Rechte der Fahrer zu gewährleisten. Dies gilt unabhängig davon, ob MBC sämtliche ausstehenden Rechnungen bezahlt hatte.




Der Lkw-Parkplatz in Venlo ist inzwischen wieder leer. Nach fast zwei Wochen Protest erhielten die Fahrer von MBC Zahlungen in Höhe von 100 Euro netto pro Tag, die ihnen direkt in ihren Lkw-Kabinen ausgezahlt wurden, während die Zeitarbeitsfirma Super Job spurlos verschwand.




Während des gesamten Protests übernahm die FNV eine vermittelnde Rolle. Die RTDD setzte unterdessen ihre Sachverhaltsaufklärung fort und informierte Unternehmen, deren Waren sich auf dem Parkplatz befanden, über die Hintergründe des Falls sowie darüber, wie sie zur Wiedergutmachung und zur Vermeidung vergleichbarer Situationen in Zukunft beitragen könnten.




Nach Kenntnis der FNV wurden inzwischen sämtliche Waren zugestellt. 

Keiner der betroffenen Fahrer wird seine Tätigkeit für eines der beteiligten Unternehmen fortsetzen

.

„




Siehe auch die 

Kurzinfo „Aktueller Wilder Streik“ bei chefduzen.de

 







Wir danken einem Leser des LabourNet, der uns auf den LKW-Streik auf dem Parkplatz Venlose Heide aufmerksam machte und allen Beteiligten für die tolle Zusammenarbeit!

title: 20 metre yükseklikten beton zemine düştü: İnşaat işçisi ağır yaralandı
content:
Kütahya'da inşaat halindeki bir binanın çatısında çalışan usta Hüseyin Karadaş, yaklaşık 20 metre yükseklikten beton zemine düşerek ağır yaralandı.

Olay, saat 17.30 sıralarında Dumlupınar Mahallesi Şehit Ömer Halisdemir Caddesi üzerinde meydana geldi. İnşaat halindeki binanın çatısında çalışan çatı ustası Hüseyin Karadaş, dengesini kaybederek yaklaşık 20 metre yükseklikten beton zemine düştü. Mesai arkadaşlarının ihbarı üzerine olay yerine sağlık ekipleri sevk edildi. Sağlık ekiplerinin olay yerindeki ilk müdahalesinin ardından ağır yaralı Karadaş, Kütahya Şehir Hastanesine kaldırıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Garsonların bıyık bırakmak için greve gittiği gün: Paris'in ünlü kafeleri kapandı
content:
Fotoğraf: Jean Pierre de Rosnay/Pexels

İsmail Cem Şimşek [email protected]

Fransa'nın başkenti Paris, 1907 yılında alışılmadık bir işçi mücadelesine sahne oldu. Kentin ünlü kafelerinde çalışan garsonlar, bıyık bırakma hakkı başta olmak üzere daha iyi çalışma koşulları için greve gitti. 17 Nisan'da başlayan grev sırasında dönemin gözde mekanlarında servis durdu, müşteriler masalarda kaldı. İlk bakışta bir görünüm meselesi gibi görünen mücadele, aslında çalışma hayatındaki eşitsizliklere karşı verilen daha kapsamlı bir mücadelenin parçasıydı.

17 Nisan 1907 akşamı saat 18.30'da Paris'teki çok sayıda kafe ve restoranda çalışanlar önlüklerini çıkararak işlerini bıraktı. Garsonlar, servis tepsilerini bir kenara koydu ve işyerlerini terk etti.

Dönemin en tanınmış mekanları arasında yer alan Café de la Paix ve Café Riche de grevden etkilenen işletmeler arasındaydı. Bazı işletmelerde sandalyeler masaların üzerine kaldırıldı, teraslar boşaltıldı ve ışıklar söndürüldü.

Müşteriler için beklenmedik olan bu eylem, kısa sürede kent gündeminin önemli başlıklarından birine dönüştü. Grev, yalnızca hizmet sektöründe yaşanan bir iş bırakma eylemi değildi; çalışanların işverenlerin dayattığı kurallara karşı ortak hareket etmesinin de dikkat çekici bir örneğiydi.

Bugün kişisel bakım tercihi olarak görülen bıyık, 20. yüzyılın başlarında Fransa'da toplumsal statünün işaretlerinden biri olarak kabul ediliyordu.

Dönemin toplumsal anlayışında bıyık, özellikle askerler, aristokratlar ve üst sınıflarla özdeşleştiriliyordu. Buna karşılık ev hizmetlerinde çalışanların ve garsonların tıraşlı olması bekleniyordu.

Garsonların görünümü, patronların çalışanlar üzerindeki denetiminin bir parçasıydı. Müşterilere hizmet eden personelin nasıl giyineceği, nasıl görüneceği ve nasıl davranacağı büyük ölçüde işletme sahiplerinin belirlediği kurallara bağlıydı.

Bu nedenle bıyık bırakma hakkı, çalışanların kendi bedenleri ve görünümleri üzerinde söz sahibi olabilmesi anlamına da geliyordu.

Grevcilerin talepleri arasında bıyık bırakma özgürlüğünün bulunması, dönemin bazı gazetelerinde alay konusu oldu. Ancak çalışanlar açısından mesele, kişisel tercihin ötesinde bir saygınlık ve eşitlik sorunuydu.

Parisli garsonların mücadelesini yalnızca bıyık bırakma hakkına indirgemek, hareketin tarihsel önemini gözden kaçırmak anlamına geliyor.

Grevciler, haftada bir gün izin yapabilmek, asgari ücret uygulamasının getirilmesi ve çalışma koşullarının iyileştirilmesi gibi talepleri gündeme taşıdı. Çalışanlardan kırılan bardak ve tabaklar için yapılan kesintilere son verilmesi de mücadelede öne çıkan başlıklardan biriydi.

Dönemin hizmet sektöründe çalışanlar, uzun çalışma saatleri ve iş güvencesinin zayıflığı gibi sorunlarla karşı karşıyaydı. Bahşiş sistemi de ücret ilişkilerinin önemli bir parçasını oluşturuyordu.

Bu koşullarda garsonların örgütlü biçimde iş bırakması, çalışma hayatında söz sahibi olma arayışının bir ifadesiydi.

Nitekim tarih araştırmaları, Paris'teki garson örgütlerinin 1880'lerin sonlarından Birinci Dünya Savaşı'na kadar çalışma saatlerinin sınırlandırılması, haftalık izin, sabit ücret ve iş bulma aracılarının yarattığı mali yüklerin kaldırılması gibi talepleri gündeme getirdiğini ortaya koyuyor.

Grev, işletme sahipleri ile çalışanlar arasındaki gerilimi görünür hale getirdi. Bazı patronlar, garsonların bıyık bırakmasına ve çalışma koşullarının değiştirilmesine karşı çıktı.

Dönemin basınında grevcilerin taleplerini küçümseyen yorumlar yayımlandı. İşçilerin daha iyi ücret ve izin istemesi kadar, kişisel görünümleri üzerinde söz sahibi olma talepleri de tartışma konusu oldu.

Buna rağmen grev, hizmet sektöründeki çalışanların taleplerinin kamuoyunda konuşulmasını sağladı. Çalışanların örgütlenmesi ve ortak hareket etmesi, işverenlerin çalışma koşulları üzerindeki belirleyici gücünü sorgulayan bir mücadeleye dönüştü.

Grev sırasında yaşananlar, işçi mücadelelerinin yalnızca fabrikalarda ve ağır sanayi işletmelerinde ortaya çıkmadığını da gösteriyordu. Kafeler, restoranlar ve diğer hizmet işletmeleri de ücret, izin ve çalışma koşulları üzerine verilen mücadelelerin alanı olabiliyordu.

Nisan 1907'de başlayan grev, mayıs ayının ilk günlerine kadar devam etti. Tarihsel kaynaklarda grevcilerin sayısına ilişkin farklı bilgiler yer alırken hareketin farklı işletmelere yayıldığı ve sürecin aşamalı biçimde ilerlediği aktarılıyor.

4 Mayıs 1907'de sonuçlanan mücadele sonunda Parisli garsonlar bıyık bırakma hakkını elde etti. Ancak hareketin bütün talepleri karşılanmadı.

Bıyık yasağının aşılması, grevin en görünür kazanımı oldu. Bununla birlikte haftalık izin, ücret ve çalışma koşulları gibi meseleler işçi hareketinin gündeminde kalmayı sürdürdü.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Zonguldak’taki maden patlaması: 3 işçi toprağa verildi, 3 kişi tutuklandı
content:
Zonguldak’ta 3 işçinin yaşamını yitirdiği madendeki metan gazı birikmesi sonucu yaşanan patlamada yaşamını yitiren 3 işçi toprağa verildi. Gözaltına alınan işletme sahibi ile iş sağlığı ve güvenliği uzmanı ve maden mühendisi ise tutuklandı.

Zonguldak’ın Kilimli ilçesine bağlı Gelik beldesinin Dereiçi mevkiinde, Demir Madencilik AŞ’ye ait maden ocağında dün saat 10.00 sıralarında grizu patlaması meydana geldi. Olayda madende bulunan 8 işçiden 3’ü hayatını kaybetti. 2’si ağır, 5 yaralı ise ambulansla Zonguldak Atatürk Devlet Hastanesine kaldırılarak tedaviye alındı.

Zonguldak Atatürk Devlet Hastanesi morgundan sabah saatlerinde alınan maden işçisi Cengizhan Bükrübaş’ın cenazesi, cenaze aracıyla Çaycuma ilçesinin Perşembe beldesi Muharremşah köyüne getirildi. Bükrübaş, daha sonra Muharremşah Camisi’nde kılınan cenaze namazının ardından gözyaşları arasında toprağa verildi. Bükrübaş'ın bekar olduğu, babası İsmail Bükrübaş'ın da aynı ocaktan emekli olduğu belirtildi.

İşçilerden Murat Kaya’nın cenazesi ise Saltuokova beldesine bağlı Sarmaşık köyü Kartoğlu Mahallesi’ne götürüldü. Murat Kaya, aile mezarlığına defnedildi.

İşçilerden 3 çocuk babası Recep Çolakoğlu (45) için de Alibüyük Mahallesi’nde cenaze töreni düzenlendi. Çolakoğlu mahalle mezarlığında son yolculuğuna uğurlandı.

Olayın ardadan işletme sahibi Mehmet Salih Demir, iş sağlığı ve güvenliği uzmanı Ercüment Yalçın ile maden mühendisi Yusuf Çavdar, gözaltına alındı. Jandarmadaki işlemlerinin ardından adliyeye sevk edilen 3 kişi, savcılık sorgularının ardından çıkarıldıkları sulh ceza hakimliğinde ‘Bilinçli taksirle öldürme ve yaralama’ suçundan tutuklandı.

İşletme müdürü Mustafa Kapanşahin hakkında ise yakalama kararı çıkarıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Randi Beers
title: Jimmy Bell – An Arctic trader
content:
Young Jimmy Bell stood 5’10” tall and weighed about 170 pounds when he joined the Hudson’s Bay Co. as a 19-year-old recruit in 1925. 




Two decades later his weight had more than doubled, by some reports reaching 350 pounds. The Inuit, whom he knew and loved, and who knew and loved him, called him Quinijuq – the fat man.




Bell was born in Cromdale, Scotland, the eldest son in a large family. He walked three miles to school and back each day during eight years of primary school and followed that with three years of higher education. 




Then Bell worked as a bookkeeper for a local garage for three years until he emigrated to Canada as a young fur trader, following in the footsteps of so many young Scots before him. 




Montreal, the city where he first set foot in Canada, was always dear to him. Much later, he decided that he would eventually retire there, but it was never to be.




That summer of 1925 he travelled on the Hudson’s Bay Company supply ship to Lake Harbour (now Kimmirut) where he was apprentice clerk for three years, before moving on to Frobisher Bay for two years in the same position. 




After a year’s furlough, Bell was posted for one year as manager at Payne Bay in northern Quebec, a post he described as the poorest-looking he had seen. He followed that with two years each again in Frobisher Bay and Lake Harbour. 
















After another year of furlough, Bell returned to Lake Harbour for another five years, before spending short periods at the Winnipeg Depot and Cross Lake, Man. Then he spent four years, from 1942 to 1946, as manager in Arctic Bay. 




After a short holiday, Bell returned for a fourth tour of duty at Lake Harbour, only a year this time, before transferring to Cape Dorset for his final year in the Arctic and his final year of life.




Bell loved Arctic Bay, the company’s most northerly post. He was a sociable man, a good cook and a gracious host. Visitors were always welcome, whether they be other traders, missionaries, policemen, or Inuit. He liked to eat, drink, play bridge, and tell stories. 




Yet one sketch of his life says, “Those he liked thought he was wonderful. Those who didn’t found him dour and reserved.”




Bell had an enormous appetite and it was said that he could eat eight to 10 pounds of seal meat at one sitting. There was a Department of Transport weather station in Arctic Bay and Bell got in the habit of visiting for Sunday supper, bringing “his huge bulk and fund of stories.”




All post managers were required to keep a daily journal and a monthly summary of their journals. For some, it was a sparse record of the comings and goings of the Inuit to the post to trade, usually with remarks on the weather. But Bell’s journals were more than that. 
















Rather than just a bare record of trading activities, he took time to write in detail about the visits of the Inuit and observances of nature. They were carefully written and showed a love of language. 




In May of 1944 he wrote, “The first snow-birds of the season were observed on the 10

th

, which is almost three weeks later than their first appearance last year. These hardy little birds must still find the Arctic nights rather chilly.” 




Bell showed the same care when writing about the Inuit. 




That same month, when Tonga died at Cape Cunningham, he wrote, “He was the oldest native in the territory and we believe the last of the ‘Angakoks’… [H]e was the last strong link with paganism. We think, however, that the old man’s brand of pagan religion was just as good as that taught by the Missionaries; at least Tonga was less deceitful than some of his brethren who have seen the ‘light.’”  




Such detail in a journal is all the more remarkable when one realizes that probably no one other than his district manager in Winnipeg would read his words at the time. 
















Bell’s Hudson’s Bay Company service record describes him as a “good reliable type,” and a “first class Eskimo trader.” One report called him a “permanent Arctic man,” but noted ominously that he was “dangerously obese.” 




Bell loved his drink. He spent Christmas Day 1933 at Frobisher Bay working, and wrote, “Christmas Day was spent in the store, where 83 foxes were traded. At night I celebrated Xmas by having a fire in the guardroom [sitting room] and having a better meal than usual. I also put up with the torture of a collar and tie, and toasted the health of absent friends in lime juice; not that it was necessary to do so, as I have three kinds of strong drink on the post, but there is no pleasure in drinking alone, although in company I can hold my own.” 




At Arctic Bay, he and his clerk hosted the staff of the Met station, as the weather station was called, for New Year’s dinner in 1944. 




“We had a first class meal,” Bell wrote, “which consisted of… mushroom soup, roast pork with apple sauce, carrots, peas, mashed potatoes, ice cream with strawberries, coffee and cake. Prior to the meal by way of appetizers the usual toasts were drunk in beer and ‘Nelson’s Blood.’” 




Nelson’s Blood was a euphemism for Lamb’s Navy rum. He also liked another cocktail of rum and port, a “smooth tasting concoction” that he called “thunder and lightning.” 




Bell also tended to the illnesses of the Inuit, pulling teeth and even amputating frozen fingers. 




Elsie Gillis, who spent a year in Arctic Bay as the wife of a weather observer, wrote of Bell, “When they [the Inuit] were in trouble, they came to him for help and he gave generously of his time, his skill, his food. Or whatever was needed to meet the emergency.”  




My next column will tell about how Bell became the ghost of Arctic Bay.




Taissumani is an occasional column that recalls events of historical interest. Kenn Harper is a historian and writer who lived in the Arctic for over 50 years. He is the author of 

Give Me Winter, Give Me Dogs: Knud Rasmussen and the Fifth Thule Expedition

, and 

Thou Shalt Do No Murder

, among other books. Feedback? Send your comments and questions to kennharper@hotmail.com.

author: Unknown
title: DEM Parti’den “Ekmek, Barış ve Adalet” kampanyası
content:
DEM Parti Sancaktepe İlçe Örgütü binasında yapılan toplantıya DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tülay Hatimoğulları, DEM Parti İstanbul İl Eşbaşkanı Arife Çınar, İstanbul Milletvekili Kezban Konukçu ve çok sayıda kişi katıldı.




Mezopotamya Ajansı’nın (MA) haberine göre, Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti) Emek Komisyonu, “Ekmek, Barış ve Adalet” kampanyasını İstanbul’un Sancaktepe ilçesinde düzenlenen basın toplantısıyla başlattı.




Kampanyanın başlangıcını Sancaktepe’den verdiklerini söyleyen Hatimoğulları, Türkiye’nin dört bir yanındaki işçilerin benzer sorunlarla karşı karşıya olduğunu belirtti.




Türkiye’de yoksulluğun derinleştiğini söyleyen Hatimoğulları, kamu emekçilerinin de geçim sıkıntısı yaşadığını ifade etti. İki ailenin birleşerek ev tutmak zorunda kaldığını, insanların bayat ekmek kuyruklarına girdiğini ve bazı ailelerin çocuklarına yemek hazırlayabilmek için gün sonunda satılmayan sebze ve meyveleri beklediğini anlattı.




Hatimoğulları, “50 milyon insan yoksulluk sınırının altında. Bıçak kemiği deldi geçti ve şimdi ilikte” dedi.




“Açlık bizim kaderimiz değil”




Türkiye’deki fon vurgunu iddialarına da değinen Hatimoğulları, yaşananları Türkiye tarihinde benzeri görülmemiş bir olay olarak nitelendirdi. Fon meselesine karşı tepki gösterdiklerini söyleyen Hatimoğulları, şöyle konuştu:




“Açlık bizim kaderimiz değil. Bu ülkenin varlıkları, kaynakları, ülkedeki kimsenin aç kalmasına izin vermeyecek kadar yeterli. Fon vurgunundan sonra rakamlar birbirleriyle karıştı. Bu bir çete faaliyetidir, hırsızlıktır. Fon meselesine karşı en büyük tepkiyi koyan partiyiz. Halkımızın ekmeğini, alın terini sonuna kadar savunacağız.”




Fon vurgunu iddialarında iktidar çevrelerinin, siyasetçilerin ve yargının da rolü olduğunu öne süren Hatimoğulları, ülkede yoksulluğun ve açlığın derinleştiğini söyledi.




Esnaf ziyareti yapıldı




Basın toplantısının ardından Tülay Hatimoğulları ve DEM Partili milletvekilleri Sancaktepe’de esnaf ziyareti gerçekleştirdi. Ziyaretlerde yurttaşlarla bir araya gelen parti temsilcileri, geçim sıkıntısı başta olmak üzere yaşanan sorunları dinledi ve “Ekmek, Barış ve Adalet” kampanyasını anlattı.




(EMK)

author: Unknown
title: Van’da gazetecilerden basın özgürlüğü çağrısı: “Artık yeter, nefes alamıyoruz!”
content:
Van’da gazeteciler, basın özgürlüğüne yönelik baskılara karşı Türkiye genelinde düzenlenen eş zamanlı eylemler kapsamında bir araya geldi. “Artık Yeter! Nefes Alamıyoruz!” başlığıyla yapılan açıklamada, gazeteciliğin suç sayılmasına, gazetecilerin tutuklanmasına, medya kuruluşlarına yönelik müdahalelere ve sansüre tepki gösterildi.




Dicle Fırat Gazeteciler Derneği (DFG) adına Zeynep Turgut açıklamanın Kürtçesini, İHAMED adına Ruşen Takva ise Türkçesini okudu. Açıklamada, basın özgürlüğünün yalnızca gazetecilerin değil, toplumun tamamının meselesi olduğu vurgulandı.




Tutuklu gazetecilerden dayanışma mesajı




Eylemde, tutuklu gazeteciler Derya Okatan ve Fatih Ergin’in cezaevlerinden gönderdiği mektuplar da okundu.




Bakırköy Cezaevi’nde tutuklu bulunan Derya Okatan’ın mektubunu DFG adına Rabia Önver okudu. Tutukluluğunun üçüncü haftasını geride bıraktığını belirten Okatan, yaşanan gelişmelerin basının ağır bir baskı altında olduğunu gösterdiğini söyledi.




Okatan, tutuklanmasının ardından Halk TV’ye kayyım atanmasını, gazeteciler Murat Ağırel ve İsmail Arı’nın tutuklanmasını hatırlattı. Cezaevi koşulları nedeniyle yaşanan gelişmelerin tamamını takip edemediğini belirten Okatan, meslek örgütlerinin yürüttüğü mücadeleye dikkat çekti.




Dışarıda olması hâlinde meslektaşlarıyla birlikte eylemde yer alacağını söyleyen Okatan, aynı koğuşta kaldığı gazeteci Nadiye Gürbüz’le birlikte tutuklu gazetecilerin sesini duyuran meslektaşlarına selam gönderdi ve dayanışma gösterenlere teşekkür etti.




Fatih Ergin: Gazetecilere sahip çıkmak, haber alma hakkına sahip çıkmaktır




Silivri Cezaevi’nde tutuklu bulunan gazeteci-yazar Fatih Ergin’in mektubunu İHAMED adına Kadir Cesur okudu.




22 Ekim 2026 tarihli mektubunda Ergin, gazetecilerin insanların hakikatle bağını kesmek amacıyla hapse atıldığını söyledi. Tutukluluklarının halkın haber alma hakkını savunmalarıyla ilgili olduğunu belirten Ergin, gazetecilerle dayanışmanın aynı zamanda toplumun haber alma hakkını savunmak anlamına geldiğini vurguladı.




Ergin, kendisine destek veren ve dayanışma gösteren yurttaşlara selamlarını iletti.




“Gazetecilik halkın yanında olmaktır”




Ortak açıklamada, gazeteciliğin iktidarların, siyasetçilerin ya da sermaye çevrelerinin değil, halkın yanında durması gerektiği belirtildi. İşçilerin hak arayışını, kadınlara yönelik şiddeti, gençlerin sorunlarını ve toplumsal eşitsizlikleri haberleştirmenin gazeteciliğin kamusal sorumluluğu olduğu ifade edildi.




Gazetecilerin yaptıkları haberler nedeniyle gözaltına alınması, tutuklanması, ev hapsine mahkûm edilmesi ya da mesleklerini sürdüremez hâle getirilmesinin toplumun gerçeklere ulaşma hakkını da hedef aldığı kaydedildi.




Açıklamada, Kürt gazetecilere yönelik baskılara ve muhalif, bağımsız medya kuruluşlarının karşılaştığı engellere de dikkat çekildi. Gazeteciler arasındaki dayanışmanın siyasi görüş, kimlik, dil veya çalışılan kurum üzerinden bölünmemesi gerektiği vurgulandı.




Gazeteciler altı temel talebini sıraladı




Basın meslek örgütleri ve gazeteciler, açıklamada altı temel talep dile getirdi:







Tutuklu gazeteciler serbest bırakılsın.




Gazetecilik faaliyetleri üzerindeki yargısal baskılar sona ersin.




Medya kuruluşlarına yönelik kayyım uygulamalarına son verilsin.




Hukuka aykırı erişim engelleri kaldırılsın.




Kamu reklam ve ilanları adil ve eşit dağıtılsın.




Anayasal güvence altındaki basın özgürlüğüne yönelik müdahaleler son bulsun.







Gazeteciler, mesleklerini özgürce sürdürebilmeleri ve toplumun haber alma hakkının korunması için toplumun bütün kesimlerine dayanışma çağrısı yaptı.




Eylem, “Özgür basın yoksa özgür toplum yoktur” mesajıyla sona erdi.




(EMK)

author: Εκδηλώσεις
title: «Όταν οι αγώνες για ζωή και αξιοπρέπεια νικούν»
content:
Ζωντανή μετάδοση της εκδήλωσης της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών στο Πάντειο, Σάββατο 24/10/2026.




Την πρώτη μέρα της εκδήλωσης, στο πλαίσιο ενός πρώτου απολογισμού, θα παρουσιαστεί από πλευράς της Κοινότητας η επιλογή του συγκεκριμένου αγώνα υπό τις συγκεκριμένες συνθήκες, οι πυλώνες πάνω στους οποίους οικοδομήθηκε, οι μέθοδοι και τα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήθηκαν, με αιχμή την απεργίας πείνας ως βασικό επαναστατικό μέσο για την επίτευξη της νίκης, καθώς επίσης και τα πρώτα συμπεράσματα και η προοπτική που ανοίγεται για το επόμενο διάστημα. Θα ακολουθήσουν διευκρινιστικές ερωτήσεις από τους παρευρισκόμενους, που θα απαντηθούν από την Κοινότητα, προκειμένου να προετοιμαστεί το έδαφος για την επόμενη ημέρα της εκδήλωσης.

author: Randi Beers
title: Inuit Child First Initiative needs to be universal
content:
It was as simple as it was revolutionary.




In 2023, 

somebody

 with the non-profit Indigenous Kids Network had the idea to help Clyde River apply for community-wide food vouchers, good for $500 per month per child under the age of 18, with an extra $250 per month allocated to children under four for needs such as diapers or formula.




Twenty-four of Nunavut’s 25 communities organized applications through the Inuit Child First Initiative. Once approved, Inuit families could declare how many children they had and receive cards loaded with money that they could use at their local grocers.




The Inuit Child First Initiative Hamlet Food Voucher program wasn’t really a program. It was an innovative way of using a pot of money meant to ensure Inuit children have equal access to health, social and education support.




Over the two years it was in place, the federal government 

spent $89.5 million

 on vouchers that helped feed 15,000 Inuit children.




The effects were unequivocal. Parents who 

reported

 they were eating one meal a day before the food vouchers were no longer skipping meals so their children could eat. Nunavut health-care workers 

noticed

 a “night-and-day” change, with fewer children seeing doctors for nutrition-related issues. Teachers said students were more alert at school and their 

grades improved

.




The food voucher program was staunched in early 2025 and Indigenous Services Canada rolled out stricter regulations for group requests.
















These policy changes are also affecting the number of student support assistants in Nunavut schools this year, because Inuit Child First Initiative no longer approves requests for student support assistance, except for exceptional needs, again on a case-by-case basis.




Classrooms 

look very different

 this year as a result, says Nunavut Teachers’ Association president Justin Matchett, with students not getting support and teachers struggling with stress and burnout.




Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty has been 

working

 on a new-and-improved Inuit Child First Initiative for the past year. Hopefully she’s considering a more universal approach to the program.




The spirit and principle of Inuit Child First Initiative is to provide a safety net for Inuit children. Making it easy for organizations, schools and hamlets to get approval for group applications makes that safety net stronger and reduces the risk that individual families won’t walk away, 

frustrated

 because of what at least one parent has described as an “inflexible, intrusive” application process that is “incompatible with life in Nunavut.”




Does a universal approach to Inuit Child First Initiative open the door for people to benefit from a program that might not be intended for them, such as more well-off families accessing food vouchers they may not need? Did the food voucher program contribute to food inflation in Nunavut? These were common criticisms.




Abuse of open-ended programs is, of course, possible.
















But Inuit Child First Initiative needs to meet Nunavummiut where they are. And laborious, extensive applications that require documentation and endorsements are not feasible for many families.




We know the food voucher program and other group-focused initiatives led to healthier Inuit children.




Reinstating the old Inuit Child First Initiative won’t fix everything.




But it would be a grievous mistake to, in the name of saving a little money now, forgo 

positive impacts

 that lead to better health outcomes — and money saved down the line.

title: YJA Star: We are the inheritors of Bêrîtan’s legacy
content:
The Central Headquarters Command of the Free Women’s Troops (YJA Star) commemorated guerrilla commander Gülnaz Karataş, known by her nom de guerre Bêrîtan Hêvî, highlighting her significance for the Kurdish women’s freedom movement on the 34th anniversary of her death. In a statement on Saturday, YJA Star Command paid tribute to Bêrîtan Hêvî’s resistance against surrender during the Southern War of 1992, describing her political and military legacy as one of the foundations of Kurdish women’s autonomous organization.




Bêrîtan Hêvî was born in 1971 in Bingöl, North Kurdistan, and died on October 25, 1992, in the Xakurke region of South Kurdistan. During clashes between PKK guerrillas and Peshmerga forces allied with the Turkish army, she was surrounded by members of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). She refused to surrender, fought until her last bullet, destroyed her weapon, and jumped from a cliff to avoid capture.




Her death became an important reference point in the development of autonomous women’s structures within the guerrilla movement. On November 1, 1993, the establishment of a women’s army was announced. YJA Star sees itself as continuing this development and the tradition of resistance among Kurdish women, which it traces from Dersim to the present day.




The full statement by the YJA Star Central Headquarters Command reads as follows:




“Bêrîtan embodies the reality of women who organize and liberate themselves, establish their own identity, and express it through their lives. She represents women’s struggle for their existence within the Kurdish freedom movement, the lived and realized reality of women who lead a people’s struggle for freedom, and their stance against subjugation.




The fact that the spirit of resistance of the women who defied subjugation during the Dersim massacre and threw themselves from cliffs took shape once again in Bêrîtan represents the continuity of a tradition of resistance. The spirit of Besê and the women of Dersim found its expression in Bêrîtan and came to life anew in the struggle of the present day.




Bêrîtan represents the fighting woman who resisted surrender in the 1992 war against reactionary Kurdish collaborationism and whose resistance unfolded at the edge of a precipice. Through her determined stance against collaboration and betrayal, she also laid a foundation, as a woman, for the unity and collective action of the Kurdish people.




“Fight, my rose, fight with determination”




Through her ideological awareness, Bêrîtan developed a strong stance. She acquired strategic and tactical skills, advanced as a commander, and put her convictions into practice. In doing so, she embodied the standards, principles, and political line of the fighting woman.




With the words, 

“Fight, my rose, fight with determination. By fighting, we liberate ourselves; by liberating ourselves, we become beautiful; and the more beautiful we become, the more we are loved,”

she expressed the holistic development of the individual and the path of struggle. Through her stance and actions, she became a guiding figure in the women’s freedom movement. She demonstrated once again that the establishment of a women’s army and the struggle cannot be reduced to armed resistance alone, but require a conscious stance and a profound understanding of one’s own reality.




Through her life, she transformed the aesthetics of struggle, the ethics of resistance, and the standards and principles of love into a manifesto. Bêrîtan inscribed her life and struggle into history, verse by verse. She gave voice once again, at the very edge of the precipices, to the existence of women who were meant to be buried in history and condemned to silence in the depths of the abyss. From there, she carried the cry of women’s resistance to all women. With the words, 

“The revolution demands a stormy personality,”

 she continually recreated herself through resistance against backward traditions and collaborationism. With every bullet she fired and every chain of enslavement she shattered, she unleashed new storms. Like a poem, she inscribed the truth of women’s resistance into history and gave it a distinct identity.




A legacy for the women’s freedom movement




Through her struggle, Bêrîtan not only wrote the manifesto of her own time. She also gave new meaning to the legacy of the women whose heritage she had inherited—the Besês. She left future generations the consciousness of a commander and a vision of resistance intended to give them the courage to rewrite the as-yet-unwritten history of women’s liberation. As YJA Star, we are today the organized successors of the line of struggle and the understanding of leadership embodied by martyr Bêrîtan. Every fighter in the women’s freedom movement who takes her manifesto as a guiding principle is committed to carrying forward this legacy and putting it into practice.




Throughout the course of the struggle, this culture of struggle and resistance has given rise to hundreds more Bêrîtans. Her legacy has multiplied and been passed down to future generations. The legacy embodied by Bêrîtan has grown through years of struggle in the mountains and cities, finding renewed expression in martyr Axîn Cûdî, martyr Sema, and hundreds of other women and men of the freedom movement.




We are the inheritors of Bêrîtan’s legacy




Chairman Rêber Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] stated that the greatest response to the legacy of the martyrs is to expand the struggle and recreate oneself in the awareness of their stance. On this basis, and with the aim of further developing the tradition of resistance embodied by martyr Bêrîtan and honoring the legacy of the martyrs, he announced the establishment of an autonomous women’s army on November 1, 1993. As YJA Star forces who follow Bêrîtan’s path and inherit her legacy, we declare that we will connect the women’s liberation movement with the truth she embodied in every moment of life and struggle.”

title: Democratic Integration Conference in Zurich discusses democratic transformation, equal coexistence
content:
The Kurdish Social Research Association (Akademî Kurd) is holding a conference titled “Democratic Integration” in Zurich, Switzerland. The conference, taking place at the Kirchgemeindehaus, is examining the concept of democratic integration from various perspectives within the framework of LAbdullah Öcalan’s Manifesto for a Democratic Communal Society.




The conference, attended by academics, politicians, legal experts, and researchers, focuses on the theoretical foundations of democratic integration as well as its social, political, and cultural dimensions. Legal reforms necessary for a democratic resolution of the Kurdish question, equal citizenship, the democratic republic, and the democratic communal economy are also among the main topics of discussion.




Dilan Çetinkaya: The process places significant responsibilities on all of us




The conference began with a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs of the revolutionary struggle, followed by an opening speech delivered by Dilan Çetinkaya, Co-Chair of the Democratic Kurdish Council of Switzerland (CDK-S).




Dilan Çetinkaya began her speech by commemorating the martyrs of the Kurdish Freedom Struggle and drew attention to the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom spanning more than half a century. Stating that this struggle has brought significant gains to the Kurdish people, Çetinkaya emphasized the historical importance of the peace and democratic society process initiated under the leadership of Abdullah Öcalan.




Çetinkaya stated that the ongoing process places significant responsibilities not only on political actors but also on all segments of society, stressing that democratic transformation must be reflected in every aspect of life. “Change must not remain merely in words; it must take place in every sphere. We must thoroughly understand Leader Öcalan’s concept of democratic integration and carry out our reconstruction accordingly,” she said.




Veysi Aktaş: Democratic integration is based on the democratic transformation of all peoples




Following the opening speech, the conference proceeded to its first session, titled “The conceptual and theoretical framework of democratic integration.” Moderated by Gülistan Arslan, the session featured Kurdish politician Veysi Aktaş and sociologist, academic, and author Nazan Üstündağ as speakers.




Veysi Aktaş began by thanking Akademî Kurd for organizing the conference. Stating that democratic integration is one of the fundamental concepts of the peace and democratic society process, Aktaş said that the concept points not only to the resolution of existing problems but also to the building of a democratic future in which peoples can live together in equality and freedom.




Aktaş explained that democratic integration is based on different identities and social groups creating a shared democratic life while preserving their distinct identities. “Democratic integration is a concept based on the democratic transformation of all peoples, not just the Kurds. It is founded on coexistence with differences, equality, equal negotiation as a method, and democratic participation,” he said.




Emphasizing that democratic integration does not mean assimilation or the elimination of differences, Aktaş stated that the concept is fundamentally based on the recognition of different identities, social pluralism, and democratic participation. In this respect, he explained that democratic integration entails not only the recognition of the political and social rights of Kurds but also the restructuring of society as a whole on a democratic basis.




‘The fundamental principle is equal citizenship’




Remarking that democratic integration rests on several fundamental principles, Aktaş said that equal citizenship is foremost among them. He emphasized that equal citizenship cannot be understood merely as formal equality before the law, highlighting the importance of enabling different identities and social groups to participate in political and social life while preserving their distinct characteristics.




Aktaş stated that democratic integration is directly linked to the perspective of a democratic republic and stressed the need to establish legal guarantees to ensure that democratic transformation becomes lasting.




“Democratic integration is also based on the Democratic Republic. Achieving this is possible through the implementation of a legal process. Certain legal reforms are necessary for it to become a reality in everyday life,” he said.




Stating that discussing democratic integration solely at the theoretical level would not be sufficient, Aktaş emphasized the importance of safeguarding principles such as equal citizenship, democratic participation, and the recognition of different identities through concrete legal and political arrangements.




‘The process is not limited to laying down arms’




Aktaş also addressed the question of why the concept of democratic integration was chosen, stating that this approach is important for understanding the scope of the peace and democratic society process.




Emphasizing that the process cannot be viewed as limited to laying down arms or ending armed conflicts, Veysi Aktaş explained that democratic integration also encompasses the participation of Kurds in political life with their own identity, language, and social existence.




In this context, Aktaş stated that democratic integration aims to create the conditions for Kurds to pursue their democratic struggle within the existing political and social system without abandoning their identities, adding that this also requires the democratic transformation of both the state and society.




Nazan Üstündağ: Kurds were forced to live as ‘smugglers’ in every sphere of life




Following Veysi Aktaş, sociologist, academic, and author Nazan Üstündağ took the floor, examining the concept of democratic integration through the historical experiences of the Kurdish people, their relationship with the state, and the discrimination they have faced in social life.




Üstündağ stated that the Kurdish people have historically faced various prohibitions, policies of denial, and discrimination in political, cultural, and social spheres, emphasizing that this situation has directly affected their daily lives and their relationship with the state.




Explaining that Kurds have often been forced to live outside the boundaries of the official system in order to exist with their own identities, Üstündağ described this historical condition using the term “smuggler.”




Nazan Üstündağ pointed out that the Kurdish people have faced various obstacles not only when crossing borders but also when speaking their language, preserving their culture, and expressing their political identity. The Kurds, she added, have been forced to live almost like “smugglers” in many spheres of life.




Üstündağ stated that one of the most important aspects of democratic integration is the creation of a social and political order in which Kurds no longer face such constraints simply to exist with their own identity. In this regard, she emphasized that democratic integration cannot be understood as the unconditional adaptation of Kurds to the existing order. Rather, she said, the essential issue is to create democratic conditions in which Kurds can live freely and equally while preserving their identities.




‘I understand democratic integration as a struggle against the state’




Nazan Üstündağ stated that democratic integration has become more important today than ever before, emphasizing that the concept should not be approached solely through legal reforms or political compromises.




She pointed out that democratic integration also entails redefining the relationship between the state and society, and cannot be considered independently of the democratic struggle. “I understand democratic integration as a struggle against the state,” Üstündağ said, adding that democratic integration should be viewed as a process involving the questioning of existing power relations and the expansion of society’s democratic rights. Highlighting the importance of democratic integration in overcoming the exclusion and discrimination historically experienced by Kurds, Üstündağ said, “In this context, democratic integration is linked not only to enabling Kurds to participate in public and political life with their own identity but also to the transformation of state-society relations on a democratic basis.”




The conference will continue with sessions featuring Syrian Presidential Advisor Mazlum Abdi, sociologist Engin Sustam from Paris 8 University, TJK-E (Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe) member Zîlan Diyar, DEM Party Central Executive Board member Derya Arslan, İmralı Delegation member and lawyer Özgür Erol, lawyer Hüsnü Yılmaz, researcher and economist Ahmet Pelda, and sociologist and anthropologist Neşe Özgen. The sessions will address the political, sociological, cultural, legal, and economic dimensions of democratic integration, as well as the democratic resolution of the Kurdish question.
