author: Chris Walker
title: Todd Blanche Won’t Rule Out DOJ Disruption of Midterm Elections Certification
content:
Seven in 10 Americans don’t believe President Donald Trump will accept the midterm results.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters on Thursday that he wouldn’t rule out the possibility of the Department of Justice (DOJ) refusing to allow states to certify their own election results in this year’s midterm races.

Blanche’s comments come as Americans are expressing deep skepticism that President Donald Trump will accept election outcomes if Republicans lose to Democrats.

According to the U.S. Constitution, states are the managers of elections, not the federal government. But the administration could attempt to dispute the election results by claiming widespread fraud had taken place, refusing to allow states to certify outcomes through extreme measures, including seizing ballots.

As Blanche was boarding a plane in Virginia, he was asked by reporters whether it was possible that the DOJ could disrupt the certification process after the midterms concluded. The attorney general said he wouldn’t rule out the idea.

“It is not DOJ’s intention to, and it’s never our intention to, improperly interfere with elections or the state confirmation process or certification process,” Blanche said, but added that he may feel compelled to do so in a “doomsday scenario.”

“To say that there’s no circumstances that we would ever do that …. of course, I’m not going to say that,” he elaborated.

The DOJ has already taken steps to purportedly root out fraud and ineligible voters in several states, despite evidence suggesting that claims of widespread fraud are unfounded.

There are reports that federal agents have started going door to door to search for supposed noncitizen voters, an action that could intimidate residents who are eligible to participate in the elections. The DOJ has also threatened state election officials, warning them of potential criminal prosecutions if they allow noncitizens to vote this November.

The administration’s claims have fallen apart under scrutiny — for example, a report the White House produced alleging that 24,000 noncitizens participated in the 2020 presidential election (which Trump lost) was deemed deeply flawed due to unusual methodology.

Polling has consistently demonstrated that Democrats are likely to win the House of Representatives in this year’s midterm races. The Democratic Party is also within reach of winning the Senate, some polls have suggested.

If Republicans lose to Democrats, most Americans have doubts that Trump will accept the results.

According to a Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll published this week, only 28 percent of voters said they were “confident” Trump would accept the results of the midterms. Meanwhile, 70 percent said they were “not confident” that he would.

Trump has already indicated that he will only accept the results if he deems them “honest,” saying as much back in February. If he doesn’t believe they are honest, then “something else has to happen,” he said.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Wir bleiben alle Friedrichshain
title: Protestkundgebung gegen Wohnraumzerstörung und Vertreibung in der Gürtelstraße 39-41
content:
Mehrere Jahre standen die beiden ehemaligen Hotels in der Gürtelstraße 39-41 leer. In den letzten Jahren sind dort Menschen eingezogen, die auf den überteuerten Berliner Wohnungsmarkt keine Chance gehabt hätten. Sie nannten das von ihnen besetzte Gebäude Hugo-Haus. Ende September wurden die Bewohner*innen mit einem großen Polizeiaufgebot auf die Straße gesetzt. Aber sie verschwanden nicht einfach. Direkt gegenüber dem


geräumten Haus errichteten sie ein Zeltdorf. So konnten sie zusammenbleiben und sich gegenseitig beim Leben auf der Straße unterstützen. Gleichzeitig konnten alle sehen, wie in der Gürtelstraße 39-41 Wohnraum vernichtet wird. Fenster und sanitäre Anlagen wurden herausgerissen, Mauern zerstört.Das Hugo-Dorf, wie die Bewohner*innen ihre Zeltstadt nannten, war ein im Straßenbild sichtbares Zeichen. In Berlin wird weiter Wohnraum vernichtet, werden weiter Menschen auf die Straße geworfen. Am 14. Oktober musste auch diese Zeltstadt verschwinden. Eine weitere Genehmigung hatten die zuständigen Ämter verweigert. So wurden die Bewohner*innen zum zweiten Mal innerhalb weniger Wochen vertrieben und zerstreut. Wir sehen es auch als große Schwäche, dass es nicht gelungen ist, mehr Druck von unten aufzubauen, damit die Bewohner*innen nicht vertrieben werden. Jahrelang wurde darüber diskutiert, ob es nicht an der Zeit wäre, wieder Häuser zu besetzen. Wo blieb dann die Unterstützung für die Besetzer*innen in der Gürtelstraße? Diese Frage stellen wir auch selbstkritisch an uns. Blicken auch wir schon zu viel auf angeblich „progressive“ Senatsmehrheiten, die Berlin bezahlbar machen wollen?


Haben wir dabei vergessen, dass es ohne Widerstand von unten keine Verbesserung in unserem Sinne geben wird? Wir verstehen unsere Kundgebung gegen Wohnraumzerstörung und Vertreibung von Menschen auch als einen kleinen Beitrag, diesen Widerstand wieder sichtbar zumachen. Nicht nur in der Gürtelstraße wurden zu Beginn der kalten Jahreszeit Menschen auf die Straße gesetzt. Auch in Habersaathstraße 40-48 wurden am 13. Oktober Menschen mit einem großen Polizeiaufgebot geräumt und aufdie Straße gesetzt. Dort hatten vor 5 Jahren wohnungslose Menschen mit Unterstützer*innengruppen leerstehende Wohnungen besetzt. Sie konnten sogemeinsam mit einigen Altmieter*innen verhindern, dass der


Eigentümer die gut erhaltenden Gebäude abreißt, um Luxuswohnungen zu errichten. Genau das droht auch in der Gürtelstraße Überall werden Menschen vertrieben für das Privatinteresse von Wohnkonzernen.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: John Berger: “Demonstrations are protests of innocence”
content:
Paris, October 17, Guillaume Saligot / AFP







With all of those who continue to demonstrate against injustice and who imagine a different world …







The Nature of Mass Demonstrations




John Berger




This article originally appeared in 

New Society

, 23 May 1968.




Seventy years ago (on 6 May 1898) there was a massive demonstration of workers, men and women, in the centre of Milan. The events which led up to it involve too long a history to treat with here. The demonstration was attacked and broken up by the army under the command of General Beccaris. At noon the cavalry charged the crowd: the unarmed workers tried to make barricades: martial law was declared and for three days the army fought against the unarmed.




The official casualty figures were 100 workers killed and 450 wounded. One policeman was killed accidentally by a soldier. There were no army casualties. (Two years later Umberto I was assassinated because after the massacre he publicly congratulated General Beccaris, the ‘butcher of Milan.’)




I have been trying to understand certain aspects of the demonstration in the Corso Venezia on 6 May because of a story I am writing. In the process I came to a few conclusions about demonstrations which may perhaps be more widely applicable.







Mass demonstrations should be distinguished from riots or revolutionary uprisings although, under certain (now rare) circumstances, they may develop into either of the latter. The aims of a riot are usually immediate (the immediacy matching the desperation they express): the seizing of food, the release of prisoners, the destruction of property. The aims of a revolutionary uprising are long-term and comprehensive: they culminate in the taking over of State power. The aims of a demonstration, however, are symbolic: it 

demonstrates

 a force that is scarcely used.




A large number of people assemble together in an obvious and already announced public place. They are more or less unarmed. (On 6 May 1898, entirely unarmed.) They present themselves as a target to the forces of repression serving the State authority against whose policies they are protesting.




Theoretically demonstrations are meant to reveal the strength of popular opinion or feeling: theoretically they are an appeal to the democratic conscience of the State. But this presupposes a conscience which is very unlikely to exist.




If the State authority is open to democratic influence, the demonstration will hardly be necessary; if it is not, it is unlikely to be influenced by an empty show of force containing no real threat. (A demonstration in support of an already established 

alternative

 State authority – as when Garibaldi entered Naples in 1860 – is a special case and may be immediately effective.)




Demonstrations took place before the principle of democracy was even nominally admitted. The massive early Chartist demonstrations were part of the struggle to obtain such an admission. The crowds who gathered to present their petition to the Tsar in St Petersburg in 1905 were appealing – and presenting themselves as a target – to the ruthless power of an absolute monarchy. In the event – as on so many hundreds of other occasions all over Europe – they were shot down.




It would seem that the true function of demonstrations is not to convince the existing State authority to any significant degree. Such an aim is only a convenient rationalisation.




The truth is that mass demonstrations are rehearsals for revolution: not strategic or even tactical ones, but rehearsals of revolutionary awareness. The delay between the rehearsals and the real performance may be very long: their quality – the intensity of rehearsed awareness – may, on different occasions, vary considerably: but any demonstration which lacks this element of rehearsal is better described as an officially encouraged public spectacle.




A demonstration, however much spontaneity it may contain, is a 

created

 event which arbitrarily separates itself from ordinary life. Its value is the result of its artificiality, for therein lies its prophetic, rehearsing possibilities.




A mass demonstration distinguishes itself from other mass crowds because it congregates in public 

to create its function

, instead of forming in response to one: in this, it differs from any assembly of workers within their place of work – even when strike action is involved – or from any crowd of spectators. It is an assembly which challenges what is given by the mere fact of its coming together.




State authorities usually lie about the number of demonstrators involved. The lie, however, makes little difference. (It would only make a significant difference if demonstrations really were an appeal to the democratic conscience of the State.) The importance of the numbers involved is to be found in the direct experience of those taking part in or sympathetically witnessing the demonstration. For them the numbers cease to be numbers and become the evidence of their senses, the conclusions of their imagination. The larger the demonstration, the more powerful and immediate (visible, audible, tangible) a metaphor it becomes for their total collective strength.




I say metaphor because the strength thus grasped transcends the potential strength of those present, and certainly their actual strength as deployed in a demonstration. The more people there are there, the more forcibly they represent to each other and to themselves those who are absent. In this way a mass demonstration simultaneously 

extends

 and 

gives body

 to an abstraction. Those who take part become more positively aware of how they belong to a class. Belonging to that class ceases to imply a common fate, and implies a common opportunity. They begin to recognise that the function of their class need no longer be limited: that it, too, like the demonstrations itself, can create its own function.




Revolutionary awareness is rehearsed in another way by the choice and effect of location. Demonstrations are essentially urban in character, and they are usually planned to take place as near as possible to some symbolic centre, either civic or national. Their ‘targets’ are seldom the strategic ones – railway stations, barracks, radio stations, airports. A mass demonstration can be interpreted as the symbolic capturing of a city or capital. Again, the symbolism or metaphor is for the benefit of the participants.




The demonstration, an irregular event created by the demonstrators, nevertheless takes place near the city centre, intended for very different uses. The demonstrators interrupt the regular life of the streets they march through or of the open spaces they fill. They ‘cut off these areas, and, not yet having the power to occupy them permanently, they transform them into a temporary stage on which they dramatise the power they still lack.




The demonstrators’ view of the city surrounding their stage also changes. By demonstrating, they manifest a greater freedom and independence – a greater creativity, even although the product is only symbolic – than they can ever achieve individually or collectively when pursuing their regular lives. In their regular pursuits they only modify circumstances; by demonstrating they symbolically oppose their very existence to circumstances.




This creativity may be desperate in origin, and the price to be paid for it high, but it temporarily changes their outlook. They become corporately aware that it is they or those whom they represent who have built the city and who maintain it. They see it through different eyes. They see it as their product, confirming their potential instead of reducing it.




Finally, there is another way in which revolutionary awareness is rehearsed. The demonstrators present themselves as a target to the so-called forces of law and order. Yet the larger the target they present, the stronger they feel. This cannot be explained by the banal principle of ‘strength in numbers,’ any more than by vulgar theories of crowd psychology. The contradiction between their actual vulnerability and their sense of invincibility corresponds to the dilemma which they force upon the State authority.




Either authority must abdicate and allow the crowd to do as it wishes: in which case the symbolic suddenly becomes real, and, even if the crowd’s lack of organisation and preparedness prevents it from consolidating its victory, the event demonstrates the weakness of authority. Or else authority must constrain and disperse the crowd with violence: in which case the undemocratic character of such authority is publicly displayed. The imposed dilemma is between displayed weakness and displayed authoritarianism. (The officially approved and controlled demonstration does not impose the same dilemma: its symbolism is censored: which is why I term it a mere public spectacle.) Almost invariably, authority chooses to use force. The extent of its violence depends upon many factors, but scarcely ever upon the scale of the physical threat offered by the demonstrators. This threat is essentially symbolic. But by attacking the demonstration authority ensures that the symbolic event becomes an historical one: an event to be remembered, to be learnt from, to be avenged.




It is in the nature of a demonstration to provoke violence upon itself. Its provocation may also be violent. But in the end it is bound to suffer more than it inflicts. This is a tactical truth and an historical one. The historical role of demonstrations is to show the injustice, cruelty, irrationality of the existing State authority. Demonstrations are protests of innocence.




But the innocence is of two kinds, which can only be treated as though they were one at a symbolic level. For the purposes of political analysis and the planning of revolutionary action, they must be separated. There is an innocence to be defended and an innocence which must finally be lost: an innocence which derives from justice, and an innocence which is the consequence of a lack of experience.




Demonstrations express political ambitions before the political means necessary to realise them have been created. Demonstrations predict the realisation of their own ambitions and thus may contribute to that realisation, but they cannot themselves achieve them.




The question which revolutionaries must decide in any given historical situation is whether or not further symbolic rehearsals are necessary. The next stage is training in tactics and strategy for the performance itself.







Source: 

www.marxists.org

author: Λουκάς Σταμέλλος
title: Ο αντεισαγγελέας ΑΠ Βασίλης Φλωρίδης γίνεται το πρόσωπο της διαφθοράς
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης: 

Ο αντεισαγγελέας ΑΠ Βασίλης Φλωρίδης γίνεται το πρόσωπο της διαφθοράς




Ο Βασίλης Φλωρίδης, αντεισαγγελέας Αρείου Πάγου και αδελφός του υπουργού Δικαιοσύνης Γιώργου Φλωρίδη, 

δημοσίευσε στην «Καθημερινή» ένα «άρθρο»

 με το οποίο 

πέρασε γενεές δεκατέσσαρες τους υφισταμένους του εισαγγελείς

 

και τα δικαστικά συμβούλια

 γιατί έστειλαν σε δίκη – που 

επίκειται

 να φτάσει στο ακροατήριο – 11 άτομα, μεταξύ των οποίων υψηλόβαθμους αξιωματικούς και τον τότε αρχηγό της ΕΛ.ΑΣ.




Το αντικείμενο αυτής της δικογραφίας; Η απόπειρα συγκάλυψης της σύλληψης του γιου του υπουργού (τότε Προστασίας του Πολίτη και νυν Ανάπτυξης) Τάκη Θεοδωρικάκου τον Νοέμβριο του 2021. Η ίδια η σύλληψη μικρή σημασία είχε, καθώς επρόκειτο για το γελοίο «αδίκημα» της κατοχής μικρής ποσότητας κάνναβης. Αυτό που έχει σημασία είναι ότι, κατά τη δικογραφία, φέρεται να κινητοποιήθηκαν «λυτοί και δεμένοι» για να μη γίνει σύλληψη του γιου του υπουργού. 

Περισσότερα για την παραπομπή των κατηγορουμένων μπορείτε να διαβάσετε εδώ

.




Με λίγα λόγια, για να γίνει κατανοητό το μέγεθος της ωμής παρέμβασης:




Aδελφός υπουργού χρησιμοποιεί την επιρροή της θεσμικής του ιδιότητας 

για να προκαταλάβει το αποτέλεσμα

 

επικείμενης

 

ποινικής δίκης

 που αντιμετωπίζει ο γιος ενός άλλου υπουργού. Κι αυτό συνέβη μέσω μιας εφημερίδας – πυλώνα της ελληνικής Δεξιάς, με μεγάλη απήχηση στους δικαστικούς κύκλους.




Η παρέμβαση του Βασίλη Φλωρίδη δεν σχολιάζει κάποια γενικά χαρακτηριστικά υποθέσεων τα οποία δεν μπορούν να συνδεθούν με συγκεκριμένη δικογραφία. Δίνει ουσιαστικά «γραμμή» στους δικαστές που θα κρίνουν την υπόθεση. Κι αυτό το κάνει σχολιάζοντας την ουσία του σκεπτικού των υφισταμένων του εισαγγελέων, με αμετροέπειες όπως:







Και οι τέσσερις εισαγγελείς που αντιστάθηκαν, κατέγραψαν στα δικαστικά τους κείμενα ένα κοινό βασικό δεδομένο: Οτι τα αποδεικτικά στοιχεία που υποτίθεται θεμελίωναν τα εγκλήματα, ήταν σαθρά και δεν μπορούσαν να στηρίξουν τις κατηγορίες. Στη συγκεκριμένη περίπτωση δεν επρόκειτο για έκφραση κρίσης πίσω από την οποία θα μπορούσε να καλυφθεί ο δικαστής. Ηταν κατασκευή κρίσης.







Ο αντεισαγγελέας του Αρείου Πάγου καταλήγει σε λυρικές περιγραφές για «φλέβες διαφθοράς» που «καταλήγουν στην καρδιά του οργανισμού» και «πόρτα της διαφθοράς» που «ανοίγει πάντα από μέσα».




Όλα αυτά επειδή κάποιοι εισαγγελείς και κάποιοι δικαστές στα συμβούλια 

δεν θεώρησαν ότι επειδή πρόκειται για γιο υπουργού πρέπει να κάνουν τα στραβά μάτια

 στην απόπειρα συγκάλυψης.




Ευχολόγια οι αντιδράσεις των δικαστικών




Όπως ήταν αναμενόμενο, η πρωτοφανής (

ναι, ακόμα και για την ελλαδική πραγματικότητα είναι πρωτοφανής μια τόσο ωμή

 

εξωθεσμική

 

παρέμβαση εν ενεργεία εισαγγελέα στην εξέλιξη μιας ποινικής δικογραφίας

) ακρότητα του Β. Φλωρίδη έχει προκαλέσει αυτό που τα ΜΜΕ αγαπούν να ονομάζουν «θύελλα αντιδράσεων».




Η 

Ένωση Δικαστών και Εισαγγελέων στην ανακοίνωσή της

 υπενθύμισε ότι 

«Είναι ο ίδιος εισαγγελικός λειτουργός που 

σε

 

παλαιότερο άρθρο του στο Βήμα

 

έγραφε ότι “οι δικαστικοί λειτουργοί που έχουν συγγενικά πρόσωπα με ενεργή ενασχόληση στην πολιτική πρέπει να απέχουν από τον χειρισμό υποθέσεων στα οποία εμπλέκονται πολιτικά πρόσωπα –οι τιμιότεροι όλων κι αν είναι”

»

. Στην ίδια ανακοίνωση, ωστόσο, η ΕνΔΕ δεν χάνει την ευκαιρία να επιτεθεί και στους… δικηγόρους, για κάποιο λόγο, παρουσιάζοντας μια ιδιότυπη «θεωρία των δύο άκρων».




Ο ίδιος 

ο Άρειος Πάγος με δελτίο Τύπου του

 χαρακτήρισε 

«θυμική αντίδραση επικοινωνιακού χαρακτήρα»

 το «άρθρο» του αντεισαγγελέα του, σημειώνοντας: 

«Τέτοιες δημοσιεύσεις, που αφορούν εκκρεμή υπόθεση ενώπιον του Α΄

 

βαθμού δικαιοδοσίας και πρόκειται να εκδικασθεί άμεσα, οι οποίες περιέχουν μομφή και καταγγέλλουν αορίστως τους επιληφθέντες δικαστές ως διεφθαρμένους, εκφεύγουν των ορίων της οποιασδήποτε κριτικής των δικαστικών αποφάσεων και βουλευμάτων και πλήττουν την εμπιστοσύνη των πολιτών στο θεσμό της Δικαιοσύνης

»

.




Πρόταση για πειθαρχική αναφορά από την Εναλλακτική Παρέμβαση




Η Εναλλακτική Παρέμβαση Δικηγόρων Αθήνας, με 

επιστολή των συμβούλων της προς το Διοικητικό Συμβούλιο του Δικηγορικού Συλλόγου Αθηνών

 επισημαίνει ότι οι ανακοινώσεις αποτροπιασμού δεν αρκούν:







Είναι προφανές ότι απέναντι σε αυτή την κατάπτωση δεν αρκούν οι ανακοινώσεις, σαν και αυτή που εξέδωσε η Ένωση Δικαστών και Εισαγγελέων, πιθανά δε να λειτουργούν και εκτονωτικά. Η τελευταία, την ώρα που κατηγορεί δικηγόρους και διοργανώνει έστω και αποτυχημένη ημερίδα για «ακραίες συμπεριφορές τους κατά δικαστών», έχει σαστίσει, καθώς βρίσκεται αντιμέτωπη με την πλέον ακραία συμπεριφορά που έχει ποτέ εκφραστεί κατά δικαστών εκ των ένδον, από Αντεισαγγελέα Αρείου Πάγου, που μάλιστα λίγο έλειψε να έχει διορισθεί πρόσφατα και Εισαγγελέας του Αρείου Πάγου.




Ο Δικηγορικός Σύλλογος Αθηνών πρέπει να αποφασίσει σήμερα την υποβολή πειθαρχικής αναφοράς κατ’ 

άρθρο 109 και επόμενα του ΚΟΔΚΔΛ (ν. 4938/2022)

, καθώς και μηνυτήριας αναφοράς στην Εισαγγελία Πρωτοδικών Αθηνών για τα αδικήματα της αθέμιτης επιρροής σε δικαστικούς λειτουργούς (

α. 167Α

) και της παράβασης καθήκοντος (

α. 259 ΠΚ

). Με δεδομένο ότι αρμόδιος για την άσκηση πειθαρχικής δίωξης σε βάρος των Αντεισαγγελέων του Αρείου Πάγου είναι ο Υπουργός Δικαιοσύνης κατ’ άρθρο 117 παρ. 1 του ΚΟΔΚΔΛ, θα πρέπει να ζητηθεί στην αίτηση η εξαίρεση του Υπουργού, εκ του γεγονότος ότι ο πειθαρχικά ελεγχόμενος Εισαγγελέας τυγχάνει αδελφός του.







Πράγματι, αν δεν υπάρξει πειθαρχική παραπομπή του Βασίλη Φλωρίδη για αυτή την ωμή και άγρια παρέμβαση, δεν έχει κανένα νόημα ούτε η επίκληση σε «ανεξαρτησία της Δικαιοσύνης» ούτε οι λοιπές επικοινωνιακές ευκολίες περί «τοξικότητας» στις οποίες καταφεύγουν συχνά πυκνά οι εισαγγελείς και δικαστές, διεκδικώντας να ασκούν την εξουσία τους πάνω στη ζωή και τον θάνατο ανθρώπων, χωρίς έλεγχο.




Ο αντεισαγγελέας ΑΠ Βασίλης Φλωρίδης γίνεται το πρόσωπο της διαφθοράς

author: James Crump
title: Berlin’s Plan to Take Back Homes Will Cost Europe’s Biggest Landlord £7bn
content:
Europe’s largest residential landlord is set to lose €8.4bn (£7bn) as a result of plans by leftwing political party Die Linke to bring more than 140,000 Berlin flats into public ownership.




The real estate company Vonovia, which owns roughly 130,000 apartments in the city and 

528,000

 across Europe, would be the most affected by the plans, with 120,000 of its apartments set to be put into public ownership. Real-estate giant Heimstaden would also be hit hard with a projected loss of $1.5bn (£1.26bn), according to the 

Financial Times.




Die Linke, which won Berlin’s state elections in September, has agreed to talks with the city’s Greens and Social Democrats as part of plans to transfer ownership of flats from companies that own more than 10,000 apartments, with the legislation scheduled to be brought forward in 2028.




Any apartments owned above that 10,000 threshold would have to be transferred into public ownership as part of the policy, with Die Linke proposing an average compensation of around €100,000 per apartment – around 40% below the market value.




Vonovia’s 130,000 Berlin properties have an average market value of $130,000, meaning the company would lose a projected $8.4bn if the legislation becomes law. The company’s chief executive Luka Mucic has labelled the plans as “unconstitutional”, adding that the country needs “reliability, legal certainty and a stable investment environment.”




Housing was a 

key factor 

in September’s Berlin elections and has been growing in importance over the last half-decade, with 10% of the city’s residents currently living in 

housing poverty 

and 160,000 reported to have 

left the

 capital in 2025. In 2021, Berlin’s residents voted in favour of the city’s government seizing privately-owned flats from large corporate landlords, although that vote was not legally binding.




In order to govern in Berlin, Die Linke has had to form a three-way coalition with the progressive Greens and centre-left Social Democrats, leading to potential political concessions from the leftwing party. The Greens came fourth in September’s election on a commitment to push the property law through, but the Social Democrats’ leader publicly 

opposed the policy

 en route to a fifth place finish.




Support for Israel is also a sticking point between the three coalition parties, with the Greens and Social Democrats insisting that “Israel’s right to exist” be non-negotiable if they are to govern together. The parties rejected general boycotts against Israel and did not state whether Palestine has a 

right to exist

 in a joint document announcing the talks.

author: Natascha Elena Uhlmann
title: Mexico Volkswagen Workers Could Soon Strike
content:
In Mexico, at the world’s largest Volkswagen facility outside of Germany, workers are weighing the risks of a possible strike.




The 6,500 workers build the Jetta, Tiguan, and Taos at the company’s Puebla plant. Their union, SITIAVW, is one of Mexico’s most storied independent unions, and is in the midst of the plant’s annual wage reopener negotiations.




Days before the strike deadline of October 22, the company presented two proposals—offering raises of 7.98 percent and 7.95 percent for a one-year duration—which were rejected by the union. Soon afterwards, the company presented another offer: an 8.24 percent increase, of which 3.59 percent is a one-time payment of 12,000 pesos, equivalent to about $641 U.S. The deal would maintain the yearly salary reopener, a cycle the company had tried to lengthen in previous offers. Workers will vote on the offer on October 28, and could strike the next day if a deal is not reached. 




On October 15, workers voted down an offer that  would have provided a 13 percent combined increase to wages and benefits over the next two years. The vote was 3,135 against and 2,452 for. 




A month earlier, workers had overwhelmingly voted down the previous offer of a 10 percent combined increase. (The union had been pushing for a 17 percent increase earlier in negotiations.) Days before that first agreement was put to a vote, Volkswagen cut one of three shifts in a segment of the plant that produces the Jetta and the Tiguan. About 

800 workers

 lost their jobs, 

El Financiero

 reported.




Although the union announced that 611 of the workers—those who did not sign voluntary separation agreements—would be eligible for reinstatement when Volkswagen begins production of its Golf compact car at the Puebla facility next April, the damage was done. 5,925 of the company’s 6,440 eligible voters participated in the ratification vote: of them, 

73 percent voted to reject the offer

, in what SITIAVW advisor Willebaldo Gómez Zuppa characterized as an expression of anger at the firings. The deal would have also 

pushed the next wage reopener

 to 18 months out instead of the yearly cycle, angering workers.




‘NOT AT OUR EXPENSE’




Workers were also frustrated with the company’s efforts to put off their next wage reopener for 18 months rather than a year. The second offer would have pushed the wage reopener out even further, to two years.




“We are not blind to the delicate crisis facing the German automotive industry, nor are we ignoring the global financial challenges Volkswagen cites,” the union 

said

 in a statement in September after workers voted down the first offer. “But let it be heard loud and clear, all the way to Wolfsburg: corporate crises will not be resolved at the expense of the sweat, the rights, and the future of the Mexican working class.”




Volkswagen did not respond to requests for comment. In a statement sent to 

La Jornada de Oriente

, VW 

said

, "We respect the result of the vote... and at the same time, express our deep worry and disappointment. This agreement represents the greatest viable offer from the company, given current conditions.” 




GLOBAL LAYOFFS




In September, VW announced plans to eliminate 

50,000 jobs

 globally by 2030, alongside another 50,000 already anticipated cuts—together representing the largest culling of jobs ever by a single automaker.




The company noted in September that its European factories have the capacity to produce 

500,000 more vehicles per year

 than it can sell. The industry faces 

“enormous pressure”

 due to low cost electric vehicles produced in China, Volkswagen's CEO Oliver ​Blume said at the Paris Motor Show in October.  Its restructuring plan calls for eliminating half the models it produces (the less profitable half).




IG Metall, which represents 120,000 Volkswagen workers in Germany and sits on the company’s supervisory board, agreed to accept the closure of four German plants between 2031 and 2034, telling the 

Guardian

 that both labor and management had made concessions to stave off “a dangerous escalation of the conflict.”




Workers at VW's only U.S. assembly plant, in Chattanooga, Tennessee, joined the United Auto Workers in 2024 after years of trying, and ratified their first contract earlier this year. So far the cuts have not affected them.




It remains unclear how many more cuts are expected in Puebla. Since 2012, the plant has cut its workforce by 36 percent, 

Milenio reported

, but it remains one of the largest employers in the state of Puebla today.




About 6,500 production workers are directly employed at the plant, which produces vehicles largely for export to the United States. Some 39,000 more work in the auto supply chain across the state, including 3,500 at the local Audi plant, and thousands more in the parts sector, 

producing seats, motor components, and electronics

.




The offer that workers voted down in October included a guarantee that the 611 members laid off in September would be rehired in the future, and guaranteed jobs for the current workforce.




AUTO STRIKES RARE




Unlike in the U.S., where companies can try to continue operations during a strike by using managers and hiring replacement workers, under Mexican labor law, companies must cease all production at a struck plant. That gives Mexican unions tremendous potential power. 




Yet strikes in the country’s auto industry, the world’s seventh-largest, have been exceedingly rare in recent decades, with most of the industry’s contracts held by employer-friendly “protection unions” who have been a key partner in Mexico’s low-wage development model. SITIAVW, one of the few independent unions, has won the highest wages in the industry.




In this case, however, some analysts have speculated that the company may welcome a strike.




In Mexico, employers must provide a justification to the government for laying off workers. Among those justifications can be losses incurred due to a strike, said SITIAVW adviser Willebaldo Gomez Zuppa: “It opens the door before the government to say, ‘That’s why I have to fire so many people.’”




“It’s not hard to go out on strike,” said Hugo Tlalpan, SITIAVW’s General Secretary. “The hard thing is ending it.”




ONE MINUTE LATE




The Puebla plant has been in operation since 1967. In the plant’s early days, workers were affiliated with the Confederation of Mexican Workers, or CTM, a labor confederation known for imposing pro-employer “protection contracts” on workers. But in 1972, workers split off from the CTM and formed the independent SITIAVW. Since then, the plant has seen a number of strikes and workplace actions—and nearly as many efforts from Mexico’s halls of power to subvert them. 




In 1992, 

14,500 workers at the Puebla facility struck

 to expel their union leadership that some workers felt was complicit in negotiating an employer-friendly contract. With the blessing of the Secretary of Labor, the company 

 locked them out,

 then fired them. About 10,000 were rehired a day later, but under an agreement that 

imposed

 higher productivity targets, flexible scheduling, and a reduction in benefits.




In 2000, workers struck again, and once more their strike was 

quashed

 with support of Mexico’s labor authorities. Because workers went out on strike at 11:01 a.m. instead of exactly at 11, their stated strike deadline, the Federal Arbitration Board deemed their strike invalid. (They struck a year later and clinched 

 14.7 percent raises

.) 




The union is carefully weighing its options in this round of negotiations; so far, SITIAVW has extended its strike deadline 

four times.

 Most recently, just two days before the September 17 strike deadline, the union extended the deadline to Friday, October 2. 




“This is an attack on one of the most robust collective bargaining agreements [in the country],” Gomez Zuppa said. What happens next will have repercussions for autoworkers throughout Mexico and Volkswagen workers across the world.

author: Ben Smoke
title: Netanyahu and 34 Israelis Have Gone on Trial for Torture of Flotilla Activist
content:
A landmark trial accusing Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and 34 senior political and military figures of crimes against humanity had its first formal hearing in Istanbul today.







Turkish prosecutors have charged 35 Israeli defendants, including Netanyahu and ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Israel Katz, with torture, unlawful deprivation of liberty, aggravated robbery, vessel hijacking and crimes against humanity in relation to last year’s Gaza aid flotilla. They are also accused of genocide in Palestine.




The trial had its first formal hearing this morning following the issuing of arrest warrants in July and Turkish requests for an 

Interpol red notice

 in August. Charges are being pursued under 

universal jurisdiction

, which allows countries to address international crimes occurring abroad. 




The case focuses primarily on incidents surrounding the 

illegal interception of boats

 from the 2025 Global Sumud Flotilla mission. 




On 31 August 2025, more than 50 ships carrying around 500 participants from 44 countries set off from Barcelona to break Israel’s illegal blockade of Gaza and deliver aid to those trapped there.




The flotilla was subject to a number of drone attacks, most notably off the coasts of Tunisia and Greece, before being 

illegally intercepted by Israel

 in international waters. Those on board were detained and have accused Israeli forces of subjecting them to human rights abuses including rape, assault, degrading treatment, withholding of medical care and more.




Turkey negotiated the release of hundreds of participants, including a Novara Media contributor, on charter flights to Istanbul, where legal and medical teams gathered evidence of severe mistreatment. 




“This trial is not just about seeking justice for the 101 victims represented in this case; it is a fundamental challenge to the doctrine of impunity,” said the Global Sumud Flotilla legal team. “When states use armed force against unarmed civilians attempting to deliver life-saving relief to a starved population, individuals within that chain of command must face judicial scrutiny.”




The trial in Istanbul comes as prosecutors in Rome, Italy, expand an investigation into Israeli officials for the mistreatment of 50 Italian participants of Global Sumud Flotilla missions. Officials including Ben-Gvir, Katz, IDF chief of staff Eyal Zamir and 11 others are being investigated for suspected torture, kidnapping, personal injury, robbery, property damage and damage causing danger of shipwreck.

author: Kenny Bruno
title: Mafia Diplomacy Will Continue After Kimberly Guilfoyle
content:
Guilfoyle’s mission in Greece — to push fossil fuels — is also playing out in the US with a permitting reform bill.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Kimberly Guilfoyle is out as U.S. ambassador to Greece. Mainstream media focused on Donald Trump Jr.’s former fiancée’s credit card bill and her penchant for extravagant partying and fashion. The next ambassador might not share those particular foibles, but the real significance of Guilfoyle’s appointment will last. She was what Dexter Filkins, writing in The New Yorker, calls “a new kind of Washington figure, for whom public office serves as a means to extraordinary wealth.” Donald Trump’s almost daughter-in-law was following in the footsteps of his son-in-law.

Jared Kushner does diplomacy and business simultaneously, and he’s getting really rich from it. While Kushner is dispatched to work on Iran and Ukraine, with meetings on the side to recruit billions to his investment funds, Guilfoyle was sent to Greece as the de facto ambassador for liquefied natural gas (LNG). In other words, her job was to shove LNG down the throats of Southeastern and Central European countries. Her refrain was U.S. energy dominance.

A more diplomatic diplomat might have noticed that one country’s dominance means, logically, another’s subservience. But tact was not Guilfoyle’s strong suit, and, according to the Wall Street Journal, another of her gaffes was not-so-subtly telling Greece’s energy minister that the U.S. could change the government of any country it wants.

Guilfoyle denies any intimidation took place, but threatening or forcing regime change for the sake of oil is not far-fetched. (See: Venezuela.)

In Southeast and Central Europe, the U.S. government is pushing something called the Vertical Gas Corridor (VGC), an opaque infrastructure initiative stretching from Greece through Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Moldova, and ultimately Ukraine. As stated by the U.S. Energy Association, the VGC “opens access to Europe’s largest underground gas storage system, located in Ukraine.”

Publicly, the U.S. is framing the project as a strategic corridor that strengthens regional energy security and reduces Russian influence. In practice, it is becoming a way to trade dependence on Russia for dependence on the U.S. Greece will be the entry point and collaborator in the plan. U.S. LNG exporters stand to make huge profits, especially when there are high prices, as has been the case during the Iran War.

Why is the U.S. going to the mat for the Vertical Gas Corridor? The fossil fuel industry sees LNG exports as the lifeboat for the sinking ship of the conventional oil industry. For U.S. LNG, as with crude oil, it’s export or die. Those were Ambassador Guilfoyle’s marching orders.

An inconvenient reality for the industry is that market enthusiasm for the VGC appears remarkably weak. Repeated capacity auctions linked to the corridor, in which gas companies bid for the right to use pipelines and other infrastructure, have attracted limited commercial interest. Several auctions failed outright, while others generated only modest bookings concentrated in specific segments of the network.

Infrastructure projects backed by robust commercial fundamentals typically attract customers on their own merits, without the need for lobbying and strong-arming. Massive terminals require long-term contracts, and the U.S. is determined to get both — whether or not it makes any economic sense.

For Greece, the stakes are particularly high.

The country is being positioned as the southern gateway for American LNG entering Southeast Europe. While this positioning promises geopolitical visibility, it also risks tying the Greek economy to fossil fuel infrastructure whose long-term viability remains deeply uncertain. Investments in LNG terminals, pipelines, and associated facilities are dependent on future gas demand that may never materialize as Europe accelerates its clean-energy transition.

At the same time, communities and ecosystems in Greece bear the environmental costs, just as surely as the Texas and Louisiana communities where the methane gas originates. From the Sea of Thrace to other sensitive marine areas, new infrastructure developments are proceeding despite growing concerns over climate impacts, methane emissions, and ecological damage.

The Greek government’s response appears less like strategic energy planning and more like appeasement of the U.S. Greece assumes the financial risk of costly LNG terminals, pipeline expansions, and related infrastructure while being encouraged to lock itself and the wider region into decades-long gas contracts. The plan not only deepens dependence on a very unreliable and fickle U.S., but it exposes Greek citizens to long-term economic, geopolitical, and climate risks — all in service of U.S. exports.

Last year, during trade negotiations, the U.S. insisted that the EU buy a preposterous $750 billion in energy from the U.S. to avoid punishing tariffs. The EU capitulated. The U.S. is among the interested parties pressing the EU to delay its methane regulation, which is designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by excluding the dirtiest fuels from the EU market. The EU is capitulating on that as well.

In the U.S., for all the coverage of Guilfoyle’s clumsiness, there has been almost no attention to her true mission in Greece. It’s hidden, perhaps, because the take-our-gas-or-else approach is working on Capitol Hill as well. The permitting reform bill known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA), meant to streamline permitting for both dirty fuels and clean energy, is one of the few pieces of legislation with supporters on both sides of the aisle. Yet the climate benefits of the bill are nil, because even though it will help the siting of wind and solar, it will help fossil fuels even more.

More clean energy doesn’t address climate change unless it replaces the burning of fossil fuels. In other words, the bill is likely to make emissions worse. Some proponents will rationalize that emissions will rise even more without the bill than with it. But playing to “lose by less” may not even work, because BAAJA will not only ease the way for fossil fuel permits but, in the name of certainty, will impede future U.S. administrations from transitioning off fossil fuels.

Even though it’s obviously a policy to lock in long-term commitment to oil and gas, some Democratic senators, and even climate champs, including Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island and Sen. Martin Heinrich of New Mexico, are supporting the bill. What’s maddening is that these senators surely understand that the only known method for addressing climate change at a large scale is to reduce the burning of fossil fuels. In the name of compromise, they are essentially giving up their cause — as if the floods, fires, storms, landslides, diseases, and other miseries caused by global heating will understand the need to accommodate a militantly pro-oil, anti-renewables government that does not negotiate in good faith. And they are doing so at a moment of minimum leverage, because their bargaining position is likely to be stronger after the next Congress is seated.

The United States is in a period of authoritarian rule, and Buy-Our-Gas-Or-Else is high on the agenda. The next U.S. Ambassador to Greece will understand the job is to communicate the demand for subservience, even if they pay their own credit card bills. The question is whether Greece, or the EU as a whole, or the Democrats in Congress, will stand up to it.

author: Saif Eddine Ghobr
title: Why does Tunisia become African only when Europe needs it to be?
content:
Tunisia is an African country that has spent much of its modern political imagination looking north. That sounds like a question of identity. In reality, it is a question of power — and more precisely, a practice of domination through classification.

For decades, Tunisia has imagined its economic future through the Mediterranean: European markets, French education, tourism, and European investment. Africa has often appeared somewhere beyond the Sahara, associated with instability, migration, and security.

Europe, however, possesses its own geography of Tunisia — one that shifts depending on what Europe needs from it. When Brussels discusses trade, investment, and political cooperation, Tunisia is a Mediterranean neighbor. When Europe discusses migration, border control, Libya, or the Sahel, Tunisia becomes something else: an African frontier state.

This is not a mere contradiction. This is a deliberate mechanism of geopolitical subordination through classification. Europe does not need Tunisia to be culturally European; it needs Tunisia to be strategically African when African space becomes relevant to European security.

The economic relationship makes this asymmetry impossible to ignore, revealing a genuine policy cage. The European Commission identifies the EU as Tunisia’s largest trading partner. In 2025, the EU accounted for 59.5% of Tunisia’s total trade. Some 73.2% of Tunisian exports went to the EU, while 49.6% of imports came from the European market. The EU is also Tunisia’s largest foreign investor, holding 85% of the country’s foreign direct investment stock.

These figures do not merely describe a successful trading relationship; they reveal an extraordinary concentration of Tunisia’s external economic relations in Europe. When three-quarters of a country’s exports depend on one economic space, that relationship ceases to be mere commerce and becomes an instrument of control, shaping industrial priorities, investment decisions, and the political imagination of what is economically possible.

Europe consequently becomes not simply Tunisia’s largest market, but its economic horizon — where economic dependence transforms into geographical dependence. Africa becomes secondary, not because it is irrelevant, but because Tunisia has spent decades learning to imagine prosperity through a northern market. As Kwame Nkrumah warned in 1965, the most insidious form of domination is control through financial and structural instruments, not direct conquest.

The contradiction becomes sharper when migration enters the picture, exposing the biopolitics of European border management. The EU’s relationship with Tunisia increasingly includes border management, migration control, and the fight against migrant smuggling. European support has included equipment, training, and operational assistance to Tunisian security and coast guard structures.

From Brussels’ perspective, this is cooperation. From a geopolitical standpoint, it is the externalization of Europe’s borders. Europe is not merely helping Tunisia secure its own territory; it is moving part of Europe’s migration-control architecture southward, closer to the routes through which migrants attempt to reach European territory. This is the essence of extraterritorial sovereignty as described by Giorgio Agamben in 2005: the European state exercises its power over human bodies beyond its borders.

This changes the meaning of Tunisia’s geography. Tunisia is no longer simply a neighbor across the Mediterranean; it becomes part of a European security perimeter without becoming part of Europe itself. Tunisia consequently occupies a peculiar geopolitical position: its economic relationship with Europe is framed as partnership, while its position on migration is treated as strategic infrastructure. The Mediterranean neighbor becomes the African frontier.

Yet another geography is beginning to emerge — one that challenges the idea of Tunisia as merely Europe’s southern security buffer. In June 2026, AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene visited Tunisia. The visit concluded with an agreed action plan aimed at deepening Tunisia’s trade across Africa.

This matters because it offers Tunisia a role fundamentally different from that assigned to it by the European migration agenda. The African Continental Free Trade Area offers Tunisia the possibility of becoming an economic actor within Africa, rather than a buffer between Europe and Africa. The African Development Bank is pursuing a similar regional logic. In June 2026, the Bank held consultations in Tunis for a new North Africa Regional Integration Strategy designed to deepen economic integration within North Africa and between North Africa and the wider African continent.

This is a radically different understanding of Africa. Africa is not merely the place from which Tunisia receives migrants, security risks, or instability. It is a market. It is a network of cities. It is a space for investment, industrial partnerships, logistics, technology, and political influence. The question is whether Tunisia will treat this geography as a strategy, or merely as an alternative whenever its relationship with Europe becomes difficult. There is a danger in treating Africa as a Plan B, because if Tunisian policymakers look south only when European markets become restrictive, African integration will remain a reaction rather than a strategy.

The choice is not Europe or Africa. Tunisia does not need to abandon its European relationship; its economic links with Europe are too deep, and its geography makes the Mediterranean an unavoidable part of its foreign policy. But Europe cannot be Tunisia’s only horizon.

The real choice is between being an object in someone else’s geography and becoming an actor in one’s own. If Tunisia is African only when Europe needs a border guard, its Africanness has been reduced to a function. If Tunisia discovers Africa only when it needs new markets, Africa becomes a fallback rather than a strategy.

Europe does not merely change Tunisia’s label; it confiscates Tunisia’s agency. By defining Tunisia as Mediterranean when it needs a market and African when it needs a buffer, Europe ensures that Tunisian sovereignty remains conditional — subject to the external power’s geopolitical needs. This is not partnership; it is strategic subordination. Africa is too often presented in European policy as a space from which problems arrive: migrants, instability, terrorism, trafficking, and energy insecurity. But Africa is also a political and economic project being built. The AfCFTA is an attempt to create a continental market; regional integration initiatives are attempting to connect North Africa more effectively with the rest of the continent.

Tunisia is already inside this geography. The question is whether it will remain inside it mainly as a recipient of European security policy, or whether it will begin to act as an African state pursuing its own economic and geopolitical interests. The problem, therefore, is not that Tunisia has forgotten that it is African. The problem is that Tunisia has not yet decided what being African is for — and has allowed external powers to determine when each geography is politically useful.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Hegseth Makes Unannounced Visit to Netanyahu Ahead of Israel’s Elections
content:
The visit came amid discussions between the US and Israel about a renewed assault on Iran.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday and met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, just eight days before Israel’s upcoming elections.

On Tuesday, in comments to reporters back in the U.S., Hegseth said that he was there “visiting our troops” and “had a chance to talk to the prime minister,” but that he would not discuss the subject of their meeting.

Hegseth met Netanyahu at the Ovda Air Base in southern Israel.

The visit comes amid discussions between the U.S. and Israel about a renewed assault on Iran. According to The Financial Times, Netanyahu had sought to launch a renewed attack on Iran earlier in October, but Trump dissuaded the attack, stating that it should not occur before the U.S. midterm elections. Hegseth, however, is reportedly among the strongest supporters of renewed strikes on Iran.

Hegseth’s visit came a day after Trump endorsed Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s October 27 elections. In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so.”

But Trump’s endorsement is unlikely to secure a majority for Netanyahu, who has been in power for 19 years — the longest of any Israeli prime minister — and is now facing a highly contested election. According to polling data, the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar Party is expected to win the most seats in Israel’s election next Tuesday, though no party is expected to secure a majority.

To form a governing coalition, the party with the most seats will need to form a coalition alongside other, smaller parties. But Eisenkot has stated that he would not form a government with Palestinian parties, particularly the Joint List.

In fact, Eisenkot’s “opposition” alliance diverges very little from Netanyahu’s ruling Likud party, particularly when it comes to Palestinians. Eisenkot has announced that he plans to continue to build Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, and that he is against a Palestinian state. He has even attempted to position himself to the right of Netanyahu on issues like the E1 settlement project, claiming that Netanyahu has been an obstacle to the project. Eisenkot has also stated his aim to expand the Israeli military by compelling Haredi Jews and Palestinian citizens of Israel to enlist in the army.

Tamir Sorek, professor at Penn State University, said in a recent Institute of Middle East Understanding press briefing that the anti-Netanyahu coalition “shares the same fantasy” of eliminating Palestinians, though “they refuse to articulate it.”

While Netanyahu’s Likud is more consistent and adamant in its attempts to exclude Palestinians from the electoral system, opposition parties like Eisenkot’s have also maneuvered to exclude the Palestinian parties, and to prevent Palestinian citizens of Israel — who make up 20 percent of Israel’s population — from voting.

The United Arab List, however, is seen as more acceptable by Israeli political parties than the Joint List, which consists of the more left-wing parties of Hadash (Jabha in Arabic), Ta’al, and Balad. The Arab List became the first Palestinian party to join an Israeli government in 2021, when Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid briefly removed Netanyahu from power.

But according to Sorek, a significant difference is that anti-Netanyahu voters are more sensitive to international pressure. “The question of who will be the next prime minister of Israel is secondary to whether the international community will press for sanctions on Israel,” Sorek asserted.

author: Tariq Ra’ouf
title: We Beat the Trump Administration in Court. Now We’re Going to the ICC.
content:
I am beginning to see a glimmer of hope that justice will be found for the dozens of family members I have lost in Gaza.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Over the course of the last three years, my family has lost 49 family members in Gaza. Their bodies were torn apart by shrapnel, crushed by falling buildings, and mutilated by bullets and munitions made and provided by the United States of America. Now, the U.S. is trying to dismantle the International Criminal Court, the only international court that can criminally prosecute U.S. officials for aiding and enabling genocide, by sanctioning the Court and attempting to intimidate anyone, including U.S. citizens, from working with them. So, in response, I joined others to sue this administration in order to take them to the very court they’re trying to destroy.

I’m a Palestinian-American organizer, and I helped establish Taxpayers Alliance Against Genocide (TAAG), which recently partnered with Democracy for the Arab World Now (DAWN) to sue the Trump administration so we can continue much-needed legal and advocacy work. Over the course of over a year, TAAG worked with an international legal team to prepare evidence against top U.S. officials for aiding and enabling the genocide of my people, but up until now, we haven’t been able to submit our evidence to the ICC because of this administration’s attacks and sanctions on the court and its judges.

Thankfully, that will now change after we successfully challenged the Trump administration in court. On October 13 we won a preliminary injunction that blocks this administration from being able to target our groups for working with sanctioned parties, clearing the way for us to proceed to the ICC. For the first time since the genocide started, I am beginning to see a glimmer of hope that justice will be found for the dozens of family members I have lost in Gaza.

Long before the Trump administration sanctioned the entirety of the International Criminal Court (ICC) on October 9, it first enacted Executive Order 14203 in February of 2025. This executive order granted administration officials the ability to sanction foreign nationals for supporting the ICC’s investigations into U.S. and Israeli parties guilty of committing war crimes and their complicity in genocide. Under this Executive Order (EO), the Trump administration also sanctioned leading Palestinian human rights groups al-Haq, al-Mezan, and the Palestinian Center for Human Rights (PCHR), as well as the UN Special Rapporteur for the Human Rights Situation on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, Francesca Albanese, along with other ICC officials.

What many people don’t know is that the EO that allowed the administration to sanction these parties doesn’t only go after foreign nationals, it also makes it a federal offense — punishable by a $1 million fine and/or 20 years in prison — for anyone, including American citizens, who provides or receives a “service” to or from a sanctioned party. This provision of the EO is exactly why TAAG and DAWN took this administration to court: Our lawsuit argued that the EO violates our First Amendment rights as American citizens to speak, associate, and engage in Palestine-related human rights advocacy with these parties. As a founding member of TAAG, I can tell you firsthand how these sanctions have prevented us and organizations like DAWN from being able to continue our work sharing evidence and advocacy ideas with people like Albanese and ICC officials, because the definition of “service” is so broad and undefined — the US can interpret it as being anything that confers a benefit to the recipient.

In an October 9 video of Marco Rubio announcing the actions against the ICC, he tries defending the administration’s actions by calling the ICC a “rogue court,” which the U.S. is “not subject to the jurisdiction of.” But Rubio leaves out a fundamental principle of international law: A country does not have to join the ICC for its nationals to fall within the Court’s jurisdiction.

If a country that is not a State Party to the Rome Statute commits a war crime on the lands of a country that is a state party, the perpetrator of that crime can be investigated. Given that Palestine is a State Party to the Rome Statute, and that Gaza (and the West Bank) are classified as Occupied Palestinian Territories by the United Nations, the ICC has every right to investigate and prosecute the United States and Israel for the insurmountable war crimes committed against my family members and thousands of other innocent civilians.

It is clear that the only “protections” this administration are seeking are for the citizens responsible for aiding and abetting war crimes, which after three years, we have plenty of evidence of. Anthony Aguilar, a retired US special forces officer and whistleblower who resigned from his work with the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) aid distribution centers in Gaza, has gone on record saying he saw the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) shooting at crowds of Palestinians, and in an interview with the BBC says he saw Israeli and American military forces of the GHF using an “indiscriminate and unnecessary force against a civilian population, an unarmed, starving population.”

Rubio consistently mentions the idea of “protecting American citizens” from investigations by the ICC, but the citizens he is referring to are the ones committing the war crimes he doesn’t want investigated. What about American citizens whose families have been killed with U.S.-supplied weapons? Who protects our right to seek justice?

In sanctioning the entirety of the ICC, the Trump administration is not only trying to cripple any attempt to hold them accountable for their war crimes, but they’re also telling American citizens like myself that if you dare to seek justice for the family members you’ve lost, we’ll imprison you.

Now that the courts sided with us in our lawsuit, we are finally able to prepare for the next steps ahead.

With the injunction in place, TAAG is now moving forward to finalize its evidence submission and plans to imminently send this to the ICC. We are also rallying support, within the US and beyond, for human rights organizations and advocates for the ICC to act responsibly upon this massive collection of evidence, in hopes that more parties take appropriate legal actions where possible. We fundamentally believe that grassroots movements like ours, and so many throughout the world, are the ones who must step up where our leadership has failed, and build the democratic, popular power capable of ensuring that legal action against genocide is taken and enforced.

We also hope that our actions inspire more American citizens to speak up against this administration and the priorities of our government. I helped found Taxpayers Alliance Against Genocide because I’m sick of our tax dollars being used against my own family in Gaza, while our communities here in the U.S. suffer from a lack of housing, education and healthcare. Those of us within TAAG recognize that we have a duty as American citizens to hold our nation accountable for the war crimes they commit, not just in Gaza but all over the world. We will not rest until we’ve exhausted every avenue to seek justice and accountability for these war crimes. We will continue collecting evidence, and pursuing every available legal avenue, moving forward with our crucial evidence work for a prospective submission to the ICC and advance our efforts to hold U.S. officials accountable for crimes against humanity. We will not be intimidated into abandoning our work, our families, or the principle that no one is above the law.

title: Three dead and two missing after flooding in Urmia
content:
At least three people have died in severe flooding in Urmia province in Rojhilat (Eastern Kurdistan). Two others remain missing, while six people have been injured. Heavy rainfall and hailstorms triggered flash floods, particularly in the northern part of the province. The districts of Selmas and Maku have been hardest hit.




According to the provincial Red Crescent Directorate in Urmia, the fatalities occurred in the village of Kaniyan near Selmas, where flooding intensified significantly overnight. Following an extensive search, rescue teams recovered three bodies, including those of a ten-year-old girl and a 63-year-old man. The search for two other missing people is ongoing.




Severe damage to homes and infrastructure




The floodwaters caused extensive damage to homes, roads, and utility infrastructure, particularly in rural areas. According to preliminary assessments, at least 25 houses were flooded and partially destroyed. Eleven vehicles became stranded in floodwaters on connecting roads and near villages.




Search and rescue teams were dispatched to the affected areas. Residents of several flooded villages had to evacuate their homes and were moved to safety.

author: Unknown
title: More than 70 Kurdish families face displacement in Kirkuk
content:
Demolition work for a planned housing development began on Thursday in the Kurdish village of Aliawa in Kirkuk province. More than 70 families face the destruction of their homes and the threat of displacement once again. Residents are protesting the authorities’ actions, pointing out that the land was officially allocated to them years ago.




The village is located on the main road between Kirkuk and Dibis, northwest of the provincial capital. According to local media reports, construction machinery arrived on Thursday and began demolishing shops and commercial premises. More than 70 residential buildings are expected to be demolished in a subsequent phase. Residents say that between 70 and 80 Kurdish families are affected.




‘Now they want to displace us again’




The residents are internally displaced people from Kirkuk who were officially resettled in Aliawa in 2011 and 2012 under Article 140 of the Iraqi Constitution. The constitutional provision calls for the normalization of conditions in disputed territories and the resolution of their political status.




“These plots of land were officially allocated to us by the Commission for Displaced Persons. Now they want to drive us out without any regard for our rights, through political interference. This means we are being displaced once again,” a villager said.




The municipal authorities reportedly offered the affected residents compensation of around two million Iraqi dinars. However, residents consider the amount entirely inadequate.




“This is our village. We grew up here, and now they want to drive us out. Between 70 and 80 houses are threatened with demolition,” another resident said.




The demolition machinery now threatens their entire livelihoods.




Dispute over land rights under Article 140




According to the villagers, an official document calls for the demolition work to be halted due to identified violations. Nevertheless, the relevant authorities are reportedly continuing to pursue the project.




The affected residents also argue that the plots of land remain subject to unresolved property ownership and territorial disputes under Article 140 of the Iraqi Constitution. They maintain that the land must not be allocated to an investment project until its legal status has been definitively clarified.




According to available information, the Kirkuk Investment Commission remains committed to proceeding with the construction project despite these objections.

title: Shengal delegation holds talks at the European Parliament
content:
A diplomatic delegation from Shengal visited the European Parliament in Strasbourg to raise awareness of the situation facing the Yazidi population and the threats to the region. The discussions focused on conditions in Şengal and the challenges confronting its people.




The delegation included Azad Hisên, co-chair of the Shengal People’s Council; Sara Şengalî, a member of the Jineolojî Committee; and Kurdish politician and former Member of the European Parliament Feleknas Uca.




During their visit, the delegation members met with representatives of various political groups and parties in the European Parliament. Those they met included Swedish MEP Jonas Sjöstedt of The Left group, Austrian MEP Andreas Schieder (SPÖ), Galician MEP Ana Miranda Paz, and German MEPs Katrin Langensiepen (Greens), Martin Schirdewan (Die Linke), and Özlem Alev Demirel, also of Die Linke.

author: Jon Queally
title: Netanyahu Orders “Full Lockdown” of Occupied West Bank
content:
Smotrich said the Palestinian Authority should be “dismantled” and called for increased demolition of Palestinian homes.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that he has ordered the Israel Defense Force to “immediately impose a lockdown on Hebron and prepare for a full lockdown of the entire” illegally occupied West Bank following a gun battle that reportedly left two Palestinians dead and at least five Israeli soldiers wounded.

Following an emergency meeting with Israel’s security cabinet and his top military advisors, Netanyahu posted a statement to social media in which he blamed Hamas for the incident and accused the group of “planning a major attack aimed at murdering innocent civilians.”

Netanyahu claimed that “large quantities of weapons and ammunition” had been discovered, but did not offer details about the nature of attack or its alleged planning.

Far-right Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who was on the scene of the shooting incident soon after it occurred, warned that “comprehensive military operation” in the occupied West Bank would soon be underway to handle those termed “terrorists.”

Smotrich also said that the Palestinian Authority, which governs the illegally occupied territories, should be “dismantled,” called for large-scale military operations like those executed in Gaza and Lebanon, and for the increased demolition of Palestinian homes.

“There is no alternative to a comprehensive military operation in Judea and Samaria that will lead to the dismantling of the Palestinian Authority, the confiscation of weapons and the elimination of terrorists,” Smotrich said. “Just as in Gaza and Lebanon.”

The order to demolish homes near where Friday’s incident took place, he added, “will begin to be implemented within the next hour, and the demolitions will continue throughout the afternoon.”

Mustafa Barghouti, founder and leader of the Palestinian National Initiative (PNI), was among those warning that what comes next will not be good for the Palestinian people, calling the complete closure of the West Bank “an act of collective punishment.”

Netanyahu, Barghouti said, “declared today that he is planning to carry out the ethnic cleansing of entire neighborhoods in Hebron.”

Such a declaration, he continued, “represents an alarming escalation in Israel’s policies of forced displacement and a flagrant violation of international law and the fundamental rights of the Palestinian people. It must be unequivocally condemned, and the international community must act immediately to prevent the forcible displacement of Palestinian residents and hold those responsible accountable.”

Yariv Oppenheimer, former director of Peace Now and a project director at the Geneva Institute, told Al-Jazeera in a Friday interview that Israeli leaders would now leverage the incident to further tighten their grip on the occupied West Bank, already rife with violence from Israeli settlers and IDF operations in Occupied Palestinian Territories (OPT).

“The Israeli army is getting into the Palestinian cities, the settlers are attacking Palestinians, and the situation is impossible” in the OPT, Oppenheimer explained.

Oppenheimer added that he expected Netanyahu and his cabinet to take advantage of this attack on Israeli soldiers in order to push “more propaganda” to justify the likely violence that is coming from the Israeli government and violent settler factions.

“There will be house demolitions. We will see [a] curfew. We will see more soldiers […] making arrests, and definitely we might see the settlers trying to target Palestinians in revenge for this attack, and trying to take advantage of this situation in order to escalate the situation even more,” Oppenheimer warned.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Ndivhuwo Mukwevho
title: Multi-million rand sports facility finally opens in Limpopo
content:
Finally, Waterval residents in Limpopo outside of Elim Hospital are now able to utilise their R55-million sports facility having waited for over a decade of delays. The Waterval facility is not the only one that has been neglected by Limpopo municipalities. Earlier this year, 

Elitsha 

reported on the R1.4-million upgrades to 

Makwarela Stadium

 that never happened.




How it all started




The Waterval sports facility, which consists of a soccer field and a tennis court, was officially handed over to the Waterval community earlier this month. This came as welcome relief to local residents who had already lost hope that the facility would ever open. At one stage, it was left abandoned and turned into a drug den and a hiding place for criminals.




The facility is set to be utilised for various sporting codes by the local communities and schools. “At last, our children have got a ground where they can play their football with ease. Even though we had to wait for years for the facility to be completed, we are happy now that the ground is ours. To be honest, I am one of the people who had already lost hope that one day, the facility will ever be used for our benefit,” says Cedric Mulaudzi, a resident of Waterval.




Mulaudzi told 

Elitsha

 that his 11-year-old son was not yet born when construction work began on the Waterval sports facility. “I am just happy that my son, who was not yet born when construction work started, will now have a place where he will be able to mature his football career,” says Mulaudzi.




The Waterval sports facility is the only decent, modern sports facility in the area and will be utilised by Mpheni, Shirly, Elim and other local communities.




Politically motivated?




“Why did it take too long for our government to complete this facility? This means that if it takes our government more than 10-years to complete just one stadium!” says Mulaudzi.




Nelson Mudzanani, who was born and raised in Waterval, also has questions about the timing of the project’s completion, while welcoming its completion. “For years, we have asked questions to the local municipality [Makhado] on why it was taking too long for them to complete the project and we never received any response. But now, we are due for elections in the coming weeks, and all of a sudden the stadium is finally completed. I just hope that the timing is not politically motivated,” says Mudzanani.




He believes that the sports facility will go a long way in empowering the local communities. “Those who want to exercise and those who want to play various sporting codes now have a decent place to do so. I just hope that the facility will be maintained accordingly,” he says.




During the handover of the Waterval sports facility, Makhado mayor, Dorcus Mboyi urged the local communities to utilise the facility properly and refrain from vandalising it. She also extended apologies for the delays they endured during the construction of the facility.

Διήμερη εκδήλωση: Όταν οι αγώνες για ζωή και αξιοπρέπεια νικούν







ΟΤΑΝ ΟΙ ΑΓΩΝΕΣ ΓΙΑ ΖΩΗ ΚΑΙ ΑΞΙΟΠΡΕΠΕΙΑ ΝΙΚΟΥΝ




Ανοιχτό κάλεσμα προς την κοινωνία




Χωρίς τη συλλογική δράση, οι ιδέες κοιμούνται στα κεφάλια και στις βιβλιοθήκες. Η γέννηση της πολιτικής ελευθερίας συμβαδίζει με τον αγώνα για τη συλλογική ιδιοποίηση της θεσμίζουσας αρχής.




Eduardo Colombo




Ως Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια του πολύμηνου και πολυεπίπεδου αγώνα ενάντια στα τελευταία σχέδια του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου βαδίσαμε και αγωνιστήκαμε πλάι πλάι με τους συντρόφους μας απεργούς πείνας μέχρι θανάτου Αριστοτέλη Χαντζή και Suzon Doppagne και από κοινού με όλους τους ανθρώπους των κινημάτων και της αλληλεγγύης. Ανθρώπους από ευρύτερες κοινωνικές ομάδες που αναγνώρισαν αυτόν τον αγώνα της Κοινότητας ως έναν συλλογικό αγώνα της κοινωνίας που αφορά όλες και όλους, συγκροτώντας ένα ευρύ κοινωνικό μέτωπο.




Και όπως αγωνιστήκαμε συλλογικά, νικήσαμε και συλλογικά!




Έχοντας κλείσει λοιπόν τον πρώτο μεγάλο κύκλο νικηφόρα, είναι ξεκάθαρο πως αυτό που έχουμε να υπερασπιστούμε δεν είναι μόνο αυτή η συγκεκριμένη νίκη ή μια ρωγμή που αποτέλεσε μια στιγμή στον χρόνο ή μια αυτοαναφορική συνθήκη εντός της οποίας βρίσκει τον εαυτό της η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών. Η παρακαταθήκη αυτού του αγώνα και της νίκης στο παρόν και το μέλλον απλώνεται μπροστά μας αναδεικνύοντας μια τεράστια δυνατότητα: Να ξαναχτίσουμε το συλλογικό φαντασιακό του κόσμου της αλληλεγγύης, της καθημερινής αντίστασης απέναντι στην εξαθλίωση, τον φόβο, την υποταγή, την εξατομίκευση, αντιτάσσοντας την αυτοθέσμιση των κοινωνιών μας και τη συγκρότηση κοινοτήτων, οπουδήποτε οι άνθρωποι αγωνίζονται, στις γειτονιές, σε πόλεις και χωριά, στους χώρους δουλειάς, στα σχολεία και τα πανεπιστήμια, στον δημόσιο χώρο.




Υπό αυτό το πρίσμα καλούμε σε μία διήμερη εκδήλωση στις 24 και 25 Οκτώβρη στις 17.00 στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο, (Νέο Κτήριο, Αίθουσα Σάκη Καράγιωργα Ι) για να συζητήσουμε πάνω στους κεντρικούς άξονες που δομήθηκε ο αγώνας αυτός, στις διαφορετικές μεθόδους και στα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήσαμε, καθώς και να δούμε συλλογικά και συνολικά τα σημεία που οδήγησαν στη νίκη αλλά και τις αδυναμίες, τις αστοχίες και τα λάθη που υπήρξαν. Αλλά κυρίως να εστιάσουμε στη συλλογική δυνατότητα που ανοίχτηκε μέσω αυτού του αγώνα και που πρέπει να διευρύνουμε. Να ενώσουμε τις αντιστάσεις μας για να δημιουργήσουμε τους όρους μιας κοινής δύναμης και να μετατρέψουμε την αλληλεγγύη από αντανακλαστικό σε σταθερή κοινωνική σχέση. Γιατί οι αγώνες κερδίζονται όταν συναντιούνται και όταν αναγνωρίζουν και συμπληρώνουν ο ένας τον άλλον.




Την πρώτη μέρα της εκδήλωσης, στο πλαίσιο ενός πρώτου απολογισμού, θα παρουσιαστεί από πλευράς της Κοινότητας η επιλογή του συγκεκριμένου αγώνα υπό τις συγκεκριμένες συνθήκες, οι πυλώνες πάνω στους οποίους οικοδομήθηκε, οι μέθοδοι και τα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήθηκαν, με αιχμή την απεργίας πείνας ως βασικό επαναστατικό μέσο για την επίτευξη της νίκης, καθώς επίσης και τα πρώτα συμπεράσματα και η προοπτική που ανοίγεται για το επόμενο διάστημα. Θα ακολουθήσουν διευκρινιστικές ερωτήσεις από τους παρευρισκόμενους, που θα απαντηθούν από την Κοινότητα, προκειμένου να προετοιμαστεί το έδαφος για την επόμενη ημέρα της εκδήλωσης.




Τη δεύτερη μέρα συλλογικότητες, οργανώσεις και ατομικότητες θα προβούν σε τοποθετήσεις, συμπεράσματα και απολογισμό του αγώνα, της στρατηγικής και των τακτικών του, καθώς και σε κριτικές αλλά και προτάσεις για τη συνέχεια.
