title: Philippe Chanial - Proudhon, Sociologist and Activist of the Autonomy of the Social
content:
Author

: Philippe Chanial

Title

: Proudhon, Sociologist and Activist of the Autonomy of the Social

Date

: 2017

Notes

: Translated by Shaun Murdock.

Source

: “Proudhon, sociologue et militant de l’autonomie du social” Revue de la Société P.-J. Proudhon, no. 3 (2017): 9–16. Source in French: 

https://www.proudhon.net/philippe-chanial-proudhon-sociologue-et-militant-de-lautonomie-du-social/




 If Proudhon can and should be read as a forerunner of sociology, is it not above all because he was one of the first to have systematically hypothesised the autonomy of its very object, the “social”? As everyone knows, this hypothesis is foundational to sociology. The late Pierre Ansart reminded us that the heart of Proudhon’s sociological thesis is an “essential heterogeneity of the social relative to the individual”.

[1]

 Before him, the Durkheimian Célestin Bouglé emphasised that if Proudhon’s work pertains to sociological theory, it is because it shares the premise that “the meeting of individual entities generates an original reality, something greater than and different to their mere sum”. And, he continued, “arguably no thinker has made greater use of this premise than Proudhon” because “he constantly opposes, to purely individual phenomena, the notions of collective force, collective being and collective reason”.

[2]




 However, this theory of the irreducibility of the social – of the collective – to the individual does not exhaust this hypothesis of the autonomy of the social. It raises another question: that of the relationship between the social, the political and the economic. In the war of the sciences, sociology was only able to assert itself as an autonomous science by rejecting the self-proclaimed status of both political philosophy and political economy as the science of society.

[3]

 It did so by refusing that the mystery of the social order – the fact that there is, among or between people, something rather than nothing (chaos, arbitrary violence, war of all against all, etc.) or, to put it another way, the fact that people manage to give a lasting form to their coexistence – can be resolved either by identifying society with a system of power, as if the heteronomy of its political establishment, even if it were legitimate, were the absolute condition for the possibility of human coexistence; or by reducing it to a market, as if commercial ties alone were sufficient to make society. But is it not this double refusal that also defines the unique anarchism and socialism of Proudhon? Is is not this hypothesis of an autonomy of the social that enables both sociology as a scientific discipline, and socialism or anarchism as paths for emancipation? 




 Let us therefore attempt to unravel some of the simultaneously sociological and normative questions raised by this Proudhonian plea for an autonomy of the social. 




The irreducibility of the social to the political and the economic




 In his Carnets of 1852, Proudhon said: “I do politics to kill it. To put an end to politics.” This confession summarises, in a particularly polemical tone, his well-known critique of governmentalism. But this desire to end the “governmental bias” should not be reduced to a purely negative injunction to abolish all powers. It is also an invitation to accede to a “constitution of society” that is no longer based on the hierarchy of political powers but on the free organisation of social forces. It is in 

Confessions of a Revolutionary

, written, as Pierre Ansart also recalled, “in a sort of anger after the failure of a hoped-for social revolution”

[4]

, that Proudhon makes this fundamental distinction: 




 “In every society I find the distinction between two kinds of constitution, one of which I call the 

social

 constitution and the other the 

political

 constitution; the first, inherent to humanity, liberal, necessary, the development of which consists above all in weakening and gradually eliminating the second, which is essentially factitious, restrictive and transitory. The social constitution is nothing but the equilibrium of interests founded upon free 

contract

 and the organisation of 

economic forces

, which are in general: Labour, Division of Labour, Collective Force, Competition, Commerce, Money, Machines, Credit, Property, Equality in transactions, Reciprocity of guarantees, etc. The political constitution has 

authority

 as its principle. Its forms are: Class Distinctions, Separation of Powers, Administrative Centralisation, Judicial Hierarchy [...]. These two constitutions are [...] of utterly different and even incompatible natures”.

[5]




 This fit of anger is also a theoretical and normative act of force, as if society could – and should – no longer be established on the basis of political heteronomy but on the autonomy of the social, on the mutual guarantee of the liberty of all by all, which on the contrary allows us, under the supreme law of justice and contract, to do without any government. By this radical gesture, Proudhon can thus be interpreted, inseparably, as a pioneer of anarchism but also of sociology. Indeed, while Proudhon constantly suggests that it is necessary to “proceed [...] to social reform through the extermination of power and politics”, such a reform, in all its radicality, assumes a science of the social (which he calls for as early as 

The Celebration of Sunday

 in 1839) capable of asserting that the social order – and Proudhon also continues to advocate for order – is an immanent order: an order that precedes the political order, and that cannot therefore proceed from it. In this sense, this new science requires dethroning political philosophy in its age-old ambition to constitute “the” science of society, in order to better assert the primacy of the “social constitution” over the “political constitution”. 




...

content:

La street medic c'est quoi

 

?




Les 

street-médics

 sont des militant·es fournissant des premiers secours dans des contextes à risque (principalement des manifestations) où les institutions ne peuvent/veulent pas forcément être présentes directement, notamment (mais pas nécessairement) pour assurer le relai avec celles-ci.




La street medic c'est militant

!

author: Unknown
title: La France fonce vers la dictature assumée
content:
Comment appelle-t-on un régime qui déploie l'armée et l'antiterrorisme contre des manifestations, qui applique des couvre-feux, utilise une justice d'exception et veut interdire le plus grand parti de gauche

 

? Article de 

Contre-attaque




Ces trois dernières semaines, nous avons vu, contre le mouvement lycéen, des images dignes de dictatures latino-américaines des années 1970. Adolescent·es étranglé·es, mineur·es plaqué·es au sol pour être menotté·es, manifestant subissant une tentative de noyade, enfants arrêtés par milliers, fouillés à nu et frappés. Nous avons vu des mutilations béantes dans des corps de lycéen·nes et des voitures de police lancées dans des cortèges. Dans une société saine, le dixième de telles pratiques contre des mineur·es ferait tomber un régime. Mais ici, les médias ont tellement intoxiqué la population que tout cela a été présenté comme normal.




Avec le 17 octobre, nous franchissons de nouveaux caps. Les personnes qui n'étaient pas encore transformées en zombies sont descendues massivement dans les rues, et ont débordé partout. Plutôt que d'écouter, enfin, Macron appuie sur l'accélérateur. Les annonces qui tombent depuis 24 heures n'ont plus rien à envier à un régime fasciste.





L'armée face au mouvement social




Des militaires de l'opération Sentinelle seront déployés samedi 24 octobre pour «

 

sécuriser l'espace public

 

» en complément de la police. Utiliser des soldats armés en complément du maintien de l'ordre est la marque d'un pays qui bascule. C'est aussi une manière d'habituer la population à la militarisation des villes, à une ambiance de coup d'État.




L'antiterrorisme dans les rues




Le Ministre de l'Intérieur déploiera aussi des unités paramilitaires chargées de la lutte antiterroriste et de la grande criminalité : le 

RAID

 et le 

GIGN

. Ce sont des unités formées et équipées pour tuer, avec du matériel lourd. L'État français les avait envoyé dans certains quartiers après l'assassinat de Nahel. Ces unités, à la manière de colonnes infernales, avaient roulé en blindé, en tirant au fusil à pompe pour vider les rues. Un homme avait été plongé dans le coma suite à un tir en Lorraine, un autre avait été abattu à Marseille. Déployer de tels tueurs contre le mouvement social est une étape de plus vers l'obscurité. En parallèle, des hélicoptères et des blindés Centaure seront utilisés en plus grand nombre. Nos gouvernants sont en guerre.




Manifestations interdites et couvre-feux




Laurent Nunez annonce qu'il fera interdire toutes «

 

les manifestations revendicatives de nature à troubler l'ordre public

 

», toutes les manifestations «

 

non déclarées

 

», mais aussi celles déposées officiellement, «

 

s'il considère que l'organisateur ou le service d'ordre ne peut garantir qu'ils se dérouleront dans le calme

 

». Cette mesure va de pair avec les couvre-feux déjà en place dans de nombreuses villes.




Ce sont deux méthodes utilisées en temps de guerre, deux atteintes majeures aux droits fondamentaux : celui d'aller et venir, et celui d'exprimer son opinion. Avant Macron, les interdictions de manifestations étaient rarissimes. Depuis les Gilets jaunes, jamais elles n'avaient été aussi nombreuses.




La justice utilise l'arsenal réservé au grand banditisme




Gérald Darmanin a envoyé «

 

une instruction à tous les parquets de France

 

» pour leur demander de passer en qualification de «

 

criminalité organisée

 

» les manifestant·es arrêtés. C'est donc une justice exceptionnelle appliquée à des gens qui revendiquent des droits. Cela permettra d'allonger les gardes à vue de 48 heures maximum à 72 heures : trois jours en détention avant un éventuel procès. Les procédures «

 

criminelles

 

» permettent aussi de géolocaliser et écouter les contestataires. Des moyens extrêmement invasifs pour de simples actions sociales.




Reconnaissance faciale et intelligence artificielle




Le ministre de la justice annonce aussi l'utilisation de la reconnaissance faciale et de drones de surveillance, pour identifier en masse les manifestant·es, notamment ceux qui braveraient les interdictions de manifester. Là encore, si cela se passait en Chine ou en Russie, tout le monde hurlerait à la dictature. On apprend d'ailleurs que l'État a commencé à expérimenter des logiciels d'intelligence artificielle destinés à anticiper les émeutes. Une police prédictive qui analyse les flux sur les réseaux sociaux et les images de surveillance. Dystopique.




L'antiterrorisme pour des dégradations




Suite à l'incendie de la mairie de Limoges, la justice utilise des moyens destinés aux attentats. La Sous-direction anti-terroriste a été saisie de l'enquête, au prétexte de «

 

lutte contre les extrémistes violents

 

». Une nouvelle manière de classer les mouvements sociaux dans la catégorie terroriste. Le Parquet national anti-terroriste pourrait aussi être chargé de l'affaire. «

 

S'il se saisit, cela veut dire que c'est un acte terroriste, c'est-à-dire que des personnes, notamment d'ultra-gauche, auraient organisé de façon évidente cette destruction de l'hôtel de ville

 

» déroule Darmanin, aux anges. L'antiterrorisme n'a pas été utilisé contre les groupes fascistes armés.




Dissolution de 

LFI

 et manipulation des services de renseignement




Une campagne toujours plus violente se déchaîne contre 

LFI

. Depuis trois semaines, les médias accusent le parti de «

 

manipuler

 

» les lycéen·nes et d'organiser des révoltes, alors que cela devrait être le rôle de tous les partis démocratiques de protéger des enfants réprimés. Bruno Retailleau avait réclamé la dissolution du parti, une demande désormais relayée par le président du Sénat Gérard Larcher, deuxième responsable politique du pays derrière Macron.




Médiapart a recueilli le témoignage d'un commissaire du renseignement territorial qui affirme que le gouvernement lui aurait demandé «

 

d'écrire que c'est 

LFI

 qui est derrière le mouvement

 

» et les violences. Une manipulation des services pour installer un narratif mensonger, en vue d'interdire le premier parti d'opposition. Encore une fois, des méthodes dignes de la Russie de Poutine.





Article 16 et état d'urgence




Sébastien Lecornu n'a pas écarté la possibilité d'instaurer l'état d'urgence ni d'invoquer l'article 16 de la Constitution, qui accorde au président des pouvoirs exceptionnels, explique le journal anglais The Daily Telegraph. Autrement dit, un basculement dans l'état d'exception et un pouvoir total de Macron, donc une dictature, uniquement pour mater une contestation. Le tout en pleine campagne présidentielle.




Selon des sources proches du pouvoir, Macron voulait même décréter l'état d'urgence dès dimanche soir, pour lancer des perquisitions et des arrestations extra-judiciaires de masse contre «

 

l'ultra-gauche

 

». Il a finalement reculé pour cause de «

 

moyens policiers et judiciaires insuffisants

 

», déjà utilisés pour éteindre les luttes dans la rue. Cela veut dire que les rafles politiques et le basculement du régime sont déjà validés au sommet de l'État, mais qu'il a seulement été décalé pour des raisons de personnel.




«

 

Traque aux jeunes

 

» et propos racistes




«

 

Il faut des images de jeunes qu'on traque, qu'on va chercher par le col

 

» aboie Gabriel Attal sur 

BFM

. «

 

Qu'on traque

 

?

 

» lui demande la journaliste, «

 

Oui bien sûr

 

! Il faut des exemples

 

» répond le candidat macroniste. Il y a quelques années, ces propos auraient pu être prononcés par l'extrême droite radicale, et auraient fait polémique.




Sur la même chaîne, la porte-parole du gouvernement, Maud Bregeon, affirme que «

 

les premiers responsables, ce sont les racailles

 

», et ajoute qu'on «

 

voit bien sur les images quel est le type de population

 

». Des propos ouvertement racistes, alignés sur ceux de Donald Trump.




État policier, extinction des contre-pouvoirs, militarisation généralisée, xénophobie et justice d'exception, couvre-feux et interdiction de manifester : ce gouvernement non-élu déploie désormais tout le répertoire fasciste. Que faut-il de plus pour se soulever

 

? Ce sera eux ou nous. Ce sera la dictature ou la révolution.




 

 

 Article publié initialement par 

Contre-attaque

author: Unknown
title: Nous, les magasins de la rue de la République, on n'en a rien à foutre.
content:
Pour tout une partie des lyonnais, c'est une rue minable, la honte de notre époque, la honte de notre ville. Elle est absurde, elle n'a pas lieu d'être. Et pourtant, elle est plus robuste que nous : une immense révolte urbaine ne parvient à l'éteindre que quelques jours. Immédiatement, les coupables sont insultés dans le monde entier, pourchassés, sanctionnés, emprisonnés. Les magasins vont réouvrir, les travailleurs seront à nouveau exploités, la publicité fera revenir les clients, l'état d'urgence permanent sécurisera le périmètre. Les 

CB

 seront à nouveau sorties, les baskets et les téléphones passeront les portiques dans un calme retrouvé, il n'y aura à nouveau qu'une partie de la population qui pourra se les payer. La publicité, le crédit à la consommation, l'obsolescence programmée et l'exploitation des travailleurs.euses reprendra son pillage, sa casse et son saccage, avec la bénédiction du maire, du préfet, et du président.




Les gens qui n'ont pas de thunes passent leur vie à s'entendre dire : ceci te rendrait heureux, ceci te rendrait beau, ceci te rendrait libre, mais voilà, tu n'y as pas droit. En travaillant à n'importe quelle condition, en économisant beaucoup, longtemps, tu auras droit à des échantillons, mais reste à ta place car cette vie là, tu ne l'auras jamais. Ce groupe de gens qui vit là et qui consomme dans ces boutiques sans regarder les prix, tu n'en feras jamais partie.


Pourquoi les commerces sont-ils répartis de manière si injuste dans nos villes

 

? Pourquoi l'hyper-centre

 

? Pourquoi la rue de la République existe-t-elle

 

? Cette tapageuse artère géante et ses boutiques ad nauseam, ce centre commercial à ciel ouvert, de quel droit occupe-t-il le centre de notre ville

 

?


Comment ensuite s'étonner qu'elle soit la cible de toutes les rancœurs et de toutes les convoitises

 

? Pourquoi n'avez-vous pas partagé avant

 

? Quelle est cette gauche qui ne comprends pas ça

 

? Qui tolère grand maximum la destruction d'un McDo de temps en temps

 

?




Si effectivement on veut «

 

renverser le vieux monde

 

», si vraiment on est «

 

anti-capitalistes

 

», il n'y a pas un seul scénario où la rue de la République à Lyon en sort indemne. La saccager, à la première occasion, c'est plutôt la moindre des choses.




L'insurrection, ça n'est pas beau à voir, ça n'est pas propre, ça n'est pas seulement de glorieux résistants qui triomphent sur les barricades. Elle ne tolère pas dans ses rangs quelques élus venant peaufiner leur image médiatique en portant ostensiblement une écharpe tricolore. La colère d'un peuple appauvri, humilié, épuisé, elle laisse des bris de verre derrière elle, elle n'est pas respectueuse du bourgeois du centre ville, elle ne prend pas le temps de réfléchir longuement à la portée politique de tout ce qu'elle fait.


Ça c'est un luxe que certains peuvent se permettre, mais qui n'existe pas dans la vraie vie.




Nous, les magasins de la rue de la République, on n'en a rien à foutre

 

!




Un anarchistes lyonnais.

author: winter oak
title: Calling on our ancestors!
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




After I published my articles on the Druids and ancient Celtic culture this summer, Franklin O’Kanu wrote on his 

Unorthodoxy

 blog about the parallels to his own ancestral culture.




He 

said

: “What’s interesting about all of this is how two cultures, across the world, Nigerian and Celtic, have the same spiritual view of the world”. [1]




And he 

commented

 on one of my posts: “From the Yoruba and Igbo perspective, what the Celts experience in one continent is what the practitioners of Ifa experienced in another continent: the same honor of the Divine”. [2]




I have now discovered similar echoes from a reverse direction, as it were, through reading 

Of Water and the Spirit: Ritual, Magic, and Initiation in the Life of an African Shaman

 by Malidoma Patrice Somé (1956–2021).




Somé belonged to the Dagara, a million-strong people spread across the artificially-created nation-states of Ghana, the Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso – he came from the latter, which was still called French Upper Volta when he was born.










The environment and particular customs of this African people are, of course, very different from those of the ancient Celts – roasted monkey would not have been on the menu at a Beltane feast in Ireland!




But there are similarities as well. In the essay series I 

cite

 Jean Markale’s account of how at their celebratory events the Celts drank copious amounts of alcoholic drinks, producing “drunkenness, in other words the trance thanks to which one can go beyond apparent reality and see the supernatural”. [3]




He adds: “For Greek and Roman writers, Celts already had a reputation for being passionate lovers of fermented drinks. Drunkenness is an oft-occurring theme in the epics, especially in Irish accounts.




“Gods and heroes compete in their unquenchable thirst for alcohol, in the form of beer, wine or mead. A religious festival never went by without a serious drinking session”. [4]




In 

his

 book, Somé writes: “Millet beer has always been a part of major rituals. Our rituals are long, and one gets thirsty”. [5]










He explains that his tribe was said to have been taught how to make beer by the Kontomboli, mysterious otherwordly beings who introduced a woman to their astonishing brew: “When she drank it, she was delighted. She felt merry and wanted to sing”. [6]




I was also intrigued to learn that the Dagara use a twenty-based counting system, so that eighty-three would be expressed as “four times twenty plus three”. [7]




In France the same number is 

quatre-vingt-trois

, “four twenties and three”, after the old Celtic system, and we used to have the same concept in English with a score, meaning twenty, using which eight-three is “four score and three”.




A more important connection between ancient European and African societies has been the effects of colonisation.




From an African perspective it must be strange to hear a white man claim to be the victim of colonialism, but such is the case.




Following the destruction of our indigenous culture by the Roman empire and its religious wing, we were then 

colonised

 by the empire of usury and commerce and used as fodder for its insatiable industrial Leviathan. [8]










With our true identities further smothered, our vital energy was hijacked to allow that same empire to enslave and exploit other peoples across the world, including the Dagara.




Somé writes: “My own elders had experienced French colonialism and the culture of the West as a force that used violence as a means to eradicate traditional lifeways.




“They had seen their own youth stolen from them as they vainly struggled against the incursions of these intruders.




“During these years, in which my people were trying to make sense of a people whose every action seemed to go against the natural order of things, creating chaos, death, and destruction, the sense of unified community that sustained their tribal life was profoundly destabilized. These foreigners seemed to have no respect for life, tradition, or the land itself…




“In spite of the best efforts of all my people, the whites kept on coming; kept on doing whatever they pleased; and kept on taking more and more of our land, our beliefs and our lives”. [9]




“It is a sad thing to realize how much my people have lost and how much yet of our reality is to be buried in the pit of oblivion”. [10]




Although Upper Volta officially became independent in 1960 (it became Burkina Faso in 1984), this was really just a sleight of hand by the usurious puppetmasters who have always been behind European imperialism.










Somé condemns “this new colonialism, whose goal is to place the newly independent countries into a state of perpetual indebtedness”. [11]




He adds: “It is important to understand that modern Africa does not exist as it is by the will of its leaders, but by the will of the very powers that divided it between them”. [12]




The Church played an important role in destroying Dagara culture, as it did in destroyng Druidic culture.




Somé laments: “Religious colonialism tortures the soul. It creates an atmosphere of fear, uncertainty, and general suspicion. The worst thing is that it uses the local people to enforce itself”. [13]




He had personal experience of this religious colonialism, with his own father falling prey to its influence and refusing to carry out the traditional rite of burying two clay pots of root juice following the birth of twin chidren.




“The truth was that he did not want to offend the white priest, appearing like a pagan devil worshiper in his eyes. My father genuinely feared going to hell”. [14]










This refusal was followed, not coincidentally in his son’s view, by the deaths of both girl twins, a brother and then their heartbroken mother.




Somé, the offspring of a second wife, was then literally kidnapped from his village home at the age of four and brought up in a Jesuit school where, having been taught some French, the boys were forbidden from speaking their native Dagara language, even amongst themselves, this being “a sin”. [15]




When he was twelve, he was transferred to a Jesuit seminary to be trained as a priest: “This titanic religious establishment was the dream-come-true of the missionary crusade that had followed imperialism into the continent of Africa. The kids came from everywhere in French West Africa: Mali, Niger, Togo, the Ivory Coast, and Benin”. [16]




It was here that Somé first began expressing his opposition to colonialism, particularly in defiance of an African priest/teacher called Father Joe, whom he describes as “a fine specimen of European brainwashing and indoctrination… he had been brainwashed to brainwash us”. [17]




He recounts that he once told Father Joe in a class discussion about a certain textbook: “I am suggesting that perhaps colonialism cannot be justified on the grounds that some people decided it was their right to disturb the quiet lives of others.




“Obviously this book was written by someone who thinks it is right to put whole villages into forced labor or to summarily liquidate them. Somebody who does not care about other people!” [18]










Young Somé’s reward for this insight was to be told he was becoming an “ideological delinquent” and bashed with Father Joe’s rubber truncheon. [19]




Colonialism goes hand in hand with modernity – the whole process of its insatiable industrial gobbling-up of nature and human lives is presented as badly needed “

development

” which “underdeveloped” peoples have the right to enjoy. [20]




Remarks Somé: “Indigenous people find their rhythms in nature. Westerners, on the other hand, seem to seek meaning in the realm of the machine, where one finds neither peace not wholeness, but ceaseless movement. In the West, people are always frenetically rushing somewhere in the countless lanes of the multiple highways of progress”. [21]




The author writes about a vision of that strange foreign world which was communicated to him by his beloved shaman grandfather on his deathbed: “Grandfather had taken me into a world of wonder, for I myself was transformed. Thousands of images of a civilization I had never seen rushed at me, all alive and real: immense metal birds gliding high above the sky, their bellies loaded with humans; dwellings and roads covering the earth as far as the eye could see; houses that challenged the vault of heaven and dwarfed men, trees, and anything around them”. [22]




He also relates a dream he once had, which reminds me of René Guénon’s 

understanding

 that the predomination of metal in the modern world is an aspect of our ongoing civilizational 

descent

 into a 

lower

 (mineral) phase of existence. [23]










Somé recalls: “The diviner picked out another item, a metallic object. Holding it, he spoke of faraway countries and cultures of wires and metals. He described men riding in strange boxes that moved by themselves; restless, moving parts hidden inside these boxes; and many other mysterious metal things not of his world”. [24]




For indigenous peoples everywhere, the shock of encountering industrial society for the first time must have been the equivalent of some ancient Celts suddenly time-travelling 2,000 years into an unrecognisable and dystopian future.




Somé, whose life straddled two very different worlds, says it is difficult even to find the right words in English to describe indigenous African life and thinking.




“One of my greatest problems was that the things I talk about here did not happen in English; they happened in a language that has a very different mindset about reality.




“There is usually a significant violence done to anything being translated from one culture to another. Modern American English, which seems to me better suited for quick fixes and the thrill of a consumer culture, seems to falter when asked to communicate another person’s world view”. [25]




“Every year I have to return home to my elders, not to visit them, but to be cleansed. After several years of doing that, I have come to understand that being in the West is like being caught in a highly radioactive environment. Without this periodic checkup, I will lose my ability to function”. [26]










Being ripped out of village life, says Somé (

pictured

), left him with “anger and inner turmoil” [27] as a young man and, despite being initiated back into his tribe, he never completely regained his belonging – “I can’t even think in my native language”. [28]




He describes what was going on his head during this delayed initiation at the age of twenty: “Myriads of questions were slowing down my journey toward traditional knowledge.




“I longed for debates, for theories, for criticism: clearly a legacy of the white world. But, I kept telling myself, one cannot continually ask questions. One cannot always sculpt theories to frame experience, or top experience with the roof of theory.




“The techniques of indigenous learning were revealing themselves before my eyes, sweeping away my preconceived notions of how learning was accomplished.




“The contrast between this state of mind and what I had been accustomed to at the seminary was the same as the difference between liquid and solid. It seemed to me that Dagara knowledge was liquid in the sense that what I was learning was living, breathing, flexible and spontaneous. What I was learning made sense only in terms of relationship. It was not fixed, even when it appeared to be so…










“By contrast, I could see that the Western knowledge I had been given had the nature of a solid because it is wrapped in logical rhetoric to such a degree that it is stiff and inflexible.




“The learning one gets from a book, from the canons of the written tradition, is very different from the living, breathing knowledge that an elder has to offer – and different from the knowledge that comes from within, from the soul”. [29]




“Unlearning” [30] his 16 years of enforced European education was not something that could be fully achieved.




“It dawned on me that literacy, from the traditional point of view, occupies a space within the psyche that is reserved for something else. So my knowing how to read and write meant that I would never be able to access certain traditional knowledge”. [31]




A chapter in one of my own (written and Western!) books, 

Nature, Essence and Anarchy

, is entitled ‘Denying reality: from nominalism to 

Newthink

‘.




Here I 

complain

 of a modern ideological manipulation which is built on “a misunderstanding of the relationship between human language and actual reality”. [32]




I write: “Postmodernists have fallen into the nominalist trap of believing that the reality of human language and thought – the subjective truth of human beings – is more real than actual objective truth. They mistake word for reality, shadow for object”. [33]










Somé makes the same point when he insists: “Reality exists independently from language”. [34] “Remember: the word is not the meaning and the meaning is not the word”. [35]




“Words entrap meaning , torture it, slice it into pieces the way a butcher cuts the meat of a slaughtered animal and serves it to us. The speed of silence has profound respect for the integrity of meaning as an entity separate from language. In silence, meaning is no longer heard, but felt; and feeling is the best hearing, the best instrument for recording meaning. Meaning is made welcome as it is and treated with respect”. [36]




The indigenous outlook portrayed by Somé is essentially the same thing as the 

via antiqua

 of the European Middle Ages [37] and “

the completely different way of thinking

” I found embraced by the ancient Celts. [38]




It is a deep and ancient wisdom, a life-rooted value system that had to be swept away by the 

via moderna

, the industrial 

Newthink

, in order to turn us all into disempowered slaves of the imperialist 

Mega-Racket

. [39]




This “progress” is surely the worst thing ever to have been experienced by humankind and its architects are surely the worst human beings ever to have lived. As Somé notes with sadness: “As modernity crept into my village, everything I held dear in my heart was disappearing”. [40]










I have shown how the ancient Celts made no distinction between history and myth and “their thinking was not square or linear, but spiralling and spiritual, capable of embracing paradox, of soaring beyond the rules of the material world”. [41]




Likewise, Somé explains: “The world of the Dagara also does not distinguish between reality and imagination… In the realm of the sacred, this concept is taken even further, for what is magic but the ability to focus thought and energy to get results on the human plane?”. [42]




Key to this different way of thinking and being is our all-round sense of 

withness

. [43] Somé declares: “I understood that what makes a village a village is the underlying presence of the unfathomable joy of being connected to everyone and everything”. [44]




Traditional customs have the purpose of strengthening this connection, not least through drumming, singing and dancing.




Somé describes one particular dance where he “lost the analytical part of my mind and was drawn irresistibly into participation”. [45]




He 

felt

 the presence of the others around him: “The feeling was wonderful. Never before had I experienced something so real, so true, and so befitting a human being”. [46]










He also remarks: “When one of our elders carves a double-headed serpent or an amphibious mammal, he is not just creating an image out of his imagination, but cooperating with the spirits of those beings for the maintenance of the natural order”. [47]




“The purpose of ritual is to create harmony between the human world and the world of the gods, ancestors, and nature”. [48] “A stable community reflects the laws of nature and dances with them”. [49]




“It is my belief that the present state of restlessness that traps the modern individual has its roots in a dysfunctional relationship with the ancestors.




“In many non-Western cultures, the ancestors have an intimate and absolutely vital connection with the world of the living. They are always available to guide, to teach, and to nurture. They represent one of the pathways between the knowledge of this world and the next.




“Most importantly – and paradoxically – they embody the guidelines for successful living – all that is most valuable about life. Unless the relationship between the living and the dead is in balance, chaos results”. [50]










Somé warns us that even in a stable community there will always be evil people who set out to do harm to others – those who are “possessed by bad spirits”. [51]




He stresses that “the indigenous world is not a place where everything flows in harmony, but one in which people must be constantly on the alert to detect and to correct imbalances and illnesses in both communal and individual life”. [52]




This is pretty much my response to those who ask me how anarchists, if we achieved a free society, would hope to keep it that way in the face of those who would seek to conquer and dominate it.




The thing is that the anarchist philosophy, like the indigenous one, 

includes the understanding that human beings are not perfect and that we need to be permanently on our guard

.




This understanding acts as kind of psychological innoculation to the danger of falling under the domination of malevolent individuals or groups and, together with the deep-seated belief that freedom is worth dying for, is a powerful defensive tool.




The ancient Celts believed that 

through nature we can touch the divine

 [53] and that is true of pretty much all indigenous human spirituality, including that of the Dagara.










Somé writes: “Grandfather used to call the rain ‘the erotic ritual between heaven and Earth’. The rain represented the seeds sown in the Earth’s womb by heaven, her roaring husband, to further life…




“The grasses that pop out of the Earth’s womb shortly after the rain are called the numberless children of Earth who will serve humankind’s need for nourishment. The rainy season is the season of life”. [54]




“I could even hear nature, its relentless vibration of love and its slow movements. Its nurturing power fed me through my nose and my pores, sustaining my vital senses”. [55]




One mystical encounter in Somé’s account, which happened while was contemplating a tree as part of his initiation, could have formed part of my 2017 book 

The Green One

. [56]







Out of nowhere, in the place where the tree had stood, appeared a tall woman dressed in black from head to foot… She wore a veil over her face, but I could tell that behind this veil was an extremely beautiful and powerful entity.

I could sense the intensity emanating from her, and that intensity exercised an irrestistible magnetic pull. To give into that pull was like drinking water after a day of wandering in the desert…

I had to lower my eyes. When I looked again, she had lifted her veil, revealing an unearthly face. She was green, light green. Even her eyes were green, though very small and luminescent. She was smiling and her teeth were the color of violet and had light emanating from them.

The greenness in her had nothing to do with the color of her skin. She was green from the inside out, as if her body were filled with green fluid. I do not know how I knew this, but this green was the expression of immeasurable love. [57]







The “Green Lady”, as Somé calls her, is clearly a representation not just of nature, but of our love-filled 

belonging

 to nature and thus also to the divine of which nature is an earthly manifestation.










A final connection between ancient Celtic and ancient Dagara thinking is the idea of a life mission, or quest.




Markale 

tells us

 regarding the Celts: “Every human being, according to druidic thinking, has a ‘mission’ to achieve something… each human being has a role to play to 

perfect

 the world, to 

complete

 it and this completion can only be brought about by individual action within collective action”. [58]




And Somé points outs: “For the Dagara, every person is an incarnation, that is, a spirit who has taken on a body. So our true nature is spiritual. The world is where one comes to carry out specific projects.




“A birth is therefore the arrival of someone, usually an ancestor that somebody already knows, who has important tasks to do here”. [59]




In order to carry out our tasks we have to know who we are, who we are 

meant to be

. The young Dagara men are told during their initiation: “No one’s center is like someone else’s. Find your own center, not the center of your neighbor; not the center of your father or mother or family or ancestor but that center which is yours and yours alone”. [60]










Somé comments: “This kind of education is nothing less than a return to one’s true self, that is, to the divine within us”. [61] “I began to realize that everything I had experienced in my month of initiation was about learning how to recall what I already knew”. [62]




“At the seminary, I had grown away from myself into a mold that tried to make me someone I wasn’t, while all the while I craved for myself. As long as we are not ourselves, we will try to be what other people are. If these people are also not themselves, the result is terrible. During the Dagara initiation process, I grew into myself. The problems I had became resolved as I entered into my own true nature”. [63]




Colonisation of all kinds 

prevents

 us from being ourselves. The societies we live in are geared to the requirements of the colonisers, not to the people. They are shaped by 

their

 rules, 

their

 attitude towards us – 

their

 contempt for us and 

their

 fear of our possible rebellion.




Without the nourishing soil of a world rooted in their own cultural values and reflecting the way they see and experience life, an individual will inevitably find it immensely difficult to find their true self and their task in life.




But perhaps that is a good thing in that this inner effort will harden their determination and sharpen their instincts in their struggle against the oppressing empire.










Somé’s own individual task was to act as a bridge between the Dagara people and the people of the West – his first name Malidoma roughly means “be friends with the stranger/enemy” and this role was apparently known before his birth. [64]




We can certainly learn from what he communicates to us, including the idea of “conjuring up the world of the ancestors for protection against evil forces” [65] and “restoring the old wisdom of the ancestors”. [66]




Today we are told we are not allowed to think that way – by a judeo-supremacist mafia that seems to be interested in 

nothing else

 than its 

own

 past and self-interest.




Remembering who we are, not just in terms of our tribal ancestry but in terms of our belonging to divine nature, gives us a solid psychological basis for resisting the great evil that is industrial imperialism.




But the process does not end with the internal transformation. As village elder and mentor Guisso told Somé: “You cannot be who you truly are until you can put what you remember into action”. [67]

author: Ben Radford
title: US must end its cruel blockade of Cuba
content:
Every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) has overwhelmingly voted to end the United States government’s cruel and illegal economic blockade of Cuba. One-hundred-and-sixty-five countries voted last year for the resolution on the “Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba”, with just six against.

This year’s vote, on October 28, takes place as escalating US economic warfare against Cuba is causing a devastating humanitarian crisis. The blockade’s impacts have been characterised as a “silent genocide”, severely restricting Cubans’ access to food, medicine, equipment and fuel, and impacting every aspect of daily life.

The Cuban government submitted its annual report to the UNGA in September, detailing last year’s impacts of the US blockade. Between March last year and February this year, the blockade inflicted more than US$8 billion worth of damages.

The economic cost of just four days of the blockade amounts to the cost of all fuel imports needed to meet Cuba’s demand.

On top of existing strangulation mechanisms, the US government imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, claiming that the country posed an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to US national security.

The US announced tariffs on goods from countries that, directly or indirectly, sold or provided oil to Cuba. Following the US’s January 3 attacks on Venezuela, it also blocked all Venezuelan oil shipments to the country.

The energy blockade is the reason for widespread blackouts, as well disruptions to water supply, waste collection and transport.

The fuel shortages are severely impacting hospital operations, including treatments that require a steady energy supply, such as haemodialysis. There are harrowing reports of surgeons having to perform operations by mobile phone lights, due to the blackouts.

The US blockade has affected Cubans’ access to vital treatment and medicine. One example is Cuba’s cancer survival rates, which, while still higher than many low- and middle-income countries, have dropped from 85% to 65%.

Cuba’s infant mortality has risen from 4 out of 1000 live births in 2018 to 9.9 last year — a 148% rise.

Cuban authorities say that the current transport crisis is more acute than during the “Special Period” in the 1990s following the collapse of the Soviet Union, which plunged Cuba into a prolonged economic crisis. Fuel shortages have affected refrigerated transport, preventing more than 30,000 children from receiving vaccines.

In May, the US imposed a regime of secondary sanctions against governments and companies that invest in or trade with Cuba.

For example, the US Office of Foreign Assets Control has imposed fines on US companies for handling cargo shipments bound for Cuba and providing services for people living in the country.

Over the past year, 34 international banking institutions suspended or declined to conduct operations with Cuba, citing risks of secondary sanctions.

Several airlines have ceased operations in Cuba and many international hotel chains also abandoned management agreements for hotels, citing the risks posed by the secondary sanctions regime. These sanctions — along with other US measures — have contributed to the collapse in Cuba’s tourism industry.

“The application of these measures has produced a sophisticated mechanism of asphyxiation directed at the Cuban population, exceeding by far the levels of pressure historically imposed over decades,” the annual report said.

It also notes that the blockade has caused US$3.9 trillion worth of damages since it was imposed. However, it said the impacts go far beyond economic losses, causing suffering, illness and death.

The US blockade of Cuba violates not just international law, but any semblance of humanity.

The US government has made its intention of achieving “regime change” in Cuba by the end of the year very clear; it is openly considering the possibility of military attacks. This has been the US’s policy since Cubans overthrew the US-backed Fulgencio Batista military dictatorship in 1959 and set about implementing a planned economy based on meeting people’s needs.

Since then, the US has undertaken or sponsored terrorist attacks, a military invasion and an economic blockade against the Cuban people, with the explicit aim of bringing about “hunger, desperation and overthrow of government”, as revealed by a 1960 US memorandum.

The Cuban Embassy in Australia told Green Left that despite the challenges facing Cuba, it “remains committed to its social development and international cooperation”.

It noted that the Australian government voted in favour of last year’s UNGA resolution, calling for an end to the US blockade on Cuba.

The embassy encouraged the Labor government to engage in “constructive dialogue and to explore practical avenues of cooperation with Cuba in areas such as health, education, disaster resilience, renewable energy and scientific research”.

“At a time when the world faces complex economic, environmental and humanitarian challenges, greater engagement and cooperation with Cuba, rather than continued sanctions, would benefit both the Cuban people and the international community.”

Since 1963, Cuba has sent more than 600,000 health professionals overseas to provide care and train personnel, mostly in low-income regions. The US aims to destroy Cuba’s model of medical internationalism, pressuring countries to terminate often decades-long Cuban medical missions.

More than 160 countries have benefited from Cuba’s medical internationalism, including its pandemic and disaster response to free training for tens of thousands of medical personnel.

The embassy also said that it “deeply appreciates” the Australian solidarity movement with Cuba, saying it has “demonstrated a steadfast commitment to friendship and cooperation between our peoples” over many years.

“Through educational activities, public advocacy, cultural exchanges and community engagement, solidarity organisations and supporters across Australia have played a valuable role in raising awareness about the impact of the blockade and in promoting closer people-to-people ties.

“The annual vote at the United Nations is an important reminder of the overwhelming international rejection of the blockade and the need for policies that promote development, mutual respect and people-to-people exchange.”

United Nations General Assembly

title: Fon düzenlemesi Meclis'te kabul edildi
content:
Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'nun (SPK) 17 Eylül 2026'da tasfiyesine karar verdiği yatırım fonlarına ilişkin kanun teklifi, dün (22 Ekim) Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi (TBMM) Genel Kurulu'nda kabul edilerek yasalaştı.




Düzenleme, 7 portföy yönetim şirketine ait 131 yatırım fonunu ve yaklaşık 455 bin 758 yatırımcıyı kapsıyor.




Kanunla fonların tasfiye işlemlerinin SPK'nin gözetim ve denetiminde yürütülmesi, hukuka aykırı işlemlerle fonlardan çıkarılan varlıkların geri alınması ve yatırımcıların zararlarının karşılanması amaçlanıyor.



















Muhalefet "soygunun kılıfı" dedi, iktidar oyladı: Fon düzenlemesinde ilk 5 madde geçti




22 Ekim 2026










Kimlere ne kadar ödeme yapılacak?




Düzenlemeye göre, tasfiye kapsamındaki fonlarda net yatırım tutarı 1 milyon TL'nin altında olan yatırımcılara yatırdıkları tutarı aşmamak koşuluyla ara ödeme yapılabilecek.




Net yatırım tutarı 1 milyon TL ve üzerinde olan yatırımcılar ise en fazla 1 milyon TL ara ödeme alabilecek.




Ödemeler, fonların tasfiye mal varlığından karşılanacak. Ara ödemelerin nasıl yapılacağına ilişkin usul ve esasları SPK belirleyecek.




17 Eylül ve öncesinde Türkiye Elektronik Fon Alım Satım Platformu'na (TEFAS) iletilen ancak fonların ödeme yükümlülüklerini yerine getirememesi veya pay fiyatlarının açıklanmaması nedeniyle sonuçlandırılamayan iade talepleri de tasfiye kapsamına alındı.




Fon yöneticileri sorumlu tutulacak




Kanunla, fonlardan hukuka aykırı biçimde çıkarılan varlıkların geri alınması için Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu (TMSF) yetkilendirildi.




Fonlarda oluşan zarar ve kayıplardan öncelikle fonların kurucusu veya yöneticisi olan portföy yönetim şirketleri sorumlu olacak.




Tahsil edilen tutarlar, gerekli kesintiler yapıldıktan sonra hak sahibi yatırımcılara dağıtılacak.




Düzenlemeye göre ödemelerde Hazine veya başka bir kamu kaynağı kullanılmayacak. Tasfiye işlemleri, fonların mevcut varlıkları ve geri kazanılan kaynaklar üzerinden yürütülecek.



















Abdülkadir Selvi: "Fon rezaleti AKP'ye 3-6 puan kaybettirdi"




20 Ekim 2026










66 fonun normal tasfiye süreci tamamlandı




Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, 20 Ekim'de yaptığı açıklamada, tasfiye kapsamındaki 131 fondan 66'sının normal tasfiye sürecinin tamamlandığını duyurmuştu.




Şimşek, 7 portföy yönetim şirketinden 3'ünün tasfiyesinin tamamlandığını, 45 bin 747 hesaba toplam 40,8 milyar TL ödeme yapıldığını belirtmişti.




Kanunun kabul edilmesinin ardından, kalan fonlardaki kaynakların durumuna göre yatırımcılara 1 milyon TL'ye kadar ara ödeme yapılması öngörülüyor.




(NÖ)

author: Unknown
title: Avrupa'da aşırı sıcakların bilançosu: 50 binden fazla can kaybıyla son 26 yılın en yüksek seviyesi
content:
Avrupa'da bu yaz yaşanan kavurucu sıcaklarda kentsel bölgelerde 50 binden fazla kişinin hayatını kaybettiği tahmin edilirken, bu ölümlerin üçte ikisinin iklim değişikliğinin etkileri nedeniyle gerçekleştiği belirlendi.

Imperial College London ve Londra Hijyen ve Tropikal Tıp Okulundan bilim insanları, Avrupa Birliği'nin 27 üyesi, İngiltere, Norveç ve İsviçre olmak üzere 30 ülkenin nüfusunun yaklaşık yüzde 40'ının yaşadığı 854 kentsel bölgede aşırı sıcakların can kayıplarına etkisini inceledi.

Araştırmacılar, sıcaklık kayıtlarını ve geçmişte sıcaklık ve ölüm oranları arasında gözlemlenen ilişkiye dayalı modellemeleri kullanarak, 2000-2026 yıllarındaki yaz dönemlerinde her bir kentsel bölgede sıcaklara bağlı olarak beklenen fazladan ölümlerin sayısını tahmin etti. Bu yöntemin, ulusal sağlık otoritelerinin daha sonra yayımladığı resmi aşırı sıcaklık kaynaklı ölüm istatistikleriyle tutarlı sonuçlar verdiği görüldü.

Buna göre, bilim insanları söz konusu ülkelerde bu yaz yaşanan kavurucu sıcaklara bağlı olarak 50 binden fazla kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini tahmin ediyor. Söz konusu can kayıplarının üçte ikisi fosil yakıtların kullanılmasından kaynaklanan iklim değişikliğine bağlanıyor.

Aşırı sıcaklar nedeniyle 2026 yazında yaşanan ölümler, 2000'den beri tutulan kayıtlardaki en yüksek seviye oldu. Yüksek sıcaklar nedeniyle 2022'de 29 bin, 2003'te 28 bin ölüm meydana geldiği belirlenmişti.

Bilim insanlarının tahminlerine göre, ölümlerin yaklaşık üçte biri 17 Haziran-1 Temmuz döneminde yaşandı. Bu dönemde, bölgenin tamamında günlük ortalama sıcaklıklar 1991-2020 ortalamasını 5 dereceden fazla aştı.

En ağır etkilenen bölgeler arasında ise en yüksek sıcaklık değerleri ve can kaybının görüldüğü Güney ve Batı Avrupa'daki kentler yer aldı.

İngiltere gibi genellikle daha serin olan Kuzey Avrupa ülkelerinin kentsel bölgelerinde ise yaklaşık 4 bin 500 kişinin sıcaklık nedeniyle hayatını kaybettiği tahmin ediliyor.

Sıcağa bağlı ölümler, ağırlıklı olarak ileri yaştaki insanları etkilese de analiz edilen kentsel bölgelerde bu yaz 65 yaşın altındaki yaklaşık 6 bin kişinin sıcaklar nedeniyle hayatını kaybettiği değerlendiriliyor.

Yaz mevsimi, özellikle Batı Avrupa'da art arda yaşanan aşırı sıcak hava dalgalarıyla şiddetlendi ve halk sağlığı üzerinde ciddi etkiler yarattı. Batı Avrupa, en yüksek sıcaklık anomalisinin görüldüğü bölge oldu.

Yaz mevsiminin genelinde sıcaklıklar 1991-2020 ortalamasının yaklaşık 2,9 derece üzerine çıkarken, bazı günlerde bu fark 12 dereceye kadar ulaştı.

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 23 octobre
content:
Dans l'éphéméride des luttes du 23 octobre, on hésite entre grève insurrectionnelle et changement de méthodes. Mais ce qui est sûr, c'est qu'on se rend encore une fois bien compte du rôle contre-révolutionnaire du Parti Communiste.




1886 :

 A Bruxelles, parution du premier numéro du journal communiste-anarchiste "La Liberté".




 

 

 

 




1905 :

 A Ekaterinoslav, en Russie, la police tire sur les ouvriers grévistes de l'usine Briansk, faisant trois blessés. Un chef de l'usine sera abattu le 26 mars 1907 en représailles par l'anarchiste Mezhenniy.




1915 :

 A New York, 33.000 femmes marchent sur la Cinquième Avenue pour exiger leur droit de vote.




1921 :

 Dans toute l'Europe, des manifestations massives ont lieu en soutien aux anarchistes italiens Sacco et Vanzetti, menacés d'être condamnés à mort aux Etats-Unis.




1956 :

 En Hongrie, grève générale insurrectionnelle : 

"interdite puis autorisée par le gouvernement, la manifestation rassemble en fin d'après-midi 100 à 150 mille manifestants, étudiante au départ, elle se grossit à partir de 17 heures des ouvriers qui sortent des usines.


20 heures : le gros de la manifestation reste place du Gouvernement, réclamant le retour de Nagy au gouvernement ; une partie des manifestants se rend au monument Staline, la statue est abattue, une délégation se rend au palais de la radio pour faire lire les résolutions.


Refus de la radio qui est gardée par 5 à 600 AVH (police politique) ; vers 23 heures la police politique ouvre le feu sur les manifestants qui essaient de pénétrer dans le palais de la radio, des unités de l'armée hongroise envoyées en renfort se laissent désarmer par les manifestants ou passent de leur côté ; des ouvriers retournent vers les usines où les équipes de nuit arrêtent le travail et s'emparent des dépôts d'armes de la milice ouvrière et des stocks des usines d'armement ; un peu partout dans Budapest, des combats s'engagent contre la police politique

". 

Repris de la chronologie des événements publiés dans "

Socialisme ou Barbarie

, 

L'insurrection Hongroise

". 


Cette insurrection ouvrière sera sauvagement réprimée par le pouvoir soviétique dès le 4 novembre à l'aide de chars d'assaut. Le Parti Communiste Français se déclare favorable à la répression. Le numéro de Socialisme ou barbarie contient notamment un "questionnaire" aux membres du PCF qui critique très durement le parti et est assez drôle à lire.




1977 :

 - A Milan, la colonne Walter Alasia des Brigades Rouges tire huit coups de pistolet dans les jambes du conseiller communal de la Démocratie Chrétienne (le parti au pouvoir depuis l'après-guerre) Carlo Vincezo Arienti.




 En France, le journal 'Libération' est occupé par 150 autonomes suite à la prise de position du journal vis-à-vis des prisonnier-e-s de la Fraction Armée Rouge (RAF) mort-e-s en prison quelques jours plus tôt.




1983 :

 - Dans toute l'Europe, de grandes manifestations antinucléaires ont lieu.




 A Beyrouth, un attentat a lieu contre les armées française et américaine, tuant 297 soldats.




1988 :

 En Italie, des prisonniers des Brigades Rouges écrivent dans un document que la période de la lutte armée est terminée.




2001 :

 En Irlande du Nord, l'IRA Provisoire commence le désarmement.




2014 :

 A Athènes, le cabinet médical d'un médecin membre du parti néonazi Aube Dorée est ravagé.




2016 :

 - A Calais, des affrontements ont lieu contre la police à quelques jours du début du démantèlement de la Jungle.




 A Brême en Allemagne, 18 véhicules de l'armée partent en fumée aux premières heures. Les dégâts sont estimés à près de 15 millions d'euros. Ce qui n'est pas sans rappeler l'incendie de 42 engins de l'armée à Dresde le 

13 avril

 2009, ce qui avait été revendiqué par un groupe autonome antimilitariste.


 

 

 

 




Voir 

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 23 octobre.

author: Unknown
title: Le sens de l'émeute / une émission de Minuit Décousu
content:
Pendant que l'ensemble du monde politique s'occupe à bomber son torse de facho, personne ne semble essayer de comprendre comment et pourquoi on arrive à avoir des dizaines de milliers de personnes qui cassent, brûlent et pillent des trucs dans tout le pays. Comment et pourquoi on a vu des émeutes historiques ce 17 octobre. Comment et pourquoi tous ces gens ont pris le risque d'être arrêté, emprisonné, blessé ou mutilé pour laisser éclater leurs colère.




Des plateaux télé aux réseaux sociaux, la figure fantasmé du casseur bas du front lobotomisé par 

LFI

, l'ultragauche, les frères musulmans ou peut-être même les francs-maçons évacue la dimension politique de l'évènement. Pourtant rien que son ampleur montre bien qu'il se passe quelque chose qui dépasse à la fois le pilotage politique et le plaisir de taper dans une vitre ou une planche d'

OSB

. Alors comme d'habitude, on a décidé de faire chauffer nos micros pour s'y coller, cette semaine dans Minuit Décousu, on se demande ce qu'est le sens de la casse.




L'émission s'écoute sur notre 

audioblog

, ici, et un peu partout en podcast. Bonne écoute

 

!







Minuit Décousu, c'est un fanzine radiophonique nocturne sur 

Radio Canut

 (Lyon et alentours), 

Radio Vassivière

 (Limousin) et 

Cause Commune

 (Paris/

IDF

). Semaine après semaine pendant une heure, on en découd avec la nuit et on tire les fils de sons, de textes, d'archives et de voix qui s'entremêlent.

title: İngiltere hükümetinden olası tehditlere karşı hazırlık çağrısı: Vatandaşlara gıda ve su stoku tavsiyesi
content:
İngiltere hükümeti, aşırı hava olayları, siber saldırılar ve devlet kaynaklı güvenlik tehditlerine karşı vatandaşlara en az 3 gün yetecek kadar gıda ve su stoku yapmaları tavsiyesinde bulundu.

İngiltere hükümetinin başlattığı "Be Ready (Hazırlıklı Ol)" kampanyası kapsamında, hanelerin doğal afetler, siber saldırılar ve kritik altyapıda yaşanabilecek kesintilere karşı hazırlıklı olması amaçlanıyor.

Kampanya kapsamında vatandaşlara, kişi başına günlük 3 litre olmak üzere 3 gün için toplam 9 litre içme suyu, bozulmayan gıda ürünleri, ilk yardım malzemeleri, el feneri, battaniye, nakit para ve pilli radyo bulundurmaları tavsiye edildi.

Acil durumlarda elektrik, su, telefon ve internet hizmetlerinin kesintiye uğrayabileceği, tedarik zincirlerinde de aksaklıklar yaşanabileceği belirtildi.

İngiltere Savunma Bakanı Wes Streeting, ülkenin Telford kentindeki bir savunma sanayisi tesisinde yaptığı konuşmada, ülkenin doğal afetler, gelişmiş siber saldırılar ve devlet destekli terörizm gibi tehditlere karşı daha hazırlıklı olması gerektiğini bildirdi.

Rusya ve diğer düşman devletlerin günlük yaşamda kullanılan kritik altyapıları hedef alabileceği uyarısında bulunan Streeting, "Bu tehditler varsayımsal değil, gerçek. Başka yerlerde değil, giderek daha fazla burada karşımıza çıkıyor" ifadelerini kullandı. Bakan Streeting, hanelerin ve işletmelerin olası krizlere nasıl karşılık vereceklerini önceden planlamalarının önemini vurguladı.

Streeting, BBC'nin "Question Time" programında yaptığı açıklamada da hükümetin amacının halkı korkutmak olmadığına işaret ederek, "İnsanların tetikte olmalarını, ancak paniğe kapılmamalarını istiyoruz" dedi. Hazırlıkların belirli bir tehdide yönelik olmadığını vurgulayan Streeting, gıda ve su stoklarının elektrik kesintileri ya da siber saldırı nedeniyle ödeme sistemlerinin çalışmaması gibi durumlarda faydalı olabileceğini belirtti.

İngiltere Güvenlik Bakanı Dan Jarvis de vatandaşların basit önlemler almasının, acil durumlarda güvenlik ve kurtarma ekiplerinin daha fazla desteğe ihtiyaç duyan kişilere öncelik vermesini sağlayacağını ifade etti. Hükümetin bu girişimle ülkenin krizlere karşı dayanıklılığını artırmayı hedeflediğini belirten Jarvis, Fransa, İrlanda ve Hollanda'da da benzer hazırlık kampanyalarının yürütüldüğünü hatırlattı.

Dünya genelinde çok sayıda internet sitesinde kullanılan PHP programlama dilinde kritik güvenlik açığı tespit edilmesinin ardından İngiltere'de 32 kamu hizmetine ait internet sitesi tedbir amacıyla erişime kapatılmıştı.

author: Unknown
title: İzmir’de kereste ve sunta deposunda yangın
content:
İzmir — İzmir'in Buca ilçesinde içerisinde kereste ve sunta türü malzemelerin bulunduğu depoda çıkan yangın, itfaiye ekiplerinin müdahalesiyle söndürüldü. Yangında ölen ya da yaralanan olmazken, depo kullanılamaz hale geldi.

Seyhan Mahallesi 722/6 Sokak’taki içerisinde kereste ve sunta türü malzemelerin bulunduğu depoda saat 03.15 sıralarında yangın çıktı. Kısa sürede büyüyen alevler, deponun tamamını sardı. Çevredekilerin ihbarı üzerine olay yerine itfaiye, polis ve sağlık ekipleri sevk edildi.

Çok sayıda itfaiye ekibinin alevlere müdahale ettiği sırada deponun sac çatısı çöktü. Yangın, ekiplerin yoğun çalışmasıyla kontrol altına alınarak söndürüldü. Yangında ölen ya da yaralanan olmazken, depo kullanılamaz hale geldi. Ekiplerin soğutma çalışmaları sürerken, yangının çıkış nedenine ilişkin inceleme başlatıldı.

author: Anikibawal
title: Lof Juan Currin de Temuco enfrenta una nueva orden de desalojo del único predio en reivindicación que queda de su territorio ancestral.
content:
Durante el mes de junio del año 2026, dos integrantes del Lof Juan Currin fueron denunciados ante el Juzgado de Garantía de Temuco por el empresario Pablo Jacobi Bauman por los delitos de Usurpación u ocupación violenta de inmueble, en el único predio que queda de su territorio ancestral, el cual figura en su Titulo de Merced. Los dos lamgen que se encuentran procesados en la causa son Leonardo Catrileo Chiguaihuan y Oscar Chiguaihuan Chiguaihuan, quien cumple el rol de Lonkopalife en su comunidad. Durante el mes de octubre, el lof y en particular, los lamgen Oscar y Leonardo han sido notificados con una orden de desalojo.




Este no es el primer proceso judicial que interpone el empresario en contra de la comunidad, durante el año 2001, Pablo Jacobi anuncio una querella por destrucción de propiedad privada, ante la negativa del Lof Juan Currin a la instalación de un cerco dentro del terreno que pretendía instalar el empresario para materializar un proyecto inmobiliario en el predio. Durante esos años, Mariquina Trecamán, dirigenta de la comunidad declaro que el empresario Jacobi tendría una visión parcial de la historia del conflicto, ya que este se remonta al año 1950, cuando Alfonso Taito Schneider llegó al lugar como arrendatario, donde instaló una fábrica de ladrillos, en palabras de Mariquina Trecamán «Este señor fue designado como tutor de un menor de la comunidad, quien al fallecer ambos padres quedó al desamparo. Valiéndose de esta situación, no sólo se apoderó del terreno del menor, sino que se apropió de casi todo el terreno de la comunidad Juan Currín utilizando distintas maniobras en tribunales» (fuente: https://mapuche.info/archivo/news02/austral010528.html).




El Lof Juan Currin lleva décadas resistiendo en este predio ante la usurpación y despojo de casi la totalidad de su territorio ancestral, arrinconados entre edificios y proyectos inmobiliarios han logrado mantener y preservar sus practiiicas sociales, políticas, culturales y espirituales, espacios ceremoniales como un un Rewe y Paliwe, ademas en el lugar se emplazan viviendas pertenecientes a las familias de la comunidad.




 A continuación, compartimos una declaración del lamgen Oscar Chiguaihuan Chiguaihuan, Lonkopalife de la comunidad: 




«Bueno, yo soy Óscar Chiguaihuan. Hace tiempo atrás recibí una denuncia aquí en mi territorio, pertenezco a la comunidad Juan Currín. Hubo una denuncia hace tiempo atrás por usurpación violenta, según yo… le usurpé el territorio a Pablo Jacobi, me acusa de haber puesto un rewe, el rewe era de mi abuela y tiene más de 30 años,… me imagino yo que tiene, yo tengo 35 años… yo me crié ahí, siempre había un rewe ahí y el winka me echa la culpa a mí que yo puse un rewe. No es lógico lo que dice.

Esta comunidad es muy antigua, tengo documentos donde se registra la comunidad, el lof, el título de Merced tiene muchos años, documentos de 1922 hacia estos años, hay documentos de que la comunidad está asentada aquí en este territorio y sin embargo hoy día me acusan a mí de yo usurpar territorio donde yo he sido toda la vida de aquí.




Y pasa que después de la denuncia, hoy día llega otra mala noticia, de que el Winka y sus abogados pidieron una audiencia de urgencia en Fiscalía, no sé cómo se harán esos temas y llegaron un acuerdo de desalojar aquí a la comunidad, digamos, despojarnos de donde tenemos el Rewe, que es un lugar ancestral para nosotros lo tomamos como donde hacemos nuestras ceremonias, jugamos al palín, tenemos nuestra salida hacia digamos hacia la hacia la calle, mi familia circula por aquí todos los días y nos quieren encerrar prácticamente, nos aislarían, no tendríamos salida, nada. No entiendo lo que quieren hacer los Winka, pero nosotros queremos evitarlo realmente porque no sería lógico que nos dejen encerrados, sin salida, ni siquiera caminando. 




Entonces pasa que salió la audiencia que pueden desalojarnos y nosotros estamos en contra y queremos apoyo, necesitamos que la gente haga visible todavía como el winka usurpa la tierra, se empeñan en despojarnos de nuestra forma de ser, se niegan a reconocer los que nosotros todavía hacemos, nuestro guillatü, nuestro palines, hacemos ceremonia, celebramos Wetripantü, entonces nos van a despojar de todo eso si logran su acometido los winka. Nosotros como comunidad, digamos, como familia siempre hemos sido afectados, siempre hemos tenido que estar luchando. Yo tengo 35 años, pero hay registro de lucha de mi comunidad mucho más de la edad que tengo yo, hay mucha historia de Weichan aquí, no sería la primera vez en todo caso que vengan con este desalojo, donde se llevan a la gente presa y hay que pelear a veces cuando los winka no hacen caso con sus propias documentaciones, porque nosotros tenemos documentos donde esta tierra se dice que ha sido de nuestra familia toda la vida, y hoy día llegan y acusan de usurpación como si nosotros viniéramos de otro lado.




Nosotros sí tenemos como demostrar que todos los vecinos que están aquí son de aquí, y nosotros tenemos muchos más años asentados, poco más de 140 años tenemos en documentación para corroborar que Juan Currín siempre ha sido de aquí, esta comunidad, este lof. Entonces no sé a dónde irá llegar todo este tema, esperamos se haga visible, también es una demostración de que el mapuche puede hacer resistencia, a pesar de toda la indiferencia, a pesar de todos los malos tratos, se pueda resistir cuidando el territorio, es nuestro deber como Mapuche cuidar el territorio y hacerle un llamado a los vecinos de Tromén, Labranza, Imperial, de todos los territorios, digamos de la Araucanía, que cuiden sus territorios, porque aquí vamos a hacer una demostración. Si nos ganan, va a ser una demostración de lo que les va a pasar si no cuidan su territorio, el winka está muy empeñado en consumirse su territorio, quieren agrandar las ciudades y van a seguir agrandándolas si no se ponen firmes, si no hacen como tienen que hacer, cuidar su tierra, que es lo que corresponde, lo que dejaron los antiguos, los mapuches guerrearon tanto para poder cuidar la tierra, para dejarle algo a sus descendientes, entonces, hoy día corresponde también que la gente se ponga en ese camino y no se tomen tampoco la atribución de venderla o no defenderla, porque esta tierra mapuche fue defendida a sangre y fuego, como se puede decir, y tuvo un costo muy grande como para no tomarle el cariño, el amor, porque somos mapuches, somos mapuches y es nuestro deber hacer honor a lo que somos, lo que lucharon, todo lo que ha sufrido nuestra raza, nuestra nuestra sangre, tanto años de sufrimiento que han hecho los winkas y aún así hoy día todavía andan con esa malicia de quitarnos el territorio a la fuerza, a la mala, sin preguntar nada, sin avisar nada, llegan y hacen cualquier cosa en sus oficinas, entonces hoy día determinan desalojarnos, nosotros, chuta, no sé qué vamos a hacer, pero bueno, los peñi hagan un comunicado como de cierta manera para que tengan atención, cuiden su mapu, se den cuenta, que no confíen en que le están ayudando, a veces el winka sabe llegar y entrar y después roba todo lo que poseemos, el territorio hay que apreciarlo, hay que cuidarlo, hay que valorar lo que nos dejaron los Kuifi, ese es el camino que nosotros queremos retomar aquí, por eso creemos que a lo mejor molestamos un poco a los winka, porque nosotros queremos levantar de nuevo, retomar el mapuzungün, tenemos Kimeltuchefe en esta comunidad, en los lof ,las comunidades de vecinos, al lado, se están levantando para retomar, enseñar el mapuzungün, hay cerca por aquí del territorio, por Pedro de Valdivia, al frente, hay Machi, hay de todo, estamos retomando el camino del ser mapuche, el Palín estamos retomando como deporte, nos estamos empoderando, tomando ese ese camino de jugar Palín que nos fortalece harto como Mapuche porque el Palín va con un nguillatü, se hace ceremonia, se comparte, se comparte en todos los sentidos, hay comida, se comparte todo, entonces se hace hermandad, es muy bonito el ser mapuche.




Entonces quizás eso creemos nosotros que quieren eliminarnos porque siempre el winka se ha molestado cuando el mapuche se une, entonces, a lo mejor por eso quieren eliminarnos de aquí, no sabemos qué van a hacer con nosotros como comunidad, digamos, entonces eso me gustaría que se vaya a hacer visible para los peñi que están en otros territorios resistiendo, que sean firmes no más. Se puede resistir a pesar de todo, aquí Juan Currín es la muestra de que, a pesar de que tenemos la ciudad encima, hay una familia de guerreros que aquí todavia está presente con las banderas en alto, defendiendo nuestra forma de ser. Así que eso, un saludo de resistencia a todos los peñi y lagmien, y también que se unan a la causa, apoyen la causa, que estén muy bien. Saludos a todos igual.

Lof Coiweko Temuko Waria 18/10/2026″

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Farmers decry government’s lack of preparation for Super El Niño
content:
Farmers, scientists and environmentalists, held a forum, October 18 on the impacts of Super El Niño on farmers and fisherfolk and the government’s lack of preparations for it.

A Super El Niño is a stronger El Niño where the temperature of the Pacific Ocean increases to 2C above the average. In the Philippines, it leads to the extreme shifting of weather conditions, bringing in severe drought, or stronger rainfall events. For farmers, it is the government’s unpreparedness that turns it into an even greater calamity, made even worse by the climate crisis.

Farmers Geraldine Patriarca and Ginny Nabia from Bicol and Negros expressed how their communities are already experiencing extreme drought, and are unable to sustain themselves and their families. They demanded Marcos Jr. to give genuine solutions to farmers’ struggles, not his proposed buckets that they say “will barely even catch any rain.”

Irish Cuaresma of Advocates of Science and Technology for the People (Agham), added that farmers and Indigenous peoples are further undermined by “disaster capitalism,” where corporations benefit from humanitarian crises.

Sharl Lopez of Philippine Network of Food Security Programs (PNFSP) meanwhile, criticized the government for not upholding their obligation to uphold the people’s right to food security, and advocated for the passing of the Right to Adequate Food Bill.

After the forum, farmers held a flash mob calling for national industrialization, genuine agrarian reform. (RVO)

Text and photos by Viggo Sarmago
