title: Viminale identifica i camnionisti per rimuovere i presidi. “Non ci fermiamo”, i blocchi a sud continuano
content:
Contro il caro-carburanti

 Scaffali vuoti in Calabria, Basilicata, Campania (bloccata la A1) e in alcuni casi anche in Puglia e Sicilia; in queste 2 ultime Regioni solo alcune sigle sindacali hanno ritirato i blocchi mentre il governo, per bocca del ministro Urso, ha iniziato a identificare i camionisti “per rimuovere tutti i presidi nelle prossime ore”. I primi numeri del Viminale parlano di 1.339 identificati, 71 denunciati, 242 sanzionati sul piano amministrativo, oltre a disporre scorte di polizia per i tir non in blocco.




Da Radio Onda d’Urto




Per ora la situazione più estesa, a livello di mobilitazione resta quella in 

Calabria

, dove sono fermi anche 870 panificatori, mentre gli aeroporti di Crotone e Reggio Calabria sono senza carburante; l’Enav avverte gli aerei in transito da Crotone e Reggio Calabria di “pianificare il rifornimento in precedenza e in quantità sufficiente per le tratte successive”. Le proteste, comunque, continuano e si aggiunge nelle ultime ore anche la mobilitazione dei pescatori.




Una panoramica su quanto sta accadendo in Calabria con Peppe Marra, compagno di Reggio e direnge di Usb Calabria che sta seguendo le mobilitazioni.







Non ha per ora quindi sortito troppi effetti quindi l’incontro di alcune sigle sindacali con Salvini, che ha annunciato lo stanziamento di 480 milioni agli autotrasportatori (soldi già stanziati in estate ma mai sbloccati) per far fronte al caro-carburante per il periodo da marzo a ottobre.




“Sono arrivate 32mila domande e da oggi cominciano i pagamenti”, dice il leghista; a fargli da sponda c’è Coldiretti, da anni braccio agricolo della destra di governo, che ha annullato la manifestazione con i trattori fissata per domani a Napoli dopo la mancia di Salvini. Sempre a Napoli, però, da domani l’intera Università L’Orientale – il più grande ateneo del CentroSud – entra in didattica a distanza, a causa dei blocchi e della mancanza di carburante per raggiungere le aule.




Da Napoli Raul del Si Cobas, lavoratore di un’azienda di logistica

.

author: CNT Ponent
title: Vivir nos cuesta la vida
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Català







Castellano

Vivir nos cuesta la vida




Llevamos años viviendo una ofensiva sostenida contra las condiciones de vida de la clase trabajadora. Trabajar ya no garantiza vivir con dignidad, cobrar un salario no asegura acceder a una vivienda digna. La productividad mejora pero la jornada laboral se mantiene. Los beneficios empresariales baten récords, pero los salarios quedan estancados. El PIB sube, pero la precariedad se extiende.

La vivienda se ha convertido en un bien inaccesible para muchos de nosotros: hoy, el coste medio para acceder a un hogar supera el 50% de sus ingresos. Mientras los grandes especuladores concentran cada vez más propiedades, las trabajadoras somos condenadas a unos alquileres impagables, vivir endeudados, sufrir pisos en mal estado o no poder independizarnos.




Esta ofensiva no se detiene en la vivienda y los salarios, también se extiende sobre los servicios públicos que sostienen la vida cotidiana. El sistema sanitario y la educación pública sufren un proceso de desmantelamiento progresivo: infrafinanciación crónica, precarización de las plantillas y procesos crecientes de externalización, mientras el negocio privado gana terreno. Mientras, el dinero público se dedica al aumento del gasto militar para librar guerras que hacen subir aún más los precios.

Nos dicen que ésta es la legislatura de la vivienda, o que la economía va mejor que nunca. Pero, en la realidad, los trabajadores no hemos notado nada de esto y seguimos sufriendo para vivir dignamente.

Pero en los últimos meses hemos vivido también cosas esperanzadoras. La comunidad educativa ha hecho huelgas históricas. El campesinado ha conseguido paralizar autopistas y puertos por decir lo suficiente. Y las manifestaciones por la vivienda han logrado obligar a los gobiernos a hacer leyes que no querían hacer. Estos meses hemos visto cómo sólo luchando podemos conseguir mejorar nuestras vidas. Ahora es hora de redoblar la lucha.




Por eso exigimos:







Bajada de los precios de alquiler

El precio del alquiler no puede fijarlo el mercado. Por eso es necesario reformar el índice de referencia de los precios del alquiler y vincularlo a los salarios.




Prohibición de desahucios sin alternativa y contratos indefinidos

Es necesario garantizar las condiciones mínimas de estabilidad residencial como condición para tener una seguridad material. Por eso reclamamos la prohibición de todos los desahucios en casos de personas vulnerables y sin alternativa residencial y que los contratos de alquiler sean indefinidos.




Expropiación de viviendas de bancos y fondos voluntarios

Es necesario recuperar las viviendas de los grandes especuladores y ponerlas bajo control público, así como prohibir las compras especulativas para evitar su acaparamiento.




Construcción de un parque público de vivienda

Es necesario construir un verdadero parque público de vivienda, financiado mediante un impuesto especial al rendismo. También hay que asegurar que sea totalmente público, eliminando los topes de ingresos mínimo para acceder.




Reconocimiento de los derechos sindicales

Los derechos deben garantizarse a través de la autoorganización de los trabajadores. Por eso es necesario reconocer los derechos sindicales en materia de vivienda, incluyendo el derecho a la negociación colectiva, a la representación sindical ya la huelga de alquileres cuando se conviertan en situaciones de incumplimiento por parte de la propiedad.




Aumento del Salario Mínimo Interprofesional (SMI) hasta los 1.600€ y Pensión mínima igual al SMI.

El salario mínimo debe garantizar condiciones de vida dignas. Hoy no lo hace.




Reducción de la jornada laboral a 35 horas semanales que los convenios siempre podrán pactar su reducción.

Reducir la jornada significa repartir el trabajo y combatir el paro, mejorar la salud, la calidad de vida y la conciliación.




Incremento de los salarios con la pérdida efectiva de poder adquisitivo.

Por parte muy importante de la población trabajadora, el alquiler o hipoteca absorben entre el 40% y el 60% de los ingresos, pero su ponderación en el IPC es insuficiente, generando una distorsión entre inflación oficial y coste real de la vida.




Defensa de todos los servicios públicos.







Ni salarios por tierra ni vivienda por las nubes.




CNT PONENT SE SUMA A LA HUELGA GENERAL EL DÍA 11 DE NOVIEMBRE




¡VAMOS TODAS! HACIA LA HUELGA GENERAL







Català

Viure ens costa la vida




Fa anys que vivim una ofensiva sostinguda contra les condicions de vida de la classe treballadora. Treballar ja no garanteix viure amb dignitat, cobrar un salari no assegura accedir a un habitatge digne. La productivitat millora, però la jornada laboral es manté. Els beneficis empresarials baten rècords, però els salaris queden estancats. El PIB puja, però la precarietat s’estén.

L’habitatge s’ha convertit en un bé inaccessible per a molts de nosaltres: avui, el cost mitjà per accedir a una llar supera el 50% dels ingressos. Mentre els grans especuladors concentren cada cop més propietats, les treballadores som condemnades a uns lloguers impagables, a viure endeutats, a patir pisos en mal estat o a no poder-nos independitzar.




Aquesta ofensiva no s’atura en l’habitatge i els salaris, també s’estén sobre els serveis públics que sostenen la vida quotidiana. El sistema sanitari i l’educació pública pateixen un procés de desmantellament progressiu: infrafinançament crònic, precarització de les plantilles i processos creixents d’externalització, mentre el negoci privat guanya terreny. Mentrestant, els diners públics es dediquen a l’augment de la despesa militar per lliurar guerres que fan pujar encara més els preus.

Ens diuen que aquesta és la legislatura de l’habitatge, o que l’economia va millor que mai. Però, a la realitat, els treballadors no hem notat res de tot això i seguim patint per viure dignament.

Però els últims mesos també hem viscut coses esperançadores. La comunitat educativa ha fet vagues històriques. La pagesia ha aconseguit paralitzar autopistes i ports per dir prou. I les manifestacions per l’habitatge han aconseguit obligar els governs a fer lleis que no volien fer. Aquests mesos hem vist com només lluitant podem aconseguir millorar les nostres vides. Ara és l’hora de redoblar la lluita.




Per això exigim:

1. Baixada dels preus de lloguer

El preu del lloguer no el pot fixar el mercat. Per això cal reformar l’índex de referència dels preus del lloguer i vincular-ho als salaris.

2. Prohibició de desnonaments sense alternativa i contractes indefinits

Cal garantir les condicions mínimes d’estabilitat residencial com a condició per tenir una seguretat material. Per això reclamem la prohibició de tots els desnonaments en casos de persones vulnerables i sense alternativa residencial i que els contractes de lloguer esdevinguin indefinits.

3. Expropiació d’habitatges de bancs i fons volotors

Cal recuperar els habitatges dels grans especuladors i posar-los sota control públic, com també prohibir les compres especulatives per evitar-ne l’acaparament.

4. Construcció d’un parc públic d’habitatge

Cal construir un veritable parc públic d’habitatge, finançat mitjançant un impost especial al rendisme. Cal també assegurar que sigui totalment públic, eliminant els topalls d’ingressos mínim per accedir-hi.

5. Reconeixement dels drets sindicals

Els drets s’han de garantir a través de l’autoorganització dels treballadors. Per això cal reconèixer els drets sindicals en matèria d’habitatge, incloent-hi el dret a la negociació col·lectiva, a la representació sindical i a la vaga de lloguers quan esdevinguin situacions d’incompliment per part de la propietat.

6. Augment del Salari Mínim Interprofessional (SMI) fins als 1.600€ i Pensió mínima igual al SMI.

El salari mínim ha de garantir condicions de vida dignes. Avui no ho fa.

7. Reducció de la jornada laboral a 35 hores setmanals que els convenis sempre podran pactar la seva reducció.

Reduir la jornada significa repartir el treball i combatre l’atur, millorar la salut, la qualitat de vida i la conciliació.

8. Increment dels salaris amb la pèrdua efectiva de poder adquisitiu.

Per una part molt important de la població treballadora, el lloguer o hipoteca absorbeixen entre el 40% i el 60% dels ingressos, però la seva ponderació en l’IPC és insuficient, generant una distorsió entre inflació oficial i cost real de la vida.

9. Defensa de tots els serveis públics.




Ni salaris per terra ni habitatge pels núvols.




CNT PONENT ES SUMA A LA VAGA GENERAL EL DIA 11 DE NOVEMBRE




SOM-HI TOTES! CAP A LA VAGA GENERAL




La entrada 

Vivir nos cuesta la vida

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: The Student Revolt in France Spreads
content:
from the 

CrimethInc. 

collective, 21/10/2026







Moving Forward with Rage and Solidarity




October 17 marked one of the fiercest days of mass protest in recent French history. Scenes of ferocious resistance unfolded throughout the day, not only in Paris but in 

Bordeaux

, 

Dijon

, 

Marseille

, 

Nancy

, and dozens of other cities across the country. Some observers have described the day’s events as 

more explosive

 than the 

Yellow Vest movement

 of 2018-19—and the rebellion shows no sign of slowing.




How did we get here? Courageous high school students 

have been protesting for weeks

 against abominable conditions in schools, the rise of the extreme right, and the bleak prospects they face in a world dominated by technocrats and tech barons. Alongside growing anti-government protests from 

Albania

, 

Italy

, 

Spain

, and beyond in recent days, the French student rebellions may herald the emergence of a new wave of global struggle.




In this article, our correspondent from Paris explains the context behind the youth rebellion, tracks the movement’s growth over the two weeks leading up to October 17 and the government’s failed attempts to repress or to pacify it, and clarifies the stakes moving forward.




Stay tuned for a full report on the uprising of October 17 and the ongoing rebellions across France and beyond.







Thousands gather to protest police violence and support the students in revolt (Nantes, October 6, 2026)







This update on the student unrest in France picks up where we ended 

our previous report

, on the eve of the national call to take the streets on October 6, 2026.




The stakes were high on this crucial day of action. It was critical to show massive solidarity with the high school students fighting like hell against the empty future looming on their horizon. The day presented an ideal opportunity to expand the scope of the current movement by joining forces to resist the authoritarian state power that has been growing stronger every day.




The following article provides further context and analysis to understand the current situation in France, along with reports on what went down in the streets over these last rebellious weeks.




Background: The 

Banlieues

 and the Enemy Within




When governments or powerful institutions feel threatened, they often strive to reaffirm their authority by inventing scapegoats to hold responsible for all supposed misfortunes. By invoking the menace of an “enemy within,” politicians can shift blame for systemic problems that have resulted from their own actions onto a specific category of individuals. In France, the most common targets are the residents of the 

banlieues

, the impoverished suburbs on the outskirts of Paris and other cities.




At the beginning of the student blockades, the movement remained limited to a handful of high schools in these Parisian suburbs. In response, President Emmanuel Macron and his ministers decided to react quickly and do everything in their power to silence this emerging wave of youth protest. Due to the location of the first blockades, authorities believed that they could act more freely and repress the unrest with impunity, since these specific territories have been targeted for generations by all government administrations across political lines.




The condition of the 

banlieues

, which remain populated by descendants of the French Empire’s colonized subjects, reflects France’s ongoing role as a 

neocolonial power

 that continues to exploit African territories. Consider the disastrous 

oil project

 in Uganda orchestrated by the France-based multinational company TotalEnergies, or the 

corruption case

 involving the French far-right business tycoon Vincent Bolloré and his bribery and money laundering schemes across West African ports.




French governments and corporations have no scruples about extracting enormous wealth from African countries. This neocolonial pillaging fuels France’s position as the 

seventh richest country

 in the world today, according to the IMF. Yet despite these astronomical profits, the nation refuses to address the problems facing its post-colonial population and their descendants within its national territory.




At the twilight of France’s colonial empire, decades of occupation and racist violence had created political and economic instability across northern and western Africa. As a result, waves of migrants began leaving their countries to come to France for work in the 1950s. Upon arriving, they continued to face systemic colonial racism, relegated to the economic margins and second-class citizenship. This cheap workforce ended up gathering on the outskirts of major cities, living in makeshift neighborhoods and slums like those of 

Nanterre

 on the western edges of Paris.




Shantytown in the Parisian suburb of Nanterre in the 1960s




Over the following decades, urban development projects replaced these slums with massive apartment blocks into which immigrant families and low-income workers were relocated. Today, these areas are known as the 

banlieues

 (the suburbs). In mainstream French political discourse, authorities and journalists invoke the 

banlieues

 as a derogatory term that embodies all the supposed flaws of our modern society.




The 

banlieues

 also offer areas of experimentation for law enforcement. Politicians ranging from moderate to reactionary have long considered these suburbs “lawless areas” whose young residents pose a threat to the ruling order. In response, the French state consistently harasses and represses these populations to instill fear and obedience and to force them to adapt to its laws. This targeted violence reproduces old colonial strategies within the territory of the nation. For example, the “state of emergency,” developed as legal tool in former French colonies for crowd control, was first used within the borders of France in the 

banlieues

.




Past governments pushed law enforcement to increase the pressure in the suburbs, invoking the “war on drugs” and defense of their sacrosanct “democracy.” They invested in new weapons and equipment, which specific police units experimented with freely in the streets of the 

banlieues

 to test their usefulness in repressing popular mobilization. These racist police forces operate with impunity in these territories and consider every person they encounter a potential threat. As a result, numerous young people of color have been abused, injured, or killed at the hands of police, such as Zyed Benna and Bouna Traore in 

2005

, Adama Traoré in 

2016

, and more recently, Nahel Merzouk in 

2023

.




In the face of such contemptuous violence from the French state and its armed henchmen, it is inevitable that people would organize on a grassroot level to defend themselves and counterattack against these intolerable conditions. It is simply a question of dignity and survival. Historically, the 

banlieues

 have been the settings of intense riots and confrontations with police forces, often leading to massive property destruction and arsons.




In this context, it is not a coincidence that the student blockades first emerged in these suburbs, nor that the government decided without hesitation to send in heavily equipped police forces to repress them. This response is only a logical extension of the long legacy of colonial racism directed against part of the population. The French state continues to consider working-class people and the children of immigrants as the biggest threat to its stability. Therefore, to maintain its crumbling power structure by any means necessary, its solution is to constantly terrorize these youths to contain their rebellious energy.




The repressive technologies used by police against students and protesters today were tested out on the populations of the 

banlieues

 (Lyon, October 6, 2026)




Keeping the Rage Alive




After more than a week of intense confrontations and blockades throughout France, it became clear that curbing the ungovernable student movement had become the number one priority of the current ruling order.




Nevertheless, the movement refused to be intimidated by the brutal repression implemented by authorities. Instead, it paid tribute in its own way to the 

Yellow Vest

 unrest that began in 2018 by rebranding its own key days of actions as “Acts.” This framework of successive mobilizations, each building on the last, maintained the pressure on politicians and law enforcement by providing regular opportunities to take the streets in massive demonstrations on a national scale.




While these national days of action appeared once or twice per week, this doesn’t mean that nothing happened the rest of the week. On the contrary, multiple forms of action—blockades, sit-ins, direct confrontations with police forces, property destruction, arsons, and more—continued to take place daily across multiple cities throughout France. This plurality of tactics, combined with the courage and determination of numerous teenagers throughout the past weeks, has enabled the unrest to last this long.




Clouds of tear gas in Rennes (October 6, 2026)




Act III: October 6, 2026




On the morning of Tuesday, October 6, students gathered in front of their high schools and universities to block access. This time, due to the state’s escalation of violence against the youth demonstrations over the previous days, parents and teachers decided to join the students and assembled with them in front of schools. Through their presence, they hoped to prevent intensifying repression from police forces.




For the most part, their strategy appears to have worked. Reports from different blockades during the morning mentioned that on the whole, tensions were not as high as on previous days. Nevertheless, some locations saw police officers attempting to break through the lines of some parents and teachers who were protecting students or using pepper-spray to disperse protesters.




It is difficult to confirm whether the less brutal state response that morning resulted from police reluctance due to the presence of adults among students, or from specific orders coming from government officials. After the increasing number of injuries inflicted on students over the preceding days, the government may have instructed its armed forces to be more careful while dealing with student blockades, especially with parents and teachers joining them.




Parents and teachers on the front line to defend their children and students (Bordeaux, October 6, 2026)




While parents and teachers joining their students on the front lines during these morning actions may have discouraged a more violent response from the state, their presence in the blockades may also have helped authorities to regain some partial control in the streets. The presence of such authority figures can play a role in discouraging rebellious behavior among young people. In the days to come, the success of the unrest may depend in part on whether students can receive support from adults while maintaining their own autonomy and momentum.




That same morning, as the first demonstrations were taking place in Lille, Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux, Nantes, and other cities, some university students blocked their campuses to join the movement. Around noon, as people converged at the Place de la République for the Paris demonstration, authorities announced that 891 of the country’s 3700 high schools were either partially or completely closed, including 250 just in the Paris region. Contrary to the official announcements made by the government, the movement was gaining rather than losing momentum.




The Paris demonstration was scheduled to depart from Place de la République in the direction of Place de la Nation. The 3.3-kilometer pathway connecting these two major squares in eastern Paris has frequently been the scene of social movement marches and intense clashes with police forces. This time, however, we learned beforehand that police units had received orders to keep their distance from demonstrators and to not be “visible” to prevent escalating tensions. The government appeared to have adapted its law enforcement strategy for the day in response to mounting criticisms of its repression of the students since the beginning of the movement.




Before the official departure time of the procession, the square was already so packed that thousands of demonstrators had begun walking down the boulevard towards La Nation to make space for more people to join. The flow of individuals passing through Place de la République seemed endless. Massive numbers of high school and university students, teachers and other educational workers were joined by leftist organizations, trade unions, and other supporters, as well as some radicals and anarchists. The feeling among the crowds was festive, impassioned, and full of determination.




As the crowd approached Place de la Nation, the atmosphere gradually changed. Police units in riot gear were blocking adjacent streets preventing anyone from entering or exiting the procession. Marchers erected a makeshift barricade and set it ablaze in the middle of the boulevard, while several targets had their front windows smashed and their offices ransacked. After weeks of brutal attacks on the protesting students, this escalation of tactics reflected the justified rage and desire to take the offensive that many demonstrators felt.




At this point, intense confrontations with police forces began at Place de la Nation. Riot police and 

BRAV-M special units

 encountered showers of stones and projectiles thrown by courageous rioters, while the rest of the crowd of protesters that did not physically take part showed their support by chanting the classic “

Tout le monde déteste la police

” (“Everyone hates the police”) and shouting, “

ACAB

”.




Police forces used tear gas, stun grenades and rubber bullets to attempt to disperse the thick crowds entering La Nation. But people stayed, continuing to demonstrate and hanging out amid the joyful chaos. At times, officers charged demonstrators in order to snatch and arrest specific individuals, while determined individuals counterattacked them head-on and without respite. The solidarity experienced during these moments was a breath of fresh air among the thick clouds of tear gas.




At the end of the day, despite the false reassurances of the authorities in the mainstream media, the third national day of action was a clear victory for the movement. The objective of gathering masses of people in the streets to join forces with the students had been achieved. According to unions and organizations, at least 450,000 demonstrators participated across France, around one fourth in Paris. As usual, authorities announced much 

lower numbers

, estimating around 250,000 total demonstrators. Moreover, to reassure the nation of its control over the situation, the government’s Ministry of the Interior announced that 488 individuals had been arrested during the day, raising the total of arrests since the beginning of the movement to an unprecedented number of 6547.




These figures illustrate the escalation of authoritarian law enforcement doctrine in France. By comparison, during the first 26 days of the Yellow Vest movement, French police recorded around 12,000 arrests, an average of 460 each day. Eight years later, these 

figures

 have been dramatically surpassed. As of October 6, 2026, approximately 935 arrests had taken place every single day since the beginning of the movement.




Despite these disturbing figures reflecting growing mass arrests, the student movement did not back down. Their persistence in the streets shows their determination to continue fighting, not only to improve the 

conditions in their schools

 but to challenge the living hell the French authorities are drawing tighter around us every day.




Students building a barricade in front of their high school (Paris, October 8, 2026)




Act IV: October 8, 2026




Two days after this impressive mobilization in the streets, student unions issued another call for mass convergence in the streets to maintain pressure on the government. As they had done for nearly two weeks, students from all over the country woke up early to meet in front of their schools, build makeshift barricades, and block the main entrances.




By 8:00 am, hundreds of high schools remained blocked in different cities. In the Paris region alone, about 145 schools were either closed, blocked or experiencing some sort of disruption. The Ministry of Education announced that 224 schools were completely closed and 151 partially closed. Authorities used these figures to once again claim that the movement was losing momentum, since “94% of high schools in France were completely or partially open” on this Thursday morning.




On this new day of action, a demonstration was scheduled to take place in Paris during the afternoon. However, the city’s Police Prefecture refused to approve the initial route requested by student unions. Instead, authorities only allowed students and protesters to converge and gather at Place de la Bastille, an ideal location for 

kettling

 large crowds of individuals by closing all access to the square.




Nevertheless, an estimated 

25,000 students and other demonstrators

 gathered at La Bastille, while demonstrations also took place in Lille, Lyon, Marseille, Nantes, Rennes, Toulon, and other cities.




After several uneventful hours in the plaza, confusion began to spread among demonstrators, as no one knew where to leave the demonstration with police units holding their lines in front of every potential exit. The crowd simmered as people moved from one street to another seeking a way to escape from this trap.




Unsurprisingly, this stressful situation led to clashes with law enforcement. As the sun set, tensions between protesters and police escalated. To “clear the square,” police forces carried out repeated violent charges and shot tear gas canisters, rubber bullets, and sting ball grenades at demonstrators. Courageous rioters answered by shooting fireworks and throwing paving stones, glass bottles, and other projectiles. Authorities struggling to disperse the remaining protesters deployed a water cannon. Reports suggested that several individuals were injured in the clashes that afternoon. While the last groups of demonstrators were still resisting police attacks at La Bastille and in the nearby streets, other demonstrators attempted to regroup at Place de la Nation, but were rapidly surrounded by officers.




Riot police units attempt to clear out 

La Bastille

 (Paris, October 8, 2026)




At the end of the day, the government 

announced

 that 71,500 people had participated in the afternoon demonstrations across the country, including 25,000 in Paris. 55,000 took part in actions in front of high schools, of whom only some joined the afternoon processions and gatherings. Officials reported 504 arrests on October 8.




But government statistics should be interpreted with extreme caution. For example, authorities claimed that since the beginning of the movement on September 17, 215 students, 85 teachers and education staff members, and 800 police officers had been injured. These figures seem dubious, given the unlikelihood that heavily equipped police officers would receive injuries at far higher rates than mostly unarmed high school students and other protesters. As always during protest movements, the war of numbers offers authorities a useful tool to build their narrative and justify their actions.




Repressions and Concessions: The State Tries to Undermine Solidarity




In the face of this increasing wave of solidarity with students and boiling anger against government inaction and 

police violence

, the Macron administration desperately attempted to keep up appearances while deploying strategies to divide the movement and regain control.




During a speech to the National Assembly on October 6, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu reiterated the need to deploy large numbers of law enforcement officers in the streets to counter the “violence” spread by the student movement. This shows the government’s willingness to legitimize the use of brutal force against the nation’s teenagers without second-guessing its policies or even admitting the existence of “police violence”.




All sorts of media outlets have widely reported how students have been insulted, assaulted, brutalized, and injured by police forces since the beginning of the movement. In response, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez 

stated

 that law enforcement actions have been carried out with “the utmost proportionality” and that he refused to apologize for any of the state’s actions since the emergence of the movement.




Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, who is in charge of the management of public order in response to the students protest movement (Paris, October 7, 2026)




In the same breath, without a hint of shame for its glaring hypocrisy, the government also 

announced

 that the use of stun grenades by police against the student movement would be suspended until further notice, following the tragic 

loss of a hand by young protestor

 on October 5. Such decisions refute the government’s own narrative of “proportionality,” as they are well aware that they are targeting teenagers with military weapons intended to cause physical or mental injury, if not death. This hypocrisy, while not surprising, remains infuriating.




Hoping to divert attention from the protestors’ demands, the government also announced its decision to accelerate discussions regarding the voting of a bill named “

casseurs-payeurs

.” This new repressive measure was first proposed last May in the aftermath of the riots and lootings that followed the victory of the PSG (the Parisian football team) during the final game of the Champions League. Its aim is simple: to make the families of suspected rioters pay for damages they allegedly caused. This law, a favorite proposal of the extreme right for years, would force any individual who knowingly took part in a group that committed violence, theft, or damage to pay up to 10,000€ [over $11,000] each towards repairs.




But the law goes beyond restitution into criminalizing participation in nearly any public resistance. Authorities will not have to prove that a specific individual broke anything; simply belonging to a group of “rioters” will suffice to find someone guilty. Any time a person decides to remain in the streets after police ordered a crowd to disperse, they would become “co-responsible” for whatever happens next. For minors, their parents would have to pay the actions of their children. And to make sure money can be extracted from the rebellious poor, the law allows authorities to garnish money directly from potential housing benefits and family allowances. In short, this law once again targets low-income individuals and families perceived as threats to the ruling order, as well as anyone who would dare to defy authority.




Beyond these repressive measures, the government also scrambled to find “solutions”—i.e., distractions—to end the crisis. During his speech, Lecornu also insisted that the government, via the Ministry of Education, had implemented tools for high school students to take part in some sort of national survey where they can express their frustrations and make requests to improve the educational system. Such strategy of watered-down participatory democracy was also used during the Yellow Vest movement to divide demonstrators and weaken their collective force. First, the French government represses students in cold blood; then it asks them for “constructive” dialogue.




Lecornu explained that by the end of the month, the government would study and work to address all the demands received by students via their official platforms to provide concrete solutions to the current crisis in the educational system. He also promised to improve “ParcourSup,” the online platform with which students list their “wishes” and apply to different post-secondary education options. He also announced that until the end of the week, each high school has been asked by the Ministry of Education to cancel half a day of classes in order to create some space and time for “a period of internal democracy” during which students and teachers could exchange about what should be changed within the school. This isn’t the first time that 

the language of “democracy”

 has been used as a tool for counterinsurgency.




Similarly, on October 8 Education Minister Édouard Geffray made a new promise to 

provide

 3000 extra teachers, while welcoming student unions and organizations to contribute their views on the current situation in hopes of reaching a political agreement to end the demonstrations as soon as possible. These promises and calls for dialogue show the Macron government’s strategy to pacify the situation by partially answering some of the main demands made by the student movement—while ratcheting up repression in the streets to maintain power on their own terms.




National media have reported that tens of thousands of demands were already made by students through these official platforms. Nonetheless, it seems to us that, so far, doing so has not stopped them from continuing to be present in the streets. Even students who may participate in such official channels recognize that their collective power to disrupt the status quo, not the government’s pacifying gestures, remains the source of their genuine power and voice.




So far, the student movement has resisted cooptation by political opportunists and trade unions. However, its success and widespread public support render it a tempting target for those who would attempt to control it or hitch it to other agendas. University student unions and their spokespeople form part of the movement, and some leftist politicians and their followers actively support it. However, none of them have yet been able to speak on behalf of all its participants, nor to control the diversity of tactics that have flourished within it.




Finally, the existing solidarity within the ranks of students is admirable. As we 

reported previously

, teenagers face vastly different realities depending on the geographical areas where they live and study. The claim of the French school system to promote equal opportunity and reward merit rather than class and geographic background is simply a lie, in the face of the structural inequalities that flourish within capitalism and the educational system designed to reinforce it. Nevertheless, while high-school students in the suburbs were facing violent repression from police forces, students from wealthier districts and prestigious universities joined the struggle by blocking or occupying their schools in solidarity. Numerous students explained that although they are well aware that they do not experience the same difficulties as their counterparts living in the 

banlieues

, they could not remain passive in the face of such police violence and injustice against their counterparts.




Students blocking the Hélène-Boucher high school. The sign reads: “Fewer cops, more money.” (Paris, October 6, 2026)




Onward Together Against Their World




Following another intense week of actions and protests, the Ministry of Justice 

announced

 on Friday, October 9 that since the beginning of the movement, more than 6800 people have been taken into custody, 86% of whom are minors. So far, 21 individuals have been held in jail while awaiting trial.




At the eve of a new weekend, the government continued to promote the narrative that the movement was declining and the situation was progressively coming back under control, trumpeting the decreasing number of blocked high schools as evidence. But despite the mainstream media’s faithful adherence to this story, students remained unsatisfied by the government’s response and determined not to give up the fight. Far from feeling defeated, they issued a new call to take to the streets on Tuesday, October 13.




Act V: October 13, 2026




As the next day of action dawned, blockades and clashes with law enforcement forced the closure of about 200 high schools. Over the previous days, that number had held steady, showing that a significant core of high school students remained willing to fight for what they think is right.




But what changed dramatically on this day compared to the previous acts is that a large number of universities decided to join the movement all at once. Around noon, the organization 

Union étudiante

 announced to the media that 90% of the seventy French universities were blocked or completely closed. This massive involvement of university students during the fifth act of the student unrest would prove to be a critical development.




The sign reads: “High-school students maimed, shot in the eye, drowned, or toothless. University students outraged.” (Rennes, October 6, 2026)




As the movement expanded and gained in strength, the counterrevolutionary backlash against it from both the government and the grassroots extreme right increased in turn. The growing number of blockades at universities over these days led to a surge in fascist attacks intended to intimidate protesters in cities such as Paris and Lille.




As usual, the first marches throughout France took place in the morning. In Paris, the official demonstration was announced for 2:00 pm. This time, the itinerary validated by authorities changed from the classic Place de la République to La Nation. Demonstrators would be storming the southern and western parts of the city, departing from Place d’Italie and reaching Invalides, not far from the Ministry of Education and Matignon, the official residence of the Prime Minister. This route evoked sweet memories from another famous student movement that took place in France 

20 years ago

, during which intense riots took place once demonstrators reached Invalides. Another unofficial call went out summoning protestors to meet in front of City Hall. This unauthorized procession was finally granted the right to walk through the streets of Paris to reach its destination not far from the other demonstration.




On the afternoon of the 13th, police forces changed their tactics and drew up very close to the demonstrators, moving at the front of the procession. Before participants could join the march, they were subject to search by the police. Officers attempted to confiscate as many anti-police signs as possible. However, this strategy to muzzle public opinion against the police’s violent behavior proved unsuccessful, as thousands of protesters took pleasure in chanting the classic anti-police slogans in unison during the march.




As demonstrators approached their final destination, tensions with law enforcement escalated. Near Invalides, some motivated protesters attempted to continue their afternoon march towards Matignon, but were quickly stopped and pushed back by lines of police near Place Vauban.




It was here that intense confrontations unfolded over the next several hours. Police deployed water cannons and blanketed the square with tear gas in order to disperse the crowd. What demonstrators didn’t know yet was that other police units had surrounded them and stood ready to kettle them if needed in order to arrest specific individuals. During the clashes, rioters set a BMW SUV on fire and looted a nearby wine store.




Street confrontations at 

Place Vauban

 (Paris, October 13, 2026)




Later that night, the government stated that 161,500 people demonstrated during the fifth act of the student movement, while the student unions claimed a total turnout of 480,000. Officials estimated 41,500 demonstrators in Paris. Further demonstrations took place in Nantes, Lens, Strasbourg, Bordeaux, Marseille and Lyon, where some confrontations with police forces and property destruction took place towards the end of the march.




By the end of the day, arrest figures had shot up further. 7950 individuals had been taken into police custody since the beginning of the student protests, 85% of whom were minors. To date, 2735 criminal cases had been filed, 2190 of which involved minors, and 26 individuals were placed in pretrial detention, including 9 minors.




Looking Forward: Will the Unrest Survive the Holidays?




As the first school holidays of the year approached, many students wondered whether their month-long mobilization would survive the two-week break from classes. Their worries were understandable; it is well known that holidays have often taken the wind out of the sails of many social movements, in France and beyond.




This is why, for days, high-school students have continuously called to take the street on Saturday, October 17, 2026. This call, massively shared online for weeks, suggests a resurgence of 

the Yellow Vest movement

 that launched in 2018. Rebellious high schoolers hoped that university students, Yellow Vesters, and other angry protesters would be able to merge with the movement to expand this social and political unrest in new directions.




We haven’t been defeated yet. (Paris, October 13, 2026)




Meanwhile, the government continued to find itself in a bind over the 

crisis

, despite its pathetic attempts to defuse the uproar through dialogue with student unions and organizations. After weeks of insisting that the movement was losing steam, now they are acknowledging that the level of militancy and determination coming from protesters has progressively increased over the previous days of action. They feared the potential outcome of the October 17 demonstrations—and as we have seen, their fears were justified.




With the fateful date approaching and tension building, important questions remained. Will other demographics decide to join the movement by also revolting against the government and their current living conditions, as authorities fear? Will we live up to the expectations of high school students and the courageous precedent they have set? Will we be able to unleash hell?




Will the student movement be able to unleash hell? (Paris, October 6, 2026).

title: Seydayê Cegerxwîn 42 sal berê koça dawî kir
content:
Bi ser koça dawî ya helbestvan û nivîskarê kurd seydayê Cegerxwîn re 42 sal derbas bûn. Cegerxwîn, di sala 1903an de li bajarokê Hesarê yê girêdayî navçeya Kercewsa (ku niha girêdayî Êlihê ye) Mêrdînê ji dayik bû. 




Bi destpêkirina Şerê Yekemîn ê Cîhanê re tevî malbata xwe di sala 1914an de koçî bajarê Amûdê yê Rojavayê kir.  




Cegerxwîn, li vir li ber destê hinek pêşengên olê yên kurd hate perwerdekirin û di sala 1928’yan de dest bi nivîsandina helbestên kurdî kir. Cegerxwîn, Celadet Elî Bedirxan û rêhevalên xwe di sala 1932’yan de li paytexta Sûriyeyê Şamê dest bi weşandina kovara Hawarê kirin û navê Cegerxwîn cara ewil li wir hate bikaranîn. Cegerxwîn, sedema vê jî wiha rave dike: “Ez jî mîna gelê xwe birîndar im. Dilê min birîndar e. Ji cegera min min xwîn tê. Lewma min navê xwe kir kesê cegera wî xwîn jê tê anku Cegerxwîn.” 




Xoybûn




 Cegerxwîn, di nava rêxistina Xoybûnê de jî cih girt ku di Serhildana Agiriyê de xwedî roleke mezin e. Di sala 1946’an de derbasî Qamişloyê bû û xebatên xwe yên polîtîk domand. Cegerxwîn, di heman salê de bû serokê rêxistina siyasî ya Civata Azadî û Yekitiya Kurd.  Di sala 1948'an de endamê Partiya Komunîst a Sûriyeyê bû û 6 sal piştre ji bo bikeve Parlamentoya Sûriyeyê bû namzetê parlamenteriyê. 




Cegerxwîn, heta sala 1957’an serokatiya saziya Komîteya Aştiyê ya ji bo Cizîrê kir. Piştre ji Partiya Komunist a Sûriyeyê veqetiya û tev li Partiya Demokrat a Kurdistanê ya Sûriyeyê bû. 2 sal piştre dîsa çû Iraqê û li Zanîngeha Bexdayê bû yekemîn mamosteyê ku bi zimanê kurdî dersê dide. Cegerxwîn, di vê pêvajoyê de ji bo zimanê kurdî gelek xebat kir û gelek xwendekar gihand. 




Li Qamişloyê hate binaxkirin




Cegerxwîn, ji ber xebatên xwe yên siyasî, di sala 1963’yan de li Şamê hate girtin. Piştî berdanê jî li gorî rêzê derbasî Herêma Federe ya Kurdistanê, Lubnan û bajarê Swêdê Stockholmê bû. Di 22’yê cotmeha sala 1984’an de jî li Stockholmê wefat kir. Cenazeyê wî li Qamişloyê hate definkirin.  




Ji Mêrdînê heta Stockholmê, ji Bexdayê heta Lubnanê, ji Rojava heta Herêma Federe ya Kurdistanê, Cegerxwîn di vê pêvajoyê de gelek berhemên navdar nivîsand. Di gelemperiya berhemên wî de jî mijara esasî têkoşîna gelê kurd a li dijî burjuvaziyê bû. Cegerxwîn, zextên li gelê kurd tên kirin, înkar, pişaftin, bêkarî, xizanî û çerxa kedxwariyê di helbestên xwe de hûnand. Her wiha Cegerxwîn di helbestên xwe de bal kişand ser azadî, aştî û dijbertiya şer. 




Berhemên Cegerxwîn




Cegerxwîn, "Prîsk û Pêtî (1945)", "Sewra Azadî (1954)", "Kî me Ez? (1973)", "Ronak (1980)", "Zend-Avista (1981)", "Şefeq (1982)", "Hêvî (1983)", "Aşîtî", "Salar û Mîdya" û dîwanên wî yên "Şerefnama Menzûm". Bi gelek çîrok û lêkolînên xwe ve ji bo wêjeya kurdî bû çavkaniyeke giranbiha. Gelek berhemên wî piştre hatin qedexekirin û gelek helbestên wî ji hêla stranbejêna ve bûn stran. 




Saziyên ku bi navê wî hatine vekirin




Piştî mirina Cegerxwîn, navê wî li gelek navendên çandan, park û cadeyan hate kirin. Lê belê piştî di sala 2016’an de qeyûm li şaredariyan hate tayînkirin, bi taybet jî saziyên bi navên wî hatin girtin û navên cade û kolanên navê wî lê hatibû kirin jî hatin guherandin.




Stranên ku ji ber helbestên Cegerxwînî hatine çêkirin




Mihemed Şêxo: Ay lê gulê







Şivan Perwer: Kî ne em?







Ciwan Haco: Pir xweş e







Gulistan - Şivan Perwer : Kurdistan e Kurdistan







Aram Tîgran: Lêv şêrîna min 







Mehmet Atli: Pismamo 







Koma Azadî: Herne pêş







Bûrhan Berken: Gulfiroş







 Yûnûs Dîşkaya: Yar ko ne mêvanê te bî







Berfîn Aktay: Mem û Zîn







Rûken Yilmaz: Dîlbera Nazik










Derbarê Cegerxwînî de




Helbestvanê kurd Cegerxwîn di sala 1903yan de li gundê Hesarê ya girêdayî navçeya Kercewsa Êlihê tê dinê. Navê wî Şêxmûs e. Qey qederê wisa dixwest, ku Cegerxwîn jiyaneke zor û zehmet derbas bike, dema dê û bavê wî dimirin ew sêwî dimîne. Jiyana wî bi zor û zehmetiyan re derbas bûye. Lê Cegerxwîn zû bi zû ji vê rewşê derket û berê xwe da zanistiyê, li cem şêx û melan li medreseyan li zanînê geriya, dest bi xwendina feqetiyê kir. Heft heşt salan bi vî awayî xwendin tewa kir û (îcaza) xwe li cem Mele Fethule stand, pişt re hinekî meletiya gundan kir. Du bûyerên mezin di herêmê de çêbûn, ev bûyer bûn sedemên guhertinê di kesetiya Cegerxwîn de, berê wî bi xurtî ber bi niştimanperweriyê de dan.




Cegerxwîn koçî bajarê Qamişlo yê Rojavayê Kurdistanê dike. Di vê demê de Cegerxwîn dest bi nivîsandina helbestê kir û di kovara Hewarê de helbestên xwe diweşandin. Piştî serkeftina şoreşa Iraqê sala 1958an Cegerxwîn derbasî Iraqê bû û li zankoya Bexdayê di beşa wêjeyê de xwend. Di sala 1963yan de ji naçarî dîsa vegeriya Sûriyê, heta sala 1979an û di wê salê de berê xwe da Swêdê û li paytexta Swêdê Stockholmê bicih bû. Di 22yê Cotmeha sala 1984an de li bajarê Stokholmê koça dawî dike.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Palantir Targets MPs With ‘Intimidating’ Letters
content:
British MPs who criticised Palantir in parliament received “intimidating” letters from the US spytech firm, Novara Media can reveal. The MPs say it won’t stop them from continuing to hold Palantir to account. 




Former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn and Labour and Cooperative MP Rachael Maskell both received letters from Palantir’s UK CEO Louis Mosley in June, detailing the MPs’ anti-Palantir contributions in the House of Commons, and offering to meet. 




Corbyn slammed the letters from Mosley as intimidation. “I am in no doubt as to why Palantir is writing these letters to MPs: to intimidate its critics into silence,” he told Novara Media. “Their tactics of intimidation will not work and they will not shut me up. I will never be deterred from speaking out against Palantir, which should have no place in our public services whatsoever.”




Palantir, co-founded by billionaires Alex Karp and Peter Theil, has close ties to the Trump administration. Its 

increasing entrenchment in the British state

 via contracts with the NHS, Ministry of Defence and various police forces has sparked 

significant national security 

and 

data privacy concerns

. 




Palantir’s letter to Corbyn listed his comments relating to the firm in the Commons on 

1 June

 as part of a debate on the appointment of Peter Mandelson to the post of US ambassador despite his well-documented friendship with the late paedophile Jeffrey Epstein. Mandelson’s now-shuttered lobbying firm Global Counsel counted Palantir among its clients. 




The letter to Maskell listed her statements and questions about Palantir on four separate occasions in parliament, from 10 February to 1 June. Both letters were sent on 3 June. 




Maskell, who represents York Central, told Novara Media the letter from Palantir wouldn’t impact her approach towards the firm. “

Clearly there is a reason as to why Palantir has paid close attention to the scrutiny that MPs have brought to this company which has been handed lucrative contracts by successive governments,” she said. “I have continually expressed my deepest concern about the government engaging with this business, before it was awarded the NHS contract.” 




Independent MP for Leicester South Shockat Adam was also contacted by Palantir. He received an email this month from Palantir’s UK public affairs lead in response to critical tweets about the warfare and AI company’s involvement in the NHS and its now-ended 

contract with Leicestershire police

.




Adam told Novara Media: “As public and parliamentary scrutiny grows, MPs who raise concerns are being sent letters from the company’s lobbyists. Palantir says it welcomes scrutiny. Then let it prove it. The public has a right to know how this American company’s software is used across our NHS, our armed forces and our police, on what terms, and who answers for it. 




“Peter Thiel, Alex Karp and Louis Mosley should come to parliament and explain their role in person. Free speech and democratic oversight of public contracts are not optional.”




A Palantir spokesperson said: “There are a great deal of incorrect claims about Palantir circulating online. When politicians – sometimes inadvertently – amplify these falsehoods, they risk misleading the public. The purpose of these letters was to set the record straight. If politicians continue to repeat false claims, we will continue to correct them.”




Clive Lewis, the Labour MP for Norwich South, revealed that he had received a letter from Palantir’s new UK senior VP, Tom Watson, 

warning him that the company was surveilling his activities

 relating to Palantir last month. Lewis described this as “very Big Brother” and an “implicit threat”. 




Watson is a former minister and Labour party deputy leader who now sits in the House of Lords, alongside his Palantir job. 




Lewis told Novara Media the Mosley letters in June indicate that Palantir was panicking as the Starmer administration crumbled. “They put all their eggs in one basket with Starmer, and then the writing on the wall was that he wasn’t going to be around much longer.” 




Corbyn has repeatedly 

questioned the wisdom

 of using Palantir’s tech in the NHS, given the company’s role in supplying military tech to the IDF during the genocide in Gaza and 

surveillance tools to ICE

 as it 

conducts brutal a immigration crackdown

 in the US. 




Palantir currently holds a 

highly controversial patient data contract

 with the NHS, which campaigners and medics say has damaged trust in the health service. The government is under pressure from health workers and patients to allow Palantir’s NHS contract to end in February 2027.  




Palantir holds swathes of lucrative contracts in sensitive areas of the British state – now 

estimated to total nearly £1bn

. Maskell raised the issue of these contracts being expanded without “due process or competition” in February. Both Corbyn and Maskell have highlighted the links between Palantir and the disgraced Labour grandee Mandelson. 




Then-PM Starmer visited Palantir’s offices in Washington in February 2025, when the spytech firm 

was a client 

of consultancy firm Global Counsel, which 

Mandelson co-founded and held shares in until February 2026

. The meeting was set up by the British embassy in the US, headed at the time by Mandelson. No record of what was discussed has been published. 




In December last year, Palantir landed its biggest ever MoD deal, worth £240m, 

without a competitive tendering process

. 




Mandelson currently faces charges of misconduct in public office over allegations he passed confidential information to Epstein during the 2008 financial crisis. 




Lewis described Palantir as an “America-first corporation”. “We stopped China building our 5G network,” he said. “Why would you want people like Alex Karp and Peter Thiel building your 21st century infrastructure?”

title: Stadtring Zweibrücken – Pride Month Edition
content:
Edit 2026-10-22: Das Video wurde schon im Sommer hochgeladen, war aber wegen eines Kopierfehlers nicht in tchncs.de auffindbar.

Das Projekt ist eine Arbeit im Voranschreiten mit ungewissem Ausgang. Eine Vierjahreszeiten-Collage wäre eine Idee, denn mittlerweile fehlt nur noch die Herbstversion.

author: CNT Galiza
title: La CNT logra el reconocimiento de la improcedencia de un despido disciplinario en la constructora JReformas
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Galego







Castellano

La CNT logra el reconocimiento de la improcedencia de un despido disciplinario en la constructora JReformas




La CNT acaba de sumar una nueva victoria en la lucha contra la arbitrariedad empresarial en el sector de la construcción. En esta ocasión, la intervención del sindicato permitió que se reconociera como improcedente el despido disciplinario de un compañero, tras la actuación de la empresa con absoluto desprecio por las garantías legales que amparan a todo trabajador.




El conflicto surgió tras una discusión entre el trabajador y su jefe. La empresa, lejos de tramitar correctamente el procedimiento disciplinario, dio de baja al trabajador de la Seguridad Social antes de que venciera el plazo para la audiencia previa exigida por ley. Este procedimiento, obligatorio desde la sentencia del Tribunal Supremo del 18 de noviembre de 2024, tiene como objetivo permitir al trabajador defenderse de los hechos que se le imputan antes de que la empresa adopte la decisión definitiva de despido.




Las actuaciones de la empresa JReformas constituyen una grave falta formal. Como establece la jurisprudencia, la falta de una audiencia previa efectiva invalida automáticamente el despido, puesto que la decisión de rescisión se adoptó sin dar al trabajador una verdadera oportunidad de ser escuchado. Además, la baja de la Seguridad Social no constituye una rescisión válida del contrato, sino que puede considerarse un despido de facto.




No se puede despedir a alguien por un hecho consumado. La audiencia previa no es un mero trámite, sino un derecho del trabajador. Que una empresa dé de baja a la Seguridad Social sin la audiencia previa es la prueba más clara de que su intención nunca fue cumplir la ley, sino deshacerse del trabajador cuanto antes.




El resultado de la intervención sindical fue claro: el despido fue declarado injustificado. Para la CNT, esta victoria es un nuevo recordatorio de que los empresarios no pueden eludir los procedimientos legales con impunidad, por mucho que confundan su empresa con un feudo.




La construcción sigue siendo un sector donde la arbitrariedad empresarial campa a sus anchas. Pero cuando los trabajadores nos organizamos, la ley está de nuestro lado.




La CNT recuerda a todos los trabajadores del sector que no están solos. Ante cualquier situación de despido injustificado, represalias o violación de derechos, el sindicato ofrece asesoría y defensa legal.




La construcción no es territorio comanche para los empleadores. Organízate y defiende tus derechos.




En la CNT, si los empleadores atacan, respondemos.







Galego

A CNT logra que se recoñeza a improcedencia dun despedimento disciplinario na empresa de construción JReformas




A CNT vén de sumar unha nova vitoria na loita contra a arbitrariedade patronal no sector da construción. Nesta ocasión, a intervención do sindicato permitiu que se recoñecese a improcedencia do despedimento disciplinario dun compañeiro, despois de que a empresa actuase cun desprezo absoluto polas garantías legais que asisten a calquera traballador.




O conflito xurdiu tras unha discusión entre o traballador e o seu xefe. A empresa, lonxe de tramitar correctamente o procedemento disciplinario, deu de baixa ao traballador na Seguridade Social antes de que rematase o prazo da audiencia previa que a lexislación esixe. Este trámite, obrigatorio desde a sentenza do Tribunal Supremo do 18 de novembro de 2024, ten como finalidade permitir que a persoa traballadora poida defenderse dos feitos que se lle imputan antes de que a empresa adopte a decisión definitiva de despedilo .




A actuación da empresa JReformas constitúe un defecto formal grave. Como recolle a xurisprudencia, a falta dunha audiencia previa efectiva converte automaticamente o despedimento en improcedente, xa que a decisión extintiva foi adoptada sen dar ao traballador a oportunidade real de ser escoitado . A baixa na Seguridade Social, ademais, non equivale a unha extinción válida do contrato, senón que pode ser cualificada como un despedimento de feito .




Non se pode despedir a alguén pola vía dos feitos consumados. A audiencia previa non é un papel para cubrir o expediente, é un dereito do traballador. Que unha empresa dea de baixa a un traballador na Seguridade Social antes de escoitalo é a proba máis clara de que a súa intención nunca foi cumprir coa lei, senón librarse del canto antes.




O resultado da intervención sindical foi claro: recoñeceuse a improcedencia do despedimento . Para a CNT, esta vitoria supón un novo recordatorio de que a patronal non pode saltarse impunemente os procedementos legais, por moito que confunda a súa empresa cun feudo.




A construción segue a ser un sector onde a arbitrariedade patronal campa ás súas anchas. Pero cando os traballadores nos organizamos, a lei ponse do noso lado.




A CNT lembra a todos os traballadores e traballadoras do sector que non están sós. Ante calquera situación de despedimento inxustificado, represalia ou vulneración de dereitos, o sindicato ofrece asesoramento e defensa xurídica.




A construción non é un territorio comanche para a patronal. Organízate e defende os teus dereitos.

Na CNT, se a patronal ataca, respondemos.




La entrada 

La CNT logra el reconocimiento de la improcedencia de un despido disciplinario en la constructora JReformas

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Isabel Seta
title: As ameaças são reais – a resistência também
content:
Nos últimos dias antes do segundo turno da 

eleição presidencial

, com o país totalmente mobilizado, um assunto ganhou destaque: o que está em jogo nessas eleições é a Constituição de 1988, que não à toa é chamada de Constituição Cidadã, porque coloca expressamente direitos como educação e saúde gratuitas e universais, igualdade perante a lei, direitos trabalhistas e também direito à natureza preservada, entre outras garantias.




O candidato Flávio Bolsonaro já declarou que, caso eleito, vai mudar a Constituição, o que causa preocupação em muitos setores da sociedade, em especial os mais vulneráveis, como os povos indígenas. O 

Bom dia, fim do mundo

 dessa semana fala sobre as principais ameaças aos direitos constitucionais, e também sobre a resistência popular que está se organizando em várias frentes. Ouça agora.







E MAIS:




PESSOAL, URGENTE: escutem a Trombeta da semana. E no quadro “Se é pra falar de economia…”, Clara Marinho fala sobre o plano econômico de Flávio Bolsonaro.

author: A Melanie Lübbert
title: Baden-Württemberg: Kettensäge gegen Datenschutz
content:
Bild: Michael Fenton Unsplash-Lizenz; Bearbeitung: Digitalcourage

Wer in Baden-Württemberg wissen will, ob ein Unternehmen oder eine Behörde rechtmäßig mit personenbezogenen Daten umgeht, kann sich an den Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit, Tobias Keber, wenden. Doch ausgerechnet seine Behörde soll massiv Personal verlieren.

Der Entwurf des Staatshaushaltsgesetzes 2027 sieht vor, bis zum Ende der Legislaturperiode (2029) 40 Prozent der Stellen abzubauen. Von derzeit 67,5 Stellen sollen 27 wegfallen. Übrig blieben gerade einmal 42 Planstellen. Für 2027 sind zunächst 5,5 Stellen zur Streichung vorgesehen; weitere Kürzungen sollen 2028 und 2029 folgen.

Eine inhaltliche Begründung für diesen drastischen Einschnitt liefert die grün-schwarze Landesregierung unter Ministerpräsident Cem Özdemir nicht. Auffällig ist zudem: Während für die übrige zentrale Verwaltung fünf Prozent Stellenabbau vorgesehen sind, soll die Datenschutzaufsicht 40 Prozent einsparen – eine achtmal so hohe Kürzungsquote.

Der geplante Kahlschlag steht in krassem Widerspruch zur Entwicklung der vergangenen Jahre. Seit die Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO) 2018 wirksam wurde, hat sich die Arbeitsbelastung der Datenschutzaufsicht erheblich erhöht. Die Zahl der Beschwerden und gemeldeten Datenpannen ist massiv gestiegen. Zugleich werden Datenverarbeitungen immer komplexer und stellen die Behörde vor neue Herausforderungen.

Quelle: Tätigkeitsberichte des Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg. Auswertung: Redaktion Digitalcourage. [Grafik: padeluun, mit Hilfe von KI erstellt]

Die Zahlen verdeutlichen, wie stark sich die Aufgaben der Behörde verändert haben:

Beschwerden: Seit Einführung der DSGVO wenden sich deutlich mehr Menschen an die Datenschutzaufsicht. Neue Technologien und der zunehmende Einsatz Künstlicher Intelligenz schaffen zusätzliche Konfliktfelder. Im Jahr 2025 erreichte die Zahl der Beschwerden mit 7.673 einen neuen Höchststand – ein Anstieg um rund 90 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahr.

Datenpannen: Mit der DSGVO wurden die Meldepflichten bei Verletzungen des Schutzes personenbezogener Daten erheblich ausgeweitet. Für die Aufsichtsbehörde entstand dadurch ein umfangreiches zusätzliches Aufgabenfeld. Die Zahl der Meldungen stieg deutlich an und erreichte 2025 mit 4.059 einen neuen Höchstwert.

Beratungen: Die Einführung der DSGVO löste zunächst einen enormen Beratungsbedarf aus. Durch standardisierte Leitfäden, Orientierungshilfen und Online-Angebote der Datenschutzkonferenz sowie eigene Praxishilfen und Veranstaltungen konnte die Behörde viele wiederkehrende Fragen beantworten. Auch das Bildungszentrum des Landesbeauftragten übernimmt einen wichtigen Teil der Beratung. Inzwischen entstehen neue Aufgaben, insbesondere durch Künstliche Intelligenz und europäische Regelungen wie den Europäischen Gesundheitsdatenraum. Unternehmen, Behörden und Bürger.innen sind weiterhin auf die fachliche Unterstützung der Datenschutzaufsicht angewiesen.

Kontrollen: Die anlassunabhängigen Vor-Ort-Prüfungen wurden nach 2018 aufgrund begrenzter personeller Kapazitäten deutlich reduziert. Während der Corona-Pandemie waren zusätzliche Einschränkungen notwendig. Nach 2022 konnten die Kontrollen mit einer besseren Personalausstattung wieder intensiviert werden. Die geplanten Kürzungen drohen diese Entwicklung umzukehren.

Personalstellen: Seit Einführung der DSGVO verdoppelte der Landtag die Zahl der Personalstellen bis 2025 schrittweise auf den Höchststand von 67,5 Stellen. Zwischenzeitlich waren es mit befristet zugewiesenen Personalstellen 70,5 Stellen. Bis 2029 ist nun eine Reduzierung um rund 40 Prozent vorgesehen. Am Ende sollen nur noch 42 Planstellen verbleiben, während andere Landesbehörden fünf Prozent einsparen sollen.

Hinweis: In der linken primären Y-Achse finden sich aufsummiert die Ereignisse „Beschwerden, Datenpannen, Beratungen und Kontrollen“; in der rechten sekundären Y-Achse finden sich die Werte für Kontrollen und LfDI-Personalstellen.

Quelle: Tätigkeitsberichte des Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg. Auswertung: Redaktion Digitalcourage. [Grafik: padeluun, mit Hilfe von KI erstellt]

Dabei benötigt die Behörde nicht weniger, sondern mehr Personal. Landesdatenschutzbeauftragter Tobias Keber hat dem Landtag in seiner Stellungnahme zum Haushaltsentwurf dargelegt, dass für eine ordnungsgemäße Aufgabenerfüllung sieben zusätzliche Stellen erforderlich wären. Angesichts von 90 Prozent mehr Beschwerden gegenüber 2024 warnt er davor, mit den geplanten Kürzungen „die Kettensäge am Beschwerderecht der DS-GVO anzusetzen“.

Der Haushaltsentwurf liegt nun beim Landtag.

Die DSGVO verpflichtet die Aufsichtsbehörden, Beschwerden angemessen zu untersuchen und Betroffene innerhalb einer angemessenen Frist über den Fortgang und das Ergebnis zu informieren. Doch wie soll eine Behörde dieser Verpflichtung nachkommen, wenn die Zahl der Beschwerden steigt und gleichzeitig 40 Prozent ihrer Stellen wegfallen sollen?

Die DSGVO und die europäische Datenschutzrichtlinie für den Bereich Polizei und Justiz verpflichten die Mitgliedstaaten ausdrücklich, ihre Aufsichtsbehörden mit ausreichenden personellen, technischen und finanziellen Mitteln auszustatten. Ob der geplante Stellenabbau mit diesen Vorgaben vereinbar ist, ist daher auch eine europarechtliche Frage.

Eine Entlastung der Landesdatenschutzaufsicht wäre denkbar, wenn bestimmte Aufgaben künftig vom Bund übernommen würden. Tatsächlich sieht der Koalitionsvertrag der schwarz-roten Bundesregierung eine Neuordnung vor: Zuständigkeiten und Kompetenzen der Datenschutzaufsicht sollen stärker bei der Bundesdatenschutzbeauftragten gebündelt werden.

Dahinter steht unter anderem die Sorge, dass unterschiedliche Auslegungen des Datenschutzrechts durch die Landesbehörden zu Wettbewerbsnachteilen für Unternehmen führen könnten.

Allerdings gibt es bereits ein Gremium, das genau solche Unterschiede verringern soll: die Datenschutzkonferenz (DSK). In ihr stimmen sich die Datenschutzaufsichtsbehörden des Bundes und der Länder ab, erarbeiten gemeinsame Positionen und veröffentlichen Orientierungshilfen. Ihr Ziel ist eine möglichst einheitliche Anwendung des Datenschutzrechts in Deutschland.

Bislang ist von der angekündigten Neuordnung jedoch nichts Konkretes zu sehen. Die Bundesregierung hat noch keinen Gesetzentwurf vorgelegt, der eine Verlagerung von Zuständigkeiten auf den Bund regelt. Wann und in welchem Umfang die Landesbehörden tatsächlich entlastet würden, ist völlig offen.

Baden-Württemberg will die Stellen trotzdem schon jetzt streichen. Die Aufgaben bleiben – das Personal soll gehen.

Sollte die grün-schwarze Landesregierung ihre Kürzungspläne durchsetzen, hätte das gravierende Folgen für den Datenschutz in Baden-Württemberg. Weniger Personal bedeutet weniger Kapazitäten für Kontrollen, Beratungen und die Bearbeitung von Beschwerden. Datenschutzverstöße könnten länger unentdeckt bleiben oder erst mit erheblicher Verzögerung verfolgt werden.

Die Leidtragenden wären vor allem die Menschen, deren Beschwerden unbearbeitet liegen bleiben. Wer seine Rechte durchsetzen will, müsste dann womöglich häufiger selbst vor Gericht ziehen. Statt den Datenschutz wirksam zu gewährleisten, würde das Land die Verantwortung zunehmend auf die Betroffenen abwälzen.

Die Streichpläne sind unverantwortlich. Datenschutz und Persönlichkeitsrechte sind ein hohes Gut; angesichts der technischen Entwicklungen und der Wildwest-Mentalität einiger Firmen ("einfach machen!") sind unsere Rechte zunehmend in Gefahr. Eine Aufsichtsbehörde muss arbeitsfähig sein, um gegen Datenschutzverstöße vorzugehen. Ist sie das nicht, wird das Recht auf informationelle Selbstbestimmung der Bürgerinnen und Bürger abgewürgt. Und das ist ganz sicher nicht das, was Baden-Württemberg zukunftsfähig macht. Die Landesregierung muss ihre Streichpläne zurückziehen.

Entwurf des Staatshaushaltsgesetzes Baden-Württemberg 2027, Landtagsdrucksache 18/700 (9. Oktober 2026)

Stellungnahme des Landesdatenschutzbeauftragten Tobias Keber (13. Oktober 2026)
