Neuquén: jurado popular encontró culpable a Roberto Sánchez por el transfemicidio de Azul Semeñenko

 se publicó primero en 

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.

author: Rubén Morvolution
title: La huelga como medio, la clase como sujeto: una respuesta al debate sobre el movimiento de vivienda
content:
La huelga como medio, la clase como sujeto: una respuesta al debate sobre el movimiento de vivienda

Sobre la centralidad histórica de la huelga y las posibilidades de articulación entre las luchas laborales y por la vivienda.

El artículo El movimiento de vivienda ante su Rubicón, de Alfredo Apilánez, plantea un debate que considero necesario. La crisis de acceso a la vivienda, las limitaciones de las organizaciones sindicales y la relación entre las reivindicaciones inmediatas y la transformación social son cuestiones que no podemos eludir.

Comparto la preocupación por el riesgo de que los movimientos sociales terminen subordinados a las instituciones, atrapados en calendarios electorales o limitados a reclamar reformas que no alteren las relaciones de poder existentes. Sin embargo, discrepo de la orientación estratégica que se desprende del artículo, especialmente cuando contrapone las posibilidades de la huelga general a la construcción de espacios autogestionados y experiencias de okupación.

La cuestión fundamental, a mi entender, no consiste en determinar qué práctica expresa una mayor radicalidad, sino qué instrumentos permiten a la clase trabajadora desarrollar una capacidad colectiva de intervención y transformación social. Desde esa perspectiva, considero necesario reivindicar la centralidad histórica de la huelga, sin convertirla en un fin en sí mismo.

Una huelga no constituye por sí sola una revolución, ni garantiza una victoria o una mayor conciencia de clase. Puede limitarse a una reivindicación salarial, quedar reducida a una convocatoria testimonial o agotarse sin producir cambios organizativos duraderos. Pero reducir su significado a los resultados inmediatos o a las concesiones que pueda arrancar al Estado supone dejar fuera una dimensión fundamental de la historia del movimiento obrero.

La huelga ha sido uno de los instrumentos mediante los cuales la clase trabajadora ha aprendido a reconocerse como fuerza colectiva. Su importancia no reside únicamente en detener temporalmente la producción, sino en la posibilidad de que quienes sostienen la actividad económica descubran, mediante su propia experiencia, la capacidad que poseen cuando actúan conjuntamente.

La preparación de una huelga exige relaciones, organización, discusión de objetivos, construcción de solidaridades y toma de decisiones. Durante el conflicto pueden aparecer nuevas formas de cooperación que, posteriormente, se mantengan, amplíen o desaparezcan. Nada de ello está garantizado, pero precisamente por eso la huelga debe entenderse como un medio dentro de un proceso de organización y lucha, no como un acontecimiento que contenga por sí mismo la transformación social.

Confundir el instrumento con su finalidad sería tan equivocado como descartarlo porque una convocatoria concreta no reúna las condiciones necesarias para alcanzar todos sus objetivos.

La centralidad del trabajo no ha desaparecido

Para comprender la importancia de la huelga en la actualidad, debemos abandonar la idea de que la clase trabajadora se limita al proletariado industrial tradicional. El mundo del trabajo ha cambiado profundamente y, con él, la composición de la propia clase trabajadora.

Hoy, la actividad económica depende tanto de la industria como del transporte, la logística, los servicios y los cuidados, entre otros sectores. Aunque las condiciones laborales y las posibilidades de organizarse son muy diferentes, todos ellos forman parte de una sociedad que continúa dependiendo del trabajo humano para funcionar. Por eso, la diversidad de la clase trabajadora no elimina su importancia ni la capacidad de la huelga para convertirse en un instrumento de lucha colectiva.

En un artículo anterior, reflexionaba sobre la recomposición de clase y la crisis de la sociedad de propietarios, planteaba que la pérdida de determinadas seguridades patrimoniales puede modificar las identidades sociales de sectores asalariados que tradicionalmente se reconocían como clases medias.

Muchos de esos sectores ya dependían de vender su fuerza de trabajo. Lo que cambia no es necesariamente su posición objetiva, sino sus expectativas de estabilidad y la forma en que comprenden su relación con el conjunto de la sociedad. Que una parte de la clase trabajadora posea una vivienda no elimina automáticamente su dependencia salarial, del mismo modo que las diferencias patrimoniales, las contradicciones internas o las orientaciones políticas reaccionarias no permiten concluir que la clase haya perdido toda posibilidad de constituirse como sujeto colectivo.

La clase no es una unidad política previamente dada: su constitución depende de experiencias históricas de conflicto, organización y solidaridad. En ese proceso, la huelga continúa siendo uno de los instrumentos capaces de intervenir directamente sobre las relaciones materiales que sostienen el capitalismo.

La okupación y sus límites como estrategia general

La okupación ha desempeñado funciones diferentes dentro de los movimientos sociales. Puede responder a una necesidad habitacional inmediata, recuperar inmuebles sin uso social o proporcionar espacios para desarrollar actividades colectivas, redes de apoyo mutuo y experiencias autogestionarias. Negar esas posibilidades sería desconocer una parte de la historia de los movimientos por la vivienda y de las prácticas libertarias.

Sin embargo, reconocer su utilidad no obliga a considerarla equivalente a la huelga en términos históricos o estratégicos. Mientras la okupación interviene principalmente sobre la propiedad y el uso de determinados espacios, la huelga permite interrumpir colectivamente el trabajo del que depende el funcionamiento de la economía. No son instrumentos incompatibles, pero tampoco intercambiables.

La ocupación de un edificio puede contribuir a satisfacer necesidades, organizar un barrio o cuestionar determinadas relaciones de propiedad. Sin embargo, la multiplicación de espacios autogestionados no implica necesariamente una transformación de las relaciones generales de producción y distribución. Existe el riesgo de confundir la ruptura inmediata con la legalidad de la propiedad con una ruptura efectiva de las relaciones sociales capitalistas.

Una acción puede ser radical en su forma y limitada en sus consecuencias, como también puede suceder con una huelga minoritaria, aislada o carente de continuidad. Por tanto, la cuestión no es establecer una jerarquía moral entre quienes hacen huelga y quienes okupan, sino examinar qué capacidad tiene cada experiencia para extender la organización colectiva más allá de sus protagonistas inmediatos.

La radicalidad de una práctica no debería medirse exclusivamente por su confrontación con la legalidad existente, sino también por su capacidad para transformar las relaciones sociales que pretende combatir.

Vivienda y trabajo: dimensiones de una misma realidad

La crisis de la vivienda muestra con especial claridad que la explotación y las condiciones de reproducción social no pueden analizarse por separado. El salario determina una parte fundamental de nuestras posibilidades de acceso a la vivienda y, a su vez, el alquiler o la hipoteca condicionan nuestras necesidades salariales, nuestra capacidad de ahorro y nuestras posibilidades de resistir situaciones de explotación laboral.

La vivienda no constituye, por tanto, un problema exterior a la lucha de clases, pero tampoco puede comprenderse únicamente como una cuestión de acceso individual a un inmueble. Las relaciones entre propietarios e inquilinos, el peso creciente del patrimonio heredado, la financiarización inmobiliaria y las desigualdades territoriales forman parte de una estructura económica más amplia.

Por eso resulta especialmente significativa la propuesta de la huelga por la vivienda del 11 de noviembre. Su interés no reside exclusivamente en la convocatoria de una jornada de paro, sino en la posibilidad de relacionar las organizaciones laborales con los sindicatos de inquilinas, las asambleas de barrio y otras experiencias de organización popular.

Esa articulación no exige que el movimiento de vivienda quede subordinado a las estructuras del sindicalismo laboral, ni requiere diluir las particularidades de cada conflicto en una plataforma que pretenda representarlos a todos. Las organizaciones pueden conservar su autonomía y, al mismo tiempo, reconocer objetivos compartidos y desarrollar instrumentos de cooperación.

La huelga puede convertirse así en un punto de encuentro entre experiencias que intervienen sobre aspectos diferentes de una misma realidad material, aunque esa posibilidad solo llegará a concretarse mediante las relaciones que sus participantes sean capaces de construir.

El 11N y la centralidad histórica de la huelga

No sabemos qué alcance tendrá la huelga del 11 de noviembre ni qué relaciones organizativas podrán desarrollarse a partir de ella. Sería equivocado anticipar su éxito simplemente porque relaciona las reivindicaciones laborales con la crisis de la vivienda, pero también sería precipitado descartarla por las limitaciones del sindicalismo existente o porque algunas de sus reivindicaciones se dirijan a las instituciones.

Reclamar medidas inmediatas no implica necesariamente aceptar que la transformación social deba quedar limitada a la acción estatal. La historia del movimiento obrero está atravesada por luchas que combinaron reivindicaciones concretas con procesos más amplios de organización, autonomía y confrontación social.

Desde esa perspectiva, el interés del 11N no debería medirse únicamente por el seguimiento de la jornada, sino también por los vínculos que puedan establecerse entre centros de trabajo, organizaciones por la vivienda y barrios, así como por su capacidad de continuidad.

El debate abierto por Alfredo Apilánez resulta útil porque obliga a reflexionar sobre los límites de nuestras propias herramientas. Sin embargo, considero que la crítica al sindicalismo institucional y a las huelgas reducidas a reivindicaciones inmediatas no debería conducirnos a cuestionar la centralidad histórica de la huelga como instrumento de lucha de clases. Del mismo modo, reconocer el valor de las experiencias autogestionarias no exige convertir la okupación o la construcción de espacios alternativos en una estrategia general de transformación social.

El capitalismo no se reproduce únicamente mediante la propiedad inmobiliaria, sino también a través de relaciones de producción, explotación, circulación y acumulación que atraviesan el conjunto de la sociedad. Transformarlas exige capacidades colectivas que no pueden reducirse a la existencia de espacios relativamente autónomos dentro de ellas.

La huelga no es la revolución, pero la capacidad de quienes sostienen la sociedad para detener colectivamente su actividad continúa siendo una expresión fundamental de su fuerza potencial. Esa fuerza necesita organización, aprendizaje y solidaridad para convertirse en capacidad de transformación.

Por eso, el objetivo no debería ser defender una herramienta por fidelidad a una tradición, sino contribuir a que la clase trabajadora contemporánea, diversa y fragmentada, pueda constituirse en un sujeto capaz de intervenir conscientemente sobre sus propias condiciones de existencia.

La huelga es un medio. La okupación también puede serlo. La emancipación social no consiste en perpetuar nuestros instrumentos de lucha, sino en desarrollar la capacidad colectiva necesaria para transformar las relaciones que los hicieron necesarios.

Rubén Morvolution — Trabajador industrial

title: Émeutes, pillages et état d'urgence
content:
Allons nous enfin quitter l'époque contemporaine ? C'est la question qu'est venue ouvrir avec fracas le soulèvement du 17 octobre. Pour discuter de cette journée, de ce qu'elle enseigne, appelle et peut-être présage, nous allons enchaîner les invitations et les discussions. Pour cette première, nous accueillons Eugénie Mérieau et Samuel Hayat. On discute de ce qui a fait événement et de pourquoi cet événement naît d'une époque, celle-là même que tout le monde veut quitter et pas seulement la GenZ. Comment la police s'est-elle retrouvée à ce point en déroute ? Pourquoi l'état d'urgence n'a-t-il pas encore été décrété ? Sommes-nous à l'aube d'un virage encore plus autoritaire du régime ou de sa dislocation finale ? En quoi le pillage doit-il être défendu contre ceux qui s'en désolidarisent ? Pourquoi faut-il soutenir ce que d'aucuns appellent la « casse » ? Allons-nous enfin devoir choisir entre apocalypse et révolution ?







Lire le très bon texte de Samuel Hayat, 

Rouvrir l'époque contemporaine

.

title: Dersim Belediyesi işçilerinden açıklama: İşe iade kararı uygulansın, kayyım düzenine son verilsin
content:
Dersim - Dersim Belediyesi’nde kayyım yönetimi tarafından işten atılan işçiler, Seyit Rıza Meydanı’nda yaptıkları basın açıklamasında işe iade kararlarının uygulanmasını istedi. İşçiler, işten çıkarılmalarının üzerinden 650 gün geçtiğini belirterek fiili ve hukuki mücadelelerini sürdürdüklerini ifade etti. Açıklamaya Emek Partisi (EMEP) Genel Başkanı Seyit Aslan da katıldı.

Basın açıklamasını işten atılan işçilerden Ali Mükan okudu. Mahkemenin işe iade kararı verdiğini belirten Mükan, buna rağmen kayyım yönetiminin mahkeme kararını uygulamadığına dikkat çekerek kararın bir an önce uygulanmasını istediklerini söyledi.

Dersim’de işsizliğin yüksek olduğuna ve gençlerin iş bulamadıkları için kentten ayrılmak zorunda kaldığına dikkat çeken Mükan, 13 kişinin işten çıkarılmasının yalnızca işçileri değil, ailelerinin geçim koşullarını ve geleceğini de etkilediğini belirtti.

İşe iade kararının uygulanmamasına bütçenin gerekçe gösterilmesine tepki gösteren Mükan, “Belediyenin bütçesi işçi kıyımı yapılarak düzeltilmez. Bütçe açığının sorumlusu da biz değiliz” dedi. Dersim halkının iradesinin yok sayılmasına karşı çıktıklarını belirten Mükan, kayyım uygulamalarına son verilmesini ve kayyımların derhal geri çekilmesini talep etti.

Basın açıklamasında söz alan EMEP Genel Başkanı Aslan ise Saray rejiminin kayyım politikalarına tepki göstererek “Dersim halkının iradesini çalan anlayışla, Gülistan Doku’yu katleden anlayışla, işçi arkadaşlarımızın işe geri dönmesine engel olan anlayış aynı. Esenyurt'ta halk iradesi çalındı. Milyonlarca doların nasıl ortaya çıktığına hep tanık olduk. Bölgeye atanan kayyumların yolsuzluklarına tanık olduk. Çünkü Saray oligarşisi tarafından atanan kayyumlar kendilerini güvencede görüyor. İşe iade davasını kazanan işçilerin kayyım tarafından işe alınmaması Saray oligarşisinin soruna nasıl yaklaştığının göstergesidir. Tek bir işçi dahi işten atılmış olsa bu adaletsizliğin karşısında durmaya devam edeceğiz. İşçi arkadaşlarımızın işe alınması için mücadelemizi sürdürmeye devam edeceğiz. Belediyenin koltuğunda oturan kayyum bugün kendisini güvencede görüyor olabilir. Ama yarın işçiler, emekçiler bunun hesabını sorar. Yarın iktidarı kaybettiklerinde ne yapacaklarını şimdiden hesap etsinler” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Uno por uno, el detalle de los proyectos que debate Diputados en otro miércoles caliente
content:
El temario incluye los proyectos de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, de Discapacidad, de morosidad familiar, combate al vandalismo rural y trazabilidad de medicamentos de alto riesgo.







La Cámara de Diputados celebrará una sesión especial este miércoles con un amplio temario que incluye los proyectos de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, de Discapacidad, de morosidad familiar, combate al vandalismo rural y trazabilidad de medicamentos de alto riesgo.




Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada y foco en la Ley de Tierras




Este proyecto llega con media sanción a la Cámara baja después del desguace aplicado por la oposición peronista en el Senado, que le volteó el capítulo vinculado a la Ley de Manejo del Fuego pero también el que buscaba derogar la Ley de Tierras Rurales, toda vez que el artículo 154 del DNU 70/23 se encontraba derogado.




Paradójicamente, ahora el Gobierno busca restituir la Ley de Tierras en el tratamiento en Diputados, después de que la sociedad le mostrara los dientes en contra de la extranjerización y la oposición amenazara seriamente con tirar abajo todo el DNU 70.




De esta manera, se reafirmarán los límites del 30% de extranjerización a nivel nacional, provincial y departamental, además del tope de 1000 hectáreas en zonas núcleo del país, espejos de agua y zonas de frontera.




La versión menguada de la Ley de Propiedad Privada que quedó en pie después de la extirpación en el Senado son capítulos que modifican la Ley de Expropiaciones, restringiendo las capacidades del Estado para declarar la utilidad pública de bienes inmuebles, y también una reforma de la ley de Desalojos para permitir acortar drásticamente los tiempos judiciales para la restitución de propiedades usurpadas o con tenencias irregulares.




En cuanto a las expropiaciones, el dictamen de mayoría estableció que habrá tope del 30% de indemnización por lucro cesante si está debidamente acreditado: el proyecto original no ponía ningún porcentaje.




Desde la perspectiva de los opositores, indexar el derecho público y el bien común al cálculo del éxito comercial de una empresa privada desvirtúa la “función social de la propiedad”.




Sobre los desalojos por usurpación, se dispone que el juez podrá disponer la inmediata entrega del inmueble y podrá intimar dentro de las 72 horas su devolución si así lo pide el propietario, que deberá mostrar con prueba documental que es el dueño de este terreno, vivienda o campo.




En el caso de desalojos por mora (es decir, cuando no hay una usurpación directa), luego de la intimación al pago los inquilinos tendrán un plazo de al menos 10 días para regularizar deudas antes de que el locador les pueda iniciar la acción de desalojo, contando desde el momento que recibieron la notificación.




Existe, de todos modos, un protocolo de vulnerabilidad que asegura un plazo máximo de 10 días para asegurar una alternativa habitacional transitoria con intervención del Ministerio Público Tutelar cuando en la ocupación hayan menores, discapacitados o adultos mayores desamparados.




Por otra parte, el proyecto de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada modifica la ley “Pierri” de regularización dominial para que puedan acceder a la escritura de esa vivienda única las familias que tengan una posesión pacífica demostrable a lo largo de los 10 años anteriores.




En tanto, se reconoce la “ocupación temporánea anormal”, admitiéndose por 90 días prorrogable por única vez en circunstancias graves verificables de necesidad pública como emergencias sanitarias, conflictos armados, desastres naturales.




Ley de Discapacidad




En el caso del proyecto sobre Discapacidad, el oficialismo no debería pasar apuros ya que tiene cerrado el dictamen a partir de concesiones a pedido de Argentina Federal y el MID.




El proyecto de “Ley de Fortalecimiento, Sostenibilidad y Eficiencia Permanente del Sistema de Discapacidad” toma en cuenta casi todo el esquema de beneficios plasmados en la ley 27.793 sobre Discapacidad pero le quita el carácter de emergencia y transitoriedad, convirtiéndola en una norma de orden público, con efectos permanentes, que exceden los gobiernos de turno.




En este sentido, para La Libertad Avanza, este proyecto cristaliza una versión “superadora” de la ley de emergencia que la oposición de Unión por la Patria, Provincias Unidas, el Frente de Izquierda, la Coalición Cívica y Elijo Catamarca busca prorrogar por un año más hasta el 31 de diciembre del 2027.




Lo que se mantiene de la ley de emergencia es, por ejemplo, la compatibilidad entre el goce de una pensión contributiva por discapacidad (70% del haber jubilatorio mínimo) para titulares del CUD y tener un empleo formal o monotributo, siempre y cuando los ingresos no superen los dos salarios mínimos vitales y móviles.




Además se mantiene el principio de nomenclador único, se ratifica la indexación automática periódica de los aranceles de las prestaciones por el índice de movilidad jubilatoria, y se garantiza la cobertura básica de protección médica del Plan Federal Incluir Salud para quienes tengan la pensión por discapacidad.




En cuanto al financiamiento, se establece que la asignación presupuestaria del Ministerio de Salud no podrá ser inferior en términos reales al ejercicio fiscal del año anterior.




Por otro lado, se crea un sistema de auditorías periódicas con cruce de datos de ANSES, ARCA, SINTyS y RENAPER bajo el principio del debido proceso inclusivo.




Y se incorporó a pedido de aliados una cláusula transitoria que exige un cronograma para el pago de las compensaciones atrasadas a prestadores, con un plazo máximo de 30 días para la reglamentación del PEN.




La oposición se aferra a la prórroga de la emergencia (por un año más, hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2027) porque por su propia naturaleza genera mayores condiciones de exigibilidad a jueces para que resuelvan de manera perentoria las 324.303 solicitudes de pensión pendientes y las compensaciones no pagadas a los prestadores.




Además sostiene que el proyecto del oficialismo mantiene separadas la pensión por invalidez laboral y la pensión por discapacidad, y endurece los requisitos.




También argumentan que la ley propuesta por La Libertad Avanza y sus aliados delega en la reglamentación la evaluación para acceder a la pensión y la compatibilidad con el trabajo, y permite suspender pensiones sin debido proceso, por simple cruce de datos.




Según advierten, tampoco garantiza el financiamiento, ni asegura el pago de la deuda con los prestadores ni el atraso arancelario del 30,67%.




Endeudamiento familiar




El dictamen de mayoría es el del oficialismo y sus aliados del PRO y la UCR, y hace hincapié en brindar información detallada sobre créditos al usuario para prevenir situaciones irregulares, pero no interviene ni con tasas máximas ni con planes de refinanciación para deudores críticos.




El proyecto se denomina “Ley de Transparencia Crediticia, Educación Financiera, Mitigación del Fraude Digital y Protección de los Consumidores”.




Uno de los pilares es la transparencia y el acceso a la información de créditos al consumo, con especial detalle en los créditos de corto plazo, que son los que suelen tener tasas más altas.




Otros ejes de la iniciativa son la precancelación de deudas, la trazabilidad completa de sus obligaciones y el acceso gratuito al perfil de riesgo dentro de las entidades bancarias y las plataformas.




El proyecto de Unión por la Patria, Provincias Unidas y la Coalición Cívica, denominado “Ley de Regularización y Alivio Financiero”, declara la emergencia por 180 días y propone un régimen de refinanciación de al menos 12 cuotas, al cual pueden adherir personas que tengan una mora de más de 60 días y por montos de hasta dos canastas básicas totales hogar tipo 2 (actualmente 3.265.010 pesos).




En tanto, se fija como cuota máxima un monto que no supere el 30% de los ingresos de las personas.




Cada persona que voluntariamente desee adherir al régimen de regularización lo deberá tramitar ante su propio acreedor, y si este no admite la gestión, interviene el Banco Central.




Por otra parte, el proyecto de UP y PU le pone un límite a la tasa de interés vinculado al Costo Financiero Total, pero le garantiza a los acreedores una ganancia moderada, que consiste en un plus sobre la tasa de refondeo mayorista (TAMAR).




Un aspecto no menor del proyecto es que se condona el 100% de los intereses punitorios, respetándose el capital, y se ponen límites a los intereses compensatorios.




La iniciativa además incluye un capítulo de portabilidad financiera, otro sobre cobranzas abusivas y otro de educación financiera.




Trazabilidad de medicamentos de alto riesgo y el recuerdo de la crisis del fentanilo




Se tratará un dictamen único firmado por unanimidad para la creación de un Sistema Nacional de Alerta y Trazabilidad de Eventos Críticos en Salud, con foco en medicamentos de alto riesgo.




La iniciativa, que tiene como autora principal a Silvana Giudici (La Libertad Avanza), constituye una respuesta a la tragedia sanitaria que comenzó en abril del 2025, cuando el fentanilo contaminado de HLB Pharma y Laboratorios Ramallo causó al menos 90 muertes y afectó a otras 44 personas.




Producto de esta crisis sanitaria, la Cámara de Diputados creó por unanimidad una Comisión Especial Investigadora, cuyo informe final recomendó la trazabilidad de medicamentos críticos.




El debate comenzó el 8 de septiembre del año pasado y el dictamen incluyó también aspectos de los proyectos presentados por los diputados Pablo Juliano (Provincias Unidas) y Victoria Tolosa Paz (Unión por la Patria).




La iniciativa establece la trazabilidad obligatoria y en tiempo real de los fármacos inyectables parenterales (intravenosos, intramusculares, intratecales, entre otros) y de sus materias primas.




El proyecto busca “establecer el deber de notificación inmediata por parte de las instituciones de salud públicas y privadas respecto del uso de medicamentos de alto riesgo, la ocurrencia de brotes infecciosos intrahospitalarios y la aparición de eventos adversos graves que puedan comprometer la salud pública”.




Entre otros puntos, se exige un registro digital en cada etapa (importación, producción y distribución) llegando hasta la administración efectiva del medicamento, vinculada al identificador clínico del paciente dentro del establecimiento hospitalario.




La norma crea también un Protocolo de Eventos Críticos de Salud, el cual se activa ante sospechas de contaminación o eventos adversos y obliga a notificar en simultáneo a Nación, Provincias y ANMAT dentro de las 24 horas.




Además se crea un Sistema Nacional de Alerta y Trazabilidad de Eventos Críticos en Salud (SNATECS), de carácter obligatorio y digital, bajo la órbita de la ANMAT.




Este mecanismo permite dar aviso inmediato a nivel nacional y proceder al bloqueo preventivo de los lotes sospechosos en un máximo de 6 horas.




El proyecto incorpora un régimen sancionatorio especial para las faltas graves, como la falsedad u omisión de datos de trazabilidad o el incumplimiento de inmovilizaciones.




Las penas incluyen multas elevadas, suspensiones, clausuras definitivas y decomiso.




Su aplicación será federal, articulada mediante el Consejo Federal de Salud (COFESA), y con alcance a todas las jurisdicciones.




Ley contra el vandalismo rural




Este proyecto impulsado por el PRO y avalado por LLA, UCR, Provincias Unidas y bloques provinciales busca incorporar la figura del vandalismo rural al Código Penal, con el objetivo de imponer duras sanciones de hasta 8 años de cárcel por la intrusión en los campos y los ataques al sistema de producción agropecuaria.




La iniciativa que tiene como autor al diputado Martín Ardohain (PRO) establece que será reprimido con penas de prisión de un mes a un año quien ingrese a un establecimiento rural, un terreno o sus dependencias contra la voluntad expresa o presunta de quien tenga derecho de excluirlo.




En tanto, “será reprimido con dos a ocho años y multas de hasta 12 veces el valor del daño quien destruya o dañe el ciclo productivo, el stock de materias primas o la infraestructura del establecimiento agropecuario, o cereales u oleaginosas todavía no cosechadas, o que luego de recolectadas se conserven o guarden en parvas, gavillas, bolsas, silobolsas, tolvas u otros sitios o unidades de almacenamiento”.

author: Unknown
title: Genel-İş 11 No'lu Şube'de delege seçimleri tamamlandı: Sandıktan kırmızı liste çıktı
content:
İzmir – DİSK Genel-İş İzmir 11 No’lu Şubede iki gün süren delege seçimleri sona erdi. Sosyal Projeler, Çevre Koruma, Kent Temizlik, İdari İşler, Mezarlık, Haller, Doğal Yaşam Parkı, Atık Dönüşüm ile Park ve Bahçeler birimlerinde yapılan seçimlerde farklı listeler yarıştı.

Dokuz birimin beşinde birinci olan kırmızı liste, seçimlerden çoğunlukla çıktı. Kırmızı liste Sosyal Projeler, Çevre Koruma, Mezarlık, Haller ve Park ve Bahçeler birimlerinde seçimi kazandı. Yeşil liste Kent Temizlik ve Doğal Yaşam Parkı, mavi liste İdari İşler, beyaz liste ise Atık Dönüşüm biriminde ilk sırada yer aldı.

Sosyal Projeler biriminde kullanılan 853 oyun 15’i geçersiz sayıldı. Geçerli 838 oyun 346’sını kırmızı, 268’ini mavi, 224’ünü ise beyaz liste aldı. Kırmızı liste bu sonuçla birimde birinci oldu.

Çevre Koruma biriminde 164 oy alan kırmızı liste seçimi kazanırken Mezarlık biriminde de 212 oyla ilk sırada yer aldı. Mezarlıkta beyaz liste 175, kahverengi liste ise 117 oy aldı.

Haller biriminde kullanılan 66 oyun 4’ü geçersiz sayıldı. Geçerli 62 oyun 42’sini kırmızı, 20’sini mavi liste aldı.

Park ve Bahçeler biriminde ise kırmızı liste 422 oyla seçimi kazandı. Mavi liste 380, beyaz liste 225 oy aldı.

Kent Temizlik biriminde yeşil liste 488 oy alarak seçimi kazandı. Mavi liste ise 405 oyda kaldı.

Doğal Yaşam Parkı biriminde kullanılan 99 oyun 97’si geçerli sayıldı. Yeşil liste 51, kırmızı liste 46 oy aldı. Böylece yeşil liste bu birimde de birinci oldu.

İdari İşler biriminde mavi liste 339 oyla seçimi kazandı. Kırmızı liste 276, beyaz liste ise 161 oy aldı.

Atık Dönüşüm biriminde ise seçimi beyaz liste kazandı.

İki gün süren seçimlerin ardından kırmızı liste beş, yeşil liste iki, mavi ve beyaz listeler ise birer birimde birinci oldu.

Genel-İş İzmir 2 No’lu Şube Başkan Adayı Arif Yıldız ile delege seçimlerini kazanan kırmızı liste temsilcileri, seçimlerin ardından delegelere seslendi. Konuşmasında işçilerin uzun süredir yaşadığı sorunlara dikkat çeken Yıldız, mevcut yönetimin işçileri ayrıştırdığını belirterek yeni dönemde birlik ve mücadeleyi esas alacaklarını söyledi.

Yıldız, “Biz ‘Ayrıştırmayın, bu işi bölmeyin, şubeyi bölmeyin’ dedikçe seçim kazanabilmek adına şubeyi böldüler. İşçiyi ayrıştırdılar. Biz ilk yola çıkarken ‘Birleştireceğiz, dert yanmaya değil mücadele etmeye geliyoruz’ dedik” ifadelerini kullandı.

Aylardır havuzda bekletilen İZENERJİ işçilerinin sorunlarına değinen Yıldız, “Biz İZENERJİ emekçisinin, 4 No’lu holün önünde aylardan beri havuzda bekleyen, bizi gördüğünde ağlayan kadın arkadaşlarımızın sorununun çözümüne geliyoruz” dedi.

Toplu iş sözleşmesi sürecine de değinen Yıldız, “İZENERJİ emekçisinin içindeki mutluluğu çalmışlar. Biz yeniden o heyecanı, mutluluğu toplu sözleşmenin etrafında birleştirerek, geçmiş dönemde yaptığımız gibi madde veren değil, madde alan bir anlayışla yola devam edeceğiz” diye konuştu.

Hak-İş’e bağlı Hizmet-İş Sendikasının İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesinde örgütlenme açıklamalarına tepki gösteren Yıldız, “Biz burada zaten 40 yıldır örgütlüyüz. Biz burada Hak-İş gibi bir sendikayı buraya sokmayacağız” dedi.

Seçim sonuçlarının işçilerin birlik talebini ortaya koyduğunu belirten Yıldız, “İZENERJİ işçisi bugünkü son sandıklarla gereken cevabı vermiştir. Bizden ayrıştıran değil, birleştiren bir süreci yürütmemizi istiyor. Hiç kimseyi ayrıştırmadan, ötekileştirmeden İZENERJİ işçisini yeniden ayağa dikeceğiz. 2 No’lu Şubeyi yeniden işçinin umudu haline getireceğiz” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: infolibre
title: Στο ΑΠΘ διδάσκεται η «καινοτόμα επιχειρηματικότητα» του μιλιταρισμού και του θανάτου!
content:
Πρωτοβουλία Πανεπιστημιακών ΑΠΘ ΠΑΜΑΚ ΔΙΠΑΕ




Στο ΑΠΘ διδάσκεται η «καινοτόμα επιχειρηματικότητα» του μιλιταρισμού και του θανάτου




Δεν το είδαμε στον ιστότοπο του πανεπιστημίου: 

https://opencoffee.gr/2026/10/17/open-coffee-thessaloniki-94/




Πρόκειται όμως για δράση του ΑΠΘ εντός του ΑΠΘ. Στις 29 Οκτωβρίου 2026 έχει κληθεί να μιλήσει στο ΚΕΔΕΑ ο διευθύνων σύμβουλος της Stark, μιας εταιρίας  παραγωγής «αμυντικών» drones, εταιρίας 3,2 δις, με συνεργάτες σε Γερμανία, Ουκρανία, Ηνωμένο Βασίλειο, Σουηδία και Ελλάδα. Στο πλαίσιο του WALK (του «επιταχυντή καινοτομίας του ΑΠΘ») φοιτητές και φοιτήτριες καλούνται να ακούσουν τον περήφανο επιχειρηματία να μιλά για το πώς, από μια μικρή startup, κατόρθωσε να πουλά τις υπηρεσίες του σε έναν κολοσσό της πολεμικής τεχνολογίας.




Αυτή είναι η εμπειρία που θεωρούν άξια να μεταδοθεί, αυτή είναι η φιλοδοξία που θέλουν να εμπνεύσουν στην επόμενη γενιά: 

Πώς να θεραπεύσει τις επιστήμες του πολέμου, πώς να διαπρέψει στην παιδαγωγική του θανάτου.




Επιπλέον, προσπαθούν να διαμηνύσουν προς Θεσσαλονικείς: Ότι πρέπει να συνηθίσουμε, από τη μια την εγκαθίδρυση της ισραηλινής SK στη Σίνδο, στη θέση της πρώην ΕΛΒΟ, από την άλλη τα διάφορα «καινοτόμα» μιλιταριστικά ερευνητικά προγράμματα που προωθούνται στο ΑΠΘ και στα πανεπιστήμια ανά την επικράτεια με την DefenseEduNet.




Πριν λίγους μήνες η πανεπιστημιακή κοινότητα, φοιτήτριες, φοιτητές και ΕΣΔΕΠ καταφέραμε και διώξαμε το συνέδριο της πολεμικής οικονομίας έξω από τους χώρους του πανεπιστημίου, κάνοντας τους συμμετέχοντες να νιώσουν έστω ανεπιθύμητοι και φοβισμένοι (όχι βέβαια ντροπή, οι κυνικοί δεν έχουν ευθιξία).




Σήμερα, την ώρα που χιλιάδες εργαζόμενοι σε λιμάνια της Ευρώπης δηλώνουν «δεν δουλεύουμε για τον πόλεμό σας» και καλούν σε απεργία στις 30 Οκτωβρίου ενάντια στην αποστολή πολεμικού υλικού για τη γενοκτονία στη Γάζα και ενάντια στη στρατιωτικοποίηση παντού, ας ενώσουμε τη φωνή μας μαζί τους:




Το πανεπιστήμιο είναι χώρος έρευνας, μελέτης, διαλόγου, εκπαίδευσης, καλλιέργειας και διαπραγμάτευσης της γνώσης για την κοινωνία, για τη φύση, για τη ζωή. Δεν είναι σχεδιαστήριο όπλων για τη βιομηχανία της εξόντωσης.




Έξω η μιλιταριστική, θανατηφόρα «επιχειρηματικότητα» του πολέμου από τα πανεπιστήμια.

author: Daron Letts
title: Iqaluit deputy mayor calls on police foot patrols to resume
content:
Iqaluit’s deputy mayor is calling for “very successful” joint patrols between Iqaluit bylaw and RCMP to be reinstated, after the project was halted in the spring due to a lack of available police officers.




“I would like to call on the RCMP to get their staffing numbers to where we can work together again,” said Kim Smith during Tuesday’s governance and priorities meeting. 

“It was very successful and we definitely saw a difference in the city.”




The pilot project ran from January through March. It ended due to a lack of available police officers, said Iqaluit’s chief municipal enforcement officer Steven Allen Tuesday during a presentation to the committee.




“While the project was in motion, it was a success, but the RCMP was unable to sustain providing a member for this project due to staffing levels,” Allen said.




Both agencies provided one officer each to patrol together daily in the afternoons. They focused on traffic-related offences and public intoxication, he said.




During an RCMP update to council in June, Iqaluit detachment commander Staff Sgt. Vlatko Nikolovski said he hoped to be able to “

secure resources

” to continue the project.




RCMP began conducting ATV patrols in June as well to compensate after the project ended, he added.
















Justice Department policy director Stephen Shaddock wrote in an email to Nunatsiaq News in June that the Iqaluit detachment is currently “fully staffed and is expected to maintain regular rotations throughout the year.”




The detachment is staffed by 26 constables, four corporals and one sergeant, 

 Nikolovski told council in June.




Councillors have long called on the RCMP to

 

step up

 enforcement of public drinking, with some 

suggesting

 that closing Iqaluit’s beer and wine store might be the solution.




RCMP previously

 

teamed

 with Qikiqtani Inuit Association to increase foot patrols of the community.




Bylaw has its own staff vacancies, including a sergeant position and two officer positions that the city is currently seeking to fill, Allen said.

author: S. Baum
title: New Ad Calls Out GOP for “Creepy Fetish of Monitoring Children’s Bathrooms”
content:
The Progress Action Fund, a left-wing PAC, is running ads to “disrupt the right-wing media bubble.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A little girl walks into a bathroom and screams. Sitting there, scowling inside the stall, is the man who might be your next representative. “I’m your Republican congressman,” the man says. “Now that we’re in charge, I’m checking to make sure there’s no trans people in the wrong bathroom.” She protests; he insists. “I won the last election, and this is my priority. Now, let’s make sure you’re really a girl.”

This is the premise of the latest ad by the Progress Action Fund (PAF), a left-wing PAC running ads to “disrupt the right-wing media bubble,” as its website says.

The ad is incisive, unsettling, and to the point. It’s exactly the kind of thing this PAC is known for.

Joe Jacobson, PAF’s executive director, wants to see the left wage a meaningful counter-narrative to Republicans’ anti-trans hate. “There was no counter in 2024, and that was devastating for Democrats,” he told Erin In The Morning. “Rather than just sidestepping the issue, we need to have a counter, and the testing shows our counter is effective.”

According to independent randomized controlled testing, the “Republicans In Your Bathroom” ad can move swing voters 8 points toward Democrats, as per a press release from PAF. The group is also the creative force behind viral, in-your-face attack ads against Republicans, like “Republicans In Your Bedroom” and “Republicans Blowing Your Taxes.”

“Republicans In Your Bathroom” will primarily run in Texas and Ohio, two key battleground states in this midterm election. The ads are expected to reach 50 million Americans.

It’s a welcome antidote to the GOP’s fearmongering about trans people. This includes an Ohio ad by the Senate Leadership Fund, which featured a Texas woman who falsely claimed she underwent gender-affirming surgery as a minor, without parental consent. There was also an attack ad against James Talarico that emphasized he’s “too weak” for Texas as a trans flag waved in the background. And Iowa’s Sarah Trone Garriott was the target of an ad campaign that lambasted her for supposedly supporting trans-inclusive sports teams.

It’s no surprise, then, that Elon Musk’s PAC spent over $100 million on ads this cycle, with a heavy focus on trans issues. Nor is it a shock to learn that in 2024, Republicans spent almost $215 million on network TV ads attacking the transgender community.

Unfortunately, some Democrats in high-profile races appear to cede ground to this hateful rhetoric. Trone Garriott, for example, released an ad in response to allegations that she supported the trans community by declaring that she opposes “men in women’s locker rooms,” which is a pejorative often used to describe transgender women and girls. But Jacobson’s response? “Republicans are creepy as hell,” he said in a statement. “Democrats need to grow a spine and call Republicans out for their creepy fetish of monitoring children’s bathrooms.”

This piece was republished with permission from Erin In The Morning.

author: Chris Walker
title: Poll: 7 in 10 Americans Doubt Trump Will Accept Midterm Results
content:
The president has said that he will only accept the results of the midterms if he deems them to be “honest.”

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A new poll demonstrates that voters are deeply skeptical over whether President Donald Trump will accept the outcome of the 2026 midterm elections, which Democrats are currently favored to win.

The Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll, published earlier this week, asked respondents how confident they were regarding how Trump will react to the midterms. Only 28 percent said they were “very confident” or “somewhat confident” that he would accept the results. Meanwhile, 70 percent of Americans are “not too confident” or “not at all confident” that he will back the outcome.

The poll comes as Trump himself has repeatedly indicated that he won’t accept the results if Democrats win over Republican Party candidates.

Trump has spent much of the 2026 midterm campaign season sowing unfounded doubts about the legitimacy of American elections. His administration has acted in kind, publishing dubious reports that baselessly suggest that tens of thousands of people ineligible to vote took part in the 2020 presidential race that Trump lost. The president has also pushed states to remove residents that he claims are illegal voters from their voting rolls, and has called for “nationalizing” the elections, despite the U.S. Constitution placing management of elections in the hands of states, not the federal government.

In June, Trump reacted furiously when “Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker pressed him for evidence of his claims of voter fraud, storming out of the interview.

And in February, Trump said in an interview that he would only accept the midterm results if he deemed the elections to be “honest.” If not, “something else has to happen,” he said.

Analysts have expressed concerns about Trump’s comments regarding the midterms, with some theorizing that he is potentially setting the stage for an event similar to what happened at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021, when a mob of his loyalists stormed the building in an attempt to overturn his loss in the 2020 presidential election.

One theory contends that Speaker of the House Mike Johnson, himself a staunch loyalist to the president, could replace the House Clerk with someone equally dedicated to helping Trump, if Democrats do indeed win the midterms. That individual could then refuse to seat the newly elected lawmakers, keeping the older, unelected ones in place, using the same baseless claims of election fraud in order to justify doing so.

Trump could also encourage his supporters to be at the Capitol on January 3, the day new lawmakers are supposed to be sworn in, to incite action from Johnson and Republicans — much like he did in 2021, when he said a “wild” event would take place at the Capitol.

Election law scholars doubt the legality of such a move, but it could still be attempted, delaying the swearing-in ceremonies or even resulting in violence, if Trump refuses to accept the results.

Notably, Johnson has behaved this way before. Earlier this year, after then-Rep.-elect Adelita Grijalva (D-Arizona) won a special election in her district, Johnson refused to seat her for several weeks, claiming he couldn’t do so because the House was out of session (despite having sworn in Republican lawmakers while the House was out of session). At the time, Grijalva was seen as being the last vote needed to pass a bill to release the Epstein files, which Johnson opposed.

Polling data indicates that Democrats are expected to win control of the House in this November’s elections, and have a strong chance of winning the Senate, too. According to polling site FiftyPlusOne, as of Wednesday morning, Democrats have a 99 percent chance of winning the House, and a 74 percent chance of taking over the Senate.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Rogue AI Must Threaten 50 Lives Before Being Shut Down, Anthropic Suggests
content:
Anthropic is pushing legislation that would only allow the US government to shut down a rogue AI model when at least 50 people are at risk of imminent serious harm or death.







The AI firm has been quietly lobbying congress to adopt its draft bill, a copy of which was obtained by 

Politico

.




Under the bill

, a state-led “blocking order” can also be triggered if there is a risk of an AI model causing at least $1bn (£750m) in damage to property. 




The rules laid out in the draft would prevent US states from enforcing tougher safety laws and make it harder for courts to put the brakes on dangerous AI systems.




They set a high threshold for federal intervention in the case of potential “catastrophic harm”. 




Federal officials, for example, would have to ascertain that any threat posed by AI was “imminent” and that no alternative could prevent catastrophe before intervening.




In a 

Substack post

, Zvi Mowshowitz, a writer who focuses on AI, described this as an “absurdly high bar”.




The draft bill reads: “The term ‘catastrophic risk’ means a foreseeable and material risk that a frontier developer’s development, storage, use or deployment of a frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people, or to more than $1bn in damage to… property arising from a single incident”.




AI safety experts, including 

Nathan Calvin

, 

Nat Purser

 and 

Nate Soares

 have warned such a bill would weaken existing safeguards while limiting federal oversight.




Mowshowitz said the bill would make people less safe than if legislators did “nothing”. He argued that Anthropic appeared more concerned about the government enforcing safety rules than ensuring it had the power to hold the wider AI industry to account.




Anthony Cimino, head of federal affairs at Anthropic, 

said on X

 that the language around risk thresholds in the draft was “pulled directly from existing standards in California law” and would not absolve companies of liability nor prevent the government from using other tools at its disposal to protect the public.




But he acknowledged that it may be “time to re-evaluate thresholds to make sure the national standard is as strong as it can be.”




Last month, former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon

 warned that AI could wipe out humanity within a decade

. 




The researcher’s comments triggered a series of similar warnings from other AI colleagues. But observers have cast doubt on the claims, as Fortune AI’s editor, Jeremy Kahn, noted, with some viewing them as a “

cynical ploy… intended to distract regulators and the public from the real and concrete risks that already exist

”.

author: Chabeli Carrazana
title: Nurses Just Helped Win US’s First Countywide 12-Week Paid Parental Leave Policy
content:
Advocates hope the Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, victory will open the door for other localities to follow suit.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

As a nurse in the neonatal intensive care unit, Jean Stone knows what it really means to live in a country with no paid parental leave.

She’s watched this scene play out so many times it’s almost the norm: Once their babies stabilize in the NICU, parents often return to work to preserve whatever parental leave they have left for when their babies come home. Stone calls the parents in the middle of the day to update them — starting each call with, “Everything is OK” — and watch them come in at the end of their workday, their faces reflecting the relief of reunion.

“They carry that weight of not being there,” Stone, who works at UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital in Pittsburgh, told The 19th.

Five months ago, she and the other nurses at Magee, who are in the middle of negotiating a union contract, decided to do something about it. They came together with a coalition of working parents, advocates and some elected leaders to draft a proposal for a paid leave program in Allegheny County. They launched their campaign on Mother’s Day, May 10.

The Allegheny County Council voted 11 to 4 to pass 12 weeks of paid parental leave — the first county-level paid leave policy in the nation.

Under the policy, both birthing and non-birthing parents would receive three months of paid parental leave within the first year of childbirth, adoption, foster placement or a stillbirth. Parents would have their jobs and health benefits protected while on leave, but to qualify they need to be full-time employees for at least six months or part-time workers with a minimum of 625 logged work hours. All businesses with 15 or more employees would be required to offer the benefit.

The chamber Tuesday night was packed by supporters of the proposal. They spent hours testifying about their personal experiences giving birth without the aid of paid leave, including one mother who had a stillbirth at 41 weeks gestation and said her husband took three weeks off to care for her but had no paternity leave. “You just don’t know how you’re going to survive another second, let alone trying to work,” she said.

Council Vice President John Palmiere said he had had his doubts about where he landed on the issue, but the stories shared moved him. He was a “yes.” When the final vote was tallied, the crowd broke into an applause punctuated by shouts of “thank you!”

The passage was a decisive step forward for a movement that has won every victory inch by inch. The United States is the only industrialized nation without a federal paid leave policy. Workers here have access to unpaid leave only through the Family and Medical Leave Act. In lieu of a federal policy, 14 states and Washington, D.C., have passed their own state-level paid leave programs over the past 20 years. Pennsylvania isn’t one of them.

The county’s policy differs from other state-level programs, and it opens the door for other counties to do the same. Usually, paid leave policies are administered by state governments through money from a social insurance fund that employers and employees typically pay into. Allegheny’s policy would put the onus on most employers to fund the benefit, which was the piece of the proposal that received the most pushback. The original proposal was scaled back from 18 weeks to 12, with an exception for employers with fewer than 15 employees.

It was an outpouring of community support that ultimately propelled the policy forward. A year ago, when the nurses, nurse practitioners and lactation consultants at Magee got together to form a union, they put out a public survey asking the community to weigh in on what would make patient care and maternal health better. More than a thousand responses came in, and though the survey didn’t ask about it directly, “people wrote in in astonishing numbers that, ‘what we need is real paid parental leave across the board,’” Stone said.

Already, the nurses were hoping to include a paid parental leave request in their contract negotiations — at the time, they only got two weeks of paid leave — but it was “kind of beautiful that it came back as a priority for the community, too,” Stone said.

The nurses leading the push say this is also about improving maternal health outcomes for mothers in a county where severe maternal morbidity — unexpected outcomes following labor and delivery, such as hemorrhage or sepsis — rose 55 percent from 2016 to 2022. Black women, in particular, face even worse maternal health outcomes.

“I care for mothers who develop postpartum preeclampsia, who are recovering from complicated C-sections, infections, mastitis, endometritis and other serious complications,” said Marchel Robinson, a registered nurse at Magee during a Labor Day parade in Pittsburgh. “My patients don’t choose these complications. They don’t choose when their bodies need time to heal. They don’t choose when they need another doctor’s appointment, another week at home or even another month to recover. And they shouldn’t have to choose between healing, caring for their newborn and keeping a paycheck.”

For Stone, paid leave is also a retention policy. Nurses, a workforce that is nearly 90 percent women, are leaving the healthcare field in droves.

“We see our coworkers come back way too early into a job that is so physically demanding and emotionally demanding to then be essentially away from your baby for 13 hours,” Stone said, forcing many to step into less demanding roles or leave the workforce altogether.

Stone said she is hopeful the passage in Allegheny County could lend some momentum to a statewide policy, which already has some bipartisan support and passed the state House before stalling in the Senate this past legislative session.

Nationwide, the issue is immensely popular. An AP-NORC poll conducted last summer found that two-thirds of Americans support requiring employers to provide paid leave for parents, including a majority of Republicans, independents and Democrats.

Dawn Huckelbridge, the founding director of Paid Leave for All, a national advocacy organization pushing for federal paid family and medical leave, said the passage in Pennsylvania shows there is “so much demand” for such policies. But, she cautioned, “we can’t keep doing this piecemeal, because you can’t have someone with rights in one zip code and not have them in another.”

Stone said this moment could be an inflection point.

“I hope it’s one of the things that will maybe someday be recognized as an early example of when things started to change,” she said.

author: Dylan Baddour
title: Texas Continued Permitting Data Centers After Greg Abbott Ordered a Pause
content:
A new report identified 35 permitting actions taken by regulators in Texas in the weeks after the governor’s moratorium.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Regulators in Texas did not stop processing permits for data center projects when Gov. Greg Abbott ordered a pause last month, according to an analysis of public records released Monday by the oil and gas watchdog group FracTracker.

Amid an upswell of public opposition to the booming buildout of digital infrastructure in Texas, Abbott directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality in a Sept. 21 letter “to halt all permits sought by data centers.”

But FracTracker, in collaboration with Public Citizen, identified 35 permitting actions taken by the TCEQ for data center projects in subsequent weeks.

“TCEQ has continued reviewing applications and issuing approvals that allow data center development to proceed,” the groups said in a press release Monday. “These actions do not signal an agency trying to pause.”

In response, Abbott Press Secretary Andrew Mahaleris indicated that the pause applied to approval, not processing, of permits.

“No permits have been approved,” Mahaleris said in a statement. “In line with the Governor’s directive, TCEQ has not taken and will not take any proactive actions related to the approval of data center permits.”

Abbott has described his moratorium as an opportunity for state agencies to evaluate the facilities’ impact on water resources and grid stability.

“No other state agency shall move forward with regulatory approvals related to data centers until this information is acquired,” Abbott wrote in his Sept. 21 letter to TCEQ executive director Kelly Keel.

TCEQ responded to Abbott in an Oct. 19 letter, which was provided to Inside Climate News by Ryan Vise, TCEQ’s director of external relations.

In the letter, Steven Schar, TCEQ’s interim executive director, wrote: “TCEQ staff are screening pending permit applications to determine if they are subject to the directive. If a permit application is subject to the directive, TCEQ has paused that permit application.”

Since the Sept. 21 directive, the TCEQ has fast-tracked or assigned engineers to 14 permits, approved stormwater coverage for 11, certified emissions estimates for seven and issued public notice for three, according to permitting documents collected by FracTracker and Public Citizen.

The permits regard construction of gas power generation facilities for energy-hungry facilities. All of the largest gas power projects currently proposed in Texas are specifically intended to serve data centers, which are primarily planned to run artificial intelligence.

The projects would release tens of thousands of tons of regulated pollutants, according to permitting documents, as well as more than 100 million tons per year of greenhouse gases — an enormous amount roughly equal to the annual emissions of a mid-sized industrialized country.

The day after Abbott’s pause on data center permits, on Sept. 22, FracTracker and Public Citizen found that TCEQ mailed notices of preliminary approval to three major projects: NRG Prairie Energy Center, VoltaGrid’s ABI-1 power plant and Nexus’s self-powered data center in Hubbard.

The agency opened public comment periods on two of those projects in following days.

FracTracker and Public Citizen found approvals of stormwater management permits for data center construction issued after Sept. 21, including for Caldwell Valley Technology Park in Caldwell County, Crusoe’s Abilene campus and EdgeConneX’s Cedar Creek campus. The report identified numerous other projects that continue to advance through permitting. For example, records show the TCEQ received a permit application for generators at Edged Energy in Dallas on Oct. 6, and an engineer completed an initial review on Oct. 9.

“Our research uncovered glaring inconsistencies between regulatory actions and Governor Abbott’s directives,” said Sam Law, manager of communications at FracTracker Alliance and author of the report. “We need an actual pause to study the threats posed to the land, water and livelihoods of Texans.”

title: Philosopher Spivak writes to Öcalan: ‘You have proposed a path to democratic existence’
content:
Indian literary theorist and philosopher Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak has written a letter addressed to Abdullah Öcalan, expressing her support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Spivak’s letter was delivered to the İmralı Delegation of the DEM Party.




Gayatri Spivak stated that she was impressed by Öcalan’s resilience despite the conditions of his decades-long imprisonment and emphasized the importance of his call for gender equality. Noting that the Framework Law strengthens the prospect of Öcalan securing his freedom, Spivak stressed that the fundamental question is how to build a democratic society.




The letter reads as follows:




“Dear Brother Abdullah Öcalan,




I have long been impressed by the resilience you have shown throughout your prolonged imprisonment, much of it spent in isolation. I have also been particularly moved by your call for gender equality. Now there is the Framework Law, which further strengthens the possibility of your release.




Your real challenges, however, are only now beginning. Because you have proposed the more complex and more productive path of democratic existence rather than a form of proto-nationalist self-preservation. This requires an education system aimed at developing a sustained epistemological approach that will enable children, when they eventually become voters, to grasp the paradox of democracy: freedom for ourselves, and a powerful desire for equality for those who are different from us, as well as for a just world.




For nearly 60 years, I have been trying to do precisely this: working with the elite by teaching European literature at Columbia University, while also working with the most marginalized sections of society by running primary schools for the children of landless, illiterate, and so-called ‘untouchable’ and Indigenous communities. Others teach how to produce knowledge, but some of us must also teach how to learn.




It is particularly important today that children learn to desire a just society, as the world is undergoing a profound transformation due to climate change and artificial intelligence.




I wish you all the best, my brother.




Respectfully.”




Who is Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak?




Born on February 24, 1942, Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak is an Indian philosopher and thinker known for her contributions to literary theory, postcolonial theory, and subaltern studies. Best known for her influential essay “Can the Subaltern Speak?”, Spivak critically examines the relationships between colonialism, power, representation, and the production of knowledge. Her academic work focuses on feminism, decolonial thought, and social inequality.

title: Oil exploration expands across Kurdish regions
content:
Oil drilling continues uninterrupted across Kurdish regions. Intensive drilling operations in Gabar, Cudî, Kato and Besta continue to displace local communities, devastate natural habitats, and deplete and pollute water resources. A similar situation is emerging in Batman (Êlih) and Diyarbakır (Amed), where shale oil drilling is expected to begin within the next one or two months. The Ecology Commission of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) Headquarters and the ÖHD Şırnak (Şirnex) Branch conducted a field investigation into the ongoing ecological destruction on Mount Gabar. The delegation announced that its findings would be compiled into a report and shared with the public. According to a report published by Mezopotamya Agency (MA), the ÖHD delegation examined tree felling and activities carried out under the pretext of oil exploration, drawing attention to pollution and environmental destruction.




The Tigris River is being poisoned




Hülya Yıldırım, a member of the ÖHD Headquarters Ecology Commission, spoke to 

Yeni Yaşam

 about the investigation, stressing that the ecological destruction in Gabar could not be considered separately from the wider devastation of nature across the region. Yıldırım said, “In Gabar, Besta, Cudî and many other places, we are witnessing tree felling, forest fires, mining activities and toxic thermal power plants, all of which are used as both instruments and consequences of war. Today, there is an oil well on every corner of Gabar and an oil production facility at every turn. As a result, Gabar has been blasted apart with dynamite. The Tigris River is being polluted by oil leaks and petroleum waste.”




Life is treated as a resource




Hülya Yıldırım said that oil operations threatened workers' health, environmental and public health, as well as agriculture and livestock farming. She noted that residents were still waiting to return to their villages, which had been burned and evacuated in the 1990s, but that these operations were creating further obstacles to their return. Yıldırım stressed that activities causing ecological destruction were not being carried out in accordance with legal requirements. Yıldırım said, “These areas, these mountains, this land and this river are all seen merely as resources. We will continue to oppose this mentality and the permit procedures being carried out without even complying with the existing legal framework. We will intensify our struggle and continue to share our findings with the public.”




24 shale oil wells planned




Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar described the shale oil exploration launched in Diyarbakır as a game-changing development for Turkey. His announcement that the project would also extend to Batman raises concerns about the future of the region. Bayraktar said that new discoveries had been made in Adıyaman, where oil production had fallen below 10,000 barrels per day. He stated that steps had been taken to increase existing production by approximately 50 percent, bringing it to around 15,000 barrels per day. He added that daily production in Adıyaman was expected to reach between 14,000 and 15,000 barrels by the end of this year. Bayraktar announced that shale gas and shale oil exploration had begun in Batman and Diyarbakır using unconventional extraction methods, including hydraulic fracturing, commonly known as fracking. He said that the project, which involves horizontal drilling, was expected to begin producing results towards the end of the year. The minister added that horizontal drilling operations were scheduled to be completed in 2027, while a programme involving 24 wells would continue until 2028.




Shale oil exploration spreads across the region




Agricultural land, pastures and water resources across Şırnak, Batman and Diyarbakır are increasingly being sacrificed to oil and shale oil extraction. It had previously been announced that a shale oil well had been drilled in Bismil. The US-based company TransAtlantic Petroleum and another US company, Continental Resources, which operates alongside it in the project, reportedly injected thousands of tonnes of water mixed with chemicals underground, leading to the first oil discovery. The drilling operations cover an area of 7 million 650 thousand decares of natural habitats, pastures and agricultural land, including Bismil and Silvan (Farqîn). The first oil was reportedly reached through horizontal drilling at a depth of four kilometres. Plans are underway to drill another 24 wells in the region, while the number is reportedly expected to increase tenfold to twelvefold from 2017 onwards.




New drilling sites in Gabar




Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar announced during Russian Energy Week in Moscow that Turkey was continuing its oil and natural gas exploration activities and could soon announce new discoveries at the Gabar oil production field. Bayraktar said, “Oil and natural gas exploration activities are continuing both offshore and on land. Oil production in Gabar is also an important part of these efforts.” Although Bayraktar enthusiastically presented these developments as good news, his announcements primarily serve the interests of business and capital. The prospect of new oil discoveries in Gabar signals that the ongoing environmental destruction in the region could intensify further.




Gabar is their ideal!




Minister Bayraktar previously stated that Turkey had developed its natural gas and oil exploration strategy through the National Energy and Mining Policy introduced in 2016. He said, “We are entering a period in which Diyarbakır will virtually become an oil city.” In another statement, Bayraktar declared, “Şırnak will become Turkey's number one oil city.” His successive statements about the region have drawn attention to the scale of the planned operations. They also suggest that oil drilling and production, which have already caused extensive destruction, will not remain limited to these two cities. Bayraktar's declaration that “Gabar is the most concrete example of our vision” raises further concerns that ecological life in the region could be brought to an end.




‘We will raise our voices against the destruction’




Ayşe Şehriban Demirel, a member of the Ecology Commission of the ÖHD Headquarters who participated in the field investigation, said that the delegation had examined oil exploration activities in Gabar and the damage inflicted on nature. Demirel said, “What is happening here is a policy of special warfare. This destruction breaks our hearts. We are working to put an end to this plunder and ensure that those responsible are held accountable. We will share the ecological destruction in Gabar with the public and raise our voices against this plunder and environmental devastation, particularly in Cudî and Besta.”

title: YRK: Our forces responded to attacks by Iranian Revolutionary Guards
content:
The Command of the East Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) issued a written statement regarding the continued attacks carried out by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).




The YRK statement on Wednesday said:




“As our people and the public are aware, the Revolutionary Guards of the Iranian regime launched military operations against our forces in Shaho and Marivan over the past few days and carried out bombardments in the region. We had previously issued the necessary warnings, making it clear that if the attacks continued, we would exercise our right to legitimate self-defense and respond accordingly. Despite all our warnings, the enemy continued its attacks.




On October 20, the enemy launched a mortar attack on the area surrounding the village of Degaga in the Kosalan region. The attack was carried out from military bases and outposts in the vicinity of Degaga, which had also served as the launch sites for previous attacks in the region. Our forces immediately responded to the attacks within the framework of legitimate self-defense. Our forces suffered no casualties or damage as a result of the attacks.”

author: Unknown
title: Mechthild Exo: Jineolojî must become a lived foundation
content:
Twelve years after the first Jineolojî conference in Europe, Kurdish women’s science has established itself in numerous countries. However, its integration into society continues to face significant challenges. Peace and conflict researcher Dr. Mechthild Exo highlighted these issues on the sidelines of the latest Jineolojî conference. In an interview with ANF, she traces the development of academic and feminist work since 2014 and explains why research, political organizing, and social practice must become more closely interconnected in the future.




When the first European Jineolojî conference took place in Cologne in 2014, those involved were still at the very beginning of their work, Exo noted. There were no established structures, extensive educational programs, or sufficient translations of foundational literature. Jineolojî, which defines itself as the science of women and life and emerged from the Kurdish women’s freedom movement, first had to be introduced, explained, and made accessible, Exo stated.




“We didn’t really know what Jineolojî was. We only knew that a new science was being developed,” Exo said. "The first conference was largely characterized by a collective search for understanding. Many of the approaches presented at the time later evolved or were not pursued in the form originally envisioned. In the following years, educational programs, camps, and research networks emerged in various European countries. Different areas of focus developed, often shaped by the experiences and social conditions of those involved."










https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261018190542_2026-10-18-haelen-mechthild-exo-akademisyen-1.mp4













From the critique of science to exploring their own history




Initially, the groups focused primarily on questions concerning the philosophy and theory of science. Their discussions centered on critiques of existing conceptions of science and the question of which epistemological foundations could support an alternative approach to research.




Over time, the focus shifted increasingly toward historical and social investigations. The emergence of patriarchy, women’s history, matrilineal forms of society, and the loss of communal ways of life came to the forefront.




At the same time, examining their own history became an important part of the work. How have patriarchal structures shaped women’s living conditions, social relationships, and ways of thinking? What forms of communal life have been lost? And why is autonomous organizing necessary? These questions became increasingly intertwined with current political developments. The rise of fascist movements, patriarchal violence, and femicides were among the issues addressed, alongside the possibilities for feminist organizing and social transformation.




Strengthening Jineolojî’s roots in the Kurdish diaspora




According to Exo, the latest conference marks another step forward in the development of Jineolojî: "Unlike previous gatherings, this time numerous women involved in the social structures of the Kurdish diaspora participated. Alongside activists from various European countries, women from different parts of Kurdistan also attended. This broad participation highlighted a weakness that had persisted until now: although Jineolojî had established its own research and educational structures in Europe over the years, cooperation with Kurdish women’s councils and other social organizations had not been sufficiently developed."




“Some of us had always maintained these connections, but they were simply not enough,” Exo noted. She argued that Jineolojî must therefore become more firmly rooted in the existing structures of the Kurdish diaspora and other migrant communities. The crucial point, she added, is that the knowledge developed should not remain confined to specialized groups, but should be shared in ways that enable people to work with it independently.




Exo described this objective as a fundamental shift in the prevailing understanding of Jineolojî: "It should not be perceived as a single organization that is consulted on specific issues. Rather, it must be understood as a collective science whose development involves different sectors of society."




Research must not take place in isolation




Cooperation between academic institutions, academy projects, and social initiatives plays an important role in this process, Exo said. She herself is involved in the Academy of Social Sciences, whose members are spread across different countries and continents, with some conducting research at universities. According to her, this geographical and institutional separation makes it difficult to develop shared experiences and establish a continuous practice of collective research. Exo believes that academia could learn from forms of social organizing in which collective working methods are already more firmly established.




Conversely, she said, academic institutions could contribute their research findings, theoretical foundations, and practical experience, particularly in publishing and educational work. “How can this exchange be organized?” Exo asked, identifying one of the central questions raised at the conference.




She emphasized that a collective effort is needed from everyone involved to ensure that Jineolojî is not merely recognized as a theoretical foundation but becomes an integral part of shared practice. The Academy of Social Sciences has therefore committed to working regularly with Jineolojî structures in the future and to strengthening coordination between research projects and their findings.




New research projects on peace and democratic society




Exo pointed to several research initiatives currently being established. One research commune is examining the history of democratic civilization, while another group is being formed to investigate concepts of peace. There is also an applied research project focusing on the democratic production and distribution of food. Exo sees numerous areas of common interest between these initiatives and Jineolojî, particularly in historical studies and peace research. She emphasized the need to build on these connections to prevent different groups from working independently on the same research questions.




Exo believes that joint publications could also help strengthen this cooperation. As an example, she refers to the journal 

Democratic Modernity,

 whose first issue already featured an article on the significance of Jineolojî for the Academy. However, she stressed that the objective goes beyond publishing academic findings. These principles must also be reflected in educational work and in the everyday interactions among those involved.




From the conference to social practice




Exo pointed out that the international composition of the conference demonstrated the opportunities for such exchanges. Women from numerous European countries, including Ireland, Scotland, Italy, and Catalonia, as well as participants from Palestine and different parts of Kurdistan, brought together diverse experiences and social perspectives. The working groups addressed a wide range of practical issues, including ecological initiatives, the development of democratic family and partnership relationships, cultural activities, and ways to encourage children to participate more actively in independent research and education.




According to Exo, the real challenge now lies in developing these approaches beyond the conference. The numerous initiatives must be taken up within their respective social structures and transformed into sustained processes of collective work.




At the same time, she offered a deliberately measured assessment of the conference’s outcomes. Despite the many encounters and new perspectives, she does not feel entirely euphoric. She beliebes that putting the shared plans into practice will require considerable effort.




“I’m not particularly euphoric at the end of this conference because I don’t think it will be easy,” Exo said. Nevertheless, the foundations are there," she added.
