Our comrade Barry Pateman was at the heart of the Kate Sharpley Library for thirty-five years. My earliest memory of Barry is of him on the KSL stall at the anarchist bookfair in London. He was in his element. I clearly remember Barry telling me the pamphlet I’d just bought was ‘as rare as rocking horse shit’. I hope this brief account throws a little more light on his life and his ideas.

Barry was born and raised in a mining community near Doncaster. Radical political ideas were common, but so was non-school learning and a love of books. ‘When I was growing up I met many self-educated working class men and women. They were everywhere in the community I lived in. […] They always recognized the “literary canon” and had, sometimes, a rather exaggerated respect for it. That said they brought their own frame of reference to the classics. I can remember sitting in a pub listening to two old miners tell me that Sir Walter Scott’s “Ivanhoe” was a radical novel because they read it as an exercise in solidarity and anti-racism.’[1] There wasn’t an awful lot of anarchist literature about though. I remember seeing the large format newsprint ‘Freedom Anarchist Pamphlets’ series at the KSL and Barry telling me that they were some of the few things available when he was finding his way to the anarchist movement.[2]

In London in the early 1970s, Barry worked with Albert Meltzer, Stuart Christie and Miguel Garcia in the Anarchist Black Cross. He was modest in hindsight about his anonymous writings and other contributions: ‘I’d never seen myself particularly important (I’d always put the stamps on the envelopes and book the meeting rooms etc)’.[3] He also took part in the bitter internal disputes of the early 1970s: was anarchism about class and revolution or were such ideas outdated? ‘I had been around the edges (and probably too involved) of some rather intense disagreements about anarchism and anarchist practice.’[4] There were other differences: London anarchist Martin said ‘I recall Barry Pateman telling me he wasn’t sure he was an anarchist when he first got involved, as he liked ska and all the anarchists he met thought jazz was the only music anarchists should listen to.’[5]

As a miner’s son, and member of the anarcho-syndicalist Direct Action Movement, Barry was heavily involved in anarchist solidarity during the miners’ strike of 1984-85. He lived through a time of ‘Mutual aid, not in a fucking book, but in everyday existence’; and of not only defeat but the pain of finding that the anarchist movement couldn’t make room for radical apprentices who weren’t yet ‘full anarchists’.[6]

His experiences as an activist and those disputes about what the anarchist movement should do or could be led him to research British anarchist history. He earned a PhD studying the Spanish anarchist exiles who came to Britain in 1939. He also researched the bigger picture of British anarchism from the 1880s to the 1940s. That laid the groundwork for his involvement in the Kate Sharpley Library. When Albert persuaded Barry to house the KSL, it shifted from a collection of books on all topics of interest to anarchists to a more focussed one. Barry said ‘there was so much material by and about anarchists that I felt KSL should concentrate on that.’ [7]

We should recognise that Barry’s first partner, Jennie Sidney, was important in making the Kate Sharpley Library a welcoming place – even if initially she was not too happy when Barry ‘arrived with a minibus full of boxes (twice!!)’.[8] With Albert working on the publications and Barry unpacking, organising and expanding the collection the KSL grew in size and influence. Barry was also an enthusiastic stallholder at anarchist bookfairs, as much for the chance to share materials as for the essential money they brought in. Matt Hart recalled how Barry helped his research into the Anarchist Black Cross: ‘When I used to go to the Anarchist Bookfair up in San Francisco, Barry Pateman, every single time he saw me, he would all of a sudden bring up a large stack of old Black Flags that he had collected and literally put aside for me.’[9]

Barry was guided by the example of Paul Avrich, the great American historian of anarchism. When Avrich died, Barry paid tribute to his ‘consistent and rigorous insistence on accuracy’, suggesting that we ‘learn from Avrich’s refusal to condescend to the people that made up his histories. He did not have a clever theory and try to prove it, a methodology that treats its subjects like chess pieces rather than people.’[10]

Albert Meltzer died in 1996, leaving Barry and the rest of the Kate Sharpley Library collective to carry on. A much greater shock came when Jennie Sidney died in 1998. Both Barry and Jennie had been teachers in East London and later in Peterborough. The next year Barry moved with their son, Paul, to a new life in California. Barry worked at the Emma Goldman Papers Project bringing his knowledge but also a curiosity about the people (anarchist or not) that Goldman worked with: ‘We are rescuing men and women from, as E.P. Thompson writes, “the enormous condescension of posterity.” On our desk, ill-lit by lamp-light, they come alive again.’[11] Sometimes people look for the Emma Goldman that they want to see, but Barry brought a vital focus on recording facts: ‘Rule 1 of researching: never trust anyone until you’ve read the original yourself’.[12]

Barry’s life improved further when he met his new partner, Jessica Moran, at the Emma Goldman Papers. Jessica also joined the Kate Sharpley Library collective. The holdings of the KSL grew once Barry started buying rare anarchist materials from American booksellers. Sometimes in part exchange, sometimes with donations from friends of the library but more often out of his own pocket. I especially remember visits to Bibliomania and Bolerium (both in the Bay Area), though Barry would never knowingly pass by any second-hand bookshop.

Barry encouraged people to think about anarchy, anarchism and history. Barry was a generous student of anarchism, who would take time to support other people’s research, whether by reading their manuscripts, pointing them to sources or simply talking enthusiastically about anarchist history. He shared a lot of information but also represented a personal connection to the history of the movement (in the same way as Albert Meltzer had for him). Barry was one of the moving spirits of San Francisco’s Alexander Berkman Social Club (formed in 2008). He was willing to be a speaker at meetings and conferences even if he self-deprecatingly claimed ‘in retrospect I had fuck all worth saying’.[13] Barry wrote many encouraging introductions and book reviews, and followed the example of Paul Avrich, ‘preferring to remain silent than chastise.’[14]

Barry worked closely with AK Press, who have co-published several works of anarchist history with KSL. He also read manuscripts for them, and shared others that came to the KSL from Cienfuegos Press via Albert Meltzer. One project with AK Press that took Barry and Jessica years was the annotated edition of Alexander Berkman’s Prison Memoirs of an Anarchist. As well as providing context on people and events for the modern reader, it transcribed the diary Berkman kept while writing Prison Memoirs.

It was fascinating to work with Barry in the KSL as he was so interested in what the material there could tell us. Picking up a history of freethought, previously owned and annotated by Mat Kavanagh led Barry to ruminate on what it meant to see Kavanagh ‘working out what knowledge he can take from this book that will be useful in his discussion on anarchism and anarchy with his work mates.’[15] Many of my conversations with Barry have stayed with me. I remember filing copies of Red Action (Marxist but not Leninist) in the library and Barry saying he would write something about them one day. Since Barry, as a DAM member, worked with them in Anti-Fascist Action, it might have expanded on his later remark about their anti-fascist work being ‘the best thing they ever did.’ We talked a lot about his research into exactly what happened to split the Anarchist Federation in 1945. That was the long-delayed harvest of his early researches into British anarchism.[16]

For Barry anarchism was all about getting to anarchy, and anarchy was all about everybody being able to realise their full potential. He warned about what we lose if ‘we raid the anarchist past to justify the anarchist present’.[17] It’s been fascinating to re-read his introductions, re-watch interviews and see Barry worrying away at questions of anarchist history. In his foreword to Jared Davidson’s biography of Philip Josephs, an immigrant worker in New Zealand (and importer of anarchist literature) Barry asked: ‘What tactics should we use, and how malleable and flexible can they be, yet still remain anarchist? […] Above all, what is it that makes people anarchists and not syndicalists, or libertarian communists, or individualists, or whatever? Make no mistake – they saw a difference and the very least we can do is to explore it. […] All those pamphlets folded and put in a pocket to read at work, at home, in the pub, or on the bus. […] We need to ask how these readers processed what they had read in the light of their own experiences. They were not empty vessels waiting to be filled by the word.’[18]

Barry and Jessica moved to New Zealand in 2012. Barry continued to work on the Kate Sharpley Library right up until his death in September 2026. The library collective is poorer without him, but we aim to carry on. He has left us with a lot to think about.

[1] Barry Pateman ‘“Nameless in the crowd of nameless ones…” : Some thoughts on The Story of A Proletarian Life, by Bartolomeo Vanzetti, 1923’ KSL Bulletin, no.81 (February 2015) https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/vhhp2j.

[2] There were eight, published 1970-71 See https://thesparrowsnest.org.uk/search.php?query=Freedom+Anarchist+Pamphlets&logic=and – some were reprinted by Freedom Press in their Fighting the Revolution pamphlets (two volumes, both 1971).

[3] Barry Pateman ‘Anarchist History: confessions of an awkward pupil’ KSL Bulletin, no.84 (October 2015) https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/02v7v0.

[4] Barry Pateman ‘The Kate Sharpley Library Then, Now and Next: An Interview with Barry Pateman’ KSL Bulletin no.63-64 (October 2010) https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/0vt50w.

[6] Barry Pateman ‘Tensions in Anarchism’ (a talk at the Bay Area Anarchist Bookfair in San Francisco). https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/h44m7w.

[7] ‘Then, Now and Next: An Interview’.

[8] ‘Then, Now and Next: An Interview’.

[9] ‘A History of Anarchist Prisoner Support (with Matt Hart)’ Final Straw Radio June 11, 2025 https://archive.org/details/tfsr-20250608-MattHartOnAnarchistPrisonerSupport

[10] KSL Collective ‘Paul Avrich 1931-2006: a historian who listened to anarchist voices’ KSL Bulletin, no.46-47 (July 2006) https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/2z358c.

[11] Barry Pateman ‘Barry Pateman is On The Edge’ Open Road: the newsletter of the Emma Goldman Papers (Winter 2000). https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/3r23ht.

[12] ‘Barry Pateman is On The Edge’.

[13] ‘Anarchist History: confessions of an awkward pupil’.

[15] Barry Pateman ‘Mat Kavanagh and the History of Anarchism’ KSL Bulletin, no.63-64 (October 2010) https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/vdnf0f.

[16] You can read it at http://katesharpleylibrary.pbworks.com/w/page/139511268/The%201945%20split%20in%20British%20anarchism.

[17] Barry Pateman ‘Free Commune and Billy MacQueen’ KSL Bulletin no.70-71 (July 2012). https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/ngf357.

author: anonerror
title: Fraga, capital efímera del Aragón revolucionario  El Consejo de Aragón en las Tierras Bajas del Cinca. Octubre-diciembre de 1936
content:
Fraga, capital efímera del Aragón revolucionario 




El Consejo de Aragón en las Tierras Bajas del Cinca. Octubre-diciembre de 1936




 




Juan Carlos Chiné, albañil y anarcosindicalista en el medio rural.




Centro de Estudios Libertarios José Alberola




 




 




Entre toda la obra de transformación realizada por los trabajadores, la que en Aragón marcha hacia su destino de superaciones continuas es, especialmente, señera. Es obra del pueblo aragonés representados por su Consejo. 




Alardo Prats. 1937




 




En agosto de 1936, las tres capitales de provincia de Aragón y casi la mitad de su territorio estaban en manos de los sublevados fascistas del 

18 de julio

; la otra parte había resistido el embate y parado el golpe militar. Entre los pueblos que se mantuvieron 

leales

 a la República se encontraban Fraga y los de la 

ribera

 del Cinca, en el sureste de Huesca. Conviene recordar que la mayor parte de los cargos de las 

corporaciones municipales

 habían dimitido a los pocos días de conocerse la noticia del levantamiento militar, provocando un “colapso” en la ya de por sí exigua 

administración municipal

 de la época.




Fraga será de los primeros municipios donde se crea un 

órgano revolucionario

 que se hizo cargo de la administración local; con el nombre 

Comité Popular Antifascista

. Dicho 

comité

 estuvo formado por destacadas 

personalidades

 republicanas y anarquistas. Se colectivizó la tierra y la poca industria existente: albañiles, carpinteros, herreros, modistas, sastrerías y los varios hornos de pan, etc. Se puso en funcionamiento un 

hospital de sangre

, además de una escuela y biblioteca; al poco tiempo emitió su propia moneda de curso local; en general, se dinamizó la vida social. La fuerza numérica del anarquismo organizado era incuestionable y fueron muchas las personas que, impulsadas por las circunstancias o por simpatía con las ideas libertarias, se sumaron a la 

causa revolucionaria

; entre ellas, 

cabe

 

resaltar el alcalde dimisionario Joaquín Viladrich del Frente Popular.




Los orígenes del 

Consejo Regional de Defensa de Aragón

 o 

Consejo de Aragón

 los encontramos, sobre todo, en la enorme influencia que la CNT y las ideas libertarias ejercieron desde años en buena parte de la población aragonesa, no solo en las zonas urbanas, sino también entre las que habitaban el extenso Aragón rural. Sin obviar el influjo 

regeneracionista 

de Joaquín Costa y de cierto 

republicanismo federal

.




El lV Congreso Nacional de la CNT, celebrado en Zaragoza en mayo de 1936, aprobó, entre otros acuerdos, la resolución: 

Concepto Confederal del Comunismo Libertario

 donde se desarrolla todo un “programa político” ante una hipotética revolución social venidera y, entre otras cuestiones, se determina la organización territorial de manera federal y autogestionada.




El 6 de octubre de ese mismo año, ya en plena guerra, la 

Regional de Aragón, Rioja y Navarra 

de la CNT convocó un 

Pleno Extraordinario

 en Bujaraloz -municipio 

monegrino

 donde estaba instalado el Cuartel General de la Columna Durruti-. Asistieron y participaron delegaciones de sindicatos 

cenetistas 

de casi 140 pueblos aragoneses, además de representantes de las diferentes 

columnas confederales

 asentadas en el territorio, entre ellas la 

Columna Durruti, la Columna Roja y Negra 

y

 la Columna Ascaso

. El 

Pleno

 acordó la creación del 

Consejo Regional de Defensa de Aragón

. En Alcañiz, días después, el 

Comité Regional

 decidió fijar la sede provisional del 

Consejo

 en Fraga. 




Es oportuno recordar el 

Pleno Nacional

 de la CNT celebrado en Madrid dos semanas antes, en el que se acordó la creación de C

onsejos Económicos

 y de 

Defensa

 que contribuyeran a sostener las 

conquistas revolucionarias

 desde julio de 1936. Se crearon 

Consejos

 en diferentes territorios de la España

 republicana

 donde el 

Movimiento Libertario

 y 

Revolucionario

 tenía mayor influencia, como es el caso de Asturias-León, aunque es cierto que no tuvieron la repercusión y el alcance del 

Consejo de Aragón

.




El 

Consejo

 fue un organismo basado en los principios y la experiencia anarquista, sin la coerción de leyes ni la fuerza de las armas; una estructura 

supramunicipal

 organizada de manera federal, que abarcó todo el territorio del Aragón 

republicano

. Hay que reconocer que nació de la voluntad y del libre acuerdo de los pueblos 

liberados

 y del 

movimiento colectivista

; sobre todo, de la necesidad de dotarse de medios que mantuvieran unido el territorio en lo económico y en lo social. Su objetivo principal era dar solución a los problemas provocados por el abandono secular del 

Estado

 y agravados por la guerra. 




En Fraga y los pueblos del 

Cinca

, se tardó muy poco en colectivizar la tierra y en crear 

organismos administrativos

 locales

. En agosto de 1936, en Albalate de Cinca se celebró un 

Pleno Comarcal

, con la participación de 21 pueblos, donde se acordaron cuestiones como la 

colectivización

 y la creación de 

estructuras comarcales

, con la idea final de implantar el 

Comunismo Libertario

, que no se llegó a dar en su totalidad, pero sí en 

gran

 

medida. El alcance de las más de 400 

colectividades

 repartidas por todo el territorio aragonés, con cerca de 100.000 personas adheridas, pone de relieve la magnitud del 

movimiento revolucionario

.




 




El 18 de octubre, Fraga se convirtió en la capital administrativa de Aragón,

 ese mismo día se hizo público un manifiesto del 

Consejo Regional de Defensa de Aragón

 en el que aparecían los nombres de todos los 

consejeros

. En esta ciudad se editaron los primeros números del 

Boletín del Consejo 

y se instaló la sede principal en el mismo edificio del Ayuntamiento, en el 

Palacio Montcada

. A los pocos días, algunas 

consejerías

 trasladaron sus oficinas a la finca de 

Monte Julia

, en el término municipal de Belver de Cinca. Así lo recuerda Joaquín Ascaso en sus memorias:




Celebramos nuestra primera reunión en el Municipio de Fraga, la ciudad que tanta participación ha tenido en la historia de Aragón y de España. Parecían resucitar las antiguas generaciones. Fueros de Aragón. Maza de Fraga, Libertad. Libertades. El dique de nuestra seriedad era suficiente para contener todo el entusiasmo de las tareas preliminares. Voluntad de triunfo que allanaría cuantos inconvenientes surgieran.




El primer 

Consejo

 se estructura en siete 

departamentos

 o 

consejerías

: 

Orden Público y Justicia

, 

Información y Propaganda

, 

Agricultura

, 

Instrucción Pública

, 

Transporte y Comunicaciones

, 

Economía y Abastos

, 

Trabajo

.

 

Joaquín Ascaso será elegido 

Presidente

 del 

Consejo

. Todos los 

consejeros

 son miembros de la CNT. A destacar la figura del maestro José Alberola, nombrado 

consejero

 de 

Instrucción Pública

, que en ese momento era el responsable de la escuela racionalista de Fraga. Durante años había contribuido a abrir escuelas en varios puntos de la geografía española, compaginando trabajo y militancia. Había participado en la fundación de la FAI y era uno de los oradores habituales en conferencias y mítines propagandistas del anarcosindicalismo, además de colaborador asiduo en la prensa anarquista.




Paradójicamente, 

Aragón alcanza así por primera vez en la historia moderna su “autonomía territorial”

, postergada durante años por las vicisitudes políticas, la escasa motivación 

aragonesista

 y 

republicana

 y, sobre todo, por la llegada de la guerra. En cualquier caso, no se puede comparar con otros organismos territoriales de ese momento, por el carácter 

revolucionario

 del proceso constituyente del 

Consejo

. Así nos lo recuerdan las primeras resoluciones del 

Consejo

 publicadas desde Fraga los días 18 y 28 de octubre, respectivamente:




(…)No se trata, pues, de un estamento más. Nuestro Consejo de Aragón no es igual a la Generalitat de Cataluña. Tendrá quizá alguna similitud, pero su diferencia es notable. La Generalitat se creó de acuerdo a unos cánones constitucionales y a las características de una región. Nosotros hemos nacido sin pedir permiso a nadie más que al pueblo soberano. (…)




(…)La revolución que viene produciéndose en Aragón nos obliga a ser distintos de las demás regiones. No quiere esto decir que tengamos un concepto cantonalista. El cantón implica reducción, frontera. Cantón, en Aragón, es un lugar destinado a juego de pelota, con paredes enfrente y a los lados: una especie, en fin, de encajonamiento. Lo contrario, precisamente, a nuestra idea de amplia, absoluta universalización. Pero repárese bien: la revolución no se hace a fuerza de leyes; que nadie nos tome por legisladores. Somos una convención revolucionaria que se nutre de la savia revolucionaria que nos llega de los pueblos liberados. (…)




La capitalidad de Fraga

 

será efímera

: a finales de diciembre de 1936, el 

Consejo

 se trasladará a Caspe, población de la provincia de Zaragoza, donde permanecerá hasta su disolución 

manu militari

 en agosto de 1937 por las tropas de Lister. La brevedad del primer 

Consejo

 no estuvo reñida con la intensidad de los acontecimientos. Desde el primer momento, tuvo que lidiar con muchos detractores, sobre todo del 

Gobierno central

, pero también de los sectores políticos más autoritarios y supeditados a la Unión Soviética. La propia Generalitat catalana y parte del 

republicanismo

 y 

socialismo

 se mantuvieron recelosos ante la hegemonía libertaria y la influencia ejercida en buena parte del territorio. No escatimaron en lanzar bulos y acusaciones infundadas, como la de haber convertido el 

Consejo

 en un verdadero gobierno. Afirmaciones que no corresponden a la realidad por su propia naturaleza, donde la 

asamblea fundacional

 descarta esa posibilidad. Además, el 

Consejo

 no dispuso en ningún momento de una 

consejería

 o departamento de 

Guerra

 propia. Eso no impidió que recibiera toda clase de improperios, como el de 

gobiernillo

 de Fraga primero y de Caspe después. 




Quizá fuera premonitorio lo ocurrido en el mismo mes de diciembre, cuando la aviación 

republicana

 bombardeó por 

error

 la antigua casa señorial de la finca de 

Monte Julia

, donde se encontraba parte del 

Consejo

. El aparato procedía del campo de aviación de Sariñena -población cercana-, casualmente comandado por Alfonso de los Reyes, miembro del Partido Comunista. De alguna manera, es razonable pensar que, ante todas estas hostilidades, se aceptará el reconocimiento legal ofrecido por el gobierno de Largo Caballero, con la condición de dar cabida a representantes de partidos políticos en el 

Consejo

.




Pero fue en Fraga donde se sentaron las bases de algunos de los proyectos más ambiciosos y donde el 

Consejo

 comenzó su andadura. Una de las primeras resoluciones, con una fuerte carga simbólica, fue la de que los 

consejeros

 no percibirían sueldo alguno, una práctica heredada de la tradición 

cenetista

, en la que ningún cargo de la organización era retribuido; manera de evitar desigualdades entre sus miembros y la corrupción. José Alberola redactó el proyecto 

La Nueva Escuela. Eduquemos instruyamos racionalmente

, en un artículo publicado en el 

Boletín número 3

 del 

Consejo

. En él se perfila el proyecto inicial sobre educación. La c

onsejería de Trabajo

 empezó a organizar estructuras sólidas sobre la capacidad productora y la distribución del consumo, y un proyecto de 

Seguridad Social

. Desde el departamento de

 Transporte y Comunicación

, dirigido por Francisco Ponzán, se empezó a organizar un ambicioso plan de comunicación de mercancías y pasajeros que incluía la mejora de carreteras y caminos rurales. Se adecuó y mejoró el servicio de correos y las líneas telefónicas. Cabe destacar la 

disposición

 de la propia 

Presidencia 

del 

Consejo

 para acabar con ciertos  abusos y desmanes cometidos por 

grupos armados

 y 

milicias 

asentadas en los 

pueblos liberados

, una cuestión demandada por los propios habitantes y colectivistas del territorio. Otra cuestión no menos importante fue la edición del 

Boletín del Consejo

, que se publicaría con regularidad para mantener a la población informada de todas las resoluciones que se iban adoptando, y que ilustra la labor desarrollada y la filosofía del mismo.




Este mes de octubre se cumplen 90 años de aquel intento revolucionario

 de subvertir las anquilosadas estructuras sociales. Es una oportunidad para mirarnos en el espejo de nuestra historia: la obrera, la de la gente común. Hacerlo sin autocomplacencia contribuirá a obtener más preguntas que certezas y nos alejará de cualquier dogmatismo, pero también nos permitirá poner en cuestión ciertos comportamientos políticos. Me parece oportuno compartir unas palabras de José Alberola, pronunciadas en una conferencia suya en Lleida en marzo de 1937:




O se cree en el pueblo o se cree en la autoridad. Si creemos en el pueblo, triunfaremos y nos apartaremos de cualquier veleidad sectaria. (…)




(…) Cuanto más vinculemos nuestro esfuerzo a los esfuerzos desinteresados, al trabajo creador, a la aspiración de libertad, a la convivencia no forzada, a la iniciativa libre, a la federación de esfuerzos, a la cultura y a la cordialidad, al progreso sin interrupción y sobre todo a los valores imponderables de la moral, más cerca estaremos del aliento popular y más propicio veremos el mañana. La revolución será así indestructible y los anarquistas tendremos, más que galardón material, la satisfacción íntima de haberla impulsado confundiéndonos con el pueblo y no apartándonos de él.




 




Fraga 18 de Octubre 2026

title: ‘Temporary’ for 41 years: Turkey’s village guard system
content:
When Turkey introduced the system of so-called temporary village guards on March 26, 1985, it was officially intended as a time-limited “security measure.” Forty-one years later, the armed structure remains in place. Tens of thousands of village guards are still on duty, even though the PKK has ended its phase of armed struggle and the Peace and Democratic Society Process now has a legal framework.




This brings a question back into focus: How should the armed civilian apparatus that the Turkish state built up over decades during its war against the Kurdish freedom movement be dismantled?




According to the Turkish Ministry of Interior, 48,365 village guards were still on duty as of October 31, 2025. Their number is likely to have since fallen to approximately 47,000–48,000 due to retirements and the suspension of new recruitment.




The system, originally established as a temporary arrangement, thus remains part of the state security apparatus in Kurdistan more than four decades later.




A temporary measure becomes a permanent institution




The legal basis was established in 1985 through an amendment to Article 74 of the Village Law. Initially introduced in 22 provinces, the village guard system was intended to support military operations against the PKK by recruiting armed forces from the local population. During the parliamentary debates, historical parallels were already drawn with the Hamidiye Regiments of the Ottoman Empire.




The system was further expanded following the declaration of a state of emergency in 1987. From 1992 onward, village guards began receiving state salaries, and by the following year, the organization was operating in 35 provinces. Their numbers rose from around 62,000 in 1995 to approximately 90,000 by the end of the decade. Between 1985 and 2009, a total of 123,476 people served as village guards.




The system’s originally intended temporary nature was also largely abandoned in legal terms in 2007. Under Law No. 5673, which was passed unanimously, village guards who retired at the age of 55 after at least 15 years of service became entitled to a monthly pension. At the same time, a standard personnel ceiling of 40,000 was established, which the government could increase by up to 50 percent. However, the corresponding implementing regulation was never made public.




What had supposedly been a transitional arrangement had thus become a permanently funded and institutionally entrenched armed structure.




Human rights violations and widespread impunity




The history of the village guard system is closely linked to serious human rights violations in the Kurdish provinces. According to a study by the Human Rights Association (IHD), village guards were held responsible for the deaths of 183 people and injuries to another 259 between 1990 and March 2009. The report also documented 38 cases of villages being set on fire, 14 village evacuations, 70 cases of robbery, and 454 cases of torture and ill-treatment.




Particularly striking is the low number of criminal convictions. According to official figures from the Ministry of Interior, crimes committed by 5,139 village guards were recorded between 1985 and 2006. Although 853 of them were arrested, only 264 were convicted. This represents approximately five percent of those whose crimes were recorded in the statistics.




State-issued weapons were also used in private disputes. In 2009, four people were killed outside a police station during a feud between two village guard families in Ergani. Prosecutors sought four counts of aggravated life imprisonment for each of the five village guards involved. The killings were allegedly carried out with state-issued Kalashnikov rifles.




That same year, the Bilge massacre in Mardin province once again brought the system under public scrutiny. Forty-four people were murdered in an attack on an engagement celebration. However, a parliamentary investigation commission subsequently stopped short of recommending the abolition of the village guard system, instead proposing its restructuring through training and stricter disciplinary measures. Akın Birdal, then a member of parliament for the BDP, criticized the report for downplaying the state’s responsibility.




The Human Rights Association also called for an investigation into possible links between the village guard system and the intelligence organization JITEM.




Forced displacement and obstacles to return




The consequences of the system extend far beyond individual acts of violence. During the war, thousands of Kurdish villages and hamlets were evacuated, numerous settlements were destroyed, and large sections of the rural population were displaced. According to a report by the Turkish parliament, a total of 3,428 settlements were evacuated across 20 provinces, including 905 villages and 2,523 hamlets. The Ministry of Interior put the number of displaced people at 378,335. Human rights and civil society organizations, however, estimate that between one and three million people were affected.




A 2011 study by the Akdeniz Göç-Der association illustrates the extent to which pressure from village guards contributed to this displacement. In the study, 65.9 percent of displaced respondents identified pressure from village guards as the main reason they had fled.




Even after the most intensive military operations had ended, returning to many villages remained fraught with considerable risks. In 2002, six families who had returned to the village of Uğrak, near Bismil, following a court ruling were subjected to an armed attack. Three people, including a six-year-old child, were killed.




In Uluköy and Altınsu, the return of displaced residents in 2004 was even made conditional on their joining the village guard system themselves. The structure thus served not only as an instrument of military control but also directly affected the ability of displaced people to return to their homeland.




Abolition announced repeatedly




The dissolution of the village guard system has been under discussion for many years. As early as June 2009, the High Council for Counterterrorism recommended its gradual abolition. Under the proposal, existing village guards were to be provided with alternative employment opportunities, particularly in agriculture and livestock farming.




In May 2013, then-Interior Minister Muammer Güler stated that village guards would remain on duty until the PKK had been completely disarmed. The system would then be abolished.




However, following the collapse of the peace process at the time, the government took the opposite course. In December 2015, 5,000 additional positions for temporary village guards were created across 22 provinces.




The abolition of the system was thus repeatedly made conditional on changing security circumstances, while the state-established structure itself remained in place and was even expanded at times.




With the current Peace and Democratic Society Process, the question has resurfaced under changed political circumstances. The PKK has ended its phase of armed struggle and recently announced the withdrawal of its forces from Turkish territory. The focus is now on implementing the legal framework and the role of the National Security Council (MGK) in verifying disarmament.




However, the framework law contains no binding provision for the abolition of the village guard system. Whether and when this issue will be addressed in political negotiations remains unclear.




Disarmament requires legal and social guarantees




For human rights organizations and representatives of Kurdish politics, simply disbanding the armed units is not enough. They are calling for a process that addresses both disarmament and the social reintegration of former village guards.




In this context, the Peace Foundation refers to the United Nations’ international principles for Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR). Such a program would need to include the registration and surrender of weapons, the transition to civilian employment, and independent oversight mechanisms.




At the same time, the process must neither create new forms of disadvantage nor be left solely in the hands of the state security bureaucracy.




International experiences with the dissolution of armed structures following civil wars, such as in Nepal, are cited as possible models. However, the key consideration is to adapt such measures to the social and political conditions in Kurdistan.




Another challenge concerns addressing past abuses. The abolition of the village guard system would not eliminate criminal responsibility for human rights violations committed in the past. Human rights organizations are therefore calling for independent investigations to establish individual accountability and prevent the continuation of the impunity that has prevailed until now.




The return of displaced people is also closely linked to any potential dissolution of the system. This includes restoring safe living conditions in villages, returning confiscated land, and providing adequate compensation for destroyed property.




The unresolved question of state disarmament




While the PKK’s disarmament is to be accompanied by state verification and monitoring procedures, no comparable legal roadmap has yet been established for the Turkish state’s armed civilian structures.




The demands of human rights organizations and Kurdish political forces therefore focus on four key areas: a legally binding timetable for abolishing the village guard system; a transparent disarmament and reintegration program under independent civilian oversight; criminal investigations into serious human rights violations; and the return of displaced people, including the restitution of their land and compensation.




Whether these demands will become part of future political negotiations remains unclear. What is certain is that the village guard system, introduced as a temporary measure in 1985, remains in place 41 years later, and its abolition has yet to be included in the legal framework of the peace process.

title: KJK calls for action for Varisheh Moradi: Do not remain silent against executions
content:
The Coordination of the Kurdistan Women’s Communities (KJK) issued a written statement regarding the Iranian regime’s renewed death sentence against Kurdish activist Varisheh Moradi.




Condemning the Iranian regime’s actions, the KJK stated that women would defeat the policy of executions through their struggle for freedom and solidarity and organize in all areas of life to gain a voice and secure their rights.




‘Varisheh Moradi has represented the will of all imprisoned and freedom-loving women’




KJK recalled that Varisheh Moradi was arrested by the Iranian regime on August 1, 2023, and sentenced to death in November 2024. The sentence was overturned by a court in 2025.




The statement noted that Moradi had made her voice heard by women and people around the world through her stance and resistance since the day of her arrest. By refusing to appear in court, she took an open and uncompromising stand against the state’s unlawful practices and injustices, it said.




The statement continued: “Through her resistance and determination, Varisheh Moradi has represented the will of all imprisoned and freedom-loving women held in the Iranian regime’s prisons. In doing so, she has helped advance the struggle of women in prison in a more organized manner.”




‘The regime uses the gallows as a threat against society’




The statement stressed that the Iranian regime aims to intimidate women and deter them from pursuing their struggle for freedom through death sentences. These sentences, it added, are used as a means of exerting psychological pressure on prisoners.




The KJK stated: “The regime uses the gallows as a threat against society. It sustains its existence by executing dozens of people every day on various grounds. In response to the external pressures and difficulties it faces, it seeks to prolong its rule by suppressing the uprisings by society and women through policies of repression, prohibition, torture, execution, starvation, and unemployment. In reality, this is a regime that has committed grave crimes against humanity and lost its legitimacy in every respect. Executions have become a daily practice for the regime. Through this method, it seeks to break the will of society and women.”




‘The regime fears the power of women’s struggle’




The KJK stated that life in Iran is under constant threat due to the regime’s policies, emphasizing that the hopes of women and young people for the future are being stifled by repression and death sentences.




The statement noted that women face the harshest punishments when they step outside the boundaries imposed by the state: “In recent years, dozens of women activists and politicians have been arrested and executed. Death sentences have been issued against dozens of women, including Varisheh Moradi, Pakshan Azizi, and Nejme Emînî. This regime is hostile to women, young people, and society as a whole. It is primarily because it fears the power of women’s struggle that it is intensifying repression and executions.”




‘As repression intensifies, so does society’s struggle’




The statement noted that the peoples of Iran and Rojhilatên(Eastern) Kurdistan, particularly women, have been engaged in an ongoing struggle against the regime’s policies, consistently voicing their demands for a democratic system and a life of freedom.




The KJK stated that the regime responded to these demands with executions, adding: “Through a racist, religious fundamentalist, and sexist mentality, the regime seeks to suppress the democratic demands and uprisings of society and women. The more a state oppresses its own people and subjects them to fear, the more those people will continue their struggle against the regime and refuse to remain silent. As the regime intensifies executions, repression, bans, and arrests, society’s resistance and struggle will only grow stronger.”




‘Zeinab Jalalian and Varisheh Moradi are symbols of resistance’




Emphasizing that women and young people have resisted the Iranian regime’s policies for years, the KJK highlighted the struggle of Zeinab Jalalian, who has been imprisoned for 18 years.




Jalalian has continued her resistance despite being deprived of her fundamental rights for years, the statement said, noting that the Iranian regime has been unable to suppress the impact of her struggle and a growing movement of resistance has emerged around her.




The KJK stated that Varisheh Moradi and dozens of other women imprisoned in Iran have continued this struggle in recent years, adding: “Varisheh Moradi and dozens of women held in different prisons across Iran are continuing and expanding this struggle. They have become symbols and pioneers of the ‘Jin Jiyan Azadî’ revolution.




Their struggle and resistance have developed from a historical, social, and political legacy and are rooted in a profound foundation. The struggle and resistance of Kurdish women gained a universal dimension through the ‘Jin Jiyan Azadî’ [Woman, Life, Freedom] revolution, raising awareness around the world.




No matter how hard the regime tries to silence the voice and suppress the influence of the ‘Jin Jiyan Azadî’ revolution, these policies will fail. This is because Iranian society possesses a profound potential and an inherent dynamic for change. This potential remains alive and is always open to transformation.”




Call to unite in the struggle against the Iranian regime’s policy of executions




The KJK Coordination called on the democratic public and all freedom-loving women to unite in the struggle against the Iranian regime’s policy of executions.




The statement concluded:




“As the KJK, we appeal to the democratic public and all freedom-loving women: Do not remain silent in the face of these inhumane executions. Make your struggle more organized and comprehensive than ever before.




Just as women everywhere stood together with one voice and a united stance in support of the ‘Jin Jiyan Azadî’ revolution, they must now stand by the pioneers of that revolution, defeat the policy of executions, and put an end to it.




Mobilize under the slogan: ‘Execution is a crime against humanity. No to the gallows, yes to a life of freedom!’”

title: Kadınlar Fatmanur ve Hifa İkra için yürüdü: ‘Hesabını soracağız’
content:
İstanbul - Hifa İkra’ya yönelik cinsel istismarda bulunduğu gerekçesiyle yargılanan Ayhan Şengüler hakkında verilen beraat kararına karşı kadın örgütleri, Taksim Tünel’den Şişhane Meydanı'na yürüdü. Kadınlar, 3 yaşından itibaren cinsel istismara maruz kaldığı belirtilen Hifa İkra ile yıllarca şiddet gördüğü ifade edilen annesi Fatmanur Çelik’in şüpheli ölümlerinin aydınlatılmasını ve dosyada sorumluluğu bulunan kişi ve kurumların yargılanmasını talep etti.

Yapılan açıklamada, Hifa İkra’nın maruz kaldığı istismarı defalarca dile getirdiği, Fatmanur Çelik’in ise kızının yaşadıklarının hesabını sormak için adliye önünde nöbet tuttuğu hatırlatıldı. Anne ve kızının şüpheli biçimde ölü bulunmasına rağmen etkin bir soruşturma yürütülmediği vurgulanarak, “Fatmanur ve Hifa İkra'nın ölümünün üzerinden aylar geçti ama hâlâ etkin bir soruşturma yürütülmedi. Biz bu dosyanın üzerinin örtülmesini kabul etmiyoruz; suç ortağı olan tüm kurumlar ve kişiler yargılansın” denildi.

Kadınlar, Ayhan Şengüler hakkındaki davanın başından itibaren eksik ve yanlış yürütüldüğünü belirtti. Açıklamada, Şengüler’in duruşmalara katılmadığı halde hakkında yakalama kararı çıkarılmadığı hatırlatıldı, “Mahkeme, hakkında hem bir çocuk hem de bir kadın üzerinde şiddet uygulamak ve birçok başka ayrı suçtan bunca ciddi iddia olan bir erkeği usulünce değerlendirmemiş ve faili beraat ettirmiştir. Bu cezasızlık politikası erkek adaletin ta kendisidir” ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Açıklamada, duruşma salonunda çocuk istismarı iddialarının ele alınış biçimine de tepki gösterildi. Kadınlar, “6 yaşındaki bir çocuğa, herkesin önünde maruz kaldığı istismarı tekrar tekrar anlatmak zorunda bıraktıkları o mahkeme salonunda istismarcı beraat etti” dediler.

Kadınlar, Fatmanur Çelik’in daha önce dile getirdiği “Başıma bir şey gelirse intihar demeyin” sözünü hatırlatarak, anne ve kızının korunması için gerekli önlemlerin neden alınmadığını sordu. Açıklamanın devamında şu ifadeler yer aldı: “Fatmanur Çelik mekanizmaların işletilmesi için uğraşırken, faili koruyan tarikat ve devlet işbirliğine karşı mücadele ederken dosya bir şekilde sürüncemede bırakıldı, beraat mütalaası verildi. ‘Başıma bir şey gelirse intihar demeyin’ diyen Fatmanur; devletin, yargının, kurumların kendisini korumayacağını bilerek dile getirdi bu cümleyi. Soruyoruz: Fatmanur Çelik ve Hifa İkra için koruyucu, önleyici tedbirler neden alınmadı? Neden şüpheli ölümlerinin aydınlatılması için hiçbir şey yapılmadı?”

Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı'nın da sorumluluğuna dikkat çekildi, şiddetin önlenmesi ve kadınlarla çocukların korunması için gerekli mekanizmaların işletilmesi çağrısı yapıldı.

“Eşit, özgür, şiddetten uzak bir yaşam kuruncaya kadar erkek egemenliğine karşı mücadele etmeye devam edeceğiz. Fatmanur Çelik ve Hifa İkra’nın hesabını soracağız” denerek mücadeleye devam edeceklerini duyurdular.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: DEM Parti ile Yeni Parti görüşecek: İzleme Komisyonu için temaslar başlıyor
content:
"Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci" kapsamında siyasi temasların bu hafta yoğunlaşması bekleniyor. DEM Parti, yarın Yeni Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel ile görüşecek. Meclis’te kurulması planlanan İzleme Komisyonu’nun yapısı ve çalışma esaslarına ilişkin temasların da önümüzdeki günlerde başlaması bekleniyor.

Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti), süreçte gelinen aşama ve atılması gereken adımlara ilişkin siyasi partilerle görüşmeler gerçekleştirecek.

Bu kapsamda DEM Parti heyeti, yarın Yeni Parti Genel Merkezi’nde Genel Başkan Özgür Özel ile saat 12.30’da bir araya gelecek.

DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti üyeleri Pervin Buldan ve Mithat Sancar, daha önce AKP yetkilileri, Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz ve Meclis Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş ile görüşmeler gerçekleştirmişti.

Görüşmelerde sürecin geldiği aşama, çerçeve yasa sonrasında yapılması öngörülen yasal düzenlemeler ve Meclis’te kurulması planlanan İzleme Komisyonu gündeme gelmişti.

Komisyonun kuruluşuna ilişkin temasların da önümüzdeki günlerde başlaması bekleniyor. Meclis Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş’un, komisyonun yapısı ve çalışma esasları hakkında siyasi partilerin temsilcileriyle görüşmesi öngörülüyor.

Komisyonun üye sayısı ve yapısının, siyasi partilerle yapılacak görüşmelerin ardından netleşmesi bekleniyor.

Meclis Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş, daha önce yaptığı açıklamada Meclis’in açılmasıyla birlikte İzleme Komisyonu’nun hızlı bir şekilde kurulacağını belirtmişti.

Ancak komisyonun kuruluşuna ilişkin görüşmelerin ertelendiği ve bu haftaya bırakıldığı ifade ediliyor. Önümüzdeki günlerde yapılması beklenen temasların ardından komisyonun yapısı ve çalışma takviminin netleşmesi bekleniyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Rizomatica
title: Invitación abierta al “Seminario Justiciables: Expectativas de justicia en un mundo cada vez más injusto” en Temuco
content:
Reflexionar críticamente sobre la administración de la justicia es lo que propone este seminario que tendrá lugar en la Universidad de la Frontera, Campus Andrés Bello, el lunes 19 de octubre en el Auditorio Selva Saavedra y el martes 20 de octubre en el Auditorio Dra. Marianela De Negri Coria, de 9:30 a 18:00 horas. Junto a investigadoras/es, abogadas/os, actores comunitarios, defensoras/es, estudiantes de grado y posgrado, y personas en búsqueda activa por justicia. Invitación abierta, sin costo ni inscripción previa.




Fabien Le Bonniec es Dr. en Antropología e Investigador principal del Fondecyt “Hacia una antropología de las injusticias en el sur de Chile: Expectativas de justicia, multidimensionalidad de las experiencias de injusticia, constitución de comunidades morales y producción de praxis y saberes situados”, desde donde surge el “Seminario Justiciables: Expectativas de justicia en un mundo cada vez más injusto”.




Instancia de encuentro en la que, durante dos días, invitan a reflexionar críticamente sobre la administración de justicia a partir del enfoque etnográfico, el análisis de las políticas punitivas y la experiencia directa de actores del ámbito socio-jurídico y comunitario. “Proponemos mirar los tribunales, las cárceles y las normativas del Estado como espacios donde se producen, reproducen o disputan activamente las desigualdades e injusticias”, señaló Fabien Le Bonniec.




Para ello, convocaron de manera transversal a investigadoras/es, abogadas/os, actores comunitarios, defensoras/es, estudiantes de grado y posgrado, y lo que se denomina “justiciables”, que en este caso, son familiares de personas privadas de libertad y víctimas de siniestros u otras formas de violencia. Para llegar al título de este Seminario, el equipo pensó en el sentir de personas con quienes se han encontrado en tribunales. “Expectativas de que van a encontrar algo de justicia, al mismo tiempo que sentimientos de desconfianza al confrontar un mundo injusto y desigual”, frustraciones cada vez más presentes en la sociedad y que “van más allá de los grupos que consideramos tradicionalmente vulnerables», puntualizó Le Bonniec.




En el marco del seminario, el término «justiciables» trasciende a la definición que uno puede encontrar en un diccionario, esto es, “persona que puede o debe someterse a la acción de los tribunales de justicia». La Dra. Gloria Carrillo, Antropóloga y Co-investigadora de Injusticias del Sur, señaló que “es importante entender a las y los justiciables como sujetos activos con agencia, personas, familias, comunidades y colectivos que entran en contacto directo con el sistema judicial, estatal o carcelario”.




Para quienes organizan esta instancia, las personas justiciables, lejos de ser receptores pasivos del castigo o del procedimiento judicial, son quienes experimentan las barreras e inteligibilidades del derecho estatal y, al mismo tiempo, organizan formas de resistencia, buscan alternativas de reparación y disputan el sentido de la justicia y de la injusticia.




Para ampliar las reflexiones, las mesas están compuestas por personas que están investigando para su tesis de pregrado, doctoral u otros proyectos, problemáticas relacionadas con los tribunales, la privación de libertad y los usos y apropiaciones de la normatividad estatal. Se harán presentes también diversos actores que como «justiciables» han experimentado la justicia estatal y las injusticias asociadas a ella.




Para este equipo de trabajo, co-producir conocimientos y teorías situadas implica generar espacios de encuentro como este seminario, donde se aborda principalmente problemáticas locales pero con una mirada que no se puede sustraer de los contextos globales. “De esta forma, esperamos aportar desde el sur, con sus particularidades, a problemas que afectan a todo el país, y que se expresa por ejemplo, bajo la forma de la desconfianza y la crisis del sistema judicial en Chile”, señaló Fabien Le Bonniec.




El seminario es organizado por el equipo Fondecyt Nº1242009 Injusticias del Sur; apoyado por la Facultad de Educación, Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades, la Línea de Antropología del Departamento de Ciencias Sociales de la Universidad de la Frontera; financiado por la Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo, ANID; con la colaboración de Conexión 2030; Doctorado en Ciencias Sociales y Magíster en Ciencias Sociales UFRO; Vio Demos; Centro de Estudios y Promoción de los Derechos Humanos y el Núcleo Científico Tecnológico en Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades UFRO. Este seminario propone una mirada a la administración de justicia a partir del enfoque etnográfico, el análisis de las políticas punitivas y la experiencia de actores del ámbito socio-jurídico y comunitario. author: David Swanson
title: Stealing Palestine, Stealing Enlightenment
content:
Asia, Bigotry, Europe, Immorality, North America, Why End War, World

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 18, 2026

Yoav Litvin and Ilan Pappé’s Wired to Steal includes a history of European anti-Semitic horrors and the development of Zionist propaganda, propaganda that from the start drew on white-supremacy, eugenics, militarism, nationalism, eventually even Nazism, and the settler-colonial ploy of stealing territory, getting oneself attacked, and then labeling and understanding genocidal violence as “defense.”

“Zionists were widely unpopular among most European Jews, who saw the ideals of the Enlightenment, emancipation, equality, and integration as their ultimate goal.”

The authors trace the origins of Zionism, at least in large part, to Evangelical Christians who, much like back-to-Africa racists in the United States, sought the removal of people against whom they were prejudiced, but in this case did so for magical reasons of the Second Coming of Christ and related myths.

Zionism took the worst elements of rightwing Western ideologies and, in the fashion of the victim of child abuse who becomes a child abuser, claimed them as its own. Certain strains of non-Jewish, even anti-Semitic, Western politics have supported Zionism since before it existed and never yet ceased to celebrate it. But it strikes me that many in the Western and, for that matter, non-Western world moved on from the levels of bigotry and racism and colonialism of centuries gone by, even while hanging onto a vestige of those things in their endless support for the government of Israel, and did so for so long and with such dedication that Zionism has been returning the favor, has been re-implanting authoritarian, theocratic, militarist notions in a Western world that had partially outgrown them.

Of course, one is not supposed to say that. Even after the U.S. government has launched so many wars demanded by the Israeli government, even after so many Congress members have been on so many re-education tours of Israel, even after so many U.S. police departments have been trained by the Israeli military, even after so many weapons have been developed and “battle tested” by or in collaboration with the Israeli government and then sold to the West, even after Western borders have been made to look like Israel’s borders, the choices offered by Zionist propaganda are (1) speak no ill of the Israeli government ever, or (2) you are an idiotic, goofy bigot from centuries gone by who believes in hateful magical nonsense to discriminate against Jewish people (even if you are a Jewish person).

Nonetheless, for many years, millions of people have believed both that

a) governments should uphold freedom of religion and speech and assembly, not discriminate on race or sex or any other irrelevant factor, and at least sometimes not kill people, and

b) the Israeli government should discriminate against non-Jews, and restrict rights and kill as needed to uphold a government dominated by Jews.

And sometimes one has to choose between these ideas. Is it more important to ban criticism of the Israeli government even if it means that there will be no more political demonstrations on a college campus about anything at all? Is it more important to uphold state-racism and state-religion in Israel even as the idea spreads well beyond Israel? Is it more important that Israel get away with its crimes even as the structures of international law are at risk of crumbling?

To be clear, these are my musings upon reading Wired to Steal, not necessarily the thoughts of the authors of that book. But I recommend the book, albeit with a couple of caveats.

First, it’s always odd to treat political policies in terms applicable only to human beings. Analyzing human emotions to explain public policy usually implies a ridiculous belief in the actual existence of democracy. Here it does not. Here the topic is the propagandizing of the Israeli public. Those doing the propagandizing are cursorily identified as driven by greed. Yet, most greedy rulers do not do exactly what the government of Israel does, and I think Israel’s rulers would not unless they were committed to acting on, if not actually believing, their own propaganda. That topic could use more attention.

Second, the book is oddly scientistic. I would skip the whole first part which is painfully familiar silliness about whether chimps or bonobos doom us all to be warlike or cooperative. Largely debunked studies like Stanford Prison and Milgram come up repeatedly. We’re told which section of the brain some process may take place in even when it’s difficult to discern why that should matter. We’re even fed questionable studies about the universality of facial expressions and highly questionable studies about micro-expressions to no apparent purpose. In my humble opinion, we should of course be as scientific as possible in areas where science has developed something useful, but as humble as possible about acting scientific where it has not.

title: Sevda Karaca’dan Antep’teki taciz davası için dayanışma çağrısı: “İşçiler, kadınlar, kadın işçiler yalnız değildir!”
content:
Emek Partisi (EMEP) Gaziantep Milletvekili Sevda Karaca, Aslansoy Tekstil’in sahibi Ahmet Aslansoy’un yargılandığı davanın salı günü görülecek duruşması öncesinde dayanışma çağrısı yaptı. Karaca, “Herkesi bu davaya sahip çıkmaya, kadın işçiyle dayanışmaya ve Salı günü saat 11.00’de Antep Adliyesine çağırıyoruz” dedi.

Sevda Karaca, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, davayı “İşçi bir kadının, sırtını hem paraya hem de siyasete yaslamış kerli ferli bir patrona karşı cesaretini ortaya koyduğu bir davanın duruşması” sözleriyle tanımladı.

Aslansoy Tekstil’in sahibi Ahmet Aslansoy’un fabrikada çaycı olarak çalışan bir kadın işçiyi sistematik biçimde taciz ettiğini geçen yıl duyurduklarını belirten Karaca, şunları söyledi:

“Parayla, tehditle, güçle susturulmak istenen kadın, onurunu ve hakkını savunmak için adli makamlara başvurmuş, ancak sessizlikle karşı karşıya bırakılmıştı. Ancak yılmamış, BİRTEK-SEN’den ve bizden destek istemişti.”

Karaca, olayın duyurulmasının ardından soruşturma dosyasının yeniden ele alındığını ifade ederek şu açıklamayı yaptı:

“Bizim olayı duyurmamız üzerine, 1 yıl boyunca hiçbir işlem yapılmadan bekletilen soruşturma dosyası raflardan indirilmek zorunda kalmıştı. Ahmet Aslansoy’un bütün gücüne rağmen suçun açık delilleri iddianame hazırlattı ve dava açıldı.”

Duruşma sürecine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde de bulunan Karaca, “Ahmet Aslansoy ilk iki celse türlü bahanelerle duruşmadan kaçtı. Üçüncü celse mecbur kalıp katıldığı duruşmada suçunu inkar etti. Mağdur kadına ve avukatına suç duyurularında bulundu” ifadelerini kullandı.

Karaca, Aslansoy’un hukuk profesörlerinden aldığı görüşlerle suçsuz olduğunu ispatlamaya çalıştığını ifade etti.

“Ahmet Aslansoy’un parasına, iktidar partisine, HSK üyeliği yapmış hukuk profesörlerine, yargıda etkisine karşı işçi kadının elindeki tek güç sınıf ve kadın dayanışması” diyen Karaca, açıklamasını şu sözlerle tamamladı:

“Herkesi bu davaya sahip çıkmaya, kadın işçiyle dayanışmaya ve Salı günü saat 11.00’de Antep Adliyesine çağırıyoruz. İşçiler, kadınlar, kadın işçiler yalnız değildir!”

Salı günü Antep Adliyesinde çok önemli bir davanın duruşması görülecek. İşçi bir kadının, sırtını hem paraya hem de siyasete yaslamış kerli ferli bir patrona karşı cesaretini ortaya koyduğu bir davanın duruşması. Aslansoy Tekstil’in sahibi, AKP Gaziantep milletvekili Derya Bakbak'ın babası Ahmet Aslansoy’un fabrikasında çaycı olarak çalışan bir kadın işçiyi sistematik bir şekilde taciz ettiği olayı geçen sene duyurmuştuk. Parayla, tehditle, güçle susturulmak istenen kadın, onurunu ve hakkını savunmak için adli makamlara başvurmuş, ancak sessizlikle karşı karşıya bırakılmıştı. Ancak yılmamış, BİRTEK-SEN’den ve bizden destek istemişti. Bizim olayı duyurmamız üzerine, 1 yıl boyunca hiçbir işlem yapılmadan bekletilen soruşturma dosyası raflardan indirilmek zorunda kalmıştı. Ahmet Aslansoy’un bütün gücüne rağmen suçun açık delilleri iddianame hazırlattı ve dava açıldı. Ahmet Aslansoy ilk iki celse türlü bahanelerle duruşmadan kaçtı. Üçüncü celse mecbur kalıp katıldığı duruşmada suçunu inkar etti. Mağdur kadına ve avukatına suç duyurularında bulundu. Şimdi de hukuk profesörlerinden aldığı yanlı görüşlerle suçsuz olduğunu ispat etmeye çalışıyor. Ahmet Aslansoy’un parasına, iktidar partisine, HSK üyeliği yapmış hukuk profesörlerine, yargıda etkisine karşı işçi kadının elindeki tek güç sınıf ve kadın dayanışması. Herkesi bu davaya sahip çıkmaya, kadın işçiyle dayanışmaya ve Salı günü saat 11.00’de Antep Adliyesine çağırıyoruz. İşçiler, kadınlar, kadın işçiler yalnız değildir!

title: Eskişehir’den çağrı: Soykırımı besleyen bağlar kesilsin!
content:
<!-- x-tinymce/html -->Fotoğraf: Mustafa Şen

Eskişehir Filistin ile Dayanışma Platformu, 18 Ekim 2026’da Köprübaşı’nda basın açıklaması yaptı. Platform adına açıklamayı Emcet Saidoğlu okudu. Açıklamada, Gazze’de ateşkesin yürürlüğe girmesinin üzerinden bir yıl geçmesine rağmen İsrail saldırılarının, ablukanın ve Filistinlilerin zorla yerinden edilmesinin sürdüğüne dikkat çekildi. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump’ın sözde Barış Planı ve Barış Kurulu’nun eleştirildiği açıklamada, Türkiye’ye İsrail’le ilişkilerini kesme, ticareti tamamen durdurma ve Filistin halkının kendi geleceğini belirleme hakkını savunma çağrısı yapıldı.

10 Ekim 2025’te Gazze’de yürürlüğe giren ve Türkiye’nin de garantörleri arasında bulunduğu ateşkesin üzerinden bir yıl geçtiğini hatırlatan platform, ateşkese rağmen İsrail’in saldırılarının sürdüğünü belirtti. Açıklamada, ateşkes sonrasındaki saldırılarda 1500’den fazla Filistinlinin katledildiği, yaklaşık 5 bin 400 kişinin yaralandığı ifade edildi. İsrail’in ateşkesi binlerce kez ihlal ettiği belirtilirken, 7 Ekim 2023’ten bu yana Gazze’deki toplam can kaybının yaklaşık 75 bine, yaralı sayısının ise 176 bine ulaştığı kaydedildi.

Açıklamada, “Ateşkes denilen durum aslında soykırımın yavaş çekimde devam etmesinden ibaret. Bombardımanlar ve saldırılara ilaveten yardım kısıtlamaları ve yeniden yerinden etmeler de devam ediyor” denildi.

Gazze’de insani koşulların ağırlaşmaya devam ettiğine dikkat çekilen açıklamada, yaklaşık iki milyon insanın barınma ihtiyacı bulunduğu, 1,4 milyon insanın yıl sonuna kadar kriz düzeyinde veya daha ağır açlıkla karşı karşıya kalacağı belirtildi. Çok az sayıda hastanenin sınırlı hizmet verebildiği Gazze’de ilaç, tıbbi malzeme ve tedavi olanaklarının yetersiz olduğu vurgulandı. En az 4 bini çocuk olmak üzere 18 bin 500’den fazla hastanın Gazze dışında tedavi olabilmek için nakil beklediği, nakil beklerken hayatını kaybedenlerin sayısının ise bini aştığı ifade edildi.

Temiz su ve kanalizasyon altyapısının yıkılmasıyla hastalıkların yayıldığına dikkat çekilen açıklamada, Filistinlilerin dördüncü kışa çadırlarda ve çökme tehlikesi altındaki binalarda girmeye hazırlandığı belirtildi.

İsrail’in ateşkes kapsamında belirlenen Sarı Hat’ı Gazze’nin içlerine doğru kaydırarak işgal alanını genişlettiğini belirten platform, bu ilerleyişin Filistinlileri yeniden yerinden ettiğini ve giderek daralan bir alana sıkıştırdığını vurguladı. Açıklamada, İsrail’in Filistinlileri topraklarını terk etmeye zorlamasının “gönüllü göç” olarak adlandırıldığı belirtilerek, “Ateşkes, Siyonist işgalin kalıcılaştırılmasının örtüsüne dönüşmüş durumda” denildi.

ABD Başkanı Donald Trump’ın Barış Planı ve Barış Kurulu’nu da eleştiren platform, yeniden inşa için vaat edilen milyarlarca doların evlerini kaybeden Filistinliler için henüz konuta dönüşmediğini ifade etti. Açıklamada, belirli aralıklarla toplanan kurul üyelerinin bugüne kadar birlikte poz vermekten başka bir şey yapmadığı belirtilerek, kurul adına yapılan açıklamaların işgal yanlısı ve direniş karşıtı olduğu kaydedildi.

Filistin meselesinin bir yardım kampanyasına indirgenemeyeceği vurgulanan açıklamada, “Filistin meselesi bir yardım kampanyası, sadaka verme meselesi değildir. Karşımızda Filistin’i Filistinlilerden temizlemeyi amaçlayan Siyonist yerleşimci sömürgecilik vardır. Gazze’nin geleceği, Trump’ın ve damadı Siyonist Jared Kushner’in yatırım hesaplarına bırakılamaz. Gazze, ‘Trump’ın Rivierası’ olamaz; Filistin halkının yurdudur” ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Gazze topraklarının beş yıldızlı otellere, lüks konutlara ve yatırım projelerine açılmasının yeniden inşa anlamına gelmeyeceği belirtilen açıklamada, “Bunun garantörü olmakla ve bunun kurulunda yer almakla barışa hizmet edilmiş olunmaz ama suça ortak olunur” denildi.

Gazze’nin geleceğine ilişkin planların Filistinlilerin iradesini ve mülkiyet haklarını yok sayamayacağını belirten platform, yeniden inşa sürecinin Filistinlilerin denetiminde yürütülmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Gazze’nin Batı Şeria’dan koparılarak dışarıdan yönetilen ayrı bir bölgeye dönüştürülmesine karşı çıkılan açıklamada, kamu arazilerinin ve özel mülklerin dışarıdan yönetilen bir yapıya devredilmesinin mülksüzleştirme tehlikesi taşıdığı belirtildi.

Barış Kurulu üyelerini, kurul görevlilerini ve yüklenici şirketleri mahkemelerde yargılanmaktan koruyacak dokunulmazlık düzenlemelerine de karşı çıkılan açıklamada, Filistinlilerin topraklarına el konulduğunda veya zarar gördüklerinde bağımsız mahkemelere başvurabilmesi ve sorumluların hesap vermesi gerektiği ifade edildi.

Açıklamada, Suudi Arabistan, Türkiye ve Pakistan’ın ortağı oldukları Mekke Savunma İttifakı da eleştirildi. Sarayları, petrol tesislerini ve Suudi Arabistan’daki saltanat rejimini korumak için gösterilen iradenin Filistinlilerin hayatını korumak için gösterilmediği belirtilerek, Gazze için işletilmeyen dayanışmanın Yemen’e karşı devreye sokulmasına itiraz edildi.

Mekke ve Medine’nin Müslümanlar açısından taşıdığı kutsallığın Suudi Arabistan’ın güvenlik politikalarına ve bölgesel hesaplarına dayanak yapılmasına karşı çıkılan açıklamada, “İttifakın adı, yapılan siyasi ve askerî tercihlerin meşruiyetini kendiliğinden sağlamaz. Bu ittifak mevcut haliyle aslında Suudi diktatörlük rejimini koruma ve kollama ittifakıdır” ifadeleri kullanıldı.

İsrail’in Yemen’e karşı savaşta Suudi Arabistan’a istihbarat desteği verdiğine ilişkin haberlerin ABD ve İsrail basınında yer aldığına dikkat çekilen açıklamada, İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu’nun Suudi Arabistan safında Yemen’e karşı savaşa katılmak istediğine ilişkin haberler de hatırlatıldı. Platform, Türkiye ve Pakistan’ın desteğinin İsrail’in askerî hedeflerine hizmet etmesine karşı olduklarını belirtti.

Hürmüz Boğazı ve Kızıldeniz’de ticaret güvenliği gerekçesiyle yürütülen politikaların Gazze’deki soykırımı gündemden düşüremeyeceği vurgulanan açıklamada, mezhepçi propagandayla halkların birbirine düşürülmesi de reddedildi. Türkiye’nin Yemen’deki Suudi baskısına karşı çıkan Yemenlilere karşı bir savaşa katılmaması gerektiği ifade edilerek hükümete bütün askeri taahhütlerini kamuoyuna açıklama çağrısı yapıldı.

Açıklamanın sonunda Türkiye’deki yetkililere seslenen Eskişehir Filistin ile Dayanışma Platformu, Filistin halkının iradesini dışlayan Barış Planı’na desteğin çekilmesini, İsrail’in de yer aldığı Barış Kurulu ve Gazze İcra Kurullarından ayrılınmasını istedi. Platform, Filistin adına işgale, vesayete ve soykırıma meşruiyet kazandırılmaması gerektiğini vurguladı.

Türkiye’nin İsrail’le diplomatik ilişkilerini kesmesi ve tanıma kararını geri çekmesi gerektiğini belirten platform, tam boykot, tam ambargo, tam tecrit ve kesintisiz yaptırım uygulanmasını talep etti. Açıklamada, üçüncü ülkeler, aracı şirketler ve Filistin adına düzenlenen belgeler üzerinden ticaret yasaklarının aşılmasının engellenmesi; gerçek alıcıların ve sevkiyat kayıtlarının açıklanması çağrısı yapıldı.

İsrail’e yük taşıyan gemilere limanların kapatılması, Maersk dahil taşıyıcılara sunulan hizmetlerin durdurulması ve ZIM şirketine ait tırların Türkiye üzerinden taşımacılık yapmasının engellenmesi istendi. SOCAR ve diğer şirketlerin Azerbaycan petrolünü Bakü-Tiflis-Ceyhan hattı üzerinden İsrail’e ulaştırmasının durdurulması, şirketlerin, alıcıların ve sevkiyattan gelir elde edenlerin açıklanması da talepler arasında yer aldı.

Platform ayrıca İncirlik ve Kürecik başta olmak üzere emperyalizmin askeri üs ve tesislerinin kapatılmasını, İsrail’e istihbarat ve lojistik desteğinin kesilmesini istedi. Gazze’ye yardımların engelsiz ulaşması ve hastaların tahliyesi için harekete geçilmesi, işgalin sona ermesi, ablukanın kaldırılması ve mültecilerin dönüş hakkının savunulması çağrısı yapıldı. Filistin dayanışmasına yönelik baskıların son bulması da talepler arasında sıralandı.

Açıklama, “Eskişehir’den haykırıyoruz: Soykırımı besleyen bağları kesin! Halkların geleceği pazarlık konusu yapılamaz!” sözleriyle sona erdi. Platform, “Soykırımcıların ve işbirlikçilerin değil, Filistin halkının ve direnişin yanındayız!” diyerek Filistin halkıyla dayanışma mesajı verdi.

title: Attack on martyrs’ cemetery in Aleppo sparks protests in Rojava
content:
An attack on the martyrs’ cemetery in the Sheikh Maqsoud (Şêxmeqsûd) neighborhood of Aleppo has sparked protests in several cities across Rojava. Unidentified individuals attacked the cemetery and desecrated graves, particularly that of YPG commander Şervan Heleb. The Councils of Martyrs’ Families condemned the attack in a joint statement and demanded an immediate investigation into the incident and the prosecution of those responsible.




The statement was read publicly in Qamişlo, Hesekê, Girkê Legê, Çilaxa, Amûdê, Tirbespiyê, Dêrik, and Dirbêsiyê, among other locations. Relatives of fallen fighters and representatives of civil society organizations and institutions participated in the gatherings. The statements were delivered in both Kurdish and Arabic.




‘A direct attack on the dignity of our people’




In their statement, the Councils of Martyrs’ Families described the attack on the cemetery in Sheikh Maqsoud as a deliberate violation of the memory of the martyrs.




“Attacking the resting places and images of the martyrs is not simply an attack on a physical structure. It is a direct attack on our sacred values and the dignity of our people,” the statement read.




The families emphasized that this was not an isolated incident. They recalled that graves and memorial portraits had previously been targeted at the martyrs’ cemetery in Shaddadi (Şedadê) and in other cities.




“The repeated attacks demonstrate that the protection of these memorial sites is not guaranteed.”




Calls for a transparent investigation




The Councils of Martyrs’ Families called on the institutions and officials responsible for the integration process to fulfill their duty to protect the cemeteries and prevent further attacks. They demanded an immediate, transparent investigation and the public prosecution of those responsible.




“This act is unacceptable under any circumstances,” the councils declared. They emphasized that the perpetrators must be identified and held accountable to prevent further attacks on martyrs’ cemeteries.




In conclusion, the families reaffirmed their determination to protect the resting places and memory of the martyrs: “The graves and memory of our martyrs are among our most sacred values. We will defend their legacy until the very end.”

title: Jineolojî Conference Delegation: Raise your voices against executions in Iran
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference Delegation issued a statement regarding the death sentence imposed on Varisheh Moradi for the second time.










https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261018113923_2026-10-18-haelen-jineloloji-konferansinda-werise-muradi-icin-basin-aciklamasi_1.mp4











The statement read:




“On behalf of the European Jineolojî Conference Delegation, women striving for freedom in European and Asian countries, and all Kurdish women, we condemn the violence and inhumane acts perpetrated by the Islamic Republic of Iran, the executions of Kurdish youth and women, and all other executions.




From here, we call on all organizations and institutions defending human rights to help amplify our voices and reach a wider audience. Stand with us, oppose the violence inflicted on women and young people by the Islamic Republic, raise your voices, speak out, and help us defend women’s rights in Iran and Rojhilatê (Eastern) Kurdistan.




We call on the Islamic Republic of Iran to release all political prisoners as soon as possible. Above all, the situation of Varisheh Moradi, Pakshan Azizi, Zeinab Jalalian, and all innocent women and young people imprisoned in the Islamic Republic’s prisons must be resolved.




No to executions! Long live Jin, Jiyan, Azadî!”




At the end of the statement, several delegates spoke in English, Persian, Italian, Spanish, and German, demanding an end to executions in Iran and the immediate revocation of the death sentence imposed on Varisheh Moradi.




The statement concluded with the slogan “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî!” [Woman, Life, Freedom].

title: IRGC intensifies drone attacks and artillery shelling in Kurdistan
content:
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has intensified its military operations in Kurdistan, launching drone attacks and artillery shelling against mountainous areas near the village of Goyleh in Marivan County, Kurdistan Province, according to sources who spoke to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN).




A resident of Goyleh told KHRN that IRGC forces arrived in the area at approximately 6:30 a.m. on Sunday, 18 October 2026, in a military convoy equipped with artillery and drones, taking up positions around the village in the Sarshiv region.




The source said the forces first struck the nearby mountainous area of Dasht-e Mil with two one-way attack drones before subjecting the area to heavy artillery shelling.




No reports of armed clashes in the area had been received at the time of publication.




The latest attacks follow similar military operations in other parts of Kurdistan in recent days.




The IRGC previously targeted the mountainous Shaho region, between Sarvabad in Kurdistan Province and Paveh in Kermanshah Province, as well as the Kalatarzan area of Sanandaj County, with one-way attack drones and artillery fire.




In a statement on Saturday, the Command of the East Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) warned that it would fully exercise its right to self-defense if the attacks continued.




According to the statement, the Iranian regime has deployed a large force of Revolutionary Guards (Pasdaran), along with heavy weapons and kamikaze (explosive-laden) unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), to the Shaho region since October 13. Iranian forces have carried out several attacks in the area since.




“We would like to emphasize that our forces have issued the necessary warnings in response to these attacks. However, this does not mean that our response will always be limited to warnings. If these attacks continue, we, as the East Kurdistan Defense Units, will fully exercise our right to self-defense and respond accordingly,” the statement said.
